This officially licensed Mortal Kombat X fight pad is a wired controller that makes it easier to play fighting games by removing the thumbsticks and changing the layout of the buttons to help have a competitive advantage when playing Mortal Kombat or similar fighting games. In theory, this is a great idea. In practice, the controller feels cheap, the buttons are click but feel cheap, and overall just feels like worse quality than the normal XBOX One controller, which isn't that great either. (I am using this with XB1). However, it does work; and to its credit, it has not broken or shown any signs that it will break in the few days I have been using it. The buttons always seem to be responsive for me and so I have to give it credit there. But with a game that relies so much on buttons that will last a while and not break, I do have my doubts about this controller. I do like the way it looks and feels in the hand, except for how light and cheap it feels. I am not an expert Mortal Kombat player so maybe this was geared towards someone who is willing to sacrifice some controller feel for lightness. I will keep using this controller and if it does break or malfunction I will update this review.

These Just Dance games are great. Disney is great. Sounds like a great formula, and it is. The only problem is both me and my 15 year old didn't know almost all of the songs. I think the target age for these songs is probably in the 8-13 range. In fairness, he does love disney songs. He loves the classics. He loves the High School Musical. So do I. but We don't know Austin & Ally or Liv & Maddie or even Teen Beach 2. So my advice: check out the song list! If you like the songs, get this, you will love it so much. If you don't know the songs but like the Disney style music in general, you will still like this game. If you like Just Dance but don't like Disney songs, you probably won't be into this. I gave it 4 stars only because to me the songs are fairly obscure. They could have thrown in a couple classics for the older kids and adults. Still, the game is fun and it's great for the family to play. The songs are family friendly as well. Little kids especially will probably enjoy this since they like any good songs that they can dance to.

Just Dance is a fun game. Plain and simple. It's not necessarily competitive, and also isn't super accurate, especially now that it doesn't require the Kinect device (but you can use it). But that doesn't matter. It is tons of fun! Lots of great dance songs and fun for up to 4 people and even more if they just want to dance along to the game. If you like to dance or want to get better at modern dancing, this game is great. My whole family enjoys it and if you liked any of the other Just Dance titles, you will also enjoy this new version. If you are using the Kinect camera, the game will show you how silly you look doing some of the dance moves, it's great fun.

The songs: They are good. Don't let the name of the game fool you though: These are obviously not all songs released in 2016 (this being 2015 at the time of this review) and some of the songs were pop hits years ago. But almost all of them are good songs, and that's what matters. You can see a song list above so I won't type out all the songs but I'm a 40 year old guy and I really enjoyed the songs. My moves on the other hand leave something to be desired, but I still have fun with it! And isn't that the point? Different and fun and highly recommended for anyone who likes dancing or think they would want to have this for a party or something. Great game.

I have an old Turtle Beach headset that I haven't been able to connect to my XBOX one Day One Edition controller. I thought about getting the Microsoft adapter but I heard mixed reviews about it. This Turtle Beach Ear Force adapter seemed interesting to me since it was the same brand as my headphones and has the interesting Super Human Hearing feature.

The Super Human Hearing basically takes quiet background sounds and amplifies them which can be extremely helpful in FPS games and somewhat annoying in certain other games (like Forza) where that feature wouldn't really help. It's great for shooter game though. It's an interesting effect and sets this apart from any headphone adapter I've seen for Xbox One.

The other features are fairly standard. General volume and chat volume control, and mute. There is also a feature called variable mic monitoring that adjusts to your voice level so you don't shout into the microphone.

Overall this is a great headphone adapter whether or not you use Turtle Beach headsets. I'm happy with it and am glad it works so well with my original Xbox one controller. The product is made very well and is plug and play. As long as your controller firmware is updated (USB update cable included) it will work right away.

I was excited to try the new Thrustmaster TMX Force Feedback racing wheel with my Playseat Evolution racing seat. Previously, I had an old Logitech G25 attached for use with my PS3, and sadly that wheel doesn't get much use these days. I didn't ever purchase the new Logitech G920 because of the cost, and so I was excited to try this new Thrustmaster wheel, even though it didn't have the clutch or shifter. To be honest, I prefer the paddle shifter anyway for games, and a manual with clutch in real life. It isn't really fair to compare the 2 wheels since they are different price points so I will say that the thrust master is a very nicely built wheel with good force feedback, and good button placement. I was always frustrated having to reach down to the shifter on the G25 to press the start, select and 4 PS buttons. All the buttons you need are on the Thustmaster wheel and you can get to them quickly without looking after getting used to the placement.

The steering feels good on this wheel and compared to a controller, which is what I was using for Forza 6 and Forza Horizons 2, the wheel is exponentially better. It's so much more immersive and fun, especially with the Playseat Evolution, which I've had for years and will probably see several more wheels as consoles progress. Most people will not having a racing seat, and that's fine. If you have a small table or even some types of chairs, this wheel mounts to it just fine in most cases, and you will be racing in minutes. I was able to test installing the wheel on my coffee table, and it worked well, and I was able to reach the pedals sitting on my couch.

The pedals are good quality as well. Again, not as nice as some of the higher end pedals, but they work fine and you can operate them just like a normal car, either heel-toe or left foot on the brake and right on the gas. I was happy with the brake and throttle pedals and They also mounted just fine to my old Playseat.

Overall, I do feel this wheel is slightly expensive as an XBOX accessory, and if you are really serious about driving, you may want to go with the Logitech G920 for $100 more. However, that is not to say there is anything wrong with this wheel. There is an optional shifter available and an optional 3 pedal setup, but by the time you purchase those things, you are closer to G920 territory as far as price goes. Thrustmaster also makes some fairly high end wheels, and I do believe much of that technology has been used in this less expensive but still very nice TMX wheel. I am enjoying this wheel a lot and see no reason to get anything else. It's so much better than just using the controller and I think Thrustmaster has a great product with this TMX force feedback wheel for XBOX One (and PC).

I did want to mention that my XBOX is positioned in a corner which was too far for the USB or power to reach. I was able to use a cheap USB extension and extension cord for power and it works just fine, so no worries if that is your situation as well.

I am impressed with Turtle Beach's new Stealth 350VR amplified wired headset. I am keeping the cost in mind as I review this headset. I usually play with Astro A40 and obviously they are a lot more expensive and heavier than these, but all things considered, I am impressed with the 350VR! They are marketed for PS4 and the PS VR, but they will also work on a computer, and I think it should work on an XBOX One if it has the 3.5mm input on the controller (UPDATE: Yes, this works fine on the XBOX One if you have a 3.5 port on the controller).

The headset is very lightweight, which is common for Turtle Beach headsets, and it's not a bad thing. It's nice to have a light headset on if you are playing for a long time. The headset has a built in amplifier which needs to be charged via the included micro USB cable. Just plug it into your computer or phone USB charger and it will be good to go. The headset features bass boost, volume control, a mute switch, and a noise cancelling microphone which can be unplugged if needed. The sound quality is not bad at all, and the bass is decent. The rechargeable battery lasts a long time (30 hours according to the manual) and overall I am really happy with how this headset feels and sounds.

The 350VR is so easy to hook up. There are 2 options. A cable for a PS4 that just plugs into the controller, or a super long cable for a computer that breaks out into 2 cables that plug into the microphone and speaker output jacks on your PC. Both work great and sound the same. To be honest, I wasn't expecting a headset with this many features at this price to sound very good or be comfortable. But it is! So much respect to Turtle Beach. They are putting out a quality product at a reasonable price, and I know they have even less expensive headsets than this with less features, which is great when you don't want to spend a lot of money for a headset.

I am not sure how well this headset will stand up to abuse, so treat it well. Don't leave it laying around. Hang them on your monitor or next to it when you aren't using them. It's amazing how much longer things will last when you take care of them. I like this headset, considering the features, price, feel, and sound quality of both the speakers and the microphone. It's not bad at all, especially for console gaming.

UPDATE: After playing with this for a few more days, I just want to note that the headset is fine but the bass has a little too much mid-bass. So it sounds muddy. Not a problem, I just turn the bass control almost all the way down. Another more annoying issue is the microphone cuts out once in a while. I think it's due to a very cheap cable between the headset and the controller. It's not too bad but if it gets worse, it's going to be really frustrating, especially for other players I am communicating with. I have changed the rating down to 4 stars, which is generous considering this issue. However, it generally works great and I like how lightweight it is. Easy to wear for hours at a time without any issues at all.

This PDP Legendary collection "Deliverer of Truth" XBOX One and PC controller is probably the nicest XBOX One wired controller I've used to date. It has high quality ALPS switches, the ability to assign buttons, and you can even remove the face and change the color of the controller. It has a very pleasing rubbery grip and the thumbsticks are grippy, although they don't have the same ridges that the standard XBOX One S controller has. I have a One S so I am comparing it to the new white controller.

The cable plugs in nice and secure, but is easy to remove if needed. It's fairly thick which is somewhat annoying to me, but it's 10 feet long, so you do want a thick USB cable when it's over 6 feet long so if you sit far from your console, you've got a decent amount of cable. I play in front of a monitor and my XBOX is right next to me, so I could use a much shorter cable, which is an option since it's a standard micro USB connector.

The controller has a 3.5mm headphone input and works with all standard gaming headsets I have, including the official XBOX stereo headset. You can adjust chat volume by using a setting on the controller, which is useful. The sound was good, I didn't hear much difference from the wireless controller.

The back of the controller has assignable buttons that click and roll up or down. It's useful when you want to reassign one of your top buttons to the back or if you have some other special use. I tested it out and it works great, although it's not really my playing style as a semi casual gamer. I will keep experimenting and see how it helps me. I do want to comment on the feel of the controller. It's very pleasant. The rubbery feeling feels so good to hold, better than the original XBOX controller. The buttons feel nice, not cheap at all. This is a well made controller and it has a price to match. It's not super expensive, and if you are looking for a wired controller, this is a great option. However, for ten dollars more you can get the brand new white wireless bluetooth S controller, and for the same price you can get the older XBOX One controller. Of course, it doesn't have as many features, so really it's a decision of if you want to go wired and never worry about batteries. The way I hold my controller, the wire is a little in my way, but I'm getting used to it.

I have no complaints about this controller at all. I was going to rate it 4 stars because of the price, but that's not fair. This controller feels like a premium product, and it's definitely much higher quality feeling than some other third party controllers I've tried. This one is licensed by Microsoft and feels like a first party product. Very nice. I do also want to mention that if your main reason for getting this is so you don't have to change batteries, you can plug the controller than comes with the One S into your USB port and keep playing, even with dead batteries. So that may be an option if you think you will sometimes want the wireless freedom. If you want the extra features this controller has, however, it's a great option and I've enjoyed using it on my XBOX. I also tested it briefly on my PC just on one FPS game really quick and it works fine. I don't usually use a controller for PC games but it's nice to have the option.

I have been trying to learn to play guitar (and bass) for a few years now but I can't afford lessons and I just don't have time to teach myself. I had the instruments collecting dust and when I saw this Rocksmith "game", I figured I would give it a try. I have a long way to go still, but for the first time, I feel like I'm actually "getting" it and am enjoying learning how to play, especially the bass which is simpler and something I have gotten more into. The included cable works great. You just plug it into the 1/4" jack on your instrument, and into the XBOX USB port. This game (which I call edutainment) is not like Rock Band or Guitar Hero since you are actually learning to play real rock guitar. I have learned so much in a short time and even though I not good by any means, I feel like I can plug in to my little practice amp and play songs I've learned without the game after playing on the game several times.

Regarding the technical side of things: I play XBOX One S on a low latency ViewSonic monitor with Astro A40 TR headphones (using the XBOX optical output) and it works great. I have read a couple complaints in the review, and I assure you that it's because modern TV's are doing a lot of processing to the signal that adds a significant amount latency (or delay), which can confuse you because you will play the string and it will take half a second or so to play. It does not do this on my setup which is great, and I can confirm that there is nothing wrong with the game. Most modern TV sets have a "game" mode which will provide the lowest latency setting available, and should help if that's your issue.

Rocksmith 2014 remastered is a funny name, I would have called it Rocksmith 2016, but I guess it's too close to the other version. However, it is great, and I am more than happy to give this 5 stars as it's educational, fun, and adds a whole new dimension to video games. If you don't have a guitar or bass, you can get one very inexpensively on Amazon or Monoprice. For learning, you don't need to get anything fancy. Once you get better, if you want to stick with it, you can buy a nicer instrument to keep learning. I am fairly busy with life, but I hope that with the simplicity of being able to learn on my XBOX, I will keep learning and one day be a decent amateur guitar player. Even knowing just a few rock songs is a lot of fun at this point and more than I ever could figure out before on my own.

DUKE NUKEM FOREVER is a now-infamous video game that some waited 15 years to play, and this alone is cause for many of the game's bad reviews. I, however, was only six years old when Duke Nukem 3D came out and, even though I played the game all throughout my childhood years (and still love it), I never really waited for a sequel and eventually forgot about it until a year or two ago. Then the game last year and no one seemed to like it and some of the reviews told of things that I knew I wouldn't like, and that was almost depressing.

But I got the game anyway and I do NOT regret it.

DNF lives up to my expectations as someone who has played all the Duke Nukem games and knows what it is that makes Duke DUKE. It is truly a worthy successor to DN3D: lots of action, lots of aliens, and more hilarious one-liners from Duke. The story is fun, too.

The only downsides are these:
1) No jet-pack.
2) Limited range of level exploration
3) Very limited weapons inventory*
4) It is sometime unclear what you're supposed to do.

*The weapon inventory has received a ton of criticism (you get two gun slots standard), but I think it can be defended as such: it ads a level of difficulty that gamers should appreciate (unless you just don't like a challenge). Also, you really should be playing the game on PC (it's the superior and intended version), which gives the option of holding four guns instead of two. The four-gun system works well, as it lets you have three of your favorite guns and a fourth slot for whatever special weapon the level demands, or just four guns you like best and screw the rest. I like it.

As for the packaging of the BALLS OF STEEL EDITION and the bonus materials: it's good stuff. It all seems smaller than you might expect, but the overall deal creates a sense of appreciation for the fans on the creator's behalf. You can tell they want to make up for the insane wait and they do a great job. The bust is detailed and awesome, the 100 page book is a nice companion piece to the game (and the game's unlockable bonus material), the comic book is great for a laugh, the sticker will look awesome on your laptop or pc, the paper craft is an unusual but neat addition; the cards are small but nice and the accompanying poker chips and dice are very cool.

And finally: all this for under $25. INSANE. You get a modern game with all that extra stuff for less than the price of the cheapest modern games for 360 and PS3. It really is an unbeatable deal that any fan of Duke can appreciate. I'd give it a TEN STAR rating if I could, just for all the fun and laughs I had playing this excellent game.

FINAL FANTASY is a gigantic franchise today. With over a dozen sequels (some of which have their own sub-sequels such as Final Fantasy XIII-2), it's almost impossible to believe there are people who have NEVER picked up a single game in the series.

Allow me to make a believer out of you, for I was one of those seemingly next nonexistent people.

After recently obtaining a PSP, however, I decided to look into its library and saw, to my surprise, that the original NES Final Fantasy had been updated (not for the first time, I would learn) and given an amazing price tag. Not being a fan of the franchise or RPG's in general (that's changing slowly), I considered the purchase of this game something a risk.

Sometimes risks pay off! This 20th anniversary edition of Final Fantasy is incredibly fun in all the ways a game should be. The random encounters, combat, level systems, traveling to the various kingdoms and locations, the music and graphics, all superb.

Finally, this is the perfect game for a portable device. You can work toward long-term goals if you have a few hours to spare, or you can engage in a few random encounter battles to pick up some currency during your 15-minute work break.

Overall, Final Fantasy 20th anniversary edition is fun, charming, and great for gaming on the go. You need this!

While the notion of bundling classic arcade and console games for modern platforms has proven to be a winning formula for some (Sonic's Ultimate Genesis Collection is a great example), Midway's arcade collection falls short for two reasons.

1) As someone who grew up playing games now considered classics I know the value of nostalgia and the simplicity of the games from bygone eras. After all, Super Mario Brothers is more entertaining than, say, Skyrim for some (myself included). However, I can't help feeling that most of the games featured here are likely to please only those who played them when they were new, and younger gamers who are simply obsessed with the arcade era of gaming's history. Reason 2 is why.

2) The games just aren't that good. Sure, there are some decent ones to be enjoyed, but it seems that only nostalgia could make many of them even somewhat worth your time. They look great, controls aren't an issue because they are customizable, and the variety is good, but I feel they fall short of even the standards of the time.

I really wanted to have the arcade experience in my home, and this does come close, but I found myself unable to justify the game's existence on my shelf because out of 30 games I enjoyed only one (Sinistar), and then only briefly. That said, if you were a gamer roaming from cabinet to cabinet of the arcade during your youth then odds are there is something here for you, and the bargain price makes the investment easier.

Bulletstorm, put simply, is a non-stop action-shooter that won't let up until the credits roll. Once I picked up the controller I could not put it back down. The result was a game I finished quickly but find unquestionable replayable whenever I'm in the mood for insane FPS action!

While the story is fairly generic, the voice acting and "crude" or "vulgar" dialogue (hilarious stuff, by the way) make the cut scenes a joy to witness. Characterizations are good, too, so you will care what happens to these people, you just might not be surprised.

Gameplay is king here. Nothing feels more rewarding that rushing into the next battle zone, pulling an enemy towards you in slow-mo, then using your gun or mighty boot to send the poor fellow into a bed of spikes, pitfall, or giant cactus. Combat is generally fast and fluid. You'll also be rewarded for embracing the "kill with skill" mentality. Get creative and you'll receive points that allow you to purchase weapon upgrades and ammo. You won't get bored!

Graphics are mostly good. Close-ups of characters tend to reveal some weakness (especially with hair detail and animation) but everything else looks great, especially the stunning backgrounds. During a brief moment of peace between firefights you'll eventually find yourself on a gorgeous seashore surrounded by mountains, waterfalls, and giant gears, all framed by a beautifully rendered sky and sunlight. The inclusion of such beauty amid the horrors of constant fighting is wonderfully effective.

The game gets a strong five stars for presentation, insane levels of fun, and creative use of vulgar language. However there is one MAJOR issue that comes up at the VERY end of the game.

SEMI-SPOILER ALERT!!!
The ending sequence sets up a sequel that will likely never see the light of day due to lack of sales. I understand that the folks who made the game are a smaller group with the enormously successful Epic Games, makers of the Gears of War franchise, but they should have known better than to put a cliffhanger at the end of a brand new intellectual property. As someone who absolutely adored Bulletstorm from the opening seconds, it pains me to know that there is no true closure to the events.

That said, I suggest starting a petition for a the developer (People Can Fly) to create a DLC package containing the final mission, so that everyone who loved the adventure of Grayson Hunt can finally get the closure they deserve.

SEMI-SPOILER ALERT OVER!

Conclusion: if you like over-the-top action shooters, and maybe hilariously off-color dialogue, this is a game you absolutely MUST play! Recommended for Xbox 360, but the PC version should be just as awesome if the demo is any indication. Get it now!

I played DmC before passing any of the early chapters of the four previous games in the series (if you want to know, I think 4 is the best of those games). I had some experience with the game mechanics and characters but wasn't really a big fan. Then DmC happened. To best describe the game I feel the need to be as impartial as possible, so here's a breakdown of what Ninja Theory brought to the table instead of me just gushing or bashing the game (yet):

Gameplay: First and foremost, the simplistic yet wholly satisfying hack and slash gameplay is back with a vengeance. Dante retains his classic weapons (Rebellion, Ebony & Ivory) while learning new tricks and picking up some new toys (ax, scythe, shotgun, wonderful spinny blade things). All have their own unique qualities and combos, so combat is as engaging and epic as you want it to be. In addition, Ninja Theory has expanded on the platforming concepts begun in Devil May Cry 4. Truly DmC is the next step in the series evolution in terms of gameplay.

Graphics and sound: The game simply looks fantastic. It's got a dark and brooding atmosphere punctuated by intense colors and all that lovely blood. Enemies range from cool to grotesque (many bosses are outright disgusting at times). Somewhat importantly, I feel the redesign of Dante to be quite refreshing. I like it a lot. My only gripe is that the lighting sometimes does little to flatter the characters facing, sometimes resulting in characters like Kat appearing less than presentable. This is a very minor thing. The sound design is also great.

Music: The music is somewhat controversial for some reason. I personally feel that the guitar-laden dubstep/electronic soundtrack is a perfect step up from the electronic beat-driven music of past games. It's all in the same vein and rather great for demon-slaying! Noisia knocks it out of the park.

Here are the two things that I find most appealing about this game.

1) The storytelling. The timeline of the original series is a messed up, knocked around, backwards-driving lunatic of a thing. Each sequel feels less like an expansion of the story than another reason to rehash all the cool stuff from the previous game and make a buck for Capcom. They're fun, don't misunderstand that, but DmC has the advantage of starting the story at the beginning. And Ninja Theory tells the story well. The combat and platforming are rewarded with an entertaining story is more like the Devil May Cry of old than some naysayers are willing to admit.

2) Devil May Cry has always had a focus on keeping the characters cool and the combat stylish. While DmC retains this important series staple, it becomes a broader kind of cool and no longer the Japanese vision of cool. I'm sorry if that sounds mean or ignorant. I love Japanese games and entertainment, but few other countries are so quick to imbue their lead characters with more style than substance. If you're okay with that then by all means enjoy the hell out of it. For me, I prefer my badasses with a little bit of something to relate to. DmC's Dante is a wisecracking ass-kicker you can really root for on a personal level. He's a good guy while also being cool. Ninja Theory gets 100 points from me for that alone.

In conclusion: DmC manages to reboot the franchise while evolving the gameplay and storytelling, adds in great music and sound design to sweeten the pot, and delivers an experience that surpasses ever single game to come before it in the series. If you haven't played this game because it's too different-looking, you're missing out on the best controls, the most rewarding combat, and a really good story. Replayability is high and [spoiler alert] Dante's hair turns white at the end. You can also now download a Devil May Cry 3 style skin in case you just have to have that old Dante look.

37 stars out of ten.

While clearly a departure from the stealth action that defines the Metal Gear experience, METAL GEAR RISING: REVENGEANCE retains the DNA of its predecessors and delivers an all-out action extravaganza unlike any other!

Raiden is perfectly suited to the PlatinumGames approach to the third-person action-adventure. Slicing and dicing your way through enemies is a true thrill, and an extremely graphic one at that. Combat is engaging and rewarding. Boss fights are epic and challenging (especially the final boss, as it should be).

In-game graphics are excellent. Cutscenes suffer somewhat, mostly due to the apparent desolation seen in city areas that should be more heavily populated. This is a very minor gripe, however, and most other settings look fine during the cutscenes.

In the sound department we have fairly kick-ass music and excellent voice talent. Raiden's lines are delivered convincingly, and you will believe his responses to the insanity that surrounds him in the post-Sons of the Patriots world.

Finally, the story is quite good. It takes some time to pick up, but when it does it hits close to home for our protagonist and roots itself firmly in the Metal Gear continuity with relying on knowledge of the previous games. So newcomers to the franchise need not worry!

All in all we have a very solid hack 'n slash gaming experience with memorable characters and great design choices. It is not to be missed by fans of Metal Gear Solid 2 and 4!

As for the limited edition extras, the plasma lamp is gorgeous and extremely cool. The steelbook case is well made and looks wonderful. The bonus soundtrack disc is cool to have, but somewhat lacking (I'm pretty sure a good chunk of the best in-game music is nowhere to be found on the disc). The box all of it comes in looks great on a shelf. All very good stuff sure to please the hardcore Metal Gear fan.

After being forced into a corner of mediocrity and shameless attempts and polygonal "sex appeal" the Tomb Raider franchise is finally given the chance to start anew with a fresh look at the beginnings of series protagonist Lara Croft.

To keep a long story short, this series reboot showcases Lara's transformation from an inexperienced young woman in search of adventure into a strong and unstoppable survivor. This isn't the unrealistically large-breasted Angelina Jolie look-alike who runs around in short-shorts with her belly button on display to appeal to lonely fanboys. This is Tomb Raider matured and honed to perfection. Adventure, danger, suspense, terror. And all centered around a well-rounded character (yes, Lara is finally a real character now).

Visually Tomb Raider is magnificent. Sure, there's a lot of browns and grays in many settings, but when the game opens up to the island the graphics showcase the wonderful designs crafted with such care at Crystal Dynamics.

Voice acting is great. Lara's portrayal (in both voice and motion-capture) is ahead of previous games by leaps and bounds. Sound design and music are generally excellent.

Finally, we have gameplay. Tomb Raider offers a welcome mixture of shooting, platforming, sneaking, and cinematic quick time events (QTE's). Many gamers dislike QTE's, and I understand why, but I personally welcome them when they are placed sensibly within the game. Tomb Raider gets it right, using these events to keep you on the edge of your seat. One wrong move and Lara dies, sometimes rather graphically.

On the whole developer Crystal Dynamics and publisher Square Enix have crafted a gem of a game that can be enjoyed by a new generation as well as series veterans. Tomb Raider is a force to be reckoned with once again, and I pity the next big action-adventure game that tries to do better.

While I am not a long-time fan of the Silent Hill series, I did play Silent Hill 2 and 3 (generally considered the best two of the franchise) before playing Downpour. I tell you this to let you know I'm neither overburdened by nostalgia nor completely ignorant to what makes the franchise great.

With that out of the way I can get to the point. Silent Hill: Downpour is a solid exercise in psychological terror and suspense for the current generation of consoles. It retains the classic Silent Hill atmosphere while making important advances in mechanics, mechanics, and overall presentation. On paper it should please fans old and new. That hasn't always been the case, but that is to be expected of gamers these days. Some appreciate deviation form the formula while some honestly prefer to have more of the same thing year after year.

Imagine the things you like about Silent Hill 2 or 3. Now imagine those things with current-gen graphics and subtract the nurses and Pyramid Head. There you go.

Consistencies include lots of fog, exploration, cryptic puzzles, monsters who want you dead, and the usual everyman protagonist. Changes and additions include a new score composer, relative realism with the fog, a couple of moral choices, and a relatively comprehensible plot.

General Pros: best graphics in the series; wonderfully foreboding atmosphere; pleasant degree of challenge; solid controls; terror,

General Cons: occasional horrific frame rate drop (for a lot of people, anyway); navigating the town is often confusing (keep a keen eye out for secret ladders or holes in the wall); not enough Korn music.

It isn't a perfect game, but I don't think any one Silent Hill is perfect either. It's fun, scary, and you'll want to replay for the multiple endings (tip: thanks to a last-minute checkpoint you can make an important decision differently and see most of the endings with only two play-throughs. Just hit continue after the credits and do something differently!)

In conclusion, enjoy this game for what it is, not for what others say it should be.
Still going strong after 4 months of heavy use. Holds a great charge and charges very quickly.
Love thes controllers. Worried about the transition from 360 to one but these were a great feel and has been working strong for the 4 months of heavy use.

My rating is solely on the Xbox One and not Xbox Live. Great console and lots of fun. Use ot heavily and have not had any issues with it. Xbox live however is horrible. Very bad connections with game servers.l but for the m9st part enjoyable,.
Very fun Mech shoot 'em up game. Being able to FPS with my character along with a Mech was a great switch for an FPS game.
Very fun game based off a great series! Hiurs of fun for my family

I decided to give this game another try. I have had it for 3 or 4 months now and played it one night then packed it back away in its case. The multiplayer was horrible and buggy. The one thing that never lets you down in any Halo game is it's story so that was the one positive.

Back to my second chance for Halo MCC. 343 has done so much work on this game to fix it that it shoukd have never been released in the first place with all the bugs. Multiplayer is finally better. Not perfect but much more bearable. I didn't experience much lag, however I do have a 100mbps connection. I finally enjoyed myself for the first time since Halo 4. There are still improvements that need to be worked on like the match making speeds and map loading. But all in all this is finally starting to look up from when I originally purchased this. Too bad they finally fixed it right before Halo 5 comes out. I look forward to that but hopefully 343 won't make me look like a fool a second time...

The xbox worked fine. This is a tough review to write due to so many complaints I have woth Microsoft and their software along with ethernet speed issues. If you are experiencing slow speeds then do a hard reset on the xbox and magically the speeds are bacl to where they should be. Pretty bad flaw on the design. Being able to play Halo though is kind of a big deal for me. One of the main reasons I picked this console up.

Controller works most of the time. Occassionally I have issues with the rechargable oem batteries where it randomly disconnects the controller. Once I pulled the battery and turn the controller back on its good to go. Another flaw in Microsofts product.

This game returns to the fun of Just Cause 2 after the disappointing Just Cause 3. Oddly, I realized after we'd exhausted all the game play, that we were still playing it night after night, just to listen to the music, I still feel like playing it for that reason alone. When you install this game, don't even bother to start it until you've done the updates. The initial copy has a ridiculous motion blur that makes it unplayable. I don't know what they were thinking pressing the discs that way, it was absolutely hideous and we thought this was another game to just put on the shelf. That was all corrected with the updates. I can't say it was quite as good as Just Cause 2, because of their decisions in how the collectables were exposed. With 2, you had the knowledge of where the stuff was and such a large number of collectables, that the game went on and on with incentive. This had less of an incentive because it required more aimless wandering, which isn't a fun way to spend an evening. Also didn't like the way you take over an outpost, but then it all respawns. One would never call Just Cause immersive, because it just crazy fun, but the respawning of stuff in captured outposts to destroy all over, is stretching the little immersion that the game concept does have. But the graphics are good enough, mechanics great, story interesting enough (in a Just Cause way), and music fantastic. We got a few weeks of nightly fun out of this one. Definitely a step up from Just Cause 3. I'm still wanting to go back and do another playthrough just to hear some of the haunting Cuban melodies.

The last Metro game I played was 2033. This one is a step forward in the same vein. Graphics are excellent, weapons offer very nice choices and customization, story is gritty and painful, what's not to like. I observed rather than play, and let my son drive other than the exploration process. This game is as bad as Far Cry 2 as far as having lots of controls sometimes with dual purpose. It's the price for having so many mechanics bent on realism. I might like that on a keyboard and mouse setup, but it's tedious on a controller. The only negatives I could see were the gas mask mechanic, and mutated creatures (just a personal distaste I have for fighting unrealistic creatures vs humans). It really delivers on the realistic depressing nature that 2033 had, these guys are real artists at creating a dark immersion. The pickups remind you of Fallout or Far Cry, and are enough incentive to search the entire map (though inventory space restrictions are irritating). The limited palette of base weapons is made up for by the ability to customize them and feels quite realistic in the environment. The characters are developed well and you get to know them. The dialog is the most extensive I've seen and well tailored the events the NPCs are experiencing at the time. We stop upon meeting a new character and wait out all their dialog, since there is so much. Had a couple of crashes in 10 nights of play, but the recovery was with no loss. The game is not a multiple playthrough game for us, but totally worth the price for the long and emotionally rich single playthrough it provides.

A note to those who are purists in art and texturing. We found only a single texturing issue in the game. That's pretty darned good. The views from the train are spectacular. They've managed to give you a feeling of little repetition in miles of traveling.

We only buy games for offline play because we are rural and have only satellite (can't play any real game that is tied to the net). This game delivers great couch coop bot play (though they made the mistake many COD games have and limited the bot count to 6, dumb). We were playing COD WWII just prior and while it has better maps, the unique weapons and capabilities of this were great. We don't have a second PS4 but it almost looks like another great tradition was maintained by this COD developer, LAN play. With so many game companies switching to money-grabbing micro trans online only modes, it is refreshing to buy a game we can actually have some fun with, not having a decent network connection. Bravo to Infinity Ward, keeping couch gaming at home alive! Buy it if you are an offline player and send a message to these blasted game companies that not everyone can play online, and those of us who can't just stop buying consoles if they don't produce products for offline.

First off, this game comes out of the box head and shoulders above every triple A game on the market quite simply because it honors couch coop. There is no other game produced by top companies that you can enjoy an evening with your friends, something I consider one of the most important facets of gaming. I would rate it 5 star just for that reason.

But more to the subject matter. It seems they have honed mechanics started in BL3 while dramatically improving on them. BL3 was fun, this is way better. The guns really work well, and while we only had the Siren in BL3, every character can have that experience. And OMG, you can hybrid the classes, how cool is that. Sword play is surprisingly fun and I find melee way more interesting than in past games, or other sword based games in the past. Let me caveat the next statement by first saying that I think they did everything right and with two exceptions, and they are not that big a deal. One is that they still made questionable choices on HUD arrangement for splitscreen, it could be better, the second is the music is less well done when comparing it to targeted themes like Eden 6 or Sanctuary in BL3. The music is generally very forgettable, with a couple of nice exceptions.

We haven't finished it yet but it is looking like a surprisingly long game for how quickly it came out after BL3. The content is also well written and follows the intriguing theme concerning Tina's emotional state where the BL3 DLC left off. That surprised me as I assumed they wouldn't have the interest in turning that depth into a thing (BL and depth have usually been mutually exclusive). That allowed them to create a bizarre fantasy that is still funny and Borderlands insane, yet with an undercurrent you can't forget, that the characters have some issues of a serious nature. I also was certain I'd hate having to acclimate to new lead characters that don't fit the BL formula, but surprisingly, after one evening, I found the new faces easy to accept, they are still the egotistical cocky types we expect from BL personalities, but these have an interesting twist in that their fallibility shows through. I don't recall that often with other BL lead roles.

The overall is that it's fun. I get sick of the "enemy around every corner" game, but the mechanics of combat are so good and varietal, that I don't get that feeling out of this. The HUD issues darken this slightly because I find myself not bothering to check if the drops are much better than what I'm using, it's just too difficult to tell what is good and what isn't (I find myself selling everything without even looking at it closely). This is offset a little by the fact that once you find a good sword, shield, spell or gun, unlike other games that graduate the weaponry, you can make them work even when you'd expect they were way too low a level. It makes it less important to find the absolute top gear in the drops you find. This is somewhat liberating since on other BL games, we would stand around forever comparing everything, testing etc. It makes this feel more like continuous action even if it is just they way we are playing it.

Reliability appears to be better than most other games. Two hangs in 7 days of playing a non-updated game, one we lost nothing (save system is more timely it seems, a sword picked up a couple of seconds before the hang was still there) and the other hang corrupted one of our characters, only instead of that being the disaster I remember in BL2 (or maybe it was BL1), it came up and rebuilt the corrupted character with seemingly no loss. We were pleasantly shocked.

If you like the BL series at all, if you enjoy couch coop, this is probably the best game you'll find on the market.

First, we played this on the PS5 even though it says PS4.

It has basics that are close to perfect:
1. Plays offline with no irritating necessity of connecting to the net, didn't even need an upgrade to play
2. Graphics are excellent, nothing to jar the immersion, some methods seem ahead of games being released now.
3. Mechanics are great, even if there are differences in controls from what we think of as shooter controls
4. Performance can't be faulted
5. Save frequency is acceptable

There are occasional glitches which I attribute to playing on the PS5 when it was supposed to be on the PS4. These are small, a character might disappear then reappear. Occasionally a mission might glitch where you walk up to the quest giver and they talk with no audio. These happened no more than twice each.

The length of the game is quite amazing. It is a story that is done so well, you are mesmerized for the entire playthrough (took my son and I about 3 weeks to not quite 100% it). As a prequel to Red Dead Redemption 1, it is unparalleled. The story weaves the two games together and you simply have to go back and play the original game again to see how much of that game was missed (story wise) without the RDR 2 information. So this game, while being the most epic game I've seen causes an even greater epic experience by revitalizing the story of RDR 1. In general though, the story is magnificent and my respect for this company could not be higher.

I waited so long to buy this because I detest games that force you to be the bad guy. All I can say is that you aren't in some ways, or actually, you have the choices to make the main characters better and you end up understanding exactly how they ended up being bad. There is no bravado that would enshrine the violence your character does, instead, it leaves aware that he doesn't want to be, but life circumstances forced him into (like really happens). Justice is done in the way they did the story. This left me able to play the game even if I hated the choices the player character has to make to further the story. But you also end up pleased of the choices you can make to try and make him more a decent person. Just have to play it to see what I mean.

I'd give this game and rockstar 10 stars if I could. If only other game companies would get off the net and start producing real story based games again, I'd have other games that might compete with this one. Right now, it's in a class by itself.

This series is such a mixed bag.

Brief Summary: if you like games solely for the sense of triumph in fighting preparation and difficulty (whether that is how hard a boss is, the grinding required to take on a boss, or prowess to work around mechanics), these three are for you. If you like games for how immersed you become, good music, consistent graphics, and compelling story, it is probably not for you.

I wanted to love this game because the company supports an off-line gaming experience and that is refreshing, and the only thing my son and I are into. Additionally, the Demon Souls remaster was a great game, even if only a mildly interesting story evolved in playing it. We were eager to get these, hoping for more of the same.

The graphics on Dark Souls 1 are so bad that in some levels, I couldn't look at it. The underground areas were painful to my eyes with what I consider very bad lighting and texture decisions. The graphics improved greatly in the next two. By 3, they were excellent.

Story was non-existent. The title tells the story, it's about capturing souls. Beyond that, no real development came about and that seemed to be the only common thread between the three. Seems that the company must have felt cut scenes or much back story would turn off their intended audience? My expectation was an epic where one would pick up where the other left off. That didn't happen, at all. That lack of story makes it really a series for individuals wanting intense physical entertainment and twitch challenge, but not for people also looking for mental or philosophical entertainment. There was the promise of a story at the beginning of 2, but it was dropped.

They did a good job on grinding mechanics for the most part. You could proactively improve your fighting ability to boost your capability to take on the bosses. This was unfortunately lost in the development of 3. It presented bosses immediately that you weren't ready to take on. Analogy: opening cut scene ends, player spawns with pathetic pistol, kills 3 NPCs, tank spawns. This is the concept (no, there is no pistol or tank, it's an analogy) of how 3 starts without spoilers. Most bizarre level development choice we'd ever seen. Fortunately that only happens a few times because you can grind and ready your character most of the time. 3 was the only one suffering from this flaw in the series. The rest let you develop your fighting skill very nicely.

These games are brutally challenging. My son enjoyed the challenge, I found it to be as frustrating as Spelunker and soon passed my turns on the controller. He noted that in all three games, the combination of some clunky mechanics on intentionally hard bosses, spoiled what would be extremely fun for those interested in twitch. I did note that it's the sort of game you can take on a hard boss and figure out their moves, after a few deaths, defeat them slowly by learning to respond correctly. For me, even though it can be interesting to do that, games like that lose immersion and it starts to matter less because even though you beat the boss, you've gotten out of character through repeated death and respawn screens.

I have to state that we didn't finish any of the games. This is odd, given that in hundreds of games played, he had only quit one game as unplayable (I think it might have been Big Rigs), and I'd only quit spelunker in the 80s. Had there been the slightest carrot of a developed story and some way to relate to the player character, we probably would not have bagged it. The clunkiness is what stopped him as he was enjoying the challenge, but we finally called it when controller response was different under different circumstances and left him feeling he was fighting the game rather than the boss. As an example, we see this often where colliders are misplaced and causing you to shoot and hit an invisible wall. That is "fighting the game" rather than the enemy. I guess that means no matter how much you play for twitch, at least a shred of immersion has to remain to focus you on the battle and not a mistake a developer made. My sons comments were that 2 became an un-fun slog and 3 fights had no ramp-up in difficulty, but it was instantly as hard as possible, there was no easing into the difficulty as one expects. Our patience with the games had already been too stretched to bother continuing. We had several excellent titles waiting we had never played. It was a relief to pop out the disk.

In all fairness, we played all three on the PS5 and they were not intended for that console. That can easily create fighting mechanics that act seemingly unpredictable. Had we put it in the PS4, possibly the review would be a 4 or 5 for him. Graphics (just DS1) and no story would still drop it down to 1 or 2 for me.

This is one of the harshest reviews I've written and it's possibly that I'm not being fair. We played this series sandwiched between LA Noire and RDR2, both of which are outstanding immersive story games, lavish in their character development. To go back to a dressed up arcade-style game (a game where the entire conscious intent is to conquer a game level) from those is obviously going to point out the difference between being emotionally involved in a game, versus an eye-hand coordination exercise. As I've implied though, for the hardcore twitcher who cares only for proving prowess in conquering difficult animated 3d models, this game's as close to a 5 star you will find... a must have. I have to note though that from the same company, Demon Souls had graphics, a good story hidden in the action, and very close in mechanics/difficulty. If only these would have had same design constraints that Demon Souls had.

The storytelling involved in this game is right up there with RDR2. The subject matter is of course disgusting, but not at all unlike real life for the type characters it targets. This game gives a realistic view of the criminally insane and people just railroaded by life into crime. Some serious thought obviously went into it. As expected with Rockstar games, no moronic faction in our society is safe from their satire, which comes across as humorous wisdom, that is to say, very good and intelligent writing that doles out mockery where mockery is due. It gets pretty wonderfully farcical at times.

I resisted buying it because I assumed it was to morally disgusting to play. But what I found is, it's no different than the realistic dramas that great screenplay writers bring to the screen. It does allow you to try and force your character to be a little bit more moral if you like, though you do have to do some missions that you might not agree with. But what they've done to counteract that, is that the bad things you do, are basically against bad people. So the moral delimma is a little softened, though not completely eliminated.

The mechanics and graphics are superb, no surprise, it's from Rockstar and they seem to get how to do games at a time when most companies are dumping swill out to capture micro-transactions and saleable personal data online. If only they could build games like they do and do couch coop, they would have everything.

Story length is very long, probably only beat out by their own RDR2 and the excellent Witcher III. If you 100% games, this will keep you engaged for a long time.

We ran it on the PS-5 and there were very few glitches. A few restarts without loss of progress. I consider that excellent.

I've assumed that 343 was not capable of producing a game that furthers the Halo series, yet alone beats the other outstanding game companies. I have been wrong. After Halo 4 and 5, I had no hopes of this being exceptional. It is exceptional, and not just as a follow-on to the Halo, it's also an exceptional game. The mechanics are probably the best I've played. Every weapon is fun to use, the AIs are fun to use in patterning your missions to see how they will do, and they actually do something useful. The open world aspects are great yet uphold the linear feel of good old Halo 3 or Reach.

The modeling, and ideas for modeling, were spot on. The Covenant are back as they should be and the vast majority of the game has them as your enemy. It feels like Halo. Real grunts, jackals, skirmishers, and elites plus brutes that are fun as they were in Halo 3.

One nice surprise is that the music is actually better while still maintaining the stirring qualities of the original Halo themes.

The one thing that 343 did right in the other two post bungie games was the story, and this exceeds their efforts thus far. Indeed, it exceeds so many other games in story quality. There are lines that are predictable of course, 117 has to give the expected "make my day" sort of lines at times, but in general it is not at all trite. It even brings out John's personality a little, something most have shied away from since a Spartan is supposed to be a machine.

It has couch coop for the multiplayer and it's good, if only it had it for the campaign, but we are hoping they will bring that out in an update because quite frankly, both my son and I agree that if that were present, this might topple every other game we've played as the best game ever made. Our massive library goes all the way back to the PS-2, and occupies an entire wall shelf, so that is saying a lot.

The only balancing flaw we found was in the Hunters. It was clear how to become an expert on this enemy class before. Not so clear in this game and frankly feels like luck when they finally die. Killing a hunter is more of a repetitive bludgeoning affair now rather than the rewarding precision operation it's always been in the past. They are less satisfying as a result.

This game can feel like Far Cry 5, Crackdown, Mercenaries, Just Cause, Fallout, and CoD while still being totally Halo, indeed, the most Halo in the series it would seem. It is like finally a game company hooked up to figuring out all the mechanics that make game play a blast, and just flat out included them all in a quite seamless integrated manner.

We've had a run of really fantastic games, GTA 5, The Witcher, and RDR2, yet this game stands out in a field of what we consider the best games. Had they just included couch coop for campaign, it would be absolutely perfect.

It isn't easy to install. Took us two days, having to install mostly useless to us multiplayer features that almost wiped our bandwidth cap for the month. Rather than pan it for that, I'll say it was worth it. Something I never thought I would say. We have an XBox One so that may be part of the problem. We'll decidedly pick up a newer console anticipating that Halo 6, because if it includes the mechanics and depth of this game, it's totally worth it.

At the time this game originally released I was a young teenager. I was hungry for videogames and had all the time in the world. At this time, I played and beat The Legend of Dragoon. I loved it. Since those days I've often thought fondly of this game. Now in recent days, I've completed the game for a second time, putting in nearly 50 hours. What I've realized is that this game belongs in the past and I want to warn anyone considering picking up this game. If this game is ever remade I'll be in line for it. Until then I suggest we leave it in the past.

Story 9/10
The greatness of the story is timeless. Truly someone took put a lot of effort into writing this story. There are a lot of great twist and the character development is wonderful. You'll start to connect the with characters in no time.

Visuals 4/10
For the time these visuals were top notch. By today's standards these graphics are lacking. This is to be expected.

Sound 4/10
The soundtrack is perfect. I could listen to the menu them all day. The music in this game blows me away every time I listen to it. I didn't really notice anything wrong with the sound effects. The voice acting in this game is really bad and often goofy. Not to mention occasionally during cut scenes I couldn't make out what the characters were saying. There are no subtitles available during some scenes. Very disappointing.

Mechanics/Gameplay 2/10
Normal movement in the game is occasionally hinder by invisible catches which is slightly annoying. The battle system is somewhat lacking and get old really fast. You are required to do timed button pushes for your normal attacks. It's fun for a few minutes but not 50 hours. My biggest complaint is that you cannot skip certain battle scenes. Every time you cast your dragoon magic you have to watch a short scene. I'm pretty sure I could have cut my playtime down by a FEW HOURS if I didn't have to watch these things every time. The final boss also has a lot of scenes. Heaven forbid that you should die halfway through that fight.

Basically my play through this game as an adult netted me nothing but some nostalgic enjoyment and watching a great story unfold again. The gameplay itself was little to no fun. Almost like a chore. So now I warn you, leave this in the past.

Hori always produces screen protectors that are of the utmost quality. The 3DS XL iteration is no different. Hori continues to innovate in the application of the screen protector and this one seems almost perfect.

I always order the protectors when I order the equipment, in this case 3DS XL. Application is greatly simplified when there has not been any opportunity for dust, fingerprints or other particulates to settle on the screens. If this is the case, you can simply take the 3DS and the protectors out of their packaging and begin the application process. Otherwise, a good wipe down with the included screen cloth is in order. To get any stubborn prints or particles off the screen, lightly dab with scotch tape.

The top (3D) screen protector can be applied neatly and quite easily. Hori has perfected this application. Simply lay out the protector, remove the tabs in the order indicated, being careful to smooth air bubbles out and you're done. This was the easiest screen protector I have ever applied to any screen on any device...ever. Very well implemented.

The touch screen is where things get hairy. The application tabs do not work nearly as well on this protector. The first time I applied it did not separate from the plastic sheeting correctly and I was stuck applying it by hand. I suspect this will happen to others, so here are tips that may help:

-Pick a corner and only handle it there.
-Place one of the plastic sheets in corner of the touchscreen that will be the end-point of application. This way, if the protector is accidentally dropped, you can easily pick it back up.
-If fingerprints or dust get on the screen protector, remove them by lightly dabbing with scotch tape. The cloth will make it worse.
-Start at one corner and work diagonally.
-Work air bubbles up or down depending on proximity to middle of the screen.

All in all these protectors are the best you can get and Hori does a fantastic job of making application easier on the consumer. However, I've used Hori products for years and nothing about this iteration makes me think it warrants an outstanding (5 star) review.
I've had issues with touchscreen application on each DS I've applied a Hori protector to. (2 DS, DS Lite, DSi, DSi XL, 3DS, and now 3DS XL) They've been in the game a long time and it could have been better by now.

Nintendo has a habit of releasing their beloved franchises in collection-style formats. Super Mario Allstars, The Legend of Zelda: Collector's Edition, Mario 25th Anniversary, etc. The list goes on. The one thing that all of these have in common is that none of them have even been fully inclusive of a franchise (which admittedly this collection still is not) but also none have been inclusive of so many previous mediums. In Kirby's Dream Collection you get exactly that. A dream collection of NES, Gameboy, SNES and Nintendo64 titles.
Included games are:
Kirby's Dream Land (Gameboy)
Kirby's Adventure (NES)
Kirby's Dream Land 2 (Gameboy)
Kirby Super Star (SNES)
Kirby's Dream Land 3 (SNES)
Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards (N64)

There are also bonus items including a CD, booklet and challenge stages.

The Nintendo64 and SNES games are worth the price of admission on their own. Whether you have played all of these or none of them, Each game is a blast. I highly suggest considering this title for gamers of all ages. Anyone on the fence should hesitate no longer. You will not regret this purchase!

Skylanders Giants brings familiar faces to an all new adventure. All of your Skylanders you have allied with in Spyros Adventure may be brought forth into this world. As an added bonus, Giants allows for all Skylanders to level up even higher!

The adventure itself is a new story with much of the same cast from the first story. RPG elements seem to be instilled with a heavier hand this time around which is a welcome development to me. The most changed is the 3DS version which now incorporates elements of the console game, such as similar characters and destinations but remains a platform-centric title.

As for what is physically presented in the package:
Skylanders Giants Game
Portal of Power
Poster of Skylanders in the GIANTS series
Cards, stickers, online codes for included Skylanders
All versions:
Tree Rex GIANT - like all giants, he is slow and lumbering but very powerful. Smaller baddies, crates, chests, etc can be run over and destroyed without even deploying an attack. As for giants, I personally rank Tree Rex 4/5 and just under Crusher in effectiveness out of the gate.Pairs well with a fast Skylander and/or angood jumper (3DS) like Pop Fizz or Lightening Rod.

Cynder- 2nd series version of this Skylander. One of my personally preferred characters from Spyro's Adventure. New power adds some versatility to the mix, but if you knew Cynder before, you'll know Cynder series 2.

Console versions:
Jet Vac- So far, my opinion of Jet Vac is that it is the weakest of the new batch. He is a great looking and fun to play but does not pack a big wallup. some may love him. To each their own.

3DS:
Punch Pop Fizz- alternate version of Pop Fizz. Alternate color Shows in game. Pop Fizz is a fun little guy. He is underpowered at low levels, but his powers are so much fun that I just don't care. He is speedy, jumps well and is a nice compliment to the super powered Giants.

Overall either package sets you up nicely for a good time with GIANTS. Those who took the adventure the first time through will have the luxury of playing all of their Series 1 Skylanders available in the GIANTS game at their current level. If you enjoyed Spyro's Adventure, GIANTS gives you more of everything to enjoy.

He does tend to have a slight pause between attacks which leaves him vulnerable after a combo. On 3DS he is moderate jumper.

From a toy/collectible perspective, this is one of my personal favorites. Fright Rider has a neat name, unique design and is well painted and posed.

The gameplay is fun, but very repetitive. Cavia (the developers of this game) produced Drakengard and Drakengard 2 (and this game is actually based on one of the endings of Drakengard, though you don't need to play Drakengard to enjoy this game). If you've played either of those games, you will know what you are getting yourself into, as far as gameplay goes. It's a little different, but not all that much. Swords and Spells. No dragon riding this time, however.

I've heard people complain about the controls in this game. I can honestly say, I don't know what they are talking about. The controls handled just fine for me, though I will openly admit that there were a few moments throughout the game when the camera was an enemy. It's mostly ok, but there are a handful of moments where you honestly don't know if you are going to live or die, because you can't see.

And that's why I struggle. The story and music are absolutely amazing, and if you are looking for a good story, look absolutely no further. But the combat, while fun for me, is admittedly repetitive. Rolling, blocking, sword swinging, and spell casting ad nauseum.
If you are just looking for a fun hack and slash, this game would get around 3-4 stars. But if you're into story and audio, giving it a 5 out of 5 is slandering it.

As a personal aside, for the past 20-ish years, Secret of Mana on the SNES has held the title of "My favorite game ever." It's finally been replaced by this game. The story is THAT good.

For that reason, I can't recommend this game, because Capcom holds the ending hostage, demanding an additional 10 dollars for a 20 dollar game.

I have to be honest. I don't like this game. They made a LOT of technical improvements over the previous title. The combat is better. The music is more generic, but in a series that requires this much grinding, I'm not complaining about that (the chaotic discord of the original Drakengard's soundtrack really gets on your nerves after a while). The camera is MUCH better than its predecessor. It's set in the same world as Drakengard, and I give Drakengard 4 stars, so one would wonder why I would rate this so much lower, with all the improvements.

The answer is the linchpin of what made Drakengard so beloved by me: The story. If you have played the original, and happen to remember the story, give this game a wide berth.

In Drakengard 1, we get Caim, who is silent and not as heroic as we initially believe. Indeed, almost all characters in Drakengard 1 had several layers to them, that you had to dig to reveal. Do not expect the same type of characters in Drakengard 2. You get Nowe, who is the typical anime protaganist (which does NOT fit in Drakengards world). You have his childhood lady friend, who wants him. You have Manah, who was a little girl in the first game. Nowe wants her. You also have Urick, a dude who has a pact with the Grim Reaper. There is almost no depth to any of them, but if utilized properly, this could work out alright. Not great, but decently.

And then Drakengard 2 has the player systematically do things that anyone who played Drakengard 1 would be screaming at the cast to not do. I won't go into spoilers, But if you played Drakengard 1, the entire game will be you saying to yourself, "This is stupid. I know what's coming. Why would they do this? Why does nobody try to explain the consequences of their actions?"

Then, when said consequences come to pass, the game splits off into 3 different endings, depending on what level you are playing the game on. Everyone starts the game on normal, then moves onto Hard, and finally Extreme. That means, in order to get all the endings, you don't just go down alternate paths like you did in Drakengard 1. You have to play the entire game 3 full times. In Extreme difficulty, the first enemy in the tutorial will kill you in two hits. Some of these levels are around an hour long, and are filled with thousands of enemies.

But I beat it all 3 times. Minus the last hour of each 40+hour playthrough, there is perhaps 10 minutes of new dialoge per run (and I'm being VERY liberal in my estimate, there). As the title suggests, this game will most likely sell thanks to its namesake and all the fond memories that go along with it. Is that a bad thing, not really but is the trip down memory lane worth the cost of the full price of admission or should you wait and purchase your ticket when the prices come down? The answer is, it's best to wait honestly besides the history there's no real reason to pick this title up for full price.

If you're a big fan of the series (which I am and the main reason I picked it up) or have someone on your holiday shopping list that is then take the chance. The nostalgia alone may make for an enjoyable gaming experience. However anyone with no exposure to the franchise and/or grew up with the belief that videogames started with the PS3/Xbox 360 then you should probably stay away. Honestly there is nothing new or mind blowing here, just a game that's better suited for the PS2.

The cons:
1. The camera is horrible at best; it would have been so much better if it was fixed. The majority of the time you're fighting with the camera at the same time you're fighting with the enemies on the screen which doesn't make for a fun experience.
2. Speaking of the enemies, most of them are very easy and the few who aren't don't really take too long to figure out before you're able to make it through them.
3. The controls are very sensitive, push on the stick that controls the camera a little too hard and you could find yourself suffering from vertigo.
4. The environments are interesting at first but get stale quickly, visually nothing stunning or breathtaking, let's just say you won't find any of the scenery on the back of a postcard anytime soon.
5. The character designs seems as if they would be more at home on a last gen system, nothing really next gen here either.
6. Multiplayer is fun, but again will get old really quick. After a couple of matches I felt as if I experienced all there was to experience and didn't really feel compelled to go back to the grid (multiplayer).

The pros:
1. The history.
2. For being a game based on an 80's sci-fi movie the story isn't too bad, actually pretty entertaining.
3. The music.
4. Um.........I guess that's really all the pros.

Overall if you're a fan of Tron pick it up when it goes down in price by at least half, if you're not a fan wait until someone gives it to you as a gift.

First things first, before the Xbox fanboy association jumps on me for my review, let me explain why I rated the Kinect as I did. By no means am I saying it isn't fun or even that it's not as or even more enjoyable then what's already being offered on the market.

In my opinion it's really nothing new. I feel like the novelty of motion controlled gaming has worn off. I know the presentation of the Kinect is different and unique in it's own way, I am however not talking about how they accomplish it, but more so the end result, which is gaming by motion.

My review is from a current Wii owner and from someone who prefers the traditional sit and play style, so keep that in mind while reading this and before making your decision whether to purchase it or not.

I own all three next gen systems and honestly spend all my time on the Xbox 360 and the PS3, with the Wii only being dusted off for get togethers with a party themed atmosphere. The argument about the Kinect being for a more mature audience doesn't really hold true either, at least not right at the moment. What I mean by this is the game library for the Kinect is very family oriented, just as it is for the Wii. This may change in the future but as of right now it is.

The Wii and the Kinect both offer great gaming experiences and truthfully there's nothing funnier than watching someone try to play them, however in my opinion one system is enough. If you don't own a Wii and you're interested in finding out what all the hype is about surrounding motion controlled gaming then pick it up, however if you already own a Wii/PS3 Move and like many other people it has just become a paperweight, then you may want to wait for either that must have game or a price drop.

Kinect is a lot of fun but is it worth full price, for the reasons I stated above, the answer would have to be no. If you're new to motion controlled gaming then I guess it boils down to which one (Kinect, Move or Wii) offers the most bang for your buck. Do your homework before you purchase any one of the three, they're all big investments.

If you're like me and most of your gaming time is when you're alone, then you may want to forego all three and just play them at a friend's house. I haven't played the Move but I can tell you from experience that the Wii and Kinect lose some of their appeal when played alone, at least for someone who is allowed to see R rated movies.

Thanks for reading,

The focus group for this review consisted of two thirty something year old adults, both male and female and two children, one nine and the other seven. Obviously there was no real focus group for this review, the only reason I tell you the genders and ages, is to show how this game appealed to everyone who played it in my household, just in case you're on the fence about picking this game up for yourself or someone else.

While I was itching to play something new, and normally spending most of my time by the PS3 and Xbox 360 games I decided this time to check out what the Wii had to offer, mainly because I have everything I wanted for the other two systems. I also knew that purchasing a Wii game meant I had to dust off the console and possibly even buy new batteries for the remotes, but when you're looking for a videogame fix you sometimes have to make sacrifices!

I don't know if anyone else has ever realized this, but the display case that holds the Wii games in the store always looks so bright and colorful, whereas the PS3 and Xbox 360 cases always seem so drab! I know that's to appeal more to their core demographic but I just found it funny and never really noticed it until yesterday. While looking at this wall of color and scrolling through game titles that seem as if Doctor Seuss came up with the titles, I came across Donkey Kong Country Returns. At first I was a little skeptic but then remembered that for the most part Nintendo's first party titles are normally pretty enjoyable, so I took a chance. When all was said and done I'm glad I did, because for the reasons listed below this game was worth the price of admission.

I myself am an old school gamer, grew up with the Atari and NES and just like most people my gaming habits evolved over the years with technology. Most of the games I play nowadays require a ten to fifteen minute tutorial alone on just how to use the controller, before you even get to the actual game play. Games today have these long cinematic cut scenes to help with story telling and to visually blow you away. This game however was not like that at all, once you hit start you're off and running and enjoying yourself. I am by no means hating on the games of today, but sometimes it is nice to get back to basics every now and then.

This game is an old school style 2D sidescroller for the most part with a few twists added to keep things interesting and current. The controls are simple and very responsive, everyone was able to pick up the remote and get right into the game without any complications. The graphics are amazing; of course by Wii standards that is, you wouldn't mistake this game for Uncharted 2. Of course the story is out there and crazy, but would you really expect anything else playing a game like this and if you do you may want to reevaluate yourself all together. The closest game I can think to compare this to would probably be Mario World for the SNES.

Nothing really mind blowing here just a lot of careless hours of enjoyment and some good old fashioned game play. Sometimes it's really nice to just sit back and enjoy a game and not get all worked up because someone killed you or because you lost a match of team deathmatch because everyone on your team suck besides you of course! So to sum things up, unless your part of a certain systems fanboy association or part of a rare household that doesn't own a Wii do yourself a favor and pick this game up, you'll enjoy it. If you feel as if you're too mature to play a game like this, do yourself a favor and bend over and take the stick out of your bottom, there's nothing wrong with allowing your inner child to come out and play, especially in an ever so serious world filled with so much doom and gloom.

Well I'm done running off at the mouth, I know a little too late but I'm done. I'm going back to playing Donkey Kong Country Returns.

Happy gaming everyone!
