I have been around the block and remember the DIY mod kits for PS3

Not gonna sit here and blow smoke up rear about how i would never use in game or that youre a cheater and a bad person if you do.

The fact is so many people, imo, use devices like this that you would almost be a fool not to use it.
I know the tell tail signs when people are using modded controllers, some streamers/youtubers are more obvious than others.

The days where modded controllers were considered taboo are long gone.
You can thank Scuf.
You can also thank them for ripping off naive gamers for years.
I find it hypocritical how Scuf get embraced by the sheeple but you frown on this?

The reality is Scuf has been getting away with overcharging in a market they have full dominance over, you should be happy these guys chose to stick their middle finger up at them by giving us an affordable solution.

You can make your own mod for under 20 bucks (with leds)

The reality is the whole competitive gaming world is using anything to get an advantage, that has been the case since the dawn of gaming, more people use Scuf / modded controllers than you might think.

I myself am not competitive enough to care BUT was very curious as to functionality Also i have to admit i have gotten a kick out of testing these against try hards.
These do work in WW2/Destiny 2
But to certain degree of "success"

Certain things like Jitter do not (yet)
The "rapid fire" show almost negligible results when using auto weapons and will not surpass output programmed in game because the controller does NOT have control over game commands (code)
Stop acting like one will get a huge advantage using these, the advantages are somewhat slight.

Incursion of Software (fairly new) is great, you now have direct control and visual representation of configuring the mod using pc ect.
Software easy to use and a Huge Plus.

Instead of having to press trigger multiple times you can hold it for rapid fire in single shot weapons BUT it matches max speed possible by human fingers (again thats coded in game)
For me thats more of a "quality of life improvement" and saves wear on controller.

Auto run - same thoughts

Drop shot is also something that can be done in game but this offers that process to be done with less input - slight advantage due to less time.

Anti recoil - so here is where it becomes grey BUT from what i have seen the results differ with game and gun.
Can have a big advantage here but not with every gun.
Didnt seem to work well in Destiny 2.

Quick scoping is another QoL feature but the advantage can be argued to be non existent.

If you want to buy em for reasons like me, have more options especially for games like Elite Dangerous (paddles are a god send)
These are worth every dime.

If you chose to use them for games like CoD well im not gonna sit here and preach like im better than you or some moral high ground, this is because firstly im not your dad but also because i know the competitive landscape is filled with scuf/mods and secondly the extent of the advantage you will get is not a game changer imo.

This isnt aimbot.

A must own device imo regardless of intent.

When i say risks im using the word very lightly what im really saying is you have a lot of freedom being indie devs, freedom many AAA devs do not have thus many generic AAA games flood the market with each passing day, mind boggling how you used said freedom to emulate AAA devs.

Some say the game is overly ambitious but i dont see it that way, it feels outright "lazy" in some ways.
i.e ideas: devs seem opposed to creating their own and relying too heavily on attributes of other games to the point where these devs ultimately end up in a constant state of of ring around the Rosie, constantly spinning around getting drunk off the ideas of other games.

After two hours of playtime on release day, my thoughts on the game are extremely positive. We used the free Just Dance Controller app on a Samsung Note II and an iPhone 6s plus. Although its not perfect in determining if you are dancing well, I do believe the app worked as well as you could possibly expect on BOTH phones. When I danced well (or at least thought I was), the app seemed to be properly registering my moves the vast majority of time. And when I wasn't properly doing the moves, for the most part the app seemed to appropriately downgrade my score. There were times still where I think the app improperly registered movement, but those cases were few and didn't negatively impact the dance experience in the least. Another nice thing is that you can put down the controller and navigate using your phone instead with the app. However, I still prefer using the controller because the menu selections tend to be quicker that way. Now the only negative thing about using the app is you still have to hold your phone. Having a smaller phone would probably be a little more pleasant. But if you have a larger phone such as the iPhone 6s, it may be a little difficult to get used to at first. My wife didn't like holding it at first, but I think after a few dances she was starting to get used to it. Eventually, we may try the PS4 camera but for now the free apps work just fine.

Overall I was extremely impressed we ran into ZERO issues (no bugs, no crashes, etc...) during our first night of playing even though the game was just released. Before playing the game, I was quite concerned the app wouldn't work based on negative reviews of the app. There were quite a few reviews, even recent ones, from people saying it didn't work or that the app crashes. As I said earlier, we used two very different phones and the app worked flawlessly on both. So whatever issues people originally had with the app, it seems they've done a good job fixing those issues.

Finally, I do highly suggest this gold edition so you have access to far more songs. Basically what the gold edition gives you is access to 150 more songs for 3 months. Some people may not find this worth it, but I liked having all the songs available right at the start of the game.

Anyway I wanted to leave this early review for those wondering if there were any early issues. I will modify my review as I start taking note of any negatives with the game or have any other noteworthy items to mention. But honestly for now, absolutely no complaints!

First, it seems a lot of people simply jumped at the chance to review the game even though they hadn't actually played it or they had only played the beta. I suggest ignoring any reviews (at the least early ones) that aren't a verified purchase for that reason.

Anyway, from my perspective, so far its an enjoyable game. First, its nice they had a little distraction game for you while the game installed. The multiplayer game types seem interesting (Walker assault is my favorite so far) and I do like how the game is intended for more casual gamers. You don't have to be the best killer on the team to help. For example, I had a game where my K/D ratio wasn't good, and yet I had by far the highest objective score since I kept doing things like activating the Uplink Stations. Even though its a simple game overall, there's still a bit of a learning curve but nothing serious. I love the graphics and it definitely gives you the Star Wars feel. That being said, it is only a typical shooter in the end so I could see how that would disappoint some people. My other complaint with the game is that the party system could be improved. I played with two friends and when I join a match, they have to say yes to a prompt to join the same game. So if one person clicks yes too late, they may have to end up waiting for the game to open up and they could also end up on the other team (which happened to us once). Other than that I personally ran into no issues with the game. However, one of my friends did get dropped from one game but that could have been for a variety of reasons which may not have necessarily been the fault of the game. But since that was our only glitch, I'm not complaining. Those issues aside, it was still fun playing with friends when you do find them on the map. My favorite moment is when I saw my poor brother slain by Darth Vader. I honestly just stood there as I watched Vader lift him off the ground and choke him using the force. I didn't know at that point whether to cheer or to avenge my slain brother. It was a fun moment. And overall concerning the heroes in the game, I don't think the heroes are overpowered per say. Especially when teammates focus their attention on an enemy hero, they can go down rather quickly from what I observed.

There are a few other things to note about this game that may affect your purchase. First, if you want a single player campaign and don't want to play online against other people...this game is NOT for you. There's not really a single player campaign. Second, if you aren't really a fan of Star Wars...well you may as well skip this game. After playing the game, I can honestly say that if I were not a fan of Star Wars, I probably wouldn't be enjoying the game so much. Finally, don't expect much out of the vehicle combat. In my opinion its a little too simplistic so when I get in an X-wing for example, I tend to get bored rather quickly. There just doesn't seem to be much to it. However, they're still important. I did see a number of games where one side took control of the skies and that clearly helped them win the match. Anyway, hope that helps anyone considering this game. I will update my review accordingly as I continue playing the game. Please feel free to ask me any questions about the game if you have one.

I have been an owner of multiple consoles over the years. From the NES, to the SNES and Genesis, than to the PlayStation and the Nintendo 64, and followed closely by the Sega Dreamcast, I have always had fun with each console generation. One of my all time favorite consoles, to this day, has always been the Dreamcast. With highly unique classics such as Power Stone and Sonic Adventure available for the system, it has always had a great line up of games. However, there was always one Dreamcast game that got more playing time out of me than any other game, and that was Marvel VS Capcom 2.

Building upon the success of fighting games before it, such as Marvel Super Heroes, X-Men VS Street Fighter, and Marvel VS Capcom 1, Marvel VS Capcom 2 is a chaotically fast and addictive game. The gameplay focuses around teams of three characters fighting it out against other teams. The character roster is deep, focusing on both the Capcom side and the Marvel side of the game's two character worlds.

That's a total of 28 characters, per side, making the roster highly balanced. The benefit that I really got out of the new version of the game is the way that all of the cast is unlocked upon initially downloading the game. This is a huge improvement over the Dreamcast version, in which you were forced to complete Arcade mode multiple times, in order to earn enough points to "purchase" new characters; a task that was truly time consuming, and tedious. It is true, however, that many characters simply do overpower others on the game, such as Sentinel, however, with enough practice, it's actually quite simple to win as any character available on the game.

The graphics have been improved over the Dreamcast iteration, making the colors more vibrant, and the animations much more fluid than they were in the past. The graphics won't compare to games such as Battle Fantasia, Super Street Fighter IV, or BlazBlue, but they are still very solid, and crisp looking. There are no issues with the framerate, and the game feels great to play on the PlayStation 3.

Online play is now an extra mode added to the re-release of Marvel VS Capcom 2, and featurs a spectator mode which allows the player to watch the fights of other users. The menus have been reworked as well, looking much better than the original "hexagon" layout for the menus that the original Dreamcast version had.

All in all, the game looks great, plays great, and feels great, on the PlayStation 3, adding new features such as online play, and tweaking subtle things such as layout. The gameplay is unchanged, still relying on hectic, fast paced, chaotic fights between two teams of three, where even the A.I. can be difficult at times on higher difficulty levels. Getting this game now will definitely help put anyone in the mood for the upcoming sequel due in a few months. This is a must buy for anyone who is a fighting game fan.

BlazBlue is a very deep, and intense fighter, despite the rather low amount of characters who are present within the game. Consisting of a mere 12 fighters, the game may seem simplistic too many fighting game veterans. However, none of the 12 characters play like each other at all, whereas in many other games, such as Street Fighter, similarities can be found between multiple fighters. With BlazBlue, you are given a smaller roster, but with more variety.

Characters fight in a similar fashion to past Arc System Works' games, fast, and chaotic. Moves are executed in similar manners to Guilty Gear, utilizing traditional down, down-forward, forward + attack commands along with other traditional move commands associated with fighting games. The characters are just as original as ever, it is Arc Systems' trademark to include rather unique characters on each of their games. If you've ever been a fan of anime series, any anime at all, then you know the routine. Anime consists of animal-human hybrids, cyborgs/mecha-humans, busty females, monsters and characters with guns and large swords. Well, BlazBlue takes the anime style of drawing and mixes it with proven 2D fighting mechanics, resulting in a great blend of the two that makes BlazBlue a game worth checking out. BlazBlue follows the fighting engine from Guilty Gear perfectly, imitating special moves, character design, and musical themes. The game features 12 characters:

Ragna (resembles Dante but fights like Sol-Badguy)
Jin (resembles and fights like Ky Kiske)
Noel (fights with guns and resembles Bridget, except for the whole "cross dressing" thing)
Taokaka (a cat-human girl with comedic relief with her constant remarks)
Iron Tager (resembles Potemkin)
Arakune (a blob monster similar to the spirits in "Spirited Away", resembles and fights a lot like Eddie)
Bang (a mixture of Chipp and Great Saiyaman from DBZ, always poses and talks about "Justice")
Carl (fights like Zappa since they both control another being)
Hakumen (resembles Justice from Guilty Gear)
V-13 (a cyborg girl)
Rachel Alucard (fights and resembles May, just a Gothic version of May)
and finally Litchi (reminds me of Bayonetta).

The game is fast paced and hectic. The story mode, at first, does not make much sense, but after several replays it will start to clarify itself more if you pay close attention. The AI can be difficult on the higher settings, and the last boss can sometimes be unforgiving. The moves are easy to perform and respond with amazing accuracy and timing. The game features a new move, known as "Drives". Each character contains a unique set of moves associated with the drive button. Depending on what combination of directional buttons is used with the drive command, different results will occur. Many of the characters' most devastating moves rely on the usage of the drive button. Characters such as Noel can use the drive command to create unique combos, while Hakumen's drive command sets him up to counter incoming attacks. The online game play is where things can truly become intense. Locating an open lobby is relatively easy and simple, and each one shows a list of users' levels within that game lobby. There is almost no lag, except for an occasional hiccup every once and a while, but it's not a major issue at all.

BlazBlue is a simply amazing game, especially when considering the small amount of quality 2D fighting games out this generation. It may not be as fast paced as games like Guilty Gear or Super Street Fighter IV, and it may not contain as many characters as games such as Tekken, but its unique spin on the fighting genre, and its usage of a new command button (drive) adds something new worth checking out. If you're a fan of fighting games or past work of Arc System Works, then this game is a must have addition to your gaming library.

Quantum Theory is the latest addition to the ever growing third person shooter genre. What makes this game stand out is the clear cut fact that the entire game is based off of one of the most successful third person shooter games ever released, "Gears of War". Trying to take what Gears of War did so many years ago and attempting to make it "fresh", "new" and "innovative", Quantum Theory adds its own unique flavor and twist to the Gears of War style. Does it work out? To a certain extent.

The game focuses around a man by the name of Syd, a direct clone of Marcus Fenix in terms of personality, looks, and even voice. Syd is a soldier whose main duty is to destroy the Living Tower that is destroying everything that humanity has loved for centuries. The power of the living tower comes from a foreign substance referred to as "erosion". Through the usage of its powers, the Living Tower is capable of manipulating the land around it, shifting the appearance of the grounds and making the game more difficult for users since cover points tend to disappear each time the land changes.

Syd joins up with a local squadron who also hunts and destroys the Living Towers. However, the AI of these assistants is very low, many times making it seem better to have been playing by yourself rather than having to worry about your partners. This is really nothing new to shooter games, however, since many times in Halo games the Marine assistants tend to simply get in the way of the fights with the enemies. The enemies on Quantum Theory aren't very difficult to beat, usually their response time is rather slow, and performing melee attacks on them is relatively easy due to their slow response.

The game adds a unique feature, the ability to throw an AI controlled partner at the enemies and have her enact as a "grenade" of sorts. By throwing your partner at the enemy, she instantly performs attacks upon contact, sometimes resulting in instant kills on the enemy. However, some points of combat are rather lacking when compared to Gears of War. Quantum Theory's hit detection seems a little bit off, making it difficult at times to shoot enemies and have the hits actually register as causing damage. Guns are mapped to the d-pad and can be changed by pressing the corresponding directional button. Picking up items is done with the down button, so the game only allows the user to carry three weapons at a time.

Critics have already begun to pour in the negative remarks on the game, panning it for "outdated graphics", "poor controls" and "uninteresting characters". However, despite the game's problems, it still has enough "pizazz" to make it stand out amongst other titles available on the market. The sum of its parts may make the game fall short in some cases, however, since many of the smaller aspects of the game simply fail in comparison to the game in which it is so desperately trying to emulate. When comparing Quantum Theory to Gears of War, it's an easy choice as to which game plays better, looks better, and simply works better. However, with its own unique gameplay mechanics, such as shifting levels which take away the players' cover spots, as well as the unique ability to throw a teammate at enemies to inflict damage (or even kill enemies), Quantum Theory is still worth checking out if you're interested in third person shooters. The graphics may not be as polished as Gears of War 2, and the gameplay may be a little more sloppy than Gears as well, but the game is still good on its own merit.

Being new to the Xbox 360, I had been wanting to try out the Halo franchise that garners so much praise and hype. However, never owning an original Xbox, instead having both a PlayStation 2 and a GameCube, I figured it would be best to start off with the first game of the series. So, I recently purchased Halo: Combat Evolved for the Xbox. However, when I heard about the various mods and extras that the PC version of the game has when compared to its console counterpart, I decided to purchase the PC version of the game. The game runs great on my laptop which runs Windows Vista.

The story is quite compelling, and quite unique as well, and does a great job of grabbing the players' attention. The story takes place in the distant future where space travel and planet colonization is standard practice by humans. Humans have colonized a planet known as "Reach" and use this planet to genetically alter humans into cyborgs known as "Spartans". This practice has infuriated an alien race known as The Covenant. The Covenant has begun attacking the planet Reach and destroying Spartans and humans. One ship manages to escape with a Spartan on board. The ship is known as the Autumn Pillar, and the Spartan is Master Chief Petty Office John-117, better known as simply Master Chief. Covenant begin boarding the Autumn Pillar, and leave Captain Keyes with no choice but to release Master Chief and other Marines in escape pods. Before launching the pods, Master Chief picks up the central control of the ship, known as Cortana, and fuses her connection to his own cybernetic suit. The two crash land and must find and gather any humans who have survived. The two must then go on to rescue Captain Keyes, who has been captured by The Covenant and imprisoned on their ship. Keyes issues a command to Master Chief to locate the control panel of the Covenant's main weapon, Halo. Halo is a giant ring-like structure that contains massive energy and could cause serious extermination if activated. Along the way to the control panel, Master Chief discovers that the Covenant have woken a dormant alien race known as the Flood. Now the fight between humanity includes a new enemy, as the Flood continue to spread rapidly. Master Chief is left facing some difficult decisions as the story progresses further.

The gameplay consists of run and gun shooting that occurs at a fast pace. Enemies are very intelligent on the higher difficulty levels, and even the inclusion of an automatically regenerating shield is sometimes not enough to survive the enemy onslaught. The lands are very detailed, but sometimes can become extremely repetitive. Many of the levels consist of the same room design repeated over and over again, making it feel like you aren't really getting anywhere and are simply running in circles. Some levels become tedious at times, and the feeling of "repetition" begins to grow as the level progresses. This rule definitely applies to the later levels where it feels as if you are simply re-entering the same two rooms over and over again in some sort of infinite loop, each time the rooms contain the same enemies as well, making the level feel even more repetitive. Stages that aren't so repetitive are quite compelling and fun to play in, but these are limited to the first few stages, as the game progresses the level designs lose their luster, becoming mundane and boring. The graphics hold up quite nicely for a last gen game, and the gameplay is smooth and addictive. The weapons the player picks up from the enemies are very effective and with enemies appearing by massive quantities, it's always easy to find another weapon to replace your current one upon running out of ammunition.

Another complaint I have regarding the original Halo: Combat Evolved is in regards to the controls of the vehicles. Some vehicles such as the Ghost and Banshee pilot beautifully, giving the player amazing control over the vehicles. However, the Warthog can be unruly and almost impossible to control and navigate, especially in tight corridors where obstacles are abundant. This is what makes the last level of the game almost impossible to beat since the Warthog has such a hard time maneuvering properly without hitting obstacles. The steering of the Warthog has greatly been corrected in the later games though, but in Combat Evolved it is a vehicle I like to try to avoid driving.

The PC version has countless mods available for download that allow the user to get even more out of the gaming experience. My favorite mod is the third person mod, which allows users to play the game in a camera angle very similar to that of Lost Planet. Using this viewpoint, the game feels more original, and allows the user to get a better view of Master Chief and his always cool looking armor. The game is relatively easy to run and install, due to its rather low PC requirements. It's just as engaging to play these days, despite its aging graphics, due to its original plot and likable characters.

The Xbox 360 is arguably one of the most popular consoles of recent memory, with even Hollywood films and television series making references to "The Xbox" or shown playing the console in some manner. The console's main advantage over its predecessor is the ergonomically designed controller. Whereas the original Xbox featured a rather large controller similar to that of the Sega Dreamcast, the Xbox 360 features a much smaller, yet larger than the PS3, design that incorporates easy to use triggers and concave thumbsticks which provide better overall grip than the PS3's analog sticks do.

However, one thing has always been a little "off" about the controller. Despite its overall design being praised left and right by consumers and gaming professionals alike, one drawback has been constantly present whenever one discusses the Xbox 360 controller and that is its directional pad. The PlayStation controllers have always provided one of the best fitting, and most useful, d-pads on a controller to date. However, Microsoft went the route of the Sega Genesis, and utilized more a disc design for their d-pad. The result: an awkward design that does not respond as intended. Pressing "up" can sometimes be interpreted by the controller as an "up-forward" making on screen avatars move in the wrong direction.

This controller promises to try to alleviate the problem, and it works, to a degree. The controller provides a much easier to press directional pad which allows the user to ensure that he/she is indeed pressing the desired direction properly. It does not move as fluidly as the PS3 d-pad does, but when compared to the previous iterations of the Xbox 360 controller, it does provide a much better overall response for each direction. If the user decides to play the games with the traditional disc that the 360 uses, a simple twist of the d-pad converts it back it to its regular form.

Overall, the controller provides a better directional pad than previous versions of the controller, with slightly improved response from the four major directions: up, left, right, and down. However, if a user is expecting PS3 level responsiveness, than they may be disappointed. The color scheme is a nice touch to the controller, providing an overall classy, and sleek design.

Mortal Kombat is a gaming franchise that has seen its fair share of ups and downs. What began as an immensely popular arcade fighter back in the early 90s, has slowly devolved into a mediocre fighting game that always felt "rushed" and never felt complete. The developers had toyed with various ideas throughout the years starting with Mortal Kombat 4. With their first step into the 3D world, Midway made Mortal Kombat 4 a game with 3D graphics that fought within a two dimensional playing field. However, the combat system was generic, utilizing a system in which all the characters played exactly the same and even had the same combos. This took the feel of "genuineness" out of each fighter, and the introduction of weapons in Mortal Kombat 4 also felt tacked on.

Onto Deadly Alliance, where the developers made every character unique once again, and this time expanded upon the weapons system added in the previous title. However, due to the lack of characters, and the one fatality format of the game, it never felt the same as previous entries in the franchise such as Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, Mortal Kombat Trilogy, or Mortal Kombat 2. Midway mixed up the formula again in Deception, bringing back many classic fighters, adding in some more, and creating new game modes such as Chess Kombat, Puzzle Kombat, and Konquest Mode. However, Konquest Mode was a poorly developed story mode that felt tacked on, and never allowed the user to truly feel like they accomplished anything by beating it despite its immensely long duration of playtime. With Mortal Kombat Armageddon, the developers thought that by returning every character from all previous entries would add enough flare to help revitalize the franchise. However, Armageddon was lacking in variety (with several challenge ladders constantly repeating themselves, level design lacking, and AI extremely dumbed down). The air combat was a nice touch but didn't add enough "oomph" to get the series back on track.

The only Mortal Kombat game to be released this generation did not feel like a true entry into the franchise due to the lack of true violence in which the series is known for. So, Ed Boon decided that a return to a more "klassic" approach may be exactly what is needed to return the gaming franchise back to its glory days. That's where "Mortal Kombat" (9 or 2011 whatever you want to call it) came into play. Seeing a return to two dimensional fighting is a major plus, adding to the challenge and the ability to perform more complex combos similar to those seen within Capcom fighting games.

The game does more than simply return to the 2D realm of fighting, it brings back classic elements of previous titles that long time fans of the series are sure to appreciate. With the move into 3D, the developers had dropped many aspects of the series in the process. The most notable changes were to characters' move sets. On games such as Deadly Alliance and Deception, classic character moves such as Cyrax's net, Sektor's homing missiles, Scorpion's scissor kick, and most notably Shang Tsung's morphing ability. With "Mortal Kombat (9, 2011)", Ed Boon resurrected all of these old moves. Classic moves such as Johnny Cage's crouch punch have returned, alongside other notable classics such as Reptile's energy balls, Jax's "gotcha grab", Noob Saibot's cloud attack, etc. All of these moves were abandoned after Mortal Kombat trilogy, and it's great to see a return of such notable attacks that had defined these characters during their early years.

Besides a return of classic moves, this latest entry also sees a return of classic modes such as "Test Your Might". The game also features the return of many classic elements such as Dan Forden and his trademark "Toasty" appearing on the bottom of the screen. Stage fatalities for classic levels have reappeared with levels like the Deadpool and the Pit making a return. Re-imagining of character designs are also present with each fighter resembling their 2D counterpart in a more updated and modern manner. The return of Babalities brings back that classic MK humor that helps take a break from the excessive amount of killing.

The story mode is extremely well developed and covers the events immediately following MK Armageddon. With Shao Kahn winning and defeating every opponent in the process, Raiden is forced to use a method of time travel to warn his past iteration about the dire future that awaits unless he can change it. Raiden tries to change the future as much as possible, and in the process, new characters are born. Gamers will see the rise of new faces such as Smoke remaining human and Sub-Zero getting automated in his place. It's a very interesting plot that the developers went with, and the story mode feels well fleshed out, rather than rushed like in previous entries.

The PS3 version sees the added benefit of playing as Kratos, lead character from Sony's hit franchise "God of War". Kratos is a great addition to the game, and he kind of fits right in. His games have always been over-the-top with violence, similar to Mortal Kombat, and his moves and fatalities not only fit his character, but fall right into place in the Mortal Kombat puzzle.

Overall, this is a game that all long time fans of the series have been looking forward to, and NetherRealm Studios delivered on bringing back fanfare to the series. The game feels like it was tailored to the fans with so many classic elements making a reappearance. All the little touches will not go unnoticed by devoted fans, and this game may be exactly what the series needed to reestablish itself as a true contender within the fighting game genre. An instant "Klassic".

"Heavy Rain" is a game touted by many to be something unlike anything else, making it a rare exception in the realm of video games where it's all too common to copy and paste a strategy and elements stolen directly from a competitor's game design and gameplay. However, there truly is nothing else on the market similar to "Heavy Rain" in terms of gameplay or design. The game has its ups and downs, but the pros definitely outweigh the cons, making this one of the most addictive games available on the PlayStation 3.

The game focuses around a series of button prompts, in similar fashion to commonly used "quick time events" that began their emergence last generation with games such as Resident Evil 4 and God of War. The difference with "Heavy Rain" is the matter in which it uses the prompts. In games like God of War, the prompts are used only to ensure that the actions are performed correctly in order to vanquish an opponent. If the prompt is failed, the player gets a chance to attempt the sequence again if the proper damage is dealt to the enemy once again. However, with "Heavy Rain" the button prompts determine the player's choice and decision based upon the available actions for that given story sequence. For example: there may be an instance where the player has to quickly press a button to shoot a man who is seemly going to murder an ally police officer. If the player presses the button, the man is killed, and the story continues with that option. If the player does not press the button quick enough, the man lives on, and the story continues with that scenario.

Moving characters within the 3D world created within "Heavy Rain" can be a somewhat daunting task. The characters control in the exact same manner as the old school Resident Evil games. For anyone who has never played these games it basically means that characters can only walk in a straight line according to the direction pressed on the directional pad by the player. Turning and navigating through a room with obstacles can sometimes be clunky, resulting in players running into tables and door frames, something common of the old school Resident Evil controller layout as well.

Despite the somewhat clunky controls used to maneuver throughout the game, "Heavy Rain" more than makes up for it with character development and a plot that is well thought out and keeps the players on their toes. Twists and turns occur every second, and players' choices will affect the gameplay even more as each action has a reaction, similar to one of Newton's laws of physics. The story plays out like a "Saw" film, with a killer on the lose forcing parents into torturing and killing themselves in attempts to save their kidnapped children. The game starts off slow, with the first 1 hour or so being devoted to learning the controls with basic elements such as setting a table, getting dressed, driving your car, etc. However, once it picks up, the game doesn't relent on the characters within the story. Throwing all characters into the hands of death at every turn leaves the player with the choice to follow the prompts and save the characters or venture into a new plotline where that character has been killed.

"Heavy Rain" is truly great and once it gets going it's hard to stop since you will constantly want to see what is going to happen next. Besides the clunky controls used to actually walk around within the game, the only other factor that holds it off from being perfect is the replay value. The killer's identity remains the same despite the player's choices and despite the fact that the game makes it seem like every character is a suspect. Other than these complaints, "Heavy Rain" is a very solid release worth looking into.

Mortal Kombat is my all time favorite video game franchise, and I've been playing the games ever since Mortal Kombat 2 was released on the SNES and Sega Genesis. I've played and owned every single iteration of the games throughout the years, including the very disheartening entries such as Mythologies and Special Forces. However, none of them have ever built me up with so much hype only to completely disappoint me in the same manner in which Mortal Kombat 11 has done.

Mortal Kombat 11 follows the release of the highly successful Mortal Kombat X (and its komplete version, XL). However, where Mortal Kombat X was able to provide fans with a ton of new features and characters while still appealing to klassic fans of the series and introduce new mechanics, Mortal Kombat 11 fails at doing the same. Mortal Kombat X introduced the variation system, where every character had 3 separate and unique variations that granted access to different special moves based upon which variation was selected. Mortal Kombat 11 aims at amplifying that system by now allowing users to create their own variations. However, this is where the first set of issues comes into play.

Mortal Kombat 11's variation system is indeed rather extensive and each character has hundreds of combinations of gear pieces that can be equipped (masks, weapons, costumes/skins, etc.). However, all of these items (even the basic variation icons) are locked away either inside the Krypt or the Towers of Time. This is where the issues begin to get out of hand. The Krypt is just a large lootbox mode disguised as a third-person adventure game. The boxes inside the Krypt are randomly generated for each user and all cost such a high amount of coins to unlock/open, in contrast to the very small amount of coins that are earned from playing the game itself. This means it will take hundreds of hours to unlock all the gear for your favorite character and will take thousands of hours to get them for the entire roster.

The rewards earned from playing any of the modes (especially the Towers of Time) are very low in quantity, resulting in players having to play hundreds of hours in these modes to earn enough points to open chests in the Krypt. This gets worse by the fact that the Towers of Time is built in a manner to truly be unfair with ridiculous difficulty spikes where enemies are using modifiers that are unblockable or in such high frequency that it is almost impossible to win some of these fights without resorting to cheap tactics of your own or utilizing your own modifiers. That in itself is another problem, as modifiers are one-time usage items and have to be earned again after using. To make things even worse, rewards cannot be earned if the game is being played offline, and it requires internet in order to validate your rewards. So, if you were looking to play the game 100% offline, that is not a possibility.

All of these make it feel like the game was designed this way intentionally in order to encourage people to pay real world money for these items/tokens through the store. Even Frost, one of the base roster characters, can either be earned by playing through the Story Mode of the game and making the character selections to unlock her in Chapter 4 or by paying real world money for her.

The gameplay itself is good, but some of the changes also detract from previous entries. The lack of true defensive mechanics such as reversals/combo-breakers is a major example of this. The game also only allows players to utilize the "Fatal Blow" attacks once per fight, whereas in MK9 and X it was possible to use X-ray attacks multiple times in a fight. The character animations are fluid and the graphics are truly remarkable. The combo system is still very well done, and builds upon the system found in MKX, but slows down the combat pace and removes the run button. This forces the players to focus more on neutral control and footsies, making the game more methodical in approach whereas MK X was more aggressive in its fighting system approach. So, speaking of the game in regards to its fighting mechanics, the game is fantastic and fluid.

Overall, the game tries to completely reinvent the mechanics of Mortal Kombat but fails by changing up the formula too much and by forcing too many microtransactions onto the kommunity. The studio has also done some deceptive and questionable practices where they have willingly mocked fans of characters like Sindel, Mileena, Rain, Cyrax and Sektor by either disrespecting the characters and their fanbases or by adding the characters into the game as NPCs, just out of reach of their fans.

As of now, I would recommend passing on the game and picking up MK XL instead, as that game can be found for relatively cheap on either the Xbox One or PlayStation 4 and it includes all of the characters (on disc) along with all of the other DLC without any need to grind. The fighting is also easier for newbies of the series to get into than what it is on MK11, and finally, MK XL also features a much more diverse and extensive roster with more fan favorites. If you're interested in this game, maybe wait for a komplete edition that will inevitably be released down the line.

The Thrustmaster T150 is one of the first affordable force feedback wheels available for the Playstation 4. It will also work on your PS3 and PC since it connects to the console via a standard USB connector (no wireless I'm afraid). Unfortunately it will not work with the Xbox One as Microsoft have fitted the Xbox One with a new security chip that manufacturers must incorporate into their controllers and a driver set.

In the box you will find the wheel which sports some fairly large paddle shifters allowing you to change gear at virtually any angle of the 1080 degree wheel rotation, a set a pedals (brake and gas only, there is no clutch pedal) and of course on the wheel the full set of PS4 buttons.

The pedals do allow you to adjust the angle of both the brake and gas peddles to suit your comfort level and the brake pedal features progressive resistance, something you used to only find on high end pedal sets like those from Fanatec. Unlike its bigger brother, the T300, the pedal set you get with the T150 is plastic and the wheel only has 12 bit resolution instead of 16. In practice you do notice the difference but it is not that big enough to make any major difference when playing a game. You do notice it more when correcting a skid as you can be more precise on the T300. Also, unlike the T300, the wheel rim on the T150 is not detachable so you are stuck with the 11 inch rubber coated wheel that comes with the set.

On testing the wheel with Project Cars (currrently the best racing game available on the PS4 in my opinion), the force feedback works well. It is not noisy and has enough resistance that you really feel it but without having so much as to break your wrists (for example the Fanatec wheel has insane amounts of resistance, thankfully scaleable).

Whilst the Thrustmaster T150 racing rig comes in at the low end of the scale, mixing up your periphels is encouraged if you want to get a better rig further down the line. You can get the TH8A shifter and also the T3PA and T3PA-Pro 3 pedal sets which will work with this wheel. This is good as personally I do not like the pedal set that comes with this wheel. They feel very plasticy and I'm almost scared that if I press too hard, especially on the break pedal with its resistance turned up, I might actually break it.

I love racing games and have been playing them with wheels for years now. I have the full Fanatec setup and the T300 (the big brother to this set).
In my opinion the difference between the Fanatec setup and Thrustmasters is night and day, but then again so is the price. For $200 Thrustmaster are offering you a fairly decent wheel and pedal set with some limited upgradeability. For the ocassional racer you won't find anything like this for the price that is currently compatible with the PS4 and comes with force feedback. If you are a little more serious about your racing then I'd spend the extra on the Fanatec or T300 setups.

The Xbox one wireless controller for Windows 10 allows you to play games on your Windows 10 PC with what is arguably the best console controller there is.

In the package you will find an Xbox one controller, the wireless USB dongle, an extension cord for the USB dongle and some batteries. The batteries are standard AA type. You do not get a rechargeable battery pack with this setup.

Setup is very easy. Just plug the wireless dongle into a spare USB port on your PC and it will automatically install the correct drivers for you. Once the drivers are installed, simply press the little button on the dongle and the little button on the top of the Xbox controller to pair them.

There is a note that comes along with the controller stating that the first thing you should do is to upgrade the firmware within the controller so that you can use the stereo audio output on the controller. In order to do this you need to install the Xbox Accessories app from the Windows 10 store and most importantly you need to directly attach the Xbox controller to your PC. You cannot update the firmware wirelessly. Unfortunately, in order to attach the Xbox directly to your PC you will need a spare micro USB to USB cord which does not come supplied. If you already have an Xbox one, you can either use the cord that came with the Xbox one or you can simply update the controllers firmware directly through your Xbox one. Why Microsoft did not supply a micro USB cord when this is fairly much a necessary step I do not know.

Some people prefer using controllers to keyboard and mouse. I use both, just depends on the game. I already have an Xbox one (so this is also a spare controller for that). This is an excellent solution for when I hook my gaming laptop up to large screen TV as I can now play games on my TV whilst sitting in my recliner. The only thing this needs is a direct line of sight to the wireless dongle (the extension cord that Microsoft supplied here comes in handy for this).

This adapter is for a Windows 10 PC and runs with no problems on that platform. I haven't tested it with any previous version of windows as it explicitly states it is for Windows 10.

If you already have an Xbox one, you can buy just the wireless dongle for your PC and use your existing Xbox one controllers.

This isn't the cheapest console type controller on the market for Windows 10 but it is arguably one of the best. If you want a console controller to play with your PC games then this works beautifully however I think it may be more suited to those that actually have an Xbox one as well and can use this as a second controller for their Xbox as well as their PC.

The fusion pro controller for the Xbox One looks fairly much like a standard Microsoft Xbox One controller and feels like one (roughly the same weight and size) but there are a number of things that differentiate this controller over the standard Microsoft one.

The first thing to get out the way is this is a wired controller, not a wireless one. So you have to connect this to the USB port at the back of the Xbox one (which can be a bit of a pain depending on how you have your Xbox one situated. I admit that I much preferred having the USB ports on the front of the console like the Xbox 360 rather than the back). It does come with ample wire (around 10ft) which should be enough for most rooms.

The next thing you will notice is that even though the controller is basically the same size as the Microsoft one, the thumb sticks are not. The ones on the Fusion Pro are quite a bit larger which is good is you have large hands like I do. I find that I have much more precision with the larger thumb sticks than the smaller Microsoft ones. Pressing down on the thumb sticks is also easier with it being larger.

On the back of the controller you will find a number of extra buttons (down the center of the controller and where your middle and ring fingers sit). These are programmable in that you can assign any of these buttons to the same control as any of the standard buttons. For example, say you are used to resting your right thumb so that you can comfortably press the A and B buttons on the front of the controller but need to move your hand a little or stretch your thumb to get the X and Y buttons. Well simply assign X and Y to two of the buttons on the back. That way each of the buttons is now within easy, comfortable reach without having to shift your hand position on the controller.

One thing you may find, at least I did, is that coming from the standard Microsoft controller I found myself accidentally pressing some of the buttons on the back when I didn't mean to. It does take a little while to get used to having them there. Then I found that once I was used to them and used to playing a certain way, I really missed not having them when I returned to the standard wireless Microsoft controller and had to re-adjust my thinking on playing games.

Programming the buttons is simplicity itself. Just hold program button down for 2 seconds, select the function you wish to duplicate then select which button you wish to assign it to. You can only duplicate normal functions (like the A,B,X,Y buttons, triggers etc). You cannot assign these buttons to other functions or combinations of buttons.

Also on the back you will find two trigger lock sliders. One of each of the triggers which can come in handy sometimes when playing something like Star Wars Battlefront or other FPS or racing games. More often than not however I found that I didn't actually use the trigger locks during play.

Overall this is a good, sturdy Xbox One controller (which you can connect and use on a PC if you wish) that can give you a slight edge in games with the additional buttons once you get used to it. It is much cheaper than the new Xbox One Elite controllers and even cheaper than a standard wireless Microsoft controller and as such is a good choice for a secondary controller (or to use as your primary if you don't mind the wire).

One of the first games released for the Xbox One was Forza Motorsport 5. Although the game itself had some drawbacks, one of the major ones, for me at least, was the lack of any kind of steering wheel and pedal set available for the Xbox One. I had a few sets for my PS3 and Xbox 360 and had grown so used to playing driving games in a seat with pedals and a wheel that going back to the controllers just didn't seem right.

Since then there have been a few (not many) pedal and wheel sets come out for the Xbox One and none of them to be honest have been very good so far with the exception of the Fanatec set which will cost you around $1500, not including a seat.

Thrustmaster has once again decided to dip its toe into the world of racing wheels with the Thrustmaster TMX set. Primarily designed for the Xbox One but it will also work with your PC as well. The Thrustmaster TMX is basically a two piece set. You get the wheel which has all the buttons for the Xbox One laid out in easily reach positions with the exception of the menu buttons which are a little too far in on the wheel for easy reach however you will rarely if ever use them in games. It has a nice set of metal paddle shifters with a solid microswitch click to them letting you know gears have changed. The wheel itself features a 270 to 900 degree turning angle (adjustable in game) and adjustable force feedback (also adjustable in game). The force feedback works very well letting you know when you are running over rumble strips or goes slightly light when you are in a skid giving you instant feedback just like you have in a real car. This really helps with controlling your car and getting the best laptimes possible. The wheel is sturdy and comes with a screw on clamp so that you can affix it to a table. I tried playing with it in my lap an you realistically can't. It needs to be clamped down.

The pedals set is a base accelerator and brake pedal. The brake pedal has a tighter spring on it giving you a simulated feedback mechanism but unlike the pedal sets from Fanatec, it is not a true feedback mechanism. Compared to the wheel, the pedals look and feel a lot cheaper and more flimsy.

I've tried the wheel with Forza 6 and Forza Horizons 2 and it works well. Force feedback works well (you may need to adjust the settings in game for your own particular preference but I found the defaults work really well), the buttons and paddle shifters work well however the accelerator pedal isn't as precise as I would have liked. I do own the much more expensive Fanatec set and you can really tell the difference.

Setup is as simply as plugging the pedals into the wheel, the wheel into a power supply and your Xbox using the USB cable.

There are some issues with the wheel however and one of them (for me anyway) is a major one. Firstly, there are no holes in the bottom of the wheel which would allow you to fix it to a racing seat, you only have the option of clamping it to a table. I have two racing seats and the clamping system really just doesn't work with either of them.

The second problem and this is the major one is that the Thrustmaster TMX set simply does not have long enough cables. The USB cable is only about 5 feet in length and the power cable is perhaps 6ft. I have an 80 inch TV that my consoles are hooked into and with the very poor length of the cables I found myself sitting 2 feet infront of it. This simply does not make for a good way to play games. You are far too close and after a while I actually started getting a headache with being so close the TV. The cables need to be 3 times as long as they are. It's not as if cabling is expensive. Whomever designed this must have designed it primarily for use on a PC where 5ft of cabling is generally long enough but is nowhere near long enough for your average console.

Overall this is quite a good wheel and pedal set, especially for the money but rendered almost unusable by the woefully short cables.

For Honor takes you back to the gory days of sword fighting. The combat system employed in this third person hack and slash game might at first seem a bit limiting. You have three different stances, left, right and upper with each stance dictating which side you can block and which side you will attack. Left stance means you will block attacks to the left and attack to the left of your opponent etc. You also have the ability for a rolling dodge and the freedom to move around the playing area as you deem fit.

After a gorgeous introduction sequence laying out the overall theme for the game, you have the choices of playing a campaign (single player mode) or choosing to be either a samurai, knight or a Viking. The fairly simplistic sounding combat system gives you quite a lot of choices in reality between heavy and light attacks, parries and counters, stuns and throws and of course no hack and slasher would be complete without some form of grisly and brutal execution.

The campaign mode is your fairly typical affair, first teaching you the different moves available to you, how and when best to use them and slowly pits you against enemies of ever increasing strength with the obligatory end of level bosses but the multi player squads is where you will probably end up playing most of this game with rewards to level up your character. Steel is however rewarded fairly sparsely for each completed match but the expense of some of the items may seem daunting and will take you quite a while to achieve. You get the feeling that ubisoft is ultimately pushing you towards its store front where you can spend your hard earned greenbacks on quantities of steel to obtain items quicker. This can be an expensive option however.

Overall this is a good hack and slash game with fairy pretty but not outstanding graphics and though the combat system may appear fairly sparse it does give you a lot of choices. Longevity of the game however is questionable as you fairly much end up doing the same things over and since some items are so expensive in the store, you may get bored trying to level up some of your items.

The Combat Tech Special Edition Xbox wireless controller is essentially your standard Xbox One wireless controller with a few cosmetic changes. The buttons, triggers, joysticks etc. feel the exact same as the standard controller, the same tactile feedback and responsiveness.

The big difference, apart from a few color changes giving it that militaristic look, is the inclusion of the rubberized diamond grip which does actually make a change. After sitting playing a game for a couple of hours, especially when it is hot or you are having an intense gaming stint, the rubberized diamond does actually give you extra grip on the controller when your hands are sweating. This is a nice addition.

One thing you will want to do when you get the controller is to physically connect it to your Xbox and make sure that it is running the latest firmware.

As with all Xbox controllers, you can also use this one on a Windows 10 PC (either wired which is not supplied or via bluetooth).

Overall this is essentially just a standard Xbox controller with a pleasant design however the rubberized diamond will give you added grip and for that reason I would recommend this over the standard controller.

Marching Fire is the first major expansion pack to the original For Honor game that was released last year.
Just in case you didn't buy the original For Honor, not to worry as you get that included with this expansion. Be prepared however for a fairly large 27Gb update to the game when you first put it in and install it, which takes a little while to download and install.

For Honor one of your standard hack and slash games however the combat system employed in For Honor is excellent giving you lots of strategic options rather than just blocking or slashing. When you lock into an opponent you can change your guard to block left, right or top. You can block incoming attacks from the direction you are guarding and you have to read which direction your opponent is guarding as it works the same for them also. So when you are attacking, you want to attack to one of the directions they are not guarding and vice versa. It sounds fairly simple and boring but it isn't and actually gives you lots of strategic options when fighting.

In the game you get to play 12 heroes from three different factions. Knights, Vikings and Samurai. Each faction has an all round good hero, an assassin who is fast and deadly but lightly armored, a heavily armored but slow hero and a hybrid who has long-ranged weapons.

As well as the single player game you have an online element as well where you progress slowly but eventually can get your hero awesome armor and weapons.

The Marching Fire expansion instantly gives you access to four new heroes from the far east and a new arcade mode as well as quite a lift in the graphics department from the original.

Graphics wise this game is excellent as well as the both the music and excellent thumping and clanging sound effects.

Marching Fire has a good but not great campaign, is very stingy with its awards of steel (which you can use to build better armor etc) but is saved by it's excellent combat system which will take a while to truly master.

Living in the South basketball really isn't a big thing here. College football is primary with basketball taking a backseat. However that doesn't stop me from watching a few games every now and then.

I like games that you can just plug in and play, get a real sense for things and progress as your skills get better. NBA 2K19 unfortunately is not like that. It has a steep learning curve right from the start and I kept finding myself getting absolutely pounded by the computer on the default difficulty level. A lot of emphasis has been placed on ball control and style (flashy dunks etc.). The AI isn't perfect either with the computer regularly dribbling straight into one of my players or bypassing an open player down the court to make sure the star player of the team gets the ball which seems a bit odd.

There are different ways to play NBA 2K19 with MyLeague probably being the strongest option. This allows you to build an NBA franchise from the ground up and has an almost overwhelming array of options to choose from. If you want however you can drop into blacktop mode for a game of one on one or street basketball.

Graphics wise the game is very good however there are oddities about the bodies of players that just seem out of place like Lebron basically having the same body as type Rajon. It doesn't detract from the gameplay, just looks a bit odd. The animations are very well done especially if you string together a few moves in a well done play and score and the players look fluid and natural.

Overall NBA 2K19 is probably more for serious fans of basketball who will put in the effort to learn the fairly complex control system and not for someone who just wants to play every now and again for 15 minutes.

As of this review, I do wish there were more games (something the PSVR has in spades for obviously being in the market longer), but what is there is enjoyable and worth owning the quest for. Another upgrade the quest has over the PSVR is the tracking. You don't need to face a camera and therefore tracking loss is kept to a minimum (if ever). I love that it's completely portable so you can share the experience with friends and family outside of your home.

Enjoyed playing this series, though wished this game would have been a litlle better.

Never thought I would rate a COD game 3 stars, but there it is. Suprisingly, this game failed in many ways.

The single player first: They are telling a story that bounces u all over the place between places and wars. It starts in the early sixties and takes you up to Vietnam. You are being questioned by unkown interigators and then it takes you to a mission you have to complete. Seomtimes, just as you are getting into the mission, it breaks and you are back in the interigation chair. This is repeated several times and gets a little frustrating. The gameplay is typical COD. Very exciting action with little time for taking in the scenery and anything else. you pretty much just keep running an firing just like every other COD game. You would think they could change it up a little, though getting non-stop action is not a bad thing, it just feels the same as all the other games. And the campaign gets shorter and shorter.

Now, the MP: Laggy best describes it right now. It has gotten better, but still has rough moments. And the Mp plays like FEAR 2 which is not really a good thing. It looks and plays cheaply. The controls seem clunky and the maps, while not the bad, are not really awesome. Some are good and are wide open giving you less places to camp, but when you spawn in and die from a attack copter without being able to move, you start to hate it, especially when it happens 4 or 5 times in a row. Also, there is very little time between maps, and while I am sure some like this, it doesnt give you time to do things like create a class (which is a good thing when you get a new weapon or perk available) or purchase contracts. You have to leave the game you are playing make the change, and then hope you can get back in. Now, you do get money for kills and winning maps that you can spend to make purchases early, which is kind of cool, but not really all that cool. As for wager matches, I can barely find anyone playing those. Surprise I say as I didnt think that was all that cool. Mp needs more work and right now, Treyarch is working on another patch that is supposed to really fix most of the problems with lag and other issues, but I dont think it will be enough to make this game as good as the others.

The graphics seema little better, but not much. Same with the sound. Not much impressed, sadly to say. As for the system requirments, not much has changed except that u need a good processor. I bought a new computer as my 3 year old CPU's processor wasnt good enough (need on anyways). I had dual AMD 64 and it wouldnt play. Oh well, one more thing I guess.

Anywasy, buy this at your own risk. I really believe Activision is gonna miss Infinity Ward and think if future releases of COD don't start getting it right and do something a little different, sales are gonna start dropping like a plane with no fuel and crash to a firey end.

Heres to hoping things get better, but I ain't holding my breath.

Being a Chris taylor fan since his first game Total Annihilation, I have been thrilled with all of his Gas Powered Game title, especially this one.

When I first started playing, i was like " what is this?? The graphics dont look as good as the previous game". But they sadi before the released the game that that would be the case. After the first mission, the graphics started matering less and less and by the third mission, i love this game.

Yes there are good and bad things.

The Good: You get a long single player mission covering 3 campaigns that can get very intense at times with alot of units coming at you. You also get alot of units to choose from and a tech tree at which to upgrade your buildings, units (ships, planes, and ground units), and your commander. The story is great and leads up to a grand finale and huge battle that once won, makes you feel good as it can be quite challenging.
There are also many different achievments you can do as well. You have many experimentals you can build as well. And with all your units, can get them experience the more the kill and it increases their health quite a bit which makes them stronger.

The Bad: The graphics leave something to be desired, but they arent that bad. The tech tree takes a long time sometimes, but when you get there, you can really build your units up. and the experimentals r are still fun, but are weaker than the original game which is good and bad. Good because 1 unit can't take out your whole army and base, though they can do some serious damage. Bad becasue they dont have anti air guns, can't build units (most of them anyways), and health isnt as good. The achievements arent all listed (I found them on the internet and would never have figured them all out as one of them was to build nothing bots to fight with. You couldnt even build anti air guns or turrets. Only bots and it was only good for one of the 24 campaigns)

I just think that compared to the first game, this is better (I liked the first one quite a bit too) and you dont have to wait forever to reach tier 3 as you just tech up which seems to be quite a bit faster. And while the graphics lacked, the cutscenes were better on SC2 as was the sound (had problems with sound on SC1. Couldn't here the guns firing from units or turrets) and the problems with game were non existent as well. Not sure why all the hate, but I think this game is better than the first. Hope you SC1 players give it a chance.

This reminds me of Civilization 5 when they tried to revamp the game to do something totally different to appease online players. Check the reviews of that game and how people felt BETRAYED from how many great features were taken out from previous iterations. A gaming franchise only gets so many chances to survive when you put out a product that spits in the face of its' most loyal customers. EA, you better change this game or your bottom line will look very RED very soon.

I honestly think this is a good game. Its definitely different from most harvest moon games. You really have to strive to beat the story line first before anything really fun and addictive happens in the game. But while you are fufilling the requirements for the story line you also befriend your "neighbors" so that helps unlock a lot of things you might have not other wise known about. Such as-- recipes for food, buildings, animal feed, more seeds to grow, trees, the little fairy guys that help you, etc. etc. Then by the time you finish the story line youre ready to really get into building your farm. Which is the whole area in the game. So like--- the world is yours to do what you wish. You make waterfalls (which i Love doing) you make the cliffs- the trees- the whole LAND is yours to control... it is a little slow but have you played the harvest moon games?? Theyre all a little slow. Theyre meant as a game for relaxing and not much concentration. I visited my family at an ACTUAL farm (lol) and played this game the whole time because there was nothing to do... (Im not a farmer in real life, people, but it was a holiday visit.) It was obviously fun enough for me to continue playing for over 45 hours. And im still not married (IN THE GAME) yet (only due to a somewhat flaw in the mining system which is my only REAL complaint.) You get one or two ores per mine and can only hit them one to seven times depending on how long you left it alone. And there are only 8 or 9 mines all together. And you NEED ores to get furniture made to get married. See how it could get annoying when there is a rare one?? Anyway. I WOULD be married and done with the game if it were not for that one flaw. Otherwise GREAT game to pass the time. I recommend it if you like harvest moon because other than the "village" being MIA it is a good addition to the series.

This Game IS NOT ENOUGH! I rented it last week and after playing it for only an hour, I could not get away from the nintendo. I was addicted to this game. The first game, Goldeneye 007 was a major hit because of it's amazing graphics and action scenes. Well, this game is 10X better. The graphics are unbeatable. The graphics look like it's a gamecube game. This addition to Goldeneye features: Better weapons, better missions, better gadgets, better action scenes, and also REAL dialogue.
The game has some of the greatest weapons you can ever shoot with. In Goldeneye, when Bond reloaded the gun, it would disappear. In this game, you see Bond actually reloading the gun. On his hand gun, the P2K, you see him taking out the clip and putting a new one in. I know it's not much but, it is an example of how much more closer it is to real life. Other cool guns are in the game like the .44 Magnum, which is barrel gun that holds 6 bullets with a scope and is EXTREMELY strong. It only takes one shot and your enemey is down for the count. The brother to this hand gun is the Raptor Magnum. This one is as STRONG as the .44 Magnum but instead of a scope, on the bottom of the barrell is a laser beam to aim that you can turn on and off by pressing B+Z. Remember the shotgun in Goldeneye? Well, the shotgun in this game, the Finesse Special 12 is a pump-action shotgun with that holds up to 8 cartridges. THIS IS EXTREMELY STRONG! It is 100X better than the 2 shotguns in Goldeneye. As you shoot one after the other, you see James's hands reload the shotgun. A weapon that wasn't in the first game was the Crossbow. This a really cool weapons. The arrows shoot really far and are really STRONG! For guns that launch grenades and rockets are in the game too. Except one of the grenades/rocket guns has a guide in the bombs. You shoot your rocket and it goes where your aimer went. It does slight turns, etc. There are a couple of the same weapons as the first like the Soviet K47, the Sniper Rifles except a lot STRONGER!
The missions in this game are really action-packed and really thrilling. Really cool missions like: King's ransom where you are in the 007's headquarters and need the find King and initiate lockdowns, turn on the sprinklet system which looks really cool. Underground Train Station where you must free a couple hostages, and defuse a terrorist bomb (be careful, down defuse the bomb too quickly because it'll blow). Remember in the movie where James and Electra were skiing and terrorists were shooting at them? Well there is a mission that does that where you're skiing and there are terrorists shooting at you from little planes, and you have to blow up the tanks at the oil stations as you go down (Don't go too fast or you'll miss and FAIL). One mission that was really hard was Nightwatch. Here's the hard part. In every mission you are shooting people right? In this one, YOU CANNOT SHOOT ANYONE! There are gaurds everywhere and have to avoid CONFRITATION! You have to photograph secret documents in safes, disable the highly equipped security systems, plant phone taps, and goe about 2 miles avoiding all gaurds to defeat the mission. That's a brief description about a few of the missions. There are plenty more to defeat.
The gadgets in this game are 10X better than the first. Jame's watch has several gadgets built into it. The first is a stunner beam that makes your enemies dizzy while it gives you a certain amount of seconds to shoot them depending on how long you stun them for. Like the first game, the laser is in the watch. Also is a couple missions you watch shoots tranquilizer darts that will knock your enemies unconsious for a long time. It's fun to shoot them when they're laid out on the ground. This gadget comes in VERY handy in the Nightwatch mission. As a weapon you can use this as a weapon to avoid confritation. The reason you need this is because when you go in the security booth, there is a gaurd you need to shoot with it as soon as you open the door so he doesn't yell, "Bond is HERE!". Be careful how you use it because there is only about a dozen in your watch and there are no enemies that have ammo for that. Also in the watch is a grapple hook. This is like Batman. In some missions to get to a higher level you need to use this. In cases where you are trapped, look up at the ceiling for a yellow and black stripped section in the beams. For missions like Nightwatch, you have X-Ray glasses that allow you to see through things like Superman. Unlike Superman, you can see through lead. Also night glasses that are made for really dark areas. Like the first game you have your safe crackers, keypad unscramblers, etc.
A cool addition to the graphics is the speech. Instead of the first game where you only saw dialogue sentences, in this one when somebody speaks, you hear their real voices from the movie like James, Christmas Jones, Electra, Moneypenny, Valentine, Renaud, Gaurds, Scientists, Airport Control room employees, etc. That is a really effect that was added into this game.
The game is totally 100X better than Goldeneye 007. Better weapons, gadgets, graphics, speech, and missions. This game throws the Goldeneye 007 game right out of the water. You must give a praise the the makers of the game. If you ignore this game, you don't know what you're missing out on.

James Bond is on the run again chasing after villanous enemies through the top of snowy mountains, nuclear plants, underwater, through Paris, Japan and even into space. This James Bond game, "Nightfire" is the best James Bond game to date and beats "Goldeneye 64" and "The World is Not Enough" by a long-shot. James Bond will take through the wildest adventure you've ever been on where you have to shoot down planes from the air, drive underwater in the Aston Martin V12 Vanquish, chase enemies through the street of Paris, travel into space and stop a nuclear launch, and chase enemies through the highest skyscraper in Japan. The weapons and the details of them are phenomenal and the gadgets are the best ever.
There are 12 stunning and amazing missions where you must complete a numerous amount of outstanding mission objectives. These are the best missions in the game and a description.
2. The Exchange:
Enter the enemy Drake's castle in the snowy mountains by passing all the security guards and then while in the castle at the party, spy on Drake's secret meeting and then escape with Dominique down the mountain in a gondola and shoot the helicopter chasing you with the ever famous AT-420 Sentinel Guided Missile Launcher.
3. Alpine Escape:
Go down the rest of the mountain with Dominique in one of Drake's highly advanced snowmobiles where you are on top while she drives and you shoot the snowmobiles chasing you with a powerful machine gun that has an alternate fire of grenades.

Save Drake's ex-trusted man Mayhew is being attacked by Drake's assassins and you must save Mayhew's servants and escort him to safety.
7. Chain Reaction:
