After the Avengers game, which was absolutely horrible, I had a hard time deciding whether to get this until I saw a few reviews saying this was not like that game. Luckily those reviews were correct.

Another thing to overcome is that these aren’t the MCU characters but they are loosely based on them as far as how they behave and talk to an extent. It was done pretty well. Obviously this isn’t the MCU, so it exists on its own lore-wise but you’ll see a lot of familiar people, places, and Easter eggs.

So what’s good? The story is good and was longer than I expected. It took me somewhere around 25-30 hours to play through (I was very thorough in searching and listening to dialogue). Then I did a second play through on NG+ to get the rest of the collectibles. Overall, the story arc was interesting and I never got bored.

The battle system is good enough. The game will start to tweak your abilities and such every few chapters so it doesn’t get too stale and you can unlock about 15 extra abilities for Peter. It’s very simplified and that’s actually OK. Most battles come down to finding a way to stagger an enemy to do maximum damage and they all have an elemental weakness of some kind. You can also give teammates commands and tell them to do attacks. It’s a good system that can probably be improved on if there’s a second game.

The game’s choices do have consequences for major events but for the other 90%, I don’t think they do. And if they have an impact (even if it says someone appreciates you for taking their side), it’s unclear how that affected anything. Again, this system could be built on to be even better in the future.

The music is also great. A band recorded some original metal music and it’s actually pretty good. Of course there are also plenty of other actual artists and songs. It’s all well done.

What are some bad things? It’s still a little glitchy (in January 2022). I had 2-3 hard crashes and some other instances of the scene locking up and requiring me to restart a checkpoint or the game. The auto-save is very generous though so you never lose progress.

The use of the words ‘flark’ and ‘scut’. I understand they can’t drop 4-letter words and not get an MA rating or even be allowed by Marvel, but these words are used no less than 10,000,000 times and it gets … exhausting.

The battles do get a little repetitive toward the finale when you’re just fighting wave after wave. I feel like this game has established a great baseline and it’ll be easier to expand and diversify the battle experience if they make another game.

Overall, I really liked the game and would look forward to a sequel. Rating it 4 out of 5 but I’d say it’s a solid 4.5 out of 5. My criticisms are pretty minor.

I heard that this was one of the best games ever made. I got about 20 hours in and I just don’t want to play anymore. I’m guessing 15 of the 20 hours were just spent walking and doing inventory management to try to keep stock of weapons that break every few hits. And when you do get a good weapon, you never use it because you don’t want it to break. It’s just maddeningly boring and tedious. There is a lot of menuing in this game. Can’t you just give me hearts when I kill something? And rupees? This isn’t a secret formula here.

People rave about the open, vast world. Okay. Have you played any other games lately? This isn’t that uncommon. And who cares how vast it is when there’s no content? Pretty much all the same enemies and just different terrains. The devs put lots of tedious obstacles in to slow you down more to give the impression that there is content (stamina, water, mountains, the same kind of shrine puzzle over and over, etc). There isn’t much to it. People who put over 100 hours into this undoubtedly spent 60+% of that just wandering around doing nothing. That’s not content, it’s the illusion of it.

I also don’t want to cook. There’s no guidance on this in-game either. Want to make something? Good luck. Spend 30 minutes trying to cook random things and see what pops. Why? Because it’s apparently an RPG now. I need a potion to protect against 3-4 elements, boost my stamina, defense, attack, or something else to keep track of. Oh, that’s snow? Better go cook something that’ll let you slowly walk through that without dying. It’s honestly hard enough remembering the 20 different buttons and quick cycle menus and now you want me to find fires to cook over to make sure I have a dozen or more potions for every element or situation? Good lord. And if you use items and then die? They’re gone when you continue at your previous save point. Just *chef’s kiss*.

Manage inventory, cook, heal, die in one hit, reload, repeat. Every few hours you might progress something in the story before you have to walk another 20-30 minutes. Not that it matters since every enemy in the game short of a blob one-hit kills me. You just have to try to run, but you can only run for 2 seconds and naturally everything in the game is also faster than you. I spent hours and hours trying to get to towers and shrines. Everything has to be a puzzle theme to try to climb the towers. Why? Don’t know. Discovering key items and stuff? Never happened to me. Dungeons? Don’t seem to exist, but I don’t know. I never found one. Why do you climb so slowly? Or swim so slowly? Why can I only run for literally 2 seconds? Don’t know.

Also why is the crouch tap so sensitive? If I put up my shield and try to move, 9 out of 10 times I press the joystick a LITTLE too hard and crouch and I’m dead. And rain? Great game mechanic. Since you can’t climb in rain (and all you do is walk and climb), you can just sit the controller down and do something else until it stops. Probably a potion to sleep to pass the time but you’d never know how to make it.

I was hoping for a Zelda game and got some weird Death Stranding simulator. This isn’t Zelda at all. At least Death Stranding, for all the criticism, took a game mechanic and perfected it.

Actually. You know what this reminds me of? Assassin’s Creed puzzles, which are the worst things in the entire series besides their rock stacking challenges in Valhalla. You know how there are like 4,000 chests behind a similar barred door puzzle? You always have to find a way in when there’s a locked door but there are only 3-4 variations of the puzzle. By the 100th one you sort of go into a rage and just ask the game why you can’t just go into the door and get the chest without a puzzle for once? This is what it’s like. You hike for half an hour to find a shrine or tower, but it can’t just be walked into. You’ll need to spend half an hour devising a plan to get by 20 enemies or over some thatch by slowly climbing a mountain for an eternity. Eventually you either get it or just give up the hour of your life you’ve just wasted. I wasted entire nights just trying to walk to a tower off in the distance. After 2 hours you realize you did nothing in that time besides get to the tower. This isn’t fun to me. Maybe it is to someone else? I mean, it obviously is fun to people based on the ratings.

After 20 hours, my enjoyment has gone to zero and I can’t waste anymore of my time on it. I just don’t get it. I just want dungeons, actual bosses, key items, just a traditional Zelda game. Maybe I’m not the target demographic anymore. Also, the music isn’t that great. I’m not sure what all the fuss is about. It’s basically non-existent compared to a game like Final Fantasy.

This franchise has fallen a long, long way since A Link to the Past and Ocarina of Time. I would say in my ~30 years of gaming, this is one of the least enjoyable games I’ve ever spent money on. No exaggeration. I cannot think of any other game I bought that I disliked this much and, in the last 10-15 years, didn’t at least complete the main story.

I’ve had every GT game since the original. I’m going to leave the whole micro transaction / bad payouts / insanely expensive modding and cars out of this review. They might actually fix some of that.

No, I’d like to seriously understand how the car line-up largely hasn’t changed since like GT5. Aside from what seems like hundreds of race-spec models given recent model years, the entire car line up is largely unchanged in the last 3 games. The newest actual street models are mainly 2010-2016. I saw a few 2019 and 2020 cars but it’s only a couple. What did you work on for all these years? It’s seriously like a game that was designed for 2017. Again, it’s the exact same cars they’ve always had for several games! C8 Corvette? Nope. New Mustangs? Nope. Any supercar post 2016 or so? Nope. Even the Lexus LFA seems to be gone. I was just blown away to (finally) unlock the ability to actually buy a new car only to see it’s 95% carry over from GT5.

What else? The soundtrack is terrible. I guess they decided to no longer license good driving music. It’s all just generic elevator sounding music. Some weird remixes of classical music thrown in there. Extremely disappointing in that regard. Even the weird instrumental Bring Me the Horizon song from the trailers is nowhere to be found.

Last in my complaints, it took close to 5 hours to unlock a handful of races. I want to just be able to race all the tracks and buy whatever cars I want. It seems like it will take a very very long time to get the tracks all open.

For positives, the game looks great and feels like a GT game when you’re racing. But as a negative, the game just hasn’t evolved. GT5 was arguably the peak and every release since has just been a clone of that game more or less. Same AI, same damage physics.

Add in real music or let us integrate Spotify or something. Update your car roster to something from this past decade at least. Unlock the game and let us just race and tune freely without having to do these silly menu challenges. It’s all just so disappointing especially after this long wait.

How can anyone NOT give this game 5 stars? Knights of the Old Republic is a near perfect role-playing experience!
This is how role-playing games should be done; open-ended gameplay, deep customization options, superb cinematics, and extreme length! I've spent 40 hours taking my time through the game and I'm not even halfway finished! But I simply can't wait until then to review it.
Other than Rogue Leader and the upcoming Rebel Strike for the Gamecube, Knights is the best Star Wars game ever made. The attention to detail is astounding. Star Wars fans will find every character, sound effect, and image faithful to the movies and literature. The camera is never a problem since you have full control over it. Animation is the weakest part of Knights. The frames per second stay pretty much constant all the time so there's no transition to notice. But you can tell the animation is subpar compared to most new games. It never bothered me.
I found Knights to be very non-linear. Players are given a great deal of freedom to do as they wish in plot, action and interaction with the game's characters. Once you get your spaceship you can select which planet you want to explore, and you can leave almost anytime you want in order to visit a different one. Dialog in the game is handled by giving the player choices of what to say. Some of the responses are truly hilarious. But take what you say seriously, it can have a major effect on your main character's progress. All of your characters can be customized greatly, from their statistics to their clothing. When you slap a piece of armor on someone it shows them wearing it on the screen at all times. There are endless numbers of tools and weapons at your disposal to further outfit your team, although certain people can't use certain items (Wookies can't wear armor). Lightsabers and Force powers make themselves available eventually and boy, are they ever satisfying! If you plan on using light side Force powers a lot be kind and helpful in your adventures. If you want to use dark side powers easily just be mean to everyone you encounter. The scope of choices in gameplay is impressive.
To keep things fresh there are a few minigames strewn throughout your adventure. I liked the Pazaak card game. It was easy to understand and proved to be a fun way to build credits even if it's mostly a matter of luck to win.
The music is what you would expect from a Star Wars experience. You'll hear some familiar tunes but most is brand new stuff that fits on-screen events well. Definitely no complaints there.
No other game I know of does such an entertaining job of ingrossing you in what it's like to be a Jedi than this one. Of course if you just want to be a Han Solo, blaster-toting scoundrel that's your choice, too. That's what makes this game so fun: FREEDOM. As far as I'm concerned this is an essential purchase for X-Box owners.

The sequel to the greatest weapon-based vs. game satisfies, for the most part, gamers' expectations. Soul Calibur II really is a marvel to behold; fluid animation, beautiful scenery, orchestrated music, perfect sound effects, and deep gameplay.
The X-Box version, for my money, is the best one. It has the best graphics, the shortest load times, and the coolest character. Yeah, Link has a bigger fan base but Spawn is just more of a badass, and that's the kind of character I want in Soul Calibur II.
When all is said and done however, what you have here is more of the same from the previous game. There are a few new characters but only three of them are fundamentally unique, including Spawn. The arenas now have walls which the fighters can be slammed up against. A new Weapon Master Mode replaces the Adventure Mode from Soul Calibur in which most of the hidden stuff can be unlocked (Weapon Master is a little easier than Adventure was, thank God). There's a larger variety in costumes and weapons for the characters, overall. Inexplicably, the Gallery pictures in Soul Calibur II are actually far fewer than in Soul Calibur! And that's it for differences between the two games. I would have liked to see more innovation in Soul Calibur II but I had too much fun playing to care.
The only real problem I have with the game is the females. Their costumes show way too much skin and certain body parts "jiggle" if you know what I mean. If I want to see that kind of thing I'll play Dead Or Alive. There's enough sexual suggestiveness everywhere else, I don't need it in Soul Calibur II, thanks.
Fortunately the pros far outweigh the cons. Any vs. game fan would be crazy not to add Soul Calibur II to their game library.

As the first true sequel to any Final Fantasy game, FFX-2 is groundbreaking. I hope Square-Enix continues with this lucrative trend. To fully appreciate FFX-2 you must be familiar with FFX.
Any good RPG has compelling characters. FFX-2's cast is...to put it mildly, odd. Their antics range from absurdly stupid to very cool. Overall the dialogue and voice-overs are done well. Voices for the recurring characters sound the same as they did in FFX, which pleased me greatly.
Depending on how quick you want to get through the game, completion time can take anywhere from 10-150 hours! Most areas in FFX-2 are completely optional. Replaying a second time is necessary to see everything, just be sure to choose new options within the story. Luckily the function of continuing a new game with almost everything acquired in the first game makes such re-exploration painless. More RPGs need this feature!
A revamped battle system makes gameplay more fun than in most other Final Fantasy releases. It takes the best aspects of FFVII and FF Tactics' combat and adds a faster pace. I love it. Utilizing the wide variety of Garment Grids, Dresspheres and accessories available never became tiresome for me.
The visuals aren't anything special; pretty much unchanged from FFX. The same can be said for the sound effects. FFX-2's music is a mixed bag, though. The title theme features one of the most enchanting pieces of music I've ever heard in a game. A few other samples are also impressive, matching the onscreen events admirably. But I found the rest of the soundtrack to be unimpressive.
The lack of new environments and enemies is a tad disappointing. 75% of everything you encounter has been seen already in FFX in some form or another.
As you're probably heard, the females in FFX-2 appear to be immodest where clothing is concerned. Rikku's standard 'uniform' consists of little more than a thong bikini! Obviously the developers thought that forcing some sexuality into the all-female main cast would keep male players interested. Sad.
Fortunately there is some real substance under the pop-singing and temporary silliness. Those who take their time uncovering all the game has to offer will be treated to a rewarding Final Fantasy experience. The COMPLETE ending, should the proper prerequisites be fulfilled, is especially satisfying.
For FFX fans, this is a MUST BUY.

As a major fan of Front Mission 3 for the PlayStation I was excited upon hearing the news that Square-Enix was making a sequel to my favorite single-player tactical-strategy game. The only thing missing from Front Mission 3's excellence was great graphics. With the arrival of Front Mission 4 on the PlayStation2 I thought the rough-graphics problem would be solved and I'd have the perfect game.
Unfortunately life has a way of playing dirty tricks. Oh sure, the graphics are much improved over FM3 with greater detail and far smoother animation. But the colors are downright bland! Also, many areas in the game appear overly dark, making it a challenge to view the screen easily unless the lights are off. I suspect the developers were going for realism here.
The length of the game disappointed me as well. For the amount of time spent working on your characters' skills and statistics the number of actual plot-developing missions is minuscule. There are only 29 stages in all! By comparison, FM3 contained a staggering 128 stages played out through two scenarios! Admittedly, FM4's stages are bigger and take longer to complete, and there are simulator battles to play. But FM3 had simulator battles, too!
Now that the bad is out of the way let me let you what was good about FM4:
Graphics - already touched on this. MUCH better than FM3 except for the colors & lack of lighting.
Sound - the most refined part of FM4. Heavy, realistic, perfect. Great use of bass!
Music - very appropriate for the events onscreen. High quality.
Speech - the main characters now speak in select cut scenes and the voice-overs are extremely well done. The accents and voice tones are very accurate to their respective nationalities. No bad acting here!
Battle System - more involved than in the last game. The Link system adds a fun new level of strategy to the gameplay. New specialized backpacks increase combat options.
Customization - a slight increase in variety of weapons and parts. Better colorization options but the blandness + darkness at times makes it almost moot.
Control - takes some getting used to, but adequate. In a tactical, non-twitch game like this it's not a detriment.
Battle Maps - daytime shifting and weather effects add new depth to missions. Battlefields are significantly larger than in FM3.
Character Skills - no more randomness in acquiring new battle skills to help towards victory! Instead characters buy skills they want as they become available! The challenge is getting the funds needed to afford them.
And finally, FM4's greatest improvement over FM3...the chaotic E-mail/virtual net system is gone!
I'd have to say FM4 doesn't match the gaming experience FM3 gave. Don't get me wrong...it's a fantastic game for as long as it lasts. The plot is solid. Just don't expect as huge a jump in quality as I did or you'll be disappointed.

This is a good effort on the part of Konami. They thought to spice things up a bit by including a forced first-person view mode for key moments in the game. Unfortunately it's not used to maximum effect. Ultimately Silent Hill 4 only offers more of the same, and that's disappointing to those of us used to it.

With the available subject matter you'd think Konami would put together a more chilling experience. Instead we're treated to the same visually compelling yet fright-limited gameplay the last Silent Hills offered. This series is known for it's creepy atmosphere. That's good, but a great survival-horror game combines atmosphere with frightful action, and that's where Silent Hill slips up. I can only recall one experience in Silent Hill 4 which really sent shivers up my spine, and nothing actually happened in it! Too often does the game make you think something terrifying is about to happen but doesn't. Expecting a sudden, monstrous noise in the background to scare players doesn't cut it anymore.

The storyline in these games has always been an issue for me. The plot, while interesting, just doesn't seem to congeal well as you progress through the game. The other Silent Hills also suffered from this. Any game that requires you to search the internet for a better understanding of it's storyline has problems. And what's with the difficulty in seeing multiple endings this time? Two of the four possible endings require keeping your partner character healthy throughout the entire time she's with you...an extremely frustrating task. I never had so much trouble viewing all the endings to a Silent Hill game.

With all that being said, I had a good time playing Silent Hill 4. I liked the voice acting, the first-person viewing mode, and the few changes they made to the play style. I just wish Konami would tweak the series' weaknesses to give us players a more terrifying experience. Then we'd have a perfectly gruesome, mature horror game.

Knights Of The Old Republic II: The Sith Lords brings us much of what made the first game so great. Nonlinear gameplay, gripping story, interesting characters, high degree of customization, it's all there.

Some things have been improved. Characters can now be raised to level 30 instead of 20, so gaining experience induces a faster sense of progress. There are more items to collect and use, more upgrade options, more force powers and more party members available.

I was most impressed with the level of depth the main characters displayed. The graphics were adequate; nothing too amazing. The voice acting was acceptional and the music was of high quality.

However, there is a sense that the developers rushed this product out prematurely. There are a significant number of gliches throughout the game...much more than in KOTOR I. Maybe it's because this game is from a different developer. There are misspellings, dialogue repeats, and unresolved quest issues. While these glitches don't detract from the overall enjoyment of playing they're enough to annoy some people.

Like KOTOR I, this game allows you to choose light or dark paths to follow. Many elements in the game change depending on which side you're on. Because of this there is high incentive to replay the game all over. After first playing The Sith Lords as a Jedi Consular I'm looking forward to experiencing the adventure again, this time as a Sith Marauder.

While good, KOTOR II just doesn't appear as polished as KOTOR I. If they had spent more time tweaking the imperfections we'd have a real winner.

The other reviewers are spot-on with their analysis of Katamari Damacy. The game's presentation is absurd, it's characters are inane and the action is just plain silly. Yet, despite these qualities (or perhaps, somehow, because of them) Katamari Damacy is ridiculously fun to experience!

There just aren't many games like this one. The goal is to roll this sphere called a Katamari over objects which stick to it. Most of the stages have you attempting to make the sphere as large as you can within the time limit. Other stages have you collecting only certain items within the time limit. Such uniqueness in gameplay deserves more exposure and be should be cherished by more gamers.

The music is worth some praise. It's inoffensive, pleasant and pretty catchy. Heck, EVERYTHING about this game is catchy.

The only character with any personality is this 'King of all Cosmos' guy. His design has to be seen to be believed. It's like the developers got together and said, "Okay, how can we make this guy appear as retarded as humanly possible?" Seriously.

I should point out that my copy of Katamari Damacy has a flaw where the PS2 takes about ten times as long as it should to load data from the game. I haven't been able to test it on other systems. Personally, I think I just got a defective disk.

Add Katamari Damacy's low price to the mix and it's impossible to go wrong here. Give it a try. Just don't let the zaniness turn you off.

I really wanted to fall in love with the Razer Wolverine V2 Chroma controller. While it brings to the table some great tech and quality of life features, it also has a very frustrating performance flaw.

In true Razor fashion, the controller is built like a tank. The plastic-rubberized shape just feels great in my medium-sized hands. I think that it would withstand a couple of angry moments (not that I go through any). The cord is well braided, long enough, and not too stiff. The Chroma RGB lighting is pretty cool and as every gamer knows, RGB makes you a better gamer, right?

The overall design does not deviate that much from the original Xbox design as far as ergonomics. The layout is slightly more spread, and the shoulder buttons demand a claw grip in my case. The buttons underneath and the additional shoulder buttons feel are a bit awkward to reach and I usually don’t remap my buttons anyway. Having said that, the buttons have this amazing satisfying click when pressing them, making them feel as if I am clicking a premium mouse. The shoulder buttons feel smooth enough and there’s a feature to change the travel, making them activate faster with less pressure. The D-Pad has one of the best feels and responsiveness I have ever tried. The analog sticks, however, leave a lot to be desired as they stick out too far. I like that you can change the analog stick heads, but it does not make it feel better in my opinion.

The Razer app provides a decent amount of customization for RGB, remapping, rumble, and sensitivity.

When it comes to gameplay, the controller buttons are highly responsive and accurate. I never felt like I missed a click when it counted. The shoulder buttons have a decent response at the default setting, and I really did not see any real benefit to change the pressure depth. Having said that, and coming from the original, there was a significant adjustment curve when it came to the option buttons.

My biggest complaint, and it’s a big one for me, is that the analog sticks have a large orbital rotation that negatively affected my competitive first-person-shooter sessions and high-speed F1 driving. Even when I adjusted the dead zone and sensitivity (through both app and in-game), I found myself overcompensating and trying to get used to the floaty movements. When milliseconds counted, the controller did not follow my reaction time, causing some rage-inducing losses. My K/D ratio suffered and as soon as I went back to a cheaper wired controller I have, I instantly noticed that my gameplay was back to normal. Hopefully, Razer will release a firmware update to fix this.

Having said all this, I still consider the Wolverine V2 Chroma a step in the right direction. While I will not use the controller for competitive gameplay, I will certainly use it for leisure and adventure games on my PC instead of the Xbox. Considering that this controller comes at such a hefty price, it was disappointing that it did not become my daily driver.

The TB Recon 200 G2 is an interesting headset due to one specific feature I have not seen in a while. The headphones’ design is not terribly unique as they look like any other TB headset out there. The matte black finish repels smudges and fingerprints effectively. I do like the carbon fiber-like accents. Being almost entirely plastic, they are rather light and surprisingly well built. The headband is flexible enough and there’s good swiveling on the cups. The fabric pads are thankfully removable. The mic can be flipped up and down with good resistance and stays in place firmly. The buttons, controls, USB-C port, and wire all are on the left side, and personally, I would’ve liked them to be spread between both cups.

The R200G2s are very comfortable in my experience. There’s enough clamping force to keep the headset in place and the super-soft memory earpads allow wearing glasses with no problem. The headband barely touches my head and did not cause any sore spots. My ears did not get hot, even after 3-hour sessions in a warm environment. Good job.

I appreciate that the volume and mic volume rockers are responsive and in a good spot. Speaking of the mic, flipping it up automatically mutes you and down unmutes you, which feels natural. I also like that the microphone is more on the side and not in front, taking it completely out of view (and even drink while in the down position). The boom mic works as you’d expect from wired mics. People heard me loud and clear, there was a little bit of fullness to my voice, and the variable mic monitoring allows for more natural conversations. No complaints here.

Now the reason this has a USB-C charging port is that the R200G2s feature amplified audio. As mentioned earlier, this is the one thing I have not seen in a while. If you want an amp, you must have the right audio card on your PC or have an external amp ready. The battery will give about 12 hours of amplification, which is all most of us need. Just in case juice runs out, you can still use them as traditional headphones.

But how do they sound? Well, there are 3 different sound signatures, depending on the mode you select. Without amplification, they’re not all that loud, which is expected, the sound is well balanced, leaning slightly on a warm signature. The bass is still felt, is quite punchy but somewhat blunt. The mids and highs are well represented and there is little harshness. Everything is acceptably clear, with good channel separation and soundstage.

Now, there are 2 amplification modes - Xbox and PS. On Xbox mode, everything becomes much louder, and the sound more robust. The bass does get a little bit loose and there’s a lot of sub-woofer-like bass, which comes too close to overpowering the mids and highs. I found this sound signature a bit sloppy, and while soundstage seems to be sparser, clarity suffered. However, to my surprise, the PS mode is louder but lowered the sub-bass and added much more impact and definition to bass. The mids came a bit more forward, and the treble was pushed higher without being harsh or fatiguing. This affected the overall soundstage quite nicely. Sure, there are certain games where the bass may cloud important sounds like footsteps and gunshots, and in such cases, I simply turn the amp off. However, for literally everything else (casual games, movies, music, etc.), the PS amp mode adds a superior level of excitement.

In the end, you can tell that I am enjoying the RG200G2s. Sure, one must put up with the cable and charging it from time to time, but at the current price, this is a no-brainer.

First of all, I am really digging the white and black aesthetics of the Kaira X- it matches my PS5, Xbox Series S, and OLED Switch. The physical design is almost the same as the Kaira Pro wireless, with the only difference being the wire and permanent mic. It is made almost entirely out of plastic but seems quite sturdy. The headband is not as flexible as I would’ve liked, however. The hinges swivel easily but I would’ve liked the headset to be foldable for portability’s sake. The mic is flexible and stays put. The braided 3.5mm cable is quite strong and has a good length. I also appreciate the 90-degree angle 3.5mm connector.

Although it is not the lightest, it is still quite comfortable. Even if the headband is not that flexible, the clamping force is not too tight, and the memory foam cloth-covered earpads feel soft around the ear. There’s no ear rubbing as my medium-sized ears fit completely inside. The headband also has some fabric, and I experienced slight fatigue on top after a couple of hours, but fortunately no soreness. Also, because the earpads are breathable, my ears did not get hot or sweaty.

The microphone worked just as expected. My voice came in full, loud, and clear. Thanks to the flexibility of the mic, I was able to bring it closer when using a quiet voice and still be heard. There’s also a mute button that is easily accessible. The volume rocker is easy to use and stays at whatever level it is set.

The best part of my experience is that the 50mm drivers deliver powerful sound. While the bass is not as “boomy” as other mainstream headsets, I found it to be impactful and precise. There’s also plenty of sub-bass (subwoofer-like sound), albeit subtle and controlled. I was glad that the midrange was present and not as recessed, making vocals, rhythm instruments, background music, and dialogue quite clear. The treble is high, but not too sharp or fatiguing. Overall, I found the audio signature pleasant when needed, or exciting most of the time. It also helps that there is good channel separation and decent soundstage. This is even better when using Dolby or Windows Sonic. I had a good experience, especially when playing first-person shooters.

Speaking of Windows, the Kaira X can be used on any device that has a 3.5mm jack. I tried it on my PC’s (Windows and iOS), PS5 (via controller), phone, Switch, and of course, my Xbox Series S (via controller). All worked just as well and again, I appreciate that I can control the volume from the headset, without any software controls.

At the current price, I think it’s a steal. Fantastic sound, good looks, strong build, a decent mic, and versatility earn the Kaira X an easy recommendation from me.

The premise is easy: just stick the USB into the second port of your PS Classic and that's that. Well, it's not that easy. Once the initial automatic setup is done, and I saw some cool graphics while doing so, I ended looking at a menu that, if you are not familiar with emulator software, you'd be completely lost. Fortunately, I am familiar with the RetroArch interface, and I made myself familiar with the options and content.

As far as ROMs are concerned, I am pleased with the quantity and the titles found in there. There are also plenty of cores or emulators available so that you'd be sure to find the best one to use. There are many systems available, including Atari, Commodore, GB, GBA, GBC, Genesis, GG, SCD, PSX, etc. Again, if you are not familiar with emulation, then you'd be somewhat disappointed that not every title runs as it should, and some require some tinkering.

One cool thing is that my 8BitDo N30Pro controller worked perfectly, which is better than the original classic controller.

Although I was disappointed that there is no easy-to-navigate menu, I found a lot of value for the price. I will recommend getting acquainted with RetroArch menus to make the best out of the item.

I was so excited to start playing some N64 on Nintendo Online. Their claim that it "works" on the Switch is true since the console will recognize it. Unfortunately, the buttons are not mapped properly at all, as the C button mapping is all over the place, and there is no START button. So, I tried to re-map the controllers from the menu, and to my dismay, you cannot assign the up and right analog actions to the C buttons on the controller. So, you are basically stuck using the Z buttons to activate those actions. While it is a slight improvement from the original controller, I cannot shake the disappointment.

I am hoping there is some sort of update to fix this as with the wireless version, but I will not hold my breath for too long. Maybe it works on a PC, but since I am not much for emulation, this is not applicable to me. Still, for the price paid, I don't feel that bad.

This HDMI cable is certainly much thicker than the original. It is built like a tank and seems it will last for a very long time. However, this makes it less flexible. It will hang a bit if you have side ports. I certainly appreciate the 10ft length. Now I can place my PS5 on the opposite side of my 75” TV’s port. The connector fits well and stays securely.

The performance is as expected, which is great. I was able to play titles at full 4K 60hz and 120Hz on the one game that allows it (usually 1080p/dynamic res). There was no distortion while watching 4K HDR content and eHRC was detected every time.

I am happy with this cable’s overall quality, and the price is rather competitive at a good value. Definitely recommended.

Being a “renewed” unit, the headset arrived well packaged in official packaging. After a thorough inspection, I found the headset in excellent condition -just like new.

Personally, I find the typical Turtle Beach design pleasing to the eye, and the Stealth 600 G2 is no exception. They are mostly made of plastic, which makes them light, but also makes them feel a bit fragile. The headband is flexible enough, but I wouldn’t push it. The part I worry about most is the swivels and headband extensions. The good thing is that I treat all my units with respect. Surprisingly, I noticed no creaking whatsoever.

The 600 G2 is quite comfortable. There are plenty of adjustment points, and the headband extends pretty far. The padded headband does a good job in preventing soreness and the clothed covered ear pads are super soft, Even though my ears slightly touched the drivers, they are covered by a soft mesh. Since I wear thick glasses, the Prospect design helped, as I did not experience any issues on the sides.

The controls and microphone are all located on the left cup and are easy to get used to. There, you can control everything from sound/mic volume, EQ mode, power, and pairing. There is also a USB-C port for charging. I appreciate that the mic gets stashed neatly away when not in use. I prefer a volume rocker instead of buttons, and I like that there is a stopping point when hitting min/max volume.

Pairing with my Xbox Series S was as easy as pairing any controller via direct-connect. I experience no hiccups or funky sounds. However, coverage is not too great as walking outside of the room immediately caused issues. This is not a problem if you are using a dongle on your PC, which unfortunately is not provided with the unit. Speaking of PC, you can update the firmware and adjust settings when hooked up via the USB-C cable.

The sound quality coming from the large 50mm drivers is great, depending on the content and EQ presets, which can be changed by the side button. On the default “Signature sound” mode, the sound is on the even side, but still warm. There is good bass, slightly recessed mids, and subdued treble. The channel separation is distinct, and there is a rather modest soundstage. The “Bass Boost” mode obviously adds a bit more sub-bass, but I found it too muddy, especially at higher volumes. The “Bass + Treble Boost” mode delivers an aggressive “V” shape sound, but surprisingly, the mids were not as recessed as I would’ve expected. And lastly, the “Vocal Boost” mode brings out the midrange forward. I found that the “Bass + Treble Boost” mode provided the most exciting experience with most content. Paired with “Dolby ATMOS” or “Windows Sonic”, the explosions and car engines were booming, the dialogue was clear, and the highs were pristine.

Then there is the “Super Hearing” mode that is activated by quickly pressing the power button. All this mode does is boosts the treble significantly and expands channel separation and soundstage. This is great for competitive games like Halo, CS:GO, PUBG, etc., when figuring out where opponents may be, but in reality, I found it was a bit gimmicky and makes any other game, video, or music sound harsh and fatiguing after a little while.

The microphone is quite good. My voice came in deep and clear, and there was no distortion. I would not do a professional podcast with it, but it’s great for gaming and that occasional video call. The headset allows for mic monitoring, which is convenient when I want to check that my voice is not too loud. I appreciate the “lift mic” action for muting and the beeps that let you know it is being activated.

In the end, I am enjoying the Stealth 600 Gen 2. The sound options are superb, connectivity is stable, and the mic is above average for this price range. Plus, it matches my XB Series S console. My only concern is the build quality -especially for being a “renewed” unit. Since the warranty is not too shabby, I would recommend giving them a try and save a few bucks.

What a pleasing surprise the MOGA XP7-X Plus (what a mouthful!) turned out to be. I really came with no expectations. The build quality is solid. I've been a platform gamer since they came about in the 1980's, so I didn't hesitate at all to preorder Astro Bot when I found out a full release game was in the making. There's no doubt this loveable little robot will become a mascot for the PS4 and win over platform gaming fans. With a very similar feel I've been used to on other consoles, experiencing this type of gaming in VR is phenomenal. While your character is running, jumping & swimming all around you, Astro Bot makes great use of the player by making you interact with objects virtually as well. In the game your presence is transformed a larger robot that is controlling the little astro robot and the end result is a very lovable duo that rebuilds their damaged spaceship and ultimately saves the entire colony from evil. Each level requires you collect coins, find hidden secret passages and items, rescue fellow robots, and adds special power-up items to help you on your journey such as a spray nozzle, grappling hook & cable, machine gun, ninja star or flashlight for example. Each power-up is activated with the center panel on the PS4 controller and adds a great sense of being present in the game.

The soundtracks are very catchy and each level's visuals are dazzling, truly immersing you in a fantasy wonderland to explore. Each world has a boss to beat, and they are large and intimidating. Bringing down your supersized foe being such a tiny robot is greatly satisfying to watch, all while your little guy runs around you dodging fireballs and enemy strike but yet still taking a quick moment to check back with you by giving a cute little wave and smile.

I consider myself an expert platform gamer and was able to casually play through all the levels in around 4-5 hours, sometimes revisiting a few of them to try to find additional robots to rescue. Even though I managed to beat the game in one sitting, I found that I had unlocked a lot more challenges I need to revisit along with the need to still revisit a few worlds to find the last few robots and chameleons. Replay value is there, and for the price, it's still $20 cheaper than other platform games out there. I do look forward to playing this game over and over again, and hope there will either be a sequel or downloadable content in the near future. An absolutely stunning game in all aspects!

Firewall is a 4 vs 4 tactical shooting multiplayer that pushes VR shooters to the limit. My first time trying the game felt a little overwhelming with all the options and weapon loadouts, but after a few games and some helpful players assistance, I was able to get it all figured out quickly and became a team asset. Lots of gun and equipment unlocks available, along with characters, skills, and dossier. I love the fact that once you buy attachments for one gun, it can be used on all future guns you buy instead of having to unlock a laser sight for each weapon for example.

[GRAPHICS & AUDIO] The graphics and sound are pretty impressive and accurate. Being that you need to be a bit tactical to survive, hearing footsteps, gunshots etc, and knowing where they are coming from is crucial. Firewall definitely brings it to life and puts you in the action with realistic immersion.

[CONTROL & FEEL] Playing this with the aim controller is the best option in my opinion, so if you don't already own it, I recommend buying the Firewall bundle. Holding the life-size rifles and guns just feels right with the aim controller. After a few menu tweaks to turn on smooth turning and disabling the vignette, I felt the realism really set in. While the camera does drift between matches, I seldom ever have an issue with it drifting during gameplay in battle. I usually hold the OPTIONS button before the round starts and I'm good to go. Physically leaning forward to peek around a corner in VR then unloading a magazine into an enemy while looking down your sight is exhilarating.

[GAMEPLAY] Each round starts with your team either being the attackers or the defenders. As the attackers, your goal is to locate 2 access points and enable them, then get to the defended laptop location and hack it. Some defending enemy players may have equipment that assists in their defense such as jammers, which are devices that must be located within a certain distance of the laptop that must be destroyed by the attackers before they can access the laptop. When you have been shot or downed by an enemy you will start to bleed out and the timer starts to run out before you are eliminated. During this time, your teammates can revive you, but the enemy also has the opportunity to finish you off as well. Sticking together in groups of two is a great way to cover each other, but sometimes branching off and flanking the enemy can also prove to be a fun and successful tactic. Team communication is a major necessity, and adds a great feel to the game as well.

[CONS] The game doesn't come without a few flaws, but I feel that future patches will fix them without issues. Just about every time I turn on my system and try to join a public match, I get the "floating Jesus" glitch. It puts you in the lobby on the floor and you see a floating soldier off to your right with his arms out. I have to force-close the game and start it over. After that, I'll enter public matches about 3-4 times with other people, only to get disconnected each time. Usually 5th or 6th try is a charm, and I'm good to go after that. Also, the host of each match is the 1st person to enter a match, so when that person decides to leave, it ends the game for everyone. Host-migration needs to be addressed. I've played some matches with people that want to be obnoxious and there's no way to mute or vote to boot them. This causes otherwise great players to leave, and one might be the host (there's no way of knowing who the host is), causing the game to stop. One last little con; sometimes the lobby is a little boring when waiting for a match (especially if you're waiting for an extra player to join). I think a little pop-up shooting range in the lobby to try out weapons would be a great way to pass the time. Sometimes the wait for a game to start will be 1-4 minutes, and I've played matches that only lasted 1-2 minutes.

[FINAL THOUGHTS] It's a MUST-have realistic VR shooter game! It's fun, addictive, and exciting. A few updates will fix the minor issues, but it is still otherwise very playable and enjoyable as-is!

Let me explain;

I got this on release day like I usually do for most FPS I'm excited for. I have no regrets about my purchase because I've played my entire weekend away on it. If this game was as bad as everyone else leaving 1-star reviews is saying, I would have quit and returned to my CODWW2 disc. It has room for improvement, and as they have done with all of the games in their series, it will be patched for the better.

I mainly play multiplayer, but have played approximately 1 hour of campaign mode and have to say that the single player mode is the best I've experienced in the series.

Graphics: The good: This is the first and most important feature I noticed going into CODMW. They are stunning! I'm playing on a standard PS4, so I'm sure the Pro on a UHD in 4k would be out of this world! The lighting is good, and characters don't "stand out" as much as they did in previous versions of COD. Which is great if you like to hide in a dark spot. Everything is smooth, and all of the visual effects are pretty realistic. The bad: The only graphic complaint I have is that you cannot set the field of view. I usually like to really crank the FOV up so I don't have to have my character look side-to-side all the time.

Audio: The game has a great soundtrack that fits the theme on this one. Playing on a surround sound system with a subwoofer is great! The guns pack punches, the explosions are realistic.

Controls: As with any new FPS, I have to dig into the options first to dial-in my sensitivity on the joysticks among other options. CODMW was no different. It took a good 5 matches to get things tuned right, but they do feel good. The bad: My only complaint I have is the side strafing seems slower than CODWW2 that I'm used to. Maybe it's just me?

Gameplay: Playing just about any mode is fun, but sometimes gets pretty frustrating because of the vast difference in matchmaking skills and firepower strengths. Now there are doors everywhere. You can rush through them, but if you're quietly trying to creep you have to hold a button to open them. It's the same button that reloads your weapon or picks up items. Just seems a bit cumbersome at times. . You won't get instantly spawn-killed much in this game, but it will respawn you fairly close to another enemy a lot of the time, and most spawn points require you to do a lot of running to get to the hotspots of the map. I've only made rank 32 so far, and still have yet to get a gun or attachment that gives me much of a quickdraw feel. Aiming down the sight on just about every gun is so delayed and frustrating. Hoping this improves as I rank up, or in an update.

Killstreaks: The killstreaks are hit or miss for me. The lower end (easier to get ones) are about worthless for me. Even some of the better ones like Wheel Son don't seem to be very effective. Then there's the chopper gunner; it reminds me of the ball turret gunner on codww2 but on steroids. If this thing is in the air it's game over. I've gotten it once organically, and once in a care package. Lots of fun to be the chopper.. not so much for the enemy on the ground.

Weapons: There's quite a few to choose from, and TONS of attachments!

Crossplay: While it may seem a bit unfair that a PC player can have an advantage with a keyboard and mouse setup vs. someone on a PS4, my experiences so far have been that I still get my rear end handed to me by PS4 players just as much. The lobby does tell you what platform the other players are on. You can disable crossplay for certain game modes, but some require it to be enabled.

Overall they did a great job on the game, but just need to make some tweaks. It's more of a BF4 than a call of duty game in my opinion. If they could implement a rank-matching system that would put low-rank people together, and people that rank higher together, it would be less discouraging. Even playing the game on release day had a high ranking player finishing the match with 30-3 and the second place low-ranking player at 12-8. At that point there's really only one person having fun in that match. I'll update this review as I notice changes.

I love the original Red Faction, I played on the PC and PS2 (pssst it's better on the PC) anyway, RF2 was alright but not as fantastic as the first one, RF has a pretty good story and the humor was great, but both where FPS games, so I was really worried they where going to hack up RFG as it is now a TPS.

Well I'm about 50% done the single player campaign, and have logged many hours of online, I can not get enough Red Faction Guerilla.

Single Player:
This is great, we have tons of fun here. The maps are really nice, very easy to navigate, and very large. There is a great selection of missions ranging from destroying a building or structure as fast as humanly possible to extracting hostages' who are being probably tortured from your terrorist actions as new member of the Red Faction, all with out them dying.
Driving around is actually really fun, I don't normally like driving in a game, but this was nice, all your vehicle options are distinctively different from each other, if you drive a big dump truck, it's slow and is terrible at cornering but you have a massive destructive power, being able to drive it through a building with ease. But if you are looking for fast and small with great handling, there is that to, but at the same time you give up that fantastic crushing capability.

As far as weapons go you can upgrade everything at one of your safe houses after you collect "salvage" I actually liked doing this, it's like my goal to get as much salvage as I can possible get, the more the better. There is really a weapon for every situation your in, and when you run out of ammo, get your hammer out and start bashing everything in sight, you can take out buildings people walls trucks and just about anything that looks like it could brake, all with a little mining hammer. As like most games the more you play the more weapons you unlock and then you can buy them.
There are ammo crates all over so if you find that there are to many EDF (Earth Defense Force, they are the enemy) around and not enough bullets or rockets then just load up and at the same time you can change you weapons selection as long as you have them unlocked.
And the whole moral thing they have is neat, the higher the moral of the Red Faction the more ammo will be in the crate for you to reload with, they also help you fight when they are happy. If you die or a member of the RF dies, you get less ammo and they will also freak out and run away from a fight when the moral meter is low.

Over all the single player is great so far, anyone who does not like it has not played for long enough, it's easy at first but once you get in to it, it's a quick jump to becoming more difficult and hopefully you have collected enough salvage to fight the good fight and free mars from the tyranny of the US government......Umm I mean the EDF, there couldn't be a major political parallel in RFG could there?

Multiplayer:
I won't spend to long on this but wow this just as fun as single player, maybe even more fun. They replace the run with a whole bunch of different backpacks, like a jet pack, my fav is the Rhino pack where you are able to smash through enemies and walls or both.
The game types are the same as you would find in most multiplayer games, nothing new here, just that an enemy can come from anywhere, so essentially no cover, they will just hammer there way to you, and beat you down, as you cower in fear because you're out of ammo with no back pack and wish you picked up the Thrust pack to shoot out the top of the building only to die mid flight from some kid with a rocket launcher.

RFG multiplayer = hours and hours of destructive endless fun.

As for graphics, no it's not like there KZ2 or anything like that, but I just think it leaves miles of room for improvement in hopefully RF4 for whatever they call it. And it seems to be smooth, no jerking around or getting stuck on a corner, just great game play.
My only real complaint is that there is no Co-op campaign, because come on that would be stellar in so many ways, maybe next time.

And I do think if you play online this is totally worth full price.

I got exactly what I wanted with the PS4 Slim...
-- An update to my Day-1 PS4. Mainly, a lighter console -- good aesthetically & easy to move around the few times I need to.
-- 5G WiFi support (excellent, I got 90mbps).
-- Super easy to install my 1TB Fusion drive (literally, 5 minutes).

This is not for everyone though. It's great for me because I'm very happy with my 2-yr old 1080p HDTV & Sound Bar & don't plan on updating to 4K until networks broadcast it regularly (or unless my TV stops working). I also don't use an optical output from my console. Therefore, the PS Pro would only cost me more for technology I won't use in the next 3-4 years & I much prefer the slimmer console.

Bottom line -- I gave it 5 stars because it delivers on what it intends to do. I won't rate it lower for what it can't do since it was not intended as such. The same as I would not give a low rating to a Honda Accord because it wasn't as luxurious as a Mercedes Benz. I'm going to rate it for reliability and value (and I must say, improved looks).

In comparison, the new console is -- I'd say -- 20% lighter & looks 33% smaller. Overall build is nice. I also prefer the matte finish. Can't speak about it's reliability as only time will tell. The drive's noise level seems the same as the Day 1 PS4 but also not a factor for me as I play mostly digital games. The price is good -- $299 with one of it's finest games, Uncharted 4 bundled in.

Also, if you're like me & will upgrade the drive -- it's very easy. Just go to [...] & download the 4.0 firmware on a USB drive (ExFAT format). Make sure to download the 900mb version/not 300. The larger version is the one you'll need for a full re-install with a new drive. Follow the instructions (towards the bottom) for "Perform a New Installation of the System Software".

Lastly, in comparison to Xbox One S, which seems nice now that they finally got rid of the power brick -- only took 'em like 10 years:) I prefer the PS4 Slim for a couple of reasons. Playstation's Baseball game (The Show) is amazing & Xbox hasn't really had one since Triple Play (again, important to me but not all). I also don't particularly like the white finish since it does not match the rest of my Electronics setup. However, it seems to be good & has a 4K Blu-Ray player which PS4 Slim does not (but once again, I stream & don't use disks so it doesn't help me). On a negative note, I have read a few reports of the XB1 S overheating (but can't confirm).

In Summary, as you can see -- the PS4 Slim works for me in every way. What it doesn't feature, I don't need and was not expecting it since it was not advertised that way. What it does is exactly what I want it for and does it well. Hope this helped those considering purchasing it.

All aspects have been improved, which says a lot since this is already a great series. Animations, game play, UI, Graphics (Stadiums & Player faces), Commentary (new announcers) + they added a retro (1 button mode) so anyone can play & enjoy.

I have not played enough to comment on whether or not the commentary will get repetitive or whether or not the online experience is stable. But as far as noticing the improvements over last year, it's a definite yes and therefore, for me, totally worth purchasing if you're a Baseball fan.

Icing in the cake, the Kid, Ken Griffey Jr. gracing the cover.

The graphics, special effects and dialog were incredible. Crashed a lot in the Batplane & the Batmobile. Would have enjoyed more episodes involving, as Joker puts it, "these wonderful toys" even though the controls were a bit difficult to handle. Only played the game through once because it was challenging but also frustrating. You could not save often. I hate spending even 20 minutes trying to complete a level only to find you were knocked out & have to start from the beginning of the level again. Had to rely on the Strategy Guide to help me find one of the secret keys to unlock Batman's steath powers (that was tough - your perspective is off because of the camera angle). I thank the designers for allowing the game to save the key even if you could not trace your steps back across the floating crates. I had to start over again but at least I had the key. If you can tolerate the annoying camera angles & not being able to save often, then you're going to have hours of fun playing this game. To the Batmobile...

You mostly work to raise your reputation to complete goals.  Also the creators of URBZ should have given us gamers a better instructional booklet.  Had no idea how to use the Power Ups and wasn't sure what to do when I had to go to work.  What do you do if the robot station burns down?  The URBZ are not very happy in this part of town.  Be prepared to spend most of your time waiting for the game to load.  That's one of the reasons I do not have the patience to play the game through again.  You can't complete the last goal - it must be a secret.  Rumors are spreading that you have to play through the game 3 more times to fulfill the last goal.  Some games I enjoy the second & third times when I play through, but this is not one of those games.  If this is a taste of where the Sims' games are heading, I won't be playing with the Sims anymore - sorry Bella.

Poor guy has only met women that use him that's why he is the way he is - SNARKY.  The voices and singing were hilarious.  Guys would probably enjoy this game more than girls. The special effects were great and the creatures were unique (never heard of some of those names before) but you couldn't see the detail of the creatures very well, and what's with the dark dungeons?  I didn't pay over $40 to run around in the dark.  Also why the air borne view fellows?  With all the capabilities of the PS2, games should not be designed with this overhead view.  So glad I put up with this annoying distraction because the ending was amazing and I can't get those songs out of my head.  But I am not replaying a second time because of the camera angle, and with the cost of games nowadays, you really want to purchase a game with replay value. Help, I can't stop playing Champions of Norrath.  After completing the game and playing with the same character (much stronger & better equipped) on the Courageous setting, I have gone the extreme by creating 10 characters (5 characters to choose from but you can play as man or woman).  The characters that are the most fun are the magic users.  I love to face a horde of orcs and goblins and just keep firing magic at them and when only 1 or two are left, hit `em with my best shot.  As you get further into the game, the AI of some of the evil creatures is amazing, especially the nesperaties (vampire-like creatures) who are tough to hit because they keep dodging your attacks.  The game designers are the Champions of Norrath.  Sounds, graphics and the artwork are beautiful.  Wish you could make the characters we gamers create speak more.  They only make a one sentence comment when they enter a dungeon/castle, ant hill, etc.  Only two complaints, I do not enjoy the airborne view.  You are looking down at the action - can zoom in a little closer but when you do, you lose peripheral vision; and why not give us a bag of holding (like from Icewind Dale) that can hold huge amounts of armor, weapons and jewelry.  After a while you leave the landscape littered with armor or weapons because you get tired of beaming back & forth to the shopkeeper.  Other than those two minor complaints, the game is outstanding.  You really get your money's worth of game play & hordes & hordes of fun.

When you play The Sims 2, you have a choice to either play in story mode or play as you wish.  The PC version of Sims 2 is a relaxing and enjoyable family game to play, especially since you are able to input your own music into the game.  I strongly recommend inputting your music into the game because the music that comes with the game is silly, and the faster your computer, the more features you can take advantage of.  Keeping track of and controlling a family of eight is a little bit of a challenge but the spacebar on your computer helps with that task.  Your Sims can paint a picture you choose, you can make movies, or you may uncover a hidden architectural talent by creating your own homes.  On my computer, at the neighborhood screen while I'm searching for a neighborhood to play, I hear There's a Place For Us from West Side Story or Lee Greenwood's God Bless the USA or Judy Garland's Somewhere Over the Rainbow.  It almost brought a tear to my eye when my Sim was cuddling her newborn and this song by Josh Groban started playing: You raise me up so I can stand on mountains.  You raise me up to walk on stormy seas,.  I am strong when I am on your shoulders.  You raise me up more than I can be.  It's very funny to see your Sims dancing to the tune of Thriller by M. Jackson.  During the wedding ceremony, you can hear Let It Be Me by Betty Everett & Jerry Butler (on my computer anyway).  I have so many video games from Christmas but after a hard day at work, I come home to relax, and playing The Sims 2 makes you actually feel good.  Thank you EA Games for producing a game that doesn't involve a lot of violence (see enough of that in the newspapers).  Here's a suggestion:  our human children could learn a language if EA Games would have the Sims speaking different languages.  They say the best way to learn a language is to go to that country.  Well, EA Games could create that atmosphere by having neighborhoods in different countries (real countries not Sim countries)  with the Sims speaking the language of that country.

The game designers of today have such a great sense of humor. I am finally getting around to playing a computer game from 2005 called Gothic II. The environment is awesome and the sounds of nature immerse you into the game. You can play as third person but if you click on the F key, you can play as first person and actually feel like you're roaming a forest where any second you will have to battle a monster. You meet other characters also and I like the fact that their conversation is shown. Many times I've played games where characters are communicating with each other but I miss a word or two and have no idea what they just said. In this game you are able to read what they are saying. Reading is good. You must find the time to stand on the highest platform of the Lighthouse and watch the sunset or the moon rise. Watch it in first-person mode but be careful not to stand too close to the sections that are not protected by a rail. I became so immersed in the game, I forgot to sleep. Looked at the clock and realized I had been playing for over 24 hours. You just don't want to leave the Gothic II world. Get the game but set an alarm to bring you back to reality.

Hmmmm, next time I think I'll join the Thieves Guild. I want to see what's in those locked chests.

What I must first say is that this game is incredibly easy, and no, I am not an adult. I am 13 years old, and I got this when I was 12. The levels of the first world, Artisans, are super easy with a very easy boss. It's harder to GET TO the boss than it is to beat it. The levels just seem to keep getting just a tad bit harder, but nothing significant. The hardest boss is the boss of the second level and he isn't very hard either. Gnasty Gnorc is a surprisingly easy boss, once you figure out how to toast him. What makes this game annoying is that there is so much treasure, spread out into so many different places, that you will just rip your hair out in some of the levels trying to get it. But there are some pros. This game is a little bit long making for long lasting entertainment. The game also has great graphics with a frame rate that never slows down, and because between screens, the game is counting treasure, so it's like there's never a single load time. Also, some of the enemies are pretty funny, like in one level, if you do the right thing at the right time, the enemy will actually MOON you, and it's hilarious to see. Also, the controls are simple enough for anyone to figure out making for not much trouble otherwise. Some points of the game are hard like recovering stolen eggs from the theives, but besides that, this is an easy game that I would recommend to anyone below teenage age. The only reason I gave this game three stars was because I know most people like a good challenge, but it wouldn't be fair to give it four just because I personally like an easy game. Still good though.

I love Game Boy Color just as much as anyone else who owns it. It's easy to carry around, has great, high quality games, a sharper screen, and good use of color. I also own a Neo Geo Pocket, and even though it is a better system, it needs two different kinds of batteries, and all the games get old really fast. This system only needs two AA batteries, and they last a good amount of time. The only bad thing about this system is this particular color. I wasn't alive when the original Super Mario Bros. came out, but I do faintly remember playing it when I was young, and I faintly remember liking it. When I went to Target to get a game, since Pokemon Pinball wasn't there, I got this game instead. I realized that this game was a better choice than Pokemon Pinball. First off, the graphics are marvelous, and proves that GBC is just as good as the NES, if not better. Another thing good about this game is the new save system(I knew it was new because I had a friend who had the original for the NES). They also installed a new challenge mode which is very tough, but later in the game, there is a new item in the Toy Box that gives hints to where all the Yoshi Eggs are. The Toy Box has options like Fortune telling which can be very amusing(And get you five more lives to start with if you get an Extremely Lucky card) and tons of printouts for the Game Boy Printer. You might also want to have a Link Cable and a friend with this game handy for the Vs. Mode. In this mode, you can race your opponent on the special race courses. You can also play this mode in one-player, with Boo as your opponent. There is also a new Photo Gallery, which takes a picture every time you do something new, like stomp a new enemy, or trade high scores with a friend with the Infared sensor. Yes, I said high scores, another new feature. But this is all aside from the main game. The game isn't really too challenging until the last world, but I noticed that you can jump higher in this game than any other 2D Mario adventure I've played so far. Once you beat the main game, you get the Star levels, which are a little more challenging anyway. And once you get the high score, you can get to the Lost Levels, which are EXTREMELY hard, and the last of them has TWO Bowsers! Definetly a great buy, because of all the time put into a game like this.

I really like this game a lot. The game has six different zones, with at least one secret level in each one. After that there's...Wario's Castle! Another thing I like about this game is that you can cash your coins in for things like extra lives in a slot-machine like manner of chance. This game also has very good graphics for a Game Boy game from 1992, and looks sharp on the Game Boy Color. The controls are easy to figure out, but sometimes, when Mario runs, he can slide, and he can't jump very high either. What I do like is that if you lose your Fire Flower of Rabbit Ears, you can still be big. I've beaten this game a lot, but it's still fun to do. It's a great buy.

I got both Gold and Silver for Christmas. I started Silver first because I got that earlier, but I had fun with Gold too. There aren't that many differences, but there is the obvious that some Pokemon are found only in Gold. The reason I prefer Silver is for a couple reasons. First off, you can't catch Lugia until you've done every single thing in this game, unlike Silver, where you can catch him once you have a Silver Wing. I prefer Lugia to Ho-oh for some reason. Also, I like Silver more than Gold because Silver acts a lot more like advanced Red and Gold is like advanced Blue. I liked Red better than Silver because the Pokemon in Red only are more powerful, which I liked. Some of the Pokemon either in Blue only or rare in Red were pretty weak, like Caterpie. Other than that, there isn't much difference. You may prefer Gold. This is just a guideline for which version to pick. If you want an in-depth review of the actual game, check out my review of Silver version.
PS: I forgot to mention one major thing in the Silver review. Most Pokemon have both male and female genders. There are a few exceptions, like the Legendary birds, Magnemite, and Voltorb. You can use two Pokemon from different genders to make an egg, that will hatch into the lowest evolution of a Pokemon. You can also use Love Ball, made from PNK APRICORN, to catch Pokemon from the opposite gender. Pretty nifty, eh? Now you have more to catch.

If this game didn't have the name "Tony Hawk's Pro Skater" on it, I probably would have confused this for another skateboarding game. The game has almost no similarites to the first. Instead of tapes, you get money, with double the objectives and bigger levels. You have a whole bunch of different tricks, and you have to buy stats instead of just earn them, and you can buy new tricks. This game also has an create a player mode and a Skate Park Editor(Which I am a very big fan of), so you can make your own skate parks, and play and edit pre-made parks. The thing about this game is, even though it's bigger, and there are more tricks and it's easier to do combos, it's just not as fun. A big contribution to this is the disappointing soundtrack. The only good songs on it are the first two: Blood Brothers by Papa Roach and Anthrax with Public Enemy in Bring the Noise. The punk is all missing. It has been replaced with rap, which any skater is plain out against. Another thing is that while the beginning parks are bigger, they stay the same size through the whole game. The game also asks you to do impossible tasks, like grind rails you can't even find and get 250,000 points in two minutes in a level where it takes 10 seconds to get to the halfpipe(Philadelphia)! Another thing is some of the graphics. There is a lot of draw-in, especially on the narrow courses, and the characters look, well...dirty in appearance. It's kind of funny to look at them though. But despite of all this, the game's still fun. I don't know why, I should be giving this two stars, but knowing that it's Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, I get the good ol' feeling. Buy it, I guess.

Never having played an Arkham game before I must say this was not a good first experience. I've seen gameplays of Arkham Knight and the big selling point for me was the ability to cruise around Gotham in the Batmobile. I assumed that I would have the same experience or at least with another Bat-vehicle in Origins. Well unless I have not progressed in the game far enough that doesn't seem to be possible. Also not even 2 hours in I'm noticing some glaring flaws. For starters the combat system is broken and not at all what I'd expect Batman to be capable of. Countering is spotty and the slow motion finisher feels rushed in order to add eye candy to the game. As for gameplay, the scroll menu using the D-pad for batarangs and such is near impossible to navigate. Im not kidding when I say I spent nearly 8 minutes just trying to get the hacking thing to pop up. Which brings me to my next point. That bat hacker thing is totally unnecessary and almost impossible to use. Another gripe: Navigating around Gotham is not what I'd expect as all you can do is run (bad idea unless you want a fight every 5 seconds) or slowly glide from one building to the next grappling here and there. Again I'm not to far in maybe you get a bat-cycle or something but so far navigating from place to place is tedious and cumbersome. The lack of mini map further complicates things tenfold. Minor gripe: The graphics are great during the cutscenes not so much during gameplay. Felt like I was playing PS2 All in all I'm really not happy with this game and am even skeptical about getting Arkham Knight.
