It's alright. Call of Duty games do not really stand out much. The new alien mode was pretty cool, but got old quick, even with the DLC.
Not the best lego game out there, but all the lego games are pretty awesome, so maybe it is unfair to compare it.

I am a huge fan of the Lego games and have played most of them by now. This is by far my favorite of all the Lego games, however to do everything it is going to cost a lot of money in the end, even if you catch good sales! Somehow, I think it is worth it though for all that you get (at least if you don't pay full price for everything).

Pros:
1.) Story-line is amazing... I venture to say the best of all the story-lines, and the mash-up of all the different characters and worlds works really well! Each level takes place in a different world (Wizard of Oz, Ghostbusters, Portal, Scooby Doo, etc).
2.) Characters: There are a lot of different characters from many beloved titles, and it is cool to be able to build them and their vehicles. The characters also interact with each other in funny ways at times... although some of the dialogue is annoying (Unikitty saying to the Wicked Witch "If you spent more time singing, you wouldn't be so "wicked", witch" gets annoying fast).
2b.) Doctor Who's appearances are awesome! And so is playing a level in his world... okay this is just something awesome for us Doctor Who fans, but I thought I'd add it as a sub-point.
3.) The main story has a good length to it, and it will be fun to replay once I have all the characters necessary to get all the minikits.
4.) Hub worlds are more fun to play than any single hub world I have experienced - the variety really makes it stay fresh for longer. Individual hub worlds of course are smaller than a typical Lego game hub world, but each universe represented has its own hub world that can be played once you have a character from that world. There will be a total of 14 different hub worlds in season one, and I have already played most of them for hours as they have a lot to do in them!
4b.) Hub World races are cool!
5.) It is very kid friendly. Even my six year old daughter is able to play along in the Hub worlds pretty well, although the puzzles are a bit complex for her, so we don't often play story levels together.
6.) Works well in 2 player mode, although sometimes difficulties can arise on the split screen.
7.) Using the game pad can be a lot of fun and adds something to the game itself. Some puzzles require you to move characters around the pad to do different things, and some boss attacks require you to move the character to another space on the pad. You will definitely want to keep the game pad close to your chair. We use a small kids table for this purpose.

Cons
1.) Price and the multitude of packs you have to buy if you want to do everything! I have already spent about $250 and estimate I will spend close to $350 by the end of Season 1 and I have bought things on incredible sales and only bought what was essential to have the skills to complete all tasks. Be prepared to buy about 11 fun packs/ team packs, as well as the Level packs if you want to complete the full game. There is an in game hire-a-hero feature, but it does not always work properly and can get expensive on in game studs.
2.) Hire-a-hero is a bit glitchy, incomplete, and sometimes resets after your hero expires after just 30 seconds. It is supposed to be a feature to keep you from having to buy all the charcters, but sometimes the hire-a-hero fails to pop up (he explodes before you can purchase); other times you cannot complete the full task in 30 seconds, which means rehiring in some instances, and the task resetting and being a waste of studs in others. Also, you cannot purchase vehicles that are necessary for some tasks (Jurrassic World Team Pack is necessary to use the Gyrosphere).
3.) There are a handful of minor glitches that can be annoying at times, but do not detract too much from the game playing experience.

I might want to rate this 4.5 just because of the price and the fact you have to buy so many characters to be able to do it all, but then again for the starter pack it is well worth the $70 investment it currently is priced at (and I got it for $55), plus if you are not a completionist you don't have to get everything to enjoy the game... just slowly buy the packs you want. Since, you cannot give a 4.5 rating, and it really is a really awesome game, I will give it a 5 star rating!

Gollum is very useful as you need someone who can use the small door hatches and he also has the ability to destroy silver objects with his fish throw. He can also dive. In fact there is one gold brick that requires a character to have all 3 of these abilities to get and he is the only one that can do all of that together. You will not regret getting Gollum if you plan to go after the gold bricks and you should get plenty of use out of him.

The spider is also very useful as she can destroy cracked tiles, track objects (2nd build), and dig. She is also fun to ride, although a little creepy as you can hear the spider legs tapping on the ground as she walks. She is also very useful for areas with lots of things to destroy as she can walk right over them, destroying them in the process, and immediately pick up the studs. Cars tends to be too fast and you have to turn around to pick up the studs (not to mention lack of easy control). Unlike some vehicles, she is very easy to control, and, although she is not the fastest, she can certainly go fast enough (I even might have won a ground race with her if it weren't for the water).

I highly recommend this fun pack as the characters are cool and it is one of the most useful fun packs... it will cover characteristics that could require you to buy multiple packs otherwise.

Cragger is absolutely necessary to do certain gold bricks, plus his sub adds a high degree of usefulness in the game. There are Chi stations underwater that only he can use (and since Chi needs to be built up it is not wise to HIRE him for these activities). I was going to buy Eris because I thought Eris looked cooler, but then noticed that the vehicle Cragger came with was more useful, so I got him and I am glad I did because afterwards I learned that he is so necessary to get all gold bricks. Other than that he is an okay character.

His Boat/ Sub is a great vehicle and fills a hole that I am not sure is filled currently by ANY other vehicles. It is great for races both on top of the water and under water, plus it makes exploring underwater much easier and quicker! You NEED this vehicle in you repatoire!

Also, a plus: Batman's line when you have both him and Cragger together... I will let you discover that for yourself!

To sum up, if you are planning to buy only ONE Chima pack: BUY THIS ONE!!!! He and his vehicle fill a gap that no other character can fill and He is necessary for 100% completion.

Cyberman has become my new favorite character to play with. Aside from the fact that I am a big Doctor Who fan, he is very fun and useful. First of all, he shoots lasers which is handy for taking out bad guys and also can be used for TARGETS and SILVER OBJECTS. His boosting when jumping is pretty cool, but is only decorative since he neither hovers nor goes high enough to be a double jump :( (It is also funny how he falls flat on his face when you try to double jump.)

Apart from that, the Cyberman is one of the most useful characters in the game to date. In addition to the abilities listed above, he is able to do many RARE abilities, such as HACK, TECHNOLOGY, DIVE (only character able to Dive AND Hack/ Technology), MIND-CONTROL (only Wonder Woman and Wicked Witch can do that), X-RAY VISION (very rare), and DRONE-USE (only Doc Brown and Cyberman are able to do this and Doc Brown will not add much else to your arsenal, so Cyberman is a better choice here).

The Dalek is just cool to play with. He is really fast on build one (once upgraded), yet more controlled than other fast vehicles. Apart from that, he is about as useful as a typical vehicle, so if you have a lot of other vehicles (like I do) you may not find yourself using him a whole lot other than for the coolness factor of riding and using a Dalek. It does rebuild into a flying vehicle (but is really slow as a flyer), so it can FLY and DOCK... it can also destroy Gold and Silver objects in its rebuilds, but so can many vehicles... plus the Cyberman that comes in this pack already destroys Silver Objects more conveniently.

If you are a Doctor Who fan who plays Lego Dmensions, this is a must buy!!!! Even if you are not it is one of the most useful packs you will buy and is necessary for some gold bricks/ mini-kits and makes others easier to get.

You could say I am an AC fan boy (I have even liked the games others have disliked), so take this into account with my review. I think this is one of the better AC games of recent years (since the EZIO Trilogy). I really liked being able to play as two different characters (although honestly the differences in abilities is only slight). I mainly played as Evie when I could (some missions require Jacob) mainly because stealth is my AC gameplay style whenever possible and I liked her outfits a little better.

The gameplay and story-line are pretty solid and on par with previous AC experiences. I really enjoyed the London scenery. Driving the carts and racing them and fighting from the top of them was a nice addition. I also liked the raids/ side missions you could do to get extra money, but it seems by the time I got around to doing them I didn't need much extra money anyway (and I think it is a while before you can actually do the raids/ side missions in the first place).

If you like AC games, then you should enjoy this game.

NFL Street is seven-on-seven football where every player you pick for your team plays both offense and defense. On top of that, you can put any player at any position, enabling you to experiment with Warren Sapp at quarterback, Peyton Manning at nose tackle, Brian Urlacher at running back, and Peter Warrick at the corner.
It's one of those games where football fans will be addicted after one score and the football haters will crossover when they see it because of the exciting gameplay that appeals to both sports and non-sports gamers alike ala classics like NBA Jam, NFL Blitz, and EA Big's other gem, NBA Street.

As you play a game, it's not just about scoring points, it's about scoring points with style. The controls are simple as on offense you can lateral, hurdle, juke, or stiff arm, utilize your turbo to speed past defenses, and hit the showboat button to perform some of the most incredible taunts, high steps, and street moves imaginable, from dribbling the football along the ground like LeBron, to throwing passes behind your back, and even cannon-balling into the endzone. The more style you show, the more Gamebreaker points you accumulate.

It's not often that we do three unique reviews for one game across multiple platforms. But given the length of time between the original PS2 release and the subsequent Xbox and PC releases, we felt it important to give it a second look. On top of that, PC gamers may have some expectations that may be a little different than console gamers so we decided to differentiate those as well. What we found after playing the game for so long is that it's still an excellent game on the PC. It looks better than the other two versions and has better combat controls while suffering only slightly in the driving department with the mouse and keyboard. It's an expansive, awesome, well produced and put together game with a ton of different missions of all sorts. While it has its problems, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a very entertaining game with hours and hours of fun for those who both want to rip right through the story or explore the gigantic environment.

Instead of a story mode and a half dozen exterior mini-games, or a Director mode, or even the great Survival mode, Parallel Lines delivers a single story mode with everything packed inside it. I like how the game has great details and Parallel Lines offers more depth than many games from escaping from cops. The soundtrack of the game is great.
My dislike was in how the makers of the game I think focused more on trying to compete with the GTA series and not on the actual game itself or this could have been a even better game if there was some more effort, thought and detail put into it.
This game is recommended for anyone who lives for crime, violence, breaking the law, car chases, gun fights, vengeance
and much more. Hope you like it :)

I don't get all the rave reviews about this game--at all. I've played nearly all the previous R&C games and for the most part have loved them (especially the ones for PS2). This game sucked. It was clearly rushed to market and is not nearly as polished as the previous games have been. It was like pulling teeth getting myself to play though this thing.

Here's a list of my complaints:

--The game is buggy. I got stuck in a weapons upgrade menu and couldn't get out! (BTW does anyone comprehend the upgrade system in this game?? It made zero sense to me...insanely stupid, bizarre & nonsensical). I also got stuck in a weapons trial & had to quit the game and reload it! Again, it's obvious this thing was rushed to market.

--The graphics are glitchy. Polygons pop in & out constantly. That didn't even happen on the PS2 R&C games.

--The camera in this game sucks. It doesn't recenter itself after you move it, so you end up constantly having to fight with it. Cheap deaths will result. There's also so much 'foliage' and other little details in this game that end up getting in the way of the camera & obstructing your view.

--Too many little nooks & crannies (especially in the first few stages) where Ratchet gets stuck.

--The initial 'gravity' stages are disorienting much of the time. In fact I found myself disoriented through much of this game.

--No customizable controls (I'm accustomed to using the O button for firing like in previous R&C games, but that's not an option here so I was hitting the wrong button CONSTANTLY throughout the game).

--Quick-selecting weapons does NOT work properly & you often end up having to fight with the analog stick & quick-select menu to get it to highlight the correct weapon.

--Some of the sound effects are downright obnoxious (like the pause sound).

--It's simply not fun. I'm glad I only paid twenty bones for it (Black Friday sale) and was able to unload it on someone else for the same price I bought it for. This one's a dog. Glad it's over.

I feel like they could have done a much better job with the story & its utilization of the incredible environment they created with GTAV, but when a company puts this much work into creating something so massive and impressive I cannot possibly knock them. This game is *gorgeous* and very challenging. Luckily, balloons (lives) are much more plentiful in this game than in the past. Same goes for the coinage. I do have a few complaints, starting with using the inventory items. If you're having trouble getting through a level and want to resort to using an inventory item, you have to exit the entire level--which requires you to wait through a loading screen--then relaunching the level after you've chosen your inventory item(s)...which of course makes you sit though ANOTHER loading screen. This really breaks up the fun. Why can't we just access our inventory at some point within the levels themselves (like at the continue points with Mr. Pig?) Or maybe after you die X number of times, a helper can pop up asking if you'd like to use an inventory item. But noooo, instead you have to decide BEFORE entering a level if you want to use an inventory item--which makes zero sense your initial play-through, since you have no idea yet if you'll need help since you've never played the level before! I also don't get why Nintendo didn't give us the option to 'restart level' in the pause menu?? It only allows you to exit (which again, forces you to sit through two loading screens if all you want to do is go back and redo the level from the beginning). LAME! And speaking of the loading screens, they are choppy. What's up with that?

My other gripe: The swimming controls. Awful. It's a shame, too, because the water levels were absolutely gorgeous. They were a pain to get through though solely because of the frustrating controls (I was using the Wii motion plus controller).

I beat the game without even realizing I was on the last level or was fighting the final boss :\ There was no sense of, "This is it...this is the end." I just beat the dude & the next thing I knew I was watching a cut scene & the credits. Surprise! So from start to finish, this game took me approximately a week to beat, playing through one world each day. I still have to go back & unlock all the hidden levels though, so I technically still have work to do.

Anyway, minor gripes mostly...I definitely recommend playing this game!

I was so psyched for this game I actually bought a PS4 just to play it (along with GTA V). What a mistake. While LBP3 had the potential to be an amazing game, it is chock full of bugs and glitchy graphics. Shadows and full-on pieces of the "set" will pop in and out of view constantly while moving about the various level hubs. It's really sad. I actually started to think my PS4 was defective, so I went on Youtube and watched gameplay from others only to see them experiencing the same exact graphical pop-in issues. I even tried going into safe mode and rebuilding my PS4 database to see if that would help...nope. I cannot believe the PS4 would have issues running such a simplistic game like this, especially since it's also available on the PS3, so something is very wrong here. The game is also FULL of bugs, so I suspect everything is a result of lazy/inept programming.

I'm also finding it annoyingly difficult to switch characters when I want to. A couple of other gripes: There are too many voiceovers, and the constant talking gets old pretty quick. Some of them are pretty obnoxious. What's worse, you're forced to "re-hear" everything when you walk past a character or play a level over again. Why can't there be an option to only have to be subjected to these voiceovers and cutscenes once and then never again? The second pocket is a great new addition, but I wish you didn't have to press X to confirm every time. That's a needless step. You should just be able to press O to open the pocket, L to maneuver to the item you wish to use, and then release O to equip. I guess I'm just used to that method of item selection from playing Ratchet & Clank, but it works flawlessly. It's also ridiculous that you're forced to go through the item tutorials over and over again any time you want to go back and replay some of the levels--again, why can't we just be subjected to those tutorials ONCE and then never again?

Another big complaint: The white loading screens!!! WTF? I hated them in LBP2 and I hate them again in this game. First of all they're blinding. Secondly they completely fragment the game since the levels are all quite dark in comparison. They just don't fit & they break up the flow of the game. Please go back to the black loading screens like in LBP1, or at least make them darker in color!

Edit: Just got to the end boss only to have my character completely disappear. Nice! I also experienced a glitch where everything outside of my pod completely disappeared. Did the developers do ANY testing before they hoisted this thing onto the market? I can't believe how short this game is compared to the others (which weren't even all that long themselves). I get that they expect the community to eventually create levels, but seriously? Only THREE worlds? The fact that they could create such a short game and STILL have it so full of glitches makes it quite clear that this was a Xmas time money-grab. I'm slinging this puppy up for sale--someone wake me up when they've fixed this mess. I'm seriously regretting my decision to buy a PS4 at this moment. Should have just stuck with my PS3.

As the owner of a PS2, PS3 and PS4 I was on the fence about even buying a Vita. I am SO glad I did. This little thing blows my mind every single time I fire it up. Sony completely nailed it (minus a few minor gripes). I'm STILL trying to figure out how the Vita can essentially run PS3-quality games in such a small form factor, and without any fan or becoming ridiculously hot to the touch. Is it magic? And all of this for essentially the same price as the original puke green Gameboy cost when it launched in 1989, when adjusted for inflation. If you'd have shown my 10-year-old self this device back in 1989 and said, "This is what you'll have in the future" my head would have exploded off of my body. I'm 35 now and every time I use my Vita I feel such amazement & gratitude for living in a time when such a thing exists. We've come so far in just 25 years.

Just had my second PS4 controller wear out on me after just over a year.  The R2 triggers on these things will fail to fully depress after a while, causing certain games to not work correctly (like GTAV).  The problem is the silicone pads Sony used inside of these things--they develop a groove in them over time, making it so that the trigger can no longer fully depress.  Do a search online and you'll find hundreds of people experiencing this same issue.  Shame on Sony for not owning up to this design flaw.  They're profiting off these things wearing out after warranty expiration forcing consumers to either buy a new controller or pry the controller open and fix the problem themselves (a massive PITA that we shouldn't have to contend with).

I am not a huge fan of Grand Theft Auto, but I like it and this game feels like a pale impression of that series. Saints Row worked for the simple fact it didn't take itself seriously and was about fun. So it had a certain charm about it and felt completely different than the Grand Theft Auto series. Mafia 3 I really wanted to love but in the end it feels like Wal-Mart brand Grand Theft Auto because it takes itself too seriously and the execution of the graphics, gameplay and mission don't match. Not to mention the bugs. Consoles have issues sure, but on PC the game crashes wildly and is unplayable at times.

The story itself is good if you can make it past the forgettable and boring gameplay. Not to mention the bugs and crashes depending on which version you own. This game had a great idea behind it, and if it had been crafted by another studio perhaps something really special here but it is a swing and a miss for Take 2 Interactive.

Imagine going to George R.R. Martin and him saying, "I want a fan fiction author to finish my series, who can't afford professional editing." That is the experience we get with Mafia III, a great concept for a story trapped behind a lack of professionalism, and execution. I thought about giving this game 3 stars on console but for PC the game doesn't even run. A future fix doesn't change the fact people who paid for the game got one that didn't even work at times.

Pros
- Story if you can make it through the host of technical issues (on PC you pretty much can't)
- Soundtrack

Cons
- Graphics
- Performance
- Bugs
- Boring mission system
- Bad execution
- wasted potential.

Grade: F for PC

Mafia 3 had potential to be a sleeper hit of the year, but Take 2 Interactive forgot to handle the technical elements and implement interesting gameplay and missions. I guess wait for a steam sale in the future, if you can get it for under 10 bucks could be worth it if they fix the issues with the game.

The best shooter I ever played was Battlefield Bad Company two and the expansion pack Vietnam. But I didn't enjoy Battlefield 3 or Battlefield 4. I especially hated Hardline. So while I always wanted to go back and play a WW I or WW II in a DICE game. I held my expectations in check due to the fact Battlefront was a shallow puddle of a game. I also can't speak for anyone else, but the future based shooters are extremely boring for me. So this was the only option for me this year. Outside of Gears 4 which I had always been a fan of since the beginning.

I fired this game up and man did it remind me of Battlefield 2, which to me is an underrated masterpiece. This game has depth, breathtaking graphics and interesting game modes that offer hundreds of hours of fun. My favorite game mode is War Pigeons, I have already been in some great heart stopping matches. With classics like Rush and Conquest you are set.

He is the secret weapon of Battlefield 1. The campaign is amazing. With great actors in them. It is the only shooter campaign I have ever played all the way through and loved. This game is Band of Brothers Battlefield, I realize Band of Brothers was WW II but you need to know the feel of the campaign and entire game. For me this is the best shooter I have ever played, and I have been playing since the original Doom.

Battlefront, I said was like trying to play a beautiful photograph but was a very shallow experience. I am glad DICE crafted a game to match it's amazing game engine. This and Dark Souls 3 are my games of the year. With Dark Souls 3 slightly losing out if I had to pick.

Only small gripe I have - if I had to find something wrong. Is the RNG nature of Battle packs. After each match players are randomly selected for a battle pack which can contain rare weapons or skins. I wish there was a currency system apart from the option to break down doubles of items. A currency we could grind on to unlock packs ourselves - like Warbonds. But I just hate RNG after my years of WoW but this doesn't bother me that much.

Pros
- Graphics
- Depth
- Gameplay
- Music
- Game Modes

Cons
- RNG nature of Battlepacks. (If I had to find something)

Grade
A+ Game of The Year

Conclusion
Battlefield 1 does everything right, which is something shooters haven't done in years - it brought us back to simpler times and apple pie dinners. For too long other shooters pushed the modern angle, with annoying future tech that overall ruined gameplay and messed with the flow of games. There is an emotional attachment for many when it comes to World War II and I later periods can't match.
The multiplayer is a masterpiece but the real shocker is the top flight campaign that is like playing Band of Brothers WW I. This game simply has no weaknesses and for me is my 2016 game of the year.

If you enjoyed the last game? You will enjoy this game. How much really depends on how fast you get bored. Because everything will feel somewhat the same after awhile. This is a very safe play by Activision and one that I am not convinced pays off. Yes it will sell millions of copies. No doubt making a ton of money but it is hard to imagine this won't be deemed the most bland game of the series.

Multiplayer feels infinitely the same. Now the campaign is amazing, and I love the modern warfare remaster I can't save how much I loved those. But let me ask you something? How many people do you know buy call of duty of the campaign? How many people do you know finish the campaign? I know some do but lets face is this game is all about the multiplayer. That is where it truly lacks.

I know I gave Battlefield 1 game of the year, narrowly beating out Dark Souls III but not by much. But that has nothing to do with this average review, I try to be as fair as possible. My friends love Call of Duty on their impression are largely the same was mine - it doesn't do anything different enough and feels the same.

Pros
- Graphics
- Sound
- Gameplay
- Campaign
- Modern Warfare remaster

Cons
- Feels infinitely the same as the previous title
- Plays it too safe
- Lacks where it counts which is multiplayer

Grade
C

Conclusion
While not a bad game, it isn't a good game either. With Battlefield 1 and the surprisingly amazing Titan Fall 2 (still working on my review) I can't make the case for anyone to pick this up. Unless your love of COD is the campaigns and you really want the remaster. The end result is a multiplayer that offers Infinitely the same warfare.

The PC version has serious performance issues. Not worth buying into it is fixed and the PC version of the game would probably be a 1 star rating.

This could have went either way for me. Liking it or thinking it was just ok. But in the end being ok just edged it out. The first thing is Dishonored 2 certainly has it's own style. One that some people will like and some that won't connect with others at all. It's not a bad looking game by any means but from a textured standpoint everything feels muddied.

The problem for me is the world of Dishonored doesn't feel original enough or it's own product enough for me to become immersed beyond the two main characters. It honestly feels like Lemony Snicket and Fable crammed all in one world. Since I am not of fan of either (except the first fable) it is largely a miss for me. But hey to you that might sound like the most awesome thing ever.

The one thing this game really has going for it is the combat system. To me it feels perfect overall and we all need more stealth games. But gameplay wise this could be the best of them. But for me that is largely wasted because the world, hit and miss art style and uninteresting story, stop me from enjoying the game's one true strength - the gameplay.

Pros
- Gameplay
- Two lead characters

Cons
- hit or miss art direction
- muddied looking textures
- unoriginal feeling world - I can't stop thinking about Lemony Snicket and fable
- typical revenge tale that is largely forgettable

Conclusion
As a far of the first game. I wanted to love this one. But the even more stylized graphics throw me off. While that is certainly only my opinion - it is the type of choice that is a love or hate thing. Beyond that the graphics feed muddied compared to the first game. While the gameplay is amazing, I am the type of gamer that gets bored quickly without an interesting world or story. For me Dishonored had neither.
While it is fine for a game to remind you of other fiction you love. Lemony Snicket meets Fable isn't all the appealing. But if you don't care about story and enjoy stealth games - you should like it.

If you have always sat there and felt you really should try to get into final fantasy? This the game to do it as it provides the best combat yet for fans of all RPGs very Dragon Age Inquisition like. If you are a final fantasy fan disappointed in this last entry in the single player series? For sure get this one. I myself have forced myself over the years to get into final fantasy without success something about it breaks my immersion.

I mean I love RPGs especially ones that tell a in depth story with great characters so you would think I would be a big fan of Final Fantasy - no. Witcher 3 is another game you would think a RPG mega fan would love and played it countless hours. Again that is wrong for whatever reason it did not hold my attention and I can't explain it - great game though. Many of the Final Fantasy games are great, as a critic and open minded fan I can say this despite my dislike.

My Final Fantasy friends (one of who failed out of college back in the day due to the series) give this game the stamp of approval and consider it one of the best ones in years. I myself coming from a RPG fan point of view? Everything you expect in a good to great RPG is in here but cars and cell phones in any Fantasy except Urban Fantasy kills all immersion for me. I imagine Skyrim killing a Dragon and calling up your characters mom in game so she would be proud of you. Lots of laughs.

So why did I play this game even though I am not a fan? Well being a critic is a hobby, I got a copy for free, and I can play through a game I am not into but still see the value of it for people who do enjoy it. The characters are great, love the sworn brothers feel, the combat is very good and the scope of the art direction is beautiful. You don't need to be a mega fan to be impressed by all that and you don't need to enjoy a plot - to really like characters who exist in a story. Walking Dead is the best example of it - bored of the plot like some characters.

I just wish it was set in a more traditional setting without cares and sell phones. Not saying no tech but through some science fiction elements in there with the fantasy. Another thing is even though I love the combat. Like the last Dragon Age game it has the same weakness it gets old after awhile. Some combat aspects (like turn based or Skyrim action combat without a party) is fun regardless of time spent. Where you don't even think of the combat and enjoy the game. The story is also somewhat weak at it's conclusion in my opinion.

The characters, music and art direction make up for those issues mostly however. And the setting and story comes down to opinion really and isn't a universal flaw. Just something to keep in mind before you buy it.

Pros
+ Graphics
+ Combat
+ Music
+ Characters
+ Art Direction

Cons
- But Combat could get old after awhile compared to other Final Fantasy games
