But downloading that driver fixed the framerate problems, I can run it at a smooth 60 fps now. I was also getting some V-sync problems, where I had v-sync enabled but I was still getting screen tears, to fix that I just used D3DOverider (Or whatever it's called, it's something like that lol) to force V-sync and that got rid of that problem. It's a great game, the PC port is still just a joke :D

Like many of you, I was hesitant to purchase Battlefield 4 after the horror stories that had plagues its launch. I recently bought my PS4, and needed some games to play with friends. I probably wouldn't have bought it if not for my friend from work constantly pestering me to buy it so I could play with him. I am very glad he did. I never got big into Battlefield 3, but Battlefield 4 is so intense words can't even describe it. Playing through headphones, you feel like you are really in the battle. Bullets whiz by your ears, explosions blinding you. It is by far the most intense shooter I've ever played. I can't speak for the campaign, as I haven't played it yet, but multiplayer is immensely enjoyable.

The environmental destruction and the Levolution are amazing. It's really scary when you're hiding behind a wall, reloading your RPG to shoot at a tank, and then all of a sudden the wall isn't there, being blown away in a blast of shrapnel and flames. The maps are big, but the matches are 32 v 32, so there are more than enough people to fill them. There are lulls here and there, but for the most part the matches aren't without a moment's rest, just go go go, action all the time. I don't know how long I will play religiously, but for the week or so that I've had it it's been an incredible experience.

The only issues I have with the game are two main ones: One, there is still the occasional lag. I don't know if this is my internet, or Battlefield itself, but I will be running across a field and I'll see my guy stutter while he's running. It's an annoyance, but not enough to detract me from playing the game. The other issue I have is that sometimes when a match loads, it will take almost a full minute for all of the textures to render. Again, not a dealbreaker, but an annoyance :P

All in all, the game is tons of fun. I didn't play it at launch, so I can't compare, but as of April 22, it's a really fun game to play. It's really fast paced, really intense, and it looks great. If you're hesitant, don't be! I got it and haven't looked back, it is by far the most fun FPS i've played. (Aside from fantasy FPS games like Borderlands, those are in a different league ;) )

**Update**
I've completed the campaign, and I don't understand all the hate for it. Sure it's not groundbreaking, but what FPS army shooter's campaign is? It was good. Some of the dialogue was a little cheesy, but for the most part it was pretty solid. I liked it :) And playing on hard had just enough challenge to attempt a few missions a couple times without making you so frustrated you don't even want to try.

I saw this game at E3 of last year, thought it looked pretty interesting, then forgot all about it until it came out. I was going to wait until the price went down, because I had heard mixed reviews about it. I bought it for $25 bucks off of Ebay, and don't regret it one bit. I'll go over the gameplay aspect, but also the PC version side of it as well. I also think that with most of my reviews, rather than peppering the things I don't like in the different sections, I'll just save everything that I don't like for the end, so that you know what I'm talking about.

Gameplay and Story: Gameplay is incredibly intuitive, but not what you would expect. It is a very laid back, calming game. There isn't a lot of action, and when there is it comes in short bursts. As I've read on other reviews, this is a thinking man's game. And, as I have been more of an intellectual versus athletic person, it fits my type of game perfectly. I haven't finished the game yet, I would hazard a guess that I'm about 3/4 of the way through, but so far I have really enjoyed it.
What the game consists of is walking around crime scenes, collecting evidence and slowly picturing together the scene, with each investigation leading you closer to solving your murder, which is the entire point of the game. There are some little side investigations, helping lost souls "find their purpose" for still being on earth even though they're dead. They provide a little bit of depth to the world, but nothing crazy.

Sound and Dialogue: The sound is pretty standard as far as games go, it's not a spectacular soundtrack but the music fits the mood and always sounds good. The voice acting isn't amazing, but it doesn't suck either. Pretty standard.

Environment: The developers did a really nice job at portraying a really dreary, kind of depressing Salem. That could also be the ghost world though, I'm not totally positive which they were going for, but it's really awesome.

Interface and controls: One thing that's nice about not having any real sort of combat is that there isn't anything to clutter up your UI. No bullet counters, no health bars, it's just you. Controls are pretty standard as far as PC games go, shift to run, E to interact, stuff like that. No real difference between games, but if it ain't broke, don't fix it, right?

PC Version: I haven't played the console versions, so I can't compare the quality of the build, but as far as PC ports go it's rock solid. I downloaded it through Steam, didn't have any hiccups installing or booting it up for the first time. The game looks good, it's not next gen quality obviously, but it still looks awesome. One cool thing is that it is not very graphics intensive at all. I have a gtx 770 and could completely max the game out, AA and v sync included, and I still got over 100 fps. If I did that on a 770, I would hazard to guess that you could completely max it out on 600 series cards, or maybe even late 500 series cards. (It was on 1080p, so obviously account for the difference if you have a different resolution).
One odd quirk that I experienced was when I walked by a police car, it dropped and capped at 30 frames per second. As soon as I turned the screen and walked away, it jumped back up to 60. I tried turning everything on low, and it still did it. So that was one weird quirk in the gameplay, but it only happened once and hasn't happened since! If you guys want, I actually did a video demo of the graphics on the 770, you can check it out here if you feel so inclined :D
[...]

So now for the dislikes:
- The length. It's not a long game at all, but I give a little more explanation down below.
- In the menus, and when choosing dialogue options, you can obviously use the mouse, but the button options are the number buttons 1,2,3, and 4. Like what? Who's bright idea was it to make those buttons the switching/choosing dialogue buttons? They deserve to be fired. Lol.

All in all it's a great game, but definitely not for everybody. It's a slow paced, thinking game. I don't think it's worth the $60 price tag, but as I stated earlier I got it for 25 and felt that that was a good deal. I would have even paid 30 for it. The only reason that I feel it's not worth the price tag is merely for the length. I'm only a few hours in and almost done with the game. I explore, but I don't look for every single nook and cranny on every single level, unless it will benefit me in-game somehow. There are a ton of collectibles, but they don't really benefit you in any other way than to say that you've gotten them. So I look, but I don't scour the map for them.
I'm pretty sure that's everything, if you guys have any questions or and corrections, comment and let me know!

**Update 6/15**
So I finished the game, and I loved it. I have 9 hours logged on Steam, with what I would put as pretty extensive exploring. I kind of tapered off towards the end, just because I wanted to finish the game lol. I loved the story, atmosphere, the characters, it was great. I would pay up to $30 for it and not regret it. Anything more than that and I think that it wouldn't really be enough, but that's just my opinion!

Being only 19 years old, I have not been around long enough to be able to participate in the nostalgia that this game could bring to older gamers. I have never played the older Wolfenstein games, so they will not bias my opinion of this game. Let's jump to it!

If you have read any of my other reviews, you can probably tell that I'm not hard to please when it comes to games. Sure I have some standards, but for the most part I'll give everything a chance and not completely rule anything out until I've played it. This game does not disappoint by any means.

Story: I'm sure you are all familiar with the story at this point, so I'll just give my take on it. It was actually a really engrossing story, and I really enjoyed it. I kept wanting to play the game because I wanted to know what happened next. It had all of the parts that make a good story: action, romance, tough choices, emotion, and best of all, killing nazis. The voice acting was great, and it had great pacing. I completed it in 12.4 hours on the middle difficulty, and I'm going to play through again on the hardest to see how the story is different. There is one point towards the beginning where you have to make a choice, and depending on the choice it will affect your game, so I'm going to play through again on the alternate storyline to see how it differs.

Gameplay: Plays like a first person shooter, pretty standard. One thing that I don't like is that most games (to me at least) are easier to play on PC, but this one was a bit more difficult. Running and sliding isn't a major part to this game, but it is required to level up some perks (which I'll explain later), and it's really hard to hold shift to run, W to move forward, and C to slide, all at the same time. I imagine that had I used a controller it would have been easier, so take that into account. I also saw a lot of people complaining that you had to manually pick up ammo, and maybe because it's because I just came from playing Metro 2033 (where you also have to manually pick up ammo), but I say so what? Everyone complains that they want more realistic games, so this one makes it a bit more realistic by having you manually pick up ammunition, and everyone complains at that! There is no pleasing gamers! Lolol.

One other quick thing that I also liked was their health system. Your maximum health limit is 100, so if you find a health pack that would put you over that 100, say to 150, your health would go up to 150 on what they called "overcharge", and then slowly deteriorate back down to 100. So you can still pick up health packs that you find along your way, but you can't get completely overpowered and get like 500 health. Your health would only regenerate to the nearest 20 I think, so if you lost health to 54, it would go back up to 60. If you hit 17, it would go back up to 20. (I don't know if it's the nearest 10 or 20, I didn't pay attention that much hahaha.) I also really liked that you really could take either level as stealth, or all out guns blazing. The stealth system was really well done.

I keep remembering gameplay aspects I need to add xD Another big complain I heard was about the enemy AI, and how they were basically really dumb. I had probably 2 or 3 spots throughout the entire game where I encountered them acting really weirdly, but for the most part they functioned as they should, taking cover, shooting, trying to flank me, etc.

Sound: As I stated before, voice acting was great. I really enjoyed the music in this game, you got into some pretty cool fights and when you did it would start blasting some heavy metal in the background to get you pumped up. I'm not an expert on how guns are supposed to sound, but all of the gun sounds were great. One thing about the voicing that really really really pleased me was that when you went up against most of the enemies, they spoke german. Not a british accent, not english with a german accent, but full on, fluent german. I loved that, because it really helped immerse you in the game. One thing that I actually thought was really funny was that with the subtitles in the game, you can set them to on, off, or just when someone is speaking a foreign language (which is what I had it set to). There's this guy in the beginning that's on your team that speaks English with a Scottish accent. He is in no way not understandable, I could understand him fine, but it still put up subtitles for when he talked. I just thought it was funny that it put up subtitles, even though he was speaking english xD

Level up system: The perks system in this game is quite different than most games, but I actually really enjoyed it. There are 4 skill trees, and instead of having to level up Perk A to get to Perk B, and then Perk B to get to Perk C, each perk had a requirement that you had to complete to unlock it. To get so many kills with a certain weapon, or get a certain amount of stealth takedowns. That way you could work on whatever skill tree you wanted, and whatever perks you wanted to unlock. (If that doesn't make sense, let me know in the comments and I can try and clear it up a little bit hahaha.)

Graphics: There was one thing that really bothered me about the graphics. They look great, from far away. But as soon as you get up close to the walls, just as an example, you could see how awful the textures looked. They were 2D, grainy, and just plain gross. I know it's just nitpicking, but hey, that's what reviews are for lol. The game also had cinematic prerendered cutscenes, which only ran in 30 fps, but looked better than the ingame. I don't imagine this game is too terribly taxing, I have a 770 and could max the game out, AA and all. There were some framerate stutters occasionally, but for the most part is was a fluid 60 fps.

Dislikes: I had very few dislikes about the game, but one of my big ones I thought was kind of a stretch with the main character. Not giving away any plotpoints, but there was a point where you get stabbed in the stomach, and then after you take the guy down you basically get up and act like it's no big deal, and at one point help boost a guy up to like a ledge. It's like really? If you really got shanked through the stomach with a bowie knife you wouldn't be doing that. One other thing that I didn't care for was the main character. I didn't hate him by any means, but to me he didn't have any believability, or emotion. He was actually really great, until about a fourth of the way through a game, and after that he just kind of clammed up and didn't have any personality. Maybe he's supposed to be that way, I don't know, but it was something I didn't care for.

Overall, I was extremely pleased with this game. I had heard great things about it, and I was not disappointed. I got it for $30 on a steam sale, and would have easily paid up to $45 for it. It has a ton of replayability, an awesome story, decent graphics, awesome soundtrack, and as stated previously, best of all? You get to blow apart nazis. :D

I previously purchased a Playstation Vita when they were fairly new, and sold it, because of lack of games and functionality. When I heard everything it could do with the PS4, I decided to give it another go, and I have not been disappointed. I'll quickly review the UI of the Vita, my likes/dislikes, and what it can do with the PS4.

I picked up my Vita secondhand, and got a great deal. I got the vita, an 8 GB memory card, two games, and a rubber case for the vita, all for $160. Not too shabby if I do say so myself ;) It has a really slick user interface, all of the apps load up quickly and you can scroll through the pages no problem. You swipe right and left for all of your open apps, and you can close the open apps extremely easily. The PlayStation button works just the same as any playstation device, pressing the button brings you to the main menu, and holding it brings up the options for the system (IE the brightness, wifi settings, etc.).

As for the actual physical design, it's not too bad. It's one of the few electronic devices that the developers actually used their brains and put the speakers on the front of the device. They could be louder, but if they're not loud enough you can just use earphones. With earphones it's more of a normal volume level. The triggers are springy and work well, as does the D-pad. The other four, the X, O, triangle and square, and the joysticks, are a little small for my liking, but it is a portable system, so it makes sense. The screen is big, bright, and vibrant. The back touchpad works well, and while I wish the back handholds were a little bigger, it still works fine. Battery life isn't incredible, but for basically being a portable PS 2.5, it's great. The device has enough weight to it to feel solid without being too heavy. The camera kind of sucks, but hey, it's still there. One thing that I wish they incorporated, or that was able to be incorporated with an external case, is that with normal game controllers, you have both of the triggers. The L2 and R2 triggers help me balance the controller in my hand and use L1 and R1 more efficiently. I know that there couldn't be a case that would incorporate additional triggers, but I wish that at least you could have a case that would extend plastic below the triggers so that I could rest my middle fingers on it, to balance the vita better in my hand. If that makes any sense... It's kind of hard to explain without any visuals. Lol.

I have the 3G version, but the 3G is a joke. First off, you can't play any games online on 3G. You would have wayyyyyyy too much latency to play any sort of a shooter or competitive game. Over wifi you're totally fine. But secondly, it's way too expensive. I don't remember exact prices off of the top of my head, but I want to say it's like 20 or 30 bucks for 250mb of data. 250mb of data that is ridiculously slow. Like what? Come on. At least incorporate 4G, or don't charge anywhere near as much. But it is still cool that technology is getting to the point where you can do that with a gaming device.

I only have two games, the PlayStation Allstars, and Uncharted. Allstars doesn't really use the rear touchpad, but Uncharted does, and I have to say that I really like how it's incorporated. The touchpad, both front and rear, and like the motion detection is used in a way where you're not being forced to use it every 5 seconds, but you still get the use out of it. I've always thought incorporating touch screens into gaming was a bit of a gimmick, it's not my favorite, but so far it's been incorporated in a way where it's not overbearing, but you still get your use out of it. I really like how it's been used so far.

Now, for my favorite thing, the remote play. It is as cool as people say it is. If someone is using the TV, you can stream any game from your PS4 straight to your vita. You can even do it on someone else's WiFi, as long as your PS4 is in standby mode. How awesome is that? When streamed, the games look amazing. I don't know how the specifics work with the resolutions and everything, but it looks exactly like it does on the PS4, it doesn't tone down the resolution or anything. One of my favorite things though, is that you can press the PlayStation button and click on the option "Button Mapping", which will completely map the PS4 game's controls on the vita controls. Another really cool thing is that the "Start" and "Select" buttons work as the "Share" and "Options" buttons respectively, so you can still use the Share function and capture the awesome moments from the vita. Like that's amazing!! I know that a lot of people had problems using remote play with the PS3, and I think that's because they made the vita after the PS3, so they weren't really able to incorporate that functionality into the PS3. I'm glad that they worked more with it on the PS4. To me, using the vita for the menu of the PS4 is laggy, but once you get into the game there isn't any lag at all. It really is amazing what technology has come to.

Anyways, I think I covered everything I meant to. Obviously everyone is going to have their own opinion, and since I've gotten older I haven't as much as a flair for portable gaming as I used to, but I'm really enjoying the vita so far. But I think it's especially awesome if you have a PS4, they really made all of the features work extremely well together, and I've been really pleased with the responsiveness of everything. Let me know in the comments if you want to know about other features, or if something I said didn't make sense! :)

So I'm not going to talk about the story, the game has excellent story and atmosphere. You can read about the story on the 360 version ;) There are just two things I wanted to bring to attention with this game.

One is graphics. Of course, the game looks fantastic. 1080p and a solid 60 frames per second, it look fantastic. I would say that it looks as good as the original on PC, completely maxed out, minus a few fog effects. I got about halfway through the PC version of the original, and then it decided to get into a fight with my PC and stop working. I wanted to keep playing, so I bought the PS4 version. So the game looks fantastic, and that's coming from a PC gamer.

My second praise is the decision to put 2033 on Last Light's engine. That is the single smartest thing that they could have ever decided to do. While 2033 was mostly good, the interface and menus were absolutely horrible. Being on Last Light's engine, everything is clean and easily accessed. The guns sound better, and everything just functions better. So I really want to praise the developers for making that decision, because it has been a huge benefit to the 2033 experience. I have experienced some bugs, sometimes the gun shots/reload sounds don't line up. Occasionally the monsters have really unnatural movements and just look quirky and glitchy.

Overall it's a really solid port, and I am very pleased with it. I haven't been able to play LL yet, but the changes and improvements to 2033 are fantastic, and I can tell that they really put some thought into it. At first I was upset, because while I like the remastering of games, I feel like game developers are really taking advantage of it. But I think these are games that are really overlooked, and deserve more attention than they've gotten. It's an especially great deal when you get 2 games and all of the DLC for $50. I got it for $40, so it was an even better deal :D

I played this game for a solid 6 hours last night, and am absolutely in love with it. It has its pitfalls, but what game doesn't? It was like Assassin's Creed and Arkham Asylum had a hot, steamy lovechild, and that child is a great addition to the world of Middle Earth. The map and detection system are straight from Assassin's Creed, complete with "viewpoints", and how the enemies detect you. The free running and climbing are also very similar as well. The combat is a copy and paste from Arkham Asylum, down to the counter icons and being able to stun enemies, and attack them with a flurry of quick, precise strikes. Everyone was complaining about this, but I think that they work beautifully together. Sorry, just had to get the initial gush out ^_^ Now for the more logical and ordered portion of the review!

Story: The biggest complaint I heard was that the story was dull and uninteresting. I honestly don't see where this is coming from. I do have some complaints about the story, but it's not the worst thing I've ever played. I have 2 complaints about the story, one is length. I'm trying to 100% the game, and in playing for 6 hours and 17 minutes last night (the game keeps track of your total time, which I love. For some reason Sony thought it was a good idea to get rid of that with the PS4... so it has to be tracked by game. Brownie points to Monolith for that.) I have about 31-32% total completion. So I'm probably looking about 20 hours total, which is in no way a really short game, but I wish that the story would be longer. There are a total of 20 story missions, and I'm on about number 8 or 9, and at this point there are almost 3 story arcs going on. If each one got its own length, you're looking at about 6-7 missions per story arc, which really isn't that much. I really think that they could have expanded on the stories and made the game longer. My other complaint is that at the beginning, you're kind of just thrown into the story, and Talion just accepts it. If you're just thrown into the story, okay I can deal with that. But he accepts that he's dead, with no real remorse, and that he's tied to this mysterious wraith within 5 minutes. He's like "Oh well, we're together, might as well go kill the bad guy". So the actual story once it starts I think is really well done, but the intro is really rough and I think could have been fleshed out better.

Graphics: The game looks beautiful. The in-game graphics are good, and the cinematics look even better. I've actually been really impressed with Talion's cape physics, they've been really good. It runs at an unlocked 60 frames per second, and I've only seen a frame rate drop one or two times, so it's a pretty steady 60 frames per second. I've been quite pleased with that.

Gameplay: As I stated before, the gameplay is really a carbon copy of those two games, but they blend and meld so beautifully together that it makes you wonder why nobody has ever thought of it before. There's only one real complaint I have with the gameplay, and it's that whatever moron decided that the X button would be the run button, should be fired. It would be fine if you could change the controls, but you can't do that! So it's impossible to hold down X to run and try to use the right thumb stick to control the camera. Like who thought that was a good idea?? They deserve to die. But other than that, everything works like a charm. The stealth is done extremely well, and the combos work every time. On a side note, I really liked the tutorial. It taught you the basics of the game, without shoving it down your throat saying "YOU WILL PLAY THE TUTORIAL".

Sound: The voice acting is great, the soundtrack is okay. I like the music, but it doesn't really feel like Lord of the Rings music... sometimes it does, but the majority of the music seems sort of out of place.

Size: This is one other main concern I have is the size of the map. I haven't beaten the game yet, so I will update this as I continue to play, but so far there's just the one area, and while it's fairly sizable, I would expect a game to be bigger... Like you can unlock all of the "viewpoints" within ten minutes if you wanted. I swear when I was watching some gameplay that the main guy in charge of the game said that there were 2 or 3 major areas like that, so I hope that's true, because if this one area is the full game then that's kind of disappointing. There is a ton of content, it honestly just seems like the size of a bigger DLC area (Like Solstheim for Skyrim), rather than the full area for a full game.

Level-up System: I really really applaud the leveling system in this game, I love it. You earn XP from kills and missions and such, and that gives you skill points to unlock your abilities. There are 4 or 5 tiers, and you can only unlock abilities on tier 1 until you get enough "Power" to unlock tier 2, and 3, and so forth. You unlock Power by killing Captain orcs, and by progressing through the Nemesis system. So I think it was really balanced. There's also a separate set of skill trees to upgrade your health, focus, ammo, as well as how many runes you can put on your weapons. These skills are unlocked by earning what is basically money from side quests. They really give you the customizability to unlock and upgrade what you want.

Nemesis System: This is Monolith's pride and joy, and it is fantastic. You can think that you killed a specific orc, and then he will show up later with burns all over him, or with huge gouges taken out of his face, saying how he is going to kill you for what you did to him. I haven't heard a single line of dialogue twice from the orcs, or orcs that even look the same. One thing that I thought was so cool though is that obviously, if the main Captain kills you, he'll remember you. But if you get killed by one of the random, nameless orcs that swarm with him to assist him, it will generate a name for him right then and there, and put him in the system to start ranking him up. Like how awesome is that?! He's a nobody, and then gets put into the game out of nowhere. That's awesome.

Parents: No language or nudity, but violence and gore are extremely prevalent. Examples include: chopping off Orc heads with blood spraying, stabbing them through the chest with blood spurts, etc. The blood is black, as in the LOTR movies, and you never kill humans with this brutality. I personally love it, I think it's awesome, but would probably recommend keeping younger kids from playing.

I believe those are all of the grounds I wanted to cover. Overall I have been very pleased with the game, it was $60 well spent. My main concerns/dislikes are the length of the game, and a few quirks with the gameplay and controls. I think that most of this game was extremely well done, and it deserves praise and attention. If they could have given it some more attention and given the game some more story content, I think it would have been perfect. If you're a big LOTR fan, you'll love this game. If you're not, I think you will still like it, because while it is a Lord of the Rings game, you don't have to be big into the series and lore to understand what's going on. Absolutely wonderful game :)

Just a final update, I have finally completed the game. It was simply amazing. I really don't understand how anyone could not like this game. My final game time was 24 hours and 9 minutes to completely 100% the game, just for those of you that need reference. But I have a friend, and he said that he's not done yet and has gotten over 30 hours, so if you take your time you can really get some good game time out of it. My main fear was cleared up, there was a second big area that was almost as big as the first, that you can travel back and forth between, so the size was really good. The total size of the game wasn't as big as I would have liked, but I felt that there was enough content in the game that it felt full. Most of the side quests didn't feel like "thrown on" junk, they actually felt like good side quests. One small thing that I really liked was when you do the final mission, it comes up with a warning that says "this is the final mission, but once it's over you'll be able to go back and play". Which I loved. I can't even count how many times I've thought the game would put me back in so that I could go do stuff, and it was like "Nope, you're done. Sucks to suck!". So that was really cool. One thing that I didn't care for is the story missions. But not in the sense that everyone else has thought they were boring. I thought the actual missions were good and had good story telling, but had no real relation with each other. It seemed like during both halves of the game, there were 2/3 story arcs all going on at once that weren't really related. Some of them seemed like they could have even been side missions. So I felt like they could have been tied together a little bit better.

One other correction I would like to make to my earlier review is that the game does run at an unlocked 60 frames per second, but this statement is very misleading. I thought this meant that it ran at 60 frames per second, with the occasional frame rate drop. What it actually means is that it's a 30+ fps, meaning that it runs anywhere from 30 up to 60, but rarely gets up to 60. Regardless, the game runs as smooth as butter. It's a beautiful game, and the only time that there were frame rate drops was whenever I would brand someone.. Every time, consistently. So that was strange, but other than that there were no frame rate drops. Overall, I have been very very happy with this game. $60 well spent, I would do it again. It's not without it's problems, but overall the game was simply amazing. And I loved every second of it. Oh, and the ending! Ahh! Very wide open for a sequel, which I hope Monolith does. There hasn't been a game that has left me with so many questions in a long time. I loved the ending.

Let me preface this review by stating that in no way do I agree with their DLC model, and because of that I have taken away a star. This is just going to be strictly about the gameplay, and the PC port, not the shady business practices that Turtle Rock and 2K have chosen to implement. I would realistically rate this game a 3.5, but you can't do that on Amazon! I feel that 3 stars is too low, so with 4 I go. I rhymed! Haha! Okay, anyways, back to the review.

The game itself is actually a ton of fun. You all know how it works, 4v1, hunters versus monster. And that is one thing that I do praise about the game, is the monster design. The monsters look incredibly cool, and they each play very differently. The effects of the attacks look fantastic, as does the environment. The hunters have a rather cartoony look to them, which I don't care for, but everything else looks spectacular. Everyone talks about how much teamwork it takes, and I try and dispute that, but I don't think that I can. Each Hunter really has its own part to play. The Assault is the main damage dealer, the Medic heals everyone, the Support gives shields to everyone, and the Trapper is the one that actually makes it possible to find the monster. Team communication isn't really that necessary, I never talk to anyone on my team and we do pretty well, but it would definitely help, as with any multiplayer game.

Obviously the story is nonexistent. They have their "Solo" mode, but it's not a campaign, just a string of matches/game modes. I like to think of it as an extended tutorial, you only play Evacuation to get the hang of your new monster/hunter, and then that's it. But then, this game was never advertised as having an amazing single player experience.

The PC port is rock solid. My system is composed of an i7 4770 (Non k), 16 GB of RAM, and a GTX 970. I can completely max it out at 60 frames per second with only a stutter here and there. (But on a side note, my system has been stuttering with other games, so I'm not sure if that's the game's fault or my system's)

Parents: Language is pretty mild, and only happens when you're a hunter (If you're a monster, there isn't any). The hunters will drop an F bomb once every few minutes, but it depends on the hunter that you pick as well. The blood is really mild as well, you just see some splashes when you eat an animal as the monster, and some blood appears on the ground. It's an incredibly mild M game, and honestly feels like they put the stuff in just to make it M, it could have easily been a T game.

All in all, I think it's a fun game, but not at full price. I managed to score mine for $30, and I feel content with that purchase, and the amount of content that you get. If you know what you're going in to, you'll be fine. It's a mainly multiplayer game with a pretty tacked on solo experience, but the core of the game is a lot of fun. It's just surrounded by bad DLC models and trying to please everybody, rather than completely focusing on what the game is about.

All I can say is that this game is addicting! I find myself playing this game all of the time. It's time is set to real life so it can be a draw back because sometimes if you want to do something you have to reset the game clock but it doesn't make me dislike the game. But yeah, this game is hours of fun and just an all around great and addicting game.

Resident Evil 4 is considered one of the most innovative, influential and popular survival horror games on the market. The fact they skipped Code Veronica and made a remake of RE4 especially after getting a spiritual successor to 4 that being RE8 Village speaks volumes on how popular this game is. If you like horror games or resident evil there's a good chance you've played this game before but if not then you are probably wondering what all the hype is about. Ill be honest I wasn't going to review this game because so many people have and I feel my opinion would be biased considering this was my first M rated game and first horror game I played when I was 11 years old on the ps2 and game cube. So I'm gonna do my best to ripe away that nostalgia lens and be honest about this game.

Gameplay: RE4 has been ported to basically every console following its original release on game cube and I've played pretty much every version of this game that exists except the Nintendo switch version so as you can imagine its gone through a lot of changes since the Game Cube release. The original game did not include Separate ways and some of the costumes and weapons this version has. So if you've never played before this is one of the best versions to play it on. This game drastically changed up the gameplay from the previous games. It added the 3rd person camera angle, a customizable inventory, The enemies are now Parasite controlled people and no longer mindless zombies. So if you've only played the originals or started with RE5 and skipped this one think more like re5 but more clunky and slower paced. This game still has a lot of puzzles like the pervious games but this game it includes a money system and has findable treasures you sell to a merchant. So overall a lot of changes but if you are used to the newer games its very similar to RE5 and RE Village. This game is basically those games dad. This game also has a bunch of separate game modes aside from the base game. It comes with Assignment Ada which was in the original along with the very popular Mercenaries mode but this game also includes Separate Ways which was a fun additional game mode to explain Ada's side of the story.

Graphics, Music/ Voice Acting: The graphics honestly still hold up pretty well. Compared to the likes of the Remake they aren't amazing but they were good enough that I along with many others were surprised this game ever even got a remake, This version still holds up pretty well. The music in this game is probably some of my favorite in the series. It fits the vibes very well and feels very unsettling at times. The save room music is actually a snip from the Devil May Cry 1 Main theme which is pretty cool (Probably because DMC 1 was originally a version of RE4). The voice acting in this game isn't bad but the dialogue still holds strong to the cheesy one liners. It's a fun break of comedy in this horror game and I only hope its some what still present in the RE4 Remake.

Story: Much like the other drastic changes to gameplay the story is very different in this game as well. Starting a new chapter or phase in this series. RE4s story abandons the Umbrella storyline and starts a new one 6 years later. Leon Kennedy from RE2 is now a government agent and is looking for the presidents missing daughter in a very rural part of Spain. She was taken by a religious cult group that uses Parasites to infect the minds of its followers and control them. Ada does play a Role in this game and there is a small Wesker Cameo. Overall the story is a bit predictable but its definitely scary. Like all the pervious games each act is split into 3 areas: Village, Castle, Island. The Island section is probably the weakest part of the game and most unliked as it falls heavy into the action and less horror aspect of survival horror. There are a few very scary enemies and areas, I personally found the Chainsaw Ganado's and the Regenerators some of the scariest. This game also doesn't hold back on the gore, There is a lot of dismemberment. This game also has a boat load of content and is one of the longest games in the series. So is this game Scary? Id definitely say so, Is it fun to play? once you get used to the controls yes. Is it a perfect amazing horror game? No it has a lot of flaws but for the innovation it gave at the time I see why it has been hailed at such a height. I still have to say it is a great game and experience and I cant recommend this game enough. A lot of people I know who played this game couldn't believe this was getting a remake because re4,5 and 6 all feel like they still hold up and don't need one. So to answer the question is it the best in the series? Well probably in the top 5 for most people. Overall: 9/10

Assassins Creed 4: Black flag is a sequel to AC3 (duh) and follows the story of Edward Kenway, Haythams father, Connors grandfather and A pirate turned Assassin. This is probably my 2nd favorite Assassins Creed game but its really not an AC game in a lot of ways, Ill explain.

Gameplay: The gameplay of this game is great, it plays super smooth and really emulates that pirate life while also playing like an Assassins Creed game. The combat plays similar to AC3 which is good but there were a lot of thing is liked better about AC3, for example you only get duel swords, hidden blades and muskets in this game to fight with and aside from other smalltime gear that's basically it. Unlike the huge arenol of weapons in 3 that provided a lot of openness to play style AC4 can get a bit repetitive over time. The other huge gameplay mechanic is the Naval combat system which is much smoother than AC3s and takes up a vast majority of gameplay, This is where this game really shines and makes for hours of good grinding and fun, the map is also huge and at this point in the series is the biggest map so far. I found this game very satisfying to progress though, there's also a wide assortment of mini games, side activities and deep sea dives that really makes this game good. The DLC Freedom Cry is short but one of the best ones (up to this point in the franchise) so far.

Voice Acting, Music, Graphics: This game is just as beautiful visually as it is musically. This game not only has great abeyance in the crisp atmosphere but fun music, Sea shanties and Peak voice acting in the franchise so far. Edwards character gives one of the best performances in the franchise competing with Ezio easily and is really a relatable guy.

Story/ Minor spoilers: The story in modern day follows after the events of 3 where we play as a nameless first person Ipad employee at a French Ubstergo head quarters looking though the memories of Edward so they can use it to make an animus video game out of it. (yup cringy and dumb) The in animus story Follows as a prequel to 3 with Connors grandfather Edward who is a swav pirate playboy only looking to score on loot but is a good man at heart. In the very beginning he steals assassin stuff and uses it to try and steal the ultimate treasure. The reason I would say this isn't a true AC game is because you aren't a true Assassins till the final act which considering this was one of the longer ac games before the rpg era this felt like way too long to be just some guy with assassins stuff but at the same time you could argue Edwards story is what makes him a true assassin too, You'll know what I'm talkin about. Ill let you uncover the rest of the story for yourselves I don't want to spoil much. This story sounds light hearted and fun but it gets very deep and personal and bitter sweet at the end. Next to the Ezio trilogy this is probably the 2nd best story Ubisoft has rolled out of Assassins Creed and if you like pirate games or assassins creed I highly recommend this game. Aside from Sea of Thieves this is the best pirate game on the market as of the time of writing this.
Overall 9/10

Resident evil 5 is a long anticipated sequel to RE4 bringing a new concept to Resident Evil that hadn't been in the franchise before, Co-op but does it hold up to RE4s legendary status? Maybe, I'll Explain.

Gameplay: Resident Evil 5s gameplay follows very closely to Re4 with over the shoulder action mixed with some survival horror elements. The biggest thing RE5 has to offer is the co-op feature which really changed the shape of this franchise. Now you didn't have to endure these games alone you always have either a friend or an AI there to help you or get in the way. This both innovates but also hurts the game, its innovative now having a friend and honestly this Co-op is pure fun but it definitely hurts this game too because well, the game really isn't as scary with a friend. Not to say it cant be scary In general I found RE5 to be a huge step down in horror from RE4 I also put this blame onto the lack of gore and dismemberment in this game plus lets be real, Its hard to be scared in bright and sunny Africa, that's like making Resident Evil take place on a beautiful sunny beach. I certainly think there are ways to make this work but the way that its done in this current version of RE5 just isn't on the same level as 4. On top of that if you don't have friend I think its safe to say the Co-op Ai in this game sucks. It gets in the way and wastes ammo every chance it gets. This game also dropped the inclusion of puzzles and the "puzzles" we got in this game are really just going from point A and pulling a lever while your buddy goes to point B and pulls another lever, Yeah not the best.

Graphics, Voice Acting, Music: The graphics on resident evil 5 are fantastic still to this day. The cutscenes and small details in the game are still extremely crisp. The music and voice acting is all well done and fits the atmosphere well. The main cast of characters are all well done and give great performances, especially this version of Wesker.

Story/ Minor Spoilers: This story Follows Chris Redfield after the events of Code veronica 10 years later working for a new anti bioterrorism group called the BSAA. Chis works with a new partner Sheva to uncover the secrets of Africa and what Tircell and other terrorists are collaborating on. Wesker is the main villain of this game and we see the return of Jill Valentine as well. The enemies are called Majini but are essentially Ganado's from RE4. This game leans into the action side of resident evil and even though its fun and has a decent story it certainly looses that horror element of the past. The DLCs and bonus modes like Mercenaries are all fantastic and will give the player lots to do, You can start with Lost in Nightmares first if you want to before you play the main game. I wouldn't say RE5 is the best of the franchise or even the best of the Plagua trilogy games (4,5 and 6) but its almost certainty a fan favorite and it plays smooth and balances well and for that I have to give it a 8.5/10

Resident Evil: Revelations 1 is a spin off taking place before the events of re5 and after re4. It follows the story of Chris Redfield and Jill Valentine and a mission involving the BSAA in the Mediterranean sea. This was a 3DS game originally so this is a pretty well done remaster of the original port.

Gameplay: So this game plays like an episodic TV adventure kinda like a Telltale game or life is strange. Each episode ending on a cliff hanger to add suspense to the game, if that's not the reason then I don't know why this game is set up like that because it didn't release episodically so it kinda makes no sense but whatever. This game plays very close to re5 but smaller and implements this scanner gun to find collectibles and scan objects and enemies. Scanning enough gives you free items for healing and such. Even though this game is very close to RE5 it plays closer to the older games with slower pacing and more focus on puzzles and saving ammo, so depending on the person you could love or hate this. Unlike re5 there is no shop to buy and sell treasures instead you find upgrades for guns and equip them at item box stations.

Voice Acting, Music and Graphics: The voice Acting is ok, definitely not the best in the franchise but not the worst either. The dialogue can get very cringe with a cast of pretty forgettable characters. One of the main villain's looks like count Dooku from the animated clone wars series but has the voice of a young man, The character design in this game is wacky as hell. The music isn't bad but isn't great either it does fit the narrative but also feels very forgettable and the graphics look pretty decent for a 3Ds port.

Story/ Minor Spoilers: The story of this game is pretty self contained and is only briefly mentioned in revelations 2. The plot is super convoluted and very hard to explain without spoiling stuff basically the BSAA is investigating the terrorist organization veltro that decimated a floating smart city in the middle of the Mediterranean. Most of the game you are on a cruse ship but you visit other locations and go somewhere in northern Russia. Honestly this game isn't terrible for a small spin off from the DS but the game definitely doesn't hold up to anything the main line games are. Revelations 2 is drastically better than this game when it comes to story and horror. Its hard to take this game seriously when it feels like this game doesn't take itself seriously. Like there are characters literally called Goofball and Jack**s... The gameplay tries to be both old resident evil horror and re5 action and I feel like it kinda doesn't work but it doesn't fail if that makes sense. So yeah this is one of those games I've met people who love it and people who hate it. Personally I could go either way with it. It's not terrible but not amazing either. Is it worth playing? well that's up to you really.

Rating: 6/10 Average

Watch dogs 2 is a sequel to Watch Dogs (duh) and vastly improves over the hacking system, open world. The whole vibe and story of this game is a huge change from the monotone first game but some of these changes aren't super great, Ill explain.

Gameplay: The whole hacking dynamic of this game feels different than watch dogs 1. Hacking wise this game got significantly better than watch dogs 1, now you have a drone you can free use anywhere and race car toy to hack stuff you cant reach on foot. You can hack drive cars, and a lot more objects in the game and use them in different ways. All of which makes this games hacking much more fun and satisfying. The location is also now bright and sunny, colorful san Francisco which again is a much better and more interesting environment then WD1. Where this game starts to suck is the combat and stealth, Much like the first game you are heavily encouraged to stealth this game because it is super easy to get shot and die but the stealth mechanics are significantly worse. The Ai seems to see me though walls and always know where I am and I remember finding this one way more frustrating than WD1 in just the first few minutes.

Graphics, Voice Acting, Music: This game is visually beautiful and lively with the color pallet/ map layout and a clean graphic composition of characters, objects and places in this environment. The voice acting is a lot better and more believable but is over shadowed with very cringe dialogue and goofy characters. This game swaps out Aiden from WD1 with Marcus and a bunch of other forgettable goofy characters. Realistically the only person you will probably remember is "the punk dude in the rave mask" or Wrench; funny thing is I haven't met anyone who actually remembers these characters names. Resident Evil 6 is a 3rd person Action Horror game and a long awaited sequel to Resident Evil 5. This game has a huge split in fan opinions, some hating it and some loving it. It has 4 campaigns with each one devoting itself to different gameplay types so what is the issue here exactly? Well this game is a little too ambitious for its own good.

Gameplay: Like re5 its still a 3rd person over the shoulder shooter, this was the first mainline resident evil to include movement and shooting which has stayed in the franchise since and honestly has had a long time coming. This game added in the ability to dive backwards and roll around on the ground and roll over obstacles while allowing you to snap to cover systems. You can preform melee moves whenever you want and counter attacks, you can aim down your sites or fire from the hip and do this weird quick shot thing. This all sounds like a better more flexible gears of war with faster more flexible movement and I think that's the first problem with RE6 , the gameplay doesn't fit the genre or resident evil. Notice how I didn't call this a survival horror game? well, it just isn't one. This game also went all in on the Quick time events from RE4 and 5 and honestly over did it. It just has WAY TOO MANY quick time events and almost every single door in the game you have to que up with your co-op partner and kick down and its just annoying after a while. Yes, this game continues the Co-op feature from 5 and this game also has some fun moments where you can cross paths with other people in their campaigns and have 4 characters on screen in a section at once. its a very cool feature that has only been done one other time by Capcom in Devil May Cry 5 and I wish more games had this. This games campaigns also have 4 different play styles but also all share the same play style. What I mean is, Leon's story is the closest thing you'll get to the old games with all zombie enemies, Chris's story is like the last section of re5 with Plaga type enemies shooting at you with guns, so its like a weird monster shooter game, Jakes story has stealth, melee, shooting with a nemesis wannabe following you around, Ada's story is sorta a mix of all of them. The thing is all of these campaigns are all filled with action and very, VERY little puzzle solving (mostly in Adas story). There are no treasures just lame chess piece currency, a weird skill store tree thing, there are first aid sprays but you mostly use TICTACs FOR HEALING... So basically everything that was core to Resident evil in the past is gone here, This game isn't really scary at all either. The C Virus is the most annoying virus on earth where one guy will basically be a plaga enemy while another guy will turn into an armored monster or in the case of the bosses they turn into things like a Clayface monster? and Man who turns into a Dog who turns into a T Rex who turns into a Giant house fly/ monster thing????........ yeah this was seriously what they thought resident evil was going to be for a while. Now as bad as this all sounds it was actually a very balanced and fun game to play though just not a survival horror game or a resident evil game for that matter. I've heard this so many times and its true this game must have been made by Paul Anderson (who made the live action movies) and Michael bay, the amount of 'run away from expositions' or 'plane/ helicopter crashes' in this game is just well, too many for any one resident evil game.

Graphics, Voice Acting, Music: The graphics for this game honestly don't look too bad and still hold up and the voice acting is pretty good. I mean these seasoned voice actors did good with the script they were given and gave great performances. The music fits the game pretty well but doesn't evoke any horror or scary elements whatso ever.

Story/ SPOILER WARNING (I wont spoil everything just some obvious stuff): SO, the story to this game is super hard to explain because its very convoluted and a lot of the motivation for the villain's feels obscured and weak as hell. Basically Leon and a new partner Helana (Discount Claire) are framed for killing the president and a zombie outbreak spreads on a college campus in the USA this for some reason takes them to a cathedra that happens to be on top of a crypt/ mining cave, that's probably 3 times bigger than the Paris catacombs set somewhere in the US even though nothing like this exists here and America isn't even old enough to have this. They then figure out the national security advisor is behind it and travel to china to fight him. (That isn't a huge spoiler its super obvious he's the villain in like the first cutscene also who cares the story sucks) Chris's story and Jakes story are split over 6 months where Chris and (Chris Jr) Peirce, are fighting bioterrorism in Edonia and run across Jake before Chris gets amnesia then he just hangs out in bars for a while until Chris Jr brings him back and immediately gives him a gun and lets him play captain for a mission or two before realizing Ada got his team killed and decides to go on an Ada hunt in china 6 months later. Jakes story starts in Edonia and Meets Sherry from RE2 (all grown up and over sexualized which is kinda weird but whatever) and the world need his blood for a cure (cuz hes Weskers son) and they have (Discount Nemesis) chasing them through their story. They get captured and don't decide to escape until 6 months later (for no reason) and they end up in china, so basically everyone ends up in china.

SO there's 2 Villain's in this game and the second one I cant talk about without spoiling it but their motivations (like I said) are weak. I also can't really mention Ada's story without spoiling anything so definitely play hers last. Originally you had to unlock her story after finishing the others so idk why they changed that, her story spoils everything. Anyways this story is full of plot holes and goofy moments that just feel out of place but the gameplay is fun and their are a lot of extra game modes included. With friends the play value of this game is pretty high and so id say for that reason its worth playing. 7/10

Resident Evil: Village or Resident Evil 8 is a sequel to Resident Evil 7 (duh) and continues the story of Ethan after the events of the baker incident. The gameplay follows closely to Resident Evil 4 and in a lot of ways is a spiritual successor to RE4, Ill Explain.

Gameplay: Re Villages game play is still a first person game (In a recent update added 3rd person mode) with Ethan as the main playable character, which is weird since this is the first time Re followed up one game into another with the same main character. The UI in this game uses an inventory case much like the one from RE4 with size management, A treasure menu, A key Menu and a map menu. There is a merchant in this game named 'The Duke' that works similar to the merchant from RE4 where you can buy sell and upgrade weapons and treasures to him. The map in this game and level design is also reminiscent of RE4 with of course a village and a castle but also a swamp and instead of an island the factory area plays a similar roll to that of the island as well. The enemies remind me of the re4 enemies being humanoid creatures with weapons but this time we have a lot of Romanian mythology coming though this game with vampire, werewolf and witch enemies throughout the game. (which are not of super natural origin in this game). Arguably the weakest part of the game or the part people seem to like the least (Yup just like re4s island) The factory. This area has cyborg zombie enemies and it is, at least to me a spooky section of the game but this area and the swamp (reservoir) are probably the most tedious areas with the most annoying puzzles. The highlight of this game is most definitely the castle unfortunately you aren't there very long and visit it within the first act of the game. Heisenberg is a cool enemy and is one of the 4 main bosses of the game but his controlling metal power feels super out of place for resident evil (like he's basically magneto). Aside from these things the overall game is super fun to traverse and I still really liked the factory area. There is an action section in this game where you play as Chris and it is a fun part but again feels super out of left field from the rest of the game.

Graphics, Voice acting, Music: The graphics are once again absolutely gorgeous and breathe taking. The amount of detail put into the environments, especially the castle is top notch. This games voice acting is pretty well done and the performances are all round fantastic, I did however find annoying that Chris's voice actor is clearly the same guy who played Carlos from the re3 remake and even though he does a great job and usually does with the games he's in, it just annoys me how similar they sound. I'm sure new comers to the franchise who briefly played re3 and re7 and then played village must be a bit confused especially since the Chris we got in Re7 looked nothing like any other version of Chris including this one, Aside from this I did like him a lot.

Story/ Minor Spoilers: Re villages story basically goes, after Ethan moved to Europe and starting a family with Mia, Chris suddenly assassinates Mia in their house (This isn't a major spoiler it was literally in the trailers) and Ethan reacts to it like Chris just told him an offensive joke, anyways from here Ethan finds himself searching for his daughter in a village over looked by a castle and finding all the horrors that await here. The story and why all of this happens (I wont spoil here) I will say it is kinda dumb, why Chris doesn't just communicate more details to Ethan is beyond me but whatever. From the Village you explore a Castle, Reservoir, Factory and small mansion and have to kill 4 lords of the land before facing the villain mother Maranda. There are a lot of lore things to look out for that ties this game back to the origins of resident evil and definitely makes a great revelation for long time fans to find and a couple of cool twists in the story you wont see coming. Aside from areas I had mentioned in this game that people didn't like I also found Mother Maranda to be a bit of a weak villain, we hardly see her till the end of the game and I do wish this game (if this game really wants to be like RE4) was a bit longer but oh well. Ethan's character is something I've never understood since 7, there are some major plot points in this game that explain him and things that happened in 7 better but I'm referring to him as a person. He is wrapped up in mystery (I remember seeing an Easter egg in re5 with his name mentioned in a note) I thought he might end up being more important to the overall lore especially since they went though trouble to hide his face only for it to not matter and for them to show it in 3rd person mode. I don't understand the secrecy , I thought maybe we are supposed to be Ethan as the player but clearly this game made that clear, that's not the case. He's also got more of a Leon personality in this game compared to 7 so I guess he has some character development but it feels like Capcom didn't know what direction to pick with Ethan and now the Winter family story ends with the Rose DLC and I don't get why, especially since 9 is supposed to end this Molded Trilogy why not keep this new family around till the end of the trilogy? Anyways, aside from all of this we got to see the return of Mercenaries mode which was great but I'm not super keen on the changes they made to it. I just don't enjoy how linear it is compared to how it once was but the Merchant check points were cool each time though, I hope they keep that aspect going in the RE4 Remake. Overall if you like RE4 you'll probably love this game 9/10

Assassins Creed Odyssey is a sequel to Assassins Creed Origins present day story and a prequel to the entire franchise in the Animus past story. There are things that are great about this game and things that aren't so great, for one this is hardly an assassins creed game and more of a standalone prequel in the same universe, If the present day story didn't exist I wouldn't even call it a sequel to Origins because this game has hardly anything to do with that story aside from a few long winded tie-ins in one of the dlcs. Personally I think this game leans WAYYY too far into the RPG aspects of the last game and at times I forget I'm even still playing an AC game, with that being said there's a lot to unpack here so lets start with the gameplay.

Gameplay: This game does play similar to origins and definitely uses the same engine so gameplay wise it is in many ways a origins successor. It has the same Eagle system instead of Eagle Vision, It has a skill tree but it builds much differently in this game and it has the same rpg mechanics as origins but here they are turned up to a thousand. Now You have individual armor pieces that you can reskin as any armor you find throughout the game (added after an update and is pretty cool customization wise). It has skill abilities you set for Bow, and Assassins/ Warrior, which personally I find annoying because you can only use 4 at a time so you constantly have to pause to switch them. All the different bows from origins have been wrapped up into one bow with different abilities for that bow (which I guess is better). You still have a full country to explore with an a*s load of side quests to the point where you will feel very overwhelmed in the beginning and all the areas are level locked similar to the last game. There are some big rpg changes this game made that definitely hurt this game and help it at the same time, one of which is the freedom of making choices and dialogue. Now there was a bit of this in origins on decisions that ultimately don't matter and probably wouldn't change history and I get the argument with this game and this trilogy (Origins, Odyssey and Valhalla) is that "this is all taking place before prewritten history and we do know some of the historical stuff from this period but a lot of the details are unclear so we can just make stuff up to make a better game" and all of that is true and the choices definitely make the game more interesting and sometimes fun but it also hurts this game because it doesn't feel like we are replaying a historical event it feels like we are playing a fantasy RPG. This game also goes way overboard with the fantasy stuff but Ill get into that in a bit and you might say Origins did this too but with Origins it at the very least kept this stuff exclusive to the DLC and late game side quests and even still kept it to a minimum, Origins still felt like an historical piece and this game loses that feeling after a while. The combat in this game has some great and not so great moments. This game has like I said a skill tree and skill points a long to spend it on but along with that you have skill enhancing stats (mastery skills) you can use those points to upgrade which makes this games build extremely rpg customizable and unless you are a skilled rpg player who likes making builds you will probably find yourself dealing with a lot of squishy enemies for 95% of the time you play. Unlike Origins you arent expected to just buy every skill you are expected to buy specific ones you want along with certain mastery skills to get stronger. If you aren't used to making builds you probably should just look up over powered builds for this game on youtube and follow one because even at end DLC level 80 where I'm very over powered and can wipe the floors with most enemies I still find myself dealing with squishy enemies and it doesn't make the game harder it just makes playing it more annoying. In Origins you naturally became over powered as the game progressed but in this one you have to very specifically build yourself to be stronger or you probably wont have a good time playing. With all that being said you can get some great over powered abilities that are amazing to use so much so at times your character feels like a super hero. On the topic of gameplay there are a few minor changes I didn't like, like not being able to call your horse into certain areas, not being able to save in certain areas, if you die in certain areas the game doesn't save and you have to redo it, No hidden blade just a broken spear used like a dagger, I could go on and on with the small changes that got aggravating after a long period of time or just change the aspect of an AC game in a bad way. On a lighter note, this game also brings back the Naval combat from black flag but revamped and when your boat is at a high upgrade status its a lot of fun to use. When I did use the naval combat I had a lot of fun but I hardly needed to use the boat because you can just fast travel everywhere.

Graphics, Voice Acting and Music:
The graphics of this game are as always with Assassins Creed beautiful and you get pretty much the whole country of Greece to explore feely which with the ocean stretches out much farther than Origins did. The voice acting in this game isn't terrible but certain characters do sound like s**t, most of the time its just npcs but sometimes its main characters too. The dialogue in this game can be really bad at times too and feel out of place and uneven. There were moments that were really sad and touching or funny that worked great but moments that absolutely fell apart under the circumstances. The music in this game is pretty decent and at times very emotional. They have yet again, another remix of Ezio's Family on the main menu and I loved it the first time I heard it but after like 200 hours of this game I was ready to mute the menu music because it gets sickening so fast (They should have just put that in certain cutscenes in the game). They did make a new humming theme for this game and it works really well, I don't know what its called but they should have highlighted that and made that the main theme for this game and not Ezio's Family (I love Ezio to death but move on from him already Ubisoft.)

Story/ Some Spoilers: So in this game you can pick which character you want to play as Kassandra or Alexios. Not sure why Alexio's is the advertised option everywhere when they made the decision that Kassandra was the canon choice, Kassandra's voice actor is much better than Alexios anyways. In the game they use the DNA found on a broken sphere of Leonidas to see Kassandra's memories (If you pick Alexios they switch spots) and that's how the game picks up. The modern day story continues with Llyla from Origins and aside from very moments you never really leave the animus. Towards the end of the game and in the DLC the modern day story gets more interesting but I also feel like the decision they made with the present day story ending and how it involves Kassandra was a bit lore breaking and leaves us with more questions than answers and again breaks that realm of "this is historical fiction". Not much happens in the main story for most of the game, everything takes place during the Athens and spartan war and there are like 3-4 different major endings to this game you can get in any order. (1) The Family storyline where you basically try to fix your family ties, If you save the entire family and restore it you get a happy ending but it feels like this ending shouldn't be canon since none of them show up in the DLC which realistically they absolutely would have. (2) The Odyssey hero/ Atlantis storyline where you try to recover artifacts and fight mythical beings like Medusa to keep Atlantis safe and this one has the ending I was talking about where the modern day ending feels ridiculous and probably breaks canon for the other games somehow. I wont spoil what I mean but if you play it you will see what I mean (It's one of those story implications of well if this person was here the whole time where were they during the events of the other games). (3) The Cult storyline which involves hunting down the cult at your own pace. This ending absolutely should have (Assuming you picked Kassandra) Alexios in it because of his time with the cult and the ending to this questline felt super anti-climactic. The openness to how and when you complete all these quests is fun but it also is frustrating to get certain endings before other ones and the fact that these different quest lines endings don't effect one another also makes them a bit lack luster. A lot of what I am saying will make more sense when you play it yourself and a lot of the choices throughout the game don't matter. I've heard a lot of people say this game is "the origins game for the Templars" and unless Valhalla says something about this game that I didn't know from playing it then I'm not sure what they are talking about. The Villains of this game are The Cult of Kosmos and in the entire main story its implied they are going to turn into the Order of Ancients, so naturally to stick with this idea I let the leader live at the end thinking it would make sense since they mention making a better organization or something and well after playing the Hidden blade DLC its made clear they are completely different organizations and the Order of Ancients is older. So honestly it makes me question the point in this story and why it exists, why does Kassandra exist and now play a huge roll in the AC universe? I did play the Atlantis DLC and its very similar to the idea of the cursed pharaoh DLC from Origins where you are going to the underworld fantasy lands and I do and don't like it for more of the same reasons, playing it for 20 hours I forgot I was even playing assassins creed anymore because its so over the top but like the DLC in origins the worlds do look great and the Isu/ Gods are interesting. This is also a double edged sword because I think making the Isu their own established characters with very human personalities kinda ruins the mystery and mystique of not knowing what they really are like in the earlier games. I remember meeting the holograms of them in the Ezio games and thinking "wow they are kinda like aliens almost" but now they we meet them they are just taller angry people. I guess my last critique of this game is that its simply too long. I thought Origins was a long game clocking in at 80-101 hours with the DLC this game supposedly is only 150-160 with the DLC but I'm currently at 200 hours at the very end of the last DLC. I think the main issue with this game is the fact that it tries to do too many different things at once, like its trying to be a Greek mythology game, A first civilization game, An assassins Creed game, An RPG, A choice based game, A historical fiction game and I think its all just too much for one game to have.

Overall it was a fun but frustrating game that was too long and doesn't really have much to do with the Assassin and Templar conflict and breaches the line of too fantasy with not much core assassin gameplay, 7.5/10

Such a great investment for PC gamers! I was skeptical of the touch pads but fell in love with them soon enough. The only draw back is that the right pad gets oily after use. Granted, it still responds great, but the thumb starts slipping and feeling oily. Otherwise, I have to agree with what many others have said: the X, Y, A, B buttons are indeed incredibly awkward to reach in-game. And if you're like me, you're playing at night, in the day, and its a pain having to reach so far down and to the side to use them. However, the controller is completely customize-able and that problem can easily be fixed by re-assigning the buttons.

That being said, the customization is a bit overwhelming for those games that still require it. I love that the Steam community has a vast base of pre-loaded settings you can choose from if need be. But I will say that for some games--like Skyrim, Oblivion, Fall-out, and the likes--I still revert to mouse and keyboard. Which, is still legit with the Steam Link. Feel free to check out my review on it as well.

Where to start? The Steam Link is so awesome! The set-up blew me away at how easy it was. Literally, I got home for lunch break and saw this and the controller at my front door and was like, "Sure, I'll go ahead and try to set it up now so I can play after work." Less than five minutes later I find myself already synced to and enjoying Steam Big Picture mode on my TV.

I am very pleased with the transfer rate of data between TV and computer. I always hated the lag of connecting my gaming PC to a large TV, but the Link makes it flawless. So worth the $50 I spent on it. And the smoothness of how it syncs with Steam accounts is so fast. I am really proud of how the interface is, also, with the Steam Big Picture mode. Whats more? I can still use a mouse and keyboard for those games that are just better with them--like Oblivion, Skyrim, Fallout, etc. All you have to do is plug in a wireless mouse/keyboard and you're good to go!

As far as entertainment, I love the Steam Link. I live in a small house, so my gaming PC is by my TV, but all my seating makes it awkward for people to watch my monitor. Having the Steam Link lets me now stream high-quality to the TV even if I'm still playing on my computer. So yes, you can use you're mouse/keyboard even with the Steam Controller plugged in. At first, I was thrown off with the sound. With the Link on, it defaults to the TV's sound, which in my case stinks. But after I turn the TV volume all the way down and then unmute my PC, we are back in business (it automatically mutes you're PC volume).

I highly recommend for anyone wanting to do everything their PC does but from the comfort of their couch. You can pretty much do anything indeed. Just minimize Steam and the Link functions as an extension of you PC. Your TV becomes a mirror of you monitor.
