The reason I gave this game a full star rating is because I've made the most out of the game before it really hit the lagging phase. Bethesda is one of the few gaming developers who are known to make huge games. Elder Scrolls are one of them. Skyrim is a very huge game. More so, the whole province of Skyrim is massively detailed. You can even see a colony of ants on a tree stump. What I like about Skyrim is you can create a character and go do what you want to do and however you want to do. If only Bethesda can jumpstart on the next patch to fix the disgusting horrible lags and the stressful pain of framerate drops then the PS3 version can be a truly wonderful and huge experience to you all. Until then, make the most out of this game before it gets to a point of unplayable. Then wait for Bethesda to finally make a patch that will fix the lag problems.

When I heard the next installment of the Tekken series, to be honest, I was just a little bit interested in. I saw the arcade version of it when I had a trip in the Philippines and I knew that it was primarily powered by the PS3 system which is quite amazing on how it looked. Of course, I knew the game is going to be hitting to the PS3 but didn't expect it to also be released on the Xbox 360 as well.  Namco introduced motion blur effect which made the game look really good and playing the game in HD just made the graphics and everything else look way better. There are more characters but none of them really appealed to me, except a few like Lars and Leo. The only problem in this game is the introduction of juggling your opponent. I know there are lot of Tekken fans out there that doesn't like this at all, including me but it's something to be dealt with anyways. Also, the nightmare train is really a cluster of nightmare which was one of the trophies for acquiring the platinum. I've platinum Tekken 6 twice and for the hard parts like defeating Nancy and completing the Nightmare train stage were seriously lucky for me. Overall, Tekken 6 is the latest and best game that I've enjoyed so far. I will be looking forward to the next King of Iron Fist Tournament.

I know, I know. If anything could be worse to anyone's perspective on dancing games like for example, Dance Dance Revolution, it would be bad right? Well, not in my case. First of all, I liked DDR and I had really good times playing it at the arcades and at home. It's much fun when you're playing the game with a friend. When times long passed, I thought that I would never get up and play a dancing game ever again until one particular dancing game and that's Michael Jackson The Experience. Since I already own a PS Move motion controller and I was subscribing from Gamefly, I thought I would take the chance to rent the game and check it out. Of course, for many things, I was a bit skeptical at first. As part of the title says: The Experience, it's telling me that I would be in the shoes of the King of Pop and experience the dancing moves and have me like his music more than ever. Which precisely what this game was making an impression out of me. So I rented the game, booted up my PS3, loaded in the disc, start it up, and play with my PS Move motion controller. Let me tell ya, it was the best experience of a dancing game I ever had since Dance Dance Revolution Extreme. There were moves that everyone had or dreamed of actually performing. You get the chance to do so in his popular hit songs like Billie Jean, Smooth Criminal, Thriller, Beat it, and other most memorable and favorable his songs. After renting for a month, thinking of getting the game, it was time to finally decide on owning it. Besides, the game seems to be getting rare as most are like Fatal Frame and perhaps becoming underrated as DDR was back then. The only thing that's a downside is that this game only has one DLC when I'm expecting that there will be more in the future. After its release and it's one and only DLC song, they haven't released any other DLC songs. It would be great to play songs like Man in the Mirror, Scream, You Rock My World, Jam, and even Hold My Hand. I think this game deserves better. It's like saying that it's already polished but it needs to polish more to get that shining effect that MJ has done so many times on stage, in front of thousands, if not millions of his fans. Overall, this game is really fun and it reminds me how great the King of Pop was. Wait, let me rephrase that. Ir reminds me how awesome the King of Pop, forever.

The series as we know it has become a milking franchise. I'm glad I got this as a gift and I truly am grateful to have this added to my video game collection. However, this game is just literally another $60 DLC. While the single player campaign is much better, the multiplayer is the same thing. They just added things in. Spec Ops returns, this time being more "innovative". There's two modes in Spec Ops, one is the usual Spec Ops missions. The same treatment you get like the one in MW2. The other mode is Spec Ops Survival. Now for this kind of mode, I gotta say, it's way better than the, imo, the awful zombies mode that everyone likes in Black Ops. Don't get me wrong, zombies is fun but that's not what Call of Duty is all about. In fact, zombies in Call of Duty are not compatible with each other and yet Treyarch feeds this kind of worthless feature into the series in which destroys what the series truly represents. Which is being a true military shooter game. MW3 seemed to do justice on that part. Sure the game engine is already established that's not needed for any changes but it gets old. I am impressed with the streamline technology that the game has. What others don't know is that there are maps in MW3 that are copied and pasted from MW1 and perhaps MW2. There are multiplayer maps where I felt that this place seemed so familiar that some of them looked like two maps merged into one and then covered over a transparent blanket where any one is unable to look under it whatsoever. While multiplayer is still the same thing and I still get the fun out of it when I play the game online, I still taken back where it's all the same thing. Others would enjoy rehashed video games but for me, I want something new and fresh. But why did I still get the game? I want to know what happens next in the story of the Modern Warfare series and I was interested in Spec Ops survival since they first introduce it from a trailer. I hope this is the very last Call of Duty game for me to own, otherwise I'm just going to buy future titles, used. If they ever decided to go with online pass in the future, I would go and buy it myself at PSN store because I would still buy them used no matter what. That shows that I no longer support the series yet I would probably still play future CoD titles. Weird dilemma, right? But, it's just how it is I guess and to each his or her own. Either like it, hate it, or even both at the same time.

I used to own the first Way of the Samurai game on the PS2 and it was the best Samurai type of video game I'v ever played next to Bushido Blade on the PS1. I'm a sucker for Samurai video games and Way of the Samurai is one of the top games for anyone looking to hack and slash at their enemies. Way of the Samurai 2, unfortunately I never got my hands on but eventually I did rented it one time and played it. It was better yet some features in the game was questionable. When Way of the Samurai 3 came around and this time for the PS3, I was ready to get my samurai spirit unleashed within me once again. The third game in the series finally improved the features that lacked from both the first and the second. So you're pretty much looking at the third game that has been merged by 1 and 2 together then got improved by its features. Of course, there are a number of new things added in the game such as the ability to create your very own sword. Gratefully, WOTS3 does not have a limit to the number of days like the two previous games and so you get to play it at your own pace yet still have to attaining yourself to the story the game offers. There are only two problems about this game. First of all, the graphics. Although, slightly improved, it still looks like it was a PS2 port, which it wasn't. Unless the third game WAS planned to be released on the PS2 before. If they improved the engine (maybe more than it is), it would have been more smoother, more precise gameplaye-wise, and more detailed on the textures. With over 20 endings, the game can keep one busy the most and again, since there's no limit to how many game days you can play, the game is more open-worldish. So, while this is getting rare and also an underrated game, I'll be waiting for Way of the Samurai 4 to be distributed over here in America soon.

Nintendo does it again.

So much to see and do in this game, it's crazy. Every part of the background and the characters look like they were crafted out of household items. Paper cups, towel rolls, cardboard, coffee creamers, milk cartons, you name it. The attention to detail is positively bonkers. There is so much going on at the same time in the stages and so much to do. The camera focuses on your character, the foreground and background will be blurred a little bit until you aim at something in either. Pretty neat visual effect. The 3-d presentation of the stages is handled flawlessly, and you have to pay attention because the entrances to some hidden areas are visible when they're near the edge of the screen, but as you approach it and the camera follows you, it obscures the entrance.

It doesn't seem to be that difficult a game, but if you're having trouble you can change the gameplay to "mellow mode" which gives Yoshi wings that let him float indefinitely and each enemy consumed produces two eggs instead of one.

A lot of replay value here, as each stage can have the camera flip to the other side and what was now hidden in the foreground is now visible in the background. You'll need to revisit stages several times to gather everything, forwards and backwards. Pretty innovative.

All in all, it feels like you're playing a Pixar movie. Enough with this review. I'm heading back to playing the game!

This game is a visual masterpiece and it plays magnificently. It's more true to the SNES (or other ports of) Yoshi's Island than "Yoshi's Crafted World" on the Switch. The targeting system is retained from the original game, and to be quite honest, I think the soundtrack is much better on this game than the Switch sequel. Don't know how I missed this game when it came out, guess I was a little late to the Wii U party. But this game is a must-have if you're a fan of platformers like the other Mario and Yoshi kind of games.

Unlike the other games, you eat enemies and produce yarn balls instead of eggs from what I assume is a dinosaur cloaca (like a chicken, one orifice, two purposes - manual doesn't really clarify the method of delivery,) or you can jump up and punch yarn boxes like those white and green cubes in the other games to produce as many yarn balls as you can have follow you, sometimes they produce big balls that do a lot more damage. There's also unlockable badges that can be used for different things, like being able to use big balls on an entire stage.

Visuals are creative, they really went all out with this one, with Yoshi turning into strands of wisping yarn when warping or going into pipes, etc. Everything looks so photo-realistic in this game, it's unreal. The textures are amazing. Have to blink sometimes just to take it in. The ground you walk around on even flexes under the character's weight, it's a really cool effect. So is the focus filter that blurs the foreground and background. Nintendo really made a flagship game for a console that sadly never got the credit it deserved.

I don't care too much for the amiibo-enhanced gameplay, it does not unlock a CPU controlled second Yoshi like I thought it would, instead, both Yoshi characters respond at the same to your controller input, without regard to their position on the screen, which can get out of hand when trying to jump over obstacles or what-not. Certainly doesn't work like the shadow ninjas on the Ninja Gaiden II game on the NES. Maybe I'll try it again some day, but I found that I did horribly worse trying to control two Yoshi at the same time. If you have to make a jump with one, sometimes the other one will fall down and then follow you around like baby Mario in the first Yoshi's Island game. The amiibo is pretty cute and collectable, for what it's worth (this is actually my first time using or owning one.)

Every stage has the sunshine flowers to collect, as well as skeins of yarns scattered over the stages (yes, I had to look up what they call that packaging of yarn, I never use the stuff,) and if you collect them all you get to re-knit a bunch of different Yoshi patterned fella's.

Oh, and then there's big ol' giant Yoshi, the honey badger in Yoshi world.

The more I play the game, the more I like it. I bought Yoshi's Crafted World for the Switch about a week or two before I discovered this game, and I'm starting to think that this is the better of the two. The other one is great, too, don't get me wrong, but this one's gameplay is closer to the original Yoshi's Island, and without that annoying crying baby Mario in the bubble every time you get hit.

Just get it. :-)

I don't know what's wrong, but you can try to move your character a lot of the time and either it freezes in place, you can't move, and it's showing the running animation, and then sometimes it will let you move but you're just moving around a standing character that doesn't animate at all.

It feels like this game was released unfinished, and I even downloaded the most recent update for it before playing, too. Not a fun experience and really don't have any desire to play it again after the first day.

Oh. My. - This is the most epic game I have played in a long time.

Let me preface this by saying that Symphony of the Night and Nocturne in the Moonlight (Japanese Saturn version that let you play as Trevor or Maria from the start screen and had a couple extra levels and songs) is my absolute favorite game of all time thus far, and if you're familiar with the gameplay on either one of those games you will feel right at home with this one.

Holy cow. The game is animated beautifully and it IS the true sequel to the SOTN game on a home console. I loved the GBA and DS sequels that were inspired by SOTN, but this one is just amazing. If you didn't know the title to it, you would seriously think it was a direct sequel. It plays so true to it's Castlevania roots, it's insane. Seems like Konami would want to have this game under their belt and have funded it, crazy that a Kickstarter campaign produced such a magnificent game like this. Everything about it is simply beautiful.

My hat is off to the team that brought this game to life because they made a true sequel to my favorite game of all time, and I'm only a few hours into it so far but I'm betting this game will knock the prequel off it's pillar. Absolutely fantastic job, y'all. I'm so glad that y'all support gamers by releasing games as awesome as this. Really. Hats off. Knocked it outta the park.

This is such a marvelously executed game, it's beautifully rendered in 2-D but with a fluid environment as you maneuver through it. It's interesting to have a character that takes up so little of the screen, it really allows for some interesting stage designs.

I apologize that my picture does not do this game proper justice. It's just one of those gems that you really have to experience for yourself. If you're into Metroid or later Castlevania games, you're going to feel right at home, gameplay-wise. And at $15, that's just the icing on the cake.

I bought the XBox One version, which comes with the original game and the "Definitive Edition," as well as a separate disc with the soundtrack to play on any CD player. Best game purchase in a long time. Right up there with Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.

This game is gorgeous, it plays so fluidly, and it's just an all-out home run, straight outta the park. Hats off to the programmers, the world needs more of these kind of games that speak to the hardcore old-school gamers and also the adventurous new players that didn't get to try this sort of game when the genre first came out.

In the event that I wasn't astoundingly clear and you've read this far - stop. Just click the little icon and put this game in your cart. Trust me.

C'mon, Nintendo. I hate dropping a star for this relatively simple issue, but y'all really dropped the ball on what had the potential to be one of the greatest remakes of one of the most fantastic games in the series.

The Light Cycle Arena game alone makes this game awesome and puts to full use the Wii controller. Seriously. It is awesome and must play. I should end here but I'll do a short review. Very fast paced gameplay (light cycle) that requires skill but also easy to pick up and play. If it was a console launch title it would have astonished and been a must have game for the Light Cycle Arena mode alone and the way you interact with the controller.

The rest of this game is just ok for a Wii title I guess, but nothing stands compared to the light cycle arena mode and racing. The other light cycle and "car" mode of (non-arena) racing is pretty good and the options you can adjust really round out this title as very replayable. Skip the tank game even though it works and is graphically pleasing, skip the people running around disc throwing game, and you can skip the platforming game of the story mode which can be played if you are bored enough. It has production value and serves a story but jumping around the environments collecting stuff is not much fun unless you like a challenge.

Overall, the Light Cycles make this an awesome game earning a 10 out of 10 while the rest of the game gets a respectable score depending on how old you are. Without the Light Cycles there is not much to bring you back to this game again and again like the Light Cycle Arena has done for me. So much fun! Wish it had online play for it. Works with Wii MotionPlus controllers and without. Really amazing arena gameplay, even the slalom and car mode can be good fun. The arena mode plays like the old 2D game of Centipede, with a centipede that keeps getting bigger and bigger, you have to not double back on to it as it races around the screen; the arena stuff is the same, but in a 3D environment and you can jump over yours and others trails. With options even to make the cycle trail very long or very short so that you have to get very close and be very fast.

Perfect Wii controller game, but pretty much skip the rest of it if you are not a young child, and a young child would actually enjoy it very much cause it is well made overall and easy to get into for its vehicular modes, but the human disc and ball throwing games are very difficult to play and even understand. So as a racer and arena game it is very good, playing as a human walking around the story mode and trying to play the disc and ball throwing games it is not so great. So it is about 50/50 and again the vehicular portions make it a very worthy game and solid movie game. Would really make a great sequal if they add online with more arenas and race tracks. Just thinking about I'm already giving it a 10 out of 10. It is just to bad the disc throw and ball throw games are so aweful. I have been a gamer for a long time and was frustrated with them but there may be some skill I wasn't grasping in the brief time I played. In the disc game can hit others up close as well as throw a disc but seems getting close and hitting them is the easy way to win and since it is a disc throw game that says something. I don't even know what kind of crazy tennis hybrid they tried with the ball throw but it didn't do anything for me especially since it auto catches, you just throw it back in a funny way. Anyway, it has a really great Light Cycle Arena mode that any Wii owner would enjoy and I wish to see more done with this type of gameplay in the future. Thankfully this game has it covered as best as it can until then.

UPDATE: The game is good, read the prior review for prior thoughts after this paragraph update. It just takes a long time to learn maps, modes and what weapons and class to use to be effective. Not every weapon is the same, the demolition class for instance has armor so the guns are very ineffective, not knowing that they are ineffective results in a lot of frustration playing while you are shooting others many times and dying a lot, and not understanding the game. Once you do learn that it is a good game, especially if you are playing with friends. And there is in-game "platoon" support, with clan tags like in Socom. Speaking of which. If you ever played Socom 2, or 3 on the map Frostfire in respawn mode with explosives turned on, in a full room with 16 players 8v8, that is what this game is often times a lot like. Lots of shooting all over the place and lots of explosions. Additionally, some modes here are similar to the Breach mode of the earlier Socom's as well. So overall it is a good game. I just personally think it was so close to being really great, and it just missed it, but still fun once you understand it, it's even fun most of the time up until you do understand it, so for that reason I change my score from a 3 to a 4.

Multiplayer review because the first few levels of the single player are stupid, no idea how it ends. Now for the multiplayer. A confusing run and gun FPS that sort of works but it's pretty much the worst shooter ever. It's as puzzling as a page in an unknown language. If you are a fan of shooters and have money then rent it to see what a mostly bad game is all about. It's not a game that can be played and keep you interested in coming back to it mostly because of the small map settings and the way the few maps and modes play. That said, it could have been a good game but simply isn't. Its annoying and unpolished and yet somehow works for close quarters combat but ultimately annoying to play. It is unfinished graphically, really ugly when it comes down to it based on whatever game engine they used. The multiplayer maps are really boggled and though various modes can be played on them with slight variations of how gameplay flows, they are small, and it is really a very boggled series of maze maps that lead to close encounters and getting shot in the back a lot and no cover or sense of purpose or direction for the player including seemingly random spawn points in addition to player spawning. As a player you actually get angry at the map design and say I wish they did this, I wish they did that, I want to snipe here, I need to camp here, I need to see this view here sort of thing, but the maps are just highly designed to ultimately I guess make you not want to play. It's a maze with deadends for useless camping. While playing you literally say to yourself I am just wasting time and wish I could get my money back. This review could really only read, "I should have rented it and now I want my money back."

Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 is the better game by far even if you are not a cod player get that game. The guns in MoH are ok and all feel the same with about the same recoil and bullet spray but the heavy gunner is not needed, the sniper is not needed cause it only takes a few hits to die and the heavy is useless with his low power hit detection and high rate of spray, nowhere to set up shop and the sniper has no place to snipe from. Additionally, each class having 12 different guns with 50 different unlocks isn't needed especially when you have to unlock every 50 unlocks for every individual gun individually, and add to that some guns are the same just named Seal instead of Sas. So you get a rifle called the seal gun, and then unlock the same gun but it is the Sas gun. Maybe all those unlocks factor in here. But you can't class unlock scopes so again individual ball breaking unlocking that is pointless for the most part. Each class also has a perk to it but guns are class restricted even though they are all just various assault rifles.

Problems include that often the clip reload animation won't happen so you don't know if you have reloaded, or are reloading at that moment, so you got to press reload a few times and it creates confusion when you don't know if are reloading but really are and have, you just stand there not sure if you have a new clip in or if your character is reloading. Also a few times I couldn't even shoot. Also the sound lags when you shoot. As in pull the trigger and the gun shoots but a second later you then hear it shoot. Seems to occur when at lot is going on, but also all the time.

The maps are pretty much unplayable no matter what mode. It's basically close quarters run and gun on boggled ugly maze maps. It is difficult to tell your team from the enemy because everyone is wearing the same various forms of camo. Servers are good to find maps and the modes you want. But the maps are just terrible. Honestly, if you have cash to burn check out this game cause it has a cool L2 character lean mechanic but there is just no real application for it given the map design, maybe if you got a group of friends you can try to have some fun, but even then the other factors detract from it. Overall, there is something almost good about this game and Battlefield 4 could take a lesson away from it, but after a few hours the initial dislike of the game only deepens hours and days later. The only thing that can save this turd is a map pack. The current maps are interesting because they are highly polished turds and for that I say rent it if you can. Camping doesn't happen a lot and I imagine the highly polished turd factor factors into why the maps are so small and boggled.

Finally, mines are a problem to deal with especially at objectives and if you think about it, some players would rather be a sniper who gets mines as a perk then use an assault rifle class, even though there is no real place to snipe. Literally the most useless class to use, but some players would rather kill you with a mine cause the mines stay around after they die. Medal of Honor: Warfighter is an annoying, broken, seemingly highly designed waste of time that really could have been good but isn't.

The customization, training episodes and general overall presentation is top notch. A lot of the characters and rings are locked though which is disappointing because so many of the characters are locked at first with only about 7 of them available. If you do not update at first and play, and like I did unlock 2 characters and rings and create a custom character, when you do update, all your progress is for nothing. This is the only PS3 game that can't use the game save after update. Had to start all over and customize a character again. And given such a deep customization system including moves it took a long time, can be quick if you want though, and you can go back and change moves and clothes. Top notch stuff. I like how it shows what moves are when selecting with no loading time really. What I did not like is two things. One is the screen bounce while in the ring. All fighting games do it, but it is annoying and can't be turned off. Second thing I didn't like is the way in which you are stuck on the ground. Can't turn that off either. When you hit the ground you either have to do nothing for 5 or more seconds until you can move and get up, or button mash the X cross button to speed up character stun recovery constantly while your character is on the ground. Button mashing becomes very tedious and annoying so I just layed around until I could move after getting bored with button mashing 20 minutes into the gameplay.

So, this game is o.k. and I would give it a 5 star if it didn't have the screen bounce and had an option to turn off that 5 second stun recovery button mash mechanic. Otherwise, gameplay is a little slow but works to make an interesting wrestling environment and the moves are easy and varied. Overall it is cool to great but watch out for that update.

The "Infestation" mode is so much fun and is a great reason why you should play this game now.  It is the online 4 player co-op mode of this game that can also be played offline in single-player mode.  It is you with a bunch of guns and a bunch of aliens to kill.  I have been spending the last 2 days playing Infestation since I got Red Faction Armageddon.  5 Stars cause I don't really like or play zombie survival games or modes, but Infestation is so much fun because all the weapons, and the level design and the way the aliens move and attack.  The game itself I only played the first mission and it was an enjoyable experience; graphics are nice, gameplay mechanics work fine, environments are well designed and look epic space like, plus everything can be destroyed and repaired, etc...  For the price this game is now, I recommend you buy it based solely on my time spent with the Infestation Mode and I would say the actual game seems pretty good as well and I now understand why the "repair the environment" mechanic is here.  Cause in Infestation Mode you shoot epic weapons that destroy everything, and so repairing the environment comes in handy when aliens are shooting and rushing at you.  Also nice to break into a building, by punching a hole in the wall, then turn around and repair it and then hide from the aliens for a moment, cause it gets intense in Infestation Mode.  Finally, I recommend you buy both of the dollar dlc packs for this game, which will both add 2 weapons (4 total) to your weapons inventory in Infestation Mode.  Says they can also be used in single player but I haven't found any weapons lockers yet.  Infestation Mode has 30 rounds per map and around 6 survival maps and 5 defend maps, each with a "dark" less light version. After a few rounds you can select the dlc weapons to be used among the various choices.  I found 3 of them to be very useful nearly all the time, however the NGK-500 not so much later on or even at all but around round 5-10 it has its uses.  The Electro-Charge is very ghostbusters like and the other 2 weapons the Lazer Pistols and Plasma Torch (flame thrower) both fun to use and effective, and with the torch you melt away the environment also.  Overall very satisfied with this Red Faction and I expect the single player missions will be fun as well.

Online Review Only: This game is not much fun if you base a review score of a shooter on how the shooting mechanics work. In the case of Battlefield 4 I am basing my 2 star score on how frustrating the weapons are. If you use a grip on a weapon it says it improves accuracy, but comes at the cost of a reduction in the effectiveness of the rounds you shoot and if you use a sight it detracts from the accuracy of the hit detection. So basically the weapons don't shoot good at all no matter what, or which you use, and are confused with weapon add-ons that say they do things but in reality are just junk the developers added to fill out the modern combat weapons, and vehicles and gadgets checklist. Even though the game has some of it right; the hit detection and weapon spray is seriously flawed. Resulting in a frustrating and quickly unplayable game similar to the prior game Battlefield 3. Additionally, Battlefield: Hardline has been getting played in beta and it is no different looking regarding gun play then this game or battlefield 3.

It is a pretty simple trade off with weapon mechanics in games and reality, if it kicks it has power, if it doesn't then it uses smaller rounds meaning less power. In this game it makes no difference cause everything regarding the weapon was flawed from the start, and just as an example you can shoot an enemy online standing still in front of you with a gun and it will take 5 bullets to kill, then add a attachment and it will take 6, 7 or 8 bullets to get the kill. Ultimately the game is based not on being a fun shooter but some sort of mathematical statistical shooter game, where and when if you fail to get a kill it is not because you had the aiming wrong, it is because the gun doesn't shoot that far, or the add-on you used was beaten mathematically by the other guys better use of add-ons, and distance and understanding of bullet drag and drop and muzzle climb variables. Mass Effect (PC) is the latest in a succession of hugely successful role playing games created by Bioware (Baldur's Gate 1 and 2, Neverwinter Nights 1 and 2, Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic). I would not hesitate to call it the game of the year 2008. To be honest, the game crashed a lot. I wasn't sure if it was my hardware or if it was because of bugs. Nevertheless, I'll still give it the highest rating I can give. I just completed the game for the 2nd time today and it was still amazing. Can't wait to run through it a third time with my level 48 soldier character.
Thanks for bringing this game to the PC Bioware.
Pros:
1. The characters, sci-fi settings and spaceship are all rendered and animated beautifully. The characters' faces look beautiful.
2. Each companion in your team has an interesting backstory and sidequests. The unique personality of each character is conveyed through engaging dialogue and superb voice acting (Lance Henriksen, Marina Sirtis, Seth Green and Keith David).
3. You will want to play it more than once because of the different classes, skills and specialties available. Your character can be a soldier, a biotic or an engineer. You can start the game at a new difficulty setting using your old character. The level cap is initially 50 but it increases to 60 after playing the game once.
4. Making full use of the equipment upgrades greatly increases your character and his/her companion's effectiveness and resilience in firefights. By carefully beefing up the entire team's gear I got to the point where the main character could stand back and order his companions during firefights and still win.
5. The story will keep you playing this for hours until the ending.

Bottom line: Buy MW2 or stick with it instead of buying this game.

With their default settings, Modern Warfare 2 multiplayer runs much more responsively than Black Ops multiplayer on my PC. Killing background processes and using the lowest graphics settings didn't help.

My PC's specs are:

AMD Phenom II X4 940 3 GHz processor
2 x 2 GB DDR2 800 MHz
Windows 7 64-bit
2 x NVIDIA 8800GT, SLI

LAG is ever present in multiplayer and greatly reduces the player's chances of dodging enemy fire, even AFTER managing to get behind cover. Aiming down the sight is slow and isn't practical. Lag makes the knife a less viable weapon because your opponent almost always sees you coming. You learn to cope with the lag but in MW2 there was no perpetual state of having lag and when there was lag it wasn't this bad.

I prefer the way human faces and objects like cars are rendered in MW2 than in BO. Human faces in BO look less detailed and seem "cartoony". I was disappointed with the way the game rendered JFK's face. The faces of the North Korean enemy NPCs weren't drawn well and their voices didn't seem real enough unlike the Russian NPCs voices which were good.

In BO the player's view of the environment is wider and it feels almost like a third person view with the gun sight placed in the center. I prefer the narrower field of view in MW2. Most metallic objects like guns look too shiny and end up looking like plastic rather than metal.

Here are some positive aspects of BO:

1. The "Jungle" multiplayer map is impressive. The outdoor environment has dense vegetation, a rope bridge and elevated huts. It's the best jungle environment I've seen in FPS games so far.

2. The in-game UI is polished and more intuitive than in MW2.

3. You can buy gun camo to "pimp your gun". XP grinding isn't needed to buy guns, perks and attachments. A larger set of guns is available to the player than in MW2.

The reason console games cost a little more is because of the expensive, proprietary manufacturing process (Sony, Nintendo) and license fees (Sony, Microsoft, Nintendo).

There are no proprietary technologies associated with manufacturing a PC game. There are no license fees to the platform.

This was an attempt by a greedy company to capitalize on the success of COD4 and the hype of MW2's release by charging above-market costs. The problem with hype is that you have to live up to it, which this game clearly does not.

Additionally, it looks like they made a lot of people mad with the lack of dedicated servers. People play this game on home networks with asymmetric internet access: your upload is much slower than your download. This means that to host a game without a dedicated server, someone has to use their slow upload bandwidth. Again, this looks to me like an attempt to control cost by not having to pay for and maintain dedicated servers and bandwidth without regard for performance.

Such a greedy move should be met with no less than abject failure.

I had not played GTAIII. I have a used copy for my aging PS2, and I've beaten Vice City and San Andreas on PS2, but I wouldn't mind replaying them. Based on that, I thought this game pack with all three is an excellent deal.

GTA III, being the oldest title, has some hardware support issues that I expect I will not run in to with the more modern Vice City and San Andreas games.

GTA III is so old, it supports 3DFX! Direct3D is an option, and does work, but selecting anything other than 640x480x16 causes the game to crash. I would have expected a re-release to be updated to support modern hardware, or what's the point? I don't just happen to have a Pentium II with a Voodoo card laying around....

GTA III runs great, with a few annoying glitches. I run XPSP3 with multi-mon. The game maximizes the window in 640x480x16 without trapping the mouse. Clicking anywhere outside the window causes the program to crash.... therefore, I have to temporarily disable my secondary monitor (Desktop properties, advanced, right-click, de-select "Attached") and then re-enable it later. I usually watch a movie on my secondary, so this is quite annoying. In addition, ALT+TAB, CTRL+ESC or anything that brings up the desktop causes the program to crash. If you have any kind of pop-up that will pre-empt the game, disable it, or you might blow an entire mission due to some innocuous desktop pop-up. Remember: You can't save while in a mission, and you can only save at your "safe house" locations. So I find myself saving OFTEN.

The plus side is that I'll actually beat the game faster, because the load times are so much better than the PS2, with game and save data pulling from the hard drive, which is much better.

I have not played Vice City or San Andreas yet, but I expect that they will play "normally" without the caveats mentioned above.

I wouldn't mind seeing a LC Stories / VC Stories / Chinatown wars pack.

It is not that it is bad, but at times it can feel like the characters are bundled together without much backstory. Last but not least was the maps i wish there was more detail instead of confined paths just a little bit more to explore, i mean that is all this game needs really.

In conclusion i find the negativity about this to be humerious and funny, because the creator of Final Fantasy wanted to change the series for the next generation, and he did not do much to it at all, it is still the same formula(trust me i played FF7 watched my cousins beat most Final Fantasy games). But to me it needed to happen because sometimes we can all live in the past with FF7,FF8, FF4,FF10,FF-12 but sometimes we need to realize what day and age we are in and not be pessemestic about the game do to the fact it changed a few things and reinvented itself away from the rest. To me it is a successful game, not perfect, but it is a step in the path of a right direction.

Yes sorry for the long title but i needed to say it. This was my 1st Katamari game of the series(i played the older Katamari's after 100% completing this game), and i have to say at first it was hard to reach the size in such a short time span, but after awhile i realized that was the point, and it felt rewarding each time that i played, becoming bigger and picking up objects i could not get when i was near the size, and some moments picking up buildings, galaxies to mythological creatures(no spoilers), and even cousins.

This game has 40 levels divided by 20 for Roboking, 20 for the regular king. Each was fun and new, especially with the King Hop ability, it made things easier for me when i was stuck somewhat(press R2 for PS3 and shoulder button for Xbox360). What i really liked was that each time you beat the levels achieve new scores, and you can unlock new modes such as.

- Speed Katamari it is so fast you do not even need to do the rolling ability and you have the same time limit, the hard part is that you have to turn around but that makes sense because it is very fast.

Different looking colors and themes for levels- i love this feature a lot, it provides replayability on it's own, you can have the classic look, wood look, metal look, etc and it will make everything in the level look like it. It looks excellent on an HD-TV and even on a normal tv, but an HD TV is recommended.

Eternal-imagine this as the relax mode, where you have NO TIME LIMIT, and you can collect everything, and just take things at your own pace. This is my favorite mode, i wish there was more because there were some levels i could imagine being relaxing and just playing for 30minutes etc.

Overall this game has a whole lot of extras for old Katamari fans, and tons of features to draw in new people into this game and make it's case as a new innovative game of the series. It has flaws such as the scores(in the older games it is a little lenient) it is nothing to bad you can do enough to unlock or do better, but i can not help but to feel that they thought only vets were going to play this game, other than that, it is worth the buy all the way. I recommend it to anyone and everyone who wants something funny, new and interesting in a game.

My number one complaint last year, was that there was not a real season mode in Smackdown Vs Raw 2010, i ended up thinking it was all for the trophies. But THQ proved me wrong this year, this was a huge step, do not listen to the negative reviewers at all, this is worth your money, the season mode is Universe mode, which when you set up an exhibition game(Universe is intertwined with it), it can play out like a WWE RAW or a WWE Smackdown storyline, even the jump behind attacks are a nice extra.

For example It shocks me when i play a singles match, i played as Randy Orton versus John Cena, and as Orton was walking down the ramp Cena jumped him from behind and attacked him, on the WWE News after i beat Cena, it says " John Cena has turned his back on the fans" which was fun and it has other news on things that is happening. Universe Mode is like a combination of GM Mode and Season mode of Smackdown Vs Raw 06, 07 that i loved so much, the only part i wish THQ improved on was maybe adding one on one confrontations and choosing what you want to do.

The unlockables are unbelievable, it might be the deepest wrestling game that THQ has ever done or even created, it has guys like Vance Archer, Mickie James(now in TNA), Goldust, Ezekiel Jackson, it even has Jimmy Superfly Snuka, and other legends with their own themes. I am not lying about the roster it probably consists of 40 to 45 perhaps. Also the player select screen has been revamped, it has a fighting game style screen like Marvel Vs Capcom but keeps it's identity like the previous Smackdown Vs Raw's, deviating from the fans who say "Same old smackdown vs raw".

The weapons have been revamped along with the creative moves that needed to be done to become more realistic. First of all you can set a ladder on top of a rope and run on the ladder and hit a wrestler, or even set a ladder on the step of a already set up ladder and use that as a high flying acrobatic move set. Also THQ fixed a long glitch i remembered in it's past games such as the steel steps, it use to be you picked it up automatically, but now the superstar turns the steel steps until it is on the back and picks it up.

As for the moves, remember how cheap the moves and animations where you had someone groggy on a turnbuckle and then it was just one move? Now you can set them up on top of a turnbuckle with there back against you(for a backwards suplex) Forwards(for a toss move) and then finally a tree of woe(which the wrestler is upside down and the legs are on a turnbuckle. As for a wrestler when he is on the top rope you can now run and then press the grapple button to counter his jump, if you time it right. It is much easier, and fun to chain moves together than last year.

The appearence of each wrestler and the crowd has been really altered, they are not like action figures, when i played Shaemus going against Triple H it is almost like if i was in front row seats at a wrestling event, or watching WWE on television. As for the crowd, yes they kind of look the same as last year, but i notice THQ has worked harder, and i was almost fooled by the fans, because sometimes they would do different things depending on what the wrestler would do. Another example was when i used my created guy used a finisher and then pinned, but Yoshi Tatsu interfeared in the match and was argueing with the ref, the crowd kind of booed him, and was standing up having cameras out, just like some WWE events on TV.

Online needs an improvement sadly, Royal Rumble is fun, but it is far to easy for people to cheat and just eliminate you, also the matches are slow if a person has a dial up or slow connection , THQ needs to work on this, because for so long this has been it's hindering problem on it's backside, i suggest dedicated servers and to buy a better server next year, because oldschool fans want to fight someone without much lag if any at all. There has been some cutdown on it, but not enough to say that it has changed much.

Overall i recommend this to people who did not buy last years game, or has not baught a Smackdown Vs Raw game in a long time, even those who had 2010, all should find significant changes and new things that will wow them over time. Sadly i just wish there was more exploration like in Here Comes The Pain to the back locker rooms, and to other places in the arena, apply some other ideas and THQ could probably out due itself with next years edition. This years edition is a solid buy, no questions about it.

I baught this game because i was watching a little bit of a gameplay trailer on youtube and reading ton's of reviews from Amazon. Granted i may not be 6 to 11 years old again, but it definitely is a pure platforming experience that brings me back a long time ago(I was 1 years old or so when the SNES was out). Enough about my past, when i first started the main menu screen, i could not help but to love it, the graphics were High Definition even though i do not possess a LCD or plasma screen(it probably would be 10X more beautiful) with Kirby turning into a cute car and waving at the screen in a few seconds or so.

The difficulty of the game is largely criticised(or so ive heard) because of how it is not in the league of Super Mario difficulty, and i am here to say that is not the case, yes it is easy to finish because you never die, but it does not mean you will not go back and see if you can better your collection of beads, and items etc. In a sense it is for younger children, but it can be challenging for adults who use to play old games like this, or adults who have not really played video games because the controls are simple and rewarding at the same time. This is fun on Co-op and is especially fun for the family, there is no violence in this game to be honest it is just a pure exciting game for children and adults.

The levels in Kirby's Epic Yarn, is kind of set up like Super Mario World, or Donkey Kong Country in the sense that the levels are divided and you have to play the 1st level to go to the next, the basic formula of Nintendo Success. I am a little bit sad on the fact that there are six worlds, i wish there was two more because i really liked the game that much and it would auctully have made it more fun, but that is just my opinion overall.

To me this is probably one of the games that at E3 people at first did not know what else to think, and Kirby fans were probably a little bit scared due to the fact it has been a long time since a legit Kirby game came out, but afterwards when all is said and done and it came out, i believe all Kirby fans,Casual Fans, and even hardcore Nintendo fans are enjoying this all the way.

Great game! I say game in the singular since it's all one story divided into three parts. It's like an sRPG meets Oregon trail in the style reminiscent of a Ralph Bakshi cartoon. There's a Norse mythology influence and it definitely gave me sort of a Lord of the Rings vibe. The story is very good and not happy-go-lucky at all.

As your caravan travels you make decisions that will influence the number of followers in your group, your amount of supplies, special items you get, etc. Your decisions have consequences that affect the story, sometimes in some major ways. When you finish one part you can carry over your save data to the next chapters or pick your main character and start fresh.

This game is not easy. You can change your difficulty at any time without affecting the story. I started out by playing on the normal setting and the game was extremely difficult. At some point in Part 2 I switched to easy as even that was very hard. The difficulty levels might only affect the amount of hit points and armor points that the enemies have. I can't imagine I would be able to finish this on the hard setting.

For what I paid I thought this was a very good deal. I would not recommend purchasing just one game of the trilogy since you wouldn't get a complete story. Definitely don't buy Parts 2 or 3 before playing 1 or else you won't know what's going on.

As a big fan of the original on PS I thought they did a really good job with this remake. Unlike some recent FF games, this totally catered to longtime fans like myself and not to first-timers (like FF XV). In fact, I can't see how this game would really appeal to players unfamiliar with the original. This game is not revolutionary for the genre like the first was. I think younger gamers might not understand the appeal unless they give the story a chance. Unfortunately there were a few things that caused me to rate this game 4-stars instead of 5.

The driving force for the Final Fantasy VII Remake is the story and not so much the gameplay. If you played the demo before the rest of the game you'll notice that the beginning of the game follows the beginning of the original almost exactly. If it had gone on like this the rest of the time I would have been very content. They ended up adding a ton of extra plot points, including some major ones, that weren't in the original and I think this actually took away from my satisfaction. Some of it was pretty corny, like the addition of a dance-off minigame. Because of this, I didn't really get into the game to the point where I could finish it quickly. It took me a few months because there were times that I just wasn't pumped to play it. The game can easily be finished in 50 hours or so, less if you want to just fly through it without doing some of the extra stuff.

The last thing that took away from my overall enjoyment was that the story is incomplete and too linear. I knew before I started playing that you were only getting the beginning of the story. FF VII on PlayStation was a 3-disc game and I believe the part covered in the remake all happened on disc-1 in the the original. You are confined to the city of Midgar, and while you're able to explore and move around the city a little more than the first, you don't get to experience the best part of the game, where the characters leave the city and you're allowed to explore the world. You only have the chance to play with 4 characters; Cloud, Barret, Tifa and Aerith. While Nanaki (Red XIII) joins your party near the end of the game, he is not a playable character. I'm disappointed because I can't imagine the remainder of this game will be released anytime soon. I don't even think it'll be out in the next couple of years. It would have been reassuring if they showed maybe a preview of what's coming in the next entry (or entries), but since they didn't I don't think they're that far along. In my head I'm seeing customers having to purchase the PS5 to finish this story.

So if you're a longtime fan you should definitely get this game. As I said, I'm not sure it will appeal much to those unfamiliar with the original. I got the Deluxe Edition that came with some extra stuff and I'm glad I pre-ordered since I don't think this version is very easy to get a hold of anymore.

I really had to debate between giving this game 4 stars or 5. It's definitely not perfect but it's the best PSVR game I've played in a long time. The game is difficult, even on the easier settings, and learning the controls takes a while and is almost intimidating. It has a really good story and the voice acting is top notch. There are times you can almost picture you're hearing Robert Downey Jr speaking. And flying around like Ironman is is just awesome!

My main issue with the game is mentioned in so many reviews so I won't get deep into it. The load times are too long and too numerous. Really throws off the continuity of the game. I'm a patient person so it's not a deal breaker for me, but it's definitely noticeable and a bit annoying.

Ironman VR makes great use of the controllers and that's what truly makes the game difficult. You have to learn how to use your thrusters while attacking at the same time. You need to constantly be on the move if you don't want to die real quick. I found myself accidentally hitting the pause or screen cap buttons constantly which is a pain in the butt in the heat of combat. I was over halfway through this game before I really mastered the controls and even now there's a lot of room for improvement. The intimidation of learning this was the main thing keeping me from being pumped to play this and is the reason why it took me several months before I actually passed the game.

In the end it was well worth it and I ended up liking the game a lot more after finishing than I did in the beginning. There is definitely a lot of replay value in this game. I recommend this game more than any other PSVR game that's come out with a physical release in a long, long time.

I just started playing this, story mode only, and so far I'm not impressed. I usually wait until I've played more before writing a review but there were some things right out of the gate that sort of turned me off.

I want to be clear that I only ordered this because it can be played in VR. Pretty much everything I've seen so far is in VR except you have to watch cutscenes in 2D. So it's a lot like Resident Evil Biohazard in that sense. That's a huge bonus to me because some games listed as VR "Mode Included" only let you play a very limited amount in VR, or you can only play a very short, separate mode.

That said, I'm really not impressed with the graphics. Slight disclaimer, though, I play this on the old PS4 and not the PS4 Pro. I heard the graphics look better on the Pro. This seems like one of those games that looks better on the TV screen. I think the inside of the cockpit looks great but everything outside seems blurry and pretty low resolution. As far as space combat games go, Eve Valkyrie looks much better in VR, though there's not much of a story mode for that game. I also hit a huge glitch right after starting story mode. I created my characters and watched the first cutscene. It immediately goes to another cutscene, but for that, the whole screen was blue with pink edges. Even when the first mission started, the blue background remained. I was able to see characters' faces pop up, dialogue boxes and tutorial instructions, but couldn't play the game since I couldn't see where I was going. I lifted my headset and even the TV screen was blank. I had to turn off the game and start over, and low and behold, it did it again. I started over one more time, this time skipping the cutscenes, and that's when it finally started displaying the game as it should look. So while I was able to listen to the dialogue, I still wasn't able to watch the other part of that first scene. I also hit a snag once after playing a mission. I was getting ready to start the Imperial missions and I removed the headset to take a little break. When I put the headset back on everything was black. There were still sound effects but absolutely nothing on the screen. Had to start the game over. From other reviews it seems these glitches are pretty common.

I do look forward to finishing the story mode and delving into the multiplayer mode but at this point I'm not too optimistic that I'll come to like this game more. I've heard tell that they will not be releasing any new content for this game...what you see is what you get. So no new levels or ships or any of that. I'm only going off what I heard on a YouTube vid, so don't take my word as gospel. The explanation that I heard is that this game started at a lower price point and the developers weren't going to spend a lot of time and money to expand a game that's cheaper than your standard new game.

Overall I'm disappointed because I loved the VR mission that they added to Battlefront on PS4 and I thought I would love to play a fully fleshed out Star Wars flight simulation game. If you're getting this to play in VR I would definitely recommend Eve Valkyrie over this one, and you can pick that up for less than half the price of this. It's a much better space flight sim. The problem with that game is that it's only in VR so there aren't a lot of other people playing online, at least not when I tried. Playing against the computer is still a lot of fun, though.

Still... Star Wars Squadrons is better than the latest three movies, that's for sure.

I will try to keep this review as spoiler free as possible. It's a game one can pick up and enjoy without having to play the rest of the games in the series, though playing previous titles helps one to understand what's going on with the underlying plot. As the "M" for Mature rating suggests, it is very violent, filled with adult language and adult situations, including sex stuff. Great for me, not so much for the kiddies.

I have not played an Assassin's Creed game since the original which came out more than a dozen years ago. This game is so far ahead of that one. It has an enormous, beautiful open world. In many ways the game reminds me more of titles like Skyrim, The Witcher III and Red Dead Redemption. There are many RPG elements as far as earning experience and leveling up the protagonist. You don't have to just sneak around and kill enemies like you might think...ultimately you decide how you want to take on the bad guys. In the beginning there's a bit of hack and slash, but as you progress you really need to learn how to better use the combat system if you want to make it anywhere.

Valhalla has a good story and pretty good voice acting. It starts out a little slow but after playing for several hours things really begin to open up. You're not confined to a linear story. You can go hunting for loot, track down sidequests, even create and upgrade your own settlements. There is a unique dynamic to this game where not only do you pick the sex of the protagonist, but the sex can be switched back and forth at any time during the game. This leads to some very interesting relationships which some may find offensive, but I thought it was pretty awesome. The game actually warns the player of this right at the beginning, along with the obligatory risk of seizure warning.

One great thing I can say about this game is that it hooked me in more than I thought it would. I have a pretty long queue of games that I've been waiting to play. Since I was given this game at no cost for my review it obviously became my priority, and I've now spent more time playing it than I originally planned on. I'm far enough in that I'll probably just be playing this one until I've beaten it. As I'm getting older I've become more prone to abandoning things like books, movies or video games if they don't properly grab my attention from the get go, and I've found Assassin's Creed Valhalla good enough to continue on with. That might not be the strongest endorsement, but it's better than me not liking it or getting bored with it right away.

One last thing. I am playing this game on the PS4. This physical copy of Assassin's Creed Valhalla allows you to play it on the PS5. It seems that all you need to do is have the physical copy of the PS4 game inserted in the PS5 and you will be able to download the PS5 version. You can only play it when the disk is inserted, though. So if one was thinking of buying the PS4 version, downloading the PS5 version, then selling the disk, that would not work.

I'm not a huge gamer...at best I'm a casual gamer. I don't feel I need to criticize every little thing about games. This game isn't perfect...I've played better, I've played worse. I grew up with an Atari 2600 closely followed by the NES. Video games today are absolutely amazing compared to what I grew up with, and if I knew then what I know now I wouldn't even be here because my head would've exploded. I think Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a pretty cool game and I'd definitely recommend it.

I really enjoyed playing this game. The word "Metroidvania" has become a pretty popular video game term and this game is a great example of it. Ori and the Blind Forest has some elements of both the original Metroid and Castlevania games on the NES, which are both games I grew up with. Also reminds me of some other classic games such as Megaman and even Sonic the Hedgehog. This game is super difficult but fun enough that the challenge is worth it. As you play, you learn skills that'll open up the map to you. In the end you really have to master those skills to advance. Split second timing is essential. I got a great feeling of satisfaction when I finally beat it. Took me a couple of weeks, I'd say at least 20 hours of playing. The story is a little sad and a little sweet but takes a backseat to the gameplay. Graphics and music are fantastic!

Just a couple of cons: First of all, there are no bosses. At the end of a few areas there are rush sections where you furiously have to outrun stuff like rising water or flowing lava. This is where the mastery of skills comes in. I think some boss fights would've made this game more awesome. The other thing I wasn't crazy about is that this game will absolutely drain the battery in handheld mode. I just use the Switch Lite and I found I had to recharge it every 2 hours or so, which is more often than just about any other game I've played on the Lite.

I would recommend this game for old school gamers like myself who grew up playing some of the games I've mentioned, or anyone that enjoys the classic side scroller. Can't wait to play the sequel!

I had never played any of the Hitman games before ordering this. When I heard that you could play this in VR, and in turn, play parts 1 and 2 in VR if you owned 3, I pre-ordered this and bought parts 1 and 2. All three of these games are absolutely amazing in VR! Before this game arrived I was able to familiarize myself with the first chapters and learn the ins and outs of the series.

Each game gives you a number of locations to travel to, where you are asked to assassinate a person or persons. Your goal is to eliminate your target(s) and escape without getting killed. How you accomplish this is up to you. There are various ways to wipe out your target, including shooting, poisoning, choking, drowning in a toilet, etc. You can hang around in the level and pay attention to your target's movements. You'll stumble across conversations which will lead to methods of wiping the person out. If you find one of these conversations the game will give you clues on how to go about it.

This game looks really good in first person VR. If the games seems a little too morbid for you it's possible just to hang around in these locations and take in the sights. Parties, fashion shows, the beach, skyscrapers...this series gives you all kinds of places to go to and you don't need to complete previous chapter to skip ahead, though it's recommended if you want the story. There are cutscenes between missions that tell a story over the entire series, and the story's not bad, but is secondary to the gameplay. There's one thing I don't like about the VR aspect. They change the controls a bit from the 2D experience. You have to use the DualShock controller...Move controllers don't work. But you have to actually move the controller around to move your hands back and forth, side to side. Also to aim with your gun. Any kind of drift with your controller can throw things off a bit. I would've been fine with them just using the controller normally without having to move the controller itself around. My favorite PSVR game is Skyrim, and I played that all the way through with the DualShock and had no problem with it. While moving the controller gives a slightly better feeling of immersion, I think it actually takes away from the overall experience, at least for me.

If you own 1 and 2, putting those levels into part 3 takes a bit of work, but it's not overly complicated. There are options in the game menus that will help you accomplish it. You'll need to register for an IOI account. After downloading part 1 you will need to order the Legacy Pack from the in-game menu or directly from the PlayStation store...it's free if you own part 1. I think you can purchase it if you don't. This will make the levels from part 1 available when you download and have registered part 2. Once you have part 2 you can bring up another in-game menu to make the content available from 1 and 2 for part 3. When you have downloaded and started playing 3 you will get a prompt to go to a website which will transfer any experience you've gained from part 2 into part 3. This can only be done once. Bam! Now you can play all three chapters from the Hitman 3 menus. You will obviously need to have an internet connection.

I definitely recommend this game as well as parts 1 and 2. I've barely scratched the surface but this might end up being one of my favorite PSVR titles, and I own at least 70 games.

Buyer Beware!!!

This deluxe edition claims to have the booster pack Northern Strike as well but either this is not the case or EA has some serious problems here. Just search the internet and you will find numerous threads on this issue with the game deluxe edition.

In short, the game installs fine claiming that you are getting both the orginal version as well as the booster pack. However, once you are done activating and registering your account you can ONLY play the orginal BF2142 maps with no issues. But once you try to access any of the Northern Strike booster pack maps the game acts like you dont have the booster pack installed and directs you to EA link to purchase it even though the deluxe edition should have installed the booster pack already. I have sent lots of emails to EA but all i am getting are useless automated or cut & paste responses. As of now there is no real resolution to this issue. If EA helps me out I will update my post otherwise think before buying.

Other than that an awesome game. The titan mode is the real winner here. I have been involved in some serious fights around and inside the Titan for supermacy. You have 14 maps of intense battles and the game rewards the players who played the most with more effective weapons as well as armor unlocks and a persistent talent system. I will however, seriously recommend all newbies(until you have unlocked some weps and armor too) to stick with armored vehicles and only try to engage one-on-one if you have the advantage or are in a group. My father is a seaman. I have seen many ships, sailed with him around the world numerous times. So ships are in my blood. When i saw this game I bought it without batting an eyelid. Well I wish I didn't because I now regret my decision.

The game is unique in its concept. We never really had a maritime ship simulation that wasn't centrally focused on war and sinking other ships :). This one happens to be just peace-time shipping simulation with different kinds of detailed ships ranging from cargo, to passenger, to rescues, to towing, to even trying to alter history by succesfully sailing Titanic to New york on its first maiden voyage etc. The game creator has gone to great details to simulate as much as possible the Intricacies of piloting as well as managing huge ships operations. Any aspiring sea captian or sea salt will identify with some if not most aspects of piloting a ship as simulated in this game. But to me thats where all the goodies end.

The cons associated with game are just too game-breaking to me and i have essentially stopped playing the game. Until these issues gets addressed i am not spending anymore money on this games series.

First and foremost this game badly needs a voluntary "Time Compression" feature. Not all of us have 2-3 hours to devote each time we decide to play this game to have some fun. Sometimes it take an hour or so just to get out of harbour and tag some hours more on this to complete the mission. With a game in which you are looking at ocean waves for hours this gets boring really fast. This is just plain very annoying and game destroying factor to me. I know some people have all the time in the world to savour and enjoy games but a lot dont too. Since its not a action oriented game the passage of time is felt even more. If they can incorporate a Time Compression feature it will make the game lot more open to different segments of gamers.

Second is the still dated graphics engine. I see lots of people commenting on how good the graphics look. I have a pretty good rig and i can play games like Mass Effect and Silent Hunter 4 in almost thearatical quality but even with everything maxed out this game just looks medicore graphics wise. The ships and ocean etc. looks very simplistically rendered from today's standard. The graphical quality of this game released in 2008 is kind of dissappointing though.

Last some of the missions in the game are just plain novice or fillers in my opinion. This game is geared towards people who like to pilot huge ships yet we have a lot of missions devoted to speed boats for stunts, hover boats etc. I bought the game to simulate a ship expirience not go around flipping in speed boats.

Anyways..i wouldn't really recommend anyone spend $40 bucks on this game. Wait until it gets to $19 or so bargain bin. And i hope the developers put some real effort into make a more viable ship simluator for its next incarnation or you are not getting any more money from me.

Finally we have a decent, and really a fun Air action combat game for PC's. I have been waiting for such a title since the days of the orginal Crimson Sky. After the first PC based Crimson Sky all its sequels were console based and the famous modern day Ace Combat series was also released exclusively for consoles. Now we finally have a modern day PC version of these Air action combat games to look forward too in HAWX and the game delivers. I hope like the Ace Combat series HAWX will thrive and spawn sequels.

The game is pure ardelanin inducing FUN. It's fast, furious and frantic in its aerial gameplay. The missions so far have been top gun movie style air combat, air-to-ground assualts, air-to-sea action and usually culminates in a combination of all these in the finale of the mission. The sattelite imagery used in this game cleary adds to the realistic looks of this game. Sometime when flying over different cities it almost feels like I was looking out of a plane in real life. The fighther planes are rendered in great details as well as the realistic standard and special effects used in the fights are almost movie like. I also expirienced no fps or lag issues at all in any of the sharp turns, steep climbs or dives and fast bombing runs. All of this combines to give almost a movie like dog-fight expirience.

This game is kind of cross between a single player game and an rpg game. You actually level or gain levels in this game just like a rpg. As you destory enemey targets you gain xp which total to subsquent increase in your levels. The more level you gains the more fighter planes gets unlocked. As you can see I am a RPG fan too so being able to level in a single player game and gaining new capabilities in my view broadens the gaming expirience of the game than to just completing one mission after another. There is a element of what awaits me at the next level (like an rpg) which gives an added incentive to play the game. Hopefully one day an MMORPG might be made out of these kind of Aerial Air Combat games by a reputable company wich will be a dream come true for me.

They are tons of modern day such as F-18's, F-16's, F-15's as well as fifth generation fighter planes like Euro-typhoon, F-22, F-35 etc. and sixth generation protype planes available to play over your flying career with this game. Each of these planes not only offer marked differences in performance but some planes offers a more varied kind of weapons payload which sometime makes a critical difference in destroying multiple targets at one go in a dogfight or be able to carpet bomb an enemy using cluster bombs in addition to normal guided bombs etc. For example I was stuck at a mission for some time with the recomended plane (A-5) which is a ground bomber and had very limited air-to-air. However the mission had massive ground forces to fight as well as constant fighter planes and helos coming to dog-fight and th A-5 was slow to manevour overall especially in dog-fights plus only could handle one target at a time that I was just not able to hold back the enemy forces. Only after gaining few levels I was able to unlock F-111-E which is a lot more manevourable, balanced ground attack as well as decent air-to-air with multiple aerial target acquisition capability that I was able to use to progress beyond that mission. So the ability to know and be able to choose from different planes might make huge difference in progressing or being stuck with a mission. Thats kind of realistic in my view.

This being said the game as you may have ascertained is an arcade stlyle action air combat game and not a simulator. It's designed for people who like to get in the midst of all the action without the need to master a 500 page manual before one can even take off the ground let alone deal with the mind-numbing realistic aspects of flying. I mean that aspect is good for players who like realistic simulators and they have lots of games to look forward too but quality PC based Air combat games for PC's are far and few inbetween. This game adds to this genre and will satisfy PC based arcade style air combat action fans. Some of have commented where is Tom Clancy in this game since its not ultra-realistic simulator. Well once you get going in your campaign you will see Tom Clancy touches there. The mission are written, setup and unfolds in a very Tom Clancy way.

The game also has a Team Deathmatch multiplayer mode for upto 8 players for about 14 or so maps. I havent yet tried my mettle against other players but in time i will and update my review but the thought of having these kinds of ardenalin rushing air combat with other players in my view will only increase the value and fun factor of this game.

I liked the game and hopefully others will too. Highly recomended.

I am someone who first finished ME1 and than immediately played ME2 with the orginal Shephard imported over. Intially I was put off by the tonning down of the rpg elements, the complete overhaul of loot/inventory system as well as the combat system. Overtime the more I played ME2 the more I realized it was done for the better. The orginal ME1 had in my view a bloated loot/inventory system with mobs dropping too many things to keep track off and money really mean't nothing as almost any item of significance came from drops. The talents trees in the original also felt too redundant and not specific enough which was also addressed in ME2 and the talents now gives you fewer but more powerful meaningful abilities. In all I now agree with the overhaul the game mechanics went from ME1 to ME2.

Mass Effect 2 with its save-the-universe plot, its conversation options, tightly knit high quality cut-scenes, and a more robust combat system truly makes the game feel like an interactive sci-fi movie. I will say games like ME2 given 4-5 years more and subsequent advancements in computer hardware/software technologies will make movies eventually obsolete. Why watch a movie when you can virtually star in it controlling the actions as well as story-line than rather watch someone else do it for you.

In all the game is bigger in scope in almost every way from ME1 including the climatic finale at Omega 4 relay. I literally couldnt put the game away once I started the final mission all the way to its ending. I don't agree with others that it didnt match the scope of the orginal. In my view it exceeded the orginal game ending in almost all aspects; graphically, plot wise and had lot more emotional trappings to the mission which will make you regret or ponder at some of the choices you made during the finale; in all the finale is lot more involved than the orginal. (*SPOILER* if you are dont carefully think over how you allocate your team members for the final mission you might end losing some really valuable members which actaully had me play the ending thrice to undo some of the choices I intially made.)

In a nut-shell highly recomended. ME2 just like a true hollywood blockbuster sequel is bigger in almost all aspects from the orginal and I am really looking forward to ME3.
