I'm not sure, but I think the PS2 version is missing some textures. Particularly when flying, the shadow below the characters is missing. The shadow is critical for knowing where you will land. Without it, it just makes things all the more difficult. I think the shadow is present in the Gamecube version.

But I love the level designs and the missions. I don't find them overly difficult. They're a challenge but that's a good thing.

If you're a Sonic fan, this is a must have.

I just got around to getting this game. I know. Shame on me. But I'm glad I got it because it's probably the closest thing to a true work of art that ever came out on the PS2. The game creates a dilemma for the player. To save your girlfriend's life you have to kill creatures that have done nothing to you. It's sad, but it has to be done.
The controls are pretty good and the graphics are some of the best on the PS2. It's really a shame this didn't come out on the PS3 because it would have been incredible. There are several times when I have a hard time knowing if I'm looking at a cut scene or if I'm actually playing the game. And by the way, the storyline is absolutely fantastic as well as the brilliant voice acting. These video game characters act more like real human beings than any game character ever has. Did I forget to mention that the controls are spot on and the camera is one of the best ever?

The only downside I could see for this game is that it is extremely linear. You can explore a little bit but mostly you will be going down the path the game wants you to go on.

I was really pleasantly surprised with this game. The graphics are beautiful, the voice acting is great, the controls are solid, the animation is fluid, and overall it's a ton of fun. The only drawback for me is that it is overly easy and it gets repetitive. You can never die. Any time you jump and fall into a bottomless pit, the girl will save you every time without fail. If you're in a fight and you're about to get killed, the girl will save you. It takes a lot of the challenge out of the game but it also saves from a lot of frustration. You should also never get lost because she will tell you exactly where you need to go. There are surprisingly few enemies in this game and the ones you will face are really easy to kill. This is not a game for you if you like the hard stuff. But if you wanna kick back and enjoy a really pretty game with some great voice acting, this is for you.

While I wouldn't call Heavy Rain my favorite game of all time, I would certainly say it is the most unique. Think of it as a movie that lasts 10 or so hours and you're the director of it. I just completed the game for the first time a few minuets ago and I can't wait to start it over again. The entire game is made up of making choices and there are countless choices to make. Your choices will change the outcome of the game so you can play through multiple times and get a different result each time. That is the game's greatest strength.

I thought the storyline was excellent. Without giving anything away, there is a killer who has a guy's son. You play as four characters: The father, a private detective, a reporter and an FBI agent who has some really cool glasses. Several times throughout the game I thought I had it all figured out only to find out that I didn't. The ending totally for a loop. Maybe some people will figure it all out at the start but I sure didn't.

The game is not perfect. The graphics, while amazing at times, aren't as strong as Uncharted 2 but they're still better than many games out there. The character models are just a tiny bit stiff but not enough to hurt the game. The voice acting, while very good, has some problems when it comes to the actor's foreign accent showing through. The biggest flaw I see in the game, and the only reason why I wouldn't give this a perfect score, is that I experienced game freezing three times so far. That's a shame for a game this good.

Overall, this is a must have game.

This game is divided up into two parts: 1. fighting and 2. cut scenes. When you're not fighting, or running to a fight, you're watching a cut scene. After you complete a fight you're given a number of CP. You use CP to level up and gain new abilities. The problem I have with it is that most of the enemies in the game offer so little CP that it takes FOREVER to substantially level up. Each character has three main roles. But there are roadblocks for those roles and the game will stop you from leveling up at a certain point. You have to defeat a boss in order for more areas to open up. At a certain point in the game, all the other roles will open up and you can level up in them. The problem is, every single new ability costs so many CP that it will take you HOURS of fighting monsters to get anywhere. For instance, it'll offer an additional 25HP for your character but it'll cost you 31,000 CP to get it and the most an enemy will give you is 4,000 CP. So it's really frustrating.

The other thing that really annoys me with this game is you have to level up your weapons and armor too. You do this by applying the items you get from battles to them. But the weapons and armor both upgrade using the same items and in order to to upgrade fully you need to use A LOT of items. So by the time you fully upgrade one weapon, you have nothing left for the rest of your weapons and armor.

Last big complaint, you can only control one character. In a battle, the other characters can die and you can bring them back. But if YOU die, it is game over. I think, if your main character dies, another character should step in to take his or her place. I have never had so many game overs before in a Final Fantasy game. I miss the days when you could swap characters in and out.

On the plus side, I really did enjoy the battle system. You have to in this game because that's pretty much all there is. When you finally level up enough, the battles look awesome.

The storyline is very good. I became invested in all of the main characters and cared about each of them. I do wish that more time was spent on the supporting characters. The main villain could have used more time although I do think he is memorable. Certainly more memorable than FF12's villain.

The music is great at times. The rest of the time it's forgettable.

The graphics are astoundingly beautiful! Even after playing Uncharted 2, I was blown away by the IN-GAME graphics. Just wait till you reach Gran Pulse. The level of scale, the number of enemies, and the level of detail in each and every single thing is amazing. The enemies actually look like animals living off the land and not just mindless drones walking back and forth. And the enemies range from tiny to GIGANTIC! It's all too easy to draw parallels between Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog. The classic mascot characters have endured the years to become videogame icons, recognized and loved by millions of game addicts around the globe. Nintendo's fat, Italian plumber helped pioneer the platformer genre and SEGA's blue hedgehog transformed it completely, placing a new emphasis on speed and rollercoaster-inspired level designs. In the old days, Mario and Sonic stood on even ground, each taking lead roles in an impressive selection of critically acclaimed titles. But as the years passed and consoles become more and more powerful, Mario's inevitable jump to the third dimension faired much better than Sonic's. Case in point: Super Mario 64 is remembered even today as one of the greatest games of all time. Sonic Adventure for Sega Dreamcast is conversely thought of as a flawed, but still enjoyable sequel by hardcore fans, and an altogether broken platformer by everybody else.

It is more than a little puzzling, therefore, that developers SEGA Studios USA and Sonic Team continue to draw upon that archaic, clunky design for various Hedgehog-based sequels. Sonic Adventure 2, for instance, hit Dreamcast and was later ported to GameCube with the same fundamental mechanics and shortcomings that blemished the original title. And now, the software house has created Shadow the Hedgehog for GameCube, PlayStation 2 and Xbox, a game that looks and plays like it was designed for Dreamcast a full six years ago. Sonic's darker half occasionally shines in the same way that its predecessors did -- namely, with an impressive sense of speed and dazzling stages complete with trademark twists and turns. And it's solely for these reasons that anybody who defends the original Sonic Adventure will probably like Shadow's one. Alternatively, though, players unimpressed with Sonic's Dreamcast outings will find more of the same here, and unlike a fine wine, age has not improved the formula.

Identity Crisis

Shadow the Hedgehog seems to be Sonic Team's unofficial attempt at aging up its platformer games and as a result the title regularly deals with slightly darker and more convoluted themes that center on the balance between good and evil. The story is kick-started by a gorgeously rendered full-motion animation cinematic that introduces players to the troubled Hedgehog, who has recently lost his memory and is struggling to come to grips with his place in the world. The tale picks up after the events in Sonic Heroes and consequently Shadow can only vaguely recall in flashbacks that there was a girl named Maria, he may have loved her, and she was murdered.

Shadow isn't allowed much alone time before his thought process is so rudely interrupted by the sounds of war and destruction. An alien threat called Black Arms explodes onto the scene and demolishes everything in its path, including nearby city skyscrapers. This is, again, all illustrated in impressive FMA cut-scenes that seasoned Sonic fans will undoubtedly appreciate. Shadow observes this phenomenon with a level of indifference before he is approached by a demon-like figure known as Black Doom, who leads the extraterrestrial forces. The menacing entity acts as though he knows Shadow and commands the Hedgehog to retrieve the seven powerful Chaos Emeralds located throughout the land. The anti-hero begrudgingly agrees, but only because Black Doom promises to restore his memory immediately after the artifacts are collected.

This oddball setup is supposed to extend into and become an integral part of the gameplay experience. Shadow is out for himself and therefore he can and in fact does switch allegiances depending on the preferences of players. The hedgehog can be made to carry out Black Doom's commands, or he can switch sides and team up with Sonic and friends, or even Dr. Eggman. Changing teams is as simple as tapping the D-Pad during gameplay. One quick tap and Shadow will find himself being guided to various goals, such as destroying G.U.N. troops, for Black Doom. Another tap and Sonic and friends will appear at his side to fight against the Black Arms.

The concept itself is intriguing primarily because it enables gamers to choose different paths for themselves as the hero advances through the adventure. The choices made will have a direct bearing on the stages that follow thanks to a branching storyline that allows for several possible paths and endings. This is a clever way to extend replay value and we're confident that completionists will play through the title several times, switching allegiances, so that they may see everything that there is to see.

However, observing the unique goals per different allegiances is a messy undertaking marred by poor design. The fact of the matter is that any level of serious planned strategizing is wholly unobtainable in the intensely frantic makeup of the game, whose mechanics perpetually dart Shadow forward with both limited visibility and control. In turn, even when gamers are trying to fight alongside Sonic and friends, they will accidentally dispose of hordes of allies and even zoom into and activate switches or complete puzzle components that they should ignore. This truth renders the entire operation of choosing sides more or less useless.

Speed, Loops and Guns, But Very Little Fun

Dreamcast owners will already have an unfortunately accurate idea of how Shadow the Hedgehog plays (and for that matter, looks). To be brief, like Sonic Adventure before it. What this means is that speed and forward momentum are emphasized over control, puzzles, or to be frank, depth. Honestly, that isn't always a bad thing. Shadow, like Sonic before him, has his redeeming gameplay moments. We're referring to the rollercoaster-like stages complete with loop-de-loops, corkscrews and pinball bouncers that send the hedgehog zigzagging up and down environments at remarkable speeds. Because these scenarios are still plentiful, undeterred supporters of Sonic Team's efforts will undoubtedly find something to like about Shadow's quest.

That noted, these thrill-ride fundamentals have outworn their welcome, as far as we're concerned. Just because they dazzled players six years ago does not mean that Sonic Team can copy and paste exactly the same loops and spins into each new franchise iteration and expect everyone to be happy with the outcome. Admittedly, Shadow is at its best when the character is zipping through 360s and or skating a rollercoaster track. But it's also during these moments that the game plays itself. It is, in fact, possible, for participants to put their controllers down for seconds at a time and simply watch what unfolds. How is relinquishing control for what amounts to watching Shadow tumble through a scripted corkscrew a rewarding play environment?

Unfortunately for Sonic's darker half, there are all-new problems exclusive to his adventure. The very first level in Shadow the Hedgehog is a shining example of spectacularly lackluster game design and probably one of the worst single stages that we've played in any title for many months. The reluctant hero is thrust into a drab environment and immediately nudged forward -- right into a progression of objects, including obstructing walls and enemies. Disappointingly, the platformer also features a horrendously malfunctioned camera system that catches on environments or even occasionally runs amok for no particular discernible reason. The result? Commonly frustrating undertakings where the goal is to burst forward and gain speed, but before that can happen Shadow crashes into enemies and loses rings, or simply goes careening off a ledge. These impossibly trying outcomes are worsened because Shadow moves loosely through the worlds he explores, which at times makes precision navigation an insurmountable hurdle.

The character can, unlike Sonic, wield a number of imposing weapons, from massive swords to explosive projectiles. But in a move that again harkens back to the days of Dreamcast, there is no lock-on system in place and therefore what is a simple process in other titles is overly complex and cumbersome here. Successfully targeting and unloading a bazooka shot at an enemy may as well be left to chance. Sonic Team has positioned Shadow's gunplay as a primary selling point to the platformer, but in practice the mechanics are really not that enjoyable.

Recycled technology and replicated production values have ensured that Shadow the Hedgehog looks and sounds almost exactly like its Sonic-based predecessors. To Sonic Team's credit, there are more than 20 levels in the game and each is varied in design. Some areas have a futuristic look to them while others feature large metropolis backgrounds and more still take Shadow through lava and forest settings. Meanwhile, the game engine draws long, stretching locales populated with a moderate number of polygonal characters. And on GameCube and Xbox, the fluidity usually aspires for the 60 frames per second mark with some dips. The PlayStation 2 version is noticeably more sluggish despite the fact that it is visually lacking compared to its counterparts. And yet, these are small graphic victories, especially when held to today's more robust standards. Shadow oftentimes looks like it could have been designed for Dreamcast simply because the worlds and characters lack polygon numbers, which leads to a generally square presentation void of curvy shapes. Worse is that many of the game's textures are downright muddy, especially when the camera malfunctions and pans up close, as it consistently does. And overall character animation is primitive and incomplete when compared to the majority of today's games.

Shadow the Hedgehog is proof that Sonic Team needs to get with the program if it plans to compete with legitimate current and next- generation software. This is Sonic Adventure with guns and less polish, and players today are far more discerning than they were six years ago. Diehard Sonic fans will cling to the fact that the title still conjures up corkscrews and loop-de-loops, as well as an impressive sense of speed when Shadow really gets moving, and this is all true. But this doesn't make up for the game's long list of shortcomings, from stupid level design, unrefined controls and useless gunplay to disappointingly outdated graphics.

Pros:
Decent length to complete.
Tons of characters to use.
Battle system is fairly deep.
I had fun playing through and using each of the characters.
Boss battles are beautifully done.

Cons:
Repetitive gameplay for quests. You have to run back and forth until you complete the game and then they give you "warp scrolls" which make traveling a LOT easier.
You can't jump everywhere like in the first one (I loved just running around in the first one!)
They still left out quite a few characters from the previous game and sagas (Zabuza!!!!!)
Although there is variety to the battle system and characters I found that online battles mostly consist of blocking/teleporting behind your opponent and then unleashing your ultimate. Or, waiting until your "support meter" is full and then going all out with your support to overwhelm defenses. Hardly any back and forth with the actual battling.
I liked the customization of the first one better where you had several jutsu to choose from for each character.

Other notes:
Online system is decent. Sometimes it's a little frustrating to connect to a game and the lag you encounter can make it a pain. Repetitive stuff, you'll run into lots of Itachi's, Fourth Hokage's and that old puppet lady (three puppet master team is unbelievable).

All in all I recommend this, especially if you want to battle with some friends!

One of the SMT series of games. I'll start off by saying that I love the Persona series of SMT games. 3 &4 were fantastic. I've played through most of the first Digital Devil Saga as well (still finishing it) and enjoy all of those ones better than Nocturne. Which is a shame as Nocturne does have an interesting premise and a suitably dark atmosphere.

The game is hard and unforgiving to the extreme. I died several times on the first battle and it appeared it was only dumb luck that let me get through that one. The next 25% of the game that I played through was only slightly less punishing. Plenty of restarts required when you plan poorly for the type of enemies you'll encounter, which I find frustrating although some may enjoy the challenge. The battle system itself is not bad, just difficult. Recruiting demons to aid you in battle was fun and is probably the best part of the game.

The storyline is very bare bones IMO. There's only a few characters to interact with and progress the storyline, otherwise you're mainly just walking from one place to the next and fighting demons nonstop. When I play an RPG I enjoy a storyline that is interesting and draws you in. Your character also has 0 personality, and your friends are equally bland so I never felt invested in anything that happened to them.

In my opinion, I would recommend the other games in the SMT universe first. This one I would only recommend if you want the satisfaction to beat a truly tough game.

A LITTLE BACKGROUND: I've been playing football video games since the Apple II had it's own text version of football. Tecmo Super Bowl for the NES is my all time favorite football game, and NFL 2k5 has a special place in my heart. The last Madden game that I thoroughly enjoyed, flaws and all, was Madden NFL 25. I've played the crud out of that game; put more time into that football game than any other in a long time. I bought Madden NFL 15 for PS4 when it was a few months old, played it for a few weeks, and found myself wanting to go back to Madden NFL 25. It just wasn't fun.

So what about this game? Well I'm enjoying it. It's entertaining. I'll be keeping it for one. I'll get some of my bigger gripes about this game out of the way.

The BAD: (1) If your PS4 connects to the internet, and it most likely does, your game may or may not load. I've found when connecting to the EA servers that the game has problems loading at times. There are times when it seems the game loads properly after the initial screens, but when trying to load actual gameplay the game will freeze. This has happened to me a few times in the past month of owning the game. The easy fix was to turn off my internet connection on my PS4. An odd thing, but it does happen on occasion. (2) The user interface can be quite daunting to a more casual football fan. If someone just wants to pick up a quick game to play it can be difficult trying to find that option. This game is really designed to be for the more hardcore football fan. It's great for someone like me, but I can see how it can be irritating to someone who really just wants to play a quick and easy fun game of football. Thank goodness I have a copy of Tecmo Super Bowl at the house for that. (3) The AI can be frustratingly difficult at times, and others it can be just downright dumb. There is no consistency with the AI. I've gone back and forth between All-Pro and All Madden. In my opinion there is a serious spike in difficulty between the two. I can thrash teams I have no business beating the way I do in All-Pro, so I'll switch to All Madden to compensate. Unfortunately, I'm the one getting thrashed by teams that I have no business losing the way that I do under that higher difficulty level at times. Now there is a part of me that wonders if this is EA's way of attempting to simulate the realism that is the NFL. There are times where even the best teams, in real life, will get beat down or defeated quite handsomely by teams they have no business losing to. However, that happens because of poor coaching, or poor game planning, or misexecution, or just better playcalling throughout the game. If I lose a game I can swallow that if it's because I know I made mistakes during the game, or made poor decisions, or whatever it was that I did. However, AI does not beat you because you screwed up. No. It merely decides that you WILL lose and there is NOTHING you can do about it. I've had pass rushers constantly beating the OL consistently all game long when at critical junctures in the game will suddenly be incapable of making the plays they once were consistently making. Or the AVERAGE running back that breaks 5 to 7 tackles on the way to a big run. Or after calling an inside blitz on the team, and guessing that it will be an inside run, the AI still manages to create a hole big enough for a MAC Truck to run through.Then when you rush in to the hole, your player is magically sucked into a block and you miss the tackle; allowing a big gain or TD from the AVERAGE running back. My teams almost NEVER intercept passes or recover fumbles. Offensively there are times where receivers will for some reason decide they are incapable of looking for the ball when thrown at. Or my QB on critical 3rd downs will throw erratic passes. Again, I am unsure if this is EA's attempt at putting something in the code to cause this stuff, but it is extremely frustrating. I would rather lose because of something stupid I did, and not because the AI is programmed to go, "Ok, Player 1. You've succeeded enough here. Now it's time for you to lose in any way I can make you lose. Even if it's borderline cheating." I still have a ways to go in tinkering with the AI sliders so that the AI will be a little bit more "fair". (4) Sometimes the game will just randomly change your depth chart and cut players you didn't intend to cut. Now as of the date of this review I haven't experienced this in a couple weeks. Perhaps an update fixed this, as we're now up to version 1.06. (5) This is just my opinion, but I still don't like the playcalling layout. It's the same layout as it was in Madden NFL 15, and I still hate it now. I thought the best way you could playcall was how it was laid out in NCAA Football 12 and 14. I'm just not a fan of this layout.

Some of the GOOD: (1) The animations are great. I really like what they've done with the tackle animations. Catching on the sidelines look great. (2) I think the presentation is pretty darn good. There are those that think it's terrible or bland. I find it refreshing. I like how they update it weekly, and I do hear new tidbits from week to week I didn't hear before. That doesn't mean I don't hear some of the same things from week to week, either. However, I think the presentation is far better than what it was in say in the over eccentric style of Madden NFL 12, or that horrible radio style in Madden NFL 08. (3) Custom playbooks. (4) Franchise mode is pretty darn deep, but not to the point where it gets ridiculous. You can easily sign and cut players. Trading is just as easy as it was back in Madden NFL 25. There are still the news stories and the nice little fake tweets that come from analysts from around the NFL media. Gameplanning is simple yet does have a nice boost to your players from week to week. Now this Gameplanning feature can also be a bad thing as because it is so simple, do not think it goes into the kind of depth that say NFL 2k5 did way back in the day. Planning for the draft throughout the season is possible and easy to do. However, with that said I miss it was done back in Madden NFL 25 as you could key in on certain attributes you found important. Unfortunately, you only get three slots per player to scout, and you only get a glimpse at the their top three attributes. So it's good for simplicity purposes, but it's bad as it's lost some of that ability to really key in on what you find important to scout for. (5) While above I just dogged the AI for being inconsistent, the gameplay and the actual game of football is an overall fun experience. Lord knows I've played some really bad football games. To give this game a one star, I would say you would be comparing this game to LJN's NFL game from the NES, or the old Intellivision NFL game, or for a more current example of poor football you would have to look back to the NFL Fever games on Xbox (yeah I know some people think they're great, but to me they're awful). Gameplay here is pretty darn good. I'm not sure how Madden NFL 25 still feels like it has superior gameplay to me, but it does. Madden NFL 17 is a little sluggish compared to other titles in it's past, but it's still good. I'm in the minority I guess when I say I like the random icons that pop up in order to break a tackle. The kicking system is great, I think. It really forces you to focus, and field goals are no longer a gimmie. All the other basics such as running and passing work great as well.

A few other thoughts: the MUT feature was fun to me for about a week and then I lost interest. I think it's more designed for online multiplayer, and I just didn't take the plunge. However, it was good to play the MUT as it helped me get more familiar with the game mechanics. The menu at the start is overly convoluted. I'm not sure when EA decided that this tile style of options was a good idea, but I miss the good old simple menus of the 90s. It worked then, and I'm not sure why it wouldn't work today. It feels like there is a big emphasis on flash and glitz in the menus. It's odd. The soundtrack leaves much to be desired. However, I'm a guy who's favorite bands are from the 90s grunge era and still enjoys metal from the 80s and 90s. I've never really cared much for music of today. The ability to choose various uniforms is awesome. I'm surprised it's not DLC in today's world. With the NFL rules making it so teams can no longer switch to different colors of helmets, it's nice that EA has decided to ignore this rule so you can break out those cool Patriot uniforms of the 80s and 90s, or the old Broncos unis from back in the day.

All in all it's a good game. It's not my favorite Madden. That's a tie between the 2005 and 25 iterations. However, this is a solid entry, and is certainly my favorite on PS4. I must admit, though, it's really only a matter of time before I put this version down, and go back to playing Madden NFL 25 on PS3 again.

I was pleasantly surprised with this game. I played the original Ghost Recon back in the day. I still have old discs. So when I initially saw the way this game was to be played I was turned off. I had no interest, and with the way Ubisoft has just come out with one average game after the other complete with way toi much DLC and bugs I didn't wish to buy. That was until a good friend of mine bought it. I watched him play it, and after taking the controls and playing it I completely changed my mind. After 15 minutes I knew I had to buy this game. Its not old school Ghost Recon by any means. You really have to go into this with the mindset that this game is more of an action/arcade open world cleanse the country of drug lords and bad guys kind of game.

So I own this game now and have put quite a few hours in. I totally recommend this game. It is not without its flaws, but the core gameplay and plot is so SO satisfying that those two elements more than make up for those flaws. DLC is there but it is not invasive which is great. If you wish to grind and get those weapons and items you can do that. If you wish to outright buy them then you can do that as well. Gameplay feels a lot like Metal Gear Solid V. The way you can approach each mission the way you want, and how the third person view works with combat and sneaking is also very similar. Using your drones before you make your approach is very satisfying and puts some strategery into the game I like. The way selecting missions and doing side missions on the map actually reminds me a great deal with how the Batman Arkham games function. Side missions are plentiful and they feel like they actually add value to the game by leveling up and fleshing out the story some more. The AI that works with you is phenomenal. They fight better than me at times. Enemy AI is a mixed bag. I find when I die its more because I was overwhelmed and not because they just outsmarted me.

Are there problems? You bet. Vehicles and flying is a pain and take quite a bit to get used to. There is the occasional bug where a character will just get stuck in the air or be phased between walls. Online play with a friend is great but it is also more difficult. When you play by yourself you have 3 computer players with you, so there are 4 of you. If its just you and a friend then you don't get two extra computer players to help. Its just you and your buddy. That has a tendancy to make the game more difficult than it needs to be.

Overall its a great experience with TONS to do. This game will certainly keep you busy and its fun. I'm actually liking this game way more than say a game like Metal Gear Solid V. I mean the plot actually makes sense and the story never loses traction to me. Its a game you can play for 5 to 10 minutes at a time or spend hours on at once. So for you parents out there who have unpredictable schedules like me, this game is a win in that department as well. Pick this one up! Its a good time!

This is a great racing title for the Xbox One. Controls are smooth, upgrading your car is a breeze, picking a race is easy, and the car selection is great. A real competitor to Sony's Gran Turismo series. However, there are a couple flaws with this game that almost kill it for me. First, there are no standings. It doesn't matter what position you end up in. As long as you make 3rd or better you progress. Oh sure if you place higher you get more money, but as you progress getting money becomes less and less important because it's so easy to acquire funds and cars throughout the game. So while the game is fun at it's core, and can be challenging, there isn't much incentive to keep playing other than to collect more cars. So those are my two gripes with the game. No standings or real championship mode, and not much of a goal to the end of the game. However, if you're an Xbox One owner who loves racing games this is still a title I would highly recommend. For those two gripes I have with the game the racing itself is just awesome and the AI is relentless. One of my gripes with the Gran Turismo series is that the AI is stale and predictable. Not here which is great. Cars will try and run you off the road and spin out in front you jockeying for position. Weather effects are great here too. Driving in the rain really makes you feel like you're on the very edge of out of control but still in control if that makes sense. Most games fail at this but not here. An overall very good experience and highly recommended.

I've said it before and I'll say it again, Universal Vivendi ruined this series for me.  This game is better than the one I have for the Wii but not by much.  There's only one world to explore and like a previous reviewer said, the level portals aren't named so that is a bit of a pain.  Yes you do have to collect something other than gems in this one as in previous Spyro titles but mine froze quite a bit (probably got one of the earlier copies released) and the load time was annoying.  I'm used to the PS games taking time to load but this one took forever!  I could've gone and made a five course meal in the time it took.  Okay so I'm exaggerating but as I recall the first 3 Spyro titles had quicker load times.  Either way, even though it's been almost six years since I bought this game, I'm still disappointed with it.

I didn't buy my Wii from Amazon because I wasn't about to pay $309 for what I could get for $250 if I was patient for once in my life. I was lucky enough to have gone into Wal-Mart at 5:30 and found one. I had previously played one of my best friends Wiis and loved it. I'm still getting used to not being able to sit down to play but that's what I like about this system is that you can't be a lazy a** playing it. I haven't yet tried out the game I bought (Twilight Princess) but I'm sure I'm going to love that game as well as get frustrated with it.
I'd recommend this system to anyone no matter the age. It's the least expensive of the gaming systems out there right now. Yeah it's going to probably take a while to find one. Me, it took me less than a week to find mine but I got very lucky.

I've had my Wii for about a month now and I've played three games previously but none measure up to Twilight Princess. This game is addicting although it is slightly different from the two other Zelda games I've played which are Majora's Mask and Ocarina of Time. It does have a few things I don't like which are:
Now you cannot call Epona wherever you happen to be, you have to look for Whistle Grass. This wouldn't be so bad if Hyrule Field wasn't so massive compared to its size in OoT.
Now when you catch a fairy in a bottle you don't keep it until you use it, you keep it until you exit whatever temple/area you are in & it only refills eight hearts instead of all them as in OoT. Not that you even need them, at least not for the bosses because they are too f*n easy to kill which is the third thing I don't like. If you die you're not paying attention to what you are doing and getting too close too many times.
One other thing that kinda gets me annoyed is that they have locations from OoT but they're not in the same place as they were before. Like the Temple of Time. Now access to it is from the Sacred Grove which is similar to the Lost Woods in that it has Skull Kids and you must follow the music, as well as the Skull Kids lantern light to find the right path. The Skull Kid now attacks you and you fight him twice. The first time is as a wolf which makes it a bit of a challenge but it's still not too awfully difficult. The second time is a lot easier as you are back in human form and shoot him with arrows.
Lastly, Midna takes Navi's place as far as informing you about the next task you need to do but she doesn't give you hints about how to kill certain enemies. I'm one who likes to know what the enemy I'm confronted with is called which Midna doesn't tell you.
But even with all these things I like the game. Midna is a bit annoying because of her attitude but I still don't hate her. There are a lot of new enemies as well as some old ones. You still must hunt down special items such as the Fused Shadows and Mirror Shards. There are also Golden Insects which I'm not sure what you get as a reward for but I think it's a bigger wallet. But I haven't gotten them and still have managed to make significant progress in the game. I have all the Fused Shadows and am working toward the final Mirror Shard but like I said, they were easy as 123 to obtain.
I still don't understand why they changed the location in which Link supposedly grew up but oh well. I still consider the $50 I paid for this game money well spent which I can't say for Spyro.

This game was too easy even given the fact that when it shows you that you need to swing the Wii-mote upward it doesn't always register.  I thought at first it might be that I wasn't in range of the Wiis sensor bar but nope, not the problem.  I did have fun playing this game but I managed to finish the entire thing in three days! I do not yet have this game but reading the reviews it sounds exactly like the second game in the Legend of Spyro series.  I am mainly reviewing to say that my opinion of Enter the Dragon hasn't changed at all... give Insomniac the reigns to the Spyro series because they did it better.  The original Spyro games (for the PS) are much better.  I loved Spyro because of the collecting of gems, eggs and other items not for the fighting and that is exactly what Universal or whoever is making the games now has done is made into a long, continous, and therefore boring battle.  All I can say is don't waste your money on the Spyro games for PS2, PS3 or the Wii.

Okay I'm going to start off by saying that I have played 5 out of the 7 Spyro games I know of. The first three for the original PS and Enter the Dragonfly as well as A Hero's Tail. I found that I loved these games until Insomniac quit being involved in making them and Universal/Vivendi took over. A Hero's Tail was better than Enter the Dragonfly which had so many bugs and not enough of the subworlds I was accustomed to.
I bought this game figuring maybe, just maybe Universal had listened to the customer's who said they miss the Spyro from the original games but no, they didn't listen.
This game is the polar opposite of the Spyro games for PS in that all you do is walk a little, kill some enemies, walk a little more and.... you guessed it kill some enemies. There's no collecting of items just fighting. If I wanted a game that only involved fighting I'd buy Mortal Kombat (which I loved back in the day). This game was so boring and disappointing I didn't finish it. It was a waste of my money and I'd sell it but I do not want to torture anyone with a game this boring. If you like fighting games then this is for you but if you've been a fan of the Spyro series from the beginning you're probably going to say the same thing I did and that is that this game stinks. Please, Universal, listen to the customers if you plan on making anymore Spyro games and if not, then just quit making them because these last few games are horrible!

Just Dance 2014 is the next version of the Just Dance series. While in the past they have been called Just Dance, 2, 3, 4, they have now decided to switch to naming them after the year they are released. This seems like a smarter plan because going by the year, you can probably get an idea of what songs are on the game for that year, since they tend to choose the most popular recent songs, but of course, they always mix it up with some old songs as well.

Each version i have played continue to be fun since you start to get slightly bored of the same songs after 50+ times. They've added a couple new features which really compliment the game well. The puppet master mode has to be my favorite addition. It lets the player in control of the gamepad determine all the moves for the player whom is dancing. pretty cool idea and good use of the gamepad. I would recommend this game for ages 7+ and it creates a pretty good workout. i work up a sweat every single time we play. good addition to the just dance series

I never have issues with them. They look and sound great, i recommend these to everyone.

Far Cry Primal is an awesome gameplay experience. Unlike most other Far Cry games, the “primal setting” puts it around 10,000 BC, instead of a time when guns, grenades, and rocket launchers exist. As you stroll though the land of Oros, the fictional open world setting, you will come across mammoths and saber tooth tigers. The main character, Takkar, is a Wenja tribesman. He has just arrived to Oros and is seeking to rebuild his tribe. As he goes about building a village, other hostile tribes are trying to enslave or murder the Wenja. As the game progresses you will walk across discovering new places, gather materials to use for building and crafting, and hunting/taming wild animals. Yes, I did indeed say taming. In the game, the main character is a beast master. See a cool dire, well make him your loyal pet. See a big bear to help you war against the other tribes, well throw him some meat and tame him. It kind of gives you that pokemon feel where you just “gotta catch ‘em all. The pets will fight for you, aid you in hunting, and will most definitely provide with entertainment.

However, I did have some reservations about the game. I like most first person shooter games, I prefer the game to give me a gun and let me shoot up the bad guys like previous Far Cry titles. Instead you get weapons like clubs and spears. These weapons are mostly suited for close quarters combat, but can be thrown at the bad guys. Let me tell you, there is something really gratifying about cracking skulls with your war club. If you want to be more stealthy about your kills, you can sneak around and perform instant take downs if you do not alert the enemy. If you want to go for range combat, you can pull out your bow and let the arrows fly. The game really lets you fight to whatever style suits you.

For the most part, the game follows the same formula of previous far cry titles. You run around an open world, take an outpost or camp, and continue doing story missions. If you enjoyed the previous game, then this will be a refreshing Far Cry title.

The story takes place in New York some time in the near future. On black friday, the spread of a disease and causes the city to go into quarantine. The resulting quarantine leads to city wide panic and chaos. Different factions build within the city. One faction pillages the city for potential loot and another group tries to contain the disease by killing the infected people by fire. At this point, the feds send in a group of highly trained agents, designated the division. On a side note, the game is called the division but i noticed nothing about math. The agents job is to contain the chaos and restore order, i.e. kill as many bad guys as possible.

The developers did a very good job of recreating New York City. A lot of famous landmarks were recreated pretty accurately to how they look in real life. Time square and the empire state building are a few of the places you can see within the game. In game movie/cut scenes were pretty breath taking.

The game plays a lot like an RPG. You create a character, level them up, and upgrade as you progress. The character itself is very organic and can be upgraded to suit your tastes based on how you equip or assign skills to your character. If you like to play the support/healer, you can equip med kits. You can throw up explosive drones, shields, and turrets. If you like the recon role you can take skills like scan pulse. The game allows you to change out your skills and equipment to help fulfill whatever role you want to play when you party up. The gameplay mechanics are pretty cool though. This game is played in a third person and allows your character to use a cover system along with some traditional first person shooter mechanics. The game really reminds me of the old SOCOM series. When you are walking around with your gun, you have a cross hair that indicated what you are looking at or aiming at when you are firing from the hip. However, depending on the gun, when you aim, your cross hair shrinks and concentrates the bullets on the target you are firing at. If you are using a gun with a scope you will go into a view of the scope and make carefully aimed precision shots. When you throw items like grenades or turrets, there is a visible arch that shows up on the screen that shows how the grenade will travel when thrown.

When you are playing the game, there are safe houses where your character is in a safe zone. At the safe house, your character has the ability to purchase weapons, armor, and mods for your gun. To make the purchases your character loots money from the bad guys you've killed or for completing missions. Aside from buying items, there is a loot system. You go out into the open world and you can find treasure chests. For every guys you kill, there is a possibility that the enemy will drop a gun you might be looking for or certain armor. In the dark zone, the pvp area, you can kill other players and loot off of them. However, each item is contaminated and you must get a helicopter to pick up your fresh loot and decontaminate it. If you don't get it to the helicopter, all the decontaminated loot you just stole can be stolen off of you if you are killed. Once it is decontaminated, that loot is your and cannot be stolen.

When you play the game, you are allowed to have up to 4 people in your party. It is pretty easy to find your friends and starting a party. Once you have partied up, you can go around completing missions, or fighting in the dark zone. What sucks about the party system is that the average level of the enemy AI is an average of the teams level. So if you are a really low level teaming up with a really high level guy, you may have a hard time playing with your low tier gear and fighting AI more stronger than you.

I like that the game is different from most games i play. The third person aspect is nice and the RPG elements make me want to keep playing it. What makes the game really enjoyable is playing with a party. This game was made to be played with friends. What i don't like about the game is that it seams to be really linear. The open world does not seems to be a true open world. You are kind of forced to these way points to progress the game rather than you exploring, finding, and initiating certain story points. Some people like this very straight forward approach, but i feel like this game loses some of its value because of how linear it is.

I have owned many, many headsets over the years. My oldest pair is some [[ASIN:B005D6EQA6 Sharkoon X-Tatic SR Gaming Headset with Dolby Headphone Technology for PS3/PC/XBOX 360]] which still work to this day and are still one of my favorites. My most recent set is the [[ASIN:B014F77FGA ASTRO Gaming A40 TR Headset + MixAmp Pro TR for PS4]] and while these LucidSound Wireless are excellent for the price, they are not as good as my astro a40's, but that is to be expected IMO. All these other reviews for "BEST GAMING HEADSET" ever seem a little too excited and maybe have not tried 7.1 surround sound headsets.
This headset tries to be universal and when it comes to gaming, i think this is a difficult task to accomplish while staying within a reasonable price point and look cool. Immediately, I noticed that these cups are round and not oval like most gaming headsets. These will not fit well on those with bigger ears or be as comfortable for long periods of time. Yes these are comfy, don't get me wrong, but not as comfy as they possibly could be. My ears start to become tender after a couple hours, not something i'm used to.
A really cool feature on this headset is the gaming volume wheel and the mic volume wheel. I thought this was really great design and you get used to using it really quick.
Overall i would recommend these to those who have small to average sized ears, and those looking for a great sounding headset at this price point. I also own [[ASIN:B0087OZ5FG Pulse Elite Edition Wireless Stereo Headset]] and these are WAY better than those.

The story of Watch Dogs 2 takes place in the San Francisco Bay area, where the protagonist Marcus Holloway has been recruited into a special organization called DedSec. DedSec is an organization for unemployed hackers who have lost their jobs because of the city. DedSec's goal is to exploit the city of their actions to people living inside San Francisco and get them to join their cause.

If you've played the first watch dogs, its basically the same idea except theres new toys (i.e. drones) and some new skills. I enjoyed how challenging the story missions were and the co-op missions were fun. The PvP was really fun. Tracking and trying to kill your opponent is exciting. Hacking your environment to try and screw them up. The level of detail was impressive. I felt like they did a darn good job replicating a lot of the San Francisco area.

The game IS included with this Gold edition. If you already have the game you would be better off purchasing it for $30 in the PS4 store.

Compared to Call of Duty or other first person shooter games, Rainbow Six Seige is a more patient, yet every second on the timed rounds count. When you load into a game, it gives you a list of all the operators to choose from (you must purchase the operators with in game credits). These operators are categorized into Offensive and Defensive operators. Each one of these operators in the game come with unique weapons or abiities such as placing down traps or having drones that can deal damage.

When defending in Rainbow Six Siege, your mission is to defend bombs, hold supply containers, or guard a hostage. The recruit operator can either be used on offense or defense but either come with essentials for both holding objectives or. When defending, the recruit can come with barricades, explosives, barbed wire etc. each delaying or killing an enemy.

When attacking in Rainbow Six Siege, you must invade the objectives, destroy the defenses and kill enemies along the way. The offensive recruit can be equipped with breach charges which can be used to destroy non-barricaded walls, drones to see past hostile defenses, flash bangs etc. Attacking is more fun than defending because instead of being inside couped up inside a room, you can be out and about trying to find enemies that might be roaming or just find them inside the objective room, earning extra points.

Though as fun as it sounds, Rainbow Six Siege requires much more patience and time as the time to kill in this game( how fast or slow it is to kill an enemy) is very quick. Running around corners is a big no in this slow pace game as there might be an enemy with a rifle or shotgun pointing down the way your coming from. Any weapon can be an instant kill to the head whether if its a sniper or a pistol (Which is why the game is not that much similar to Call Of Duty).

With the Year 2 season pass, it offers two new operators every season(3 months or so) with an offensive and defensive character with access a week earlier. The first two operators of this season (when this review was written) is Mira on defense, and Jackal on offense. Starting with the defensive operator Mira, her main ability is to create a kill hole on re-enforced or regular walls allowing her and her team mates to shoot through. Keep in mind the enemies can shoot right back at her. The offensive operator Jackal comes equipped with a headgear that allows him to sea the foot prints of enemies and can trace their location which will pulse every 5 seconds 3 times, which isn't really that game changing seeing as most people don't like to leave the objective room.

Overall the game play is really smooth and enjoyable allowing players to have a more casual and fun time playing Rainbow Six Siege.

The mic and sound quality are amazing so I will continue to use these till they break. The controls are easy to use, the buttons are very large and have clear symbols on the functions each button does. I was able to figure out the headset within a couple minutes. There are two audio wheels for controlling the voices of people online as well as special effects/music audio; however, whether I'm in a party chat or in an in-game chat, the audio wheels are very confusing when I'm trying to adjust the sound because even though they display their according functions, it is not the case. Very often, only one wheel controls all of the audio, so it becomes a hassle to communicate with my friends in a high-paced game while still trying to adjust the audio.
I would opt to skip these and look elsewhere for a better headset.

This is the same old kirby game except with robots and amiibo compatibility. It is really easy and it would have been nice if they added a difficulty setting. Some more challenging stages and Ai would help as well.

You can't combine abilities and movesets are very limited compared to other platformers. It also doesn't take advantage of the gyroscope, camera, microphone, and touchscreen features the 3ds has.

I just wish kirby would step its game up because as of now, it is just better to get the dream collection for the wii and not buy any new (same) kirby games.

2 things that you will notice right away is that you are not getting budokai 2 with this collection, so keep your ps2 copy, and it hasn't held up with the times. It makes me feel sad saying this. I really wanted to enjoy it, but with more polished games like xenoverse, the tenkaichi series, and other anime fighters like naruto storm. This just didn't hit the spot.
Everything was great about this game, but it still lacked being challenging. It was far too easy, can you at least give us a difficulty setting?

This title is trying too hard to be like front mission except that it is definitely the weaker cousin. This doesn't even feel like a true zoids title. You only have a story mode and don't have a selection of zoids.

The tactical combat is slow and repetitive. Can't compare to fire emblem and front mission. I recommend to get the gamecube and ds zoids games. If you really need a mech tactics game then get Front Mission.

This game does have stealth elements but it is no where near as good as tenchu. You can find people online despite this game being dead. Just don't expect to get 4 people. Wait like 5 minutes and you can get 1 person to play with. It is much more fun playing with people than by yourself, it is meant to be a co op experience.

Not as great a game as I thought it'd be.  It's very artistic and visually very appealing, but the storyline was lacking.  It felt too predictable, even though it had some twists they were typical Hollywood twists where you respond with "ah I should have known."
Works great.  Looks official.

Works great.  A little bit difficult to attach. You have to kind of stretch the controller to fit it.  I always felt like I was going to break the controller every time I plugged it in.  It does fit perfectly and really you don't have to constantly disconnect it like I always did.

First off I want to say that I do like these headphones. The sound quality is nice, but just as importantly the mic quality is nice. My words are very clearly heard and the mic feedback is appreciated.

They get plenty loud and for just hearing sounds they're pretty impressive. I am however disappointed in the quality of the surround sound. I've very rarely ever heard a sound that seems to be coming from behind me. It could just be that the games aren't designed with 7.1 in mind, but I'm suspecting that the speakers are so small and bunched together in the headset that you just end up with a slightly more dynamic stereo sound than a 7.1.

Not return worthy, or replacement worthy. If I could go back in time I might consider spending the same amount of money on a higher fidelity stereo set, however.

You can't as quickly just run your fingers over the remote and know where the buttons are. Eventually mine stopped responding (kept falling back asleep in my hands).

I bought an Insignia Media Remote for Xbox One from Best Buy (not available on Amazon for some reason) for $10 less than the Microsoft remote and I like it MUCH more. No back lighting, but it has the same layout only with physical buttons and it's much more responsive.

Bought it to use as a wii classic controller and as a wiimote for New Super Mario Bros U. Be warned that this is not a wii U pro controller, I understood that when I bought it. It works fine as a classic controller that doesn't need to be attached to a wiimote. The wiimote function on it I wanted to use with New Super Mario Bros U and honestly it does work but you'll have a heck of a time trying not to press the A button by accident, sending you into a bubble when you're trying to use 1 and 2 for run and jump which are mapped to X and Y on this controller and cannot be mapped to A and B. I still give it a 4 star rating because I mainly wanted it as a Classic Controller that didn't require a wiimote hanging from it. Works just fine on Tekken Tag 2 and anything else that works with the classic controller like virtual console games.

Awesome game. It's a great version of the game, but the PS3/Xbox 360 version is better if you really want to be competitive, I can hardly find anyone online in this at any given time. Half the time it's someone in Japan who's lagging and it's not fun.

This is a basically a speed challenge mode version of Mario bros as the timer is already at 100 seconds left. If you want a challenge pick it up, if you're a casual Mario player I'd avoid it because you will be very frustrated on some parts. My biggest complaint is that with multiple players you cannot use the Gamepad as the controller, you have to have pro controllers or Wiimotes for each player. I think that is a major turn off for people who only have a Gamepad and one extra controller or Wiimote. It seems like a tactic Nintendo is using to force players to buy more controllers. In multiplayer the Gamepad just become a toy for someone else to hold and interact with the environment (sort of) in each level. For that I will mark it off a star.

First and foremost, this is NOT a game for children. The cover could deceive some in thinking its safe for kids, but it is mark "Mature" for a reason.

Now on to the game review - which this game took a very different and welcomed approach for a third person action game. The concept of having the character you control actually interact with you is pretty damn cool. I'm on the very last mission and I can tell you that you will enjoy this game if you like crude humor and some damn cool bloody violence in your super hero games. I laughed out loud several times playing this game. This is not a serious game and shouldn't be taken seriously either as the premise is that it is a game. Dead Pool himself reminds you of that often throughout the game.

You use Dead Pool points in order to build up your health, strength, get different combos, and purchase different weapons. You will find that a bear trap, yes - bear traps, will come in very handy when fighting bosses and I recommend get them early. Also, a well planted mine will help big time when dealing with the "clones" because if enough of them get close to you and they explode, well you're dead. Throwing a mine out as they are chasing you will do the trick exploding every one of them within range though.

If you are a Marvel fan you will find the cameos really cool, from Cable, Wolverine, to Rogue along with a few others. The game does somewhat get repetitive, but not enough to bore you. High Moon Studios did a good job with changing things up for the player. I found myself wanting some more of the repetitive waves of baddies coming after me just to try out the new stuff I upgraded. Now, the camera angle at times can be your worst enemy as you will get in spots where you can't even see yourself or your opponent. In these cases you will just have to run out into a more open area or you fall to your death due to the camera angle.

All in all this is a very cool, rude, crude, uncouth, and violent good time. If you are not familiar with Dead Pool just look up "Dead Pool in three minutes" on YouTube and you can get the quick down and dirty on him before you start your game. What do you call the sound of a robotic arm clapping? - Dubstep.

This is a multiplayer review as I don't play the Battlefield games for their campaign.  I've played the battlefield series of games since Battlefield 2 first came out on the PC and I've been hooked on them ever since.  I would have reviewed Battlefield 3, but there were already so many reviews that what I had to say had already been said.  BF 4 has some of the same glitches as BF 3 did on launch.  This one hasn't had as many for me as I had with the launch of BF 3 though.  The game locked up (froze) on me on launch day once and it locked up on me once on the second day of release also.  With that said I remember several lock ups with BF 3 on launch amongst other things as being stuck on or in an object within the map etc. the first month or so after release.  I honestly believe that BF 4 was created for the PC and the next gen consoles and that is why we have the frame rate drops when there is a lot of action going on around you in BF 4 on the 360.  For the most part I have really enjoyed the changes in the game i.e. tanks are harder to kill with rockets and the interaction with the environment.  You have buildings you can totally collapse killing anyone left in it, on it, or in front of it; you have flooded areas that if the supporting structure is blown up by someone, you will be killed by the impact of the water and debris - there is also other maps that have similar interactions with the environment.  Unfortunately though, at this point (as others have mentioned) you can't form a squad with your friends in order to launch into a game together.  This is a real pain the butt as you then have to find an empty server then have them all join on you.  This is something that really has to be fixed and I will also post this issue on their Battlelog web page.  The Dice team has been pretty good in the past with listening to the issues we have with their games and they patch it.  Even though there are bugs that need to be fixed, which is common on launch with most games - I still really enjoy BF 4.  Once the issues are fixed I will probably upgrade "my" opinion of this game to 5 stars, but then again I will have the Xbox One on the 22 November, so I won't be playing BF 4 on the 360.  In closing I believe this is an excellent multiplayer game with some launch day issues that need to be fixed.

If you are the owner of an SNK neo-geo system, then chances are you've either owned, played, or spotted some of the earlier installments of Metal Slug in some shape or form (if not this one). To those who haven't, just look at it as being SNK's answer to Konami's "Contra." SNK has finally decided to port one of their 2d classics over to the xbox gaming console.
The player is given the option of choosing one of four characters (two males and two females) to drag along into battle through five immense stages. Five immense solid 2d stages. No 3D (2.5D) influences whatsoever. This is classic 2d shooting at it's finest.
The player can choose to go into battle alone (one player game) or can also have a friend tag along (two player game with shared continues) for an even greater challenge. During gameplay, the player/s will collect several crucial weapons (firearms) to help them through battle. Rescue fellow hostages and be rewarded with vital items (rescuing hostages also adds to bonus points once having finished completing a stage).
The game's difficulty is tough (I must admit) it's no cake-walk. Player's may find themselves constantly replaying certain stages in order to complete. Since the game does force the player/s to restart the stage he/she die on all over again from scratch when they've lost all their lives (no checkpoints) even if the player/s have continues left. This may come as an annoyance to some, given the fact that continues are limited. However, there is a save feature which lets players replay stages over (stages they've completed in general) so if all continues are lost, they can replay the stage they were just on from the title screen.
Metal Slug 3 offer replay value in the sense that when having finished completing a game mode, others will soon be accessable. Why only four stars? It all comes down to the simple fact that Metal Slug 3 isn't a game for everyone. Fans of high polygon-count titles, tremendous graphics, etc., may not find themselves at home. Metal Slug is a game that's mainly aimed towards the oldschool 2d veterans of fast-actioned arcade platformers. Classic 2d shooter at it's best. Just don't expect to be too blown away.

Xbox owners are finally able to experience the hype behind the GG series with an extended version the PS2 GGX2. The xbox version features three characters that are selectable right off the bat (from a bale of selectable characters) that weren't in the PS2 version, one of which is an entirely never-before-seen new character as well.

Like Capcom Vs. SNK 2 EO, GGX2R is an arcade port with every single frame kept intact. GGX2R also harneses some of the most beautifully-detailed 2d backgrounds and character animations ever seen in a 2d fighting game (only game that rivals in this aspect is the SF3 series).

Controls are fairly decent, though at times they can feel a tad unresponsive and rigid. This mainly depends on the players preference on controller setting. Overall, the controls are virtuos.

Unfortunatley, also like CVS.SNK2 EO, GGX2R lags in the online department (but not nearly as faulty as CVS.SNK2 EO). Despite the developers working on hard to prevent this problem, there is STILL slowdown when heading off against opponents online. There are times when the connection status will show "Excellent" and still have slight delay in play (slowdown). Also, if the connect shows "bad" or "poor" you can forget it. The controls will be so slow to respond that it's nearlly impossible to pull off moves correctly. However, this isn't an all time aspect, it just appears from time to time, so have no fear.

That said, GGX2R is a perfect port to an excellent 2d fighter, and with a price tag for under twenty bucks, you simply cannot go wrong. A must have title, for any sincere 2d gamer.

I must confess that I am a die-hard fan of the BR series (I absolutely enjoyed the first BR). So when BR2 was confirmed, I was ecstatic, and seeing the screenshots of the title sent me to my game retailer to pre-order the title. Now that I finally own the title, I must confess that I'm left with a result that leaves me with a sour taste in my mouth.

As we last remembered, BR1 left off with Rayne discovering that her father is still alive, so she thus seeks out found him. BR2 practically pick ups from that spot after years of Rayne's premeditation, but doesn't seen harness that magic that was of the BR1. As I went through BR1 I felt compelled to play on, to learn more about the story, and about Rayne. BR2's story just appears watered down and doesn't truly give any incentive as to why to continue playing the game. In BR2, Rayne just works as an agent that's assigned to do this and that instead of working upon her own free will (as to that of BR1 in the second half of the game).

Another complaint is the combat system. What on earth happened to being able to pick up firearms?!! One thing I truly adored about BR1 was your freedom to pick up practically any weapon the enemy dropped (shotguns, rocket launchers, etc.). BR2, Rayne can only use her blades and blood gun (which runs out way to fast, and takes too long to recharge) which supposedly eliminates/takes the place of using or picking up firearms. The computer AI also, seems very dumb at times (characters running into ways etc)or occasionally stating comments such "Gotta Go!" or "Se Ya Later!" In this aspect, the game feels waaay too sanitary.

Throughout the game, Rayne learns several different skills (as did with BR1) and combination attacks, though several of them are pretty useless and probably won't ever need to be used.

Battles seem pretty repetitive (though the developers eliminated the "find a key" type missions of BR1) it's now replace with tedious "destroy all enemies to progress" ones now, and boss battles are either too easy or too tough. The graphics in the game don't seem to surprass BR1's very much (in fact, I'd go as far to say that BR1 looked better in every aspect, with the exception of BR2 using motion capture).

BR2 does have some advantages tough, the game contains unlockables such as movie sequences, and cheats password (from BR1) is still kept intact.

BR2 is alright game, gamers new to the series may love it. However, to the die-hard BR fans, don't expect to be too impressed. One thing I noticed when playing BR2 is that Rayne didn't appear to be the hardcore-bad@$$ she was in BR1. Well perhaps she's just upset that she's in this mediocre sequel. An average game.

Now, I don't have a problem with the characters all being animated in low-res, nor do have a big gripe with the completely bland & generic background music. What I DO have a quarrel with, is the completely broken gameplay & unbalanced character roster.

The character roster is one of the most marred to date for any vs series (no Zangief, Morrigan, Blanka, Yuri, no Rival School characters, no Last Blade characters, etc.) & having two different types of Ken, Mr. Karate, Akuma, & Iori don't really count as variety within the character roster. Shin Akuma & Shin Mr. Karate (of all characters) have infinite supers. This results in these types of characters being heavily abused online by noobs. Also, there is no rematch option online, & the ranking system is broken (at times if you defeat an opponent online, that opponent can acquire your win/points).

Don't think for a minute, that by placing the difficulty level on the hardest setting will give you a challenge against the computer in arcade mode. All the computer does is turtle you, shooting projectiles & spamming the same moves over & over. The hit collision is very poorly executed, with punches & kicks going right through characters (supers as well). There is even some lag-input inbetween supers at times. Also, grapples/throws which miss, result in one's power/super meter slightly decreasing (for each throw missed).

What really kills this game is how obsolete the Capcom characters feel. Characters such as Guile & Bison have had their charged-based moves/proportions adjusted drastically, making them practically useless to play as.

It's pretty neat how the characters have dialogue throughout the arcade mode. The gallery section's also a nice touch (though, unlocking each character pic via survivor mode, can be quite tedious) as well as the replay mode (which appears to have been completely stripped from CVS2 EO) which allows one to save an indefinite amount of replays to the xbox's hard drive.

All in all, this game would have been alright it were to have been released back in the mid 90s', but with it's unbalanced roster (& limited modes of play) this game's not guaranteed to hold one's interest for very long. Best wishes on seeing this one make it to a tourney.

Well first off, let me just state that I hope that noone was expecting this port to be graphically superior to it's pc counterpart. The graphics which the pc version harness could pass for next gen. Besides, just how many console ports nowadays are graphically superior to their pc cousins in general (games of which were originally developed on the pc)?

With that said, the Xbox version of HL2 is phenomenal. Of course the game's not going to look as graphically on par with it's pc counterpart (what games do, with some notable exceptions with titles such as FC:I & D3?) but you must remember that Valve build XB HL2 from the ground up with an entirely different graphics engine. Even so, the game still looks graphically superior to a majority of the games out on the current gen consoles. The physics engine is still intact & looks wonderful along with the character models.

The only real gripes here are that there's some slight framerate issues, especially noticeable right after the game boots up when entering a new area or after saving your game (very brief, but noticeable). There's also the lack of online play or even a multiplayer sequence. This port isn't exactly like the RE4 transition from GC to ps2, as to where the later port gets a host of special or exclusive features (extra modes, weapons, missions etc.). Though extra modes, weapons, multiplayer, and missions would have all been nice for the xbox version of HL2, the reality is that HL2's(gameplaywise) an exact replica of it's pc counterpart.

HL2 for xbox is a port developed on xbox for xbox owners (not pc), so if you've already experienced the game for pc, you might just want to steer clear & consider investing in HL2 Aftermath (for xbox version of HL2 is the same as the pc) for pc. However, if you haven't already played HL2 on the pc, you'd definitely want to check it out for the xbox. You simply cannot go wrong with the experience that is of HL2.

Black is one of the very few new fps' to be released this year. The game places you in the shoes of an assassin who's assigned to kill without mercy or looking back. The game consists of approximately seven stages with multiple side missions & secondary objectives. Alot of that time will be spent destroying enemy documents as well as resources. After having completed a mission, you can choose to replay it on a harder difficulty level to unlock extra weapons. So if you're the type of gamer who likes to blaze through an entire game in one sitting (on numerous occasions), this will fit well for you.

PROS:

Astonishing Graphics- Black truly pushes the current gens to their limit, proving that there's still enough juice to last them for throughout the year. However, there is the notice of dotted lines spotted thoughout stages (noticeably on walls & the ground).

Excellent Physics- The physics rival even that of some next gen titles. Explosions & smoke are nicely crafted/executed. I'm anticipating that the engine used in Black will be used by others in the near future.

Great Musical Score- The score in which the game harnesses makes you feel as if you're in a Hollywood action flick. Truly does manage to convey the feel & emotion of that in battle.

CONS:

Short Campaign Mode- While this can either be a plus or neg for some gamers (given that the game can be replayed through in a sitting), the ending leaves the gamer wanting more. The lack of multiplayer or online play leaves much to be desired.

Lack of a lean mechanic- There are several times in Black in which a "lean" action would have come in handy. Therefor, making it less of a hassle/risk attempting to maneuver when sorrounded by a flood of enemies shooting in your direction.

No jump or sprint mechanics- Being able to run or jump (or even roll) would have helped out greatly in Black. Especially when attempting to evade a grenade or explosive device.

With that said, Black's a great fps that (with a few minor tweaks & features) could have been phenomenal if it wasn't for the lack of multiplayer & online play. Those looking to Black for longterm play may want to simply stick with a rental. However, those who enjoy playing through games over & over on higher difficulties won't be disappointed with Black. I'm anticipating many great aspecs in store for the newly crafted franchise. Definitely worth checking out. In the meantime, lets keep our fingers crossed for Black 2.
