Xyanide's a sidescrolling shooter in which you're charged with the task of trying to prevent to a substance (Xyanide, which can transform thoughts into reality) from being dispersed into the planet by an evil witch by the name of Aguira, of whom was sent to be exiled. The control scheme in Xyanide is a tad different from other sidescrolling shooters. You primary shoot by holding the right thumbstick, and secondary fire using the left trigger. While the controls can be altered, the basis of them is still the same (analog for primary, L or R for secondary).

The graphics are exceptional for a current gen shooter and the colors (along with the stages) are live and vibrant all throughout the huge areas of the game. You even have the opportunity to take various routes within areas in hopes of trying to immune yourself from massive danger. The only real problem is that at times it can be a hassle locating your ship on the screen given that there is some much going on onscreen at once (paritcularly when enshrouded with a swarm of enemy ships about the same size as yours). It does however help that your ship is highlighted in green. Xyanide especially shows off it's best within stages that parrallel from one area to the next (though those with 3d motion sickness may want to be aware). The cutscene sequences are all very well composed and help accompany the storyline to the fast paced action.

As you play through the game, you'll acquire all sorts of different power-ups and specials for your ship (which is one of Xyanides main strong points, the effects in which the specials & power-ups have). Some of these power-ups can range from Energy shields, Slomo (which slows everything onscreen), invulnerability, and stealth. With specials, you have a bustle to choose from such as; Lighting Storm, Freeze, Nuke, Fire Storm, and drones. What's truly unique about specials is that you can level them up to unleash even more of a devastating effect on the enemies.

All in all, Xyanide's an exceptional shooter. Albeit there may not be enough here to satisfy the casual gamer (need I mention the game can be played with two players?), those looking for a classical shooter symbolic to those of the 80s and 90s, will definitely want to give Xyanide a look. Infusing the elements of 2d and 3d, Xyanide offers enough to distinquish itself from the current titles out, while remaining genuine to the genre. All for a low retail price. If this keeps up, gamers may just very well have a new shooting franchise on their hands.

Lost Planet is a third person shooter spearheaded by Keiji Inafune (creator of the Megaman series) in which manages to place equal emphasis on both on-ground and mecha battle sequences. The setting takes place on an entirely cold driven planet. So cold in fact, that the player is required to gather "Thermal Energy" while in battle to maintain their body at a substantial temperature. You play the role of an amnesiac character by the name of Wayne of whom must unravel the secrets of his past, in the process bringing unity to the land.

The graphics and physics in Lost Planet are easily some of the best seen on a console game by far (rivaling that of Gears of War). In some instances (where the climate is cold as can be) excess snow can be seen accumulating on your character's clothing and track (on the ground) once having entered an opened door area. The particle effects and audio are perfectly done, along with debris physics. There are cases where you can interact with the environment, like say, shooting down a boulder (which will dissipate into rubble) on a mountain or fort to clear from an enemy stronghold. Another instance, is how you're enabled to shoot down a steel rail from a ceiling ontop of the enemy. The smoke effects can come with a price, as at times, it can be hard to maneuver yourself once enshrouded in large amounts. This helps add to the intensity of the battle. Music is also very coherently composed. Mostly orchestral, which helps give the game it's cinematic feel.

The detail in each enemy is simply amazing. Some boss characters are so well detailed and animated that they practically look tangible on the screen. Several enemies can been onscreen at once with rarely a trace of slowdown or a single drop in framerate (and some bosses take up nearly the entire screen).

However, that doesn't go without saying, as there are a few notable issues (nothing breathtaking) in LP. For one, the enemy A.I. is dimwitted for the most part. Snow pirates can easily be mowed down with simple run and gun tactics. It's also discouraging as to how (in some instances) an enemy can be knocked off of a mech, and won't even bother to get back on it. This is especially questionalable when there are several unused vehicles spotted on point, yet the enemy won't even bother to use any of them to their advantage. In other cases, the a.i. comes off too sensible, with the slightest sound setting them off on full alert without scrutiny. All in all, the enemy a.i. is a mixed bag.

Another complaint is it seems as though your character is constantly getting knocked down, then heaving (rinse, repeat). For instance, there was this time in which I was hit by a laser (which sent me sprawling to the ground) only for my character to raise and immediately get blown away by a rocket launcher. This can be frustrating at times. A better wake-up mechanic/command could have helped out to suppress this problem. Especially when you're having a hard time locating your character on screen due to all of the smoke and debris particles surrounding.

Last complaint is the lack of NPCs'. During the very first mission in LP, (the backstory stage) your character Wayne is fighting alongside multiple NPCs. This was a unique trait and feature, and it was rather disappointing to discover that none of this was carried into any of the latter stages in the game (unless you count the online mutiplayer). From that point on, you're all on your own.

With all of that said, Lost Planet is still an exceptional action-shooter. Some critics have panned the game for it's lack of innovation. Who said the game needed to be innovative, much less claimed to be unprecedented? The title does what it promises; deliver an action filled (but rather short, the game can be completed in under ten hours) shooting experience. While LP's not tactical like say, Rainbow Six or Gears of War, it's still a masterful shooter in it's own right, in how it manages to blend the words of third-person shooting and mecha immersively into one.

Lost Planet managed to sell over a million copies just two days after it's release in both the US and Europe. It's fairly safe to say that we'll be seeing more from the franchise on the 360 in the near future.

Even though I've given this game a two-star rating, the truth is it is quite fun, but the two-stars stems from a major design flaw in the game itself, and that pertains to the Health Care aspect of the game.

Maxis was founded in Orinda, California, an East Bay subburb of Oakland, Berkeley and San Francisco. Orinda, like most bay area cities has a small public health facility run by the metropolitan government, but most people living in Orinda do not frequent this facility.

Will Wright himself, founder and designer of the original Sim-City, probably never visited the public health facility in Orinda when he founded the company. And if you were to look up the Yellow Pages for Orinda from the late 1980s up to today, you'll note a number of private practitioners in private hospitals or with offices nearby private run health care facilities.

In fact the entire San Francisco Bay Area is populated with private University hospitals, Kaiser Permanente, Mills in San Mateo, Seton Medical Center, and dozens and dozens and dozens of other private health care providers.

So, with that in mind, Sim City, in ALL OF ITS INCARNATIONS, does not have a free-enterprise health care system built into the game, and therefore your success with this so-called simulation, is literally contingent on how many Tax Dollars you funnel to the government run health care facilities you build and fund in the game.

This is true from the first Sim City way back in the 90s, to the current 2014 release, and this slightly older version titled Sim City 4.

For you people outisde the United States, that doesn't bother you too much because odds are your government does provide all your health care, save for select countries (Japan, the UK has private hospitals for the very wealthy and so forth).

But , in the United States, it is free-enterprise that gets the best medications and equipment for patients, and gives the best care anywhere in the entire globe (yes, that includes places like Sweden, Switzerland and Japan; our medical technology cannot be matched....life-styles on the other hand, is another issue altogether).

I doubt Will Wright so much as stepped into either a Santa Clara or San Mateo County health center for so much as a cold, and more likely stepped into a Kaiser or market competitor for some ailment.

So why, oh why, are there not more private health care providers represented in this game?

The paranoid and cynical might say that there was an agenda at work by one or more of the designers with political leanings to sublimate a public health care agenda to Gen-Xers and now the Youtube gen, EVEN THOUGH THE COMPANIES THEY WORK FOR USE PRIVATE ENTERPRISE.

Ergo, Sim-City 4, like its predecessors, is an interesting take on a version of a utopic society where finances, food, cars, and other goods and services, EXCEPT health care, are represented, even though the bio-technology and medical-technology knowhow in the United States of America, all propelled by private corporate and private free enterprise money research, is no where to be seen.

Look, I'm a poor guy. I'm still using my old 4gig P4 computer to play this game, and when you got a guy like me raising his eyebrows about the subversive nature of this game, when I should be shouting prasies at it, you know something's amiss.

All in all it's an interesting take on an old and aged (and politically skewed) city-building genre, and it does entertain, but wouldn't it be cool if there was a REAL sim-city game somewhere in the offing?

Maybe in the next iteration we can have various game companies competing with one another, and see which simulation game company sells more; the utopic government-health-care provide for all your needs version, or some true game designers who puts in a buyer-be-ware mod, and markets the new game as his own.

Gee, where have I heard that idea before?

Buy it, give it a shot. Have fun, but understand what it is you're buying.

So, Will, next time I go grab some medication at the pharmacy, will I see you at San Mateo County General or Orinda's Public Health Works, or will I bump into you at Kaiser?

Think about it.

I have an older system that I specifically built and tweaked to play this game, and I get some very choppy frame rates, even with graphics turned down. I liked the original Shogun because of its strategic simplicity and tactical challenges.

I didn't get much into the game, unlike the original Shogun. The original Shogun strategy section was easy and intuitive to learn. The tactical portion was far more challenging to learn, but once mastered was fun, even if the graphics were relatively simple compared to this newer iteration.

The real reason I'm not giving this game raving reviews is because it's a resource hog. The installation weighs in at 24Gigs, and where I have than plenty of disk space, I did have to uninstall some other other games, and shuffle some files around. On top of that it took nearly an hour to install and tweak, even with a super fast DVD drive.

I really did want to play and like this game, but it'll have to wait until I can build a new system that exceed its recommended requirements (which, by the way, my system meets).

I wasn't a huge fan of the original game, but the improved graphics and H2 interface add a little something to the first game.  If you're a fan of the original HW game, then maybe spend a little extra money to relive the experience.  If you're not, then don't bother.  The price was right enough here on Amazon that I took a chance, and I am not dissapointed.

It's okay, and that's generous. Truth be told I don't like it all that much.

Missing;
Rope Arrows
Large fully explorable maps
The monsters

The reason that's important is because that's essentially what made the first two games a success. And this game has none of those missing elements. And instead of large explorable maps a-la D&D, we get graphically detailed maps that are lacking in scope, and have an odd mix of themes.

The game mechanics are interesting enough, but the need to load sectors like the Half Life series from years before, really leaves something to be desired. I didn't get the sense that I could explore a map with any route and strategy I so chose. I didn't get the sense that I was exploring large areas and using my wits and guile to use that massive environment. Instead I got the sense that the designers felt they needed to give the series a visual facelift, but sacrificed a lot of gameplay to do so.

I'm really bothered by this. And also by the fact that you can complete the game within a few days. It doesn't have a lot of staying power on your hard drive.

There's the infamous Shalebridge Cradle level, which did not disappoint for the first half. But after that the game gets bogged down in telling a story as opposed to letting the player let the story unfold in their gameplay.

Not recommended unless you're a huge Thief fan.

A game really meant for the adroit younger crowd, this game is a more realized remake and departure from the original SEGA game which I played while in college. There was as kind of exploratory aspect that I think newer players (young and old alike) will find here, and where the old sprite game has left its magic and mark in the past, this remake helps revitalize the tale, and, to be honest, it told better than the first game, but is also much harder as well.

It's a decent game, and I', glad I cot a copy off of Steam, but not everything from the previous game made it to this one. Note that the surgar cube jar sequence, which was picturesque, has been replaced with a cup of coffee adventure swimming sequence. Kind of strange, odd and a different visual flavor (so to speak), but interesting. There's a few other revamps here and there, but otherwise this is a solid game.

It would be curious to see the sequel, World of Illusion, similarly remade.

I've been doing FPS games since the old 286 days, and I bought this game against my better judgement when it first came out. After killing armies of demons in doom, an equal number of Strogg in Quake 2, I decided to take a chance on this thing.

I couldn't get through it the first time around. There's a real disgusting torture porn scene where your character is brutally being transformed into a Strogg, and you see it from your characters point of view. I had to stop there. All of the computer generated gore in the previous games seemed to go with the kind of game and game experience being offered in Quake 2 and the addon mission packs, but this really seemed unneccesary. And so I told a coworker at the job I was at that very thing. I simply couldn't get through it.

Well, fast forward some ten to fifteen years later, and I decide to re-install it. And my assessment is that not only was the game kind of gratuitously gross, but the production values seemed over done, and to be honest, the maps weren't that interesting, nor very large. The other aspect is that the game gives you friendly AI to make you feel like you're part of an international military coalition. And of course, you're a marine.

Eh, that last part bothers me a little because "marines" are pretty mush ship's troops. The proverbial "soldier from the sea". I mean, they're specifically meant to defend ships, and, when needed, go into enemy territory. I bring this up because it begs the question of what does the regular army do during the Strogg-Earth war? Watch from the sidelines? In ID Games you're always a marine. Well, okay, but it strikes me that whoever designed this really invested a lot in "mariness" (so to speak), and for a marine force to be international in scope and nature, to me, speaks of some ignorance on the part of the programmers.

The other aspect is that there's a lot of production value in this game, but it almost overwhelms the play at times. The original Quake was a kind of ambiguous high-tech military D&D foray into the underworld. Neat. Not my cup of tea. Quake 2 created this cyborg-tech civilization gone bad, and seemed to make the setting interesting. I mean, you really can't take anything in these games seriously on any level. In the previous games were you were essentially a lone gun fighting some generically evil bad guys. But the Quake 4 developers really tried to add unneccesary "substance" to the game with all of the international "marines" and military jargon and friendly AI. It just seemed way over done.

In short, I don't like the game a whole lot. Heck, I didn't like the original DOOM games because they were so dark. Quake 2 was somewhat interesting, and the addons created for it were kind of interesting to play. But this game tries to bring a kind of level of sophistication that I think is misplaced. Q2 was essentially shoot the evil bad guys. Q4 tries to add depth and dimensionality to Quake-realm, and again, it struck me as being a little beyond odd, and into wonky territory.

I'm about 99% done. I just need to kill the final boss, and after a few tries … I just don't feel like doing it. I didn't like the game the first timer around, and find it annoying now. On the plus side the artistry in the game, the character models and skins, for the time are pretty top notch. So, if you're into game art, then maybe check it out for that, but otherwise I might pass this one up for some of the better designed shooters out on the market.

I bought the original Rollcage on a whim. It was cheap, it was ported to the PC, I had never heard of it, but it looked interesting. And it turned out to be a pretty fun game, though frustrating at times.

A couple years back I tried the PC version of this game, and boy what a poor difference it was. The cars craw along at a snail's pace, the tracks are shorter to accommodate the slower speeds, and overall it's just not interesting.

Original Rollcage had you tearing up the tracks at 500kph plus, and with dynamic weapons to shoot at other cars or to help you get ahead. This game has some of that, but the game play is so painfully slow that it's a wonder you need those extra weapons at all. It's also a wonder as to anyone who's played both games would give this game five stars.

The cars move painfully slow, the tracks are shorter, there no real need for any weapons but they're there, and where some of the locations are interesting the game play just is no fun at all. Original Rollcage may have comparatively less detailed graphics, but the gameplay is infinitely better than this thing. You really move at incredible speeds on really interesting tracks ... why the designers and developers of this game just didn't repeat that formula is beyond me.

Give this game a shot if you're really curious, but believe you me if you played the first game, then you'll hate and scratch your head at this game.

This came out a few years after Half Life, and even though it predates Half Life 2 and a few other shooters out there, it far surpasses them in every way, and even surpasses more recent games like the Call of Duty series, Battlefield and both Insurgency games.

No joke. I bought this some years after Unreal came out, and Unreal was supposed to be the FPS game to end all FPS games at that time, but to be honest Jedi Knight and Quake 2, for all of their graphical quirks had more action and story than Unreal. Then comes Far Cry, and it blows the competition out of the water.

You're a CIA agent teamed up with a scientist and a journalist who go to seek out some strange goings ons in the Indonesian archipelago. Blue skies, sandy shores and turquoise waters cannot mask the villainy that lies within. You, Jack Carver, must fight and puzzle your way through this incredibly lavishly rendered near "sandbox" setting.

The shortcomings are that when the game was first released it had to borrow from Half Life and Quake 2 in that it would have to "load sectors", or so I recall. Today that's no longer an issue with very robust gaming hardware that's out there, and you can essentially explore the huge world without having to wait for your computer to render more of it.

The maps are much larger and weapons far more accurately modeled than today's FPS games, and includes both Insurgency Sandstorm and Counter Strike Global Offensive. The downside is that the you can take more damage and carry more than those other games, but this game came out a full decade or two before Insurgency and Global Offensive, and looks and plays much better than either.

To be honest I had almost forgotten about this game. I recall the AI being really hard to beat, and the "monster" or "tri-gen" being nearly impossibly to kill, and so I played through it once or twice and forgot about it. But, I think I was playing through it on the hardest settings. Playing through it again on regular settings or "realistic" is a lot more fun.

One of the drawbacks was that even though the map is nearly an open world experience, you do get easilly killed by the AI in the form of a sniper gattling minigun from a black hawk or a man eating great white shark. So, trying to sneak your way around the main path for your objective can prove effectively impossible, and a real let down.

The story, like the Quake series, Unreal series, Star Wars Dark Forces games, is comic book stuff, but has a little more bight to it and is a little more adult in nature than those other games.

A much richer game in terms of single player, and far far more rewarding and fun than the trolling and hacking one experiences in multiplayer for other games. And, on top of that, this game also was years before Quake 4, and has larger maps and better graphics. How is that possible? I don't know, but check out the original Far Cry if you want something different and fun on your computer.

A true arcade classic and a true classic on the Genesis as well. While its a bit scaled down when compared directly with the Arcade version's graphics/sound, however, the soundtrack to the Genesis/Megadrive is superior. The individual who composed the music for this game did a very good job. Its also about one of the few areas where this version beats the SNES version which has really good graphics for a 16-bit version. This game is very easy to figure out, particularly the first few stages. The third stage is a bit tougher, just rememmber to focus on the HK air's (flying machines) and not the endoskeletons. You have a decent amount of weapons in this game, the first half of the game you have a particle beam rifle that you can upgrade with plasma energization, where in the later levels you could upgrade your basic rapid fire weapon to a gattling gun. Your secondary weapon also changes from a rocket launcher in the begining of the game to a shotgun. This game is a lot of fun, and its really fun with 2 players. The only really flaw of this game is it is FREAKIN hard. There are a few stages that I swear are impossible or, just so hard I haven't had the time or patience to figure out why I haven't beatin it yet. Though this is a really awesome game, and so is its SNES counterpart.

Mortal Kombat 3 wasn't a junk game, but it really seemed like garbage compared to the original MK1 and MK2. Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 was a shot at trying to make things right for fans and also tried to expand Mortal Kombat 3 even further. In fact, when this game came out everyone I know forgot MK3 existed and jumped straight for this one. I found out also this year you can buy a special controller set up for newer systems like PS3 that is a direct copy of the old Arcade-style controller for the original MK arcade games. And in the package it has MK 1, 2, and this game, regular MK3 just got completely dropped! Anyways, this games isn't junk either like MK3 but it missing a lot and it could have been MUCH better.

For one thing the music sounds way worse than the Genesis version. It also has a different sound a together. It has more of an industrial sound, where the Genesis version has more of a metal/electronica sound to it. The graphics are also not as good either. Probably the biggest difference between the Genesis and this version was the sound, the sound is terrible in this version of UMK3. The gameplay has got a few glitches here and there as well. This is odd because usually SNES ports of Arcade games are generally really great, but this one fell very short. For the most part the gameplay is alright, not as nearly bad as MK1, that game was puking out glitches and other issues. This game also has kind of a funny glitch, instead of saying Brutality, it says fatality after completing one, that was pretty funny in a really bad sense. This isn't a terrible game but I would just recommend getting the Genesis version instead.

This is where it all began! One of the greatest Genesis series ever was the Streets Of Rage games. This game is very fun and challenging at the same time, and with its varying levels of diffuclty you can make it either really easy or hair rippin possibly impossible lol. Anyways you can start off as either of the two classic characters in this game Axel Stone, or Blaze Fielding, and you can also use some dude named Adam, who didn't make any other appearences in the series. While this might be the first in the series the moves list for the characters is still pretty impressive. All the characters have their own combos, grappling tactics, team attacks are possible, deffensive attacks, and also each character uses weapons differently. 1 thing that is unique in this game that is not seen in the others is that you can call for some back up! If the punks literally start kickin your A$$ you can call this Police Car that looks like a Civic CRX (which adds to the retro feel and makes it great) and the dude in the ride shoots up all the enemies on screen. This game is a very good length its not to short but its also not to long. I do like the Streets of Rage games that came out later, probably more so. Though this game is a true classic that influenced many games of this genre.

Don't get me wrong, its an ok game, its kinda fun, at the same time I don't see why this game is so amazing. The music is suppose to be good, I thought it didn't do the SNES sound chip any justice. Gameplay is quite repetitive, I know a lot of games can be repetitive but its a repition that bores me. Your constantly locating stuff, that got boring. But I will say, if I was bored or just killing time before I go out it would be good for a few rounds to play. The story line is pretty impressive, so I guess the game deserves props in that area. The game is good in its own little ways, but I just don't rank it up there with some of the other classics. I have some friends that love this game, so I guess I respect it for what it is.

The second installement in the final fight series, or the cousin of Streets of Rage. Final fight was like streets of rage for SNES back in the day. The gameplay handled much more like an aracde style game than a streets of rage game. Streets of Rage had a lot of grappling and other special attack tactics. This game lacked that. FF2 had mostly simple combos and basic (clobber everything) super attacks. Still this game was a lot of fun and had some cool stages here and there. It was produced by Capcom so it had a lot of similarities to street fighter, some people even wrote it off as a street fighter meets streets of rage kind of hybrid. Decent game though.

The third installement of the SOR series! This game is also one of the best walkthrough action beat-them-up style game ever made! You have 4 characters to choose from with one secret character as well. This game is a little different 2 than the previous 2 games since there are multiple hidden paths you can take, and depending upon how you select your path determines the outcome of the game itself, it was a smart addition and added some level of detail for the game. Anyways, the game play in this SOR game might be some of the best, the controls are really well laid out, and are responsive. Each character has their own combination of attacks and speical moves, and also each character has a variety of speical attacks that can be utilized with different weapons gathered through out the game. Another very different aspect of this SOR3 is the music, its very high tempo and has some rather odd time signatures, particularly on the song cycle, and fuze. Then there are tracks that sound like nothing but classic SOR music such as the song Moon, and Poets. The graphics are great, and are the best in the series, particularly when or if you get the 1 of the final levels, the ending shows off the power of the Genesis 16-bit console. Another thing I will say is that the diffuclty in this game is also pretty high, this has got 2 be also the hardest of the SOR games. Play this game on the HARD mode and you will see what I am talking about. Lenght wise, I think its perfect, some people might find it a little long, but I think its perfect in that regards. With SOR you just can't go wrong, and this like the other SOR games is a great example of why the Genesis is a timeless game system.

Some of the sounds of the dinos roars to the sound of pounding kicks, flesh ripping bites, and explosions sound like the arcade.

However, I would have too recommend the Genesis version of this game, or the Playstation/Saturn versions also. But this version is ok, its still a pretty fun game overall.

First of all, I mean no other fighting game matches this one in replay value, due to insane combos (of which there are many different variations), great "No Mercy" (finishing) moves and a great cast of characters. I was a fan from the moment I played it for the first time, and 10 years later it is still without a doubt my favorite game of all-time. Do not be mistaken though, I am not saying all of the other fighters out there are bad(Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat are also 5 star fighters), but when Killer Instinct hit the arcades there was nothing like it, at least in my opinion. The graphics were beautiful, the combos were amazing and it seemed like an all around original game.
Other reviewers might have you believe this game rips off the others, but nothing could be further from the truth. Sure, they all share similarities, but Killer Instinct was the first to develop this complex combo system, consisting of linkers, auto-doubles and enders, not to mention the ULTRA combo. To me the ULTRA is the greatest concept of all-time as far as fighting games are concerned. It is a move performed at the end of a combo that adds many more hits to give a great-looking combo to finish off your opponent. There are also combo breakers to stop your opponent from performing a combo on you. So by now you should be able to understand that this game takes a LOT of practice to get good at. Learning the combo theory, mastering each character's moves and getting comfortable with each character's style is hard work, but with enough practice will be rewarding once you know your stuff. There are 8 great characters to choose from, each with their own background level, and depending on the location you can knock your opponent off of buildings. It has pretty decent music to boot, giving a great game experience--in my opinion one of the best games you could own for the Super NES. So if you are a fan of fighting games or own a Super NES, try this one out. You can find it for very cheap these days, so it is definately worth picking up if you see it around. You will either hate this game and never want to play it again, or you will be hooked instantly and develop an addiction to the style this game presents.

Viewtiful Joe is one of the most fun games I have played in a while. It has been stated many times that it is a highly creative, action-packed game and it certainly is. Here's the short version on the story: Joe gets pulled into a movie in order to save Silvia who has been kidnapped and taken to movieland.

The graphics in this game are awesome. Combining 2-D sidescrolling action with 3-D cel-shaded graphics gives the game the look and feel of an adventure straight out of a comic book. The fighting system in this game is very unique. Of course Joe has punch/kick abilities and combos, but as points are earned in the game you can buy new moves that definately will come in handy at some point in the game. The VFX meter allows Joe to either attack enemies in slow-motion(this becomes ideal against some enemies) or in mach speed.

The levels in VJ often contain puzzles which you must solve in order to advance. Some are very easy but others may take a little while to figure out. Plenty of characters and bosses are featured, and the bosses each have weaknesses which must be exploited to advance to the next episode.

Overall this is a must-own if you like constant button-mashing action. I love the graphics in this game and the music that accompanies it is pretty cool as well. There are secret characters to unlock also and other good stuff for beating the game on the different difficulties. But I definately recommend at least renting this title and judging for yourself. Chances are you will want to add this game to your collection and that would be a wise choice also.

Super Mario World must be considered by many to be one of the best Mario games ever created, even one of the best games of all time. The side-scrolling action we are all familiar with is as good as ever, but this game has so much more to offer.

All 96 levels are here from the Super-NES classic, almost exactly ported to the GBA. The graphics look great on this system and there may have been more secrets in the game in this version. Everything great about the game has been included: different exits to a lot of levels, keys to find secret levels and 5 dragon coins to find in each level. I guarantee a lot of gameplay and replay with this game because it will take a while to find everything in this game(unless you are using a strategy guide). I have had this game since it was released and I still havent quite found it all. There are 96 levels through 7 worlds with each world being ruled by one of Koopa's kids. Plenty of the Super Mario action that you remember.

Super Mario World represents the finest of the Super NES and it is perfectly translated here to the GBA. It is great that the game lives on and it is portable now so you can enjoy it anywhere, anytime. I definately recommend this classic to GBA owners and it is an essential part to any game collection.

Kingdom Hearts includes everything great about gaming: characters, an interesting storyline, unique gameplay, and probably some of the best graphics I have seen on the PS2. You play the game as Sora, who goes from the calm paradise life to a battle between light and darkness. Along the way you pick up many allies to help you out, each with their own strengths and weaknesses. Some of these are characters from the Final Fantasy brand but the majority are Disney characters. But do not let the Disney part fool you: this is no easy game by far. I just completed the game at over 46 hours and I still did not find everything that the game had to offer. There are a lot of puzzles to solve, some not so obvious. It gets frustrating at times but its always worth it when you figure it out. As far as the plot of it, its hard to explain but it all makes sense in the end. To top off a great gameplay experience there are some amazing cutscenes that will amaze you. As far as the controls, it takes a little getting used to, but its nothing too awkward to master. Most of the time in the game you will be accompanied by two partners, for the most part Goofy and Donald. As you visit new worlds you get the ability to swap a new partner in based on their abilities when they are needed. You can set what items your allies carry and even how they use those items.

Overall this is the best PS2 game I own. It took me forever to beat it but it really is a complicated game to get through. If you like to be challenged then this is a game for you. Any FF or Disney fan should appreciate what this game has to offer. And one last thing: I could see some people not really into this game, but to rate it one star you have to be an idiot or either 7 years old.

Mike Tyson's Punch-Out is the best boxing game ever created. Period. Sure, there are fun titles out now with gorgeous graphics (Fight Night), but the gameplay cannot be beat here. The controls are simple: you move side to side with the left and right buttons on the directional pad, duck with the down button, and A and B are for right and left jabs respectively (hold up with these to perform uppercuts).

The game consists of you, Little Mac, as you make your way through 3 divisions until you finally earn the right to face Tyson himself. The fighters in this game range from rediculously easy to very difficult to beat. But it is all about patterns. Once you learn the fighter's techniques, get your reflexes down, and beat them you are that much closer to fighting Mike Tyson. This is where it is almost rediculously hard, as he is no joke! It takes serious practice and concentration before you will be able to defeat him. Even Mr. Sandman and Macho Man before him are difficult for a while. Bottom line is, this is still one of the most difficult games to beat after more than 20 years. It is one of those must-own games for NES owners and I highly recommend it. It is one of the most fun games in my own collection.

Katamari Damacy is a hard game to describe to someone. All you can say is "You push a ball around and roll things up and make the ball bigger". This doesn't sound too appealing, but put the game in and you will more than likely be hooked instantly. With catchy music, many different types of levels to play in and different objectives for you to solve, this game just might be one of the PS2's finest.

Here is the basic premise of the game: you have to make big enough "Katamari" balls and when you do they become stars in the sky, since the stars were gone thanks to the king of the cosmos. The first level doesn't require too large of a ball at the end of the time limit, but it gets more difficult with each level. You may roll around in a house, in a park, or around the city. Additionally some levels will require you to roll up as many crabs as you can in order to create the constellation "Cancer". The bigger you make the ball, the bigger the objects you can roll up, like people and cows.

This really is a fun game and the best thing it has going for it is its simplicity. You only use the right and left analog sticks through each level, so you don't have to even think that much when you are playing. This is a game that all ages could enjoy. The music is very catchy, the graphics are pretty cool, and the camera angles are awesome. I am usually big on RPGs but this game is one I will keep in my collection. I give it 5 stars for being original and most of all for providing a fun gaming experience.

This is the first game in the Sly Cooper series, and even though it was released in 2002 I have just recently had the chance to play it. Better late than never, right? Anyhow, it is a great game all-around with not too much I can say about it that is negative. You are Sly Cooper, who comes from a long, proud line of professional thief raccoons. The basis of the game is this: the Thievious Raccoonus, which contains all of the secrets of the Cooper family, has been stolen. It has been split up among The Fiendish Five, all adversaries of the Cooper family. Sly, with the help of his friends Murry and Bentley, must defeat the Fiendish Five and reclaim the Thievious Raccoonus.

As someone who plays a lot of time-consuming RPGs, I found this game to be a great light-hearted alternative to the norm. The graphics (done in cel-shading) are absolutely gorgeous. The controls are excellent as well with fluid movement. As you progress through the game Sly will learn super sneaky moves to help him progress to the next area. Each area has a certain number of clues you can collect, which if you find them all will allow you to open safes which will increase the moves in Sly's arsenal. These aren't essential to beating the game but are fun to attempt anyway. I actually beat the game without finding them all (finished at 75% in about 6 hours).

About the only bad I could say about this game is that you will lose a life if you are hit once (unless you are holding a lucky charm) and this is aggravating at some areas in the game. The boss battles are a little too easy as well. That's okay though, this is a great game. Others have said the next two are even better but I have yet to play those. If you own a PS2, you will most likely find that this is a fun game, albeit a little on the short side. I really think it is a PS2 must-have, and I recommend that you play it.

Even if it DIDN'T work well, you can't go wrong for that price, but it worked perfect, and it was so cheap that the shipping cost more than the product. Highly recommended if you have a PS2 or a PS3 and want a better picture but can't use HDMI.

For the record, even though it's advertised as a Playstation 3 cable, I bought it for a PS2 and it works out of the box just fine. On the PS3, you'd get a better picture with HDMI, but if you don't have a flat panel display that supports it just go with this. You will NOT regret it.

This is the difference between a hard-to-see picture and one that's extremely high quality. I suggest buying from eForcity because they have by far the best price. It works perfectly, just as good as the official cable, and it's a hell of a lot cheaper. Really, if your TV supports it, you NEED this. You'll be amazed at the difference, even before you switch to progressive scan mode.

Please note some older CRT displays with component input don't support progressive scan, so they'll get a black picture if you use them with it, but you'll still get an excellent picture WITHOUT progressive scan. It's just not as good.

Better than the official N64 Rumble Pak. Why? Here's why: you plug this into your controller, you plug a memory pack into the TremorPak Plus's piggyback slot (it comes with a standard 1x/123 block card, but larger models are available that allow you to "page" between multiple virtual cards), you insert two AA batteries (NOT AAA like the official Rumble Pak, and who has AAA batteries around these days anyway?!) and boom you're done. You wanna save? Switch the little bottom switch to the left. You want rumble? Switch the little bottom switch to the right. No unplugging or replugging needed, which is so much more convenient than swapping Controller Pak and Rumble Pak. No hunting for AAA batteries when it's running low.

Oh, by the way, those AA batteries are more powerful, so it shakes a little harder than the official Rumble Pak, so Interact were sweet enough to include a Lo/Hi rumble effect switch. Switch it to low to get a more authentic Rumble Pak feel (and save some battery life while you're at it), or switch it to high and really, really feel the recoil from your gun or when you get hit.

And the best part? As far as rarity goes it's worthless, so you can get it for dirt cheap. The two I bought on amazon came sealed in the box for probably what I would have payed back in 2000 at GameStop. You'll probably spend at least twice this on a used official rumble pak.

The only two cons with this over the original OEM N64 Rumble Pak are that it's big and heavy, and perhaps a little unsightly compared to the seamlessly designed official unit.

But seriously, ****ing Turok 2 alone is enough to make this guy necessary: every time you save you gotta swap to the memory card, but the game features rumble. I'd much rather wear out the switch on this guy than the slot on my controller!

This controller isn't without its faults, but if you focus on games designed to take advantage of it the Steam Controller is the best controller money can buy right now. The haptic feedback makes the use of touch surfaces instead of a d-pad, joystick, etc a non issue, and the right touchpad is configured by default (including without any other software installed) as a trackball. Not a touchpad, a trackball, with momentum. You can "flick" it. And if you use Steam Big Picture mode to launch a game or program you can customize it to do nearly anything you'd want with a mouse and keyboard. Even text input on it is fantastic, as the controller simulates a thumb keyboard like you'd find on a phone or a chat pad for another controller.

This, however, leads us to the one fatal flaw with it: the controller is in "dumb" mode, pretty much solely emulating a mouse, unless Steam is running. And even then, unless you launched whatever app or game you're using through Steam's Big Picture mode your custom mappings aren't going to apply. However, it's not difficult to add custom shortcuts to Steam, and there are guides online to even give them big artwork for Big Picture, etc. That said, Steam is a little bloated, and Big Picture is even more bloated. It would certainly help to have a "lighter-weight" program you can use to program it. And you WILL have to customize the mappings, or at least pick a community preset, as well. Maybe both — some games have pretty poor presets. This isn't the end of the world because Big Picture lets you tap the Steam logo button and change mappings literally on the fly in the middle of a game, but it still doesn't run as fast as I'd like. Mac compatibility is also slightly lacking compared to Windows, though it has much better official Mac support than the Xbox 360 controller...

I'm giving this 4 stars because my N64 didn't always detect it at first, but that may have been a fluke as it seems to be working consistently now. I also am a little unhappy with the color — it's a slightly darker, greener gray than matches the rest of your N64 stuff, but chances are this is probably the memory card/controller pak you want for your N64. See, these things have batteries in them and they work just like the 256k SRAM in Game Boy games, albeit with a bigger battery due to larger space. What that means is that a 20 year old controller pak might not save anymore because its 20 year old battery is likely dead, whereas to the best of my knowledge these are brand new, with brand new batteries. In short, I'm not positive this is quite as reliable as a Nintendo brand Controller Pak was back in 1997, but I *am* positive it's more reliable than a 1997 Nintendo brand Controller Pak would be in 2016. And although the color doesn't match, if you have a dead Controller Pak and a "Gamebit" screwdriver it should be a cinch to swap the board.

This sensor bar isn't great. Really. You can't mount it to anything, it has a bright blue light when it's on, it turns off after a period of time (with no way to disable that "feature"), it eats batteries, and the only way to attach it to wall power involves modifications and still won't prevent it from turning off.

Don't buy this. If you need to power an old Sega Genesis/Mega Drive or a Super Nintendo buy something else. This adapter puts out 9v 350 mA. The Sega Genesis Model 1 that it is advertised to work with requires about 1000 mA (1A), and the SNES 850 mA, both at 10V (and they CAN tolerate 9V just fine), but this adapter can supply at most a third to half the required current, which means at best you'll have glitches in your games and at worst you'll damage your valuable game hardware.

The ONLY reason I didn't return this was because I had another power adapter that COULD supply enough current for a SNES and a soldering iron, and hacking the end off and soldering it to another adapter takes less time than waiting for shipping.

To be clear, DO NOT BUY THIS TRASH.

As I said the game play is not like KZ 2 & 3. I loved KZ 2 and loved KZ3 for multiplayer. But this one is just a golden garbage! Golden because it’s just beautiful and it has the best graphic I have ever seen. Garbage because it has the most frustrating gameplay that I have ever seen in my 20 years of gaming. I even broke my headphones due to this game; I throw it so hard to the wall… I don’t get angry at games, but this one is just crazy! You get killed over & over & over & …. Due to glitches and bad gameplay. Enemies can shoot you even if one pixel of your body is out of cover; AIs are accurate but dumb at the same time. They charge you when they shouldn’t, and they just stand there when you are charging them.
Most of the time, I did’t know where the hell I’m supposed to go or even what to do. You need to press the up button like 100 times in every chapter to show you the point that you need to go. How you get there is the mystery that you need to figure out.
The beginning of the game didn’t catch my attention at all. You start as a little kid, and just run around for almost 5-6 minutes; that’s how the game starts. No intense action or anything. At some point I just wanted to turn my PS4 off and never play the game.
Story: I really didn’t get it. But ending was surprising.
Graphic: I give it 10/10
Sound & music: 10/10
Controls: 4/10
Gameplay: 5/10
Over all, this game needs lots of time & patience. It’s a hard game, even when I played it on Normal difficulty. You can’t rush through the game at all. It’s not like KZ 2 & 3. I had more fun even with Killzone Mercenary on small ps-vita screen. Makers of this game focused so much on the graphics, they totally forgot about the fun factor and gameplay. ( watch Angry joe show on Utube, he explains everything for you about this game)
Multiplayer: I spent almost 4 hours on it. So far I like it. No ranking in this game; you unlock things by doing challenges. I heard they are going to release a co-op mod for the game soon. It is going to be fun.

I played both PS3 & PS4 version of TR. Also, played it on PC. I should say they couldn't have done it better. Graphic feels real and bright. Ps3 version was kinda dark and Lara's face didn't have much detail into it. But PS4 version is amazing. They have added all DLCs as well for free. So, that is like a huge discount for people who didn't play and pay for DLCs on PS3. However, multiplayer is still suffering from lag, but since it's 60 frames per second, it looks smoother.
One thing that I wish they add is CO-OP. Something like Uncharted 3 Arena or Gears Of War. If you haven't played the game on PS3, just get up and go to the closest store and buy it. If you never ever played Tomb Raider, I highly recommend it to you if you are a 3rd person action/adventure fan. Right now there aren't many great games on PS4, we all know what Battlefield 4 and COD Ghosts did to us, so take a little break from first person shooter games and enjoy the beautiful/ stunning next gen TR graphic. Oh, BTW the game supports voice commands. Like you say, show map, it shows you the map, or you say, switch to handgun, it switches to hand gun... It's really fun to impress your friends.

I got the game when it came out on October 29, 2013 on PS3. I had plenty of issues with this game just like other players. So, I was hopping PS4 version solves some of the issues. Time passed by and I finally decided to write a review about this game because I think EA/Dice had enough time to fix things.
Issue #1: Single player save games delete by itself. I was trying to get some dog tags for MP that can only be unlocked by playing SP and finding them around levels, but all my saves were gone.
Issue #2: Constant updates and game changes. I follow BF on twitter & Facebook, and pretty much every month there is something changing. Like added recoil to X gun, decrease damage to Y tank,... So, I really need to relearn things every time I play.
Issue #3: Playing with your clan or friends is a pain in the ass.
Issue #4: No customization allowed in the game menu. Only by joining a server or playing test range.
Issue#5: CRRRAAAZZZZYYY LAG. I never ever thought I would say this about BF. Sometimes the lag is so bad that you can't play at all. People jump around, rubber banding, and bad net code makes SOME games unplayable. Some servers are ok ( 4/10 games that I play are good)
Issue#6: This one is a personal opinion. I think BF community has changed and they are more COD players in BF than before. As a BF player since 2005 on PC, I can tell you team work is getting weak in BF4.
Issue #7: LAAAAGGG. It's so annoying that I have to mention it again. People join U.S servers from all over the world. Last night I was in a server with people from Germany, France, and Canada. No wonder the game lags...
Issue #8: Map design is not as strong as BF3. I literally loved all BF3 maps( from CQ maps to huge maps like Alborz mountain), but BF4 has a couple of really bad maps that I just quit when I end up in them.
Issue#9: Zero health kills. This happens a lot to me. I see an enemy, shoot him 12-15 bullets and I get some hit marks, he shoots like 2-3 bullets with an Assault rifle with no attachment and I'm DEAD. I look at his health and it shows ZERO. I know it's a glitch or net coding problem and he actually has 2-3 health left, but I'm damn sure he should have been killed.
Issue#10: Dog tags are ugly and shows nothing about your skills. In BF3 we had dog tags that showed amount of kills that you got by a particular gun or equipment. My favorite was MVP( most valued player which I got it like 370 times ). I was really good to show your skills in your dog tag, but it's all gone in BF4.

Of course there are many positive things in this game like graphic/ Guns/ Attachments/ Huge maps/ 64 players/dynamic maps...
This game needs updates & fixes. Net coding problem needs to be solved. Region lock MUST be in this game ( US players in US servers, Canadians in Canadian Servers ).
Anyway, I recommend this game if it's cheap. I would say wait a little longer till they fix more issues.
My Battle-log ID is streetracer475 in case you are wondering this review is written by a COD fan boy.

I'm not a huge RPG fan, I got the game just to take a break from COD,Battlefield, and KZ. To be honest, the first 5-6 hours of the game was fun, but after that it gets reallllyyyy boring and repetitive. You end up fighting like 5 enemies at the same time, but all you go to do is attack then block immediately after. I recommend this game if you have nothing to play & have lots of patience. Get the game when it's cheaper around 35$

The best racing game I have ever played, period. Finally, a game that allows to customize your car the way you like it to drive. Do you like a Honda civic? You want it to compete with a Ferrari? No problem, tune the car the right way and you get yourself a monster car. The details in this game are mind blowing. Graphic is just perfect. Cars' engine sound are perfectly designed. You can make the game as easy as you want OR as hard as you want; also, you get more points for making it harder. I love using manual + clutch transmission. If you are a racing fan, this game is a heaven for you. Imagine NFS carbon + Test Drive Unlimited 2
I LOVE THIS GAME... In fact, I purchased an Xbox one just for this game.

A little introduction first: I'm a huge FPS fan, and owned/played all Call Of Duty & battlefield & Halo & TitanFall .... many more FPS games. I spend 1-2 hours daily on gaming ( not a ranking/prestiging addict ). Now back to the game.

Single Player: I love the graphic and the story. Missions are actually fun not like the older CODs like ghosts which you only run around and go from A to B and kill this guy/ kill that guy, yahooo the mission is over. AW offers a gorgeous looking graphic and so much content in the SP itself, like upgrading your Exoskeleton and abilities. Therefore, I give it 10/10 for campaign

Voice acting/ music/ sound effects: It's amazing! I really liked the sound effects; different guns sound totally different. Voice acting perfectly matches the facial expressions and mood.10/10

Coop: Kinda disappointed!! Why? I expected to see a zombie/robot mixture as it was advertised on lots of websites. But all you get is a copy/past of MW3 survival/arena gameplay. You fight waves and waves of enemy while upgrading your guns and gears. However, the zombie would be a paid DLC, meaning you can buy it for 14.99$ or buy the season pass for 50$ to get all DLCs. Activation did what they always do( Destiny DLCs) now this. 6/10

Multiplayer: As a long time fan of COD, I see how they tried to bring something new to the table. Lets be honest here, we always complain about the fact that all CODs feel the same; therefore, here it is, a totally mutated version of COD. Is that what we wanted? Hell no, I never wanted something like this! The Exoskeleton and jumping up & down sounds good in theory but when you combine these abilities with COD community, you know the result won't be fun. There is a huge learning curve for this game(or may be no learning curve at all). I did whatever I could to make sense of this game and the new abilities, but all I come up with is that you randomly run around, jump from a rooftop to another, and randomly get kills or die ( that's how the game is). Lets say previous CODs needed 50% tactic and 50% luck and randomness, but AW feels like 90% luck and 10 tactic. It didn't take long for people to figure out how to play the game; it's simple, go on top of a roof and camp. That way you get 3-4 kills before someone kills you from behind. Or you can head glitch behind any of the windows that you like and get couple of kills before you die. Here are some of the issues that I find really annoying:

1- Lag is still a problem. I have a 25 D/ 5up direct connection, but I still have the same issue that I had with BOII( not ghosts). I empty half a clip ( GAL or AK12) on someone's body and they just jump and dash, but when they shoot me, I die very quick like in 4 bullets in the leg.

2- There are plenty of guns to use, with different varieties which you get them from random care package rewards, but people prefer to use GAL and AK-12 for some reason. I think they find them easier to use.

3- Maps are very small for Exo abilities. I can jump from rooftops and buildings to get to the other side of the map in a matter of seconds. I wish we had COD ghosts maps with exo abilities, it would make lot more sense.

Some positive aspects:

There are plenty of customization in this game, like character face or even shoes' color. It's really fun! Also, there are plenty of attachments( not as much as BF4) but more than Ghosts. You run out of ammo really fast, since you lose your ammo if you reload a clip while it has ammo left in it. On the other hand, most of the shooting happens at long distances, therefore, you need to fire more bullets. Obviously you can use scavenger to receive ammo from dead bodies.

My biggest problem!! I play COD for fun and competition. I always love killstreaks; it is the blood and juice of COD. But this game (pretty much like Ghosts) managed to kill this aspect of game for me. You have a set of KS just like previous CODs, but they are all useless; unless you upgrade them to a higher streak. Lets say you like sentry gun and you get it when you earn 400 points, but it's absolutely useless because you need to take control of it. Who enjoys stopping at a corner and controlling the sentry gun?? Now, you can add AI control ability but it's gonna cost you another 200 points, which the total is 600 points. You can get a goliath with that much point! Again, Killstreaks are pretty much under powered. It's also because half of the maps have buildings and covered spaces; therefore, a "laser from the sky can't kill more than 1-2 enemies"(referring to XS1 Vulcan)

Overall, I recommend this game if you are not a competitive player. Or just want to have fun for a while and not giving a a s*** bout getting killed from all angels over and over again. You really don't need any tactic for this game, just run and get couple of kills before getting killed by a camper on top of a roof. BTW, spawn system is still having problems, not entirely because of developers fault, but because people are everywhere and have the ability to get anywhere they want in matter of seconds.

I have played a couple of MMO RPGs on PS4 and PC, but I'm not a huge fan of this kind of games. However, as a long time gamer, I think I need to write a short review for gamers like me who would like to know how this game works. Well, approximate wait time till the review is 1 second...

That's the message I get every time I try to play the game. I connect to U.S north servers( which are located in Texas, and that's where I live), but I'm very angry at the fact that I have to wait till I can play the game. If you have a busy life, this can be a very negative aspect of the game; in fact I have my Ps4 logging in as I'm writing this review.

For those who say this is normal for MMO RPG, I like to bring up Final Fantasy 14( a realm reborn), I have played that game since its lunch on PS4 and never had an issue with logging in or disconnection. Just so you know, FF14 is a multiply platform game which PS3, PS4 and PC players, play together.

My 2nd problem with the game is that, there are so many people doing the same mission with me that it kills the experience. Imagine a simple skyrim side quest done by 10 people. Every time I'm doing a quest, there are at least 10 more people jumping ahead of me and trying to kill the enemies. All I do is just run to the objective and get what I need and finish the quest. However, this is the norm in MMO RPG, but for some reason this game makes me feel like I achieved nothing when other players do the quest for me. Speaking of quests, they are really basic. Most of them are like go to this area and kill this enemy and bring X item for reward. If you are looking for impressive quests like skyrim or oblivion, this game doesn't offer that.

The graphics are ok for MMORPG game, and voice overs are done nicely. Music and soundtracks are perfect. Looting system is very rewarding and fun. Character creation and classes are simply stunning and perfect. There are some lags here and there, when there are more than 10 people running around, I see the screen freezes for 1-2 seconds, which is not a big deal.

Sorry if I sound like a noob, but these are the things that annoyed me over my 11 hours of game play. I could spend more time on this game, but the wait time message is just killing the mood. In my opinion, get the game 2-3 months from now, maybe the price will drop to $30 soon. Also, as some of the reviews on PC pointed out on youtube( Angry Joe Show), the game offers many micro transactions. If you don't feel like grinding for golds simply pay $39.99 for 5500 crowns so you can get a horse(14000 gold) for 1000 crowns or just buy the imperial edition( that's what I did) which comes with a horse, or just walk for hours and hours. As you may have noticed, I didn't point out lunch day logging problems because I understand it's a normal thing to happen, but the wait time is just driving me crazy; every time I tried to play since last night I got this message. I'm done with the short review, but my screen still shows " approximate wait time is 1 second "

UPDATE: June 14 2015
After an update, I had no issue with loging in to the game. One more star added to my review. 4.5/5
Quests get interesting after level 11.

As the screenshots show, I finished the game in almost 12 hours. I have been a big fan of NFS and any racing game since I was 8 years old. So, this review is going to be my opinion based on what I expected from this game after all these years.
Over all the game is just boring and simplified to the point that you just need to hit the break button to drift in any car. Hopefully the following list helps you decide if you want to spend $60 on this game or not:

Graphics: It's very satisfying ! However, the game has a grayish filter that kinda bothered me when I was playing. The lights are very amplified in this game, and when you are going 170mph in highway, the lights constantly flicker in your face. The cinematic parts look pretty cool as well.

Gameplay: It is SUPER cheesy and simplified. Even NFS Rivals required more skill and had a better overall feeling to it. The controllers are very straight forward and there is no way to change them. There is no manual transmission. The game needs to be online all the time. But don't expect intense online races, simply because it doesn't exist. There is no lobby for racers to get into in order to choose a race or activity. It's a free roam game style with little to no player-player interaction.

Car handling and tuning: The customization and tuning looks very cool and reminds me of NFS carbon/underground. However, all cars handle the same PERIOD. All you need to do is to go with either drift or grip set up and the car will take care of everything else. I drove BMW, lambo, Ferrari, Nissan GTR and all of them handle the same way. Just press the brake button and you are drifting in no time.
Installing elite and high end parts on your Toyota Supra can make it as good and even better than a lambo which is very cool and awesome.

Soundtrack / sounds: Soundtrack are very bad ! Thanks to Ps4 ability to play spotify in the background, I was glad to turn the music all the way down. But engine sounds are awesome and very real.

AI: The stupidest AI system ever. Cops are just jocks in this game. They are camping around the city just to follow you for 3 seconds and then lose you. Sometimes they smash to buildings and other cars and stop. They can't catch up with you if you are going over 120mph. I had to slow down and beg them not to lose me so I could finish my Outlaw missions. Other races are very aggressive and they just ram you in to walls and rear end you.

City and over all feeling: the city feels death and boring ! It is raining most of the time and the day/night cycle is just a jock. Sometimes the sky soddenly turn blue and you see a bright sun rising and after 5 minutes, it suddenly turns dark. It's like the earth flips into a day light and then to night time. lol

Car selection: It's pretty good. You can see the list in their website, but over all I'm satisfied with the list. BUT, you can only have 5 cars in your garage. VERY STUPID !!! I ended up selling my Ferrari just to buy a lambo. So, you have to sell your cars to empty spots in your garage.

Over all the game feels like NFS Most wanted( not the original, the 2012 version) + NFS rivals.
I have hard time recommending this game to racing fans. Pick it up when it is $30. Unfortunately I bought it on Psnetwork; and yes I was that excited to play the game the minute it comes out, but it was another disappointment for me.
