As a 70 year old gamer, whose 8 year old nephew got me started by showing me how to get 99 lives on Mario, back in the Nintendo days, I have since, played most old school RPGs. I was a retailer for PS2 back in the 90's. I have always said that Final Fantasy VII, was the greatest old school RPG ever made. Us old school gamers, are more or less set in our ways, and of late, there is little to play in the way of old school RPGs. They have all turned into mindless button mashing hack N slashes. So, let me say, that after 30 odd years of RPGing, THE LEGEND OF HEROES: TRAILS OF COLD STEEL, is the greatest RPG ever I have ever played.

I made the mistake of playing through the Unchartered Series, before starting Rise Of The Tomb Raider. In comparison, I found ROTTR to be boring, clumsy and redundant. I think Nathan Drake did more for this type of gameplay, than Lara Croft ever could. The Unchartered Series, is Tomb Raider, done right!

I waited till I could buy FFXV for $20, because I knew I would dislike it. And I did! The Franchise has gone downhill since FFX, the last great FF game. FFXV is plagued by an incomprehensible story line, characters you do not give a crap about, mindless button mashing and another boring combat system, and camera problems. It is too bad developers these days, think all RPGs should be fast, over the top, real time action oriented. LEGEND OF HEROES / TRAIL OF THE COLD STEEL VOL 1 & 2, has proved that wrong. There still is a place for turn-based RPGs, with characters you care about, and a solid story line. (Vol. 3 is on the way)
If this over the top, action oriented path, is the route FFVII REMAKE is going to follow, then count me out! I have played the FF Series since it's inception, and FFVII has always held a special place in my heart, until LEGEND OF HEROES came along.
I believe there still is a solid market place for turn-based RPGs, with characters you care about, and an engrossing story line. Please give the LEGEND OF HEROES a try. It is what an RPG is supposed to deliver.
The old developers at SQUARE-ENIX are gone. And so is the anticipation of a forth-coming FF game.
Now, we await each new installment, with dread.

I recently revisited this game, and it is one of the most perfect, old school turn-based RPGs you can experience. I have played them all, and this ranks highly with me. Originally released in 2005, it is one beautifully thought out game. From Square-Enix & Level 5. An enchanting story line. Challenging bosses to keep you on your toes. Hundreds of items to find, scattered across the vast world. Two casinos, where you can spend days, trying to hit the jackpot, for those rare items. An arena to test your mettle with creatures you have collected. A few thought provoking puzzles and mazes. And wonderful cel shaded art work, which still holds up very nicely on your big screen TV. (I finished the game recently in 105 hours at level 40. And, There is a new game +, which opens up a new, exceedingly difficult area!)
I know there is still a market for turn-based RPGs, and hope there will be more in the future.
The Dragon Warrior / Dragon Quest Series, has now turned into Dragon Quest Heros, another mindless Hack N Slash Fiasco.
But, if you want to relive The Golden Age of RPGs, start here. (In Mid March 2018, a remake of Nintendo's SECRET OF MANA! will be available for download on the PS4! That, will be an event!)

I hope this turned-based entry sells a bunch, and shows Square-Enix, that there still is a market for this type of RPG. Dragon Quest VIII, for the PS2, was one of my all time favorite games. With so many classic RPG Franchises, turning into mindless Hack N Slash, Dragon Quest XI, will truly be a breath of fresh air. Square-Enix developers of the troubled FFVII Remake, should take note. 9/8 - 30 hours in. Fabulous animations. Not one glitch yet. Interesting story line. Fun combat system. Can even put it on automatic, if you wish. If you grind enough, it is a bit on the easy side, but so much fun! Spent a day at The Casino and won 300,000 tokens! Got some bad-ass weapons! So much to explore. I am so happy Square-Enix did not screw up this franchise. Turn-based combat lives!
9/15 - 107 hours. A Bona Fide Masterpiece! Onto New Game+! More Quests, a whole new variety of tougher creatures, many side quests and challenges. The Ultimate Key!

As a huge fan of the first RDR, I certainly was looking forward to this. I received it from Amazon day of release. First, you have to load a Data Disc, and then more loading with the Play Disc. It took about an hour and a half. First thing I noticed, was there is no difficulty setting. So, I figured I would die a lot. The first couple missions are linear, so it gives you time to learn the numerous controls that you will be utilizing. The detail and scenery are pretty awesome. You finally get to do your own thing, once you get near the town of Valentine in Chapter 2. I managed to kill my horse, which left me on foot for quite a spell! After that, I decided to start the game over, now that I was familiar with the complex controls. Looking forward to exploring more, as the game progresses. Worth playing, but I still have a soft spot for the 1st game so far. 11/6 - After 2 weeks with this game, I am finding it laborious, slow & no incentive to keep playing it. You wander into a mission that triggers automatically, and you cannot leave it, or it ends with Mission Failed. The 1st RDR was so much better designed. I will keep on trying to play & enjoy this game, but the cumbersome controls, the overwhelming vastness of it, and the slow pace, urges me to play Dragon Quest XI for the thrid time instead...

For decades, FFVII was tops on my list, until Trails Of Cold Steel Series came about. For those of you that long for an in depth story line, countless characters who are all fleshed out through endless text and spoken word, and a turn based combat system that is fun, The Trails Of Cold Steel Series is for you!
It is not imperative that you play 1 & 2, but I would strongly recommend it, to familiarize yourself with re-ocurring characters, and the vast world of Erebonia. One would think this was based on an anime series.
Complex dungeons, fetch quests, 3x grinding speed available. And no bugs or freezes!
The translation for such an important series, is done so well, you would be hard pressed to think this is a JRPG.
If you are looking for an RPG, whose main goal is, the ability to get to know a multitude of characters intimately, and a story line full of twists and turns, look no further.
This is the best turn-based RPG series in decades.

Final Fantasy X was towards the end of Square-Enix great run of games. I will include Final Fantasy XII, as being the last great Final Fantasy Game.
From great fantasy turn-based battles & story lines, to 4 dudes in a car you did not give a crap about, to mindless Hack N Slash and the ruining of the Final Fantasy VII Remake, Square has lost it's touch with RPGs.
Stick with this remaster, the XII remaster, and FFIX Remaster on The Switch.
For it is the end of RPGs, as we have known it.

I just finished this game a moment ago, and boy, all I can say is booooooooring. What was with that ending? Hyrule Castle and final fight. Too short and rushed. Like the latter half of the game as a whole.
The ending of Wind Waker was LEGENDARY! I yawned once I finished Twilight Princess.

Listen, this game had a wonderfull beginning. I liked the cutscenes and the first time I transformed into a wolf I was in awe. But then I hated how weak and rushed the plot became. Why the hell did those orcs just drop the kids somewhere? And around the time Ilia got her memory back the plot fizzled completely. Also the plot in this game was too little about Triforce, history, the world/land of Hyrule etc. They were touched really superficially.
The plot and dialogue were *extremely inferior* compared to Wind Waker.
Twilight Princess was boring, choppy and jumpy after a great beginning.

And the dungeons. Something was severely lacking. In the beginning they were ok, though nothing great, but then they got horrible. Like the City in the Sky and Twilight Realm. Horrible.
I guess they went for quantity not quality. The dungeons were boring and repetitive, the puzzles old and they lacked any atmosphere.
Also if I remember correctly in Wind Waker you had to use many of the items you had acquired in different places. Not here.

This game was also *WAY too easy*. I'm not a good player, honestly, but I never once died during the game. As a matter of fact I was near perfect health nearly all the time. Once you got the Master Sword you just needed to swing the nunchuk and the enemies would vanish. I mean I'd want standard enemies that would be at least as tough as Ganon was in the final swordfight.
The bosses were also very easy and somehow lamer than in Wind Waker.

I liked the Wii controls and they were well planned and easy to use. But I have one complaint. Circling behind an enemy's back really didn't work that well. First you had to sidestep and then roll. But guess what, most of the time the roll (+sidestep) brought you around the enemy to where you started. It was irritating (though not by any means impossible) to hit the enemies in the back.

Oh, and why did most of the characters have to look so retarded? They showed with some models that they could make neat looking ones as well...

Riding on the horse was the greatest part of this game!
You should really buy Wind Waker instead of this. People complain about the graphics but they're quite nice once you get used to them. And did I mention that the dialogue and plot are awesome. The Triforce Hunt is the only annoying and tedious part of that game. TP felt the same all the time after the beginning. Just scores of poorly designed dungeons and a choppy and weak plot.

Lezard makes this game. That is the best voice-acting I remember hearing in a game ever. I love his voice. And it just gets better near the end. Most of the other voices are decent to good as well.

The story and dialogue are nice, using elements from Norse mythology.
There are many interesting cutscenes, but unfortunately the characters' movements and expressions in them look unnatural.

In fact, compared to the lovely looking environments, the character models are rather horrible. And it's a bit silly how they made Rufus look like captain Jack Sparrow and Lezard like evil Harry Potter.

Some people might complain about the 2D-scrolling, but it doesn't bother me. In dungeons enemies appear on screen (no random battles) and the ability to turn them into crystals to use as platforms is interesting. It's a nice change of pace trying to figure how to reach treasure chests using those platforms and the teleportative ability.

The battle system is a refreshing deviation from the standard. I much rather have the option of walking around the field and mash buttons, watching different kinds of attacks, until my hands/wrists literally hurt, than have my characters stand in a stupid row and repeatedly choose the attack command watching the characters perform that boring same slash through the game. That's been done since NES.

I don't know if I'd give this game 5 stars unless I laughed at Lezard all the time. But it's a really good game and quite original. And it doesn't fizzle in the end like so many other RPGs (it actually gets better I think).

Wiiak, very weak.
The Nintendo Wii console has approximately the same stats as the 10-year-old X-Box system. And still it carries the same price tag as the next gen consoles.

The graphics look very gamecubish and sometimes plain atrocious (Red Steel, anyone?). You can't access pages with more than a dozen pictures with the Internet Browser or the system crashes due to lack of memory and computing capability. It lacks HD support or DVD playback option.

None of that would really matter, as we all know it's the games that make the console. But not surprisingly all they offer are just rehashes of games published in the late 80s or mid 90s. All the innovativeness is long gone, buried in the dark past.

The Wii is controlled via a motion sensing system, which you'll find appealing if you're a toddler. The revolution of gaming? Come on people. Give us virtual reality.

You can buy old "classics" through the internet at prices even the mafia daren't ask. If they'd at least put Amiga games available...

Yes, this console might be fun to play with family or friends, but true gamers have neither. This is the revolution of non-gaming. If you want to buy an actual console, I suggest buying X-Box 360 or PS3 instead.

This installment of Final Fantasy is definitely story driven. Sadly, however, the story is weak. Six months after playing the game, I can't even remember what those triangular spirits were about. Thank goodness for the nice dialogue. Without it the game would be untolerable. Character interaction is minimal, and there is no real team spirit.
The main character Vaan and his friend Penelo seem to be nothing more than luggage. There's no point in them being in the game. I can't say that's a good thing.
The evil guys and side characters are lame and their doings seem pointless. As with the main characters, none are truly explored.
Talking with the townspeople is utterly pointless.

The graphics are nice, though nothing mind-blowing. I didn't want to stop to view the scenery at any point. I have to applaud them for making the cities even a bit lively looking, by adding a lot of silent characters. One point of complaint is the very lame spell effects.
The CGI scenes are nothing spectacular, definitely a step back from FFX. This was the first installment in the series where I wasn't looking forward to seeing the CGI scenes.

The voice-acting is good, all the main characters give solid performances. *But* the Marquis and Al-Cid almost succeed in spoiling my respect towards the other performances. Thank goodness they have so few lines. All in all the voice acting is one of the best aspects of the game.

The real-time battle system is a radical change from past games. It's nice but doesn't make the battles less tedious or repetitive in the long run. The enemies are also mostly boring.
The party AI doesn't really shine, but thank goodness you can limit its stupidity with the Gambit System. Too bad that lots of the useful gambits appear only at the later stages of the game.

The license board works for someone who likes perfect customization, but unfortunately I don't. I want characters who truly differ in their abilities. And talking about abilities, I found all the skills and most of the power ups really lame and useless.
The summons, called Espers, are stupid-looking and useless in combat.

The maps are at times annoyingly large. The fact that there are no secrets or secret places, and the randomized treasure, add to the insult. Many times the game devolved into a multiple hour running through empty fields, between short cutscenes.

The music is bad. Nobue Uematsu left them and they replaced him with some clueless punk. There is zero memorability and some themes are just annoying. It's the worst I've heard in any RPG I've played.

CLOSING COMMENTS:
When I started playing, I was positively surprised by the good voice-acting, the nice - and at times witty - dialogue and olden style of speaking used by some characters.
However it didn't take long to become annoyed by the pointless main character Vaan, the trite and stupid plot, lack of character interaction, huge and empty fields/dungeons with random and often useless treasure.
All in all this game is about running hours and hours through fields, fighting repetitive enemies, so you could see a 5 minute stupid cut scene that advances the inane plot.

Many associate the Mario games with fun. I associate the name Mario for one mediocre platformer from the 80s/90s and a load of marketing hype and crazed fanboys.
There's no real story, the weak and uninteresting main character has no personality, the platforming has been done better before, all the "innovations" - most of them eon-old rehashes - feel forced, no sense of completion can be gained and the "fun" the game radiates seems false.
I suggest playing Spyro the Dragon for PS1 instead.

My review of Odin Sphere Leifthrasir for the PS4 & Vita

Pro

Art style - One of things that really stands out in Odin Sphere Leifthrasir is it beautiful art style. I really like the hand drawing animation by George Kamitani. It was a really good looking game when it came out back in 2007 for the PlayStation 2 and while that game still hold up today. This remaster is even better thanks to the fact that the game (the PS4 version) runs at 1080p at 60fps. The Vita version isn,t that bad either.

Story - I really like how they use Norse Mythology as inspiration for the 5 main characters (Gwendolyn, Cornelius, Mercedes, Oswald, and Velvet). Each of the character story are well told and are connected to each others. So for example (minor spoiler for those haven’t gotten far or haven’t played Odin Sphere before) when you play Gwendolyn story there a scene when someone inform her that King Odin was defeated in the latest battle. In Mercedes story you see how King Odin was defeated.

Gameplay - One thing I like about Odin Sphere Leifthrasir is the improve gameplay. First off the level design not only look better but have a Muramasa Demon Blade (or Rebirth for the Vita) feel to it (In which that game had a Metroidvania feel to it). Combat has been improve as well and has a bit of a Dragon’s Crown feel to it (another great game from Vanillaware) along with new stages and enemies and finally if you really want to go old-school you can play the original PS2 game (which is under classic mode). Also the alchemy system has improve as well (In my time with it while you can easily get recipes for your alchemy. You can easily do it on your own even if you don’t have the recipes the game will still show you what the result of your alchemy).

Cons

confusing leveling up (for newcomers that is) - one thing that might be confusing for some people is the leveling up system. You see in Odin Sphere Leifthrasir while you can leveling up by attacking your enemies the quickest way to leveling up is by eating food. There are many ways to get food. You can buy (or find in the battlefield) seeds that you plant in the ground and grow them with Phozons (which are collected by defeating enemies or by making them with alchemy) or by going to a restaurant (some restaurant required you to find or buy recipes and have the right food items to make certain dishes while others you just pay with the in-game currency). For some this may come off as being a bit confusing if you are used to the traditional way of leveling up in RPG games (action, adventure, or traditional). It took me a while when I played the original back in 2007 but after a while (for me) everything click.

Overall - Odin Sphere Leifthrasir is a game I would recommend for those who are big on 2-D games (like me). I do hope the game does well in sells because not only would I be open to seeing PS4 ports of GrimGrimoire, Muramasa: The Demon Blade (or Rebirth on the PS Vita) and Dragon's Crown (which is also on the PS Vita) but I do hope we get to see there next game come over here as well. I believe its called 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim.

My review of Mighty Number 9 for the WIIU

Pro.

Fun and challenging gameplay - Base on my time with the game I will say if there one area Mighty Number 9 gets right its it gameplay. The game follow a similar root that the classics Mega Man games did but with a twist this time. Instead of defeating them by just shooting them (you can do that to certain enemies). You shoot them until they change color and depend on the color (blue give you points for your score and grade at the end of each level, yellow give beck a temporary shield, green makes beck move quicker for a bit and finally red increases fire power for a bit) and then dash into them. It can help you a bit in some of the levels (which depending on your view can be difficult). The boss battle (for me though) are both challenging but fun at the same time. Not only do you have to memorize there pattern but you got to wear them down by shooting at them until they turn purple. Then you got to dash into them but be quick because if you take too long they will regain lost health.

Good Contents - Mighty Number 9 definitely has some cool content that help the game replayability. Beside the 12 stages in the game you also have stuff like new game+ (for those who want a bit more challenging experience), challenge mode for those who want to test out there platforming skills, boss rush mode to see how quickly you can defeat them and of course 2 player online co-op which can be played in either online race battle (in which you go head to head as you race though the stage) or the 2 player online co-op challenge mode where beck & call work together to complete these challenges.

Cons.

Not great graphics - Unfortunately when it comes to the visuals of the game it doesn’t look that good. In fact it (to a certain degree) looks like I’m looking at a early PS2 games and for the record there are plenty of PS2 games that look better then this. Hell there are 3DS and Vita games that look way better then this.

Framerate Issues - Although not as bad as say assassins creed unity was (that not saying much) it still not that good. To me the game feel like its have a hard time and why it doesn’t make the game unplayable (at least with my time with it) it still feel like this game lack polish.

One use for the Gamepad (WIIU version) - Anyone going into and thinking the the WIIU version of Mighty Number 9 is going to take advantage of the WIIU gamepad well prepared to be disappointed. Outside of off-tv mode (which is still a cool feature the WIIU has) that it. The Gamepad doesn’t enhance or bring in anything new to the WIIU version of Mighty Number 9 (weather you think that good or bad that your call).

Difficulty Spike - As a gamer who grew up playing these games (I was born in the 80’s) the difficulty spike isn’t as big of an issue for me (I’m aware the game can be a bit frustrated). That said for those who are new to these type of games that a different story because you will be dying a lot in this game. This is a game that require you to time your jumps well and memorize enemies patterns and for some that might be difficult (one bright spot out of this is that you can go to the option menu and change from having 2 lives to having 9 lives).

Overall - Mighty Number 9 isn’t bay all means a bad game but a disappointing game. While the gameplay is certainly fun and the game has a good amount of content. The graphics, framerate, difficulty spike (for some people) combine with the reputation the game has garish (the multiple delays, the game not looking as good as the concept art, the red ash debacle, pushing for a movie, anime, toys line and amiibo and not focusing on the game and last but not least the god awful launch trailer) I feel this will not only hurt the developer who made this (I can’t see them doing another Kickstart after this) but I also believe it will more then likely kill off any chance the series has. Which is really a shame because there was so much potential this game (and series) could have had.

My review of Tokyo Mirage Sessions for the WIIU

Pros

Beautiful Graphics - While I won’t go as far as saying that (on the visual side that is) it blows Xenoblade Chronicles X visual out of the water. Tokyo Mirage Sessions is still a good looking game for the WIIU. I definitely like the anime look to it and I certainly would put it next to other good looking games on the WIIU like: Super Mario 3D World, The Wonderful 101, Bayonetta 2, Rayman Legend, Xenoblade Chronicles X and so on.

Fun Battle System - Even though this is my first time playing an RPG made by Altus (I never played a Shin Megami Tense, Devil Survivor or a Persona game before. Sound crazy but it’s true) I will say I am enjoying the combat. Basically the game is a turn-based RPG (in which you have your usually stuff like attack, spells, guard and items) but I’m also liking the whole session attack combination (in which you and another party member can chain attack base on the enemy’s weakness. For example if and enemy is weak against ice and one party member attack with and ice attack and an other member of your party has a ice attack as well then they will follow up with an attack as well).

Gamepad use - While the Gamepad won’t change the way you play JRPG it doesn’t do anything that make it hard (or unplayable) to play like Star Fox Zero did. Basically the Gamepad does two things. The first one is the in-game app called Topic. Here you’ll receive messages from other characters to receiving update on when you can upgrade your Carnage & Radiant Unity (Carnage Unity uses Performa which can be obtain by defeating enemies and by performing crowd-pleasing techniques such as Session Attacks. These are use to upgrade your weapons. Radiant Unity uses Performa as well but can only be obtain by going through parts of the main story, completing sides stories aka side quests or by increasing there star ranking by going into battle. These give you permanent skills like increased health or extended a session attack and so on). The second part is that the Gamepad also display the map so it comes in handy where you need to go (Sadly it doesn’t support off-tv play).

Difficulty & Save (mostly) everywhere - One thing I do like is the fact that you can save your game pretty much everywhere. You don’t need to go (or find) a save point. All you need to do is push the Y button (I believe that the one but i could be wrong) and to system and select save and that it. Plain and simple. As for the difficultly although you can play the game on easy you can also play it on normal or hard so don’t worry. This game isn’t being dumb down for casuals so if for some reason your a die hard fan of Altus RPG you can still play it like the other Altus RPG.

Cons

Ok Story - While I won’t go as far as saying that the story is terrible (it isn’t for the record) it just doesn’t click with me. Mostly because I’m not that big into the whole J-pop/idol thing. Which is pretty much what the whole game evolves around and if your not that into the whole J-pop/idol thing then this game isn’t for you

Ok dungeons - While the enemies in the dungeons are fun (and can be challenging) to fight. The dungeons themselves are so so. The puzzles in the dungeons (at least the ones that I’ve gone to) comes off as being a bit too easy and while they don’t look terrible when compare to the dungeons in the Zelda series. I have to say there not that impressive (at least that how I look at them).

Not a Fire Emblem game - If you were going into Tokyo Mirage Sessions expecting it to play similar to the Fire Emblem games then prepare to be a bit disappointed. While the game borrows some elements from the Fire Emblems series (characters, leveling up, the whole rock, paper, scissors battle) for the most part this is still a Altus RPG and its more gear towards those kind of gamers. Again that not a bad thing (it’s still a good game) just don’t go in expecting it to play exactly like Fire Emblem.

Overall - Since I never played a Altus RPG (Persona, Devil Survivor Shin Megami Tense) before. I can’t really compare it to other Altus RPG. That said I will say I did enjoy the game (I’m aware of the whole localization controversy but to me I’m not losing sleep over it). The combat is fun (i’m not a huge fan of turn-base RPG but I don’t hate them either. There are good ones out there). The graphics are good and the the gamepad was used properly and doesn’t make you feel like your banging your head into the wall (like Star Fox Zero did). Being this is a niche title I don’t see this pushing (although I could be wrong) a lot of WIIU out there(it obviously clear the WIIU is on its last leg).

My review of Kingdom HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue for the PS4

Pro

2 games and a movie (X back cover) in one disk. Not bad

Cons

X Back Cover movie is good but I felt that you only need to watch it once and there no reasons to watch it again

Overall - Kingdom Hearts HD 2.0 Final Chapter Prologue is still a fun games. It may not have as much content as the remake of Kingdom Heats 1&2 did on the PS3 (which is also being remade for the PS4) but to me its still an enjoyable game nevertheless.

My Review of Yakuza 0 for the PS4

Pro

Bizarre but interesting story - (has its serious moment but also has its funny moment as well)
Fun gameplay mechanics - (you can choose from 3 different style. My favorite is Brawler for Kiryu)
Enjoyable side actives like: Bowling (outside of videogames this is another hobby of mine),Karaoke (not 100% good at it), Darts, Talking to girls on the phone (Yes this is a things). Plus fun side quest ranging from beating up a thief who stole a popular video game from a child to helping a sushi chief by going fishing to convincing someone to stop selling there underwear to stranger (Yes for some reason that also a things)

Con

So so visuals - While the game looks nice don’t expected to push the PS4 hardware. This is mostly do to the fact this was a port of a PS3 release in Japan
Outdated combat system - While the combat in Yakuza 0 is fun and satisfying (nothing more thrilling then seen Kiyu grab a bad guy and either slam him into a wall or repeatedly punch him in the face) it also feel dated when to say games like Mad Max, Middle Earth: Shadow of Mordor and the Arkham series.
Japanese Culture (unless your familiar with it) - Unless your a longtime fan of the series (or happen to be into the odd stuff that come from Japan) then this games might be a hard sell to recommend to someone (being that this is a niche game after all).

Overall - As odd as Yakuza 0 is I still enjoyed the games. Its story (which can be both serious and silly), its fun side story & actives and its fun combat has keep me hook to it.

My review of Resident Evil 7 for the PS4 (also on Xboxone & PC)

Pro

A return to horror - After been absent from 5 & 6 we finally get a Resident Evil game that returns to horrors elements (conserving your ammo, solving puzzles and a Resident Evil game with a scary atmosphere).
The Baker Family - Not side the Ganados from Resident Evil 4 that I have fought an enemy that are both creepy and fun ( to some degree the baker family kinda give of give off that Nemesis vibe and for those who don’t know who Nemesis was he was the main villain for Resident Evil 3)
FPS perspective - I definitely like that Capcom decide to go with a first person view (with traditional first person controls although you can change it in the option menu). It also makes head shot a little bit easier.

Cons

Item Chest - One area that don’t like that they brought back was the item chest. I never was a fan of having to backtrack so many times to a save point just to get that one item you need (I felt 4 did it right. Although you can find backpack in 7 to increase how many item you can carry with you)
Lack of enemies - Other then the Molded (which are cool enemies by the way along with a a fly like enemy) I am a little bit disappointed over the lack of enemies in Resident Evil 7. I wish there were more (would have been nice to see the lickers, Hunters, Zombie Dogs and other creatures from past Resident Evil games make a comeback).

Overall - Resident Evil 7 is a game that I enjoyed but at the same time feel divided about. On one hand it returns the series back to its horrors after what happen with 5 & 6 (which isn’t a bad thing though). on the other hand I don’t like it that stay too close to the past Resident Evil games (I really hate the item chest) where 4 was a step in the right direction (not 5 & 6). While 4 will always be the best Resident Evil game out there (that my take) I’m will to call Resident Evil 7 the second best Resident Evil game out there.

My review of Poochy & Yoshi’s Woolly World for the Nintendo 3DS

Pro

Colorful visuals (surprise that they were able to pull it off on the 3DS)
Solid gameplay mechanics (using pretty much the same mechanics that has been use in pretty much every Yoshi game since 1995)
Good amiibo support (unlike like some games like Splatoon that gated out certain weapon that can’t be access unless you had a Splatoon amiibo)
Some new stuff like the theater (where you can watch short Poochy & Yoshi movie), Poochy pups that can help you find selects in a level and some new stages that are design for Poochy.

Cons

Good but not great visuals - While I’m impress Nintendo was able to pull it off. It still doesn’t look as good as the WIIU version
Very easy for some - While the game can be challenging if you are planning to find everything its not if you just want to breeze through. If you take away the secrets in the game it comes off as being way too easy for some.
No 2 player co-op - Unlike the WIIU version there is no 2 player mode
Very little new content & Amiibo support - Outside of the movies and Poochy levels there isn’t really a whole lot of new things in the game. Plus amiibo support is limited to just skins

Overall -Poochy & Yoshi Woolly World isn’t going to top the original 1995 Super Mario World 2 Yoshi Island and all this is is a port of the WIIU version. That said though its still a fun game nevertheless (following the tired and true formula that have been used in past Yoshi games) and if you enjoyed the past Yoshi games (or never played the WIIU version) then give this one a go

My review of Nioh for the PS4

Pro

Fun Gameplay -Really like that then went with a Dark Souls route with this game its both challenging and fun
Graphical Option - For Nioh you have the option to play the game in either cinematic (movie) mode (which make the visuals look good) or action mode (that make the game have a steady frame rate at 60FPS). Personally I went with action mode because while the visuals look nice I would rather have a steady frame rate (60FPS) over enhance graphics (but then again that my take).
Good Story - One thing about the story in Nioh that I like is that it give off an Onimusha vibe to it

Cons

Dark Souls Difficulty - If for some reasons your not a fan of the Dark Souls games (or Bloodborne for that matter) then this isn’t the game for you. These games are know for there difficulty and that might turn off some people
Graphical Options (The Negative Part) - While its nice that we have the option to play Nioh in either cinematic (movie) mode or action mode I am a bit disappointed that you have to chooses between those two (there a third option called movie mode/variable fame rate) and that there isn’t a 1080p/60fps option (Note: this criticism is base on my time with Nioh on a standard PS4. I don’t have a PS4 Pro)

Overall - Nioh is definitely one of my favorite so far for the PS4. Its challenging gameplay (which can be brutal), its story (which as I wrote early give off that Onimusha vibe which is a good this. Not to mention Capcom needs to do another Onimusha game) and and its visuals (which for the record it still looks good even in action mode) keeps me coming back for more. Dark Souls fans will more then likely enjoy this one.

As I write this review I am debating whether or not to finish laundry or go back to play more of this game.  I haven't made it too far in the story because of my play style in that I enjoy exploring new areas versus heading straight into the objectives.  That is what makes this game so great, it adapts to how YOU want to play.  As with previous games in the series, Fallout 4 is centered around survival in  radiation infested wasteland.  This one is set in/around Boston and Bethesda has done a fantastic job of recreating that immersive feeling here.  What exactly makes it so adaptable are the numerous activities or mini quests you can begin.  You can build various settlements, farm crops for food, create custom power armor, cook your own food, and customize weapons/armor.  Virtualy every item you can pick up breaks down into it's base materials much like in the real world so you can scavenge for exactly what you need.  Sure the game has it's minor bugs, but the developer is continuously improving the game and it runs/plays very smooth in it's current state.  New features such as free mods even on consoles set this apart from the rest.  Also, the planned DLC is very intrigueing and the first one called Automatron looks impressive!  You will not regret picking this game up.

This is a great wireless headset for the Xbox One with a few minor quirks.  I have owned it for about 2 months now so I can provide an honest review.  First the pros:  Very lightweight, crystal clear sound, audio presets work well, excellent battery life, and the microphone is very good quality according to my friends/other players online.  As for the cons: The fit a little snug even after a couple months of use.  It has loosened up a bit but still a little fatiguing for long gaming sessions.  One thing that did help to make it more tolerable was replacing the earpads with Brainwavez HM5 memory foam earpads.  Another reviewer had recommended these and I would as well, so much better as the included ones cause my ears to sweat badly.  They run about 20$ and are well worth the trouble to install them.  A few other thoughts....The battery life does reach the advertised 15 hours.  I can game for several nights without having to charge it.  One comment about the range and it might be due to interference but sometimes I experience audio dropouts. Please note this is when I am further away from the unit, for instance if I go into the kitchen which is maybe 15 feet away it will cut out on occasion.  However I can go all the way down the hall without any problems! I would be open to more customization and it does mention you can connect to your pc and use the Earforce hub to update.  I did this a few weeks ago and no updates were available but hopefully they will work on it in the future.

Excellent quality aluminum thumbsticks.  These fit well in the controller and allow for a buttery smooth transition in games.  The main issue I have is the lack of grip, the outer rim simply doesn't provide enough grip for me so I would suggest using something like a grip-it to help this.  Having used an elite controller for a while these will give your control that same premium feeling.  One thing to note and I didn't see it specifically mentioned in the package:  One thumbstick is slightly shorter than the other and this one is the right stick; there is also a slight difference on the bottom edge you will notice.  By design the right stick needs to be shorter otherwise it will grind on the plastic.  I would also recommend a slight amount of electrical tape, this helps to avoid the thumbstick moving around from the base and a secure hold.  Otherwise these are great and definitely will last a long time!

This game is still amazing even 6 years later! It was Bungie's swan song as it was their last Halo game and it really shows how much detail they put into this one.  The story puts you in the role of Noble 6, a new Spartan recruit to the Noble team. For not being in control of the Master Chief it still feels solid, this game takes place before Halo Combat Evolved.  The mechanics are all familiar here and the multiplayer is top notch.  My personal favorite is firefight as you fight to survive endless waves of enemies. You can tweak the settings to set things up just as you prefer.  My main gripe for this game is the state of the Backwards Compatibility release for the  Xbox One.  It is just inexcusable at how poor the game runs.  I  attempted to play with my friends and even on co-op the frames dipped below 15 with frequent stutters.  This game is very much optimized for the Xbox 360 and although the emulator for Xbox One Backwards Compatibility is continuing to improve, it is worth noting that you shouldn't expect top notch performance for the One as of yet.  I will update this review if that does change.

I have used a day one edition controller, the newer controller with the headphone jack, and finally this one with the textured grip/other changes I will describe.  This is exactly how a controller should feel.  No creaks or strange feelings when pressing buttons, this is a sold controller.  First the design, the white matte and it looks very clean even for the standard S controller.  I don't own an Xbox One S, but this is working flawlessly with my regular Xbox One.  The bumpers feel even more refined than before, just the right amount of pressure to engage them. Also the face buttons feel a touch more responsive, you will really notice this in the home button which is actually lit up in a different way.  Finally my most important concern seems to be addressed with the thumb sticks.  They have just the right amount of tension and there is no grinding whatsoever.  Essentially Microsoft has taken everything learned from the Elite controller and worked that into the manufacturing process for the standard S controller.  The shell is also put together a bit different, as you can see there is no longer 2 distinct pieces around where the guide button is.  I forgot to mention the grip, it feels great!  Although it is very subtle it is just enough to keep a comfortable grip.

This controller is decent for the price, but I decided it's not my cup of tea.  It does actually work with the Afterglow app for Xbox One.  It wasn't working at first for me but once I selected a profile it would let me adjust settings. You can adjust the rumble features and remap buttons, the light options obviously won't function.  The grip/texture on this controller is fairly nice and it feels fairly well built. I do like the sticks, they are different than the stock controller and actually feel better in my opinion.  It has a headset button to adjust game/chat volume plus the headphone jack is a plus. It is a wired controller which might be a preference to some but the fact that it is removable is a huge plus.  You could replace it with a longer cable if you wanted but the included one is long enough for me.  My biggest gripes are that the shoulder buttons don't have a satisfying click to them at all and are very spongy feeling.  Plus after a few days of use, some of my face buttons began to stick pretty consistently. The wheels on the back take some getting used to, I found I could use the up/down functions easily but clicking them in consistently was virtually impossible since the degree of feedback isn't really there.  In other words there is no physical feedback in your fingers.  Overall it's not a terrible controller if you want a spare or have a backup for friends, but not something I would ever use as my primary controller.

Wow!!! When I first saw the announcement trailer for this game, I was absolutely SHOCKED! Why? Link's Awakening is a CLASSIC Gameboy game from the 90s that I played and absolutely ENJOYED. After playing, enjoying and beaten the first 3 Zelda games: The Legend of Zelda (NES), The Adventure of Link (NES) and A Link to the Past (SNES) which by the way were groundbreaking games at the time back then. 2 years later after A Link to the Past, Nintendo released Link's Awakening for the GameBoy. I was very intrigued that Nintendo would release a Zelda game for the GameBoy because I wondered how Nintendo could transform the magic of Zelda games into a portable gaming device. I remembered purchasing Link's Awakening just 3 months after it was released in 1993 because I was doing landscaping jobs for my neighborhood and saving up money from mowing lawns, raking leaves, trimming bushes, etc. Games were insanely expensive back then and it can be difficult to decide which game to purchase that will be worth your money's worth. I purchased Link's Awakening from Toysrus store, rushed home and booted up the game. The opening scene of the game instantly had me excited and I was blown away how detailed it looked! I went ahead and beat the game over the course of 3 days because the game was THAT good. Plus, I absolutely loved exploring every inch of the game as well. I loved this game so much that I even rebought the game again on the GameBoy Color which was titled: 'Link's Awakening DX' and again for the Nintendo 3DS via eshop. So, you can imagine how insanely excited I was when I saw the opening scene of Link's Awakening when Nintendo revealed the game during Nintendo Direct. I couldn't believe Link's Awakening was getting a remake for the Nintendo Switch! Plus, I was happy that Nintendo released this remake at the right time because Link's Awakening can tide me over while waiting for Breath of the Wild sequel releasing on the Switch in the future. Everything about this Link's Awakening is absolutely 100% faithful to the original gameboy game and the graphics just make this game even more appealing to see. It reminds me of Zelda Wind Waker for the Nintendo Gamecube because so many fanboys were absolutely upset about how the graphics look for Wind Waker. Eventually, Wind Waker ends up becoming one of the best Zelda games to be released since Ocarina of Time. All the same fanboys that were very angry and upset at the graphics, they suddenly forgotten that they judged the game so quickly during the reveal and they suddenly say how much they love the graphics in Wind Waker, LOL!! Wind Waker also went on to become one of the favorites Zelda games to play in the speed running community. Anyways, if you haven't ever played Link's Awakening, then I strongly recommend that you buy this game ASAP because you wont regret it one bit. If you have played Link's Awakening, guess what? I still recommend buying this remake as well. If you enjoyed or didn't fully enjoy Link's Awakening on the GameBoy or Gameboy Color or Nintendo 3DS virtual game via eshop, then this remake will definitely make you love Link's Awakening. Forgive me for the long/boring review I've just typed up and buy this game asap!

A real step in the right direction with the next-generation of video gaming. The Xbox One certainly fell flat on it's face after announcement and launch, but damn is it back up and running like Usain Bolt in the Olympics now! There aren't any major problems I have with anything about the console, software, hardware, or otherwise. Yes, I have complaints, but they are minor and pale in comparison to the positive features that the console has. I'm also not sure why anyone would be buying the Xbox One w/ Kinect bundle that has no games. Even if you don't like AC, why not at least get a console that comes with games, even if you aren't going to use them. In fact, at the time of purchasing this one, the Xbox One w/ Kinect bundle and no games, was actually more expensive than this rendition of the console bundle. Also, I understand if you don't have the money to afford the luxury that is the Kinect, but I really feel like the Xbox One just isn't itself without the counterpart. Some may find it as a novelty item and that it cannot be useful in gaming and that the voice commands are just fluff and whatnot. And then there's the tin-foil hat society, reeking their havoc all over the internet, convincing people that the Kinect is always watching and listening in on you and that Microsoft is recording that data and could be recording constant video and selling your information to private parties and whatnot. First of all, if you're buying a Xbox One and plan to connect it to the internet in any way shape or form, your information is bound to be farmed, that is the unwritten privacy agreement of using the internet in the first place, is that of course putting your information in a virtual world that is accessible to the world is going end up having people see it. After that rant, let's begin:

To prevent TL;DR issues, here's a quick summary:

PROS:
Kinect features (voice commands, recognition software, no motor)
Xbox One's low temperature from large powerful fans
Xbox One's completely silent operation
Xbox One's slot-loading (compared to disk tray loading)
Xbox One's Blu-Ray capabilities
Controller (everything about it)

CONS:
Xbox One's whirring power supply
Xbox One's small storage space
Xbox One's inability to sit vertically
Xbox One's size
No indicator as to how many controllers are in use and which controller is which player
No more green indicator lights on the Xbox or controller, they are now white
Must be connected to the internet to initially set up

If you want any detail regarding anything mentioned in the summary above, read on...

Kinect:
The Kinect is amazing. The voice-commands make multi-tasking while using the console an absolute breeze. You can start up the console, open up Netflix, search for a movie, select a movie, play a movie, then pause, rewind and fast-forward that movie, all without touching anything except the TV/TV remote. For those concerned, you CAN make it so that the Kinect and console both SHUT DOWN when turning the console "off." And if you're really paranoid, they sell Kinect privacy covers here on Amazon and in stores. The Kinect has many abilities. The microphone has been revamped massively, even so that in a Skype call, the other player cannot hear your game through the television, but can hear you when you speak. It can recognize your heart-beat, every limb (including fingers and the direction of the limb facing the camera). Instead of having a motorized base like the older Kinect, when in a Skype video call, the camera itself will follow you around the screen (it's software powered, not hardware, nothing moves) and will zoom in on you as you get further away from the screen. Some games also chose to incorporate motion features, such as Battlefield 4. They allow you to look around when in a vehicle using your head, as well as lean around corners in game, not to mention the voice-commands they included. The Kinect also has the ability to sense who is in front of it, and will log all people with an Xbox account that are in front of it, in.

Console:
The console is obviously the meat and potatoes here. The console itself is a large-sized VCR essentially in dimensions and even look, to some extent. It is massive, but light. This is due to Microsoft's due diligence regarding the past issues with overheating and cooling malfunctions on the Xbox 360 that led to the infamous Red Ring of Death error. There are huge fans installed in this bad boy, and let me tell you, you wouldn't even know they were there. When using the console it is whisper quiet, and if I mute the TV, I can't hear anything at all while it's running. The satellite/cable feature is nice, but I don't use it since I don't have satellite/cable. The only hardware complaint I have, is that the power brick for the Xbox One makes a whirring noise when on, and it happens to be the only thing I can hear when I mute the TV, as mentioned earlier. The Xbox dashboard has been completely overhauled, some ways good, some ways bad. They did make it much harder to get to where you want to go most of the time and some things are ridiculously hard to find on the console, but you'll get it all sorted out soon enough, like I did, I'm sure. The only other console complaint I have, is that the 500GB hard drive space GOES FAST. VERY FAST. You will run out of space before you hit 15 games for sure. I have 5 I think, and I'm at 41% hard drive space usage. Fortunately Microsoft is allowing users to attach external hard drives to the console and use them for storage, and I know at least a few 1TB drives that will work, so the problem is really moot, considering you can fix it fairly easily. It also is required to sit horizontally now, however, it was NEVER a good idea to operate a console in a vertical position, even when it was a option. There's also no more indicator on the controller/Xbox as to how many controllers are connected and as to which controllers are which players, and the green indication lights on the Console and the Guide button on the controller have been changed to white now. You must also connect it to internet to use it. Period. There's no getting around it, but once you set it up, you can take it off the internet and leave it off, if you like.

Controller:
The $2 billion that Microsoft poured into improving and modifying the Xbox 360 controller design and style and functionality, paid off well. The new controller is a home run for sure. The new triggers are heaven on your fingers, as you can now wrap them around the trigger and controller smoothly. The triggers also have very nice quality rumble motors in them individually, as well as a dampened/muted contact point when pulled all the way against the controller. An issue I am having with the triggers is that my right trigger squeaks occasionally when pulled toward to the controller, but that may be an isolated case and shouldn't be present on every one of them, so I wouldn't worry about that. The new buttons look great. They are every so slightly closer to each other on the controller layout, and seem slightly smaller in circumference, and have a more "buttony" feel when pressing them down, as they seem to have a slightly noticeable actuation point.

The bumper buttons are a decent improvement over the old controllers, however I do have a complaint in that they make much, much more noise than the old ones did. Be warned, they are very "clicky." The new battery pack housing is the second best improvement, as it now sits flush with the back of the controller and doesn't protrude as the old one did, which makes holding the controller much nicer. The start button and back button were replaced by the "menu" and "view" buttons, but they essentially function the same way as before when in most games. The Xbox "guide" button got flattened and moved up the controller on its own little section and now illuminates white instead of green, and does not show which controller number it is, nor is there an indication on the Xbox One itself either, which is a slight disappointment.

The analog sticks stayed the same distance from the controller I believe, however the actual part your thumbs go on got smaller, but the improved textured rubberized edging on them makes up for that because it allows for great grip on the sticks. However, I can imagine someone with bigger fingers having a problem using this controller's analog sticks. If you have this issue or are concerned about it, I would look into Kontrol Freek's analog extensions, as they may help. They seem to move and click pretty much the same as before, but I am noticing a slight wear in the left analog stick towards to front of the shaft from holding it upward/forward in games like Call of Duty and Assassin's Creed. So far it is not impeding on anything, but a forewarning, in case it becomes further worn and becomes inoperable or impaired after a long period of extended daily usage.

The D-Pad has been improved as well, getting it's own little crater to reside in so that it is not so obtrusive from the face of the controller, and now makes a very distinct "click" when pressed, which is something I love dearly about the new controller, as I hated the completely muffled D-Pad buttons from previous controllers. Some may find it too loud or maybe slightly annoying, but I can't foresee anyone having a major issue with it.

All in all, the new controller definitely shines, and the $2 billion in research funding and tinkering definitely went to good use and will not go unnoticed. This controller should go down in history as the best ergonomic game pad created thus far, I feel.

EA finally did a game some justice and released some fairly quality material after a while.  Battlefield 3 is the Call of Duty competitor and it's got it's eyes set on a much bigger prize with it's ambitions.  Battlefield 3 boasts much, much larger map sizes than most AAA FPS titles, with plenty of vehicles to suit your fancy scattered around pretty much all of them.  It features everything from small boats, to tanks, to jets in the ways of vehicles and your standard arsenal of foot soldier weapons as in any modern-day FPS.  This game is a nice refresher from Call of Duty with the larger maps, more team-based multiplayer play and a generally more simulation feel rather than action like the Call of Duty series.  The campaign is absolutely terrible, though and I wouldn't even recommend you touch it.  It's a waste of time and the story is dull and boring and every single character is totally forgettable and the plot is mediocre at best. A great continuation of the ever famous series of Mario Kart.  The graphics on this game are utterly beautiful and very distracting when first playing new tracks and you're in awe over the landscape they have created and then you end up drifting off of the edge of the map and then proceed to hurl profanities at Lakitu as he does it duty and saves you from imminent death.  On a serious note, the graphics are great and crisp and very colorful.  There are a lot of different customization options for your kart in this game with a lot of new ones, the biggest being the new glider attached to the kart.  There are a decent amount of different characters to race as, but the issue becomes that there are much, much to many of the Koopas from the Bowser realm, in fact, there are 30 racers in Mario Kart 8, and (not including Bowser, Koopa Troopa, Lakitu or Dry Bowser) there are 7 of these little Koopa characters, that really aren't anything special and I don't care to play, especially considering the fact that they certainly don't hold the reputation of the more common Nintendo characters that we've been with since the NES days.  Also, there are a lot of tracks on this game, but they DO get old. Don't get me wrong, the remakes are cool to play on, as they have a little more life in them and the graphics are very pleasing, but I've already seen these tracks before, and would have liked to have seen much more NEW tracks to play on.  The gameplay mechanics themselves are great and the controls are great, and the online is fairly balanced and fun to play.  There really isn't anything significant to complain about with this title.  This is definitely one of the Wii U's strongest titles to date.

GTA V is certainly a worthwhile game for any fans of the series and can certainly hold it's own in the franchise.  The world size is enormous, which I liked, but it has it's drawbacks, such as needing to get from Los Santos, to the northern part of the island, it's quite the trip, and you'll surely roll your vehicle once or twice.  The graphics in GTA V blew me away.  Everything looks fairly well defined and the shadows, reflections and lighting system looks phenomenal.  The acting is absolutely great.  The plot is one of the best from the GTA franchise in my opinion, and Rockstars decision to follow 3 intertwining characters in this game was an amazing twist on the usual gameplay.  The actual game controls and mechanics are a great as ever and the driving is fairly responsive.  The driving physics are a little meh, and I personally think the vehicle damage system and the vehicle physics are a step back from what they showed in GTA IV.  My only reason for rating this 4 stars instead of 5, is that the story seemed too short for me, and I wanted there to be much more meat to it.  Saying this, the story is still great and develops the characters well and gives a great backstory and explains everything well and so on, but I just wish there was more.  It was over before I was ready for it to be over.  I get the feeling this is due to Rockstars inclusion of GTA Online in this game, which I personally don't really see as much fun and really never play much because it seems like more of a novelty than a new feature.  All in all though,  I give GTA V a 9/10.

EA did it again, as everyone was no doubt expecting from them. Battlefield 4 was released per it's schedule, to continue the war in the modern FPS gaming market.

Battlefield 4, for starters, expands and improves on Battlefield 3 in almost every conceivable way. The graphics are much better, the sound is much clearer/crisper, the weapons are better balanced, the vehicles got a touch up, the maps got better, and generally the entire multiplayer experience got much, much more enjoyable with this fourth installment.

This is all to be expected, of course, given that this game is the first Battlefield to be released on the next-generation of consoles.

Owning Battlefield 4 on both PC and Xbox One, I can offer a bit of insight into the advantages and disadvantages of both, and an overview of the games quality as a whole.

Firstly, the game itself is a welcome improvement over last-generations Battlefield 3 shooter. I still have my one large qualm with the Battlefield series as of late, however: Why is there a campaign for this game? In all honesty, the campaign from Battlefield 3 was horrendous. The characters were not memorable at all, the story was not memorable at all, and the general goal of each and every mission just felt menial and boring. Unfortunately, this carries over into Battlefield 4. The campaign is slightly more memorable, due to the characters being slightly more interactive and well thought out, but the story itself was just as boring and just as menial and drawn-out as ever. I find myself wondering why EA/DICE even bother with the campaign mode. They have to realize that no one really every purchases a Battlefield game for the campaign experience, and it shows. They never seem to put any worthwhile effort into the campaign of these games, and in doing so, make it even less meaningful than it was prior. Just a pet-peeve, if you aren't going to put in the effort to make a great campaign, and focus on multiplayer, then just make it multiplayer only. The campaign in Battlefield 4 is almost solely there to set the stage for the maps you'll play on in multiplayer, and then forget about where they came from.

But the purpose of Battlefield (the multiplayer) really came through on Battlefield 4. Despite launch issues and whatnot, I think the servers and issues have been handled at this point, and at least for me, the multiplayer experience has been a smooth one. There are never any connectivity issues or latency problems beyond the norm, and nothing seems off-putting in this regard.
They added more weapons, re-designed the classes a little bit and added in a few new features, but as far as gameplay goes, this is a prettier Battlefield 3, with a few new features and new maps.

One of the biggest things I purchased this on Xbox One for was for the new inclusion of the classic Battlefield 32 vs 32 player multiplayer matches, which were previously "impossible" on the last generation of consoles. This is a very fun new feature and having the full sized maps, with a whole 64 players in tanks, jets, helicopters, AA guns, jeeps, on foot, sniping from rooftops and rocks and the general mayhem that ensues with so many people, really brings the multiplayer to life with so much to do and so many other players to interact with.

The PC version, as usual, is capable of looking much, much better graphically and have much, much better sound quality, but as always, the cost of a machine to take full advantage of the game is also much greater than that of a gaming console one would typically buy at a store. The PC version also has a weird and annoying quirk, in that EA/DICE decided that it would be a good idea to require PC players to access the online Battlelog page to actually physically launch the game. Clicking on the play button from Origin, will lead you straight into the default web browser on your machine and take you to the Battlelog page, which inconveniently no longer works with Google Chrome. However the PC version does tend to have a more stable connection to servers, and a more diverse group of players.

The console version is much simpler, there are no graphical settings to mess with, and when you want to play, the server browser is right there in-game. There is also the added benefit that getting into the multiplayer matches on console seem to take a lot less time than on the PC version.

In any event, the game itself is worthwhile for fans of modern multiplayer FPS games, and I would recommend it, especially considering that at the time of this review the game is about half the price it was at launch.

Despite an utterly broken launch from 343 Studios, and massive let-downs yet still in regards to the multiplayer capabilities of this collection of the Halo installments, this game still deserves some amount of praise for it's accomplishments, and reprimands for it's shortcomings and failures.

The Master Chief collection was a great idea, and as far as the campaign aspect, and keeping the story alive and well, this collection did a great job. All of the campaigns have been remastered for the newer generation of hardware, and it shows. It's even more entertaining that the developers took the time to add in a feature that allows you to press the back button of the controller at any time in the remastered games to change the graphics between the remaster and the original. 343 Studios did a bang-up job with the remasters for all the games, and stayed very true to the originals throughout, with absolutely no story changes whatsoever. Having the iconic main installments to this franchise all on one disk is a very powerful thing. The cohesion that 343 was able to achieve between the games in the collection was very well done and obviously had some thought behind it's execution. The campaigns are all enjoyable in their remastered and original glory, and still thoroughly enjoyable.

This collection, does however, only include some of the Halo games, and not all of them. It includes, as expected, only the ones where the protagonist is Master Chief. This means you will find Halo: Combat Evolved, Halo 2, Halo 3, and Halo 4 in this collection, but you will not find Halo 3: ODST, Halo Reach, or the RTS Halo spin-off, Halo Wars. I really would have liked to have seen Halo 3: ODST and Halo Reach included in this collection, but I completely understand why they were not included, and nothing was docked for that, just a preference thing, as I really enjoyed Halo Reach.

The reason I docked a star is for the multiplayer that 343 decided to implement within the collection. It is still yet broken and has many bugs and issues, even this long after launch. I personally, don't attempt to play much of the multiplayer, and really just wanted the collection for the single player stories, but the fact that a section of the game is utterly broken and was even worse at launch leaves a bit of a bad taste in my mouth and hole in my trust for 343 Studios capabilities in the future for the Halo franchise.

In short, if you want to relive the glory days of the Halo franchise, in remastered graphics glory, this is the place to do it, and have them all in one place together to experience one after the other, is a great thing. But if you're looking to play the multiplayer of the collection, be aware that is is severely crippled and has a lot of issues, many of which make it not worth the time to try and play.

ACRPG (Assassin's Creed Role-Playing Game)

Welcome ladies and gentlemen to the freak show.

If you purchase this game you will witness a transformation like never before. Ubisoft will trick you into believing this is actually an action free roaming platform; however, you have been tricked into purchasing a metamorphic circus. A game that is actually a cross-breed between an "action" game and an MMORPG (Massively Multiplayer Online Role Playing Game).

This game tries desperately to cling on to it's roots, but fails miserably and succumbs to the developers will of being the first ACRPG.

The developers of this game could not hide their blatant love of MMORPGs if their life depended on it.

"UNIQUE CO-OP EXPERIENCE YOU MUST PLAY TO BELIEVE"
- dictionary(dot)com definition of an mmorpg: "any story-driven online video game in which a player, taking on the persona of a character in a virtual or fantasy world, interacts with a large number of other players."
-AC Unity forces us to now interact with large numbers of other players just to complete missions that would otherwise be completed on our own.

"DEEP CUSTOMIZATION OF ARNO, THE MASTER ASSASSIN"
- Allow me to translate: You are now forced to purchase new equipment, weapons, and skills that have ill-conceivable stats much like MMORPG equipment and weapons. If you need a new belt be prepared to sift through 2 dozen (or more) types that have as many as a half a dozen stats which no one even cares about!

"Mix and match from hundreds of possible combinations and build your stealth, fighting, and navigation abilities."
- This paves the way for "talent trees" much like what are available in MMORPGs. Most MMORPGs have Tanks (warriors), Damage Dealers (magic or melee), Ranged (archers or musketeers), and Healers. Obviously this is what Unity is trying to accomplish, and they do this by your weapon choice. Equip a musket and you're locked into a Ranger class. Equip a heavy weapon and you're locked into a Tank class. Equip sword and pistol and you're a typical melee Damage Dealer. Look at the cover art for this game and you'll see: Tank (warrior with 2 handed ax), Damage Dealer (1 handed sword), Ranger (musket), Rogue (melee Damage Dealer).

WHO needs all this customization? It's confusing and if I wanted to play an MMORPG with all these options I would, but Ubisoft don't hide your love for MMORPGs in your flagship action game!

Do I even need to bring up all the MMORPG-esque micro-transactions?
- Yup just like typical MMORPGs where you are forced to spend real-life $$$ to upgrade or acquire in-game items/upgrades, you will do the same here in AC Unity. Everything from equipment, weapons, and your skills can now be purchased via micro-transactions.

Don't have a smartphone? Guess what you can't open certain chests in the game! YAY Ubisoft has alienated gamers who might not have the smartphones! Discrimination at its best!
- Does Ubisoft have stock in smartphone companies like Apple or Android?

This is by far the WORST Assassin's Creed game in my opinion. The graphics suffer from low fps plus there are plenty of glitches that will have you restarting your beloved PS4 or Xbox One just to continue progressing through the game. This game is definitely a step backwards in comparison to Assassin's Creed IV.

So forget about everything you have come to love about the Assassin's Creed series. Forget about great story lines that lead into equipment and skill upgrades. Welcome in a new era. Say hello to the Assassin's Creed Role Playing Game (ACRPG)!

Do not purchase this game. I honestly cannot even recommend you rent this game.
