If the PC port of the game is even half as good as the PSX version, it's going to rock. Medal of Honor (and to a lesser extent, its sequel) is one of the best first person shooters I've ever played. It also happens to be a very good representation of World War II combat. The weapons represented in the game really are what was avaiable during the war (in other words you're not running around with an M-16 wasting everything in sight) The ammunition dispersal is realistic. You take it off dead enemies, steal it from warehouses.  The missions are very plausable. You had to take out German weapons productions, stop the Nazi A-bomb, and destroy a V-2 rocket lab.  And, unlike most other games, you do have to watch what you shoot! If you nail an oxygen tank, for example, you and anything withing ten feet is done for. I've seen some screen shots for this game. They look absolutely amazing. Then again, that's what gamers can expect from a Quake III engine game.

Although this game doesn't have any other brand of car in it, I don't care. I like Porsches. I also liked the fact that this game allows you to drive some of the older cars because previous NFS titles and most racing games in general are fixated on the brand new, 300-something horsepower rockets that are on the market today.
The tracks are generally well laid out, even devious. The designers stuck hard objects (such as trees, walls, stuatues, etc) in places that skid-outs and fishtailing cars are likely to hit.
The graphics are amazing. The design team, so I have heard, worked with Porsche to get this game right.
Early on, I ran into the control problems. ("Ice racing" is the term I've read most often)
This can be solved through several ways:
Experience- race the car more often so you can predict what it will do.
Upgrades- a lot of the problems with spin-out have to with with the standard parts your car comes with. Upgrading to better ones solves this problem.
Downforce/Weight distrobution/brake distrobution- when set correctly, they allow your car to stick to the road like glue or go flying head long around corners, whichever you prefer.
All in all, this is an excellent racing game. The physics modeling is superb, the graphics will amaze, and the competitor AI will impress.

I have thoroughly enjoyed this little monster. I am not going to go into the specs or everything it is capable of, you need to read that on the product overview page. But put simply, it allows you to play your Steam games on an HDTV located elsewhere- whether it be in the same room or another- as long as you have wired or wireless connectivity at both ends.

I have a gigabit wired network with gigabit switches in my home. Trust me when I say a wired network will make a big difference as opposed to running a wireless network when playing with this unit. Although wireless has grown leaps and bounds over the past ten years, it is still in no way perfect and is something else to troubleshoot when problems arise in networking realm. You are almost always better going wired.

First - lets start with my host computer build: 2nd Gen Intel i5 processor 3.4 Ghz / 24 GB DDR 3 RAM / RAID MIRROR / and most importantly, an Nvidia GTX 970 MSI OC edition. With that said, I have been able to play every game I have tried on the Steam Link with no complications. With games that require or depend heavily on a keyboard and mouse, there are USB ports just for those very components, and so far my wireless KB and wired gaming mouse has worked perfectly without any hiccups. There is an additional USB port for a wired controller if you so choose, but the Steam Link supports many wireless controller schemes, and I use my PS4 controller with no problem whatsoever.

The interface is very simple. It boots and begins by default in what Steam calls "Big Picture Mode" I have found this to be the friendliest mode to use, especially when there are other children in the house who play. I cannot speak highly enough at how well this unit games as far as smoothness is concerned. At the time of this review, me and my youngest boy are working on Dark Souls, and it streams in 60 FPS at 1080p on my 55" LCD HDTV.

There are limitations however. As one would or should expect, only so much information can be transferred at one time over an ethernet wire, and no matter how good equipment you have (I have great gigabit switches in place with large packet handling and I use solid copper Cat6 wiring. My host computer has a TP-LINK gigabit PCIe card installed) you are going to see motion blurs and fine details blur on a fairly regular basis, especially when a lot is going on in the game. It should also be noted that the Steam Link has a fast ethernet port, or a 100 Mbps port as opposed to a gigabit port (1000 Mbps) which is up to ten times faster.

*Opinion Alert* Some might suggest the fast ethernet port on the Steam Link could be the bottleneck and reason for the graphics blur. Getting a stronger processor to handle gigabit speeds, along with getting a gigabit port on a new improved Steam Link means driving the cost of the unit up, maybe even considerably.

*Other thoughts* When I upgraded my video card on the host computer from a GTX 770 to the GTX 970, there was a noticeable improvement in how well the gameplay translated to the Steam Link. The colors were a little more colorful- the action seemed to be a little smoother, there were noticeably finer details, etc.

If you go in with expectations reasonable, this is a fantastic purchase at full price, and an absolute STEAL when they put it on sale for $35.

I have been intrigued by the VR for a long time but never wanted to commit financially. It’s expensive for just being curious. I finally decided to try it though to play the new Resident Evil 7 game. The VR did not disappoint. There are hardly ways to describe how the VR impacts gaming, needless to say I am less drawn to normal console games now. This transports you elsewhere. However I understand those of you that are on the fence about this product so let me break down the pros and cons:

Pros:
Each game transports you to another world. Each game is interactive and takes more energy to play than your standard game. It will have you moving across your living room. It’s sucks you in. The two games that are included are amazing. Superhot is like the Matrix. You will be dodging bullets left and right trying to survive. Meanwhile Creed is a massive workout. Boxing is a ton of work and when you get in a match you are going to be bouncing all over the place avoiding the hits.

Cons: Although new content is still coming out, many VR games are short. Many VR users are waiting for more premium content to come out as a lot of it is more in the horror genre. Another big con is the mess of wires it comes with. It took a long time for me to set this stuff up and if you have a receiver a whole new complication gets added. The VR doesn’t like to run through receivers so setting up your surround sound can be difficult. Finally, the Move controllers are only needed for some of the VR games. Unless there are specific VR games you want that require them, go for the other set that doesn’t include them. First person shooters actually want the “Aim Controller” versus the Move Controller so know what games you want before you commit to this package deal. Otherwise you might be spending 50$ you don’t need to.

Overall my experience has made me want to further dive into VR rather than investing in other games. This is worth the investment.

First of all, I would not recommend buying this game if you don't have an xbox live account where you play online with friends/other xbox live players around the world. This game was designed mainly for online play with your friends, and it does a fantastic job of that for sure.

First, a little about the game. It is your tipical zombie movie story line come to life. We've seen it all before in the movies. Dawn of The Dead like situation where the entire city is infected with zombies, and 4 survivors are trying to continue to survive by working together through out the game. You have a typical set of characters to choose from. A biker, an older war vet, an office desk junky, and a spoiled rotten princess. All 4 struggling together to survive the zombie fest.

There are 5 sinerios in this game, each having like 4 to 5 stages in each one. They play out as short movies, where after each one you get credits that roll down the screen, showing you stats of each level such as who killed the most infected, who took the most damage, ect. This isn't exactly as decked out as I was hoping, as it only takes 30 to 45 minutes to beat each sinerio, leaving the possibility of beating the game in a couple of hours. Before you judge the game on how short it is, trust me.... the game makes up for it in many ways! Especially if you play online with friends.

Valve made a great move by making the AI director advanced in this game. You could reply each sinerio over and over again without being in the same situation twice. An example of this is, lets say you and 3 other friends are doing major damage to the zombies coming your way at the beginning of a sinerio. The game will boost up the challenge a bit and double or maybe even triple the amount of zombies you will encounter in the following sections of the sinerio. Or, if your not doing so well, the AI may take it easy on you; giving you less Zombies and more health packs and ammo to reload with. So, even though there are not as many playable levels in this game as I was hoping for, it makes up for with the advance AI director. There have also been rumors of downloadable content to add to the game, but I have not seen anything confirmed on that.

Another way to play this game is in a single player mode where you play with 3 bot controlled characters. Although this is fun and challenging, you will find it harder to play as you can not communicate with the other computer players like you can human players. You are at the front of the line, and pretty much leading the way of the other 3 computer controlled players. Meaning your first in line for any infected enemies to feast upon.

If you don't play on xbox live, but have a friend over, you can jump in with a split screen setup and play locally with that friend like you would online. Bringing another fun factor to the game.

Another mode on the game is the versus mode. I have only tried this online with xbox live friends, and we found it to be a great fun play. You can have up to 8 people playing. 4 people pick the human survivors, and the other 4 pick to be infected players. The survivors will go through the game like normal to try and survive, except the other 4 people who are on the inffected side have to try and take down the survivors. So its basically playing the game like normal, except you have human players controlling the major boss like infected people. You can't play as any zombies however, just the bigger 'boss' like infected. Either way, it is still some wholesome fun.

Overall, this is a fantastic online game. I myself played it on single player mode a few times, but it just isn't the same as online with friends. With a high speed Internet connection to Xbox live, and the headset to talk to friends while online, this game delivers in a huge way. It is a very intense game at times, expecialy on the harder skill levels. A group of friends and I played on normal and it took us over 2 hours to beat one sinerio. So it does have its challenging ways!

Over all, the game is great. It is short, but the game play itself makes up for it. Graphicaly, it is pretty good as well. Nothing like 'Assasin's Creed WOW', but great for a nextgen console. The lighting in this game is amazing. Your player has a flash light on there gun to light the way, and it mocks that of a real flash light in an amzing way. If you reload your weapon, it even takes the beam of light upward making it hard to see anything directly in front of you in certain sections of the game. Great feature.

All in all, if you an online player... BUY THIS GAME.

First off, I wanna say that I have been a happy supporter of the NHL franchise from EA Sports since 2007. I have owned every game since then, and have enjoyed the series tremendously. When i bought my PS4 in November of 2013, I was bummed out that there would not be a hockey title until September of 2014. So I was keeping a close eye on the development of NHL 15 through out the year.

This game show tremendous promise with the new presentation and game play upgrades that they where making. New NBC broadcasting presentation, new physics system for all skaters on the ice, new physics system for the puck, fantastic live crowds in the arenas with over 9,000 character models in those crowds... lots of fantastic upgrades. All the things that EA where hyping about this game got me super excited. Even the demo showed lots of promise!

However, when early access to Xbox One people hit, the list of game play modes and features that where taken out of the game began to grow. EA left fans with the impression only 3 or 4 major modes would be missing, but as you can see, the list at the bottom of this review shows other wise. They even removed the basic offline Season mode that has been a staple in sports games since the regular Nintendo in the 1980's and 90's for crying out loud! But before I get to that list, I want to share my personal gripes and issues with this game.

First of all, I got a PS4 system crash with this game 5 times in 3 days. Error code CE-34878-0 would occur at random times during game play. I would be in the middle of a game, and it would just crash to the PS4 menu showing this error. It is the ONLY PS4 title that I have played that has done it on several occasions in such a short span. The demo did it several times as well.

Second, in the Be A GM Mode, there was no way to lock your position. Meaning you could not take control of a single position in a game, but you had to switch players to whoever was closest to the puck on the ice. This was annoying, because a couple friends and I practiced on the demo where one of us would played center, the other left wing defense, and the other right wing offense. We couldn't do that now, because locking your guy in Be A GM mode was no longer an option. Also in Be A GM mode, and this is a small gripe that isn't a huge deal, but shows EA rushed the hell out of this, but there where grammar and spelling mistakes in the menus when you would receive a scouting report!

The A.I. in this game is terrible. Leaving the game difficulty in the standard "Pro" setting without touching the sliders for the AI adjustments proved to be disastrous. I would win one game 7 to 0 and then get crushed the next by a lower rated team 9 to 2. Completely unrealistic. When bumping the difficulty to "All Star", the CPU turns into the incredible hulk and I would get scored on 6 times in 2 shifts. There are heavy goal glitches where friends I know who have the game are winning 20 to 2 by the end of a 5 minuet 2nd period.

When playing Be A Pro mode, the announcers during commentary would constantly say my players name wrong. I chose 'Johnson' as my player's announcer name, and they would constantly call me "Jones" through out the game. Also in this mode, you can not simulate between your shifts when your off the ice or in the penalty box. And if you get ejected from the game due to an illegal hit (which it calls constantly for no reason), you either have to sit in the penalty box the entire game and watch the CPU play until then end of the game, or quit the game and start it over.

The presentation and the game play overall is very solid. The NBC Sports presentation is awesome to see with Dok Emerick on the mic. The crowds look great, the player models are top notch, but looks are not everything. Game play is solid, but is so buggy and glitch filled, leaving it feeling unfinished and incomplete.

Being super frustrated with the modes I played and the constant crashes, I put this pile of garbage up for sale. Below is the extreme long list of missing features, followed by the extremely short list of planned updates/patches for it. Does anyone else find it ironic that one of the modes EA left in the game is HUT (Hockey Ultimate)? Can you guess why? Because I know a few people personally who will spend several hundred dollars... REAL MONEY for card packs. In other words, cash cow EA made sure THAT mode stayed in....

Rock Band 4, in my opinion didn't get the love it deserved when it was first launched in 2015. Whoever is at fault - either Mad Catz for the lack of production of peripherals at launch like Harmonix claims, or if it was Harmonix for the lack of promo to get sales up like Mad Catz claims, or if the genre just ran it's course from over saturation in the 2007 to 2011 stretch. You can claim who or whatever you want, but the truth is, Rock band 4 is a solid title, and still a fantastic party game for everyone!

I was able to get all my Rock Band 3 songs over to Rock Band 4, which to me surprise also included all the Rock Band 1 and 2 tracks. Apparently, if you have exported your Rock Band 1 and 3 track into Rock band three on your Xbox 360 in the past, they come along in the $15 export purchase for Rock Band 4. I was aware of this, as I ready it was to late to export Rock Band 1 and 2 into Rock Band 4, but that's only if you are trying to export them directly into 4. I already exported them into Rock Band 3 for my 360, so they all came over to 4 which was a pleasent surprise.

There is a $30 expansion to Rock Band 4 called 'Rivals' which adds online play and a couple of offline/local play options as well. There is some people complaining about paying the $30 for an add-on of online play, and although I can see where they are coming from, I am also willing to support Harmonix and purchase it. Harmonix is an independent company now, and they are some what on their own. PdP, who took over for Mad Catz when they went under helps out, but there is still licensing that they need to cover for music and to keep servers up and running, ect. So I purchased the expansion without any issues.

Game play wise, there is not much to talk about. If you are a fan of previous Rock Band titles, the core game play is exactly the same. They didn't go into a different direction like Guitar Hero Live did, so it is new, yet familiar game play. One of the things I absolutely love is the new peripherals. I have not used the PDP ones yet, but Mad Catz did a great job designing the new instruments - for being plastic controllers of course.

The drums are pretty solid (wireless as well which is nice). The pads are more rubber type instead of Rock Band 1's original clacky and ridiculously loud pads, which makes them a LOT more quiet. They still make a little noise, but nothing more then a standard drum practice pad would.

The guitar itself has a very well done quiet strum bar. The buttons have nice clicks to them, and are nice in size, although if you are use to playing with older Guitar Hero controllers like I was, it will take a little getting use to, but not a deal breaker at all. One of the best features I think, is the audio and video sync option the controller has. I play through a surround sound system, and when the 4k tv and surround sound system both have volume, you can clearly hear latency. So what I do is, turn the TV all the down, turn the surround sound up, and then use the game's calibration tools. The guitar controller has built in Mic and video sensor, making it a breeze to calibrate the game to your sound system of choice. For audio, it makes a click sound and you just hold the guitar up to the speaker. Within seconds the audio is calibrated. You then do the same for video. You just hold the guitar up to the TV, start the video calibrator, and it flashes white on the screen to calibrate the video. The end result is a dead on accurate setup, making it easier to hit notes on the screen. I ended up manually calibrating the game at first, and I was missing notes and runs I was clearly hitting. But once I used the auto calibrator, it ran fantastic.

The add on DLC songs is where it is at, as the on disc sound track is not the strongest. I knew this going in, but I love a lot of the DLC they are offering on the store. Each song is $1.99 or there are special collection packs you can get.

Overall I love Rock Band 4. Some of the customization options for your characters are a little lack luster,and even the the Rivals expansion adds some more to the collection, it's not as strong as previous installments of the game. But if you are into it for just the good 'ol fun game play, you can't beat it.

If you are a fan of the franchise, I would recommend Rock Band 4. Esecially if you plan on buying the Rock Band 3 export and the Rivals expansion. With the band bundles currently being about $170 here on Amazon, it is the cheapest it has been since it launched. I am enjoying the title very much.

I'll start off with my honest opinion of Takahashi (and his wife too!) as a storyteller and game designer. I honestly believe that this man is capable of making some of the absolute greatest stories and games of all time. Unfortunately, it seems that with every game of his that I've played, I have enjoyed either the story or the gameplay much more than the other aspect in question. For Xenogears, I found myself very intrigued by the story. At the same time the gameplay, while fun at times, definitely felt dated and slow to me. This has to be a personal feeling though, because so many other people on the internet and elsewhere find the gameplay to be some of the best in an rpg to this day. Don't get me wrong though, the battles can actually be really fun, especially when you get to create deathblow chain combos. Despite my qualms about the game feeling slow and clunky, I still have to hand it to Takahashi for creating easily the most ambitious Science Fiction story that I have ever experienced in a jrpg. For this fact alone, I could easily recommend Xenogears to anyone who wants to experience a jrpg with a very interesting and captivating story. In the end, I would highly recommend Xenogears for anyone looking for a great story or even if you are simply a fan of Takahashi's later work.

Pros:
-The story is very deep and interesting and keeps you playing the game even if the gameplay turns you off.
-The characters are very well done, and you will likely get attached to some of them.
-The music, composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, is amazing as per usual with his work.
-Mecha combat, while painful at times, looks really badass.
-The ambition of the game as a whole really shows, and it's great.
-Deathblows (button combos in combat on foot) are actually really fun to mess around with.

Cons:
-The gameplay as a whole (at least to me) feels dated and slow, especially in gear dungeons.
-The dungeons themselves can get quite tedious, and several of them can take hours to dredge through.
-The encounter rate in certain areas can get annoyingly high, but not enough to make you ragequit.
-When walking around in an area with encounters, there seems to be a lag between when an encounter is programmed to occur and when it actually starts. You WILL notice this, and at times (especially when you are about to enter/exit an area) it probably will annoy you.

Mixed:
-There seems to be a slight preference by the creators towards gear battles. Depending on how much you like battling in gears, this could either be good, bad, or not an issue at all.
-There is some religious symbolism in this game, and while it does not specifically target any religion, someone who is (or isn't) religious could be offended by it depending on how they view fictitious depictions of religion.
-There is some nudity (both pixelated and in cutscenes) but you don't see too much. It still could be a bad thing if you're strongly against nudity in any form though.

The Tales series is one that has seen a fairly large number of entries, and so by this point each entry may appear to follow a certain formula established by prior entries. While this definitely happens to be the case with Tales games, the formula that is followed isn't so engrained that there is no room for improvement between successive titles. In fact, Tales of Vesperia, which was developed by the team that made Symphonia and Abyss, happens to improve on the formula of both of those previous installments quite well. By creating a very well rounded game in terms of gameplay, story, and music among others, the developers did a fantastic job of keeping the series fresh and relevant. Graphically, Tales of Vesperia takes the cell shaded route, but for the first game in the series to be released in HD the visuals in this style work marvelously. Character wise there is not much to complain about. While some of the standard anime tropes do appear in the story and characters, each character is enjoyable enough to overcome these stereotypical archetypes and let the game's story shine regardless. As far as gameplay goes, Tales of Vesperia plays much like Symphonia and Abyss. The one important thing to note to newcomers is that the gameplay does take a while to get going. Once several artes are learned and combos are available, the gameplay becomes far more solid and enjoyable than at the very beginning of the game. Overall, Tales of Vesperia takes everything that the previous games in the series do well and blends them together to create an overall solid and highly recommended action rpg.

Pros:
-Battle system is very similar to Tales of Symphonia and Tales of the Abyss, but manages to improve upon the formula
set by those games.
-Story is engaging enough to keep the player interested the whole way through.
-Characters, while sometimes stereotypical, are great overall and are memorable as well.
-Music is solid and fits the scenes and environments well.
-Cell shaded graphics work great for the first Tales entry in HD
-Difficulty is adjustable at any point in the game through the settings menu.
-The new game plus mode allows you to compound stats, artes, and more through successive playthroughs.

Cons:
-If you have played a Tales game before, the formula of the story can sometimes be predictable but never to a major extent.
Only one of the batteries was dead on arrival, so I have minimal complaints. We will have to see in the long run though!

Katsura Hashino is easily one of my favorite game directors of all time. With Persona 5, you can tell that he has truly brought Persona to the next generation. Overall, I would say that Persona 5 is very much worth your time. While there were several things about the game that made me enjoy it less than Persona 4, I still found it a worthy game of the Persona name.

Note: This is a review for the Playstation 3 version of the game, which if you have any concern runs very well on the console. It seems that the Playstation 4 version is in 1080p instead of 720p and has better loading times than the PS3 version.

Pros: -Persona 5 has easily the best gameplay the series has ever seen. We see a return of the great gameplay of Persona 3 and 4 with a smooth and streamlined execution that really makes battles and Palace exploration/sleuthing a treat. The Baton Pass feature is also something that I found added a really cool layer of depth to the battle system.
-Artistically, this is by far the best looking Persona game released to date. The art direction is stunning, and I would be hard pressed to find another game that I have played with a better sense of style and artistry. Playing Persona 5 really feels like you’re playing an animated manga in the best way possible.
-The soundtrack by Shoji Meguro is once again a highlight here in Persona 5. If you liked how Persona 3 and Persona 4 differentiated themselves musically to fit their respective themes, you’ll especially like how the jazzy soundtrack fits Persona 5. Also, Life Will Change is bar none the best song in any Persona game to date.
-This is a minor pro, but being able to date adults in this installment was a very nice addition.

Cons: -Mementos is essentially Tartarus from Persona 3 but with less personality. It does serve a purpose, but when contrasted with the hand-crafted palaces, it is painfully obvious how much the dungeon design has improved in this installment and it feels like Mementos is there to provide filler.
-The pacing issues I had with Persona 3 appear to rear their head yet again here. I’d even say that Persona 5 has the biggest pacing issues of the three Hashino directed installments. I believe a big part of this can be attributed to the fact that the deadlines for each palace are clearly outlined, whereas in Persona 4 you’d have to check the weather and even then you’d have to make a judgement call as to whether the rainy weather would be enough to cause fog and a subsequent missed deadline. By knowing how many days you have to kill before the story progresses, I found myself often just trying to rush through a bunch of days just to find out what happens next instead of taking my time and enjoying the slower parts of the game. I found myself playing the game at a much more relaxed pace on the days between a story point and the next palace opening up with a new deadline.

Mixed: -While the art style is amazing as I mentioned previously, it can really be a pain on the eyes at times. The flashiness of the whole package is definitely not something that anyone with photosensitivity will find pleasant. Even without photosensitivity, because the game demands so much of your time and attention, there is a good chance that by the end of some play sessions your eyes will be quite fatigued.
-The customizability of the options leaves a bit to be desired. Specifically, being able to turn up/down the volume of voices, sound effects, and the music would have been an appreciated feature. However, this doesn’t detract from the game enough to make me consider it a con.
-The loading times (I’m reviewing the PS3 copy, so I’m specifically referring to the loading times of that version. The PS4 version may be much better in this regard for all I know), while not really bad, are compounded due to the game’s length, making them feel more noticeable as the game goes on.

The D-Pad for this fightpad is horrible!

I really like the layout of this controller. The buttons and d-pad are perfect for me. The killer for this controller is the d-pad, it just doesn't work. I read about this controller having a lot of problems, I figured maybe these problems have been fixed by now, but apparently I was wrong.

The diagonals on this controller just don't work. I have this controller plugged into my computer, I can see the input of the directions I press as I press them, I am getting real-time feedback on it. When I press each diagonal on the d-pad, it doesn't always register a diagonal. What it registers is either right, left, up, or down. If I press down HARD on the diagonal, I may get a diagonal command, but ONLY if I press hard on the diagonal, and it will ALWAYS register another direction first BEFORE it registers the diagonal. There's an arrow located on the d-pad for each direction. Up, down, left, right, and the diagonals all have arrows. When I press a diagonal arrow, it goes in a different direction. Huh? If I press the DOWN-RIGHT arrow, it goes RIGHT, and not DOWN-RIGHT.

Some examples: If I press UP-RIGHT on the d-pad, it registers RIGHT. If I tap UP-RIGHT fast on the d-pad, it will iregister RIGHT and only sometimes will it register UP-RIGHT. If I press down hard on UP-RIGHT, it will register RIGHT and then it might register UP-RIGHT.

It never registers only the diagonals first, it will always register another direction first. UP-RIGHT will always execute RIGHT first, DOWN-RIGHT will always execute RIGHT first, UP-LEFT will always execute LEFT first, DOWN-LEFT will always execute LEFT first.

I can NEVER execute just a diagonal command. I tried this many times. I have other cheaper controllers that have no problems executing movements on their d-pads, why does this more expensive one find going in a diagonal so hard.

The buttons work fine. The feel of the controller is great. But what's the point of all that if the d-pad doesn't work.

Maybe people with working controllers got good ones and the rest of us got bad ones, or maybe they just have lower standards, all I know is that this controller sucks. It's not worth all this money for a controller that can't get the basic function of a d-pad right.

I haven't played a platformer in well over 10 years. I was intrigued by the game idea, using 3 different switchable characters to get past physics based puzzles. Each character has their own strengths, and not only that, but you can use a different character to get past the same puzzle. For example, near the beginning, you can either use the wizard's magic to move a battle ram to destroy a door blocking the path, or have the knight use his sword and hit it multiple times, till it finally moves and knocks the door down. I liked this idea, and in the game, it works very well.

And that's the most coolest part of the game. That you can kill monsters with any of the characters, that you can solve most puzzles with any of the characters(though the knight has a tough time reaching a few places), that how you solve the problems you face is up to you. What character you use, what tactics you use, is all up to you. You can try fighting, try swinging, try smashing, try to make a bridge, or even try using more than one character's skills to get past a puzzle. I don't have to follow anyone's guide, or follow anyone's way, I get to fight, solve puzzles, and play it my own way. This is a great thing.

I enjoy the little RPG element to the game. You can find items in chests, some are very hard to find. These items will help you out in a variety of ways, and you can give the items to any character you want. Another RPG element is experience points you collect, in which you use to level up. Experience points are collected by defeating monsters and finding experience potions throughout the levels. When you level up, you get points to raise a skill of your choosing, but first you have to find the skill. The RPG element isn't anything in depth, but it does add another layer of funness to the whole affair.

I do have some problems with the game. My first problem, is that it is way too short. I finished the game in just a few hours. Another problem, is that some of the puzzles are way too easy, I skipped more than a few puzzles just by moving really fast. Maybe moving really fast is just a way to beat them, but it seemed too easy for me the first time through. If you really want to challenge yourself when you first play, try the hard difficulty, anything below that is just too easy.

Another problem is the lack of variety of enemies. You'll fight skeletons, and then some more skeletons. But that's not all, you then have to fight more skeletons. And then some more skeletons. Lots of skeletons. Don't be too sad though, there's also annoying bats to fight, which will attack you and fly away, only to come back and attack you again till you finally dispatch them. The lack of variety is nothing I found bad, and there is more than one type of skeleton to fight, but if you want more monsters to fight, all you'll find here are skeletons.

Other than it being way too short and not having enough challenging puzzles, everything else in the game is spot on. The music is just gorgeous and fits the fantasy world. The voice acting is nicely done and does not irritate, though there are only a few lines in the whole game. The graphics are just as gorgeous, as you travel through the game, you see a lot of detailed and attractive backgrounds. Sometimes you'll see a chest of gold in the background and wonder to yourself "why can't I get that". There are some problems with the graphics I have found, mostly with the characters themselves. It's nothing major, but there are some oddities, like the thief's grappling hook sometimes shoots out a few feet in front of her, and not from her hand like it's suppose to. If a monster hits the grappling hook, the thief will take damage, which doesn't seem fair(not that it happened a lot). It's nothing that subtracts from the game, but with such nice detailed levels and backgrounds, they could have fixed the character models up too.

The story in the game is very limited. There's a little interaction between characters, some narrative, and nothing more. It's the typical good against evil story, not that there's anything wrong with that. The game is a physics based platform puzzle game, and that's all it is in the end, with the story taking a back seat.

There is a multiplayer mode in the game, which allows up to 3 people to play at once. I have yet to try multiplayer, but I have to say, trying to get past these puzzles with three people playing at once would be very fun!

I found the game to be very enjoyable, and being my first platformer in many years, it's a nice surprise. I've already beaten the game on two different difficulty levels, and I still enjoy picking it up and playing it to see if I can get past a level using a different character and strategy. It's a big reason why I like this game, I get to solve the game's levels my own way. I just wish it was longer, for a well put together game, there's more that should be enjoyed.

If you're a casual gamer, you can still enjoy this, because while there are a lot of hidden items to be found, you don't need to find them all to win the game. You can safely ignore the really hard to get items and still beat it. But once you pick the game up, you'll probably want to find the hidden items and try to figure out how to reach those out of reach areas, it's just too much fun not to.

It seems no one mentioned this games DRM. The game itself, is a fantastic fighter. Since DRM is very important when making a purchase for many shoppers aware of it, it's worth mentioning what kind of DRM is on this game.

FIrst, a little history. Street Fighter 4(the original) came out with Windows Live. You had to have a constant internet connection in order to play that game to it's fullest. You could still play the original Street Fighter 4 offline, but you couldn't play your saved games and it wouldn't save your progress, you were also limited to only half of the fighters, because you had to unlock them all in the original. If you didn't always log into Windows Live everytime you started the game, you weren't able to access the other fighters you unlocked. What the original Street Fighter 4 had, was a DRM where you needed a constant internet connection to play.

Did they change the DRM in Street Fighter 4 Arcade Edition? Yes, and no.

DRM in the Arcade Edition is still Windows Live. You need a Windows Live account and you will always have to be logged into Windows Live, thus you always have to be connected to the internet, to play Street Fighter 4 Arcade Edition to it's fullest. They have now all the characters unlocked, so if you want to play offline, you can do so with all the characters, however you must download a patch through Windows Live first before all the characters become unlocked. Saving still only occurs if you are logged into Windows Live and only if you are connected to the internet. If you don't have an always online connection, you won't be able to play your saved games, nor will you be able to save your progress, just like how it was in the original Street Fighter 4.

Great game, but horrible, horrible DRM system is in place.

I am dumbfounded why so many people give this game glowing reviews. What is wrong with this game? Plenty.

Monsters level with you. Items level with you. Shops level with you. Dungeons level with you. This means, everything in the world depends on what level you are. Where's the feeling of my character being stronger, when I can go back to the easy areas and fight the creatures that once gave me a hard time? Where's the challenge of fighting creatures that are twice my level? A good RPG lets you fight tough battles so you have to think of a tactic to win, with multiple reloads. A good RPG lets you fight weaker battles so you feel more stronger and feel a sense of achievement in your characters development. Where's the feeling of finding a good item in a dungeon? You can't, all the items you find are leveled with you as well.

Combat is a click-fest. This is not a PC RPG. It's a console game that tries to act like a PC game, with console features and console combat. Click the mouse button as fast as you can to win. There is even a glitch that I found, when holding a torch and casting a destruction spell, I can actually cast faster than normal. With a game that won so many awards, bugs are all over the place. You don't have to think or plan to win any of the fights in the game. Can you run around and click the mouse button? Congrats, you just won. I prefer some thinking involved that you find in a PC RPG.

Lackluster NPC's. They all sound the same with the same voice actors. What a bore. How can a game get so many rewards when they stick every person in the world with the same voice actor. It gets annoying when everyone you talk to sounds the exact same. There are beggars in the game, they are used for several quests. When you talk to them, they try to sound "poor", and are quite annoying. But that's not all the beggars do that's annoying. When you talk to them, they will try to convince you that they're "poor" with their voices, but when you ask them a question about something else, their voices change to match everyone else in the world! This game is ridiculous when it comes to the voice acting. Not only do all the NPC's sound the same, they actually change their voices during conversations.

Arrows tell you where to go. If you get a quest, you get an arrow on your map that shows the exact location where you have to go. In a PC RPG, you have to figure out where to go, you have to stop and think of how to solve a quest. Because this is a console game, you get arrows pointing all over the place showing you how to solve every single quest in the game. You don't even have to listen to any of the NPC's, not a single word. Ignore them and skip all their dialogue, follow the arrows and you solve your quest without knowing what's going on. In a PC RPG, you have to take notes and think how to solve a problem. Having arrows point to exactly where I have to go makes doing quests pointless, and you could even say the game plays itself without me. What fun.

Maps are pathetic. You can't even type in notes on your map. Ultima Underworld got the auto-map done right, you could type in notes and everything was perfect. How can a game that comes out 14 years later not even include the basics of what a PC RPG has to offer?

A.I. is dumb. There's no other word to describe it. Sometimes you get A.I. companions, they run in to fight without any tactic or thought to their well being.

The interface is clumbsy. You don't even get a spellbook. All the spells you learn get thrown into your inventory like items do. It's not even organized properly. If you're a magic user, you want every spell you can get a hold of. It's not fun when you have hundreds of spells in your inventory, and you have to cycle through them all everytime you want to find ones you want to use. I'm a spellcaster, I want to cast lots of spells, what's wrong with wanting a spellbook like a normal mage. If you get a lot of items, you'll have to do a lot of scrolling up and down just to find what you're looking for. How hard is it to get inventory management done right in today's age? Even budget games can do it right. There isn't even a key ring. Key rings have gone back for years in PC RPG's. It helps you keep all your keys in one place, so they don't clutter your inventory space. Well, no key ring in this game. If you get lots of keys, prepare to do lots of scrolling.

You can be good at everything. What makes a good PC RPG? Diversity, challenge. When you're good at everything, you can't overcome your weakness. You can't use your strengths. You become the best at every skill, you can join every single guild with one character. You can do *everything* there is with one character. Not only does this kill any replayability in the game, since there are no classes, no diversity in any type of character development, it also kills any fun in creating a unique character.

Leveling up is too easy and simplified. Instead of gaining levels through defeating creatures and solving quests, you gain levels by doing the same thing over and over again. You can become a high level without ever leaving town, cast the same spells over and over again, and before you know it, you're level 30. Leveling goes up fast regardless of your character level, so it only takes slightly longer to reach the max of each skill the higher you go, but it's still fast. Go from 30 conjuration to 100 conjuration in less than a few minutes. Summon a skeleton in a tight corner and cast the undead spell on him over and over again. I much prefer using a PC RPG's way of leveling, this console way is too easy and boring. I even heard about people using a rubber band on the mouse so they can do something similiar while they are at work or school, just to level a skill up high while they are away. How lame that is, have games really sunken this low? PC RPG's do it so much better.

There are 2 good things about this game, it lets you create your own spells and enchantments, and it's an open world. Creating your own spells is fun and done well, but you can't make any complicated spells. PC RPG's have been open world going back 30 years, so this game does nothing new in this regard, it's just nice to see. You can explore lots of places, anywhere you want to right from the start. But know what? Every dungeon looks the same. All the forts, caves, ruins, all have the same look. All ruins look alike, all forts look alike. You go inside one cave, you've been in all the caves. They even have several copy and paste rooms, with several rooms being the exact same in different areas. There are unique rooms here and there, yes, but what's the point when they still look the same and have copied areas? It's the same as it was in Daggerfall, only here it's not "random".

This game doesn't deserve all the awards it got. It is a console game, not resembling a PC RPG at all. It's bland, boring, and requires no thinking on part of the player.

- Online play is horrible. The lag time was so bad that I needed to start my swing just as the ball was leaving the pitcher's hand. Here's an idea, 2K Sports: don't offer online play. Honestly, I got four hits in an online game, only because I just gave up on swinging and started bunting every time. It was the worst online gaming experience I have ever had. The only benefits of an Internet connection with this game are MLB Today and Living Rosters.
- When playing My Player, many achievements, such as trucking the catcher and hitting three home runs in a game, are reserved for other modes (although it doesn't clearly explain that). Also, I played two seasons on My Player and the only achievement left for me to earn is making the Hall of Fame; no way I'm going to play a bunch of seasons to pursue 80 points.

I've read reviews in which people report game freezes, but I've played two seasons in My Player and about 15 games in Franchise and have had no freezes.

This game is definitely worth buying if you're into Franchise or My Player, but if you're looking for something to play online, this is not it. I'm happy with my purchase, but until I read rave reviews about a future MLB 2K game I won't buy another.

Batman Arkham Asylum is hard to put down.  Graphics are awesome, story is interesting, gameplay is challenging but not something only hardcore gamers can figure out.  The strong language doesn't occur too often, but I didn't feel like it added anything to the game and should have been omitted.  I borrowed the game from a friend and soon purchased it for myself.  You're not going to find a better game for the price.

LEGO Pirates of the Caribbean was well worth the wait!  Gameplay is a bit more challenging than some of the earlier LEGO games, but my five-year-old can still get through it with a little work.  The cutscenes are hilarious.  The split screen is a bit annoying at times, but it looks like that's the way all newer LEGO games are going to be.  The price should come down on this in a few months just like the other LEGO games, but if you're a fan of Pirates of the Caribbean or LEGO games it's definitely worth the full price.

I've loved almost all the LEGO video games, but this might be my favorite yet. LEGO: Marvel has a wide range of characters with unique characteristics and skills, from Spider-Man to Mr. Fantastic to The Incredible Hulk. It's simple but challenging, something that has made the LEGO games so popular with my whole family, and, like most other LEGO games, the replay value is high. There's plenty of humor, but not so much that it slows down the stories or distracts me from the game.

As much as I've loved most LEGO games, none of them could match the entertainment value of the first one I played, LEGO: Batman. LEGO: Marvel is on its way to taking the top spot on my list. Highly recommended.

Let me preface my review by saying that I have never spent $60 on a game I didn't intend to like a whole lot, I loved Arkham Asylum & City, and I this was THE game I looked forward to playing all year.

Arkham Origins was decent (albeit far more violent than its predecessors) until I ran into a glitch after losing to Copperhead. I simply fell into infinite space, where I remained in free-fall until I finally died. The game auto-saves, and I am stuck. If I make Batman spin in circles for a couple minutes as he's falling, I land on a randomly floating board, that I can stand on for eternity, but nothing can get me out of this area.

It's release weekend for the game, and I've lost everything I've played during the first two days.

I'll update this review if/when they fix the glitch, but until then I'm stuck playing challenges. I'm not going to start a new game because I don't want to run into a game-ending trip to infinite space again.

Update 2: The more I play, the more I enjoy this game. I am currently about 80% complete and the story missions is where this iteration of Spider-Man games really shines. I am so glad they didn't redo an origin story or play off an existing movie IP and threw us in the middle of the Sinister Six's New York. The side missions are equally impressive with additional characters and bosses to enjoy. However, the crimes, research, challenges, etc. get very repetitive very fast and I feel penalized for not wanting to get gold medals on everything because at this rate, I don't think I will be able to unlock roughly half of the suits and possibly unable to fully upgrade my last gadget with the amount of challenge tokens that I have already unlocked. Unless there are additional missions that I have not yet unlocked? In any case, this is not the perfect game, but I highly recommend it for any fan of the series. I have been mostly playing over remote play on my desktop PC which leads to some grainy graphics and brightness issues, but I am actually able to read the text better on the smaller, lower resolution screen, which is mind-blowing to me. Not many people are going to experience this game this way, so I still stand by my statement that they need better accessibility options in regards to the text size.

Update: I have spent a few hours with the game now and I am mostly enjoying it, but it doesn’t exactly live up to the hype. Mostly mindless fun so far. It’s assassin’s creed meets Batman Arkham night meets Spider-man. Most everything has been done before. Web swinging is fun, but frustrating. I am unlocking towers, taking poorly framed pictures of landmarks, and collecting backpacks. The story seems very slow to start and it hasn’t really grabbed my interest yet, so I am staying distracted by trying to hit all the icons on the map. It’s a love-hate relationship so far. Combat is fluid but camera issues and no manual lock on ability get to be bothersome. Graphics are decent, but still rather cartoony, which I don’t think is what they were going for. Text size is a HUGE problem in that it is way too SMALL. I have perfect vision and play on a 46” 4K tv and it’s nearly unplayable because I can’t make out anything in the menus or on the HUD. Same issue that God of WR had at launch. I can only hope they patch this game the same way they did with that one.

Original 3-star review:

Didn’t come with the steelbook case like in the product photo. 43 GB install right out of the box. 4 GB day one update is still downloading. Just learned that there is already paid DLC available for purchase. Not impressed so far and I haven’t even got to play yet. I will return to update this review with actual impressions of the gameplay. At least I was able to get my game on time after Amazon mysteriously stopped preorders.

This game is not going to break any records by any stretch, but that doesn’t stop it from being a truly enjoyable atmospheric experience. My only legitimate complaints are the random fluctuations in volume of the main character’s audio (tends to be WAY louder than the rest of the game and then taper off mid-sentence) and the long load times in between chapters. I have found that it’s best played with headphones on to really immerse myself in the environment. I will likely find myself playing through a couple times to see how things unfold by approaching the puzzles and conversations differently.

The original games were classics in their own time but they haven’t really aged well. That being said, this is a faithful remaster of the originals in that it is the exact same game(s) just with a beautiful new coat of paint (graphics redesigned from the ground up). Unfortunately, there isn’t much in the way of story and you’re left to your own devices to figure out your goals. I truly wish they had tightened up the controls with this modern rerelease but it’s still just as clunky as I remember from days long past. The other major downside is that the physical copy only contains about 250 MB of data on the disc and you are left to download an additional 42 GB before you can play the full game. Might as well have just purchased it digitally. Not great but not bad, either. If you’re a glutton for punishment and looking for some nostalgia, this collection is for you. If you want a solid, fun, modern gaming experience devoid of technical glitches and enjoy instant gratification of playing a game on disc, probably not so much.

Had a delivery snafu and ended up having to get a refund from Amazon, but I was able to get the game digitally through the eshop (14GB for those wondering). I am absolutely stunned by the amount of content in this game! It has the nostalgia and simplicity of the earlier entries in the series but there’s so much to do and unlock between the many different game modes and the challenges that it feels completely brand new. The roster is huge, but you only start with the original 8 characters. However, you begin to unlock new ones very quickly. Not sure if there’s any method to how you unlock certain characters, but they’re coming along at such a steady pace that I should get to my favorites without a hassle. The level selection menu is a little overwhelming so I tend to just stick it on random. The Adventure mode map is HUGE and will likely keep me busy for many hours to come. Online is pretty seamless for matchmaking with strangers but the inability to directly message or invite friends is a little cumbersome. Also, relying on the phone app for voice chat is just ridiculous. I like that it limits my kids online interactions but it makes it so much more difficult than it should be.

Looks great, feels great, performs great. Mostly. X button was a little sticky at first but has broken itself in over time. I do have some issues with it desyncing at least once a week, which I haven’t experienced with any of my other Xbox One controllers. I also feel like the guide button has a further amount of travel and needs to be pushed longer in order to respond than what I am used to.

I absolutely hated having to swap between controller and a full size keyboard when playing FFXIV on PS4. After reading many reviews of many different controller chatpads, I settled on this one but still didn’t have much hope. Boy, was I pleasantly surprised! Nice travel on keys and just the right amount of clicking for feedback when typing. Space bar is a little weird to where you have to press the sides and I wish it had hard keys instead of rubbery ones, but those are minor issues. I like having the option to turn backlights on or off with one button. Setup was a breeze and the built in battery for playing while charging the controller is a huge selling point. Would definitely recommend.

... I ordered two and they both had data from Perfect Dark already on them. Working great so far, though, so no major complaints. Just odd to me. They were carded and appeared new but the design of the packaging was such that it would be very easy to put a used controller pak in it and have it seem like it was brand new at a glance.

I enjoyed the first Dead Rising, so picking up this was a no-brainer. Although it seems that they have continued on with the same theme of taking place in a shopping mall, they have added a ton of new weapons and weapon combos for endless hours of Zombie killing.

The bosses are a bit overpowered and difficult to beat, but the normal zombies are a piece of cake. So when going against those bosses, remember to stock up on weapons and food to overcome them. Most of the boss have a secret way of killing them, so if you find yourself stuck, just google the solution.

As for the game itself, you are timed again and need to keep finding Zombrex to keep your daughter alive in the game. Although not difficult to do, I really hate timed games. Especially ones that you can just get caught up killing zombies for a while and not relies that time is ticking by.

Try saving as many survivors as possible! They are key to leveling up faster.

Also, Capcom has added an additional little bonus of multiplayer play! Now you can compete in a gladiator style match against players online. It's pretty fun, and any of the winning money that you obtain will be directly deposited into your campaign.

I love a good Mafia based game, and this one takes you back to the 1940's during WWII as a Italian immigrant to the United States. At first you think it's going to be mostly a open world sandbox game like Grand Theft Auto, but you quickly discover that you need to follow the set Chapters in order and finish things in a normal RPG setting while driving from one job to another. You can't really change things up and spice up your mob experience, and the little things you can do, are not really worth it in the end.

Also, some of the missions are pretty boring. I don't want to spoil any of the boring missions because they play a part in the story, so i'll just move on to the pros and cons of this game. I also want to add that I have the setting on the hardest possible and it's not really a challenge. You'll most likely pour hours and hours into it, but after that you can't really do much after the story has been completed.

Pros:
-Decent Storyline
-Good graphics and cut scenes

Cons:
-Easy to play
-Lots of driving
-No variable in guns

I picked this game up when they had the december deals on video games. The price is still great and I suggest picking this version up because it includes all the downloadable content that you normally would have to purchase separately if you bought the original borderlands. The game itself is challenging and unique. There are tons of weapons to choose from and unique abilities that will appeal to any type of player. If your not into first person shooters though, I would stay away from this one. If your also looking for one that is more realistic then this is not for you. They use a unique artistic style when presenting the game. Its much more cartoonish then I originally thought it would be, but it's rather appealing after a while to have a change in model for first person shooters.

This game is also a great co-op game if your looking to play with friends. Other then that there is no multiplayer available, it would be awesome if they did though!

I picked this game up a while ago because of the ability to just freely kill zombies with unique weapons. Although the game play is interesting, and the story challenging. I couldn't give the game 5 stars because I feel that the controls are not user friendly. I find the controls to be somewhat non-responsive. Either way though, the game is a lot of fun and challenging. The bosses are difficult to beat and if you hate games that time you, this one is all about timing, so beware!

I picked this game up the day it came out and had a marathon playing it. Rockstar seems to be utilizing the same game engine to run L.A Noire with some adjustments to the gameplay. The graphics are amazing and you'll find yourself driving around the town and never really hitting the same parts of town multiple times.

L.A Noire is a genius idea for a game. Being a detective and solving cases creates a very unique game play that has not been created before. This premier title brings about challenging opportunities to jump into the job as a detective and bring justice in the early age Los Angeles background. I find that at times though the game play can get a little monotonous and you find yourself solving similar crimes time after time. I also never ran into a situation where I arrested the wrong person during the crime. You can answer a question wrong, but I was never skewed off the criminals path.

Rockstar throws in mini-missions to spice up the game play. During these mini-missions you are chasing criminals through L.A, involved in a shoot out, or required to arrest a suspect disturbing the peace. The shooting is pretty easy, and I never really found a challenge in any of the mini missions. They add a little spice and distraction from solving the case but nothing spectacular.

Overall I think that this title has a potential to only improve and the overall experience you get from the game validates trying it out! If you have patients and like solving situations and crimes, this is a great game to get. With the long hours of gameplay, it's well worth it.

Gear of War 3 bring all the functionality of the past two games with even better graphics, more blood and a few new changes. The campaign itself has enough twist and turns to have any Gears of War fan enjoying the campaign mode. With the addition of multiple co-op. You can now play with up to four plays through the campaign mode.

The multiplayer has also received a more dedicated server then past Gears of War games making the connections more secure and lag less of an issue while playing online.

The Gears of War team has also also guaranteed new content throughout the year making this game a must have and must keep.

Saints Row 3 picks up the story in an action packed new city and characters. This action packed game may look like another Grand Theft Auto, but boast many unique features and tasks GTA never brought. The campaign itself was easy to follow and allowed you to customize your experience by making certain decisions along the way. Some missions do feel like they drag on, so it's helpful to throw in a few side missions to change up the game play experience.

Saints Row 3 brings about new and exciting weapons as well as some cool upgrades to change up the chaos and destruction your going to be doing around town. Driving both cars and helicopters seem to have been made easier thus long drives and distances don't seem as long as before.

The game does feature a co-op option as well as a survival mode that is unique to the brand. Biggest thing it lacks though is the absence of a multiplayer experience. There is no multiplayer mode that lets you battle against others on Xbox live.

*If you plan on purchasing this game used. Remember that you cannot access the online features of the game without an online pass. Most likely the previous owner used it on his system.

The Battlefield brand has brought all out war in the comfort of your home. Being able to choose from an arsenal of weapons that can level up to unlock some unique attachments makes for a unique experience with every solider class. The addition of vehicles adds for an extra challenge in the game. You can jump into a tank, jet or helicopter and start an all out battle. The vehicles have also been upgraded to take more damage unlike Battlefield 2 where the vehicles could be destroyed with only a few hits. This time around it feels a lot more realistic.

The campaign though is a let down. The story is not that interesting and it is very linear with little challenge or variables. It's pretty much running and shooting and trying to get into the campaign.

The game is really all about the multiplayer experience though. The multiplayer experience consists of 24 people going through various categories such as rush mode which is pretty much like a capture a point to advance mode. Conquest which is like a domination and of course the normal Death match.

Overall, the game is a great multiplayer game that will have you putting a lot of time into the online experience. The campaign is weak, but the multiplayer experience is well worth the purchase.

I got this game a while ago when I was shopping for something else entirely and I just happened to see it on a shelf. It seemed like a good game and I bought it since I likes my Dragonball Z.

First off, this is how a DBZ game should be. You certainly feel like you are in the show. Budokai was cool but the charcters moved very stiffly and slow. The only problem is now you move much too quickly and it's hard to control your guy at times. Also, the amount of characters avaialable to play with(after you've done a quick sweep of story mode that is) is quite large. Super Vegeta is my favorite.

Also there is a rather beefy customization option available. You upgrade your characters with z items. Though it's a bad that you have to upgrade every form of goku, vegeta etc with different items. For example if you give super saiyan goku a +2 attack item then super saiyan goku 3 won't have it. Basically what I'm getting at is if you want to play as a variety of characters then you're gonna need a lot of z items or do a lot of item switching.

The downside which has been mentioned is the controls are somewhat stiff but I still like the attempt to make the game intense like the anime. The game also has it's chokepoints. The single most annoying thing I have done at least recently is surviving two minutes against Kid Buu as Vegeta. It's not Super Battletoads hard but its close. Also, there is not much emphasis or need to engage in fisticuffs. Most fights are won by charging up and letting rip with your special moves as soon as you can. And then not letting them get in close. The only time I fight hand to hand is when the enemy closes in and I have to knock them back. Still, for all it's flaws I love this game. Grab it and enjoy wailing on people as Goku/Vegeta Super Saiyan 4

I have had this game for awhile now. It's really the only mmorpg I have played so I can't compare it to any others. I must say this is one of the best rpgs I have played. It has problems which I will go into later but all in all it is the best game I have played in recent memory. The world is large and fun to explore. The dungeons you can explore have a wide variety of challenges. There are a lot of ways to customize your character from the skills they learn to the proffesions they develop. It is very easy fun to play since there are a lot of cool items to find and use. Sure, people complain and say that it is addictive like it's heroin or something but that just means it's a good game. If it sucked no one would play it unless they really did stick drugs in the game. It's not Blizzard's fault if you have no self restraint and can't say no to a video game and let it ruin your life. If you set aside time to do other things then you won't become a shut in that plays this game constantly with no life. Still, people are right to say this game is addictive but really there are worse addictions to have. If I had kids I would rather they played this game and maybe make a few friends online (granted, that's asking a lot) than go out and smoke crack or something.

That being said all the good gear requires you spend hours upon hours of play time to acquire. Although I can't say I like this I think it makes sense. Otherwise when you logged in everyone and their grandma (well, maybe not their grandma) would have fancy elite epic gear. That would just suck. You gotta pay the time to get the results. If you don't like it play a less tedious game. So in summary, if you have a life you'll probably never get the best gear but you don't have to have the best gear to play the game and have fun. You can always PVP, explore undiscovered territory (there are a few easter eggs to be found in this game) and other activities

Now let's deal with some of my complaints, first off, in regards to equipment once you start playing you will quickly learn that the auction house is the place to get good equipment. I remember fondly, sort of, the days I actually saved up money to buy stuff from the various item vendors only to see that the stuff on the auction house was much, much better and also in many ways cheaper. I'm not sure why they even have weapon vendors in this game, no one buys from them except people who don't know any better. I'd like to see vendors at least sell decent gear. Anyway, the auction house is key but people sell stuff on the auction house for way more than it's actually worth. The good stuff anyway. The only way to afford it is to buy gold off the internet or get higherlevel characters to buy said items for you. If you have a higher level character buy an item with his accumulated wealth and send it to a lower level character that you play that is what is known as 'twinking'. Basically, what it means is that first time players will have a hard time competing with people who have played for a while. They can never afford the best gear. Once you start to get towards the higher levels it gets better but there will always be some item on the AH you can't get. The cloudkeeper legplates and the skullflame shield are two examples.

Although leveling your charcter and questing is fun during the early levels once you hit the level limit it becomes a lot harder to just hit up a dungeon and get some nice loot you can work all the lower level dungeons with "pick up groups" which means you hook up with random people for a specific goal. Well, try finding 39 other people to go with you somewhere. Um, it ain't happening. I'm not even sure why the designers thought a 40 man dungeon would be fun. Way too many egos and personalities to mangage. Furthermore, IMO having 40 people in a group takes a bit away from the whole sort of intimacy that you usually associate with sword and sorcery dungeon crawl games. I've never read a fantasy novel or seen a movie where "forty heros rose up to slay the mighty dragon whatever it's called" Frodo didn't need 40 people to destroy the one ring, sheesh. It's hard to feel tough even once you hit the level cap because there will always be someone tougher than you, never mind the almost godlike npcs you interact with on a regular basis. I always find it funny when an npc gives you a quest to kill some lame thing and usually my response is "why don't you friggin' do it? You're a level 63 elite with ten times more hit points and better gear than me." Arrgh, my Morrowind charcter was an unkillable machine, my charcter in this game gets owned by random blacksmith's in alterac valley. Granted, I'm sure this a problem with all MMORPGS but as I mentioned before this is the only one I've played.

Getting back to pick up groups even if you mangage to get a group together then you probably won't do well since 40 man dungeons are very hard. You can't just 'wing it'. Every boss fight is very tough and requires knowledge of the boss and in many cases third party software, the acquiring of which is almost a prerequisite. This leads to an experience that can be summed up as...not fun. IMO of course. Thus comes the need to be in a good guild with people that have run the hard runs and know what they are doing. But all the really good guilds are hard to get into.(Or so I've heard, I don't obsess like some people about belonging to an elite guild since I don't need to have the best gear in the game to have fun) I've heard about how people have to fill out applications to join guilds. Sheesh. I don't filling out applications when it's required to have a job and not be broke why would I want to do it in a friggin' game. That means if you don't belong to a top guild you will either have to find ways to entertain yourself that don't involve raiding dungeons with large masses of people or make a new charcter so you can have your level 60 spoil him with gold (been there done that) This makes getting the best gear hard. True, as I noted earlier you don't want everyone in the game to have the best gear and make it less special but still, if you don't have a good guild backing you it doesn't matter how much you play or how bad you want it you ain't gettin' it.

Your only option in this case is to enter the PVP system where you fight other players for honor and hope to advance in the ranks. Once you reach a very high rank you get rewarded with good gear. Although, as other reviews pointed out it isn't quite as good as 40 man loot but if that's your only option... It takes long hours spent farming honor. I know I've done my time. I was ranking up fairly smoothly until I hit rank 9 and then the proverbial door got slammed in my face. Oh, well, once again if you really want something bad enough you'll put in the time. The only thing I don't like is that if you don't PVP for awhile your rank will go down. This sucks, because it means once you start PVPing you have to keep going or you risk losing all your progress and starting from scratch. This develops a very tedious grinding process that makes it more of a job than a fun game. I heard they will be fixing that in the expansion though, which I am hopeful for as I'm tired of Alterac Valley.

Anywho, although I've given a much longer list of cons than pros concerning this game I still have to say that I love it. Every day I wake up and see the fugly face of my dwarf it makes me want to play. I like hanging with my homies in the lower level dungeons and playing one of my many lower level characters. Sure, I would like to have all the best gear in the game and am frustrated that I can't get in a Molten core run to save my life but I still have fun with this game. Having real life friends play this game with you helps I guess. Let me put it this way, if your playing this game just to get cool gear then you may or may not enjoy your gaming experience. But if you can make friends or bring pals with you then the game becomes a lot more enjoyable.

Have fun, and always remember, it's just a game.
