It's been a while since I've finished Legend of the Crystal Skull, but whenever I hear about the series, this game always comes to mind. Rather it's the fact that this is one of the only games in the Nancy Drew series that actually involve being in a morbid place such as a cemetery, or the fact that the central plot of the game revolves around a murder, this game is probably the only game in the Nancy Drew series that comes close to solving a murder mystery. And it's really, really fun!

Plot:
Throughout Legend of the Crystal Skull, Nancy is basically going to visit a guy's house because Ned requests that she should check up on him after the death of his grandfather, I believe. Right from the beginning of the game, Nancy is greeted by a monster, something that not many Nancy Drew games usually have at the beginning (or at all for that matter) in their games. Nancy faints and soon finds herself succumbing to the house's eccentric owners, walking through endless intertwining paths of cemeteries, discovering mysterious eyeballs, and even encountering a rather keen lizard. The central plot of the game essentially revolves around Nancy's desire to find out who exactly was the monster that she encountered, which eventually leads her to the discovery of the existence of the Crystal Skull, a mysterious artifact that can give the individual who has it in their possession immortality...except if the individual was murdered. Nancy soon realizes that the monster she encountered may have some connection to the skull and the mystery begins...Overall, the central plot of the game was very fun and constantly kept me interested as I played.

Gameplay:
The puzzles in the game weren't too difficult, yet not too easy either. I did really like how each of the puzzles in the game were all different in their own way and each had a different approach to actually solving the puzzle. Nancy also has the ability to call Bess and switch characters, but there really wasn't too much gameplay involved on Bess's part, which turned out to be disappointing. I also didn't like how the game doesn't really involve too many puzzles that involve manipulating characters or utilizing a character to complete a puzzle. Most adventure games nowadays involve characters having to manipulate characters in certain ways to solve puzzles, which I find very creative. (For example: Monkey Island and Agatha Christine games.) While these gameplay issues can be annoying, the gameplay was still solid nonetheless.

Music:
The Soundtrack in Legend of the Crystal Skull was on par with the Nancy Drew game series. My favorite song would probably have to be the one that plays when Nancy walks through the cemetery. To be honest, this song should really be the trademark of the game, it's that good. The songs in this game made the tone and overall feel somewhat somber and yet mysterious, especially when playing as Nancy. When playing as Bess, the soundtrack became whimsical and relaxing which was fine, but some of the songs didn't feel like they belonged in a game that supposed to be about a mystery, not a vacation to New Orleans. In conclusion, the music was good and really set the suspenseful tone for the game.

Conclusion:
A lot of the Nancy Drew games that come out usually don't have too many changes except for a change in scenery, new puzzles and items, or characters. Never are there any changes in gameplay or graphics, which I found to be a disappointment. The graphics were very nice and definitely portrayed the suspenseful and spooky theme to the series, but everything always feels the same. HeR needs to incorporate new gameplay mechanics to the series.
Overall, Legend of the Crystal Skull was a really, really fun game that had plenty of good fun solving puzzles, exploring many mysterious locations, eccentric suspects that were memorable, and a conclusion that will make you coming back for more long after the game is completed.

HOTEL by Cateia Games is a fun and interesting mystery adventure, but nowhere near the quality of a legitimate Nancy Drew or Monkey Island adventure game. The game itself has a good plot as well as some interesting puzzles, but the overall length of the game as well as some silly plot points really bring the game down on my scale of a good quality adventure game.

Plot:
The plot of HOTEL centers around anything but an actual hotel. Players assume the role of Bridget Brightstone, a detective who has an uncanny resemblance to Laura Croft. While you won't see any action like that of Tomb Raider, HOTEL does provide you with a semi interesting plot at the beginning of the game.
Before your arrival, one of the guests at the hotel has been robbed of a necklace. Shortly after the robbery, she falls into a coma. Brightstone's job is to find out what happened to the guest's necklace and figure out who the culprit is.
At the hotel, Brightstone will get to interact with many different characters; however, the lack of any real character progression as the story continues really hinders the game's plot.
At the beginning of the game, players are introduced to a cinematic cut scene of Bridget getting the case assigned to her while she is on vacation. We get to hear her voice as well as many interesting sound effects. All of that soon goes to nothing when the gameplay actually begins. No more character voices; instead we get to click through on screen dialogue and read through them. While this isn't necessarily a bad thing, it really does take the depth from plot away and players feel like they're reading a book more than anything else.
While the first half of the game seems promising, HOTEL then changes into this completely off-the-wall story line that really makes players question what happened to the original plot in the first place. With supernatural figures, ghostly dreams, and ultimately a centuries old ritual, HOTEL's plot runs a muck and things go from bad to worse very quickly.
A lot of the characters in the game seemed very pointless and extremely random. They held no real link to the story line, and the game would've been better off without them.
Overall, the plot of HOTEL was interesting to say at least, but once you finish the game, don't expect to be coming back another time.

Gameplay:
The gameplay of HOTEL is in 3rd person, which means that if you're a fan of games like Monkey Island, this is definitely for you. While the quality of HOTEL is no where near as good as Monkey Island, the game does have similar gameplay qualities. Players will guide Brightstone throughout the hotel by clicking on various area hot spots.
HOTEL's puzzles are somewhat of a mixed bag. Some of them are very obvious and others have no solution except to tinker with them until they are solved. For the most part, a lot of the game's puzzles honestly had no explanation and it seems like they were just put into the game to increase gameplay time.
Talking with characters in the game is also a massive bore. Characters will often at times talk for ages. While that can be good, this game implements it in the most boring way possible. Unlike Monkey Island or Nancy Drew, players converse with characters by simply pressing continue and reading through linear dialogue trees. The dialogue can get very repetitive and often at times very confusing.
Throughout the game, the player never really gets this sense of a "mystery". The player simply travels from location to location, trying to find as many items as they can, talking from character to character, and ultimately finish the game with no emotional ties to the game whatsoever.

Graphics:
While I'm not one to say that amazing graphics make or break a game, they do add to the game play immensely. HOTEL's locations were very beautiful and interesting to see. However, a lot of the locations didn't really have any animations in them. Outside trees or clouds didn't move, doors didn't open or close, even puzzles seemed very clunky and created lazily.
The characters in the game looked very robotic in their movements, which really made the realism very poor. Every action that Bridget did with an item looked poor and often at times strange. All in all, while the in-game characters were slightly designed well, they could have been better.

Soundtrack:
Overall, the soundtrack of the game is decent, to say at most. The music is very dry and often at times boring to listen to. The sound effects in the game sound like they came from a stock version of Microsoft Office, and they really serve no purpose to the realism of the game. The game also lacks character voice overs, which really hindered the realism of the game as well.

Overall:
HOTEL is an adventure game with a decent story line, although it could have been so much better. It's disappointing too, I really wanted to like this game. Ultimately, I would give this game a skip.

When it comes to Nancy Drew games, I have played them all. Starting with Secrets Can Kill, I have solved every puzzle, exhausted every conversation blurb between characters, called all phone friends, and even beat the games more than once. I guess you can call me a Nancy Drew Veteran (Or crazed fanatic, take your pick.) When I finished "Tomb of the Lost Queen" last year, I had mixed feelings on the game overall. The plot felt rushed and the characters weren't developed enough. Something was missing.

When I saw the Teaser for the Deadly Device, I have to admit, I was a little skeptical. After all, science and I don't really mix too well. When the game finally came out, I pushed that thought aside and bought it. What I got, was not what I expected...but better. Better than the fan favorite, Curse of Blackmoor Manor? That's for you to decide. In my opinion, Deadly Device comes pretty close.

If you are looking for a Nancy Drew adventure that truly imitates the style of what made the original games enjoyable, then your search is over. With Deadly Device, I felt like I wasn't playing a Nancy Drew game at all. For the last decade, HeR has shifted their game's audience to a younger generation. In this electrifying 27th installment of the series; however, they are calling back their veteran fans, listening to our requests and removing the childish mini-games and monotonous chores. This welcoming return of the classic Nancy Drew that we all know and love comes across as very nostalgic and refreshing.

Another thing that I liked about the game was that HeR focused the mystery solely on the development of the characters. While the classic Nancy Drew games used backstories to carry the plot, Deadly Device lets the historical Tesla references take a back seat. Instead, the game is entirely focused on story driven gameplay. I found each of the suspects to be very unique, mostly because they all had good reason to kill Nico. I found myself suspecting multiple characters, especially when discovering new evidence.

In terms of the gameplay, Deadly Device does not disappoint. Unlike the previous games, Nancy can now combine various items to solve puzzles. While the ratio of table puzzles to item integration ones is still much larger, I did like that HeR is making more use of Nancy's new inventory system.
One of the recurring features in the game is the Day/Night mode. Whenever Nancy wants to explore the various areas of the lab, talk to certain characters, or solve time-related puzzles, she'll have to go to her bedroom and change the time. This in itself did make the game feel less linear and more open to the player's input. In my opinion, I found snooping at night to be much more scary than in the morning.
The soundtrack in Deadly Device was also very memorable. I liked the Research and Discovery themes since they made the tone of the game less disturbing and more cheerful in such a grim location. The Danger Themes were also very well made and never ceased to scare me.

So why did the game not receive a full "5 star" rating? Like anything, nothing is perfect. There was a few things that I still didn't understand...
At the beginning of the game, your boss tells you that power outages happen very frequently throughout the lab. This only happened in the game once. Why include that tidbit of information if it doesn't affect the storyline whatsoever? In my opinion, it would've been best taken out.
Throughout the game, Nancy keeps a box of evidence that contain key items from her investigation. While this was a cool idea, Nancy doesn't do anything with it. Why not bring it back to her bedroom and make suspect board out of it like in Alibi in Ashes? Nope, it just sits there, collecting digital dust in your inventory.
Another issue was the game's achievement system. After solving the case, it shows me all the possible achievements that I could have won. Why show me the achievements after I beat the game? It would make more sense if the achievements were accessible at the main menu, that way players know what to do and look for them as they play. I know this may seem like an afterthought, but HeR should definitely reconsider this feature if they plan to keep using it.

Overall, Deadly Device was definitely a fun Nancy Drew game to play. The characters were definitely more developed than they were in Tomb of the Lost Queen. The plot in Deadly Device was also much more engaging as it was scary. I would definitely recommend this game to any Nancy Drew fan or adventure gamer looking for a good challenge.

Before everyone goes crazy for my score, let me establish some fine points...

1) I've been a SimCity fan since its SNES days. I have played many iterations of the game, from SimCity 4 to Societies, and even Simcity for DS and iPhone.

2) A lot of people are giving the game a bad review only because of the online DRM and server issues, while failing to mention what the game is like WHEN IT WORKS.

3) And this is what I'm writing about, what kind of experience you'll get when the game is working properly.

4) I'm surpised that a lot of people are complaining about this single player online issue. It makes me question where these people were when games like Farmville, SimsFreePlay, and many others were around, secretly puttng their foot in the door to your wallet. The so called gaming genre, "Freemium" has ultimately paved way to consoles and computers, and at the end of the day, it's our own fault for promoting these wallet snatching thieves. Another thing, we also play games like Minecraft, WoW, and Guild Wars and don't complain. It should NOT come as a surprise that EA is making this game online. (Note, I'm fully aware of the antipiracy measures as well...)
Now that all those points are aside, let me start off with the fact that SimCity is not a bad game. The user interface and controls are all very intricately designed and intuitive for even the most basic gamer to use. The graphical art of the buildings are very well animated, from "plopping" them down on the ground to watching as sims walk into them. The game even has a "Tropico" esque feel to it, allowing players to click on sims and view their daily lives.

In terms of City Building, I find it pretty fun to be able to draw roads and make all kinds of wacky designs. From curvy cul de sacs to winding paths, I found it very natural and unique. I also liked the fact that people could "upgrade" their various schools, hospitals, and even parks by dragging new additions to them. Need more classrooms? Let me just plop some down for you. Want a larger park? Let me just add a gazebo and a fishing pond. In terms of zoning areas, I also liked that it is much simpler this time around. Instead of being confused about which zones to add first, it's as easy as choosing one of three types and then watching them as they upgrade themselves. In order to place buildings, players are required to have them be adjacent to a street, which I found only natural, given that the streets also automatically give power, sewage, and all other background services to the player.

Which leads to my next point. In the other SimCity games, players had to look at graphs and stock charts of all kinds of information, which just left me scratching my head in confusion. Whenever players want to view land values, power supply range, or anything else, the city goes into this white dimension mode, coloring all the important information and giving your 3D virtual bar graphs on top of various buildings, land, etc. This in itself allows you to "visualize" your graphs and charts instead. Very easy, not confusing, and simple.

A lot of people are complaining about the game's city sizes being too small. Before coming into the game, I had the impression that the city sizes would be terrible. They aren't that bad. If you manage your roads right, you could easily make your city a metropolis. Not to mention the fact that players can also "claim" more regions around the area, which don't increase your city size, but they do give you more freedom to disperse your creativity to multiple locations. I also like the fact that players can also get help from friends by claiming regions near it and give each other money, resources, services, etc.

And might I add, the soundtrack to this game is simply put, amazing to listen to. Do a search on the game's theme song, it honestly makes you want to build something after listening to it. For that, I applaud the musicians for their hard work.

I know that many people have been complaining about Origin's issues, but I'm going to disagree. Origin is basically a simple version of Xbox Live with chat, game libraries, and stats. While I'm fully aware of the fact that people are complaining about adding another game streaming service to their collection (i.e Steam), it's not that bad people.

While I'm NOT advocating that SimCity is a great game, it needs work. Just like anything. Nothing is perfect. Keep in mind that we need internet for pretty much anything nowadays. If the internet was down, we wouldn't be able to write such bad reviews for this game. Like I said, SimCity 5 is not "bad" by any means, EA just needs to reform and pick up from this mess. This game has the potential to be good, especially when it works. For now though, I would recommend getting the game ONLY when the server issues get fixed.

When it comes to Nancy Drew games, I have played them all. My adventures have led me to solve tough puzzles, interrogate suspects, and catch some devious criminals. I guess you can call me a Nancy Drew Veteran.
When I finished "The Deadly Device" several months ago, I was very satisfied with the mystery. All the core gameplay elements from the classic ND games that we all know and love were there. No more tedious mini games and chores! The Nancy Drew franchise has taken a turn to an older, more mature audience, and it is most certainly the case for Ghost of Thornton Hall.

Nancy Drew's 28th mystery takes her to the Thornton Hall Residence on Blackrock Island, where Jessalyn Thornton, the youngest member of the Thornton family, has inexplicably gone missing! Left with only Jessalyn's dead cellphone, a group of wacky family members, and a malevolent ghost on the loose, Nancy must try to keep her sanity in-check, or risk having a mental breakdown from all the house's scares and dangerous traps. I'm not joking either. Thornton Hall is literally filled with one dead end trap after the next. This is Nancy's most morbid case yet. As many have mentioned, the game does revolve around solving two mysteries: finding out the truth behind Jessalyn's disappearance, and bringing to justice Charlotte Thornton's death, which happened a decade prior to Jessalyn's disappearance.

I must applaud the animator's work, the graphics in this game were simply put, amazing. From all the interactive environments, to the emotional cutscenes, and even the characters themselves, one could tell that a lot of work was put into each individual deatil. While the outside of Thornton Hall is eerily spooky, the inside is just plain breathtaking. The Thornton cemetery was also an interesting place to explore, filled with ominous fog and one archaic crypt.

When it comes to the plot, the historical Civil War references took a back seat and HeR focused the core gameplay on the development of the characters. What made the game so intriguing; however, was the fact that each of the characters were all hiding a dark secret surrounding the night of Charlotte's death. I'm not going to spoil anything, but it is very rewarding to interrogate the Thornton family and feel so captivated by how believable and dramatic they are. The plot and role development really shines through in this installment. Overall, I found the plot to be very smooth. Everything transitioned perfectly well and nothing seemed out of place or just thrown into the game to make it longer. While I would have liked more places to explore inside the Hall, (after all, the outside of the place is huge!) or even around the island, HeR did a good job on tying up loose ends and justifying why the Hall was so small.

The soundtrack in GTH was also very memorable. (as is the case for all the Nancy Drew games) I particularly liked the songs played inside Thornton Hall. The outside songs were good too, but I sometimes felt that I could not hear them enough. The ambiance of the game overall fit the soundtrack perfectly though, and I wouldn't expect anything less from a Nancy Drew game.

HeR Interactive has also added plenty of new features to the game as well:
+Reformed Achievements System. Players can now track their achievements in the game whenever they want! Whenever you earn an achievement trophy, you even get subtly notified about it as well.
+Fast Forward. Ah, the feature that we've all been waiting for. Players now have the ability to fast forward entire conversations with suspects. So if you've played the game already, or you're faster at reading than listening, you no longer have to wait long periods of time for the characters to finish talking.
+Plot Adjustments to Choices. I don't want to spoil anything, but this game takes your choices seriously. This player input ultimately affects the overall ending of the game as well. Yup, you've heard me, this game has multiple endings.

Honestly, there wasn't too many gripes that I had in GTH:
-Deadly Device had a phone app called YRChat, which was similar to a video conference calling. I wish HeR could've done the same and had Nancy do YRChat with Bess and Ned, or Addison. I'm not taking a point off for this, but it would've been nice.
-While the inside of the Hall was beautiful, some of the places were a little too dark for me. Literally. I understand the game was trying to be scary. It was just a pain to make sure that my laptop was running on its highest brightness to play.
-Some of the suspects were a little too forgoing with their secrets. HeR should make the interrogating a little more choice based. If the player makes a mistake, why not just play the "You made a fatal error" screen and try again?

Fire so red, night so black, dear sweet Charlotte, please come back...Ghost of Thornton Hall will not disappoint. If you loved Deadly Device from Nancy's last episode, you will most definitely love this one.

I'm going to start out by saying that I'm a HUGE Nancy Drew game fan. I've played all the games in the series more than once. I stream them on Twitch. I'm what you might call a "Nancy Drew Veteran" with all the times I've played these games. I'm going to start out by saying that I can understand the negative reviews and critiques with this game. I would like to address these critiques now before going into my full review.
There is a character in this game named Sonny Joon. Sonny is a character that has been around since Nancy Drew: Secret of the Scarlet Hand, dating back to the early 2000's Nancy Drew games. Wherever Nancy goes, she always seems to "just miss" Sonny. Which is both sad and intriguing and because we, as the Nancy Drew Clue Crew, are always wondering, "who is this Sonny Joon!?" Nancy Drew: The Shattered Medallion, gives us the opportunity to FINALLY meet Sonny Joon in the flesh.
I bet you're wondering, "Now that we get to meet him, what's the big idea? Why is this game negatively reviewed?" While I can't speak for ALL the Nancy Drew game fans out there, I think the biggest critique with Sonny's involvement was the following: a lack of acknowledging past experiences between Nancy and Sonny resulting in no closure, Sonny's character model looking vastly different from the cover art of the game, and finally the overall mystery being on a game show set in New Zealand wasn't exactly a "choice destination" for players and fans to meet Sonny.
I'll start with the first of the critiques. Yes, it was disappointing that we didn't get any amount of closure between Nancy and Sonny. Sonny's been referenced in a A LOT of Nancy Drew games, and for HeR Interactive to not include any kind of conversation between them, addressing any of the past games was a HUGE disappointment. The only reason as to why HeR may have not done this was to avoid spoilers from past games, but even then wouldn't it be free advertising for players to go back and play/buy those games? The lack of conversation or any sort of heart to heart with Sonny and Nancy felt anti-climatic, and it's sad we never got the chance to see it done here. Without spoiling too much of the game, I'm suspicious that HeR Interactive's story team may have done this on purpose in an attempt to bring Sonny back in a future game. After all, there isn't any Nancy Drew games that solely revolve around an "alien" theme. I digress.
On to the second point: Sonny's character model. This kind of feels like a chicken and egg scenario. Which came first? The cover art or the in-game 3D model? Both characterizations look completely different, and a lot of fans noticed. For example, cover art Sonny has a wild aurora borealis hair style, and in game it looks like he got a haircut. For being on this game's FRONT COVER and making Sonny the focal point of the game, it's disappointing that they didn't spend more time perfecting Sonny's 3D model. A lot of fans were disappointed by this oversight and it's apparent here.
Finally, the last critique, the game's environment. Before this game came out, HeR ran a contest to let a Nancy Drew fan "pick" the next destination for THIS game. The fan picked New Zealand from a list, and that's why we have this Nancy Drew game environment. This is one of those things that I think HeR probably shouldn't have let a fan pick. Don't get me wrong, community involvement is great, but a lot of these in-game environments look like they could be potentially anywhere. What makes this place look like New Zealand? Sure there might be sheep and native flowers, but there isn't exactly anything else that indicates this game's environment. I think this disjointed environment came across to a lot of fans and players, and I think a lot of people struggled with it. I agree as well. One of the problems with International Nancy Drew mysteries is being able to capture the environment that Nancy is in, and in this case, it just seems like any other great outdoors place in the world when this game could've just taken place somewhere more realistic or less expectations on trying to capture the essence of New Zealand and moreso the "reality show".
Now that we've talked about those three, glaring critiques, let's move on to my review.
I'm going to start by saying that I thoroughly enjoyed the Shattered Medallion and that I think this would be a great game for "Beginner" Nancy Drew fans. The story is paced quickly, the puzzles are easier for a Nancy Drew title, and a new Nancy Drew fan might find the story exciting and fun, and perhaps entice them to purchase all other Sonny Joon games.
What makes Nancy Drew: The Shattered Medallion a "good" Nancy Drew game is that coming from the previous game, Nancy Drew: The Silent Spy, Nancy, timeline wise, is probably exhausted from her emotional journey trying to fight an evil organization bend on taking over the world. I feel like HeR Interactive wanted to pick a game and storyline that wasn't as "intense" and decided that this reality TV show mystery would be a great way to bring back the humor and positive charm of Nancy Drew titles. And I can't blame them, Nancy Drew: The Silent Spy is a masterpiece and also one of the most emotional Nancy Drew games in the entire series. Switching over to Shattered Medallion may seem like a confusing turn of events for Nancy , but in my opinion, it was much needed. The puzzles in Shattered Medallion range from tile placement and picture difference finding, to word searches and scavenger hunts. I personally enjoyed these puzzles. They fit the "game show" format very well, and I think they are effective in keeping the game's pace consistent.
The Story of this game is on the lighter side. We don't have any greater evil organizations here. Sonny Joon's involvement in this game is important, and while I won't spoil anything, I will say that HeR Interactive did do an amazing job at pacing this game well. I genuinely feel like the "game show" format was fantastic. Nancy going around asking other contestants about their lives, deeply personal questions actually felt appropriate this time around. I imagine producers of the show being so happy to have casted "a detective" because of Nancy's barrage of non-stop questioning to each of the contestants. It was really cool getting the opportunity to be in the mind frame of both a contestant on the show AND a detective trying to find out what or who could be the show's saboteur. Nancy's friends, Bess and George also make an appearance in the game, and their involvement is well needed. George serves more as a plot device, while Bess is on the humor side of things. I'm happy that HeR was able to include both characters in this game, and it helped not only carry the story, but gives fans the opportunity to spend time with Nancy's friends in-person rather than phone friends. Speaking of phone friends, including Jamila from Nancy Drew: Tomb of the Lost Queen was a welcoming surprise and I'm glad we got the chance to talk to her in this game. It helped the story a lot and if we aren't going to get any sort of conversation with Sonny about past cases, being able to contact Jamila was an emotional experience and very welcoming. I always love it when we find out what happens to past Nancy Drew characters, and HeR did a great job with letting us hear from Jamila again.
Without spoiling the game, I will also address this game's ending and miscellaneous points. The ending was on par with other Nancy Drew titles in the series. HeR Interactive sometimes has a tendency to go in directions of "the fantastical" to tell a story (I'm looking at you, Haunting of Castle Malloy), but it was well deserved here and if HeR ever decides to make an aliens themed Nancy Drew mystery, I hope that writers will reference this Nancy Drew game.
Overall, if this is your first time into the Nancy Drew series, Shattered Medallion is a great place to start. It's funny, the pacing is spot on, and the game show format is great.

I want to start my review by saying that this is my first Kirby game that I have seen to completion. Besides playing as Kirby sometimes in Super Smash Bros, I've always considered him to be more of a Nintendo character geared for younger audiences. Therefore I never gave the game series much attention.

When Nintendo announced Kirby Team Clash Deluxe for Nintendo 3DS as a Free To Play title, I had a blast with the game! I fell in love with the flow of Kirby's moves, his ability to fly when missing platforms, and ultimately his amazing copy abilities. Without hesitation, I knew that I had to give Planet Robobot a try.

The story in Kirby Planet Robobot is on par with what I'd expect from a Nintendo game. World is peaceful -- some strange and evil force attacks the world -- world is in chaos -- hero saves the day. In this case, planet Pop Star, Kirby's home planet, has been taken over by aliens. All of the planet's regions have been infested with alien robots, trying to mechanize the planet. It's up to Kirby to travel to each of planet Pop Star's locales, taking out the mother ship's hold on the planet, one leg at a time. About halfway into the game, the story will pick up, introducing the villains and why they chose planet Pop Star as their destination for domination. If there's one gripe I have about the story of the game, it would be the lack of King Dedede and Metaknight in the main story. It's not until post game that you really get to see what happened to them, which disappointed me - considering how I wanted to learn more about these characters.

If you've played Super Mario 3D Land, then you'll feel right at home with the world map. Players progress through worlds, each world having about 5-6 levels + 1 Boss Level + 1 secret level. Unlocking the boss and secret levels require Kirby to find "Code Cubes" scattered throughout each of the levels (3 cubes per level). Trying to reach the cubes typically involve solving puzzles in the bonus rooms or defeating a tough boss. For the most part, I enjoyed that code cubes had a true purpose to grabbing all of them, and I often found myself re-playing levels to make sure I nabbed them all. (At this point in time, I have 100% of the code cubes in the entire game.) After completing a level, you'll enter a bonus round where Kirby gets fired from a canon towards numbered goal posts in the sky. Depending on how far Kirby gets is based on how much power you give the canon. Unless you're trying to get Kirby to Goal Post #1 rewards consistently, there isn't much of a challenge here, the game rewards you accordingly. One criticism that I have against the world map is how empty it can feel sometimes. At least in Super Mario, we have Toad Houses where Mario can interact with NPC's. There's nothing like that here, no character building between King Dedede, Metaknight, or Bandana Waddle Dee.

Compared to Super Mario 3D Land or Donkey Kong Country Returns, Kirby's Platforming Gameplay mechanics are very different. If it's your first time playing a Kirby game, like it was for me, mastering the controls doesn't take too long. Thankfully, pausing the game allows you to view a reference of Kirby's abilities and how to perform each ability. I found the reference to be especially helpful when using a copy ability that I wasn't familiar with. The game advertises over 27 different copy abilities, each one completely different than the last. I found myself gravitating to the bow and arrow, fire, electric, and telekinesis abilities since I used them to solve more puzzles than not.

Here's a few tips for players that will save you a lot of time:
- Kirby can swallow a mini-boss and copy their ability after beating them, but BEFORE they disappear off screen. (This isn't ever explained in the tutorial but VERY necessary when finding code cubes that require specific abilities to reach them)
- Doors with one orange star on them are considered Bonus Rooms, while doors with three yellow stars on them are considered level progression rooms. If you mess up the puzzle in the bonus room, you can always go exit the room and repeat the puzzle again by going back inside.
- Make sure to thoroughly search a room before moving on to the next, chances are, there's probably a code cube in there.
- EX (Secret Levels) trick you by making you think you're going to find a code cube, only to get a sticker or 1UP instead. Be aware that you'll find yourself annoyed often by the structure of these levels.
- At any time in the game, you can scan amiibos to help give Kirby a special copy ability. Scanning amiibos also gives Kirby health.

Moving on to the Mech Suit. The mech suit allows Kirby to blast his way through a level, solving puzzles, use the suit's copy ability, and transforming into different vehicles. The mech suit by no means makes the game easier; levels in the game are designed to accommodate for the mech suit's skill set and adapt appropriately. That being said, not all levels contain the mech suit, but I found the levels that did contain it to be far more enjoyable than the ones that did not. The mech suit vehicle transformations include a sports car and rocket ship. I found these levels to be very fun and engaging. I honestly feel like the developers of Kirby could easily make an amazing Star Fox game with the game play they have here.

As far as unlockables go, Kirby can collect code cubes and stickers. Stickers are special concept art that can be used to customize your mech suit. There's over 100+ unique stickers in the game with plenty of customization options that you can apply to your mech suit.These stickers are purely cosmetic. Beating the game unlocks two other game modes as well: Meta Knight Time Trial Mode and The Arena. Both modes are fun for post game goodies and beating both of them also unlock an additional "True Arena" mode as well. Other included mini games are Kirby Clash (an RPG-esque game where Kirby chooses a class and fights monsters to level up) and a Kirby Arcade mode where you fight monsters on a grid. The Arcade mode only has three levels, each varying in difficulty. For the most part, you'll probably spend more time on the Kirby Clash.

Overall, Kirby Planet Robobot is definitely not the game I was expecting it to be -- but better! From a challenge standpoint, I would say that Kirby is much, much easier than Super Mario and Donkey Kong, but in a relaxing way. I made my way to through all six worlds and 100% of the code cubes in about a week. I can honestly say that I've enjoyed every moment of the game. The ending even got me a little teary eyed -- no spoilers! This will most certainly not be my last Kirby game. Honestly, I'm tempted to beat the game all over again.

I highly recommend this 3DS game to anyone's library. It's the true epitome of a fully packed game with plenty of content, unlockables and game modes.

I felt compelled to write a review early. I've only thrown 5 hours into Persona 5. This is my first time into the series.

This game will change your life. The best way I can describe it is the high school life you wish you had. Living an honest high school life by day, fighting evil monsters by night.

Persona combines RPG elements with a life simulation. You live in a Tokyo city, you follow a calendar, you have responsibilities, etc. But you also have this secret and adventurous life, saving the world.

I would give the game's battle theme a listen. It's called "Life Will Change". Simply a masterpiece.

I can immediately tell that Persona 5 might be a turn off for some, just because the game has heavy reading sequences and the plot can be slow. Unfortunately it's your loss.

Persona gave me the confidence to jump into my own life challenges, even when I'm afraid.

Thanks for reading!

Not as fun nor interesting as the previous MvC games, but still entertaining. The story mode is mostly cliche and predictable. There is a decent arcade mode with adjustable difficulty levels along with a local vs and player vs comp modes. There is mission/ tutorial and practice modes too. All-in-all, it's a decent game with a slightly above-average entertainment level. Many of the character designs are kinda derpy; Ryu needs a nose job, poor Chun-Li looks like she's had bad plastic surgery, Haggar looks like a roided-out hunch back, and Spiderman has larger-than-life trapezoids. Other characters look decent. Captain Marvel, Gamora, Black Widow, and Monster Hunter are my faves.
Worth picking up on the cheap if you're a fighting game fan.

Standard 3D Sonic fare; nothing mind-blowing. A tad on the easy side even on the more difficult setting. Pretty short (30 stages with some unlockable bonus stages). The create-your-own-avatar feature did nothing for me; they could've left that out and the game would've been a bit better. The graphics are great, there's still unfortunately some screen shimmer and warping along with screen tearing even despite have XBox One X enhanced settings.
All-in-all, a fun little diversion to buy if you get it on the cheap.

Take away all the cynicism, sexiness, intrigue, and creativity from Saint's Row and add in a sleek, futuristic motif, and you get Agents of Mayhem.
It's a decent, good game, but there's nothing especially intriguing about it. I mean, it took me nearly two years to finish the campaign mode. Not because the game's hard- but it's just a hard game to get into. I would play for an hour or so, then lose interest. I went months at a time without playing it. Contrast that with Saint's Row 2 and 3 which I couldn't get enough of, playing through several times within a month's time of purchasing them.
AoM has the usual open world formula; power up, go do main missions, do some side missions, find hidden stuff, buy skills... but beyond that there isn't much more. It's definitely a well-designed game and very pretty to look at. Controls are fine - although driving is a bit dodgy.
With the abundance of AAA games out there, AoM offers nothing special in particular that would turn heads. But if you're in the mood for some pretty good open world shooting action, it'll keep you entertained for a few hours. For the price of $8 that it's currently going for, you can't lose.

Being a MK fan since the 90's, I initially had this preordered since the official announcement. Promptly cancelled the preorder after the publicized hypocritical comments of the developers and early reviews reporting excessive grind, spiking difficulties in tower mode, online-only, and microtransactions. I'll still buy it one of these days, but I'm so glad I cancelled my preorder.
MK 11 is a good game. But it's not $60 good. It's not even $50 or $40 good.
One of my coworkers brought it in to work on Friday, and with it being a slow weekend, I got the chance to play it for several hours. And yeah, it still plays like a MK; it's still fun... but it just seemed like the devs were in try-hard mode going out of their way to virtue-signal their game to the millennial SJW liberal hipsters while beefing up the microtransactions and online connection requirements. I'm not a political person and don't identify as either liberal/ progressive nor republican/ conservative. So lines like "make Outworld great again" comment had me shaking my head. It's not that it bothered me; I just thought it was patronizing and stupid. Pretty much most of the dialogue is lame drivel, where they try to sound oh-so edgy, but just comes across as corny instead.
One of the devs, Steve Beran, came out to announce they were becoming more "mature" and "respectable" in their costume designs for the female Kombatants, because "you're not going to wear a bikini to a fight." And he's right; in the non-video game real world, girls usually are not dressed in swimwear in competitive fighting. I mean, in WWE, many of the females ARE dressed provocatively... but oh, that's not real- it's fantasy... kinda like... video games?? Hmmm... Anyway, looking at MMA female fighters... I don't see any who are cloaked from head to toe with long flowing monk robes like the female MK fighters, so I don't know where Beran is getting his "realistic" fighting clothes argument from. Many of the male Kombatants in 11 are still running around with their shirts off, exposing a lot of skin. But oh well, that's video game gender politics these days for ya.
The good news is the alternate costumes and gear are much better than the defaults... but then that brings in a bit more bad news; the unlock grind. Or, you can just microtransaction your way through. Oh yeah... you will need a constant online connection to get through the Towers mode and utilize the rewards in the Krypt. Nonsense!!
Back to a positive - From a technical standpoint. MK11 is superb. The character models are fantastic and make MKX look like it’s last gen. Faces are wonderfully rendered and animated. Bodies are properly proportioned with smooth motions and gestures. My personal character faves are Jade, Jaqui, and Kitana - stunningly well-done and their move sets are quite enjoyable. The stages are also mostly very detailed and atmospheric, although there were a couple of drab ones.
If this game wasn’t so weighed down with online-only BS, grindiness, microtransactions, and pretentiously puritanical attitudes with regards to the female attire, I would’ve gladly payed full price on day 1 release. As it stands, I’ll eventually pick it up once it drops down to the $30 range.

Dear PDP/ Mars - When you release a new product in the gaming market, you need to make sure you include specific, clear, and accurate instructions so that your customers understand how to use it.
The camera set up was easy and only took a matter of seconds, but the gun calibration was confusing due to incomplete instructions. In both the manual AND the video for the gun calibration, they forget to mention a very important step: you need to be pressing the trigger and rear X button at the same time on the gun before pressing the power/ calibration button. I spent about 45 minutes of frustration troubleshooting and reading through their manual and website before finally finding the answer here from another Amazon reviewer.
So anyway, after the initial frustration subsided, it worked well and I had a great time with the game. It's no House of the Dead nor Time Crisis, but still fairly enjoyable. There is a main story campaign accompanied by several arcade type mini-games. The story gives you several different character archetypes to play as (a few being unlockable). As is quite obvious; this is your typical zombie shooter done in goofy cartoonish style. It runs well for the most part (I played it on XBox One X), but there was still some frame stuttering and slow down here and there. The gun accuracy is excellent.
Personally, I am a sucker for light gun games. So, as cliche as this game is, and despite the initial calibration issue, I would still recommend it for fans of the genre.
I'm hoping this hardware will continue to be supported as I really enjoy light gun games (probably more than the average person). I'd love to see some of the classic light gun series from the 90's and 00's re-released such as House of the Dead series, Time Crisis series, CarnEvil, and Cobra Arcade.

Another great DOA game that still looks and plays well 15 years later, but don't expect anything groundbreaking that necessarily makes it stand out from the other titles in the series.
Each character has their own story mode. Play through the story modes and time attacks to unlock new costumes and characters. You also have tag-team options in all of the non-story modes.
As with other DOA games, you can customize button layout. Only downside is there is no option to set the 'Free' action to RT (which is actually my preference instead of RB). Not a deal-breaker though since you can just press back to block and set RT to throw.
There are understandably fewer costume options and most are not as revealing as DOA 5 costumes.
Visuals are great and the stages are very detailed for a 2005 game. The high detail does cause slight screen tearing in some of the match intros and cut scenes.
It's a fun game to spend a few hours playing through this chapter of the DOA evolution, but it's nothing that will make you switch long term from DOA 5 & 6.

This collection gives you a good handful of amusing games mostly from the 80's. I remember a lot of these games from when I first started going to the arcades in the late 80's/ early 90's. While they are still fun to play and the nostalgia factor is strong, this collection doesn't really offer anything more than what you got on Midway's previous PS2 releases or Mame.
Similar to their arcade collections released on PS2, Midway offers the games themselves with difficulty and controller setting wrapped up with a short, entertaining opening title animation and menu art displaying the arcade cabinets. You can change the controls and map the buttons to your liking. But two games were not very playable no matter what control scheme I set up; 720 and Marble Madness. It's difficult to steer in 720 and the marble goes way too fast in Marble Madness. I was much better at the arcade versions of these games (track ball and twisting directional joystick make a huge different), and even on Mame they are easier to control.
Otherwise, there are some very unique classic games to be enjoyed here; Defender I & II could be described as 2-D open world side-scrolling spaceship shooters where you attempt to eliminate alien invaders who try to abduct humans and use them to supercharge their fighters. Gets to be very challenging. The Joust games are where you mount an ostrich to do battle with other knights flying around on their own ostriches above a lava pit. Games like Robotron, SmashTV, and Total Carnage make great use of the PS3 controller's dual sticks and are chaotic, violent indulgences. Root Beer Tapper is another classic game where you rapid-serve thirsty patrons in order to keep them at bay while trying to catch their empty glasses they slide back to you.
All-in-all, it's a good collection, but only worth it if you don't already have it on PS2 or Mame. If you want to specifically play 720 and Marble Madness, look elsewhere as the controls for these two games on this collection are very poor.

I really wanted to like this game. And at some level I did enjoy it since I've probably played over halfway. But the HUD and on-screen pop up displays continuously intrude on the otherwise awesome graphics and fun gameplay, and there are *no* options to turn them off. You have: count'em, SIX different pieces of data popping up each time you target a prey; the enemy level, name, life bar, outline glow, DNA type, and the reticule. Look at the pics I attached; the catfish and human are completely covered up under a needless barrage of information. I understand that some RPG gamers like and want this type of feature. But there are plenty of us who do not. Which is why there should be an option to turn it on/ off; everybody could be happy.
I know that this game has been endlessly compared/ contrasted to Jaws Unleashed, but seriously, that game did it right, where you could turn your shark senses on and off, and your screen was not constantly flooded with words and enemy levels and life bars.
Jaws Unleashed was also far more gorier and brutal. In Maneater, it's basically chomp chomp and your victim disappears in a cloud of blood. In Jaws Unleashed, you could tear your victims apart, limb by limb, and then leave their dismembered, mutilated corpse floating in the water like chum.
Maneater definitely has pretty graphics and amusing gameplay, but is heavily hindered by all that constant HUD and onscreen label garbage. I don't need 6 pieces of data popping up and a glowing outline every time I target a prey. Seriously, how hard can it be to just make it optional??

We can all admit the last Assassin’s Creed game had a lot of problems.  Fortunately the developers appear to have learned from those mistakes, fixed the technical issues and brought in a really great story.  The graphics look great, clearly they are learning how to better use the next gen systems now.  There are some fun new toys to use in the game (I love the rope launcher).  There is real reason to build up your gang instead of just moving through the game as fast as you want.  Great music as always that helps keep you interested and my favorite part, the story.  Truly this may be my favorite AC story, lots of historical characters to interact with and maybe because it is more recent history it seemed more alive to me.  Occasionally I had trouble falling of edge of missing jumps but that wasn’t that often, plus I am not that good of a gamer.  But overall I have really enjoyed this game.

Rock band is back for the Xbox One.  This product comes with the game disc and one guitar.  The game plays very similar to previous games, with great tutorials to teach you how to play.  It does not get as much into authentic playing as Rock band 4 did.  Also there are no keyboards.  You can buy the drums or a microphone and use them as well.  The old Xbox 360 accessories do not automatically with the game, you need to buy an adapter to use them, but that is cheaper then new guitars.  Another nice function is that the guitars will now automatically calibrate with your tv screen, which helps with lag problems.  You can import songs you have previously purchased as DLC, but not songs form the discs, which kind of stinks.  But on the plus note there is a huge library of DLC songs now.  Overall still a fun game, especially with friends.

The controller is wired, so no need for batteries. This controller works with Xbox One and Windows 10. Cord is plenty long (9 feet) for attaching to system and sitting on couch on other side of the room (At least for most rooms), it also has a breakaway feature, like the old Xbox controllers so you don’t break anything, if someone trips. And I used this with a USB extension cable and it worked for me.

Hair trigger locks on the back along with four additional underside buttons. Built with a standard audio jack that supports all normal Xbox One compatible headsets.
Buttons are all super responsive, never missed a press. There is LED lighting around thumbsticks and middle of controller which can be nice when playing in the dark or distracting, depends on your style of play.

Thumbsticks are a little taller and wider, which I like as I have bigger hands, I think it helps me feel more comfortable with the controller. Very responsive. Overall a great controller and no longer wasting money on batteries.

So this is basically my new favorite controller.  Feels great in the hands with a good grip and find that my hands don’t sweat at all with this controller (Also I have XL sized hands).  The button response is the best of any controller I have yet used, of course it is wired, but even out of the wired controllers I have used, this beats them all.  Very quick pushes and not noisy either.  Great work on the hardware by increasing the responsiveness but not the noise levels.  The programmable buttons on the back of the controller can be a little “clicky/loud” but it isn’t too bad, plus the sound since it is on the backside of the controller is directed away from you so it isn’t disturbing.  Hair trigger settings work great as well I have had no issues at all with my use.  The built in audio is decent but every now and then the controller would freeze unless I disconnected my headset from the controller.  This problem is sporadic and I can’t seem to nail down why it happens, so until then I am just using a wireless headset, no problems with freezing at all.  Others I have seen have complained about button assignment issues, I have had zero issues.  If I do have any I will be sure to update this review with them.  I know people also have complained about the customer service provided by Razer, I have never had to deal with them, and so I can’t speak to their level of care.  I do hope there will be some sort of firmware update to fix the freezing with the headsets, otherwise, I love the controller and use it all the time now.

So think of it this way.  An Xbox 360 controller that you can easily use to play games on your PC, or android tablet/smartphone.  It uses Bluetooth and pairs easily with almost all the devices I use.  If using windows you can actually customize the buttons, if using android you are stuck with the button layout the program decides.  The controller is not heavy, but does not feel cheap.  The buttons feel good, with a nice press to them.  Response time is great.  It does take two AA batteries, but I have gotten plenty of time on them without having to replace.  Overall a great controller with a feel I am used to form all those Xbox 360 sessions.  Highly recommended, just wish you could customize the button layout on android uses.

First things first, the sound on this headset is great. The 60mm drivers in each ear are some of the largest I have ever seen in a headset and it pays off in these. The mids, lows and bass really come through, you feel explosions as well as hear them. My only qualm is I feel it doesn’t pick up the highs very well, but in gaming that isn’t much of an issue.

Other details this is large headset. It fits my extra-large head very well, but if adjusts down easily for smaller heads as well. The ear pads do a great job of noise isolation, and keeping the outside world, outside. It feels comfortable on the head, no real ear sweat issues. Great to wear for those long hours of gaming.

The set is wired and since it puts out so much sound it requires its own power source. So you will need charge a separate inline power source to use this to its fullest potential (Charge via micro-usb). I get about 22 hours of play out of a single charge. The control panel is okay, not my favorite and I don’t quite like the way the buttons feel. The mic can be plugged in, or left unplugged if you don’t need to chat. It gets the job done, it isn’t great, I have used worse, but I have also used a lot better. For the price of this headset you would think they could invest in a better mic that just retracts of even just flips out of the way.

So I have some minor issues, but for sheer volume and bass strength these cannot be beat.

Like many others I have several gaming headsets I have used over the years. Some good, some great, some average, some painfully bad. I tend to like wireless headsets when I am gaming on a console. Mainly that is because the even if I use a wired headset I am typically connecting through my wireless controller anyways.

However, when gaming on my PC I use a wired headset, and out of all the wired headsets I have used this one is by far the best. First, I have a very large head and this set when set to its largest size fits me comfortably. Which is rare when it comes to gaming headsets.

The ear cushions are simply the softest I have ever worn. Like a soft memory foam that contours perfectly to the sides of my head. Great at isolating outside noise and yet it still stays cool and you have no ear sweat. Also, if you wear glasses the cushions have soft spots to allow them to contour around the glasses, so it doesn’t squeeze your head, I like it so that I can use some digital glasses I have that reduce eye strain.

The sound, is freakin’ amazing. In playing games it is clear, crisp and distortion free. You can hear quiet footsteps, and you can hear loud rumbling bass equally well. And then if you just want to listen to music with these bad boys you will be impressed I promise. Everything sounds great with this headphones, form Jazz to Death Metal. I kind of love them for their sound quality.

The microphone is removable and pretty good. Slightly above average if you compare it with others. No complaints but no one ever said it made me sound great. It is fairly flexible, it will stay in place and it is removable.

As far as control for the headset go there really are none. On the cord you have a mic on and off switch and that is it. Any other control you have to do through your hardware, which in the end is fine I guess.

But the sound and fit on these is killer and that is the reason you should get them. Highly recommended.

So can a boutique audio company put out a gaming headset that can compete with the big boys? The answer is yes. LucidSound, I feel really made an effort to make a gaming headset that sounded great, felt great, and you would feel okay wearing around when just listening to music on your phone.
The headset feels great on the head. It fit my XXL head just as comfortably as my nieces. So great job on design. The sound isolation is great, with earpads that are soft and comfortable, but don’t cause you to sweat.
There is an internal battery so just charge it up after using, it comes with a cable just for that. Setup is easy. Overall a really great headset for gaming and other applications.

When this game was announced I wasn't really interested in getting it, unfortunately there have been a few Batman videogames worth getting, in my opinion. As the game developed and the first images and trailers were released, I really got excited by how the game looked and the story Paul Dini himself wrote for this game (for those not familiar with him, he was the producer and writer of 'Batman The Animated Series')

This I am not afraid to say, is the best Batman videogame I've ever played! As a fan of the character (comics, movies, cartons, you name it) I can tell you this game does justice to the Batman universe. The story, though a little flawed at the end, is just great. Many characters from the comics appear, some of them have major roles in the plot and some other have cameos during the game. Some are even hidden as Easter eggs in the form of the Riddler Challenges (you have to solve riddles during the story mode, some of them include looking for Scarface, Catwoman's suit and others, even Ra's al Ghul makes an appearance) All of Batman's skills are used as well as many of his gadgets (which you have to acquire as you progress in the game) While the game has many memorable sequences with Bane and with Scarecrow's fear gas (to name just a couple) some of the boss battles felt as remakes from prior games, they were not bad, on the contrary, but the battle with Poison Ivy seems like a remake of the same battle in the SNES animated series game for example. I just felt I should mention this as additional information, that fact does not demerit the game at all.

The graphics, even in it native 720p look stunning, the environments are detailed and creepy, the music, loosely based on that from the Christopher Nolan films is also a great addition to the game. The voice acting is definitely one of the best things here, as it is voiced by the original actors from the animated series, those familiar with the TV show will remember Kevin Conroy as Batman and Mark Hamill as The Joker.

Replay value? Definitely, many of the trophies and Riddler challenges can be unlocked until you have all the gadgets, so you can definitely return to certain areas to obtain those. Also when completing the game in story mode, you are free to continue and roam in Arkham to complete the Riddler challenges. Which I thought was kind of cool so you don't have to start over again just for that. The challenges also offer a good chance to play specific areas in the game to achieve specific goals.

Exclusives: the 'Play as the Joker' PS3 exclusive is neat, though you can only use the character in challenge modes, it would be neat to play as the Joker in story mode but well, may be next time. The Amazon exclusive comic-book while a nice add on, it is not really an essential piece to the story, it goes back to show some things mentioned briefly during the game but nothing you would regret missing.

If you are into Action/Adventure games this is definitely a must own game. Way better than what I had expected. Now all we need is a sequel!

As a video gamer and a fan of The Beatles, this Rock Band title is one I was eagerly awaiting. After playing it and completing it, it is clear that the game is aimed at fans of The Beatles and potential newcomer Beatle fans that have never played a Rock Band/Guitar Hero game. Important to note, I used a [[ASIN:B001BXACDA Playstation 3 Rock Band 2 Special Edition]] guitar and the [[ASIN:B001ABN82K Guitar Hero World Tour Band Bundle for PlayStation 3]] band kit to play this game and all of them worked ok with no compatibility issues at all.

The cinemas, from the very opening sequence that was published in the web before release date to the final one at 'The End' are just incredible. Well designed, with easter eggs like those in the 'Free as a bird' video, they retell the story of the band, the story mode is divided in levels to play, each accompanied by its respective and nostalgic cinema display, the Cavern, the Ed Sullivan show, the Shea Stadium, the Budokan, all the famous places are here. The final levels in studio are accompanied by psychedelic landscapes each fit to the song being played . Visually the game is stunning, it is so well designed and it has so many details that I found it distracting sometimes, you wish you could stop playing just to be able to watch the band perform in the game.

The track selection is pretty good too, while there are many hits missing in the 45 song track list, the ones that made it into the game are classics and represent a challenge when playing the, for instance, I've heard people complain about 'I me mine' being included, truth is, when playing in hard, it is a real challenge playing the song with the guitar controller (it is so satisfying when you finally master it) The track selection should not be a problem at all for fans of the group. On a side note, the mastered audio for the game sounds way better than the remastered CD versions in my opinion, the quality and clarity is impeccable, it reminded me of the 5.1 mix released with [[ASIN:B000JJS8TM Love (CD + Audio DVD)]], with the difference that the game does include original versions unlike the mixes created for the Cirque Du Soleil show. Additionally, the game includes studio recordings of the band chatting before and after a song is completed, some of those recordings unavailable until today.

The game supports trophies, for those of us gamers who like the challenge of collecting and unlocking items in the games. You also collect photos that you accumulate to obtain hidden tracks or additional videos. The fist downloadable content was released on 10/22, the remaining songs to complete the Abbey Road album, while I found it to be a little pricey for the amount of songs offered (more expensive than buying the actual remastered Abbey road remastered CD), I can't deny it was a pleasure to be able to play the famous Abbey Road medley. Future releases have been announced for the rest of the year, the remaining songs for 'Rubber Soul' and 'Sgt Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band'

The downsides: the difficulty level and the calibration tool included. The difficulty level is incredibly low, the medium difficulty for instance feels like playing in easy using four buttons in other similar games; the only real challenge for me, as a player familiar with this kind of games, was in hard difficulty . I can understand this may have been done as an attention to the newcomers that will play a Rock Band game for the first time, I just thought I'd mention it.
The calibration tool included was a nightmare! I calibrated the game to earn the calibration trophy and ended up messing the game, I tried to recalibrate and every single time I tried the problem was worst; I researched on the web and found a lot of users in the same situation so I don't think it was a user problem. I ended up finding a video with instructions on how to manually calibrate the game, it was more difficult but the end results paid off. I am giving you a heads up in case you do want that trophy, well, be prepared for the consequences.

All in all, a great game and without a doubt, a must for Beatle fans .

The available songs for download are quite varied as well, of course since GH5 was released no more new content for world tour has been released.

The addition of the microphone is great, although the one included is wired, so there's room for enhancement there. I was worried when I received the box from Amazon as it had a note that said "Do not sell before release date", you may already know that the early Guitar and Drum kits for World Tour have known issues not playing well in some cases; well after a month or so of using the guitar, the strum bar would fail making the game unplayable, it was not really a big deal for me as Activision offers warranty after three months of the purchase, they will gladly replace the defective items at no additional cost once you enter your information in their website. You can provide a credit card number and have them ship you a new one immediately, once received you ship back the defective one; or you can also not provide a credit card information, print a shipping label they give you, ship the defective guitar and as son as they receive it they will send you a new one. I did the last and it took no more than 2 weeks for me to get my new guitar.

So last year my wife decided to give me a red Wii as a Christmas present, which was great! I now can play the classic Nintendo games on Wii such as Mario Bros, Legend of Zelda, Metroid, Donkey Kong and all the other Nintendo exclusives.

Being the proud owner of an 80 gig PS3 the first thing that jumped to me was the quality of the graphics, as you may know, the Wii does not include component cables but the average composite cables instead (the yellow, white and red ones) Even when using component cables, the most resolution you can get from a Wii is 480p/480i.

With this in mind I decided to order these cables despite many people saying they would not make a big difference. Well? They do! I am playing on a Sony LCD 55" TV set, so even with the TV calibrated accordingly the color definition was not the best when using composite cables.

After plugging these to the Wii and setting them up accordingly*, the difference was not small but the opposite, the colors and the definition improved in a very notorious way. Again, the pixelation that comes with a 480p resolution is still there but the clarity and color is definitely better with component cables. I can't say much about the sound as I have this plugged directly to the TV (I still need to update my audio receiver to one that accepts HDMI)

I can definitely recommend these if you want to see an improvement in the video quality, but please consider the Wii limitations in regards to HD graphics.

*I happen to have a friend who was telling me these type of cables were not worth it in his experience. Well, he did plug them, but forgot to go to the Wii menu and change the video output from composite to component, which explained why he was seeing no difference.

'The Smurfs 2' published by Ubisoft, is the video game adaptation of the 2013 film 'The Smurfs 2'; as such, the goal of the game is re rescue Smurfette who has been kidnapped (I will not get into further details to avoid spoiling the movie/game)

As you may guess, this is a game that was created to aim for the younger market that will pay to see the film and will buy the DVDs and other merchandising. With that in mind, you can expect a short game, a difficulty level appropriate for kids and a simple (yet kind of repetitive) gameplay. The game is an action-adventure platformer that reminds of the style (but not the quality) of the 'Super Mario Bros.' games. You are able to choose from a selection of Smufs available to play and rescue Smurfette. Part of the adventure consists in gathering Smurfberries while going through 6 different levels to reach your final goal while battling the Naughties, Azrae and Gargamel. The game is quite simple and I believe it does what is intended, kids will spend hours playing it through and will find it entertaining like my kid did. Based on that, I am giving this game 4 stars.

I believe it is a little bit unfair to compare this game to more adult oriented titles out there, again, keeping in mind the target audience I can honestly say the game is good. To me, as an adult (who used to watch the cartoons when I was a kid) the game was really not that good and I even found it repetitive, but I didn't get the game for me. It has really nice visuals and the controls are easy to get used to.

If you also consider the fact that the WiiU version allows your kid to play in the controller I would say this would make a great game for kids. If your kids are not into platformers or like challenging games that will have them spend hours trying to solve puzzles and the like, this game is definitely not for them.

A well made game and spot on its target audience.
