This is a decent game. It captures the W40K lore and atmosphere well, putting you into the boots of a tough Space Marine. The story focuses on an Ork invasion of a planet that has a super-weapon on it that the Imperium of Man is attempting to safeguard. Your character is a captain in the famous Ultramarines charged with thinning out the Ork horde. And what a fun job that is. The combat is bloody and impactful, and you definitely get the sense that your guys are powerful soldiers with firepower to spare. There are a decent array of weapons, though only three melee choices. There is not much in the way of character development, beyond the unfolding story. However, the combat and plot twists do stay interesting enough to warrant finishing the game. The game looks and sounds good, with solid level design and animations.

So, why three stars (really, I would give it 3.5)? The game suffers from a lack of diversity in enemies. There are about 6 varieties of Orks and 2-3 other enemies, and you see those same models over about 20 hours of gameplay. It gets old after a while, even though the kills are good and gruesome. To make it worse, the fights toward the end of the game get longer and more tiring, even though they are against the same group of enemies that you've been slaughtering for hours already. The combat, while entertaining, is simplistic and repetitious. Especially when it comes to melee, you'll find yourself doing the same combos and finishing moves in every fight simply because this heals your character's injuries. Other minor annoyances include the clumsy jump-pack sequences, occasional difficulty spikes, and the checkpoint save-game system.

If you like the W40K universe and/or shooter game, Space Marine is probably worth a try. While I only played the campaign and not multiplayer, the story is okay and the gameplay is polished, though it gets repetitive over time.

+Very kinetic, impactful combat
+Nice graphics, sounds, and other effects
+Story line stays true to W40K lore and universe
+Good array of weapons
+Solid level design and convincing atmosphere
+You get to play a Space Marine

-Lacks diversity of enemies
-Long, tiresome fights toward the end of the game
-Some awkward camera angles during melee combat
-Clumsy jump-pack sequences

This is one of the cheapest turtle beach headsets for the xbox you can get - but surprisingly, it doesn't feel overly cheap and it doesn't sound cheap. This headset only supports two channel analog audio using the RCA plugs - no digital optical option on this budget headset. However, setup for this could not be easier, plug in the usb for power, plug in the rca pass thru plugs and attach the talkback cable to the xbox controller.
Since this is not wireless, the included cord for the rca/usb is very very long - could come in handy if you like to roam around while listening to your xbox audio. I like this headset personally, its a good price and even though it's budget it still seems to be built nice and sturdy.
However, I will say, if you have a young son who wants a turtle beach for his xbox - do not get him this one - he will be disappointed. Boys love the turtle beach Ear Force x12, which is similar and only costs a few bucks more or the x32 which is wireless and can sometimes be picked up pretty cheap on sale. Other gamers will likely find this headset to be more than adequate as long as you don't mind the cord and stereo audio only.

Nintendogs is a cute game that any dog lover could appreciate. Where else can an average person have up to five dogs at once and still live a normal life?

Once you get the hang of it the training for the dogs is a breeze, although I may just be picking the right dogs. The animation is fairly realistic as far as animal games go.

The contest options are also fun. The disc competition is my favorite as it doesn't require you to speak perfectly, like the obedience competition, and the dogs seem to catch on quicker than they do with the agility competitions. Regardless, all three modes can be a fun way to earn more money to pamper your dogs and upgrade your living environment. I'm currently saving up for the most expensive home style.

As you train your dogs, you also earn trainer points which unlock different dog breeds in the kennel. This is also a fun option, leaving you plenty of choices when choosing a new dog.

My only dislike, however, is that Nintendogs runs on real time based on the clock option in your DS, making it a necessity to play every day if you want to keep your dogs happy while continuing to train them. If one's leisure time is limited, this could become an issue. Sometimes you have to neglect your dogs if you want/need to do other things, possibly leading to runaway dogs or who knows what else.

Bully is a pretty fun video game. The playing format is similar to [[ASIN:B00005O0I2 Grand Theft Auto III]] and those after it. Your character is pretty much free-roaming in between missions, there are a certain number of missions until you complete the storyline, there are side missions and collectibles in order to achieve 100% completion, and you have to complete certain missions in order to open new areas of the game.

The main premise is that you play a tough kid named Jimmy Hopkins who has been dumped at Bullworth Academy by his mom and brand new (rich) step-dad while they go on their honeymoon...for a year. While at Bullworth, you quickly discover that there are very divisive cliques throughout the school. You have the jocks, the preps, the nerds, the greasers, and the townies. You just want to get on the good side of all of them and get them all to stop fighting so your school experience goes smoother. All of this while trying to pass your classes and not get kicked out of the school.

This objective is somewhat hard to complete, however, because of sociopathic nut job named Gary. Gary's sole mission is to improve his standing in society and to piss on everybody else. It's his opinion that nobody is smarter than him and nobody is better than him. Everybody is there simply for his amusement, like chess pieces on a playing board.

So your ultimate goal is truly to defeat Gary. Once you defeat Gary and make nice with the leaders of the major cliques, your time at Bullworth is much simpler.

I haven't hit 100% completion yet, but I did complete the storyline at about 76% completion. Now I'm finishing all the bike and go cart races, and I'm trying to find the last of the G&G cards, rubber bands, and lawn gnomes. This can get a little tedious once you've passed all the classes and completed the storyline, so I would suggest getting a walkthrough that lists the locations of collectibles so you can make sure you collect them all in between missions. If you want 100% completion, that's the best way to get it.

I have confirmed that this game is so totally not worth its retail price tag ($49.99 last time I was at Best Buy, I think it might be about $5.00 cheaper on Amazon). I guess I'll start with the negatives because those are easier to remember.

-There are only 30 songs total, as opposed to the previous games' 58 tracks. There are no unlockable tracks that you can buy in the store. You get the set 30 and that's it.
-Way too many obscure songs. I recognized most of the bands, but some of the songs they chose from certain bands are most definitely not their recognizable hits. Even some of the encores (which are supposed to be the super secret awesome songs that everybody knows and loves) were disappointing. Who the heck is Limozeen, anyway?
-While it's great that they got master tracks for The Warrior and I Wanna Rock (two of the better songs on the game), the master tracks on those songs fade out. Live bands don't fade out. It kind of killed my Rock Star mood when I discovered those two songs faded out. Surely they could have managed decent covers of those two songs with creative endings to compensate for the fade-out.
-Speaking of covers, I understand that the original version of Ballroom Blitz by Sweet did not come out in the 80s, but trying to throw in a cover of a crappy cover by freakin' Krokus was lame. They should have just picked a different song.
-The extras are limited. As I said, there are no extra songs to buy in the store. All the guitars you can buy in the store are the same as the guitars you can buy in GH3, as are all the skins for those guitars. The only other thing you can buy in the stores besides guitars and skins is an extra character, the Grim Ripper. There are no extra styles or outfits to buy for the characters. They have one 80s style, and that's it.
-While the playable characters were altered into 80s style clothing and hair, the stock band members were not. They all look the same as the previous GH games.
-The venues are not noticeably different. The only main change I noticed was that the venue that was the Vans Warped Tour in previous games changed to something called Rock for Safety, or something like that.
-The gameplay seems easier, which makes the lower levels somewhat boring. The only song I didn't 5-star on the first try was Seventeen by Winger on Medium, and that was more because I was distracted by something rather than the difficulty of the song. Perhaps Hard will still be difficult enough for me, but the way things have gone so far, I wouldn't be surprised if I actually try to play Expert.
-Lack of songs with female vocalists, which may just be a testament to the state of rock bands in the 80s (or ever). But still, if I'm remembering correctly there were only 3 songs out of the 30 that had female vocalists.

Now for the positives. Yeah, this list will probably be shorter, but the game is still good overall. It's just overpriced.

-It's still fun. It's Guitar Hero. It's addictive and fun, and there is really only one song I dislike enough to only play in order to advance through the levels--Krokus's cover of Ballroom Blitz. I don't mind the other songs at all and would be fine playing them multiple times if I needed to in order to get 5 stars.
-The 80s styles for the characters are pretty fun. I like the Grim Ripper's 3-D glasses. :op

Okay, yeah, definitely a short list. The game is definitely worth playing. It's just not worth buying for $50. I would suggest renting it or if you absolutely must own it, wait until you can find a really cheap used copy.

I haven't read all the reviews, but I'm sure multiple people have mentioned the glitch with melting the ice at the end of year 3 that causes the game to completely freeze. I also have the glitch in which the screen goes blank when using a Time Turner. After using the Time Turner, depending on where my characters walk, the screen goes completely black or it goes to grey fish-eye type screen with no images, just blank. It has also crashed on me a few times for no apparent reason. My system isn't up to date. I run Windows XP, but it should certainly be good enough to run this game on lower graphics settings. Despite these issues, the game is still a lot of fun. It has the same tongue in cheek humor I've come to expect from the Lego games. I actually laughed out loud at the handling of what happened to Cedric Diggory at the end of year 4. I wondered how they would handle such a dark moment in the series. I have yet to go through free play, but as far as playing the story mode goes, this game is a lot of fun, even if it is frustratingly buggy.

I got Uncharted and Uncharted 2 in a PS3 console bundle, and once I finished Uncharted 1, I was so glad I had Uncharted 2 right there because I loved the first game. The second game was even better than the first. I loved the story, the new characters, the return of old characters, all of it. I really liked some of the changes made to game mechanics as well.

Weapons - I liked the expanded variety of weapons. The addition of sniper rifles, sub machine guns, rocket launchers, even crossbows, all with different damage-causing capabilities helped add variety to the shooting experience. I liked the blind firing option as well. Grenades were infinitely easier to use in this game. I never did figure out grenades in the first game.

Stealth/Fighting - Stealth tactics were a great addition to this game. I'm a big fan of the Splinter Cell game series, so adding stealth to this game was right up my alley. Being able to sneak up on enemies from behind to subdue them or to yank or push them over the edge of a cliff or ledge added a different challenge to the game than just working on your aim in a firefight. I also thought the hand to hand combat was well done. It wasn't just button mashing but actually required you to pay attention and put some thought into it. There were a couple times when I just barreled through a group of enemies and relied on hand to hand over shooting because it was faster.

Climbing - The climbing mechanics were also improved. Not only was the climbing more intuitive, it utilized the environment more. There were ropes, bars to swing from, street signs to climb on, giant moving gears to navigate. The creativity behind the way characters interacted with the environment was excellent.

Art - The art and animation was really spectacular. The environments were beautifully rendered, the movements of characters had a realism to them. The depth and texture to everything was spectacular.

Story & Characters - One of the great things about a game series is when the creators are able to keep the old characters and mesh in new ones. I was really glad to see Sully and Elena again, but I also liked the addition of Chloe and the other new characters. I enjoyed the way all the characters played off each other, even when Nate was stuck dealing with the language barrier between his Tibetan guide, Tenzin. The overall story was exciting and kept me wanting to know what would happen next, which is obviously good because it kept me playing.

Overall Gameplay - The difficulty options are Very Easy, Easy, Normal, Hard, and Crushing (which is locked, I'm assuming until you beat the game on Hard). Very Easy gives you assisted aiming. Since I did okay aiming in the first game without this, I played on Easy. It was still fairly challenging. I think my only "gripe" I might have is that the final boss battle actually seemed a little too simple to me. I only died twice and one of those times was because of careless jumping on my part, not because the boss killed me. The rest of the game seemed more challenging in comparison.

Like the first game, I feel this game definitely has strong replay value, and I look forward to playing Uncharted 3. I only wonder how they could possibly improve on the game any further.

This product is a Steam activation key for Rocksmith 2014 and an attached cable. There is a CD that includes software for activating the key over Steam, but it is necessary to use. Unfortunately, the activation key was defective. It seems to be an issue with this particular product, not for everyone, but more than just me. Since I got a review copy from Vine, I did check first to make sure that others who purchased the product were getting activation errors. The Ubisoft forums showed a few reports of this as do other reviews here.

I then contacted Ubisoft. After some runaround, the email response I got was that this is a known issue and to please monitor the forums for an update. My ticket was then closed. I then tried phone support and was told that the key was legit but Ubisoft couldn't determine what it was intended for. I was told to contact Valve to determine what the key was for. I did so and found out the key was in fact defective. I then contacted phone support again and was told that there was nothing they could do as they don't reissue keys. This would've been nice to know up front rather than making me go contact Valve, email them the defective key, etc.

So Ubisoft's customer support is a pain to deal with and not particularly helpful and there appears to be some risk of getting a bad key and having to deal with them. Wish I could've actually played the game as the earlier edition was fun.

EDIT:
Having received an activation key through the help of Ubisoft staff lurking in the Amazon reviews I was able to install and play the game. Off the bat the lack of effort in porting this to PC is quite apparent. The menu system is clearly designed for a controller, with only intermittent mouse support and a clunky UI. While I got sound over my USB headphones, there were clicking artifacts present on any music, even when the guitar cable was unplugged. Trying to resolve the problem led to losing sound altogether and having to switch to motherboard sound and a headphone jack (which worked without artifacts).

The gameplay itself is enjoyable and the ability to change difficulty on the fly or switch into riff master mode is very helpful. Relying on the game to increase difficulty, especially when starting at the bottom level just took way too long. It took me a while to get used to the presentation, maybe due to the way I visualize the fretboard (going up as the pitch goes up). This made figuring out chords on the fly a little tricky. This is cool technology that comes with several caveats.

First among these is that if your eyes are outside the rather limited spacing range you will have visual issues. There is some software adjustment available but it is also limited and a pain to adjust. The headset is a bit of a pain to adjust as well, the cables run through the headband and restrict its movement unless you put some slack into them first. The cable placement also made it difficult to wear over the ear headphones.

The display is high resolution but the optics are not great. The focal range is limited and blurs quickly. The result is that there is a great image but only when looking straight forward. This makes things like navigating pages and menus frustrating. There also was no clear way to control display settings, such as dimming the display or changing the color temperature.

The controllers connected fine and seem responsive. However, there doesn't seem to be a common interface among WMR projects so there was often a lot of guessing as to what each control does or doesn't do. In particular, when using the seated VR mode it was difficult to navigate using the controllers.

The headset is designed for WMR, which is the newest and least mature of the VR formats. There is support for SteamVR but the WMR framework means jumping through some hoops.

Ultimately, as neat as the VR was, my use of this product was limited due to excessive eyestrain caused by spacing mismatch and the optics. For those who match up better with the screen, the experience should be much better. I feel that tech, both hardware and software needs some time to mature. This is still at an enthusiast stage and needs a way to go before it becomes consumer friendly.

I was really impressed with how easy this game was although I have to admit I did watch my niece and nephew play this for the first time last night and they did struggle a little to get the hang of it. I haven't beat this game myself as I dint have much time to play it as an adult. Not only do I feel like doing that makes it more kid friendly but it gives us adult gamers simmering to reminisce on and something new to play in our free time! Way to go, another awesome game!

I think this game was revolutionary for Nintendo. I've been a Nintendo gamer for roughly 18 years now. I've played almost every Mario game there is to play. This was definitely something new. I loved that you could make your own courses, clear them, and post them for other gamers to try to beat. I think it is a great concept, especially because you've got to spend some amount of time playing the game in order to "unlock" different blocks/enemies/items to make new and awesome worlds. I think another feature I LOVED with this game was the Event Courses. Most event courses offer you a small reward after you clear them and that's "skins" for Mario for in Mystery Mushrooms. Basically this allows you to change your character when you hit one of these blocks and get the mushroom inside. This is a super cool feature, ESPECIALLY if you've already unlocked everything else because it gives you something new to do all the time. I absolutely loved this game and think they could definitely make more like it. Would I love to see Zelda in this same game type? Absolutely! I think this concept could really take hold in the gaming community. It's like combining the idea of Minecraft and bringing it to Nintendo in ways we've never seen before. I'm actually pretty knowledgeable when it comes to this game so for anyone having any questions at all please feel free to message me! And enjoy the game. Definitely worth the money you'll spend on it. This game is tons and tons of fun!

Like for example...there are what I call dark matter stars, which make you lose ministars. And if you're the unfortunate one to be next in line to roll after someone got you right next to them you lose stars. I don't know, in ways I just think it's really unfair. Also, I didn't particularly like the way it decides who the winner is. In Mario Party 10 there's regular stars and bonus stars calculated in the end (unless you choose not to have bonus stars). Which makes it pretty easy for even kids to know who is going to win before they even get to the very end. I can't complain much, though. I really did like Mario Party 10 and would buy it again in a heartbeat. All the kids in the family seem to love it and it's something we can all play as a family. Again, kudos to Nintendo for the great games!

I have to admit I was excited to see a new game for the Ar series as it's been a while since the last Ar Tonelico game. I don't like to write long reviews as I think those can kind of defeat the purpose of giving someone a quick overview of the game also my reviews tend to be a bit disorganized and I apologize I just like to talk about items I like in the game instead of talking about sound, graphics, controls, etc.

The game has you taking the role of two separate duos one being the main character of the game who's name is Delta and the other a robot guardian by the name of "Earthes" that is controlled by you the player. Earthes is a character that allows you to interact more with the Ar world as you sometimes get more than one choice of how Earthes responds to the other players which I thought was very unique as some of the responses are humorous. Once you progress in the game you have to "zap" back and forth between Earthes and Delta's parties when you become stuck with one to move the story along. The overall game play is very similar to the other Ar games if you have played them, basically in all the Ar games you have a female character that performs "Song Magic" which is extremely powerful, while she is singing your main characters protect her and deals out physical damage. One difference in battles is they are back to being turn based and now the enemies come in "waves" meaning when you clear out one group of enemies the next wave appears. The better you fight you build up a burst gauge that powers up your song magic allowing you to activate the song and destroy multiple waves of enemies.. getting you a higher battle rank with better bonuses the most I've taken down is about 10 waves so far 3 earning an A rank I've yet to get an S rank yet. The game has plenty of story interaction between the characters as well with of course the return of diving where the main character dives into the heroines' minds to weave stronger song magic. These dives can be a bit unique so be prepared for a bit of a surprise when you start diving if you are new to the series after all you are viewing the innermost secret of a person's heart. The game also has the return of synthesis where you can create powerful items to equip or use in battle which is enjoyable as I like gathering ingredients to make new items which are then available for you to buy and use (those who have played other gust games like the Atelier series will know all about this). There are many other features but I'd rather not spoil everything. To wrap up I'd say the biggest thing about the Ar games that can throw people off is they can tend to be a bit slow when you start them but believe me they do get better the longer you play them so you have to have patience. I haven't played far into the game but have enjoyed it thus far. I do hope this game is received well so we can expect more games in the Ar series. Happy gaming everyone.

I usually don't write very long reviews but I received this game yesterday and have played it around several hours and have enjoyed it. As an intro for those who don't know Dungeon Crawlers are games that allow you to create a party and then explore randomly generated dungeons defeating enemies and gathering new items in the dungeons like weapons, items that you can use, throw, etc, also along with money and materials. You can sell your materials in town and then create new weapons and other items from these materials which I think is a great feature as it makes you work for better stuff. The visuals are very impressive on the game and the AI of your party members are pretty smart, they know when to heal and use abilities depending on how tough and how many monsters you are fighting. The controls are simple to learn and easy to master. In keeping it short if you like Dungeon Crawlers and the Etrian series definitely give this a try I don't think you'll be disappointed. You'll also get a free sound track and art book (be aware the sound track and art book will be in limited supply with the first copies so you'll need to order soon).

I received this game yesterday and have enjoyed playing it so far. You take the role of Innkeeper who makes a living selling Crystals to a town which are used as an energy source. He made a promise to his father to always take care of the Inn and treat the guests as they are family. One day an Earthquake happens and he finds a mysterious girl in a crystal who saves him from Monsters and it goes from there with the story which has been great so far as they don't give away too much at a time so it makes you want to keep playing to find out what's going on. The battles are interesting as the monsters each have a "leader" that can summon soldier mobs that fight with them.. only killing the leaders give experience so you can go straight for them and ignore the smaller monsters if you wish. However, a lot of battles have "sub missions" which reward you with extra items in example one battle's sub mission may have you kill all the monsters on the field. Each person takes a turn and can move a limited range and each characters have different attack ranges and also have different skills with different attack ranges (if you have played disgaea the battle is VERY similar to it except that the movement and attack is not grid based). Each turn you gain one AP (action point I believe) and you can attack, guard, use a special skill (sometimes requires more AP like 2 or 3) or you can finish your turn and store the AP to use better skills. The controls work well although I found myself sometimes getting my characters stuck and roadblocking my other characters so you have to be careful how you move on the battlefield especially in smaller areas. When you aren't battling you can enjoy the story and view events with the heroines which unlock more abilities and make your characters stronger. Also you can do free battles by leaving the Inn on your own that aren't a part of the story to practice fighting and also to level up your characters. I try not to go into too many details in a review and just explain why I like the game. Overall, I think it has a great story the battles are easy enough to learn and pick up on so IMO it's a very fun game and I recommend it to anyone that likes RPGs or if you are new to RPGs.

I received the game on it's release date but just got around to playing it yesterday. Etrian Odyessey is a dungeon crawler game but one the best aspects about it is you get to draw your own map. You paint the layouts of the floors and walls as you go along. You have special symbols to place on the map like a treasure chest symbol that changes it's appearance (when you mark a treasure chest then open it the symbol shows an open box). You can place annotations on the map marking special locations or just to make your own personal comment so you have a lot of free will in this game. You have two modes in this game a story and classic mode, the story mode is preset with already made characters and plot to go through while classic allows you to be the creator and make your own team and adventure. If you have played Persona Q then you will recognize the map system from the start. The game has several difficulty levels you can choose from, allowing you to either easily play through and enjoy the story or spend many hours grinding to get your level up so you can proceed.. so whether you enjoy playing through easily and enjoying the story or proving your skill at grinding and putting the beatdown on your enemies you won't be disappointed. If you are new to the series it won't leave you in the dark either, you can enjoy this game without having played any of the other games. The graphics and sound are impressive and the controls are simple enough so I won't go into detail on those. I basically like to leave my reviews at what I like about a game and my personal opinion on them. I'd recommend this game to anyone who's new to RPGs or who wants to give a dungeon crawler a shot. Happy Gaming to all my fellow Gamers.

I can't give it 5 stars yet, because I am still fumbling through this baby. The thing is, I am not all that adept at games. I think I am okay, until I get into some sort of head-to-head play with people who take things really serious. THIS is different. SPARK allows you to design games, play games, and do all sorts of things. It has a tutorial that has been very helpful, and I have even managed to screw up doing that a few times, but it is still teaching.

One feature that I have enjoyed and been amazed by is the one where you can play other people's games. I see what these folks have done and then I go back to my design and want to just weep. (Not literally, I am just making the point that I feel like a dweeb when I compare my creation to others.)

The graphics are beautiful, so give it a try.

If you are a fan of movies like "House on Haunted Hill" and wondered just how you might fare if you were dropped into that sort of scenario, then this is the game for you. With the rise in popularity of the horror genre, maybe we will get lucky and start seeing more games like this. While not perfectly "open" world, there is a lot to see, do, and see again. This game will make you jump a few times, be prepared. And if you play in the dark, then the sound and visual creep factor only intensifies.

No game will ever be perfect, but the more games like this that hit the scene, I believe the better it is for gamers who love horror. Perhaps I will update after more time playing, but for now, I say grab this and turn out the lights.

UPDATE: After a full day with this game, I am now convinced that my rating and initial assessment is correct. I have been beheaded by a chainsaw wielding maniac more times than I can count, have endured countless assaults that left me a mutilated corpse (there is NO SHORTAGE of blood in this game), and despite writing horror for a living, I have jumped out of my seat on several occasions.

Okay, I realize the five stars is going to instantly collect a string of "no" clicks on the "Was this review helpful" tab, but some of the gamers need to get over themselves.

I will start with the negatives. YES, there are some glitchy graphics. And on the XBox One, we should be seeing better, but take out the occassional group of citizens that poke through a wall or meld into the road, and you still have some great things to look at. I can't be so bold as to knock the story since I have only had the game for a day. The people smacking that pinata are not likely to ever be happy, so take it for what it is worth. There are so many things to explore and look at instead of rushing to the finish line to say you "beat the game" in "X" amount of hours.

Personally, I like to climb every tower and open every box.

The AC game should be familiar by now, but if this is your first time, it eases you into the controls, so don't worry, you will get the hang of it before long.

My personal favorite in the franchise is AV4, but I am a pirate fan, so what can I say?

bottom line from an almost 50-year-old, this is more than enough game. I am not much for playing with other gamers because most are young, rude, and really in too big of a hurry. You will have to read other reviews for that info. But if you like to wander around and just soak it in, there is plenty of game here for you.

First, I want to start by saying, "What a game!" It is everything that DEAD ISLAND wanted to be but just fell short. And you can certainly see that they borrowed a few DI ideas as well as the single appearance of a "clicker" (at least I only ran into just the one) from THE LAST OF US.

Overall, I enjoyed the game a lot and found that it was not only full of depth, but also very challenging. And the story unfolds in a way that allows you to learn how to manage the game play. I am an old guy, so some of the fast action took me a while to get the hang of. One chase in the finale was proof that I am old and that the younger folks who have their controls melded into their hands have a definiet advantage.

I did feel that there was a bit of "borrowing" in regards to the crying baby zombie. I am an author, and I introduced that in my books back in 2009, but this is the era of samples and "creative borrowing" so there is not much can be done there.

Overall, this is a spectacular game to become immersed in for hours. I look forward to the story being continued.

This review starts off as a 4-star. I received it as a gift and have just settled in to begin play. I guess it is my age (almost 50), but I don;t much understand reviews that come out the day the game is released with either effusive praise or troll-ish vitriol. As a kid, I watched the old Adam West "Batman" episodes. I saw that old Batmobile at a few car shows. I was not huge as far as comic books, nor am I a fanboy of this sort of thing. I play games to decompress and have fun.

That said...I started with the Harley Quinn (the subject of my next tattoo) add-on. Her brief adventure works as a nice way to get used to the controls. I still haven't beaten the "boss" at the end and saved Ivy. I keep getting my behind handed to me. I have come close...once. With the frustration from that reaching its apex, I finally moved on to the actual game. The cinematic scope is amazing. It beats most of the so-called summer blockbuster movies. I have just dipped in a toe, so check back for more soon.

Okay, so I finally beat the Harley story. I am just not that nimble of finger, so it took a while. I toyed with the Red Hood add on, but have run into another roadblock almost right away.

At last, I put Red Hood to rest with a win as well as the Batgril story which was surprisingly easy.

On to the main event. The Batman story is epic, the graphics are amazing, but the puzzles can get the best of you quite often. With little to no instruction, it can be a mystery as to how you need to go about accomplishing many of the tasks. For instance, the "Breakable Objects" side quest...I found nothing that told me I needed the Batmobile to destroy them. I stood over one and threw about a hundred Batarangs at the cursed thing to no avail. (Thank you internet gamers who post for the assist.)

I have never done well with driving sims, and this is no different. I hit everything in my path while driving through Gotham, and I have found the controls to be very touchy. So far, I have captured Ivy and have gotten through about 3% of the story over a few hours here and there for a few days.

The Riddler puzzles do get a shade tedious, and I am one of those people who needs to beat every aspect of the game to feel satisfied. Perhaps fewer of those silly Riddler Question Mark Statues behind seemingly impossible cages and the like and more emphasis on regular gameplay.

I do enjoy the Joker's role in this adventure. I found it a clever little way to progress the story.

The graphics are amazing. that bears repeating, but this game can frustrate a person to no end.

I know it is cheesy to write a 5 star review for a game that many will enjoy bashing like a pinata, but I am an old dude (50-ish) and I never believed I would see myself running around as Darth Vader, or flying a snowspeeder. I will also note that I am NOT a shooter-game player type of person. I prefer solo campaign style games because you youngsters out there turn me into swiss cheese the moment I re-spawn. After listening to all of the naysayers bashing this game before it was released I was a tad bit concerned but ordered it anyways...and glad I did.

This game stayed entirely true to the franchise in every way possible, it is scarry as hell and Alma does a fantastic job of randomly appearing from time to time just to remind you that you both will meet again.

The gameplay mechanics are probably the BEST of any FPS I have ever played and that is not something that comes easily. When I say they are the BEST I mean it, the weapon and player control are unlike any game that I have ever played!! The cover control reminds me of a highly improved and polished Rainbow 6 Vegas contol scheme but smooth as ice. You can run up to a crate or other obstacle and hit the leap button and slide right over the top, this is especially cool when you engage slow mode and are tearing up the enemies at the same time.

The graphics are very good, probably a 4.5/5 and the gibbs...holy crap!! when you hit someone with a shotty as they come around a corner, you will not need to worry about them getting up since their body has just exploded in a mist of red rain. The weapons are highly detailed and work like a champ, the grenades cook off a little quicker than I would like so you definately need to pay attention to the counter or you will join the enemies demise!

AI, holy crap!! if they see you, they will call out your location to the rest of the team and they will come looking for you, no more standing behind a box and waiting for you! All you will hear is, "there he is, he is hiding behind that box, take cover position, team 1 go in"...and they always do. If you do not use cover in this game, you will die very quickly since the health meeter seems to deplete in no time.

Sound: FEAR at its best!! nothing like walking through the prison at the beginning of the game and having an inmate jump up through the viewing port in the door screaming at your and throwing various items out you.

Overall this game is a highly polished work of art!! Anyone who bashes this game is just doing so for attention and does not truly enjoy a good FPS. Granted I have only played the single player campaign so I will update the review once I jump in and try the multiplayer modes...and I can't wait to play full campaign coop!!

My inital impression was that Prototype was terrible. After deciding to just ignore the story and run around having fun it has been upgraded to average.

To let those of you who can skip the rest of this, the game is almost exactly like Spiderman 2 but with slightly better graphics and the fact you are forced to be a complete jerk at all times.

Anyway...

You play Alex Mercer, a man who's been missing for five years and who comes back having all these powers of genetic transformartion that do not surprise him one single bingle bit. Me, I would be a little taken aback were tendrils of LIVING FLESH to sprout out of my belly and absorb some guy whose head I just punched until it exploded. I could afford a gasp. But that's me. You, gentle reader, are maybe made of sterner stuff.

But no, Alex does not care that he sprouts 6 foot blades on his forearms and can run up 200 story buildings without breaking a sweat. All he cares about is getting revenge on the man what gave him all these great super powers that let him do anything. That big jerk! Alex is just another uber-macho dork designed to make 12 year olds and people who are mentally 12 years old think they're hot stuff. Hunched walk, check, stands on tall things, check, gravelly emotionless voice, check.... The man is just pathetic.

So, basically, this is a game where you run around and kill things. Mostly innocent civilians since, if anyone walking the street even comes close to Alex, he back hands them so hard they fall over or spin across the street. Spiderman pushed through, that dude in Assassin's Creed gently moves through crowds; SUCH a gentleman. Alex is a big jerk. More importantly, Alex HAS TO BE a big jerk unless you take to the rooftops; the game does not give you the option to not be an immature loser.

The main mission is pretty par for the course. It starts 18 days into the infection of the city by the same virus that gave Alex his terrible terrible wonderful powers. You have every power available to you in the game and you basically fight off a big old military/infected monster fight. It's pretty dumb, needlessly confusing and a terrible way to start any story much less a game. Plus the whole "I tell the story as you do it" thing just never works as a narrative; it totally removes you from the story every time they cut back to Alex. And, really, the writing never gets any better. Then the game switches back to Day 1 and you wake up in the morgue yadda yadda yadda.

There are a number of wacky side missions to go on and you unlock them as you continue on in the main mission. None of them are very interesting; they've pretty much all been done before in Spiderman 2 and most of them are frustrating because of the sloppy targetting system, camera and poor graphics. A lot of reviewers are making much over the stealth missions into army bases to consume certain people that raise your skill levels but even these are lame, all you do is walk slowly behind the target and hammer the Stealth Consume button. Stealth Consume won't activate unless you're completely safe so it's basically a really boring game of follow the leader.

And yeah, the graphics are bad. I'm not a graphics snob by any means, give me 2-d, low-res sprites any day of the week but this actually affects gameplay. There's tiny red printing on black backgrounds which is pretty much impossible to read without an HD TV and even with one it's gonna be tricky and the character models are blocky and weird looking, like early Resident Evil games. Everything is grey, black or red; the city is incredibly washed out and lifeless. There's about 7 different people you'll see walking the streets and about 4 different cars. It's almost impossible to tell the infected zombies apart from the normal citizens which also affects several missions, but this may actually be a choice on the part of the developers since you can unlock a power that lets you see enemies clearer, however. But since you have a HUD that tells you when enemies are near, it hardly matters.

Powers are another mixed bag. Most of them are just upgrades to what you have already and the controls to get most of the later ones off are impossible to read and unneccesary anyway, the game is crazy easy as it is just with hammering the default combat buttons. Or, just ignore the combat completely and spend the entire game in a tank. By the time the game unlocks the next set of powers to buy, you have so many Evolution Points they may as well have just given you all of them at once instead.

That's the really big problem with the game, none of it is neccesary. Yeah, I can buy power upgrades but why? I can go on side missions to get Evolution Points but I already have a ton of them. I can absorb certain people to keep the military from noticing where I am but they don't anyway; the Awareness meter that fills up as you do unnatural things just doesn't. I regularly run down the middle of the street doing 30+ foot jumps and nobody bats an eyelash.

It IS fun to tear around the city tho, and unlocking the Glide power makes things even more fun. But I don't just want a game where I run to the end of a boring city and then run back.

All in all the game is a Spiderman 2 clone that tries to break out more but everything it does pretty much falls flat. It's not a terrible game but there's better.

Before I go into the review, let me give you a little background so you can consider my experience and bias when it comes to this MMO. I loved EQ 1, the game that exposed me to MMOs in the first place and opened my eyes to the possibilities of an online world with others. I have also enjoyed City of Heroes, Lord of the Rings Online and Uncharted Waters Online. When it comes to Bioware, I really enjoyed Dragon Age Origins (NOT DA2), Mass Effect 2 and Jade Empire. Of those three, I enjoyed Dragon Age Origins the most. Finally, when it comes to Star Wars, loved 2 of the 2 original movies, enjoyed the first 1.... Find the last 3 worth a late night nothing else on watch.

Now that this is over, let me start by saying this is not an Sandbox game. If you are looking for a hit the road and explore as EQ offered and Uncharted Waters Online also kind of offers (UWO is mostly a strategy title though), this is probably not the game for you. If you enjoyed Mass Effect 2's style, minus the combat which is very different, and would enjoy playing in the Star Wars Universe, might be worth having a look.

There are two sides to choose form, the Jedi and Sith, basically good and bad although, as you play the varying class stories, each class, 4 for Jedi and 4 for Sith, have their own stories, you will see that some of the choices and events happening make you stop and wonder, if only for a moment, what is really "good" or "bad". The good is the classes do play differently although their mirror counterparts are very much the same. I play a Smuggler which is basically a long range DPS. I also played the Imperial Agent on the Sith side in beta which plays very similar to the smuggler. Although there were early claims from Bioware about maybe not relying on the holy trinity, healer, tank and dps, they still do BUT the trinity is not required to complete the game. You can finish your class quest, enjoy a lot of encounters with other people and due to companions or some hybrid classes are fine without the trinity. If you are taking on flashpoints that are higher than you, like my group does, or just hitting areas that are purposefully challenging, the holy trinity is more important but still not 100% required like others. I play a DPS. I do fine on my own, my companion (all classes are pretty much "pet" classes") tanks for me and if I join up with others, and I am still very functional. I also have a very handy mez against droids so versatile on some levels too.

The two sides have interesting stories, but the Jedi, at least at this time, seems more flesh out to me. They play differently because of the story, but beyond that... not that different.

Character Creation

Lacking. There is a variety, yes but not really on par with other game releases. I play a cyborg. While I could get a single eye replacement on the Sith side, I couldn't with the Jedi. I know where I wanted my implants but there was nothing I could do to get what I wanted. Hair choices are limited, skin tone is a good choice. In a world of aliens... surprising lack of choices, EA/Bioware defended this choice earlier on... I still don't buy it. It is certainly possible to run into your exact twin... unlikely. There are games out there that such a choice would be one in maybe a million, but these are not this game. I've actually found myself chasing after the wrong group not realizing it. Everyone looks too similar. The clothing choices, the color scheme... even heights are all so drab it's unfortunate. Don't get me wrong. It is a nice looking world but it's just lacking in this department.

Flashpoints

Flashpoints are my favorite, by far. They are basically instances where a group, usually a full group, spends about an hour trying to complete some sort of mission together with ample reward and sometimes death. They are challenging and fun, and the death penalty isn't so great to try and avoid them. You can repeat the missions, and we do, challenging ourselves to do better each time until we move onto the next one. The only real down side to flashpoints is Jedi or Sith... they are, at least as far as I have gone, the same. Sure the story is different, but the map is repeated, the bosses are even the same and it's not really something you could play on the "other" side and feel you are getting a fresh experience.

Crafting

I am a crafter. I craft in every game and enjoy it. Having said that, crafting in this game is so easy and non-intrusive even those against crafting are enjoying it. You don't need to spend an hour each day crafting or, as some would see it, not I, not playing to get crafting down. Your companions can do it. If you are in a full group not using your companion or have more than one, you can send them on their way making things for you, getting things for you and you can pick up supplies/material as you are playing without delaying your whole group for long.

Inventory System

Sucks, it really does. I feel like I have fallen back into some sort of early 2000s game that has no clean way to organize my stuff. It's just a bunch of squares that don't sort nicely. You have to turn on, in preferences, your ability compare your companions gear to the gear you have acquired and only then if they are with you. I haven't found a way to compare my ship upgrades to what is acquired at all and have to manually toggle between that. The nice step up from the early, early days of MMOs is the mission items are separated into their own tab, thank god, and the currency you can use to exchange for items is also separated out, though slightly buggy. I have one commendation I can't spend or destroy or do anything with. Customer Support has yet to personally respond to me on anything I have inquired about. I don't know that they will ever address any of my minor issues.

Spaceship Combat

I was pretty against the rail, watered down system that was released with this game. I still find it... lacking on a number of levels. For one, it is a single-player only. When I play these mini missions I just keep wishing others on the massive online game could play with me. The controls are simplistic and the challenge is... there but not in a strategic way so much as itchy trigger finger way. There is some fun to be had. Because they have this minimalistic space combat in the game... I fear there may never be a richer offering.

Bugs/ Servers

Some servers seemed to have 2 hour waits. Mine had 20-30 minutes tops on peak days. I just come home, clean up, eat, whatever while I que and have plenty of time to play after work or during the weekend. I have not found the queues to be a problem at all.

Bugs, yes there are bugs. One of our flashpoints, we couldn't tell if my long range attacks was being read as an exploit or bug which made a particular boss incredibly difficult at times or standard at other. There are bugs in either case. The mail system is shockingly slow. The eyes of characters keep disappearing in my conversations. The leaves are flashing like mad around me. We had a treasure chest not unlock during the flashpoint. Having said that, this has to be one of the cleanest MMO releases in recent memory. This might even be one of the cleaner just plain game releases for me in a while. The industry is just so used to release buggy, shoddy, barely working products to fix later after they've taken our money that I wondered if they cared at all about what they are putting out on day 1 anymore. There is no reason to wait for this game to be "cleaned up." It's pretty good already, although I suspect Slicing (crafting skill) will be nerfed at some point. I should also mention I thought Rift beta'd pretty cleanly as a reference and Star Trek Online at release was a disaster.

Solo vs Grouping

Although I question why some people would join an MMO to play solo, it's entirely possible. You can play 1 or 2 or 3 or 4 and enjoy all thoroughly. You will want 4 for the flashpoints, but you won't be held back by them. I've played in mixed level groups, had plenty of fun too. While the xp and loot is garbage, I've played grey quests (no xp) to finish off story lines. The Flashpoints are the reason why these side missions and my class missions turned green or greyed out on me.

Overall, this is a nice MMO to play, for veterans and certainly new entries into the genre a like. Is it everything I hoped it would be? No, not necessarily. For all the story emphasis, unlike the single-player RPGs, our choices in the storyline have no real effect. It's an MMO after all, and we're not at the point where player choices are changing the world in any meaningful way. It's hard for me to real get drawn into a story I feel I have no real... "choice" in that matters, but not impossible. I am not sure what EA/Bioware is going to offer to justify their monthly pittance, possibly nothing. This might be another pub claiming they need 15 dollars a month to house data and offer servers... I hope that is not the case. I know what servers cost... and it isn't 15 per person.

This game has a lot going for it out of the box. That says a lot for any PC game and certainly bodes well for an MMO. I hope they don't drop the ball and figure their job is done and it's time to nickel and dime players to death, read milk to death, and offer no new content and overpriced expansions. It is my hope that Bioware, and EA will let them, will treat this game and their player-base, well. For now, I am willing to ride along and ride with that hope, enjoy the game while doing so, and hope to see the rest of you online.

Guild Wars 2

Let me start with some credentials. I've been playing MMOs since Neverwinter Nights days on AOL. The highlight of my MMO experience was Everquest though, the original EQ. I've enjoyed many games since like Lord of the Rings Online, Star Wars the Old Republic and Vanguard, but none of them long-term.

My review may be repetitive to those who play MMOs and followed the game's release. I have opinions and information beyond the marketing material as well so some points might be geared more to non-MMO players but gives some insight into how it works in practice.

Pros

1. No Subscription. This game does not require a monthly fee, but there are options to buy thing in the cash store. This, however, is not a grab for money kind of Free to Play cash shop. I have hit 80; I play in dungeons, fractals, WvW and have yet to buy anything. I am most likely going to buy more bank space because I am a pack rat. Other players laugh at the idea of buying more space which is fine. Other things you can buy are things like cosmetic items, essentially trying to get your character to look more unique in some way, or play boosts consumables, things that boost your XP, grant you access to the bank on the move, or repair your gear without having to go back to town.

2. Character Creation - It's fun, offers a variety of nice looking toons you can cater to your liking. I know there are some options coming to the cash shop soon that should offer more variety, but let me assure you that there are a good amount of options to tinker with. I have not run into my exact twin ever, and the dye options in this game, which expands as you play when you buy dye or find it, makes the clothing intriguing even if it is similar to others. I had fun creating my characters, and the variety of classes, races makes it fun. Unlike other games, there is no supreme wrong combo. Just have fun. Leave the calculators stay in the office.

3. This game is certainly doable solo. You do not have to be in an organized guild or have a bunch of friends online all the time to enjoy this game. In the open world, events that require additional players almost naturally get them. People running by will help you kill that giant troll... eventually. Events are like moths to a flame, players just want to do them. I know I love them. Also, pick-up groups, groups of people who do not typically work together, can certainly work well.

4. The game's content does not scale, but you do. What this means is as a level 80 player, if I have a friend who is just starting the game I have two choices. I can take my level 80 over to their starting area, and have my level downgraded to 3 or 6 or whatever that area's content is and still be challenged, still have fun. I'll have some bonuses like better gear, which also scales, and skills and traits that I have as an 80 but everything is down so I really can't just clear an area all by my lonesome. The other option, of course, is to create another character and enjoy it all again.

5. The world is huge, feels absolutely huge. If you roll another character, or three, it's very likely you'll run into things you missed with your other character the first time around. This might keep things fresh for some. I am not that easily bored with repeat content, so doing more quests again is fine with me.

6. Completionists - There are tons of things for you to do to get access to some completionist geared titles, badges and actually get real game rewards for it too. Each time you complete a map, visit all those points of interests, do quests/tasks in a certain area to fill in hearts, find out how to get to vistas way up on the side of the cliff and see some nice aerial views of the game... finish all of those in an area and you get some rewards and a change to move your percentage complete of the word map up and up until you finish it. I assume there is a reward for finishing the entire map, but I am not there yet so I cannot confirm.

7. Jumping Puzzles - This is almost a con for me because it is not my strength at all, but some people just adore those jumping puzzles. You know the kind where if you are off a bit you have to start over or maybe you just die. These jumping puzzles are in Story Quests, Fractals/Dungeons, Events and wind up in places you don't expect it... like some of the Vistas can be a little tricky. If this is your thing, seek them out, they are there.

8. Crafting - Crafting is fun, expensive, especially for some trades, and 100% optional. If you don't like it, don't do it. Just harvest and sell on the trading post, you'll make some money. If you do like this sort of thing, well it's not as fun as Vanguard was or EQ2 (the mini game crafting), but entry into crafting is easy and leveling up, discovering recipes, just enjoying making things is there.

9. PvP - I almost never play PvP. I actually hate it in most games, but the way GW2 does it is my cup of tea. People who like to gank and get their jollies on weaker players are not going to like this game. You don't get to strip players of their gear or anything of that nature. World vs. World, WvW, is kind of like a big siege map where your team (server) is trying to capture or defend different points on it. It's a group effort, easy to do hard to master and definitely a team sport. There are some issues with cheating and overpowered classes in this part of the game, but it is still fun and ArenaNet is supposedly working on it. I played the PvP team mini-game during the Halloween event and enjoyed that. These mini games could use a little more instruction and maybe a PvE demo round so you understand what was going on, but it was a fun, more intimate PvP part of the game I enjoyed. Again, if you love killing players that have no chance against you, this is not your game. If you avoid PvP because of that former issue, you might have some fun in this game. PvP also has its own reward system, everyone is leveled up enough to do it, and so you can't kill some low level character for funnies aspect. You could feasibly do PvP and nothing else if you really wanted to.

10. Community - The game is designed to the point where you are not competing with other players for hardly anything which creates a pretty friendly community. No one is running up to mine that gold before you get a chance to because it's there just for you too. Events are group efforts, so working together well works. There really isn't any kill stealing that I can think of.

11. Travel - Way points make travel easy and expensive if you want to, otherwise running around on foot is the way to go. There are areas that are more dangerous to travel, especially areas without a lot of people in them, but there is no artificial cap on traveling. You can head to that dangerous area and know that some stray animal might instakill you if you want.

12. Death - Die often enough and you'll probably be poor. It's not prohibitively expensive but repair bills can be weigh you down. On the other hand, exploring is worth the risk.

13. Events - Events happen all the time in the game, on timers like the dragons, or occurs when another event ends, successfully or fails. It's not nearly as cool as they previewed because some of them happen too fast. Before you even get a chance in the fun of overtaking a centaur camp that it resets and you are in hostile territory again. It's partially successful though because they are fun. I think the timing and the results still need work. I don't know they are working on that or not. Onetime events are a lot of fun, offer interesting rewards and the unexpected.

Con

1. Low Population in low level areas - Because of the way events are, starting now gives you a different experience than when the servers were bursting at the seams. Some events are just not taken care of because the population isn't there. This is not an uncommon issue for MMOs, but it seems a little more of an issue because of events in this game. As a level 80, I travel in some areas getting to others, and occasionally stop to do an event because they are still fun, and I am downgraded that they remain a challenge

2. Short One Time Events- I think ArenaNet is looking at this, but these one-time events that happen over a weekend that trigger at times when some people are sleeping or working, never to repeat again seem unfortunate to me. I hope they stretch them out longer eventually and maybe rerun them a couple of times a year... keeping them rare but still playable for those who missed it.

3. Gear - This is under Con, but it's really only an issue for some. At some point towards the end game content, what you are working for is no longer levels but gear. Gear is not extreme in this game, however, not like say raid gear. The stat differences are minor, so a lot of it has to do with how it looks. Getting a complete set of some sets is extremely hard. Some people love that challenge, others hate it. I am working towards gear, and don't mind it at all, still having fun.

4. Lack of Raid - There are big events, for certain, like the Dragons and the recent one time Karka event. The game lacks the big risk and big rewards that other games have, and this could be a deal breaker for some. I've never seen a dragon event fail, and the reward is a random chest. It's nice to roll on these chests, and I do them all the time for a chance at the chest and because I still like the events. The Ancient Karka event almost felt like a raid. Almost in that nearly half our server group fighting it wiped during some unexpected attacks. The rewards were awesome as well. IF the game is missing anything for traditional MMO players, it's this. Big events, huge risks, and likelihood of dying but possibility of winning... that's a sweet spot for some, and it is not here yet, not on the huge scale of raids in other games.

5. Story - The voice acting in the game ranges from okay to did they really just grab the mailroom kid and ask him to read a few lines. Some people will certainly play this down. I've muted the story many times, and have yet to finish my story quest. I barely care; can't stand the voice acting, the content scales but the reward does not so I am often destroying or just selling what it gives me. Overall I find the Story Quest line a generally unpleasant experience. Every few weeks, I might do one or two and then forget about it.

This is a great game. It's a lot of fun for those who love MMOs, but dislike some of the time consuming, hardcore unpleasant parts of other games. The community is generally pleasant. You can play dungeons and usually not get yelled out, kicked or otherwise rudely treated for doing something wrong often because there is room for mistake and recovery. It's not a sandbox, so you are generally working on quests or towards some obvious goal. You are not as forced down one path as say Star Wars leads you, and new characters can very well encounter content you skipped or missed the first time around. Exploring can be interesting and rewarding, even dangerous but I am hesitant to suggest this is even close to a sandbox experience some desire.

Downgrading higher characters to the area's content works marvelously, especially if you want to go back and pick up some map completions or specific crafting materials. If you didn't like the time consuming, punishing nature of other MMOs, give this one a try. If you like MMOs, but are open to some of the content ideas in this game, don't expect 7 years of content perfection like some other games might give you, and give this a go.

Without the subscription, there is little to lose, even if you play it, stop for a while, and come back only for events or with updates. There is no real "end game" content, but it's not needed. There is plenty to work for, dungeons to explore, gear to work for, and maps to complete, crafting to master. The only people I would truly advise to stay away from these games are players who want a solo RPG experience. Yes, you can play this game almost entirely solo, only needing others for events, dungeons and other kinds of group content, but why? There are better RPGs out there, actual single-player RPGs on PC for you to play instead. The sad experience that is the Story Quest lines in this game are unlikely to satisfy anyone looking for an epic story like those found in Baldur's Gate or Dragon Age or something truly one player driven. This is, of course, is different from wanting to just play most the game solo and join in group content without the group, which you can do as mentioned above, and only run dungeons when you want to, not because you have to which again, is possible in Guild Wars 2.

So the benefit of a wireless headset is fairly obvious right. It gives you the freedom to take your friends and gaming team with you into the kitchen or to answer the door etc. It's only as good as the wireless connection though, and this worked well. I didn't experience any issues with that. This also has a charge and play cord so you can continue using it while it charges if you are going to be immobile for a bit. So why the three stars... it's not that comfortable. It's fine for a larger head. The ear piece is where I find it uncomfortable. Don't get me wrong. It's pretty light and not something I think about when it's on but I just find the ear pads a tad uncomfortable. The last quip is really the microphone. It's not adjustable, aka can't move it up and down.

In summary, it's exactly as advertised and would be a great step up for anyone who has been using bargain basement kind of headsets. For those of us who have been using the headsets with a lot of features on the luxury side of thing, it's lacking in some small ways. For wireless though, most would sacrifice those features readily because to me wireless is worth it.

Okay. Let me start by addressing my set-up. I have a PS4 slim, not pro, and a gaming PC, actually several gaming PCs. My PS4 is hooked up to a receiver, relatively new, and the PC well it also has a surround sound system but plenty of additional ports.

Problems with PS4:

The PS4 recognizes the headset just fine, immediately even. It doesn't have an optical port so it plugs into the usb just fine, and there are plenty of detailed and even picture driven instructions on how to do these set-ups so don't worry about that. I know it works fine because the PS4 recognizes it. It might even work as a communication device, but despite descriptions saying otherwise, the PS4 won't use the headset when the receiver is on. The receiver is always on. This is normal because there are several devices that plug into that receiver, not just this. I can't get it to actually play sound through the headset which makes it kind of worthless to use. You'd think when it's plugged in, it would use the headphones but it won't. When it's unplugged then of course it's fine to go through the receiver. Days of looking through manuals for the headset and the PS4 doesn't really point to a solution, and gain, the PS4 clearly recognizes it's there.

PC

It's terrible. It sounds thin and is by far the worst headset I have for the PC, and I have several... HS70, Man of War, Logitechs and this is just so disappointing.

Android Phone / Tablet

Bluetooth mobile... constantly disconnected, for no apparent reasons. I have a Bose and a Sony wireless headset I use with these, and they don't have disconnect issues, like at all, when they're in range. I can be holding the phone or tablet in my hand and this just drops the signal.

I wanted this to be used with my PS4, that was the primary purpose. I don't know that I would care much at all if it didn't perform well with the others, but again I can't get it to make the headset a primary device short of unconnecting the PS4 from the receiver which of course I won't do because that receiver doesn't just control audio, it actually sends the image to the TV too.

This was pretty big disappointment. It might work fine for simpler set-ups, but I'm not changing my entire set-up to get one headset to work. If there was some software set-up, like in the console itself, sure I would but everything I've read says once it recognizes the headphone/headset it should use it and simply does not do that.
