I started playing guitar in mid-1999 and really got into it for a few years. I had a band for a while and enjoyed playing with the group, even using now-ancient recording software and CD burners to put out albums to give away at the few shows we did. But then, like most things I pick up on, I got interested in something else and more or less abandoned the hobby. Just a couple of weeks ago, someone brought their guitar to work, and when he gave it to me, I practically forgot everything I knew how to play even just 5 years ago when I bought my last guitar. Where did all those riffs go?! Rocksmith 2014 is here to save the day. Honestly, you don't need yet another 5 star review telling you what's so great about this game and that it really does work as a tutoring program for guitar. This is one of the few games/programs for guitar that I know of that I can say is absolutely worth every penny, and even if you're a regular guitar or bass player, you could benefit from a few things that the game has.

When it comes learning in a way that works for you, this game has you covered in spades. You can select what specific areas of playing you work on, from distortion to slide to scales. There are even a ton of different amps you can choose to play through in order to get the authentic tone of the original recordings! One of the coolest additions is that as you get better in the game and start hitting everything perfectly, the on-screen notes fade away and you're left to pull it off all on your own. The game does this automatically, serving as a way to acknowledge that you've gotten better. The only bad thing I can say regarding Rocksmith 2014 Edition is that there's nothing along the lines of notation, something that musicians would benefit greatly from over time. And I say that with 100% honesty. I still feel like an idiot when someone hands me sheet music asking if I know how to play it. Tabs, absolutely! That stuff...not so much. Who knows, maybe there'll be a DLC pack in the future for this. Also, the lack of a recording feature for the awesome improv session mode hurts, though you can always find ways to record it on your own with the right programs and devices.

Beginner, intermediate and even self-proclaimed pros should invest in this game as soon as possible. If I had started playing guitar more recently, or if this game had been around when I was 14, I'm sure I would've gotten more into the instrument and been more serious about it. The fact that the game features a cool little arcade game mode to help you with different techniques in the form of old school arcade games kept me in this mode for longer than expected, and especially considering I used to know all of this stuff. This game is perfect, and there's only so much written reviews can explain for you. Get the game for yourself or watch some videos online to see how it works better. Now you can be a real guitar hero...with a real guitar!

[Amazon finally put PSN game codes back on the site, so I'll put up my review for the game again since reviews for digital downloads aren't spread across platforms for some reason.]

There is no other game that I've played this year that's won me over as much as Guacamelee has. Whereas most people will be saying that Bioshock Infinite or The Last of Us is their choice for Game of the Year, my vote goes for this little beauty right here. No, I'm not joking. Guacamelee does so much right and gave me so much fun in just the right amount of time that it's impossible for me to say anything else this year has given me as much enjoyment. I guess I'm just a sucker for great PSN titles, as last year Tokyo Jungle beat out everything else I played, and just a few years before, PixelJunk Shooter did the same. Old school and newer gamers alike should try this game out if they're looking for a challenge or just all around good platforming action fun. And hey, the creators even managed to sneak in a couple of huge game references too, including Metroids, Mario, Castle Crashers, Journey, Grim Fandango and more! No seriously, there are practically legit Metroids and Chozo statues here!

Juan is a regular man who's in love with the president's daughter, Juanita. Sadly, things go horribly wrong when Juanita is whisked away by Calaca, a skeleton in a sombrero, who also kills off Juan. Things aren't over yet though! Juan awakens in the world of the dead, and is given a magical luchador mask by a masked woman, Tostada (yeah, I know). With it, he's able to return to the land of the living and begins his journey to rescue Juanita and stop Calaca from going through with his grand scheme of starting a new world order.

Gameplay is just like your standard Metroid or Castlevania game. That's the most common thing you'll hear about this game, and it's not a complaint. Just like how Okami is the best Zelda clone that's ever come out, Guacamelee might be the best Metroid/Castlevania game that's ever come out. Platforming is fun, combat is great and whenever I'd learn a new ability, it was always exciting. Juan and Tostada will travel through various areas like great jungles, mountains, a chicken cave, a desert and more before they can come mask-to-skull with Calaca. There are so many hidden areas in each map that you'll have just as much finding them to upgrade your health and stamina as you would advancing to the next area. Combat is easy to learn, though you can really go nuts with combos. Square is punch, and pressing it several times makes a basic combo. You can also press up and square to launch your enemy into the air, and jump with x to follow them and continue with your combo with the square button. Pressing down and square while in mid-air smashes them back down. As mentioned, you'll learn special abilities from a transforming goat, like a frog splash, Rooster Uppercut and a massive headbutt. You can throw these into your standard combos to deal massive damage, and just plain make a flashy spectacle. And since the game supports an extra player, you can have both characters beating up the same enemy to really bring the pain.

If you've played a Metroid game before, you'll know that certain doors could only be opened when you had a certain weapon. Like in Super Metroid, the pink doors were opened with 5 missiles (or one Super Missile), orange ones were opened with the Super Bomb, etc. There's something similar here in Guacamelee where different colored blocks will be in the way of special areas on the map. If a red block is laying around, you'll have to hit it from below with a Rooster Uppercut. If there's a yellow one, headbutt that sucker to smash it open and see what lies ahead. Not only do you have these abilities to help you out, but you're also able to wall jump, and later on, learn the ever-useful double jump. Getting the hang of these is necessary to navigate through some very tricky areas, which leads my to one of my favorite parts of the game- the platforming.

I honestly don't remember the last time platforming sections got the best of me. It was probably Super Metroid back in 1994! There are so many tricky areas in this game that I had to set the controller down and really think some of them over before trying again (and before I threw the controller at something). This game does NOT hold your hand even once, and if you have a hard time with some of the earlier sections, just wait until you go for the special mask pieces to unlock the true ending. There's one stage that's sure to test your patience. Heck, there were even times when a room full of enemies would get the best of me because I was outnumbered or one would distract me while the other would come in with a giant attack. Seriously, your reflexes need to be good in order to progress to the next area.

Gameplay's awesome, but the animation, art direction and soundtrack are even better. I'm absolutely in love with the look and sound of this game. The whole thing looks like a missing episode from Samurai Jack, and when the game would get to a part that zooms in on your character more, I'd do all kind of moves just to see how well they animated everything. When I beat the game and the credits rolled, it was downright stupid how few people worked on this game and how incredible the outcome was. I feel horrible for buying the game when it was a few bucks off during a sale now, as it definitely deserves every dollar of the small amount it costs. There's nothing big I can complain about, other than that you can beat the game in about 6 hours, and maybe 8 or 9 if you want to get everything. One other slightly minor thing is that several people have been vocal about the game's "racist" nature. I can see how they might think that way, but it didn't bother me much.

If you haven't bought it yet, what are you waiting for?! This is one of those games that I'm happy to replay regularly, and it's pushing me in the direction of buying a Vita just so I can play it on the go too since I got that version for free.

This is the first Assassin's Creed game I've played. I almost went the entire console generation without playing any of them, and it's not that I was trying to avoid them by any means, but they just never interested me that much. Part of this is because of how many AC games have come out in just a few years. It's almost like every November, you can expect another Assassin's Creed game. I'd seen enough gameplay videos from a few of the previous titles to get an idea of what they'd be like, and when I got offered a chance to play Black Flag, I figured I might as well and see how one of these games plays for myself.

Playing as a pirate, doing battles at sea with ships, was exciting the first couple of times, but later on, it became a chore, especially when there wasn't much of a point to doing it. Surprisingly, the main character in Black Flag, Edward, is a pirate for the most part, rather than an assassin. Be that as it may, the guy has some slick moves. Being able to use two swords at once makes for some devastating attacks. There were a couple of times where I thought "ok, that was cool" after taking out someone. The last time I got that feeling? Adam Jensen's insane takedowns and kills with his augmentations in Deus Ex: Human Revolution. Combat, both on land and at sea, is fun and where I got most of my kicks. The main story, however, is something I avoided almost entirely. I beat the game, and was letdown by most of it, and I hope it's not like this with the other AC games if I get around to playing another one. Being forced to do something, or read a 4 page note completely killed the momentum that you get in this game from running on rooftops, jumping from beams and ropes, and all the stuff that makes the game what it is. And don't even get me started on the multiplayer. You have THIS GAME, where a big focus is on ship battles at sea, and all we get is -another- round of cat and mouse, walking around a market trying to kill the right target?

And people complain about the Call of Duty games being uninspired.

As far as the graphics are concerned, I was impressed with the water effects. The oceans here look like real oceans, and I can only imagine they look even better on the new systems. Character models and landscapes look fantastic as well. Ditto for the voice acting and soundtrack. It's not the kind of soundtrack that I'll remember a few years from now, but it gets the job done and done well.

Assassin's Creed IV is a game that I'm kind of glad I played, just to see what the big fuss was about, but I guess I was telling myself to stay away from the games for a good reason. It's just not my kind of game. Clearly I'm in the minority here, as it has mostly 4 and 5 star reviews, mainly from people who seem to be fans of the franchise. You can blame part of it on my lack of interest in pirates too I guess. Still, if you're not sick of these games by now, you'll probably enjoy another round. If I could, I'd give Black Flag 3.5 stars instead of just 3.

I've never used a gaming headset before, although I've been getting slightly more interested in them after seeing some of the more respectable top fighting game players using them. Granted, there aren't many people who I play with online that also have headsets, and I don't play that many games that are team based or require much communication, but it's always nice to be able to do so in something like say, Borderlands 2. When I was offered a chance to get one of these RIG headsets, I figured now was the time to give it a shot. Given that this is the first one I've used, I can't say that it's the best out there, or worth its price. I -can- say that this sucker is comfortable, clear and makes for an enjoyable gaming experience, letting you hear all the game's audio while talking to your friends. As an added bonus, you can even listen to music on your phone or mp3 player with it with the right jack.

It may seem gimmicky to include a port for your phone, and I can safely assume that most people won't be using this feature. However, it's still nice to have in case you're waiting for an important call, or have a job position where people are calling you frequently. Both the mic that flips out of the headset, and the one that hangs from the cord are great and worked without any problems.

If I had something to compare this to, I'd give a more detailed review. Since it's my first item like this, it'll serve as the standard if I get another one. I haven't used it a whole lot for games since I don't play many multiplayer ones, given my work schedule, but for anyone who's looking for a quality headset that isn't going to break the bank, this would be an optimal choice.

Despite the games being huge when they first came out, I never played a full Tomb Raider game. I played a demo for TR2, and a demo for the first one that was on the Dreamcast, and that was it. The games never seemed that fun to me, and it felt like the only reason the games were as popular as they were was because of the main character's appearance. Something happened though when I saw footage from the 2013 reboot of the franchise. Everything I saw looked incredible. Lara Croft had a regular body type! The story sounded interesting! Gameplay looked fun and realistic! How was this a Tomb Raider game?? Last year I had a lot of other games that I was busy playing, and I ended the year by picking up TR for a stupidly low price. Very rarely do I stick to playing one game when I buy it. Usually I'll go off and finish up something in another game, be it trophies or trying to get an extra item or something. With Tomb Raider, I stuck with it from beginning to end. I don't just give out 5 star ratings for games, and I'm not anti-mainstream, but most of the major titles don't catch my interest. I'm very happy to say that Tomb Raider is a 5 star game, and one that I look forward to completing 100%.

As usual, you play the role of Lara Croft, a young adventurer who gets shipwrecked on the island of Yamatai with several other people. This is no tropical paradise- the locales carry automatic guns and machetes, dangerous animals are on the prowl, and the terrain is just plain hazardous. The main plot focuses on an ancient Japanese queen, Himiko, who led the Yamatai empire and was able to control the weather with mysterious powers. One of the other survivors, Sam, happens to be a descendant of Himiko, and early in the game, she's taken away by a man named Matthias, who claimed to be a teacher that was also stranded on the island. Things go from bad to even worse when Lara begins to explore the island while looking for her friends, and discovers the truth about Himiko and what Matthias is after.

From what I've heard, Tomb Raider plays out a lot like an Uncharted game. Unfortunately, I've never played any of those! But now I want to, given how incredible this game is. I haven't had this much fun playing a full fledged AAA title in a long time. Usually I don't have much time to play games during the work week, but this is one of those games that made me put aside a little extra time now and then just to keep going along. The story had my interest from the beginning, and I was curious to see what was going to happen next. Not only is the story good- the game is fun as heck. Lara only gets 4 main weapons- the bow, an assault rifle, a shotgun and a pistol, and each one is nice to have. As you progress, you'll find salvage parts to upgrade your weapons, although you'll also need to find specific weapon parts in boxes and on corpses to upgrade them to their full power. It's not very often that I run around the entire map looking for more parts to upgrade something, and yet that's exactly what I did with Tomb Raider because I -did- want to see everything that each weapon had to offer.

Lara gains experience from killing enemies and animals, as well as finding treasures and documents scattered on the island and in hidden tombs. It's kinda funny that raiding tombs, the main point of the franchise, is optional here. It rewards you with a lot of experience though, and each one, while not difficult, gives you a break from the action with solving a quick puzzle. Killing an enemy with a headshot nets more experience, and you can really stack up the exp points by blowing up a red barrel when a group happens to be standing by it (this doesn't happen much, unlike most action games). Hunting animals starts out by being necessary to Lara's survival, as she needs food during a plot point. Once you kill your first deer, it becomes kind of addicting to chase after other animals and take them out. I liked that killing animals or enemies with the bow lets you pull your arrows out of the body to put them back in your inventory. I also appreciated that the bow is a strong weapon, as it should be- too often in games, the bow is an underpowered weapon, when in fact, it's one of the best, strongest weapons ever made.

It took me about an hour before I really got the hang of things, getting used to the mechanics of the game, like QTE sequences and realizing that I was controlling Lara during certain parts, like when she's sliding down waterfall. Tomb Raider caught me by surprise when I learned that you actually get to control what Lara does 99% of the time. I figured this out near the very end of the game, when I thought to myself, "I'm surprised the game doesn't just do this part for you".

All of the animations, voice acting, music and visuals are outstanding. There were many times where I wished there was a way to view the world in first person mode, just to see details better. And you gotta love how Lara keeps her wounds as the game goes on. The poor girl gets messed up big time early on, and it just gets worse from there. When she sees her reflection for the first time, that's really when what she's been through sinks in.

I can't say you'll like this game if you love the older Tomb Raiders. As I mentioned earlier, I've never played any of them, or any of the Uncharted games. Maybe that's part of why I loved TR so much- it was something genuinely now for me. I've always wanted to go on an adventure somewhere and explore the land freely. Maybe it's time for me to go back a little and try out the Uncharted games, and maybe even get the Tomb Raider Trilogy to see how those games fare. Now that the price has dropped on TR big time, you don't have any excuses to not play it. Had I bought this for the original retail price when it came out, I wouldn't have been disappointed. 5 stars all around- an instant classic.

I remember when Minecraft was first created a couple of years ago. Back then, and even up until recently, it didn't look that interesting to me. I'm into all kinds of different games and genres, but Minecraft just didn't pull me in when I'd see gameplay videos. Late last year, my daughter really got into it when she'd visit her friend's house, and not long after, it finally got ported to the ps3, which she immediately used a gift card on. Since then, no other game has gotten as much playtime, and I get to see her creations on an almost daily basis. She'd create dozens of worlds, all with something different and unique from one another, and while I was glad that she was playing a game where you could be so creative, I still wasn't that interested.

Then I started up a file for myself and I got it.

Minecraft is a game that this past console generation desperately needed. All-ages games of great quality are rare, and kids usually get the short end of the stick when it comes to games aimed at them. Unless it's Skylanders or Disney Infinity, there aren't many other options. Sure there's Rayman, Sly Cooper, Mario, Little Big Planet, the Lego games and a few others, but they're few and far between. And it just so happens that it appeals to people of all ages too. There's nothing really "kiddy" about it- Minecraft is a solid game worth checking out if you haven't already.

There's no real story here- you start up the game and enter a randomly generated world where you get to do whatever you want. Your world could have lush forests, massive beaches, tons of rivers, or mostly be water with just a couple of small islands (as was the case when I started my first world. That one quickly got deleted). When you start out, you don't have anything, so you need to walk around and destroy things with your fists, taking the material with you in block form so you can make things out of it. Crafting is challenging and fun, and there are -tons- of things to make. You'll probably start out by making a pickaxe out of wood, mining away at stone and rock so you can make a better pickaxe that won't break as easily. Then you can break up stronger materials that make for strong homes, which keep you safe from the various monsters that come out at night.

The number of things you need to make in order to make better things is overwhelming at first, but you'll quickly get the hang of it. Break up a tree to get wooden blocks, get x number of wooden blocks to make wooden planks, get x planks to make a sword and so on. Rarer materials like diamonds can make super strong swords and armor, making you a nightmare for Creepers and zombies. Making homes and buildings is a blast, and more simple than I expected. You just set down the blocks, as if you have giant Lego bricks, and insert things like a bed, stove, windows and more as you get the appropriate materials. You can even make potions to enhance your weapons and other things.

Minecraft is one of those games where there's really no "point" to it. You do what you want. It sounds boring at first, and the easy-listening soundtrack may not help that impression, but once you start playing and see just how time consuming things can be, it becomes fun. Once I saw how long it took to make a house, a steel pickaxe and find materials I needed for other stuff, I had a whole new respect for my daughter and how much time she put into each of her worlds. When I saw just how big the worlds can be, and how deep you can go underground while mining, it really put things into perspective. And don't even get me started on the steps needed to face off against the game's "boss". If things get too tough in the game's main mode, Survival, there's also a Tutorial mode to help you understand things better, as well as Creative, where you can pretty much do whatever you want with unlimited resources and no worries about dying. This may take some of the fun out of the game, although if all you want to do is build a world however you want without having to spend a lot of time getting the right materials, this is the place to go. The best thing to do when you've gotten the hang of things, is to hop online and invite a friend into your world, or go to theirs. Have fun exploring the area, which I can almost guarantee will be completely different from yours, what with the number of worlds that can be generated.

Visually, there's not much to say about Minecraft. it looks like an 8-bit game that got 3D treatment. That being said, it looks good for what it is, and I rarely experience slowdown. As I mentioned above, the soundtrack is on the snoozy side, with some relaxing piano tracks that loop, and there aren't many voices to be heard aside from grunts and growls.

Notch, the creator of Minecraft, is pretty much rolling in cash with the success of this seemingly simple game that started out as a downloadable title for just a few bucks. Word of mouth helped the game become the phenomenon it is today, and I gotta say, he's earned it. Now, you can't go anywhere without seeing a kid in a Creeper shirt or seeing merchandise, from key chains to big foam swords and pickaxes. It reminds me a lot of when Mario really got popular in the early 90s when games weren't anywhere near as big as they are today. Perfect for people who just plain enjoy playing games or creating things, Minecraft is here to stay.

When it first came out in 2003, Kingdom Hearts was a phenomenon. Prior to its release, a lot of people were worried about Squaresoft teaming up with Disney, blending their worlds of Final Fantasy and the Magic Kingdom into an adventure/RPG game. A lot of people have the mindset that anything with Disney on it is automatically "kiddy". Luckily for Square, KH was a hit and quickly became one of their biggest titles ever. Years went by and people wanted more, and more they got. A sequel came out after a couple of years, and before and after that, we got an ungodly amount of side games. More new characters, less Disney, it seemed. It took until just a few years ago for fans to finally get sick of this and want their true sequel, Kingdom Hearts 3. Well, it finally got announced not that long ago, and what better way to hype it up than with an HD collection of a few KH games?

The Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 ReMix, if you don't know by now, is the first Kingdom Hearts game remastered in HD. It's actually the second Japanese version- Japan got the game first, then the US did with some extra stuff, then Japan got the US version with even more extra stuff. The game looks gorgeous in HD, and you can tell what's been completely redone from scratch as soon as you see it. If I didn't know any better, I'd think that some parts of the game were from an early ps3 title.

The plot centers around a young by named Sora, who keeps having weird dreams about flying around his island home, entering a world filled with shadow creatures, and wielding a weapon known as the Keyblade. He lives with his friends Riku and Kairi, and they seem set on exploring the world to see what's beyond the ocean someday. Just when they're about to set sail, a little something happens- the island is caught in a huge storm, and the shadow creatures Sora dreamed about are there. He finds the Keyblade, vanquishes them, and ends up in another world. At the same time, good ol' Donald Duck and Goofy are out looking for Mickey (who's the king of their world), who left on an important mission. Sora meets the two, and they team up, looking for their friends. It turns out that there's a big mess right now, with the shadow creatures, known as the Heartless, interfering with other worlds. It's up to them to seal the world's keyholes using the Keyblade to restore everything.

Gameplay consists of a little exploration and a lot of combat. It seems weird at first, at least it did in 2003, to use the analog stick to control Sora while using the d-pad to select from items, magic and special attacks, but you get used to it quickly. You'll get to explore all kinds of memorable Disney worlds like Atlantis, Halloweentown, Tarzan's jungle and more. Characters from well-known Squaresoft games like the Final Fantasy series are thrown in as well. Chances are, if you're a fan of either company, there's something here for you.

I enjoyed the game's story when it came out. However, I was also 17 at the time. I know a lot of the game's fans were younger than that when they first played it, which makes them more attached to the series, but I didn't enjoy the plot very much playing through it 12 years later. Too many scenes are played out as being huge, important events...despite only lasting a couple of minutes and never being referenced again. I also completely forgot how underwhelming the boss fights were, save for the new special one that was only in Final Mix. Most of the time, the bosses will stand around, letting you hit them with huge combos, do their big special attack, and the process repeats. Some of the worlds are stupidly small when you look at them now too- Deep Jungle is basically 5-6 screens that you backtrack through several times before taking on the bosses. I also need to mention that I never understood why so many people adore the game's main song- Simple and Clean. It's an autotuned disaster that's overproduced and the vocals are forced.

...ok it sounds like I hate the game now. I don't. It just has its faults. You can play through Kingdom Hearts in about 20 hours and enjoy it for the most part. Spend a little more time and you can take out the optional bosses. Spend even more time, and you can go crazy trying to collect all the special items. That's one thing that did legitimately bug me- they changed the items needed for the Ultima Weapon. I gave up on it this time around. Given that they changed the strength of certain Keyblades, it wasn't even worth going for when you had say, the Devine Rose. And I'll also throw in that there are some genuinely touching moments here and there, one of which was a surprise since it's in Winnie the Pooh's world.

Also included are Chain of Memories and 358/2 Days. To be honest, I didn't care much for Chain of Memories' card-based gameplay. It's not my thing, though many KH fans didn't seem to mind. It's not a terrible game, and does expand on the side-story portions a bit. Plus it's a big visual upgrade from the original version that came out on the GameBoy Advance. Just like with the first game, it looks beautiful in HD.

358/2 Days however, is such a waste of time that I don't even understand why it was included, and nearly bumped the score down to 3 stars. Sure, you can argue that it's to reveal a little more about select characters, but all you're doing is watching what feels like hours and hours of clips of Roxas and Axel eating ice cream. I swear, you can have a drinking game to this thing. There's a pattern of this: eating ice cream, something boring and dramatic happens with the Organization, more eating ice cream, text scene where gameplay would have been, more ice cream and more boring drama. Because they couldn't port the whole game onto the disc for various reasons, you never see any of the action from fights, regardless of how big they were. Nope, all you see 80% of the time is Roxas and Axel sitting on the castle, eating ice cream. I stuck through the whole thing, expecting it to get good at some point. It didn't happen. Had I known that in advance, I would've just hit Play and went off to do something else. I didn't care for any of the characters here. Granted, I didn't play Kingdom Hearts 2, but if these collections are being released in a specific order at all, that shouldn't matter. They overcomplicated the KH story for no reason with all these extra characters who are linked to other extra characters who barely have a purpose. I already dread the other games included with KH2 on the next HD collection.

The first Kingdom Hearts is a ps2 classic, great for younger gamers, or for people to just relive memories they had with it. It has memorable music, great art design, and it's fun seeing Disney favorites come to life with new material, even if it is limited. It may sound weird, but I had a lot more enjoyment with Disney characters showed up, and much less when the Squaresoft guys were on-screen. The game definitely has some faults that are much more visible now. Still, getting a remastered edition of Final Mix, as well as its sequel, at this price is a pretty good deal. Stay away from 358/2 Days though, and just read a plot summary online somewhere.

I missed out on Shadow of the Colossus and Ico when they first came out on the ps2. I actually bought Ico, and played through about an hour of it, but got distracted by other games and just never went back to it. Shadow of the Colossus always looked like something I'd enjoy, yet something came up in my life where I had to sell all of my gaming stuff to make some extra money, so I missed out on it entirely. When both games were remastered for the ps3, I knew that this would finally be my chance to experience the two games that people are constantly proclaiming as "art", above anything else. The HD remaster looked great from gameplay footage I saw, and with the budget price, there was pretty much no reason for me to miss out on them this time.

Unfortunately, I didn't care much for either game. I knew they might be hit or miss, because as I just said, the only thing I really heard about them is that they're "works of art". Rarely did I hear anything about the games being fun or enjoyable. Now and then someone would bring up the soundtracks for both games being masterpieces, but that was about it. I decided to play Shadow of the Colossus first, mainly because it's hailed by so many as one of the best games ever made. Before I say anything about the games, I need to make one thing clear, because I know a lot of people on Amazon will look at a review's score, then vote that it wasn't helpful (NOT if you agree with it or not) because it's for something they care a lot about:

These games are not terrible. I'm not saying that they're bad. I'm saying that I didn't enjoy them.

The plot for Shadow of the Colossus is simple- you play as a young man who entered a desolate land with his horse, trying to revive the woman he loves. The only way to do so is by vanquishing the 16 Colossi that roam the land. The majority of these beasts are huge, and on paper, make for exciting battles since it's just you with your sword and bow against them. The world is beautifully lonely and I had fun exploring it.

My problem with SotC is that there isn't much to do aside from wait around. When I found out where a Colossus was, I'd get on my horse, take off, and spend several minutes going in a straight line (most of the time) to the desired location. Nothing would happen- no enemies would attack me, no natural disasters would happen, nothing challenging would prevent me from reaching the Colossus. Look, I'm not someone who needs something going on at all times, but this is how it was for every Colossus. Sometimes you'll have to climb a few buildings to reach the monsters, but it's over in a couple of minutes. The land is beautiful and if you want, you can explore every inch and see how much time the team put into creating it. However, there's nothing going on aside from an occasional animal wandering around.

Battling the Colossi was boring 90% of the time. Your horse is only required for two of the fights, and as others have mentioned- these are the most exciting ones. All of the other Colossi will slowly lumber around before they slowly charge up for an attack that should kill you in one hit, yet it only takes around 1/3 off your health bar. I'll admit that it was something scaling a Colossus, hanging on for dear life...at first. There are many points in the game where all the hero would do is flail about while the Colossus would shake violently, and I couldn't do anything for minutes at a time.It got boring. There's another Colossus, one of the smaller ones, that can knock you down and keep attacking you before you can get back up, killing you in a matter of minutes. It's not challenging, it's an annoying design choice. Why does the hero take forever getting back up? I KNOW I need to jump out of the way of the Colossus' attack, but I -can't- because the hero is so slow. This was the only fight that was a challenge for me, because I had to find the perfect spot to jump on his back without falling off, or find something to hide behind when he'd charge at me so I wouldn't get knocked down. And you know what really sucks? Realizing that the Colossi never start a fight. You feel like a jerk killing these poor things because they're just walking around, minding their own business.

A special mention needs to be given to the hero's horse. Controlling it is so cumbersome that it got me killed more times than I'd like to mention. There were also times when I'd whistle for it, only to have the horse keep running on past me and right at the foot of a Colossus. I get that the horse is supposed to be your only companion in this big, empty world, and there's supposed to be an emotional bond with it...but I never once cared if this thing survived a Colossus attack. I won't lie- there were a few times when I'd run it off a cliff just to see it fall.

Ico didn't fare any better with me. You play as a young boy who was imprisoned in a giant castle because he has horns. A girl with magic powers is locked up in the castle too, and you help her escape. This game is more puzzle-oriented, with a little more to do than SotC. However, the girl nearly caused me to quit the game. Want to run ahead to the next area that you know you need to go to? You can go there, but you'll need to hold her hand while you exit the room you're in. If not, she'll still be in the previous room, waiting for you to hold her hand and take her there. Shadow monsters coming in to attack you? You better hope to God that she's far away from them, as she doesn't put up much of a fight. For a magical woman that can manipulate objects, you'd think she'd do SOMETHING to combat these dark forces.

Of the two, I like Ico better as far as gameplay goes, but the girl was such a pain that I almost missed the horse from SotC. I beat SotC not that long ago, and I can only remember a few of the Colossi. I can't believe they were planning on putting more fights in that game. Both games can be completed in around 8 hours. Again, these are not terrible games. I just didn't care for either one. They obviously had time and effort put into them. They just weren't fun for me to play through. Maybe it's a good thing I missed out on them during the ps2 era. I was busy having fun and memorable experiences with Panzer Dragoon Orta and many others.

I do not recommend buying it until you see it in a bargain bin, and even then it probably won't be worth it because I don't think people will be playing this for very long.

I am waiting for the PS3 edition dropping in March of next year, so I picked this up to hold me off until then. Let me start by saying this port of the experience is not like the experience you get on the Wii, PS3 or Xbox 360. Of course the controls will be different (i.e. Wii Motion, PS3 Move, Xbox 360 Kinect). I am talking more about the graphics & gameplay. The graphics are cartoonish & the gameplay is simple. When you first start playing the game, it is really cool to see the Michael Jackson avatar dance along to the songs using the moves specific to that video as you hit the notes in time with the music. Though the longer you play through the 17 tracks, you will realize that the dance moves start getting a little repetitive during the course of the songs. Some moves even get recycled for other songs.

As far as the gameplay goes, it is simple but fun. The only two buttons you will be using to hit the notes will be the left d-pad & the "O" circle button. After you successfully hit enough gold points, you will fill up the gold star on the left side of the screen. When this happens, you will be prompted to press the triangle button to earn bonus point multipliers. You will also enter a screen during gameplay where you have to alternate between the left & right shoulder buttons to make him spin to earn points.

The cool thing about the game though, is to see the backdrops & outfits that were used in the original videos re-created for the game. As you progress, you unlock collectibles with the coins you earned. These collectibles have a descriptive story to each one as you scroll through them.

The game was a little different than I expected. I was hoping for a more complex system for hitting the notes as in using more of the button variations. And I was also hoping to see more realistic graphics as in the commercial for the Wii version. I know the PSP could have handled that.

But, Like I said before, the graphics are cartoonish in nature but sharp, the gameplay is simple but fun. For what it is, It's a cool game for the PSP, especially for kids. I would recommend purchasing this title.

So i'm about 12 hours in. I got the pip-boy edition but i'm reviewing the game itself instead of that. I'd actually knock a star off that cause the Galaxy S6 won't fit inside :( WTH guys, and it's by 1.4mm. seriously.

The game itself though is luckily great. This is my first time playing Fallout on a console. I've played all the rest on PC and my wife actually got a 980 TI before this game's release so she could run it very well, so i've had the opportunity to compare graphics and performance with her PC.

Pros:
1. Third person is finally good. I use it most of the time in this game, it makes melee fighting more fun and still works great for shooting. Did I mention melee fighting is more fun? Cause people react, you're not just hitting a brick wall. Plus you can melee with every weapon!
2. Crafting. I really didn't craft much in 3 and new vegas... I love the system in this game. Pick up everything you find, go home, 'move all junk' button, and then go to the weapon or armor bench... Add a bayonet to a rifle, a new site to a pistol, extra pockets to pieces of armor (to increase storage capacity), add flames to your power armor... I mean it's pretty robust. I didn't play with the settlement creation too much, but honestly it's impressive. You can put stuff wherever you want, at any angle, and it'll work for the most part.
3. Graphics. Shut up. I like them. The ps4 has hiccups but generally the game looks great. Watching my wife's PC at ultra next to the ps4 isn't night and day.. it's a really keen eye staring at some edges, maybe some more bushes and a slightly further view distance... but the game still looks great on console. However if you're from the school of thought that the game looks terrible in general - I can't convince you. If you look at it on the surface, no it isn't The Witcher 3 or Until Dawn or something... But think about how dynamic the environment is, how bodies stay forever from every battle and how you can custom build entire towns in this game that live in the open world. I feel keeping the graphics simple and targeting a brighter art style was a worthy exchange for the world we get to experience. Plus imagine how bad the glitches would be if they went one level harder with graphics :P If you're a graphic nazi though you should be playing on PC and you'll get your high res mods soon.
4. Dialogue - is good. I like how there is always a sarcastic option. It fits my character perfectly.
5. Awesome new enemy types
6. Grenades are a button, not something you have to equip by itself (more on that in cons)
7. Power Armor feels special and powerful
8. QUICKSAVE! I don't know if Fallout 3 or vegas had this on consoles, but I was blown away that a console game has a quicksave button. Thank god for it.
9. You can put clothing on your dog.
10. So far most of the characters I've run into feel natural and are pretty interesting.

Stuff I don't love or hate-
1. The critical system. I always do high luck in games because of criticals... now criticals are treated like Final Fantasy limit breaks but way less climatic. Critical work with a meter that fills up every time you use VATS or certain perks. During an attack (the actual attack, not while selecting the attack) you press an extra button to turn the attack into a critical. I don't love that system. I like random crits, I unfortunately forget a lot about the crit button and end up not using it nearly enough.
2. Leveling in general - goodbye skill system, hello really simple perk/special system. There are 7 stats with 10 perks each, 1 for each level. You can also level up the stat itself. Every level up you can level any 1 thing up and many perks have multiple levels now. So to max everything out you'll have to be roughly at level 210. That's maxing out every stat and maxing out every associated perk.
That's fine and only the most dedicated player will get that far, but it feels a lot less like i'm focusing on my strengths and instead working with a system to get a specific move or benefit. Even stuff like lock picking falls under a perk, level 1 lets you do advanced locks, level 2 lets you do expert locks, ect... Instead of building up a skill that will naturally make me better.
I mean, it's not bad, it's just different, and I love how it used to be. I'm getting used to this, and there is some amazing variety and bonuses for maxing out a perk, but it may take me a while to love this system.

Cons:
1. Why the hell is the melee button the same as the grenade button? Hold it down for a sec and you'll throw a grenade and tap it to just attack. I've blown myself up so many times.
2. It's a little glitchy. I mean, what did you expect? I've had nothing game breaking but i've had some weird conversations that ended up getting completely repeated. But that's it so far...

I almost chose to give it 4 stars instead of 3 because I'm scared of how angry the supporters of this game are. But it had flaws. And one of them were especially disappointing for a brand new piece of hardware -
-The frame-rate drops are not excusable. Certain areas are painfully sluggish.
-The weapon breaking and temporary buff nature of this game are very odd features for such a long game. Though the ability to cook and create things is pretty nice, it's unfortunate that so much effort can lead to just 3 minutes of benefit. You can't repair or modify weapons to make them better really and the fact they break in 3-4 combos for the most part is pretty painful. All enemies drop weapons you can use to defeat them but it really makes being rewarded a special sword or something seem very pointless...
-The dungeons were easily my favorite part of the game, but there are so few and while fun, they're very short. Most of the game has this quantity over quality feel to it, with so many generic shrines (aesthetically at least, the actual puzzles were almost always different, some more creative than others. But they kind of blur together eventually) and those seeds... but the dungeons are the opposite. So few and very high quality feeling.
-The weather really hurt the pacing sometimes.
-Voice acting. Just because this is the first Zelda game with serious voice acting that isn't an excuse for putting such little effort into it when the rest of the industry is doing pretty excellent.
-Most of the side quests/upgrades are just fetch quests. Eventually nothing was very difficult... you just had to have patience. And that's fine for a few hours, but when you have to wait through weeks of in-game days (even with a fire) to farm scales it's unnecessary and not fun.
-My biggest pain point was that ultimately this didn't feel like much of a Zelda game. It felt closer to open world Ubisoft games where there is a serious quantity over quality issue related to the number of map points, items to collect, and places to go but a lack of relevance as to 'why' and little effort to mix up.
-Since this game really nailed that 'true open world' experience there was no story progression. Only a beginning, end and a few non-sequential story points scattered throughout the middle (dungeons). The memories were more world building.

Almost perfect.
I got this right before a group of friends came to my place for a seasonal party. So perfect timing. However first flaw showed up instantly - limited to 4 players. The switch can handle 8 controllers however this game has a hard limit at 4. It feels more lack of wanting to rebalance and build the game than a hardware limitation.
Second gripe is the reliance on luck. The bonus stars are meant to offset this a bit, however winning minigames does not really help you win the game, good dice rolls do. And you have limited control there. For a game with only 10 turns, for example, you shouldn't be able to roll a 0 two times in a row. Yes your standard dice can't, and maybe that's enough balance to have options, but a reroll ability or some type of throw me a bone mechanic would be nice.

That's all I got negative. Otherwise this game is excellent.
-The coop river rapid mode is an oddly amazing addition after one of your friends feels like the game totally jipped them in party mode. My friends wanted to replay this one a few times.
-The coop party (vs) mode has really cool mechanics and options that I sort of wish the main party mode could have.
-The dance games are actually pretty fun, as long as the controller is reliable.
- the number of characters is great and everyone at my party could find someone they liked
- the load times are great and the instant sample of every game before you play is very well done

I'll give this a 5 if they update and add any of these
-handicap mode, especially if you want a casual game, to add mechanics for a reroll or something to balance the randomness of dice
- A fast mode, where the minor actions, happen at a 2 or 3x rate. This would be especially nice for AI players.
-Extra player support, even if it's just a stylized way to have 4 teams of 2

So my daughter had a DS Lite and traded it in at GameStop to get the DSi xl. We didn't know what to expect because we pre-ordered it and just hoped it lived up to our expectations. It definitely does and here is my little list of good and bad...

Good
*The screen is quite a bit larger making it easier and more fun to play with picture editor.
*It comes with a full size pen stylus AND the small one that fits in the DSi
*It comes with 2 brain age games already loaded on it and the photo editor.
*It has a full web browser if you have a wireless network at home.

Bad
*The web browser is time consuming and almost useless because of all the scrolling you have to do to see a whole page.
*Like the DSi it does NOT have the GBA port at the bottom so you cannot play Guitar Hero on this.
*The only thing you are getting more than the DSi is a bigger system and a couple of preloaded games.

If you already have a DSi I wouldn't upgrade unless you really really want a larger syster (and it's not really THAT much larger. My daughter had the Lite and it was 3 years old so it was worth trading in for $60 at Gamestop for a credit towards the XL. Because it's brand new it doesn't have a lot of accessories yet and the screen protector pack I bought her only came with 1 screen protector for the bottom screen.

This game has several different playground oriented games to play.  My son at age 4 loved playing the paper airplane racer and the car race that looks like hot wheels cars on one of their plastic tracks.  There is also handball and tetherball which he got the hang of quickly.  This is one of the first games he could play on his own without my constantly helping him along.  If your kids are older... above 7 probably...  then I don't know if I'd get it.  My 10 yr old plays it with her brother just to do something with him but it isn't her first choice when she wants to play Wii.  Good family fun if you want to include the whole gang.

This Wii game is made up of tons of mini games.  It's great for kids that have short attention spans and want to try a lot of different things.  Not so great for kids that like to start a game that progresses and has levels.  I found that it leads to arguments between my kids with choosing which game they are going to play since they are so short.  Some of the games are easy enough for my 4 yr old to play and others are a little tricky, but overall I'd say that it's good for all ages, even young ones.  My 10 yr old only plays this when she has to play something that her brother can play with her.

My husband and 10 yr old daughter played this game every day until they completed the game, then they went back and tried to get the gold medal on each level.  They loved it.  I found it a little hard and headache inducing.  If you don't hold the gun perfectly level at all times the screen spins around and around until you level it out again which makes me dizzy.  My husband got the hang of it pretty quickly, and my daughter too.  There are two ways to play, either a career type thing where you go along on a long string of hunts looking for specific animals and trying to find the trophy animal of the herd/group/gaggle.  Or you can play like the old nintendo way that Duck Hunt was, the animals or birds come out onto the screen and you try to shoot as many as you can in the time allotted.  This game was a big hit in my house and was worth purchasing.

I have had Wii fit for about a year and a half and have enjoyed it but wanted something more. Wii Fit is fun with the games and stuff, but I really wanted a more intense trainer style workout while at home. I started the "6 Week Challenge" on this game and am getting much more of a workout than I ever got with Wii Fit! I purchased this game from Amazon and bought the leg strap, resistance band and some boxing hand weighted gloves from Target in the video game section for pretty inexpensive. I do not have the first EA Sports Active, only this More Workouts so I can't compare the two or tell you how different it is.

This game will work with the Wii balance board and will keep track of your weight for you if you want it to. It also helps you with getting your diet and daily activities in proper order if you take advantage of the daily diary they offer to enter your food and other activities besides Wii exercise. You create your own person on the screen and as you exercise your person moves in sync with you. There is a smaller box in the bottom right corner with a person doing the exercise telling you when to move and what to do. So far, the only exercise my Wii has had a problem with picking up properly are crunches. I can't get it to register when I'm up or down, no matter how much I move the Wii-mote according to their direction. It was frustrating and caused me to skip that exercise all together and I just did them on my own for the number of reps they had on the screen.

You do not need to have a balance board. During setup it asks if you have one and would like to use it, just make no. You will want some kind of floor mat if you don't have carpet. You are on the floor for the stretching and crunches and is pretty uncomfortable without it. You can workout on your own, with a friend or choose to do the 6 week challenge with goals set and days programmed for you to work out with your "trainer" through a preset workout that is very effective! Raising and lower your heartrate and mixing in some strength training with the resistence band and some boxing (I recommend getting weighted gloves to enhance the boxing which is the funnest part for me)

You have 2 different ways to play so it's like having 2 games in one. There is a puzzle way... Figure out how to get the princess back to the castle without the pack of wolves eating her and without killing the wolves. There is the adventure play... Your character has to find a way to retrieve the star from each level to move on to the next. You are given the basic scene and instructions for each level and then it's up to your imagination to figure a way out. For instance... You have to get a star in the bottom of the sea but there are sharks and pirhanas and eels between you and the star. You first need a scuba tank to be able to swim, then you need to come up with something to kill the other animals so they don't kill you. We figured out that a toaster in the water would electricute them although I'm sure many other things would work as well. There are so many options that your mind is the limit.

I bought this game as a gift for my husband because he's a huge Metallica fan.  I am so glad that it has turned out to be his favorite Guitar Hero game of all! I must admit that I have only ever heard about 4 of the songs on the list (wasn't a metal fan in High School, and still am not) and find them to be EXTREMELY challenging when you have no clue of what's coming up in the song.  The guitar solos and all around playing are quite hard (we always play on Medium).  On the other Guitar Hero games and on Band Hero I can generally get up in the high 90's on all songs and play on Hard for a few songs.  With this game I am barely hanging in the 80's on Medium for most songs.  Mostly because of my lack of familiarity with the songs and rhythms.  Being both a Guitar Hero and Metallica fan my husband has give this game two enormous thumbs up and highly recommends it.  Being a Guitar Hero fan and loving a challenge I give it 2 thumbs up for giving me something I have to work at!  A must have!

I originally had this game for Gamecube, but now I also bought it for the DS. I really like this game, and I think it is a game more suited for handhelds than it is for bigger systems. This game is pretty simple and easygoing. You move to a new town and you don't have any money at first. You start off doing odd jobs for the local retailer, who is also the person that built your house. After a short time your are freed from working for the retailer, but you still have a hefty loan left to pay him for building your house. To pay it off, you have to do whatever you can. You can do favors for neighbors and in most cases they reward you with money or objects - the objects they give you, you can sell to make money. You can also fish, catch bugs, and dig - and whatever you find doing these things can always be sold. Of course, if you choose not to sell stuff there are other things you can do as well. You can always keep any thing you've got and use it for your house. You can donate fish, bugs, fossils and paintings to the local museum. Finding new bugs and fish is tricky, however, because the game is in real-time and some insects and fish only come out in certain seasons, but it's fun to see how the museum builds up over time and how many different types of insects and fish you have caught.

You can also send letters to the neighbors, and give them gifts, both of which makes them like you more (and give you better and better gifts!) Another fun part of the game is trying to find objects to make your house look it's best. Your house gets rated from time to time and you want to make your house as spiffy as possible.

Holidays and birthdays are fun in this game because the neighbors actually acknowledge them and do things to celebrate. Like on July 4th there is a fireworks show in the town square.

One thing that is new to this game is that you can be friends with other animal crossing players around the world and you can visit their towns, and they can visit yours too.

I love this game and I think it's great because there are so many things you can do in the game and so many things you can explore, and some things I probably didn't even mention because there is so much. But I digress, the game goes at a rather slow pace and if you like games with more action this is not the game for you. This is one of the more creative games I have ever seen. You have to have an open mind to play this type of game, because the game is much like real life in the sense that you never really know what will happen next, the game changes as you go along.

I highly recommend everyone to give this game a try. It can be very addictive. You may even be surprised at how much you like it once you start playing.

In the The Sims2 Castaways you get stranded on an island and you have to do whatever you can to survive. You fish, hunt for bugs and build things that help you progress. Here are some pros and cons:

Pros:

-it has simple and easy to use controls
-there are actual goals in this game which you have to pass in order to progress
-the goals are challenging but not not enough to frustrate you and make you not want to play
-there are a lot of places to explore and objects to interact with
-as you go along in the game you can meet other people that are stranded on the island
-you can craft tools and clothes and other objects
-this game has needs like the Sims computer games

Cons:

-some of the objects are really hard to find
-its hard to keep friendships with some of the the other islanders

Overall the gameplay is just what the typical Sims 2 player is expecting. All the needs are the same; bladder, hunger, hygiene, etc. What really sets this game apart and makes it fun is that you have to figure out what to do to get what you need, and maybe find a way off the island. It's like Survivor: the sim version. Having goals also makes you feel like there is a purpose to the game. I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes the Sims.

Good game. The puzzles are challenging and interesting, and there are plenty of them. What is good is that the solutions are always within reach, and you get three hints - which you have to buy - but a lot of the puzzles you don't really need hints for if you think hard enough.

There is not very much I can say about this game that other reviewers have not already said. This game is obviously well thought out. It is amazingly full of detail. The developers managed to squeeze all of Liberty City into such a tiny cartridge, and they did it with flair. The city is bustling with life.

Unlike console versions of GTA where raids and stake-outs are large scale, with 20 characters shooting at you all at once, the developers of this game kept in mind that this a hand held and they scaled down these battles as well. This is a plus since trying to take out 20 or so gangsters on the DS might have felt a bit overwhelming.

This game takes good advantage of the DS touch screen. It's use is seamless and it is used in interesting ways like scratch cards, digging in dumpsters, hot-wiring cars, selling drugs, and more. The use of the touch screen takes the customary GTA tasks and makes them interactive. This is another plus because it makes you feel that much more involved in the game.

The only tiffs I have with China Town Wars are that the radio stations don't have any of the funny dialogue or any recognizable songs - this is understandable, and doesn't take anything away from the game at all - and that the graphics of the story scenes are kind of ugly, luckily the dialogue is just as off beat and funny as the console versions. These things weren't big enough cons for me to take any stars away from my rating.

Overall, I am very happy to have bought this game. It is a great addition to the collection of any GTA fan, and the best adult DS game that I have seen so far. Every time I turn it on I find out something new. This game is definitely worth owning, even for those who are not the biggest GTA fans. This game will not disappoint.

Graphics: 5/10 - The colour shading is nice when you're playing outside, but for the rest of the time, this looks pretty effortless and droopy. It's also hard to see where a passage leads.
Sound: 5/10 - The usual cartoon racing score hangs in the background, while the cars don't do anything too dramatic with their engines.
Value: 5/10 - Most racing games are worth the money because they're entertaining, but to make a long story short, this one isn't really worth paying for unless you're a really big fan of the muppets.
Overall: 5/10 - This is the sort of game you play in the game or record store while your waiting for Mum to finish her grocery shopping. In a game where you can hardly see where you're going, is it worth even playing? Yes, but only if Mum takes a couple of hours to find a broccoli stick.

Sound: 9/10 - Great uses of evil voicing and fantastic sound editing detail makes Crash 3's sound get a notch up.
Value: 10/10 - You'll be begging for more!
Overall: 10/10 - Fantastically detailed game that mixes genres and characters into a big story that erupts with fabulous enjoyment. In short: buy it.

Graphics: 8/10 - Really neat little things you might not notice. Sometimes a little too computerized, but still eye-catching.

Value: 10/10 - This is one game you will start repeatedly and still have the same enjoyment level every time you play.
Overall: 9/10 - A big improvement from the great first game. Crash Bandicoot 2: Cortex Strikes Back has it all - story, characters, levels and fantastically constructed colouring and visuals.

Graphics: 8/10 - These are often stunning but at times a bit murky. Mostly they are really fabulous to look at, though, in every scene the makers of Crash have put in a lot of effort.
Sound: 7/10 - The animals could've made some more sounds but the creatures that talk do it clearly and well. Mostly the score is playing in the background so there isn't much sound to be heard.
Value: 9/10 - Value for money indeed! Once you've finished, you'll want to start all over again!

Graphics: 9/10 - Fantastic effort in this area. There is hardly a fault to be found, all the settings look fabulously well-planned.
Sound: 8/10 - Good dragon sound effects and neat little sparkling sounds as you collect and find things. The little things matter, and the big things boom!
Value: 8/10 - I haven't played this game much, but after my friend let me have a turn, I was really intrigued! Spyro 2, because it has neat missions and cool effects, is well worth the price you pay to buy or rent it.
Overall: 8/10 - I would like to play this game more. It is intriguing and not too hard, but has the odd dose of complexity that gives it the intelligence and less cuteness than most of the fantasy-creature games.

Graphics: 7/10 - Neat character creations and fantastic hard guns make up for the occasional sense of effortlessness in the graphics.
Sound: 9/10 - Great guns fire away with heart-pounding brilliance in sound and editing!
Value: 10/10 - With fun games like Duke Nukem: Time to Kill, you can't get enough. It's worth the money you pay for it because it's fabulously entertaining and will keep you glued to the screen for ages!
Overall: 8/10 - Dirty, sexy, hilarious, neat, action-packed, thrilling, fun...it would take another few reviews to put all the adjectives that describe this game. Just play it and see for yourself! Not recommended for people under 16 years of age.

Graphics: 9/10 - Nothing is ugly in Ape Escape, it all looks totally fabulous. The character movements and designs are extremely nice and the attacks and training scenes are all beautifully put together.
Sound: 8/10 - A groovy score and neat sound editing techniques make Ape Escape's sound thoroughly plausible.
Value: 9/10 - Endlessly fun to play. Ape Escape is a game you will start once and start again, start once and start again. You'll play it so many times; you may take over 10 whole memory cards!
Overall: 9/10 - This shouldn't be overlooked because of its frankly silly plot. It's stunningly enjoyable to play and really gives a good use to the analogue controller.

This is a great controller for gamers who want a more classic feel for their fighting games. Coming from the days of Street Fighter Arcade, it was hard to make the transition from large buttons and a joystick to a d-pad and thumb buttons, and holding a ps2-ps3 controller in one hand was difficult. This controller's unique design allows players to hold the left side of the controller tightly and use index and middle fingers to press the buttons. The controller feels well made and solid and the buttons are really satisfying to press. The buttons are large and make a solid clunk when pressed, like miniature arcade buttons. Another unique feature is the rotating/angling d-pad. Although I never found a need to rotate it, I'm sure that super serious fighters will swear that it makes all the difference. From the picture it was clear that this was missing the digital (wobble) sticks from the standard PS3 controller. I thought that this could make navigating menus between fights cumbersome or all together impossible. The manufacturer of this controller over came this with a switch in the middle that allows you to turn the d-pad into the left or right digital stick, an awesome idea. Although you still have to flip the switch, it is much quicker than picking up your standard controller. This is a corded controller but the cord is so long I rarely notice it. This controller also has a turbo feature, which although not really useful for me in fighters, was kinda handy in mmorpgs where you may need to press a button a few thousand times,(ahem..DCUO).
The only downside I have experienced with this controller is when you dominate your friends in Tekken Hybrid or Soul Caliber, they sometimes blame your "special" controller.

This is a great headset for PS3 multi-player gaming.I have used a few different blue-tooth headsets on my PlayStation before but the inconvenience of pairing them or turning them on and off for lack of a mute button often led me to plug in an old Logitech PS2 headset. This is a great wired replacement! It has volume controls and a mute button in the cord that is easy to reach and use while playing. The sound is good and the ear piece is comfortable. The microphone is on a long bendable piece that is easy to position in front of your mouth and rotates around so it can come from the left or right side of your face. These are not full stereo gaming headphones, but as a stand alone headset for chat, they work great.

Every real guitar player who has played games like Guitar Hero or Rock Band has said something like, "Man, wouldn't it be cool if you could use a real guitar?". This game finally did it and did it VERY well!

Using the included cord, players plug their actual electric guitar into their PS3. The game then helps you set up and tune your guitar for the game. The first tuneup places the player in a stadium and each successfully tuned string causes roars of applause from a virtual audience. It is about this time the player realizes, "I am actually going to play my own guitar in a video game!".

Similar to games like Rock Band, Rocksmith uses colored bars moving down the screen to tell players when to pluck a certain string and hold each fret. The guitar as a controller gives much more variation than on/off button presses. The game integrates bends and slides as well has hammer-ons and pull-offs. For users unfamiliar with these terms, don't worry, the game gives very useful and descriptive technique instruction and plenty of practice to get them right.

The songs available with the game are GREAT and I enjoyed learning and playing all of them. Fortunately these songs are great and fun to replay because there aren't as many DLC (downloadable content) songs available for this as there are for other rock games and they are typically $2.99 each. Fans of Rush and Queen and a few other bands will find song packs available that save you a couple bucks if you buy 4 or 5 songs packs.

This game is a MUST-BUY for any level of guitar player who needs more opportunity to feel like a Real rock star!

UPDATE: A $29.99 expansion for bass players adds bass support and bass lines for all the standard content and previously released DLC music.

So many improvements from the first Rocksmith!
First I would like to say that as a guitar player, the original Rocksmith provided hours and hours of fun while learning to play some new songs. For that reason alone I would have bought this version just for the new songs to practice and learn. I was surprised to find how much Ubisoft was able to improve upon an already great product!

Features that used to take a long time to unlock, are now available from the beginning. Song difficulty is easy to change in the practice mode, so experienced players can turn up the difficulty so they aren't just plunking one or two notes during the whole song. You can also adjust difficulty for just a particular section of a song, so if you really want to focus on a solo or know the chords to a section, you can turn those sections up while letting the game adjust difficulty automatically in areas you might not know as well.

This game has also been fun for family members that do play guitar. The scaling difficulty really does allow players of all levels to play the game and most of the music is great and easy to listen to.

Overall, if your looking for more of the same Rocksmith, or would like to learn to play the guitar in a no pressure home environment, this is a sure thing!

This PS3 version of Minecraft is a blast, just like its PC and XBOX clones. Listed below are some of my favorite features and a few features I did not like.

Favorite Features:
1. Play Minecraft on your TV/PS3 in HD: Being able to use a big TV for Minecraft makes a real difference in enjoying the expansive terrains and various biomes.

2. Built in tutorials: Unlike older versions where you had to learn everything as you played or consult the internet, this console version includes a beginner tutorial to familiarize users with the basic actions in the game and controls.

3.SPLIT SCREEN!: This is by far my favorite feature. Being able to run around your world and build and create with someone sitting next to you adds a new aspect of fun to survival and creative games. It is great to play alone in your world then have a friend jump right in to help you build great structures, care for crops and livestock, or explore the virtually endless randomly generated world.

Least favorite features:

1. Not Cross platform: I know there must be technical issues to overcome but since this game is such a faithful recreation of vanilla Minecraft, I wish I could play with friends who have the XBOX or PC version. Unfortunately you cannot.

2. Console controls tough for some PC players: When my friend who loves PC Minecraft plays with me he is always complaining about the controls being so much better on PC. This may just be his preference.

3. No Modding: The PC version of Minecraft has every mod imaginable to change the way the game plays, from DAYZ survival style to Pokemon capturing. Unfortunately these are not available for console users.

Overall Minecraft is an incredible game that can be very satisfying and peaceful, and frantic and frustrating. This PS3 version has everything from the vanilla game so you can mine and craft on your console.

This game is the PERFECT solution for PS3 owners who love Vanilla Minecraft and want to split screen with friends!
