Ah, Christ. I wish "Alice in Wonderland" had never entered public domain. I'm so stick of these bloody, steampunk versions. You've seen one, you've seen them all.

And this one is no different: the same predictable look that you've seen done a hundred times so far.

. . . which leaves the gameplay, which isn't compelling.

Here's a example of what I mean: I played about halfway through this game and then had to leave on vacation. In other words, I was interrupted mid-way.

When I came back, I was surprised to find it in my PS console. I had totally forgotten I had been playing it.

That shouldn't happen with a video game. A good game should compel you -- even haunt you -- while you're on vacation.

This one is really just a bunch of annoying timed and jumping puzzles. It's like the creators had no other ideas than to do what we've all seen a jillion times before and we're all sick of.

Worse, the game makes you pay for all these weapons and then has it so they don't affect most monsters.

The creator of this game, American McGee, is a drooling idiot who needs to be restrained . . . and then flogged.

I'm stunned that everybody is talking about this game and that it's selling so well. I mean, it's got nothing! It's just pure gimmick. How can I be the only one who sees that?

Consider: the story is awful. Most of the time you don't know what you're trying to accomplish or why. You spend the first half of the movie attempting to ring a couple of bells, for example, but you never learn why this is necessary. Then you have to collect a bunch of souls. It's never explained why this is necessary: it's just that it's stipulated that it is before you're permitted to move on to the next level. What's stopping me from simply marching off to Gwyn's headquarters, doing battle with him, and taking his job forthwith without further ado? Beats me.

I can think of a long list of other reasons why this game is totally forgettable. The interface is poorly done (think of how awkward it is to equip items, sell something, or search your inventory). The characters are silly (e.g., Mushroom people? A giant floating worm? That's the best you can do?). The graphics are unremarkable (think of the way water looks in this game, such as when one of the hydras shoots at you). Even the setting makes no sense (like I'm so sure there'd be merchants setting up shop in in the middle of the battlefield).

And the combat! The combat is very awkward. For the most part it consists of just one cheap shot on you after another. Boss fights are confusing because the bosses are so huge that your view is typically obstructed by the posterior of some giant demon. You can't even see your guy, so most of the time you're just swinging wildly.

Most unforgivably, you can't pause! What infernal innovation is this? A video game that's intensive is one thing: a video game that punishes you for having children or wanting to answer the phone is something else entirely.

Despite all these things, I managed to make it all the way through this game.

And I would have to say, of all video games I've played, this was the worst, the most hateable. You might think you've played an unfair, sadistic video game before. Hah! You don't know from sadism until you've played this. The whole time I was playing it, it was like being in an abusive relationship. You don't want to back out of it because you told all your friends and family you were doing it, but it gives you no joy when you're with the person.

That's what I'll remember about this game: it gave me no joy. With other games, you might hoop and holler when you accomplish something. In this game, when you beat a boss monster or survive a level, you find yourself with a dirty "that's it? that's all I get?" kind of feeling.

Have you ever driven down to some government office, struggled to find parking, and then waited in line, only to learn that you didn't bring some document you needed? Remember the feeling you had driving home? Well, that's the feeling you'll have when playing this game: a unrewarding waste of time that provides no delight, no satisfaction, and no sense of getting anywhere.

In fact, this game only has one thing, one claim to fame. It's very difficult. Not enjoyable, original, mind-blowing, genre-expoding, or even immersive; no, no -- just difficult.

Soon after this game was released there was a video online of a guy who raced through the entire game in about 1.5 hours, using some sort of cheat. Seeing that helped me understand something about this game: see, if the game played like normal video games (such as Skyrim or Diablo), you'd be done with the entire thing in about 4 or 5 hours. That's how little there is here.

But coding all that content is expensive, so what I imagine the gamemakers did once they were about a third of the way through the coding was say, "Hey, instead of doing all that pesky level-creation, let's just ratchet up the difficulty instead!" It's a substitute for game content, you see. Make the hits of monsters incredibly damaging, while having your hits be puny. And every time you die, you have to do everything all over again. That way, the game will take you hundreds of hours before you can complete it and feel like a full game.

Making it so difficult was clever in another way, too: Geeks are notoriously competitive, so even though the game aggressively has no story, content, originality, etc., there's still a sizeable subculture of geeks out there who will be drawn to the game merely so they can boast that they got through it. Enough at least to make producing such a game financially worthwhile for a software company.

But "difficult" is not even the word for what this game is. A more precise phrase would be "infuriatingly repetitive." When you die, as I say, all the enemies repopulate. But they're all in the exact same spots and attack you in the exact same ways and at the exact same moment every time you draw near. So to beat the level, all you have to do is learn how to hit here, run to there, shield up here, arrow there, etc. at the correct times. In other words, the fact that you're getting more skillful at the game is an illusion: you're actually just memorizing a maze, like those guys who used to memorize patterns in Pac-Man.

What would true difficulty look like? Howabout having the nature, number, timings, and strategies of the monsters changing with every attempt to clear an area? That way, clearing an area would truly be a matter of skill and quick thinking rather than simple memorization.

Perhaps you say, no, no; you don't get it! The whole point of the game is to be sadistic. It's for people who like to play sadistic games!

If that's the case, you masochists need to ramp up your standards, for if sadism is what draws you to this game, it's also going to prove a let-down in that area.

After all, your character can defend himself. Not just that, but your character can get more powerful. One can try and try again to clear an area. The game's rules make a kind of internal sense. And most importantly, the game is finishable.

You find this satisfyingly sadistic? Hah! Move over. Here's some ideas for a sadistic game: levels that cannot be completed because you come across locked doors to which there is no key; powerful items in merchants' inventories that are always out of stock; monsters that can damage you but cannot be damaged in turn; puzzles that cannot be solved by any means; instructions that cannot be followed; floors that suddenly give way below you, without your being able to do anything about it; monsters that arbitrarily change their resistances; weapons that suddenly break; traps that cannot be avoided; spells that suddenly don't work; savegame files that become corrupted for no discernbile reason. Or how about this: every time you die, it randomly deletes savefiles from other games on your PS3. Or how about, most evilly, a game that couldn't be finished by any known means? Now THAT would be sadism.

In comparison to such a vision, this game is child's play -- sadism light. What I'm saying is that if agony is your bag, you should also account this game a failure because it only glancingly provides it.

When this game finishes, it sends you right back, willy-nilly, to the beginning for something called NG+, which is supposed to be much harder. Folks, I immediately popped the game out of my console, never tempted for a second to open that cursed cell door.

I confess I was moved (pity?) to buy this because I had heard the stunning news that the state of Rhode Island was leveraged in bonds to the hilt, and, by investing heavily in this game, thought they could dig their way out of the red.

It's basically a WoW clone, with nothing particularly different to recommend it: same sorts of spells, weapons, characters, enemies, plot points, settings, you name it.

It got unpleasant to play after a while because the camera, which you pretty much have to control with a mouse, jerks around so fast (even if you slow it down in the options) that you'll soon be seasick.

This is a completely unremarkable first-person shooter. Evidently some alien robots are plotting something dastardly in the jungles of Central America, and it's your job to make your way through their base of operations, shooting them as they obligingly pop out from behind obstacles in native villages (whose city planners for some reason seem to have designed their living quarters to resemble paintball arenas).

One thing that makes this one different is that, from time to time, you get to use a jet pack, and that offers moments of good clean fun floating about.

But there are problems.

The first is that you don't get to simply float about with this jetpack exploring the world: this is not one of those games that encourages you to explore the world. Every time you get to use the jet pack, there are aerial enemies that must be defeated.

Sadly, it's this very combat that dampens the fun of this game. While exploring with the jetpack is fun in theory, fighting with it in the air is typically not, on account of your usually not knowing where enemies are, the way you certainly would if you really were flying through the air with a jetpack. Instead, getting your guy to face the enemy can be tiresome and annoying. Usually, if there's an enemy in front of you to be shot, it's just a conincidence: it's not like you were able to hunt him down or guess his next move. Most of the time you're flying in the wrong direction.

Another problem is that this is another one of those cookie-cutter adventures. We present these problems for you, and there is only one way to solve them. No other ways will be accepted. You're going to follow the path this way, in this order, and accomplish the goal in this way, regardless of what your other ideas might be. For example, you're only allowed to use your jetpack to jet to pre-approved places that the programmers provided the coding for. The world you're in may appear open and inviting, but in reality you're forced to walk a narrow but invisible gangplank to get from here to there. There are many cases when you can think of ways of flanking your enemy, but no such luck: invisible walls prevent you from going any further in that direction, or landing on this or that ledge. Why? Do I have an effin' jetpack or not? Then why can't I use it?

Most troublingly, though, the game falters storywise. The whole premise of aliens setting up shop deep in the jungles of Central America during WWII was certainly a worthy one, but only if you allow yourself to be restricted by it. The gamemakers certainly did not. Suddenly they all speak English? And your native guide suddenly starts talking like he's from Southern California? And they go nowhere with the story: I was taken by surprise when the credits rolled. That's the end?! I felt the story had gone nowhere.

I've played this game through three times completely, to 100% -- although once I was cheating.

I can tell you this: it's far better on the PC, assuming you have a fast system.

The PS3 version is a disaster for several reasons:

1. The loading times are long and frequent! Get ready to spend a long time staring at a black screen.
2. The mechanics of the Playstation controller work against you. For example, when you are about to take down a warchief, one of the things you can do on a computer is unload all of your arrows into his head from a distance. Then, when his health is about half down, you close in for combat. But you aren't able to do this with a PS controller: your right thumb is far less precise than a computer mouse, so you'll only be able to get about 2 or 3 shots in before your focus is exhausted.
3. "Last chance" events are super easy on the PC. You're going to miss a lot of them on PS3 because the cursor moves a lot slower. I know you can go into the options to adjust "camera sensitivity," but if you do, every time your character turns his head around the world whips around, disorienting you. You don't have this problem on the PC.
4. The graphics are not as good on the PS3 as they are on the PC.
5. The button combos are much trickier on the PS3 to handle well, for advanced moves. For example, if you want to sneak up on a prisoner to release him or a flower to pick it, you're sneaking with your forefinger on R2. But you have to lift your forefinger from R2 to R1 to actually release the prisoner or pick the flower. During this split second, your character stands up and you can be seen by enemies. I've died many times this way. On the computer, it's much easier: there's no conflict between LSHIFT and LCTRL. (Even if there was, you could remap it.) One solution is to play with your middle finger on R2 to sneak about, reserving one's forefinger for R1, but this feels unnatural to me.
6. There are some things you can do on the PC version that you simply aren't allowed to do on the PS3 version, even leaving aside the awkward layout of the controls. An example is sneaking up behind an Uruk and holding him. On the PC, you can sneak up to him and move into the hold seamlessly. On the PS3, though, this is not permitted, so your character must stand up for about a second before he is allowed to hold the Uruk. During this second though, the Uruk frequently gets a whack at you.

The essential, unfixable, unworkaroundable problem with this game on the PS3 is this: it is too much for the system's resources. The graphics -- and the fact that the game does not scruple to load 20 orcs simultaneously to attack you -- tax the PS3's resources beyond what they were purposed to endure. The effect of this is that frequently when you push triangle or square when set upon by enemies on all sides, the game won't register it, or register it in time. The CPU is simply too busy. Thus you're frequently going to miss many blocks and "last chance" saving throws that someone sitting next you to can plainly see you hit in time.

All of these reasons mean that the game ends up being FAR HARDER on Playstation 3.

This thing might be better on the PS4, but I have no direct knowledge to convey.

A clone of ModNation Racers, nothing more. Utterly nothing original about it. It's the same as every other karting game for every other platform.

Additionally, you aren't given the option of having others not attack you, meaning you can't focus on racing. Since "defense" is unreliable, whether you win the races or not is pretty much a matter of pure chance. It doesn't matter how quick your reflexes are or how well you know the track. Kids may not mind the looniness of this (perhaps viewing it as analogous to the world around them), but it's sure to puzzle and then infuriate any adult.

Having said that, though, I must admit it's not difficult: you can usually win each track within three tries.

The game has a lot to it: you can make your own tracks and race other users' tracks. If, however, you simply race through the tracks in a rush to get to the end, you'll finish the game in about 4 hours.

The game has a good amount of levels, but difficulty spikes sharply at random. Its Angry Birds so you know what you are getting, wich is nothing really special. The absence of bgm is actually distracting. Still, overall fun with levels having good variety.

As one of the last games to be made for the 3DS I had to give it a try. This is actually my first time playing any persona games. But seeing as it was made by Atlus I knew it had to be good, right? Well yes, the game and story are very enjoyable. My three star rating comes from the ridiculous DLC cash grab.

Like many other reviewers have stated, playing solo is beyond a chore, and playing online is just as frustrating. Good luck finding a compident player, let alone two. Still, the game has tons of charm and challenges. Great job by Nintendo incorporating a service that was cancelled just a few years later.

Shin Megami Tensei games are not for everyone. In fact, unless you have heard that name you will probably hate any game with his name in the title. I love so many things about this game, yet am so annoyed by others. My biggest gripe is a strange... one. No English character dub on a remade game. The Japanese chatter becomes so annoying you will turn voice sound off. When remaking Devil Survivor, they added english voice actors. Still, an amazing game!
I'm not a huge Super Mario fan, but with it being 20.00 i went ahead and got it. It didn't take me long to beat it, but it was a ton of fun. There is a lot of content packed in the game.

I can't get over how much better they've made this controller. It was already the best controller out, and now with the little tweaks here and there...MS has done it again. Using another control device for my games just doesn't seem right. lol! Good job on NOT messing with perfection.

I've played the Alpha and Beta of this game, and I have to say that it has never gotten old.The way your Titan falls from the sky is so cool! I really do think that this game was needed, there are way too many "me too" shooters on the market, and it was just time for a change. Titanfall is a blast to play! It's refreshing, and fast paced. If you own an XB1 get this game! There really isn't much of a single player portion, but that's not why I bought this game..enjoy.

I'm glad that TR was remastered and re released for the XB1. I purchased TR and Watch Dogs on the same day, and I ended up returning Watch Dogs. TR was just more interesting, and it held my attention all the way till the end. I haven't enjoyed a game like this in a long time. Great Job Square Enix!!! The only issue for me now, is waiting on the second TR to come out.

This is easily one of the best racing games that I've played since GT2 on Playstation. I love the ability to go off road anytime you want. I really like how the map is setup for you to go almost anywhere. There are a lot of side tasks to keep you busy. It's not all about racing, you can drive around and explore, or just do stunts. The only drawback is not being able to sell your cars....other than that, I love the game.
My kid loves this game. It's seems to be a bit better than FIFA 14 was.

I've checked out all types of wireless headsets recently, for the price and performance, I went with the 500X. Now if I can't sleep and I wanna play my XB1 without waking my neighbors up, I can simply turn on my wireless headphones, and still get the same great sound that my home theater makes. My only concern is how wonky and cheap some of the plastic is. Hopefully they can stand the test of time. Overall, I really like the 500X...

I was never a big Tomb Raider fan back in the day, but I took a chance on it after purchasing an XBOX ONE...After completing Tomb Raider, I couldn't wait for Rise of Tomb Raider to come out. I have to say that the visuals are top notch! Love the opening scene and I am excited to put tons of time into this game. I haven't noticed and frame rate issues so far...I also think that most of the negative reviews, are from gamers that are upset about the timed exclusivity....I'm not sure how one can rate a game badly, just because they choose to game on ONE platform. Trust me, once this game hits PC and PS4, a lot of people will change their negative tune.

I've had my eye on this beauty since it was first announced. I gotta say, It's so much smaller than the older model. I bought my xbox one s from Gamestop and received $50 off per black Friday promotion....Good deal considering it comes with the $99 version of GOW4...If you're in the market for the a UHD player and video game system, look no further..

This game is one that may be best left on the Ps2, the story goes places far and wide without very much explanation and the combat enjoyable at first becomes rather repetitive. This is an Ok game at best, although a very deep game it all depends how much patience and time you have, for me i was not a fan of this title. With the rather shallow collection of games available for the 3DS i gave this one a shot hoping for an exciting experience and great story, but all i got was a game i wish i would have bought pre-owned so i could take it right back, for some maybe its worth it but if you love games with great and easy to follow stories and varied combat avoid this title!

Anyone who thinks this is not one of the best games made for a portable in a while is either in denial because they dont have a 3DS or because they are upset they could not find this game in a store or their pre order did not arrive on time. Trust me this is a Grade A classic, story and strategy come together to make one exceptional game that every game should experience! find it somewhere or if your like me there is the eshop, which is fine by me all in all i do not need a case or little booklet to enjoy such a great game, that is all!

Yes the lack of checkpoints can be annoying, but this is Nintendo at it's finest! Have we not forgot how difficult those old Mario games were?! But i regress, This has some of the best graphics on the system and also an amazing sequel! This is pure gold and I cant seem to put it down! 5 Stars! the year of Luigi has begun with a huge bang!

This game is one i had largely ignored, I have always heard such awful things about this game but I actually enjoyed the hell out of it, its a unique dark and beautiful adventure that everyone should try, not just Zelda fans! The dark story provides a narrative unlike any Zelda story told before it so eat your heart out Majora's Mask this is the true King of Zelda Darkness!
Is it a good as its PS3 counterpart? I would say no but hey its amazing and has all of the same game modes and its The Show in your pocket, love it!

When I heard about this game i jumped at the chance to play it, I read reviews about how deep the game can be and can last for hours upon hours and i saw the art style and i rejoiced! As a complete obsessive fan of anime and just Japanese gaming in general I thought this one would be hit for me... Boy was I wrong, I spent hours and hours trying to convince myself this was rightful purchase and hoping it was in the ballpark of a Fire Emblem, but after trying and trying I admitted Defeat. The Story not much of one is very childish for me (Im in my early 20s) I didn't like the battle system or the foes and the main character is plain annoying, Just because this game has hours upon hours to play does not mean you want to. Just me but i highly do not recommend this game if you are looking for a deep intriguing story as well as something that is completely fun!
I do not have much to say other then this is a must buy  every aspect of the game from story to combat to dialogue is amazing get it you wont regret it!

This was a pretty fun game, and I enjoyed my time with it. It's full of craziness, but it's pretty much all of a cartoonish variety, there really isn't any gore or reality to any of the violence. The story is pretty goofy and basic, however there are some kind of cool choices in the big story missions that were interesting and probably changed your game significantly. Overall, it's a decent game, and one I'd recommend to anyone that enjoys sand-box games.

This was a good game, and there's a lot to like about it, but overall I just didn't love it. The graphics here are pretty amazing, especially if you remember the previous Max Payne games. The bullet time third person gun-play can be insanely fun, but I really don't think it's enough to sell the entire game. I love that every slow jump is controlled by you, leading to either hilarious failures or glorious successes when you kill everyone in your jump. However, the fact that there really aren't any ways to modify the bullet-time jumps, leads to them eventually being very repetitive and boring. I would love different jumps, like maybe a slide, or something else to add a different flavor to the combat. Also, this game relies a lot more on cover based shooting if you want to survive, but it is a little different from the normal Gears of War style. I must say that the AI is pretty intelligent. However it becomes annoying when they stay hidden and invulnerable behind cover for very long periods of time, yet you will be shot/killed many times when you're shooting from cover or even hiding behind it. My other biggest problem with the combat is that it feels a little wooden at times, and Max is like an old man getting up and moving around (when not in bullet-time). After a dive, you are completely screwed if any of your enemies are alive while you slowly come to your feet. Related to this, if you are "killed" when you have painkillers you will automatically enter bullet-time with a chance to kill the person who shot you. There are multiple problems here, where sometimes the enemy can't be shot where they are, but the biggest problem is that if you succeed no matter where you were before you wake up lying on the ground. With how long Max takes to get up combined with the fact that you cannot go right into cover, you have to stand up fully before you regain control, I usually took so much damage that I was right again in danger of dying. It was also incredibly annoying with how much damage the enemies can take, as over and over I would unload into them and turn to continue the fight and then be killed by the guys I thought I'd finished. Sometimes the characters would fall down and get back up, but most of the time they would just absorb multiple bursts from an assault rifle and not flinch.

Now on to other parts of the game. The campaign is relatively long, but it is completely linear with no possible variation (and no reason to replay it) with multiple jumps along the timeline. It was kind of nice to have different versions of Max, but since they didn't control any differently they just made the story more convoluted. I think I would have liked to play the game missions in order, it wouldn't have improved the story itself at all, but I think it could have helped a little bit. The story is idiotic, there's a gigantic plot hole I won't spoil as it's supposed to be the big twist, but it really makes the whole set up of the story incomprehensible. I also wish Max wasn't such a bitchy whiner in this game, he's always bashing himself without realizing all of the bad ass things he'd done (I mean I killed thousands of paramilitary forces/gangsters/dirty police while flying through the air!). I think the biggest problem with the story is that there's no higher purpose for what you're aiming to do. There are parts where it's kind of a rescue the princess deal, but the princess isn't likeable and will always die anyway. Then there's a bit of revenge is best served cold storyline, but the villains are all interchangeable and the game never gave you a chance to like the people you're avenging. I just didn't care about the story other than wanting to kill everyone (which they prevented you from doing in the very end, even though the guy dies off camera in the epilogue).

For the multiplayer, I tried it but personally I just didn't really like it. It just felt too wooden and the best parts of the single player game have to be mostly eliminated to play against/with others. Other people might find a lot of hours of fun here, but for me I played it for a night and was done with it.

So overall, I enjoyed the game but by the end I was just left disappointed by what it offered. This isn't a bad game, but I don't think I would readily highly recommend it to anyone.

Edit: I increased my rating to 4 stars because I did enjoy the game, and I haven't liked some of the other games I've played lately.

The only thing really wrong with this game is the tower defense mini-game (which is absolutely horrible). Everything else is simply the same as AC: Brotherhood, which means that the game is really fun. I loved playing the game, but I must say that the gameplay was getting a little old as the only addition really since AC:1 is a hookblade, which really doesn't change anything other than being able to go zip-lining (Sadly there aren't too many lines for you to use). I will say that the story is much weaker than all of the previous campaigns, there's really no story in the present, and for what little story they have in the past I wasn't too interested in the setting.

The only other gameplay addition to this game was an interesting and sometimes annoying first person virtual reality game. There were some interesting puzzles and platforming here, and it was nice to get to learn about the main character's past, but I almost wish they had given more information. The monetary/leveling system in the game is again kind of messed up, but now it's almost worse than the previous games. You still have the whole buying/upgrading buildings and increasing your salary, and unlike Brotherhood I didn't have a crazy amount of money by the end, but instead there was really nothing worth buying. All of the best weapons and armor in the game could be attained relatively early if you do some of the challenges and fully train your assassin apprentices.

Overall, if you liked the previous Assassin's Creed games, you're almost assuredly going to like this game even with the horrible tower defense (I only had to play it 3-5 times, though the 3rd challenge was impossible) especially since you can probably get it pretty cheap now. I do find this game a year schedule without changing anything very annoying, but thankfully for the past two games a separate team has been creating AC3.

I will admit that some of the visuals in this game are amazing, and the story is slightly interesting. However, the gameplay is extremely generic, repetitive, and annoying. It's really just a button masher, without any room for creativity or strategy in your playstyle. I also didn't like how there was no way to improve your weapons and armor. Then, each of the weapons have some good and bad things about them, and if you were able to use them interchangeably they would really benefit each other. However, you only have access to one of them at a time, and for most of the game you can only change weapons by disarming/cleansing the enemy. The other biggest problem for me, was the way the game uses extra lives. When you run out of health (which is coolly shown by losing your armor/clothing) you have to mash your buttons to wake back up, however there is a limit to this and each time it's harder to wake back up. This inevitably ends with you dying, and the game then lectures you about how to stay alive by mashing the buttons even though that was just what you were doing, and you have to revert to the last save/checkpoint which at times can be way far back, there's also incredibly long load times. For the platforming, it's very basic, and it's pretty floaty and many times hard to be accurate, especially when holes in the world blend in with the environment. I probably would have enjoyed the game more if I chose Easy instead of normal (as the worst problems may not have occurred as frequently) but once you choose at the very beginning of the game you can never change it for some reason.

In the end, I would definitely not recommend this game, but some people could possibly find a good game here if you could overlook all of the faults, something that I couldn't do.

I kind of hate giving this game 4 stars, because I did have a lot of fun with it in my 100 hours or so play-through. However, I just feel like too much of it was busy work. The world is absolutely huge, but it's separated into sections, each one having new quests and some sort of hub-city. The problem is that almost every new quest you get is some sort of uninteresting fetch quest. The only reason I completed so many of them is because of my slight OCD completionism when it comes to video games. Also, each new area while it has different color pallets, they are all very similar.

With the main gameplay, the fighting, it is relatively fun and deep in the beginning, but by half-way through and especially the end, it will just feel like a chore. I only died once in the game, and that was due to an apparently malfunctioning trap that took out my 2,000 or so health in a few seconds when I wasn't paying enough attention. The only challenge is when you have a bunch of the larger types of enemies surrounding you, as their actions cannot be halted by any attack, while every attack they do sends you flying. Related to this, it is incredibly annoying how every little attack against you completely halts your action, even when you're in the middle of a high XP attack and some tiny monster strikes you from behind. This can be slightly halted by some of the abilities, but you still have to worry about being interrupted while you're activating the ability. I really wish that there was another set of actions that you could set up in the right bumper, instead of it being taken up by the sneak ability which I almost never used (and could have been placed on one of the analog stick buttons). Since you can only have 4 abilities available at a time, I had many that I couldn't use. Because of this I really just had a go to set of moves to deal with every enemy. Also, they try to say that you can be anything you want, but if you want the best abilities you really have to focus only on being a Warrior, Mage, or Rogue. I would have tried to experiment later, but it was halted when I hit the level cap relatively early, and that made my last hours with the game really a chore, as I didn't have the positive reinforcement of leveling up.

With the crafting, parts of it is really well done. However, it was frustrating when many times you couldn't get some of the parts that you wanted to have to make the best weapons and armor. Related to this, you arbitrarily get access to a main type of material either attached to your space in the story or your level, and it really makes any previous armor or weapon useless. Also, all of the unique armor and weapons are useless, and always weaker than what you can create. I wish that they would have let you dismantle them, and rebuild them to make the special items as powerful as the ones you can create. One more thing about the crafting, I liked how all of the items could be dismantled into parts, but it was very strange where even if you've maxed out your Smithing, the number of parts you get from the item is completely random. I probably lost a lot of useful parts, and there were multiple times where I'd have to save right before I dismantled them and then reload to get the next important main building block. It was really just frustrating, and didn't make any sense.

For the story, this is where the game completely fails. I was hopeful after I saw one of my favorite authors R.A. Salvatore was helping craft the world or the story, but all of my hopes were smashed. The story doesn't make any sense, and it isn't suspenseful at all. Thankfully I didn't get attached to any of the characters, because many of them would just be randomly killed. I could sum up the story with this: You wake up after being killed by the end boss and you are stricken with amnesia with the new ability of changing everyone's fate, you travel around the country getting stronger while doing random jobs, in the end you attack the dark fae (or whatever they're called) and go to the leader's home and kill him, then you kill the god he was trying to raise, the end. It's extremely basic, with random plot twists that I didn't care about at all. None of the missions really had much of a separate story. However, some of the group missions were better than all of the other ones. Also, the two best sets of missions were the DLC, which is kind of horrible. I actually wish that I would have played the DLC earlier, as it's the best part of the game, and might have kept me going stronger in the main part of the game. Instead, it was too little too late.

Overall, this is far from a bad game, there's a lot of excellent parts of it, and I would recommend it, especially if you're looking for a lot of bang for your buck. It's just too bad that the developer went under after releasing the game.

If I was to just review the gameplay of Spec Ops: The Line, I would just call it a weaker and less polished version of Gears of War, and rate it at 3 stars. However, there is so much more to this game than meets the eye. I think that the developer knew they couldn't make a game on par with COD and GoW, so they focused on the story and making a statement on all of the military shooters out there today. This is really the only reason I bought the game, as I'd heard so many great things, especially from Extra Credits. At first, I didn't really see too much originality, and the problems with the gameplay were frustrating me. Thankfully, the few really cool moments made me continue, and there were huge payoffs later in the game. I will say though, that I wish you had to hold down A to sprint like in GoW, and the AI was a little erratic, with it at times being very simple, but at other times being too smart, where I would move around in cover and as soon as I popped out I would be shot and killed. The checkpoint placement was also a little hit and miss, making frustrating parts of the game even worse. Also, multiple times I ran out of ammo, and I think this was partly due to the fact that many of the weapons from dispatched soldiers disappeared instead of giving you ammo (usually it was enemies that were farther away from you).

Right from the beginning, you immediately had interesting interactions with your enemies and team mates. Where you are confronted by Dubai citizens (that you are supposed to save) with machine guns, the great part is that you are in control of your character, and at any time you can open fire. The only problem with this situation, is that eventually they open fire and you have to kill them. This problem is present in most of the game, where even as everything the game is telling you that what you're doing is absolutely horrible, if you want to beat the game you have to do these atrocious things. However, this may actually be a reference to real life soldiers, where if their superiors give them an order they have to follow it. As the game progresses, I love the art style, where all of the characters are getting more and more beaten up, where the outside of the characters mirrors the turmoil and growing insanity inside.

Spec Ops: The Line is truly the first game where I actually questioned the morals of what I was doing, and parts of it still stays with me. There are two parts of the game where this was the strongest. The first was a scene that makes the COD airport level look like child's play. In it you are being surrounded by an angry mod of Dubai citizens, they are inching closer and closer, and your team mate is constantly asking for your permission to open fire. Here I held out for awhile, but then I just opened fire and mowed the civilians down like leaves of grass, with my team mate following suit. It was such a strong moment, and it was made even stronger with the fact that there were multiple outcomes here, all of them occurring in real time. In every RPG game where you are given the choice, I always choose the good route, I'm always the paragon. However in this game, I almost always took the seemingly evil route in the heat of the moment, and I at times felt regret about it. The second strongest moment actually occurred after the credits, where a company of completely innocent American soldiers confront you in front of the ruins of Dubai. Again you have multiple choices here, and I went with probably the most horrible one, but I wanted a chance to kind of win the game, and let the character walk off in relative freedom. It was so powerful though, as you are given an automatic shotgun (one of the coolest guns in the game) and the person confronting you seems like a nice guy. He tries to get everyone to lower their weapons, that your character was shell shocked, and he just wants you to drop your weapons and surrender yourself. This is made even worse as if you want to fight them and walk off into the sun, the first person you have to kill is that guy right in front of you that's talking to you, and with that shotgun his head just explodes if you make the decision to fight. Those are just two moments, and there are multiple other ones that aren't as powerful, but really make the game amazing.

I will go a little into spoiler territory here. I really think that this has the best use of unreliable narrator in a game I've every played, and it's one of the best in any form of media. I almost always see the unreliable narrator plot device coming, but I really didn't see it coming at all in this game. I just thought that my character was going crazy, but not that crazy. However, the payoff was a little weak, it could have been done better, a little tighter. As I really wasn't sure what exactly was real and what wasn't real. Also, it doesn't fully hold up when you consider your two sane team mates were following you, even though it was very clear to them that you were crazy. This makes crazy ideas possible, especially one where your character actually died in the first helicopter crash, and everything that happened after wasn't real. I'm not sure if it works, but it's an interesting idea.

Overall, I really enjoyed the game, and I would definitely recommend this game, although kids should probably stay away.

Depending on your experience, this game can be an absolutely amazing experience, or it can be absolutely frustrating. Personally, I experienced a bit of both, hence the 4 star rating. While the story is relatively linear, there are dozens of different ways to go about each mission, though when you get down to it, it's mainly either killing everyone or sneaking around. I tended to start out sneaking, but after I kept having to replay missions in the beginning, I later just switched my methods when things didn't go exactly as planned. Consequentially, even though I was in the middle of pack in regards to the morality system, I got the worst ending. It was just so frustrating, and I felt like I was being punished for playing the game the way I wanted. I almost wish that they would release a sequel with the same gameplay but a completely different story. This is definitely a game everyone should try, but it is far from a perfect gaming experience.

This is a relatively long game, and depending on my point in the game, I would could have either given it one stars or five stars, so I'm going to have to average it out with three stars. One of my biggest problems, are with something that shouldn't have happened, something that should have been tested and either removed or made easier, and that's the multitude of quicktime events. There are hundreds of them in this game, and none of them are easy, while some of them are damn near impossible. More than once I almost quit playing the game because I couldn't get by a quicktime event (most notably the one with the giant boss where you have to remove the armor around its spine/antenna thing). There's no reason for quicktime events, which are already annoying at the best of times, to be so difficult. I also found it very annoying for most of the time I played the game, where even though I was playing solo I wasn't allowed to pause the game (even if the controller lost power), which is something I've never seen in any game I've ever played. In my third campaign I finally figured out that you have to go out of your way to select offline play when starting your game.

This game was touted as having three separate campaigns (it actually has four), but it was surprising how similar they are to each other. Even the game seems to recognize these as new game+ campaigns. I almost wish that there had been a way to combine all of the campaigns into one large campaign where you switch characters after every mission, and the parts that are copied between the campaigns you'd only have to do once. My enjoyment of the game was greatly harmed as I played the Leon campaign first, and I found it to be the weakest of the bunch, even though it was touted as being the one most like the earlier Resident Evil games. In fact, other than killing standard zombies more often, it is not at all like the early RE games, instead you play the weakest character with less ammo, no cool melee attacks, and not as many cool weapons. Personally my favorite campaign was with Jake, mainly as it was the most different of the campaigns, and it had the best story (which isn't saying much).

Utlimately, there is a lot of game here, but most of it is a frustrating mess. I wouldn't recommend this game, but if you can suffer through the annoyances there is a decent amount of fun to be had in Resident Evil 6.

I really liked the Phantasy Star series but was upset with this port. When creating this port they left out Phantasy Star IV which is the best game in the entire series. On top of that all 3 games now have a tin sound to them. It can be ignored in II and III but in Phantasy Star 1 it makes the game unplayable with the volume up.

All in all, if you're looking to pick this series up again, or for the first time, it is a great game to have, especially if you like the convenience of having 3 great rpg's packed into one small cartridge. But you will have to find some other way to play the 4th and final game in the series.

I picked this up out of the blue, after expecting to buy a different game. But I was quite surprised at how fun this game was. To clarify, this is a remake of a Gameboy Game called Final Fantasy Adventure. It is in fact not a Final Fantasy game but that series was popular in the US and it was pretty much used as a marketing tactic.

The game play is fun, you go from screen to screen hacking away at enemies and leveling up. Each time you level up you get to choose a weapon class to go up by one point, like a sword, or mace. What you choose to level up will bring your up stats accordingly.

This is a fun game and I would recommend it.

They always say that the Virtual Memory Unit, or VMU for short, was ahead of its time. And they said it with good reason. This baby was slapped into your DC controller to store game saves but it did more than that. It displayed your score in Sports games among other things. Some games even had mini games that could be stored onto it for portable play, like the well known Chao Adventure which acted as virtual pet.

This is a fantastic game. Its got a great storyline full of twists and turns. It has a lot of optional dungeons and bosses an optional characters too. Its your average 40 hours but obtaining the gold chocobo and gttings couds final limit break can be chalenging and take hours themselves. I recommend this game.

This game has a pretty decent plot and the characters have some backstory to them. But what this game is all about is job system. There are so many jobs available it's crazy, and you can take abilities that you learn from one job and apply them to another, for example having a white mage with the ability to cast all levels of black magic or a chemist with the jump ability. This especially makes the free lancer job that much more useful end game.

If you are looking for a first Final Fantasy than I highly recommend this game.

Whenever my friends ask why I like this game so much, I can usually only spit out a four word response, which is "It's just plain fun."

But there is more to it than that. You have a story that is packed full of emotions, you have abilities and skills and what could overall be the best looking game to be released on the original Playstation.

I would highly recommend this game for anyone looking to get into Final Fantasy for the first time.

The updated graphics and new features put a fresh spin on a classic Legend of Zelda title. You can now aim with the 3DS' gyroscope and all boots have became C-Items, which is great because originally, putting on and removing boots was a tedius process. There is a tiny frame drop in some areas but it can be easily overlooked. This remake got it right, so I give it 5 out of 5 stars.

I loved Tales of the Abyss, but I couldn't bring myself to finish it, because the original PS2 version had lag on the overworld, and it was serious. So I put it on the shelf to collect dust. But then Tales of the Abyss 3D is released and right from the start I noticed a few minor issues. Issues that were expected for a game on the 3DS really, such as a lower fps during battles and lower graphics detail. But once I reached the overworld, all those issues flew right out the door because NO LAG ON THE OVERWORLD. Finally this game becomes playable to me, and it's portable. What more could you ask for? I give it 5 stars.

I actually wanted to buy WD2 first but it made more sense to play WD1, so I did. Played it before buying the second game and managed to finished it in well over a month or two and I pretty much enjoyed that. I like WD2 mainly because the protagonist was poc and I feel like more games should represent diversity. Not to mention, this all took place in San Francisco and the far reaches of Oakland, my hometown. It's a shame that the entirety of Alameda wasn't included. It would have been funny to drive past my own house in-game and have Marcus take a selfie with it.

I enjoyed the game throughout and the characters are all unique and eccentric (talking to you, Wrench. lol).

I was pretty hyped when the gold edition had almost everything and I was totally thrilled when Jordi returned. He was basically everyone's favorite fixer and that Aiden Pearce easter egg was a brilliant bit. I only wish there was a DLC where Marcus actually gets to meet him but one can only dream.

Overall, if you want the full package and don't plan on buying all the DLC content separately, I recommend getting the gold edition because you also get some free stuff. However, the Zodiac Killer mission could have been better. I was actually disappointed because I feel like all of what I did was for naught. I almost gave this 4-stars but my love for Jordi won me over. Here's to hoping for a future DLC where you can play as Jordi Chin.

P.S. It would make more sense to play WD1 because it also connects with WD2. You would get a better understanding of certain things and characters mentioned in the game. And if you haven't played WD1, do it if you haven't already.

2001 has made its way to my Vita, and its just as good as I remember. Square Enix has used a Phoenix Down on this game and it is back from the grave. Considering that this is a remastering of a 13 year old game I'm not going to bother summarizing the story, chances are that almost everyone reading this has already played the ps2 game or knows how to use Wikipedia.
So what makes this game different from the original Playstation 2 game? Two things: Graphics, and international content. The graphics for this game have been smoothed out and look really nice, and on the Vita's OLED screen they look really pretty. But enhanced visuals aren't the only thing this game has going for it. Nope, for the first time we have easy access to the international content. Which means new super challenging bosses (Dark Aeons), and a new Expert Sphere Grid plus a few abilities that weren't included in the original NA release. So even if you still own the original PS2 there is some merit to buying this game, plus the inclusion of Final. Fantasy X-2 the, while not as good but still worth playing, sequel to FFX.
Closing statement: Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remastered is a great title for the PS Vita and PS3 but despite the updated visuals this game's age does show, the character's facial expressions are non existent, and the voice acting, while good for the time is just bad. But despite those few set backs this game is still worth playing as the game play is still as solid as it was in 2001, and the story, regardless of the shoddy voice acting, is still an epic and enjoyable story.

I never had a Sega Genesis growing up, I was born at the end of that generation of gaming and had my first game in experience on consoles like the PlayStation and the N64. But I remember playing the Sonic Advanced gba games, and I did play the Genesis classics later on. Out of all the Sonic games I had played up to this point Sonic CD had always been a personal favorite.

,As a kid I was a pretty big Sonic fan, if I had been born a few years earlier I would have picked Genesis over SNES.

That out of the way let me say that this game is nothing short of fantastic. I adore this game, the pixel art is beautiful, and the game runs smooth. Sonic is so fast, and the controls are so tight. It's just nothing short of amazing. Christian Whitehead has really out done themselves here. This feels like the perfect Sonic game for anyone who missed the old 2D goodness of the 16 bit era. Truthfully I was actually more excited for this game than Forces (not that I'm not excited for that, getting SF for Switch on launch) and this game was worth the wait.

Graphics 10/10: perfectly recaptures the magic of the Genesis era, and makes it look even better.

Gameplay 10/10: Controls are responsive and Sonic is fast as ever.

Soundtrack 10/10: Downright amazing. The remixes on this are very pleasant to the ears, and the new tracks belong as well.

In conclusion this game feels like a long overdue love letter to any Sonic fan who longs for a simpler time. If your a fan of old school Sonic buy this game you wont regret it.

Now let me go over the collection we have here. The statue is very nice, it doesn't feel cheap, but it doesn't feel overly expensive. I do need to get some batteries for it at some point so I can hear that go old SEEGAA whenever I want to.

The Genesis cartage looks realistic and is also pretty cool. Wish I could pop it into the Genesis that the statue stands on. And the ring inside is really sweet as well. The card has some nice artwork and feels nice.

If your a fan of Sonic and a collector this is a nice set. If your just a fan or don't want to pay 60+ dollars you can buy the game for 20 dollars which is worth it.

I am going to try and be as fair as I can with this game. I want to give it a higher rating than three stars, (in my opinion it's closer to 3.5) but I can't.) This game has a lot of glaring issues, but it also has a lot of good things.

Let's start with the good.

By far my absolute favorite part of this game is the soundtrack. My God there are so many catchy tunes in this game. I am actually currently listening to some of my favorite tracks. (I actually replayed certain stages just to hear the music.) This is easily one of my favorite game tracks in a Sonic game.

The graphics are really good in this. They're crisp and clear, and just nice to look at. Also when running through stages there's a lot going on in the background, some nice touches here and there.

Now let's get to the things that are a bit of a mixed bag for me.

The gameplay is fast, fun and fluid...for the most part. Playing as modern Sonic is exhilarating, you're so fast it's not even funny. Really it's not funny. I lost count how many times I had a stupid death because I was going too fast. It's hard to explain, while the controls aren't bad they're aren't the best. And sometimes you just slip off on a narrow curving walk way or fail to make a jump over a bottomless pit that you should have been able to. Despite that, Modern Sonic was my favorite part of the game. The sound breaking speed on certain stages was just tons of fun.

The OC character was...good. Surprising, but yeah I actually enjoyed most of the original character's stages and his gimmik was pretty fun too. His stages went similar to MSonic, but with less speed and a little more strategizing. (Never thought I would enjoy this characters segaments, but there ya go. (Cough-I still think that this custom character is a deviant art users wet dream-cough) Other than a few platforming issues I had this character's implementation wasn't bad. (Wish I could say the same about Classic Sonic... we'll get to that later )

The stages with both Sonic and the OC combined the best and worst of the individual character's stages and add in a double Boost with a catchy yet lyrically cringe worthy song. (... despite that I like the song...)

Classic Sonic...what the hell are you doing here? You were breath taking in Sonic Mania, and you ruined that. Come on man, you can do better. Classic Sonic stages were by far the most annoying part of this game for me. The platforming was okay in some places, but coming off the heels of Sonic Mania playing CSonic in this game was draining. The tight controls and the way he moved in that game is not present here. Also the level desgin was head scratching in some spots. I didn't have it happen to me, I used spin dash to get the momentum I needed, but at the beginning of Chemical plant there is an upward curve that you cannot get enough momentum to run up. Another complaint I have with CSonic is that he feels unnecessary in this games story. Like he was just thrown in because Sonic Generations had both Sonics and it was regarded as a really good game. I love classic Sonic game play, but I wish that they had left him out of this and focused more time on Modern Sonic and the OC character stages. (Plus they could have taken more time to improve the game's story. (Which leads me into the next part.)

The story. Oh I wanted to like this story, I really did. And for the most part I didn't mind it. It was serviceable. And the character interactions weren't too bad, the voice actors did pretty good if you ask me. I just wish they could have fleshed things out a bit more and extended the game's story. Not going to spoil anything in particular but I'll just say that near the end of the game, there is a moment that is supposed to be the hype climax, but it feels rushed. It seems like the end, yet through no development all of a sudden we can make it and win the day. It would have been nice if they had dwelled just a little bit on the moment where it seems hopeless and let it sink in before the big climax.

The bad I basically already covered but I will sum up. The characters don't quite respond how you want them to at times. The story is a bit lacking, and there's no real sense of development. And Classic Sonic was just not necessary.

All in all this is a game I would recommend for Sonic fans. I am a Sonic fan, and despite my harsh critism I enjoyed this game. But despite that I felt it important to point out the flaws I saw in this game. If this had been a sixty dollars game my review would have been much harder, but since I only paid 34 dollars for my copy I was more forgiving. I hope that in the future Sega learns from there mistakes with this game.

Growing up back in Staten Island , NY I had a friend of mine show me a variety of games on the PC. One of the games that he loved to play was a game where you had to travel around the world and battle aliens that were bent on conquering earth. The game was called X-Com and recently it has made a comeback with such great games as X-Com Enemy Unknown. Now the folks over at 2k games have released The Bureau: X-Com Declassified but is this one file that you will want to read?

Instead of this game taking place in the future it takes place in the past back in the year 1962. The bureau of strategic emergency command was created to help protect it's citizens from enemies that were not of this world. You take on the role of William Carter and you are charged with stopping an invasion of aliens that are making a foothold on american soil. You are sent out into the field with two other agents that have their own powers as they make up one of four classes: Commando, Recon, Support and Engineer. Each of these classes have their own powers and you can use these via Battle Focus mode. During this mode time slows down considerably as you can command each of these units to use special powers, mark targets and outflank the enemy all in real time.

As with other games in the X-Com series your agents can be damaged during combat and they will need medical attention if wounded severely. If one of your agents does not get the help that they need within a certain amount of time they can die during the mission. And once a character has died they are gone for good (meaning that you need to recruit a new agent). This forces you make tough calls on the battlefield as you want to get all of your agents home safely and not get them killed recklessly in combat. You will also be able to research new weapons and technology that you will get off the aliens in each mission.

The best thing I love about this game is that it is set when the bureau was starting to take off. It is set in the 1960's and the tech might seem primitive but with some good decisions you will be able to eradicate the alien threat. For more information on this game go to [...] and get ready to fight against the alien invaders.

Growing up one of my favorite toys were legos as you could create anything you imagined. There have been a series of video games based off of serious movie and comic franchises. From Indiana Jones to Star Wars there have been a lego video game based off of it. Now Tell Tale games have unleashed their latest game called Lego Marvel Super Heroes but is this a game you will want to play?

The game centers on the villains that have banded together to free their brethren from secured facilities. From Rykers Island to the Raft six groups have been formed and each of them are in charge of all the lackeys underneath them. The six teams are led by such iconic villains such as Ultron & Loki , Dr. Doom, Tinkerer, Dormammu & Baron Mordo, Magneto & Mystique and Enchantress, Executioner, and the Mandarian. They have banded together to build a Doom Ray of Doom to unleash against the world. Nick Fury decides that he is going to need some help on this one as he summons the worlds greatest heroes to help him capture these bad guys.

And the roster of heroes that you will be able to play as is just as immense. Thor, Wolverine, Spiderman and Deadpool are just a sampling of the great characters you can play as. Each of the missions allows you to choose between two heroes and go against hordes of a common enemy. For example the first mission that takes place in New York has two heroes (Spiderman and Nova) going after the Sinister Six. And the bosses of course reflect this as you will be going up against Doctor Octopus , Electro and others.

One of the unique features of this game are the comic missions that you can undergo. Some of the more iconic missions are going after your uncles killer as Spiderman. Or you can head over to Japan as Wolverine to battle the Silver Samurai. These comic missions are a nice touch to the game as you can relive some of your favorite memories in Marvel history.

With a huge roster of heroes and villains, a great story and some really cool comic missions this is a must have if you're a comic book fan.

For years when you were to mention wrestling the first name that comes to mind is the WWE. With colorful characters, intense action and some great plotlines it is one of the best shows to watch. Now 2k games has released their latest game called WWE 2K14 but is this going to be a match you'll want to take or will you want to tap out?

One of the most awe inspiring things of this title has to be the impressive roster that has been assembled. There are over sixty wrestlers that you can choose from that reflects both current and past WWE greats. Some of the wrestlers have their current look but also have some retro costumes. So imagine taking a match where you can play as the classic undertaker with the widebrimmed hat.

You can also create your own wrestler in the career mode as you can customize the look of your character. As you start you will be virtually unknown but as you win matches you will be more well known. Do you have what it takes to reach mega star status like Hulk Hogan?

Exhibition matches are the heart of the game where you can pit various wrestlers in whatever match your heart desires. One of the newer modes is called Universe Mode where the computer will create random matchups. Instead of assigning all the teams, scenarios and rivalries all of these are going to be completely computer generated. You can choose who you want to play however, when the game starts it feels more like you're watching an episode of monday night raw instead of a planned match.

Another new mode that's being introduced is a single player mode entitled "30 years of Wrestlemania". These are 46 matches that are going to relive some of the epic events of the classic matchups that occurred in previous Wrestlemania's. You will be able to go up against such greats as Andre the Giant, Macho Man Savage, The Rock and others. You need to complete certain objectives to get past the match and you will go on to the next match. Another thing that's awesome about this game is there is classic video footage that will make you reminisce past matches. These videos also establish the storylines that occurred way back when and set the stage perfectly for the match.

With some great game modes, a huge roster of wrestlers to choose from and some new game modes to choose from it's obvious to get this if you're a WWE fan.

In the past few years the modern military FPS has been growing in popularity. And the two biggest contenders have been the Battlefield series and the Call of Duty series. Battlefield 4 was released in October and fans have been ranting and raving about it. Now Activision has answered with the latest entry called Call of Duty Ghosts. But will this next entry be a game worthy of your time or should you wait for it to disappear?

The single player campaign is very unique instead of taking place in the past or present day it takes place in the near future. A group known as the federation has unified all of South America and is moving towards world domination. To make matters worse a team has taken over the Orbital Defense Initiative (or ODIN) Space station and has laid waste to the United States. With all the destruction the US tries to hold out against a vast superior force.

What I love about the game is how the once beautiful lands of California are now turned into a war torn battlefield littered with wrecked buildings and a scarred landscape. You won’t be alone on your mission as this is the first Call of Duty to have a canine companion along for the ride. Riley is a German Shepard that can scout out targets, sneak around and even take down targets at your choosing.

Multiplayer is where Call of Duty shines and there are new features that have been implemented in Ghosts. The first is the squad’s mode where you can compete against AI opponents and gain experience that can be used in other multiplayer modes. The various game modes rank from standard free for all and team death match to newer ones. Search and Rescue is similar to search and destroy where you have one life but your team can revive you. There is also a mode called Cranked which is a TDM variant when you kill someone you need to kill someone else in 30 seconds. Failing to do so means you explode but if you manage to get a kill the timer resets.

I was hoping for a zombie mode in this game and got something much better called Extinction. This mode pits four players against an alien race that has taken over earth. With every kill you earn money that can be used for ammo, weapons and equipment. This mode is very team oriented as you will face waves of enemies trying to defend an objective. This can be played either solo or with other people online and is a great addition to this game.

The only problem that I have with this game is running it on the PC that I have at home. I have a laptop (which is an alienware) and a desktop (an older machine that runs almost anything flawlessly). The load times on the desktop are outrageous while the laptop handles it with ease (as this is supposed to be for cutting edge PC’s). The system requirements are even outstanding as you have to have a 64 bit OS, 6 GB of ram and at least a 450 GT graphics card. These are some of the highest requirements I have seen for a PC game to date and the game will run on my desktop (but very slowly and I can run any game out there with zero issues).

With a compelling single player campaign, tons of multiplayer modes and even the ability to customize your online avatar this is a no brainer. Run out and get this game today and experience the latest in the Call of Duty saga.

Far back as I can remember I was in love with role playing games. From discovering the hobby with buying Dungeons and Dragons at a garage sale to playing Ultima 3 on my C-64. Role playing games allow us an escape from everyday life. Now NIS (the creator of the Disgaea series) have created a new series called The Guided Fate Paradox. But is this a journey that you will want to go on or should you just stay home?

The plot behind The Guided Fate Paradox centers around a 17 year old named Renya. He goes on to say that he is very unlucky and has never won anything in his life. While in a mall he comes across a cute girl in a maid outfit. She coerces him to spin the wheel as he might win a prize and he eventually does so. It turns out he has won the grand prize and the prize is that he is to become God. Renya is stunned and at first doesn’t believe her but it turns out she is an angel named Liliel. The angel transports him to Celestia and explains that his job is to alter the fates of the people that pray to him.

What Renya has to do is enter the Fate Revolution Circuit and explore the areas within. In these dungeons various monsters manifest as the persons fears and slaying these monsters help them overcome these doubts. This is one of the most interesting concepts I have ever seen in an RPG and the story is very engaging with cutscenes and great voice acting.

The dungeons that you enter are randomly generated almost giving you a rogue-like experience. Each time you enter a dungeon you will encounter different enemies, various traps and gimmicks that can hinder your progress. Unlike other games where the action occurs in real time this is a turn based game. Nothing will happen unless you move and you can get the jump on some enemies attacking them before they can even see you.

You will not be going alone in the dungeon however as you can have one angel accompany on your expedition. Each of these angels has various powers and can turn the tide of battle. There are also various items you can find in the dungeon that you can equip or give to one of your angels. Later on there are huge boss battles that will require you to think and plan out your actions to beat these superior foes.

If you are a fan of some of the earlier Disgaea games or want a change from the traditional RPG’s you need to get this game.

As the seasons change from fall to winter some people start to think about outdoor sports. The culmination of this season is the Winter olympics as people from all around the world compete in various activities. Sega has created a few games based off of olympic events in which various characters competed in olympic events. Now the latest entry in this line of games is called Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Winter Games Sochi 2014. But is this a game that you will want to pick up for your Wii U or should you give it a pass?

The game takes place in Sochi Russia and there are a total of sixteen events that you can compete in. From the exciting ski jump to the ferocity of ice hockey those are some of the events you can partake in. Also there are eight dream events that you can participate in as well and these are different than the regular events. These dream events take place in the various themed worlds from Sega and Nintendo. Some of the examples are Bullet Bill Sledge Race or Hole in One Curling (which takes place in the Green Zone from Sonic).

You can participate in these events as one of twenty characters (ten from nintendo and ten from sega). The iconic characters can be played such as Sonic, Mario and Luigi but there are also some of the lesser known characters such as Waluigi, Vector and Silver. You can also play as your Mii as well if you want to see your character snowboarding down a mountain.

While it does sound like it could be a fun game especially with the Gamepad the gameplay is rather repetitive. You use the Wii Remote to control your character as you swish and wiggle your way either down a mountain or for the ski jump. This could have been done a lot better as they could have used the gamepad for some of these modes. Some of the games such as Ice Hockey use the analog sticks so the controls are better with this event. Also there is an event called Action and Answer that injects trivia into the game and do we really want to answer trivia about the olympics?

This could have been a great game but it is plagued by repetitive controls and just some boring gameplay. If you own a Wii U and you love the olympics you might want to rent this title first otherwise give some of the other Wii U titles a try.

Barbie has been an iconic character for young girls for generations. From various playsets that Mattel has offered to videos, games and even videogames. Each of these games however in the past have been downright horrible. Most of the games that were released had no point and were really shallow and have no redeeming qualities. Now the folks over at little orbit have created the latest installment called Barbie dream house party. But is this a party that you will want to go to or should you just skip it altogether.

The game is based off the webisode series that is available online as you can play as one of the characters from that show. These mini games range from the various activities that Barbie that would participate in. Fashion, Grooming , Gardening and Baking are the games based on as you can compete with your friends. Also you can customize the character that you are playing with as you can do their makeup or dress them up in different outfits. You can also explore the dream house as well as you can go from room to room.

There have been many shows made off the DC universe but none as ambitious as a show called Young Justice. This show focuses on younger counterparts on an alternate earth (earth-16) and how they deal with threats in that universe. Now the folks over at Warner Brothers Interactive have created a game called Young Justice: Legacy. But is this a game that you will want to play or should you just go and watch episodes of the series?

This game bridges the five year gap that occurs between Season 1 and Season 2 of the television series. The Young Justice team finds out that an accomplished archaeologist Dr. Helena Sandsmark has been kidnapped. The mysterious group called the Light have taken responsibility and it is up to our heroes to rescue her. You will travel around the world as you battle various supervillains and uncover a sinister plot. The light is using Dr. Sandsmark to locate pieces of an ancient statue that contains untold power. Can the heroes of the Young Justice save her and stop this threat before time runs out.

There are fifteen levels that you will have to battle through and you can select from a roster of sixteen heroes (12 included in the game and 4 you can download: Bumblebee, Lagoon Boy, Wonder Girl and Blue Beetle).The roster includes such greats a Kid Flash, Robin, Superboy, Batgirl. Each of your heros has unique abilities that they can call upon on the battlefield to aid you in rescuing the doctor.

As you progress throughout the game you will level up and grow more powerful as you play. But you need to be careful as you might need a different character later down the line and if he’s not strong enough you will most certainly fail. Also depending on your playstyle there are three costumes that you can unlock that not only change your appearance but your abilities as well.

Cute game with a unique idea and good story ... but pretty short play time.

It's easy enough that my 5 year old son can play (on easy mode) ... though he does have a little trouble with walking over narrow "bridges".

My biggest problem is the second player option - Yes, it does exist but it was obviously an afterthought.
* P2 is a silver knack character which is slight smaller (but slightly faster).
* When P1 grabs relics (which make him grow in size), then P2 automatically also gets larger.
* None of the cut-scenes have P2 in them
* The camera focuses on P1 which means that P2 can easily get lost (it makes fighting goblins sort of difficult)
* When P1 dies, the characters return to the checkpoint ... when P2 dies, he can push any button to return (after a few seconds of forced waiting time)
* P2 can take much fewer hits than P1 .... I guess that's ok since P2 can keep regenerating, but it can be frustrating to die every few minutes

All in all, i did enjoy this game ... I think it's better if you are the only one playing (ie: no P2).

If the Knack2 game has fixes to the second player mode, i'll consider buying it ... but it's not on my "must have" list, by any means.
