Lets start with the good:
The new controller is good, i like the two layer layout, it certainly brings more feeling of playing a guitar as opposed to a video game. The new presentation is certainly an upgrade, very smooth, very vivid, and a hell of a lot less cluttered than the old games. The song selection is good, certainly better than the track list present in Rock Band 4. The "Live" section does occasionally have a cool moment or 2 and when those moments come up you can see how cool the concept could have been if done properly.

Now...the bad:
The "Live" section is garbage, the concept is sound and the stuff in the background can be pretty cool sometimes but for a game called "Guitar Hero" it features the songs from the tracklist that least require a game made for them, either piffy pop songs, whiny rock songs, or just dubstep or rap songs that don't actually have a guitar in them, several tracks i found my guitar suddenly doing the synth track or a bass line. Barring one metal song right in the middle and the last playlist that had The Who, Rolling stones and Queen the rest was just boring as hell.

The GHTV mode is your standard "pick a song" mode but even after the painfully frustrating and unnecessary tutorial on how to use it, it has flaws everywhere. Let's start with the fact that to change the difficulty you have to get OUT of GHTV mode go back into Live, change the difficulty there, then go back and try it out. Now the part that i hate most is the fact that you are only allowed to play so many songs, you get a counter that you can BUY plays for and each time you do a song the counter goes down. Once the counter reaches zero you can't play your own tracks anymore, now you have to do one of the painful "channels" where basically it's just a string of music videos that you have no choice over and just hope you do well at them to earn more in-game currency, or spend more of your actual money if you have a surplus of money and deficit in brain cells. Then you have the tracklist, which is good and has a nice pool of various songs and styles with plenty for the casual gamer and those who like crazy amounts of riffs and solos, but this brings me to one of the worst parts in that the individual songs are now tied to music videos, so not only does that mean that in the future you can only play songs that have music videos (no more buying an album from your favourite band and rocking out to whichever song you want) but also for some of the longer metal songs you only get what's in the music video. I was playing Hanger 18 by Megadeth and was surprised when the song ended before i even got half way through the solos, because the music video Megadeth released cut the song in half so as to be shown on music stations, the same will be true should they ever do a Dragonforce song since almost all of their videos cut the songs down to fit, imagine going to play Through The Fire And The Flames and finding yourself only playing half the song.

Finally let's discuss the new gameplay, which is both good and bad:
As i said i like the new guitar, the new two layers adds both more to do with the guitar but also more challenge, it takes a little getting used to at first especially if you're already familiar with the earlier games in the series but once you get the hang of it it makes for a far more interesting experience. That being said problems rapidly crop up when you start playing on the higher difficulties, because now the fret board starts coming at you at speed and the faster it goes the harder it is to differentiate between the black and white notes, your brain registers that you need to use your index finger but with all the other notes flying at you you end up with you fingers all over the place, this is especially true if the song has a lot of hammer-ons/pull-offs (the notes where you don't strum you just press them after pressing the button before) because they have a light blue aura around them which can occasionally make it almost impossible to tell what colour it is even when it's not in a bunch of other notes. Doing any of the more advanced songs on higher difficulties, such as Pantera's Cowboys From Hell or Trivium's Strife, just become a blur of buttons without actually being able to discern which ones are white or black.

This last section may mostly be down to me being rubbish at this game and therefore i concede that it may not be a problem you want to take into consideration, and like i said when you can make out the black from the white notes the new guitar controller is alot more fun. But the overall experience of this game is just painful, Guitar Hero Live is markedly too short and basically made up of throw away songs and boring strum fests, the GHTV is too stop/start/stop/start to enjoy consistently, the introduction of limited plays makes me want to cry, and the drawbacks of the medium of using solely music videos gives the game a very stunted feel.

Overall, if you're going to get this game, make sure you have friends to play it with and have them pitch in for the cost because the price of the game plus the new controller is not worth the brief but glorious moments of fun you'll get from this.

From the gameplay trailers I assumed this game was going to be Dragon Age: Inquisition but set on Mars. I was sadly mistaken.

The story has a lot of potential and some of the voice acting is pretty impressive but a lot of the lines are strung together no break in between so occasionally the dialogue just seems more like a quick-fire round of a quiz show rather than actual dialogue, and most of the people have no animation to their faces beyond the lips so they all have that blank "head on a pike" look to them.

All of this would make for a fairly enjoyable game but the combat that ties it all together and makes up the bulk of game is nothing short of abhorrent. What this game could really have done with is a Arkham style attack indicator since you spend most of the game dodging people and thus causing about 6-7 other enemies to disappear off the bottom of the screen where you can't see them coming. Then there's the enemies with guns who shoot you from a distance but give almost no sign that they're attacking even when they're on screen, so it's basically just the games way of saying "we're taking some of your health now, enjoi".

The technomancy skills would probably have made up the slack but they have almost no impact. For a game based almost entirely around lightning abilities they look and feel like getting slowly pawed by a kitten, and are fairly ineffective until the late game.

I feel inclined to finish off by pointing out that, while a lot of the areas have good atmosphere and unique feels, the game looks like a high end PS2 game rather than anything remotely current-gen. Now there will be fools who say "well it's a small team rather than a big-budget AAA game" but this game has no right being sold for full price as it is.

For the record I should point out that I wanted this game to be good, it looked really cool and had a cool premise, but the combat that ties it all together is just atrocious. Would not recommend buying (but still preferable to Homefront: The Revolution)

It's FIFA, if you've liked previous FIFA games you'll love this one, the animations are good, the opponent AI has been cranked up a bit, everythign feels a bit more fluid than last year's.

My one complaint would be the "story mode" called "The Journey" it starts off pretty damn great, i wasn't expecting it to feel quite as good as it did, but it ends so anti-climatically. You get one season, the resolution with your childhood friend is basically non-existent, your dad turns up at the end and says....hi? then you say hi back and walk off? Then right at the end it says Alex hunter has been selected for the England squad, but that's Alex hunter the character, not you the player, your just some scrub that EA couldn't be bothered to finish writing the story for. I have to knock off a whole star for that because it was genuinely gaining some traction, then it just...ends. Imagine Die Hard if after Professor Snape finds the body with Ho-ho-ho written on it it cuts to the building exploding and it just cuts to McClane walking out to meet the cop, then credits roll.

It....it's too good! Moving the plot to another galaxy makes it feel fresh, the characters all feel genuine which is mainly what I look for in a Mass Effect game.

The new combat system feels great, with a feeling that you genuinely have to take cover otherwise they're going to have to pull a brand new "Project Lazarus" on you, rather than most Third-Person Shooters where you can run out take a billion bullets to the face, then run back to cover. The skill tree is an excellent addition, giving you the freedom to choose whatever skills you want, but giving you the incentive to specialize, so the whole thing balances out.

The story does feel very much like the original Mass Effect and I don't consider that a bad thing. The main difference here (and what actually comes through during the missions) is that unlike Shepard, Riley is fairly new to this, he has some experience in the field but he is not an N7 god figure who once stopped the Skyllian Blitz (yes that was the best character background, don't even try and lie about it).

The game did have several bugs when it was first released (none of which actually ruined the game) but they've all been fixed now.

The Multiplayer is pretty much the same as ME3 and that was the best so I have no complaints. The rounds have been cut down to 7 instead of the old 11 but they also tend to be much harder, with each wave having considerably more enemies in it than in ME3. Ultimately it's down to teamwork and this game carries the same badge of honour as it's predecessors in that it is designed for people to work together without needing a microphone or having your own group of friends. You can go to any random mission with complete strangers and still everybody will know what they're doing.

My main criticism is that this game only introduces 2 new sentient speciesi, the Kett and the Angara. Compared to the previous trilogy that had the Salarians, the Turians, the Asari, the Quarians, the Geth, the Volus, the Hanar, the Drell, the Krogan, the Rachni, the Batarians, the Elcor, amongst others, just these 2 felt kind of weak. I'll note however that by the end both of these feel real and fit well with the rest of the cast.

All in all, Andromeda ticks most of the boxes I had for the beginning of a new trilogy, I'm hoping that the morons who work for review sites haven't stopped EA from making what is clearly built to be a whole new series.

I haven't played a PES game since the very first one and that's not because I thought it was bad or I was a "loyal" FIFA fan, it was just always one of those games that was just sort of there. But for the last 3 years all I hear online and in comment sections is "you should switch to PES, it's so much better than FIFA, much better play" and it's so sad because I gave into those comments this year and decided I’d get it to see if people were right and they were....wrong! Like woefully wrong, now I don't know if maybe these people just haven't played a FIFA game for a while, or maybe they've got inflated ideas of PES gameplay but it's just not anywhere near as good as people said.

Pros: Let's start with the good. Despite what people say I think the graphics of PES are generally better, especially players, you can very easily tell who players are, they do have a slight plastic look to them but they are very well designed, good parallels to their real life figures // Likewise the stadiums look good and the crowds look dynamic and real, though they're slightly quieter than real life // I’m going to put this under good just to round out the list but it does pass to the player I actually want it to more than FIFA does // I like that you can mostly customize the manager in career mode, which is something I’ve wanted in FIFA for some time rather than just a load of preset heads // EDIT: I also wanted to praise the commentary from Peter Drury and Jim Beglin, it's not quite as robust as FIFA but i much prefer the 2 and it continues to add that little extra spark any time you hear "AND COUTINHOOOOO!!!"

Cons: Like FIFA this game has a stupid tendency to pick the wrong player to switch to when I’m on the defensive. I'm trying to select a central player and regardless how many times I hit the switch button I always end up with a player out on the wing, or a play a couple of meters ahead, or someone on the other freakin' side of the pitch // Despite what people say this game, like FIFA, still leaves me time to go get a drink, maybe read the evening news, take the trash out, all between pressing a button and the player doing something. So many times in this game I’ve gone to shoot but my player seems to go on for another couple of steps before taking the shot, the same with through balls where you end up just sending it into the wall of players that weren't there when you initially pressed the triangle button // Single player career is a joke, I have no idea, and the game makes no attempt to teach me, how to improve my player, there's a menu you can select training from but it seems to have no effect regardless of how many games I play or how well my player did in the match // the same goes for club career mode, the GUI makes the transfer process needlessly difficult and it was messed up to begin with, clubs sometimes just turn you down, I didn't even say how much I was willing to pay and it just said "talks have broken down".

At the end of the day, if I had known that the gameplay is basically "FIFA but the screen is slightly brighter", and had I known that the game focus is almost 95% multiplayer, I would never have bothered buying this. Very disappointing for something I was hoping was going to be super fun. Back to FIFA to see what they've improved (if anything(probably nothing)).

Now can I attack? No because it's run away, and will take you nigh on 1-3 minutes just to catch up with it, and your stamina drains while you run after it. Can I attack now? No because your weapon is blunt. Right, I've sharpened it and he's run off and I've caught up, can I fight him now? No because another monster has come along and rather than fighting each other like common sense would dictate, apparently they both have a taste for you so enjoy running away.

I realize some of these are established things within Monster Hunter, and the game does look very nice, but it's been quite a while since I've had a game that makes me so aggravated and bored at the same time. I've played a long line of wwII games such as COD2, B&A & Earned in blood, MOFH Pacifc and Allied assults which are all great wwII combat similations but this game is a little different than the above mentioned and the difference is what I enjoy the most.

Instead of running and guning or ordering your troops around you are mainly solo and I mean solo. In war know one fights alone and that is true with most soldiers but with a sniper, 9x out of 10 he is alone because he does not want to attract attention to himself moving silently through the rubble.

With Sniper Elite you get to do this and more. Even though the graphics are not state-of-the-art by no means they are suficiant and get the point accross. You have to take out soldiers (Russian's this time) which I like because it seems that almost all wwII themed games these days focus on the Allied side of the wwII and not the Axis. Not saying I wish they won but I like fighting a different adversary once and while. In this game you are represented as an American soldier sent behind enemy lines (Berlin, Germany) at the end of wwII when the Russians had Hitlers SS with their backs against the wall in Berlin where they were defeated. Your job is quit simple, prevent the Russian military from obtaining the Nuculer Bomb plans from the German scientists. Though that seems easy enough it will literally take you 28 missions or so to succeed with this goal and many hours of great gameplay. I don't want to ruin it especially since I am still playing the game so I will narrow it down to and tell you what I like about this game:

Gameplay=1: great stealth gameplay makes you keep your head down and your body out-of-sight (THIS GAME IS not for the quick-fix-war-junkies via COD or MOFH fans)but the patient minded and slow movers taking in the scenery.

Game Physics=1: Awesome, you can't just shoot away expecting to hit your target, you will acually have to aim and take your time but setting the difficulty down to easy will lessen this a bit. Great bullet time effects and grusome blood effects!

Sound=1: It seems as though you were trans-ported to 1945 in the remains of the once mighty German empire! You hear bombs exploding, rockets soring through the air, screams and cries of the wounded, great sound though you may have to adjust your sound acceleration setting on your s card, there seems to be a bug at time making the sound distorted or an ecoing affect.

Graphics=-1: This is were I took off a point because of the overall detail of the graphics and the below adverage pixel count, some levels look better than adverage shooters and others, well not so revolutionary but it gets the job done. Not bad overall, just not great.

Replay Value=1: Once you get through the single player levels you can go online and duke it out will fellow comrades which is about what every other game offers these days to increase their replay value. I am however, not so much into multiplay because of bad past experiences namely (Red Orchastra) which is an awesome Eastern Front Multiplayer combat shooter than raises the bar on realism of war but has some bad players who rather see you dead than to help you out which are on your own team. I believe the multiplayer in this game is a solo advent so you shouldn't have an issue with this.

Overall=4/5: Worth the $29.00 dollars I paid for it! It's stealth gameplay, nerve-wracking missions are worth every penny and it's lengthy campaign will keep you busy for days if not weeks depending of course how often you play. Worth the money but not much more than this.

Final score: 4/5 points

Final comments: If you like to take your time in a game and draw your sites on a relentless enemy, this is the game for you!

I wont go into any spoilers but I will say that as a huge fan of the franchise this game was a giant step backwards. There were a few neat little additions like the ability to physicaly interact with people such as hugging, kissing and dancing with them but the game takes all of the control away from the gamer and in the hands of chance. You can no longer choose how you interact with people. 3 choices are randomly selected for you (most often dance or fart) and you are left with no other option. Further there is a real lack of clothing and hairstyles in this game which limits the customization of your character. Anyone familiar with the franchise knows that customization is a huge draw to the Halo franchise. Also your physique changes very little. And rather than allowing you to spend experience to physicaly customize your character's physical structure as in previous games simply performing certain actions slowly alter's your character's physique over time. This means most people can be assured to end up with the biggest strongest physique possible without even trying. Swinging your sword makes you more buff (even if you dont upgrade your mele damage) shooting a gun makes you tall (even if you never upgrade your shooting skills). Becayse there are so few clothing/hair items in the game there is very little variance in the kinds of treasure there is to be found. By the end of the game you may be so dissapointed and borde by the chests and dig spots in the game you may find yourself skipping right over them. In previouse games being good or evil slowly morphed your character either growing horns or sporting an halo with etherial butterflys. Fable 3 is distincly lacking in this area. At the finaly battle you do finaly get to sport a pair of wings that are different based on your alignment but these are only visible while performing a charged up mele or ranged attack. The whole interface of the game is a bit iritating. LH realy tried to remove all menues, hud and anything else that would make you feel you were playing a game to make it more imersive. Unfortunatly this means that all of the menues have been morphed into a sancuary where you have to actualy walk around to navigate what a menue handles much more simplisticaly. Finaly the main story line has very little to it and is actualy quite short with a rather anti climactic final battle. YOu are left with a "is this it?" feeling.

This is not to say there arent some dramatic improvements. As mentioned before you can physicaly interact with others making the NPC's feel a bit more life like than in previous versions. The Dog's interactions with the main character are also a bit improved. As well the multiplayer has been revamped actualy allowing other people's heroes into your world where you can marry, have kids and even partner up on business ventures. The spellcasting system is a bit inproved over the second game but in this gamer's opinion still a step back from the first game. For those who are not familiar with fable 2 the revamped spellcasting stystem made it nearly impossible to crate a pure spellcasting character. Also there is a new map screen which allows you to buy, sell and rent out properties without having to actualy travel around. This is a fantastic tool that leaves however one glaring problem. Houses you own slowly fall into disrepair over time. This means if you want to rent out properties you will have to spend a significant amount of time returning to the map room to repair each house individualy (they did not inclued a repair all option). Further there is no list of your houses and in what state of disrepair they are. Instead you have to search around the map clicking on each one and reparinging them one after another.

In the end if you are a hardcore Fable fan like me you will want to pick this game up if only to uncover the lore involved and to enjoy playing fable with a friend via the new multiplayer functions. I doubt however that many other than a few realy die hards and super casual gamers will find themselves holding on to this game like a treasure of gaming past like many of us do with Fable the lost chapters. Sadly this game will either fade to obscurity or be a permanent stain of the Fable franchise. Time will tell.

I have been waiting in gitty anticipation for this game for a long time. I bought the origonal Halo when it first came out and have been a diehard fan of the franchise ever since. This was not what I was expecting. Let me say that graphicaly this game is realy nice and parts of it are fantastic. I realy love getting to delve deeper into the character's of Cortana and Master Chiefe. But these things were not enough to save the game's shorcomings in my eyes.

SPOILER ALERT------------------------------------------------------------

From the getgo when you start the game something feels wrong. the new soundtrack does not jive with the old Halo spirit. It instead is somber with exotic wailing voices. It doesnt speak "here comes the invincible hero to save us all" it screams "lets all cry". getting into the game things look up. MC has a new look I dont realy like all that much but it isnt enough to spoil how beautiful the game looks. Immediatly I was impressed with the new cortana. You can realy feel her emotions and humanity just pours from her. Almost immediatly you are thrust into a fight with a splinter of the covenant that didnt get the memo. This just all feels wrong, the voices of the various creatures are messed up and while their tactics are similar I just couldnt shake the feeling that the flow of combat was completely off. Grunts have wierd buzzy voices that sound like some sort of swarming insect and the elietes barely make sounds other than growling. What happened to "wort wort wort" and "die devil!". Most noticable as well grenades seem powered down, almost useless against anything but grunts.

Continuing on eventualy hou have to fight the prometeans. At first I was exited but then you quickly figure out that fighting the prometheans realy doesnt differ much at all from fighting the covenant. The big guys behave almost identicaly to elietes other than they can telleport and the little ones are like fast moving grunts that crawl on the walls. Further promethean weapons just act like human weapons with new visuals. Fortunatly with incredible writing was enough to keep driving me through the game.

The story unfortunatly takes a turn for the worse. While we get to find out loads more about the MC and Cortana (like that they were both planned creations by an ancient forerunner called the librarian), and while we learn all sorts of interesting things about the forerunners and ancient human ancestors all this is spoiled in my eyes when they decided to write the death of the most beloved character from the Halo franchise. As many would know one of the major plot points of the game is that Cortana is going rampant "basicaly breaking down" and MC is trying to get her some help. Hope is always on the horizon in this game, hell they even find an artifact that can turn information into physical reality. But the end of the games sees Cortana sacrifice herself so MC can get home (So the librarian put a seed in humanity that would lead to the cration of MC and an AI who would who would be driven torturously insane and have to become a scfifical lamb, kinda screwed up and n my eyes the reason she couldnt go with MC was a copout). Cortana has always been MC's human side and I think 343 is trying to kill her off so they can humanise MC. Whatever the reason I was left feeling sour and kinda pissed. But still I held on hope thinking "maybe they will show us she is still alive after the credits" because halo always has a legendary ending. So I waited till the credits rolled and I was greeted with a scene of MC taking off his armor and seeing a glimpse of his face.... thats it... I dont care about his stinking face I want Cortana! Without Cortana there is no Halo franchise.

End Spoilers----------------------------------------------------------------------

Anyway, great graphics, mostly awsome visuals, great writing with a terrible ending, strange new voices for the covenant and a horrible soundtrack.

All the elder scrolls games have a few flaws that to me break the game and make them not quite as fun as they could be.  The open world system is a grand idea but without other players populating it there is a sense of emptiness that exudes.  This is probably because most of the NPCs are very cardboard and most of the open spaces are just that.  IT sort of feels like logging into an MMO only to discover you are the only one there.  Another issue with the Elder Scrolls games is their animations.  Monsters and animals seem to be animated ok (not fantastic but acceptable) but people are stiff and move in really awkward ways. This is especially true for the main character.  These games are obviously designed with first person in mind and third person control style is always just kind of thrown in.  Because of this not only is interacting with the world in third person sometimes difficult but the animations for the main character are painfully bad.  Just watching the main character jump in third person makes me cringe.  This wouldn't be a terrible problem if I didn't mind first person but in an RPG I am defiantly a third person player.  Now let me talk about glitches.  Skyrim like most Bethesda games suffers from many glitches, some of which are game killers, others will just crash the whole system.  They are done releasing updates so the numerous glitches that still exist aren't going anywhere and almost anyone wanting to complete a game is going to need to look up at least one work around before they are done.  Lastly some of the gameplay mechanics are just broken.  For instance the stealth character not only is the most powerful but the easiest to level.  You can have max stealth in a couple hours and be killing everything in one shot the rest of the game.  Also if you happen to stumble onto just the right items or quests early in the game you will be god like from there on out.  This can make the game so easy its dull.  This is not a problem unique to skyrim either.  Every Elder Scrolls game I have ever played has had ways of stumbling onto powerful items WAY too early in the game.  That being said Skyrim was certainly the most enjoyable in the series to date,  I have always loved northern myth and this game certainly portrays it well while still making it it's own.  If you like Elder Scrolls games you will love it, otherwise you may just find it OK.

This game is nothing like what I was promised.  I bought this game mostly because I was told that I could play halo 2 and 3 exactly as they were.  The only difference would be an update in graphics.  This however was sadly a huge lie.  Also I was promised the ability to create custom play lists, also a lie.  The game comes with pre made play lists but there is no possibility to create your own.  Also there is no ability to play say "big team battle halo 2"  You can play a halo 2 play list or a big team battle play list that includes all 4 games there are no deeper options.  Also nearly all of the customizable feature from halo 3 are gone.  You can choose Spartan or elite, and you can pick a base armor and 2 colors but the original allowed for armor, helmet and 3 colors.  Halo 2 anniversary mp has very few maps and most of them aren't even the popular ones.  To top it all off the "multi kill" voice has been changed entirely constantly spamming "protect your flag" every couple of seconds that someone has your flag.  Single player is completely whacked out as well.  First all the controls have to manually be set to play like their originals or you will be playing with the halo 4 control scheme on all games. Not a deal breaker but there are much deeper issues.  The enemy AI is much different than it used to be.  Elites rarely care to find cover instead preferring to charge at you guns blazing.  This is especially true if your shields are low.  Load areas that used to be fixed and allow you to bypass enemies have been changed.  And even the physics of the game just seem a bit off.  All in all this was a huge disappointment.  If all I cared about was single player I might be able to look passed the issues but the huge deal was the revival of halo 2 and 3 mp and in my mind they botched it.  This game was made for the Halo 4 crowd not the old school fans.

I hated Assassins Creed Revelations and Assassins Creed 3, I was more than prepared to never play an Assassins Creed game again. But then a funny thing happened, fans seemed to love this one and when it comes to gaming I take fan praise into consideration. As a gaming community we sometimes must rely on one another's opinions because sometimes we can't trust professional reviews.

With that said this game was truly amazing. I haven't loved an Assassins Creed game this much since the 2nd of the franchise.

Positives:

+The gameplay remains for the most part the same, so if you enjoy the good old Assassins Creed gameplay you feel
right at home in AC4.
+Stealth is great as usual, it's funny creeping around the cornering stalking your target.
+Naval battles are a complete joy and upgrading your ship is very addicting, you also control other ships but you only see them on a map and you use these ships to earn you extra money.
+If you enjoyed collecting items in prior games, this one definitely has plenty of things for you to collect.
+Story is one thing the Assassins a Creed series usually does a good job at.
+Blackbeard, the Pirates singing is also quite a joy to listen to.
+Graphically it looks good, and their is a good variety of locations to explore throughout the game.
+Main character is really compelling much better than Conor.

Negatives:

-Stealth missions can feel derivative and get annoying after you fail them 3-5 times.
-The story outside of Edward Kenway's is just plain bland and unnecessary.

Multiplayer-Standard AC multiplayer it's good fun, but it won't hold your interest for very long. Still it's a worthy addition to the series of multiplayer.

For the most part I highly recommend AC4 if you loved AC2 and enjoyed AC Brotherhood you will love this one. It gets a number of things right a few things wrong. Overall it's my favorite in the series and I've of the best games of 2013.
9/10

There is something about this game that keeps drawing me back. I find myself thinking of it when I'm at work, and I can't wait to get home to continue Geralt's quest for a couple more hours. It's weird... the game is a little slow for my liking, and I find the interactions between quest points (random encounters in the open world) to be rather sparse. Yet, I find the world of this game utterly compelling. It's a fascinating place, beautifully realized, and I just want to keep on exploring it with Geralt. I haven't yet been able to wrap my head around all the crafting and inventory details, but that hasn't impacted my enjoyment. Although animations aren't the best I've seen, the combat is very much enjoyable, thanks to the inclusion of magic with Geralt's superior swordsmanship. I don't think I would recommend this game to people who have nevery enjoyed RPGs, but if you're a fan of the genre, this might be the last game you need for a long, long time.

Though this game does not in any way look like a "next gen" title (at best, it looks like a decent PS3 game), that doesn't really matter, because it's just plain fun to play. The mechanics of this game work wonderfully, particularly the hand-to-hand combat and the driving, which has perfect, arcade style physics that fit the wonkiness of the premise. I love that this game lets you do all the fun stuff you want to, without punishing you for doing so or making the game harder to play if you cause a ruckus- that's the way I like open world games, to encourage freedom and wackiness at all moments. The story of this game is also awesome, as is the voice acting, although its serious nature creates a very odd contrast to the totally goofy gameplay.

I was rather skeptical when ordering these. However, like many, many PS4 owners, I had begun to destroy the rubber coating on my analog sticks, through nothing more than long term wear and tear. I tried these as a last resort, and much to my relief - they work even better than advertised! Indeed, I would recommend putting these on your DualShock 4 analogs even if they haven't begun to deteriorate yet. Why? Because these covers provide WAY better tactile feel and grip. They're just plain comfortable. I tried using my other DS4, without these covers, and I was amazed at how lacking the sticks felt without these. This is a bulletproof purchase (especially for the price), and you won't regret it!

It's hard to put the "wow" factor of this particular game into words. It's a very solid action game, mechanically speaking, but what puts it into a whole new level is its graphics. Sure, the cell-shaded approach has been used many, many times in previous games, dating all the way back to Jet Grind Radio on Sega Dreamcast (maybe even further back than that?), but never before has it been pulled off as successfully as it has been in Transformers Devastation. The look is downright mesmerizing, and playing this game makes you feel as if you're inside of a cartoon, embodying some of the most powerful and charismatic Transformers to ever set foot on your old tube TV. Fans in their 30s will obviously be tickled pink by this love letter to the old cartoon, but I find it hard to believe any fan of action, Transformers, or cartoons (even better if you're a fan of all three!) won't be delighted by what's been put on the disc here. Extra points for the inclusion of Grimlock and knocking $10 off the retail price ($50 upon release, as opposed to $60 for most games). I really hope Platinum Games and Activision build upon the winning formula they've crafted with this game and bring us more Transformers!

The one sentence summary: Three of my favorite all time games collected on one disc, polished beyond compare, delivering untold hours of fun.

The longer description: When I first played Drake's Fortune on PS3 in 2007, I was so floored by what I was playing, it compelled me to write my first ever Amazon review. I felt I simply had to tell gamers to try it. Eight years later, Drake's Fortune is still one of my favorite games, along with its two sequels. Each of them is unbelievably fun, featuring the best cast of characters I've ever experienced in gaming. Sully, Elena, and Nathan became like family to me as I engaged in our fast paced, thrilling adventures across the globe, and I cherish every moment I've spent in the remarkable world of Uncharted. These games have aged incredibly well, and the remastering of them has only improved upon their presentation and fun factor. And if you're like me and enjoyed spending plenty of time achieving the platinum trophies for these games on PS3, you can look forward to that challenging experience once again on PS4, along with some new, fun trophy challenges and a whole new difficulty setting.

Personally, I love to battle my way through these games on the "Crushing" difficulty level. I find the challenge to be perfect - extremely hard, but never frustrating. It sometimes takes me 50+ attempts over the course of an hour to clear ONE ROOM, but it's a very fun and rewarding experience. If you're a casual gamer, the game can be set to "Easy" or even "Explorer" (which is new for this edition, and sure to make you darned near invincible, if you simply want to enjoy the stellar story).

The second that iconic music starts up on the title screen, I start getting excited for the "interactive Indiana Jones" experience, which I've come to love like no other game series. And if you're new to this whole Uncharted thing... boy, are you in for a real treat.

Below is my original review for Drake's Fortune on PS3. Every word of it remains true, but now the impossible has occurred: the game is even better now on PS4! Now if I can only hold out for the tantalizing Uncharted 4 next year...

Original thoughts on Drake's Fortune in 2007:

Drake's Fortune is not only the best title yet released for the PS3, it is also one of the finest games ever created, for any platform. Production, production, production... quite simply the production values for Drake's Fortune are through the roof. From start to finish, developer Naughty Dog took zero shortcuts, and delivered exactly what gamers deserve to receive. The graphics, voice acting, game-play, interface, pacing, and reward system are all top notch, and they come together to form a sum that is a masterpiece of modern video gaming. (Naughty Dog has come a long way since the original Crash Bandicoot on PS1!)

Perhaps the most impressive accomplishment of Drake's Fortune is the pacing. Over the course of the adventure, I was never once bored, and I attribute that to the brilliant manner in which the story is delivered- not only through magnificent cut-scenes (featuring some of the finest face modeling, motion capture, and voice acting ever witnessed), but also because the game-play never gets stale. One level you're fighting for your life on a ship that is besieged by pirates, the next you're exploring a lush jungle, then onto a high-speed jeep chase with gunfire galore, followed by wave-runners, booby traps, duck and cover battles, submarines... you get the idea. You won't become bored, because Drake's Fortune won't give you a chance to. Even the delivery of the puzzles is brilliant- they are just challenging enough to provide a quick change in game-play, but they never slow down the pacing of the story.

And without revealing any spoilers, I will add that at one point in the game, I experienced the most authentic "survival horror" type game-play I have ever endured- even more so than in Resident Evil 4 or Condemned: Criminal Origins. I was literally sitting on the edge of my seat (gripping the controller far too tightly), and the muscles in my arms and shoulders were seizing up. Only when I gasped for air, did I realize that I had been holding my breath in fearful anticipation (wait until you see these lighting effects and character animations in action). Now that's convincing game-play!

At eight to ten hours, Drake's Fortune is of perfect length to maintain the excellent pacing. Every minute spent in this world is enjoyable, and never are the production values reduced. It is somewhat akin to an Indiana Jones movie, but far more rewarding. Instead of passively watching a character go through the motions, you become the character, and actively direct the adventure. Becoming Drake for a few hours, and joining the lovable Sully and Elena (your main companions), is so much fun, this is one experience that most gamers will want to revisit, multiple times, even after they have completed it.

At sixty dollars a pop, games are not particularly cheap, but I can assure you that Drake's Fortune is worth every penny, and plenty more. Naughty Dog (along with a handful of other studios- Kojima Productions, Insomniac, for example), has taken the challenge and the responsibility to deliver product of the highest quality into the hands of gamers. Fans of the industry are those who also support the industry, and when they pay out their hard-earned money, they deserve to receive a game that is as enjoyable and highly polished as Drake's Fortune.

Game developers, be advised: The bar has been raised!

Insomniac's reboot of their most cherished franchise does not disappoint. Whether you're a returning fan who has faithfully followed the series for 15 years, or a newcomer who enjoys platformers, you're sure to be delighted with this latest effort.

For those of us who grew up loving these Lombax adventures, this is everything we could have hoped for. All the things that make Ratchet and Clank so enjoyable are present, but executed at an extraordinarily high level. This is a game with character, a game with soul, and a game with peerless mechanics. Although the story has been slightly tweaked from the original, I feel all the revisions were made for the better, and they improve the development of the characters. Needless to say, the gameplay is also vastly improved, benefiting from the past 15 years of advancements that Insomniac has made, perfecting their platforming formula. There is nothing quite as satisfying as engaging in the twitch-style strafing action, amassing huge quantities of bolts while collecting and leveling up your hilarious arsenal of goofy weapons.

And what would a Ratchet and Clank game be without the visuals, which bring the amazing planets, space ships, aliens, robots, and various creatures to life? This reboot is the best looking Ratchet game by miles (which is saying something), and quite possibly the best looking console game I've ever seen. Although the art styles are completely different, I would argue that it looks as good (if not better) than this generation's heaviest hitters, like The Order and Until Dawn. It's a feast for the eyes, but more importantly - it's sustenance for your Lombax soul!

The icing on the cake is that this game is oddly priced well below standard retail. At $39, it's quite possibly the best investment in the solar system!

First off, it bears mentioning that I'm a huge fan of the series, so this is coming from the perspective of somebody who loves UC1, 2, and 3, and was hoping for more of the same. I've played each of those games about 30 times from start to finish, and I probably have the levels memorized better than some Naughty Dog employees (that's a slight exaggeration... possibly). If you did not like the previous games, you probably won't like this one any better, and I wouldn't spend time trying to convince you otherwise. However, if you're a UC fan... you're in for a treat; a magnificent reward for your 5 years of patience.

I expected UC4 to be an improvement over the previous entries, given the additional technology and experience on hand for Naughty Dog. But I wasn't expecting the improvements to be just... so... great. The thing I love foremost about this series is the strength of the characters. Nathan, Elena, and Sully have almost become like family to me, and I get such a kick out of having their company over the course of the campaigns. In 30 years of gaming, I don't think I've ever actually cared about the characters in a game - except for UC. This fourth entry takes that investment in character development to a whole new level, one rarely even seen in film. If you've been adventuring with Nate and Elena over the last nine years, just wait until you witness their interactions in their own home, playing PS1 classics on the couch and trying to dodge dish duty.

Story and character are my top priorities in UC, but fortunately the game plays as flawlessly as ever, with mechanics even being better than they were in UC3. Platforming has been overhauled, making for an experience that's much more challenging (and fun) than before, as you have to be very careful, quick to react, and have proper planning. Unlike before, there's a very good chance you will die a whole lot while swinging and leaping about like a crazy monkey. Stop-and-pop gameplay is still a blast, with vastly improved enemy AI and a more dynamic flavor that leads to greater challenge.

Finally, I need to mention the game's visuals, which are positively astounding, and really put me "there". The character animations during cinematic scenes are the best I've ever seen (even better than The Order), beautifully conveying the emotions of these beloved characters. There is, of course, a slight drop off from those sequences to the live gameplay, but the game looks remarkable every step of the way. Go ahead and zoom in on the texture of that carpet or the grain of that wood... rest assured, it will look amazing. The most impressive part of all this is the staggering attention to detail. Just wander around Nate and Elena's house, and marvel at how natural everything looks... the placement of dirty clothes on the floor, dishes in the sink, clutter in all the right places... it really puts you there, and makes you feel as if you're living these adventures with these people, not simply standing back and watching.

Naughty Dog raised the bar for adventure games with UC1 in 2007, and they just did it again with this game in 2016. Congratulations, Naughty Dog, and most of all... THANK YOU!

This game is hard to describe because it does so many things, it's practically bursting at the seams with creativity and content. At its heart it's an action game, similar perhaps to games like Bayonetta, but using a "crowd" of people instead of a single character. Don't be confused thinking this is at all like Pikmin, as it's completely different. On top of the frenetic, punishing action is a story that is mesmerizing in its scope and audacity, though it doesn't take itself seriously at all. This is a game that revels in the joy of playing games, and makes no apologies for it.

The game can be quite difficult to master but it's extremely rewarding when you do. Until then, there's always easy mode to get yourself acquainted and not get too frustrated.

If you like platformers, get this game, it's as simple as that. The game is highly polished, offers some great challenge, and the music by Donkey Kong Country series veteran David Wise (from the SNES originals!) is in absolutely top form with this game, with perhaps the best soundtrack of the year.

This is the "lesser" entry in the Ace Attorney series, a generally more forgettable adventure in an otherwise fantastic series.  With that said, it doesn't take long to get through, and it's worth it for the character interactions and story, and what they lend to the unparalleled third entry: Trials and Tribulations.

One of the best stories in videogames, and if you've been with Phoenix, Maya, and the crew from the first game until now, it might even make you shed a tear.  Really great cases and a fitting end to a story arc that really began with the first game.  One of my all time favorites.  Newcomer prosecutor Godot is a fan-favorite, and it's easy to see why when you play this game.

The Ace Attorney games are some of my favorites. You (generally) control Phoenix Wright, attorney, and this game covers his first cases as the lead defense attorney. Each case has you investigate a crime scene, talk to some witnesses, and your own client -- and then face off in a battle of wits in the courtroom with the prosecutor!

The games have a great sense of humor and are also quite touching as well. Things are certainly over the top with a cast of characters that is unforgettable and endearing, even when they're not on your side. This is a game that anybody can play -- winning cases are basically logic puzzles with simple touch controls -- but are enjoyable for everyone. Give it a shot, and you may find yourself enthralled. A great series and this game makes a great jumping off point.

By far the most revamped Pokémon game out of the series. They worked out a lot of the bumps to make it more user friendly. Old Pokémon are recycled into new forms/types, along with more efficient battling and menu screens.

Perhaps the biggest change is the lack of gym battles. This invites a whole new system of island/ tribe leader type battles. Pretty cool right? There are "trials", varying in all shapes and sizes. Never a dull moment here, that's for sure.

As for the story it's pretty quick with little to tell. If this is your first game you might like it, but I didn't.The whole idea of an evil organization just isn't that new anymore. Definetely made for a newer audience for sure (common themes). Has a lot of that island charm, but not a full fledged emotional adventure (Heartgold). What a letdown! Definetely fits the E for everyone 7+ ideaology.

Speaking of newbies I'd say I'm no stranger to battling, and this is the most complex it's ever been. The story is easy enough to beat, but with a steep level increase at the Pokémon league. The real issue is online battling which is where the game ends for me. New Pokémon wipe out classic ubers with effortless ease. The path to victory and glory is long and hard fought. Hope you have a good plan because mine went out the window.

Besides online there's not much else afterwards. You can catch 'em all pretty easily through wise trading and shrewd business deals. The gameplay mechanics are pristine though, with a lot of nonsense cut out. The story is good enough and heartfelt. All the games are good in their own right and so is this one. For a 3DS game, this is top tier merchandise. Why not give it a shot?

First off I would like to state that I'm a big fan of the earlier tiger woods golf games. 2003, 2004 (my personal favorite) and 2005 were all very good golf games. 06, 07 and 08 however were all pretty sorry affairs - my primary beef? The normal swing mechanism (pulling back the directional joystick and then pulling it forward)somehow became broken - it's almost impossible to make a good shot. This HAS NOT been fixed in 09 HOWEVER you have the option to use a 2 click method - in short this works very well and doesn't hurt from the overall experience.

Combined with everything else - tons of beautifully replicated courses and everything else I remember from the older versions - this is a fun game where everything for the most part works well.

My only other minor beef is that save times are unusually slow and putting has a serious learning curve (at first it's easier to chip in a ball than putt it in from a similar distance).

At the low price I got this game for I certainly feel like I got a bargain.

For the record I grew up with a NES, played computer games during their hayday ( the 90's ) and my second console was an N64. I missed out playing these games always assuming that there was little fun to be had from the Sega brand - most of my friends growing up played computer games and Nintendo systems.

In short I was wrong.

I'm playing the 2 Shining Force games for the first time (I'm a huge tactical RPG fan) and I'm having alot of fun playing them despite the simple gameplay and AI. These 2 titles by themselves are worth the current price of admission. Add in the ability to play the 4 Phantasy Star titles, which I've wanted to play for ages, this is one heck of a deal.

Even if you're not a fan of RPGs there are a host of other great titles here to play. The 2 Vectorman titles are alot of fun if you like side scrolling platformer/shooters (they play pretty well when being experienced by me for the first time. Ditto for the Sonic titles.

I haven't had a chance to play ever game extensively yet (that would take a huge time commitment) but so far I've enjoyed everything I've played (I've avoided what most people consider the few stinkers on this collection).

No collection this big is going to have nothing but gems ,and everyone who grew up with the console will be disappointed that every game they loved growing up isn't included, however for the money you can't go wrong if you're capable of enjoying older games. (Great gameplay isn't something that's new, or dead for that matter.)

Enjoy.

The pin connector may solve your problem but in most cases you can easily salvage your old one.

Simply remove the old pin connector and clean with an old tooth brush and Brasso. Be gentle when cleaning and immediately wipe off all of the Brasso residue (it's strong stuff and can damage the connector). Before reattaching clean off the part that the pin connector connects to on the board. Even a new connector can have problems if you don't clean the grime off of the board. You should also clean off your cartridges in the same manner. Cue tips and diluted rubbing alcohol can be used if you want to minimize the risk of damaging your game cartridges but rubbing alcohol is less effective. You will need to order a proper screwdriver http://www.amazon.com/Steel-3-8mm-Screwdriver-Security-Nintendo-Games/dp/B000F8GWH2 and open the cartridges to clean them properly.

Buy a new pin connector if you can't salvage your old one.

A final warning to be gentle when cleaning your connector/cartridges with Brasso. Again clean off the residue when you're done.

Hope this helps you save a few bucks.

There are 3 major Jet Ski releases to come out in 2001. The first, Wave Race Blue Storm, was good, but didnt live up to expectations.  I was disappointed with the awful play control and lack of very creative courses.  THen there was wave rally for PS2, which is a mediocre game all together.  Then there is splashdown- the one that blows the others out of the water! (no pun intended) This has got it all- silky smooth play controls, great graphics and framerate, plenty of tracks and riders to keep you occupied, multi player, and so much more.  The tracks are innovative and creative.  The multiplayer is even better. It also takes up hardly any memory card space.  If you like these arcade-like racers, this should definately be your number one pick.  The only complaint i have is that if you are doing a circuit- you have to race by yourself first on the course, to figure out where you will be placed for the next race, in which you race against challenging, but not extremely hard computer racers. This makes the circuit take a long time. But there is a time trial mode which is more worth your time.  Get this game for the PS2.  Its the best wave-racer to come out since Wave Race 64.

I can't believe I am the first after weeks of this game being released to make a review!

Nonetheless, here we go.

This game is amazing for a portable game. The graphics and sound are just far above what you expect when you think portable gaming and they actually tied the story to the original well too.

Gameplay: The Gameplay is top notch. Not only do you explore towns, talk to NPCs and have the Final Fantasy experience you would expect, but there are also side missions that act as a quick fix incase you don't have enough time to actually focus on the story. You can play these whenever you find a save point and they serve as a nice way to get you some extra potions and experience. Interactivity is similar to what you would find in the classic game as far as finding items by exploring the environment and seeing unique sights because you were curious enough to explore every nook and cranny. There are even side missions like having professor hogo making you face huge monsters in an attempt to kill you because you disturbed him. The Story is what shines the most in this game, and it is by far one of the most engrossing stories of the series.

Graphics: This game seriously looks like the first Kingdom hearts on the PS2. Their facial expressions and animations are the best you can find on a portable system to date. This game could be ported to the PS2 and considered to have gorgeous graphics. The CG scenes are on par with Advent Children.

Sound: The Voice acting is actually pretty good, and the music from Final Fantasy VII that was redone for the game isn't bad either, but the new music to the game is pretty forgettable. I honestly can't stand the shinra building's theme, which feels like it is 10 seconds long and just set to loop. This is one of the game's biggest strengths and downfalls at the same time.

Replay Value: You could speed through the story and still expect hours upon hours to be spent doing side missions. The story itself takes a good amount of time to beat. Expect to invest maybe 30 hours into this game.

This game is a fantastic deal. Expect to have a blast with it and you wont be disappointed.

SPECIAL NOTE: There are some things to this game that you might want to take into consideration. I started playing this game on my old PSP then early into it bought the new model. The difference is HUGE. The load times on the new PSP are cut not only in half, but takes the load time from up to 18 seconds at some points to maybe 3-4 tops. There is also a very low amount of blur when Zack is running around on the screen on the new one compared to the old one. The new screen is brighter, higher refresh rate and the load time on the new one is way shorter. The new PSP is almost a must for this game otherwise load times will destroy the experience.

The original Ninja Gaiden was an incredible feat of gaming. It alone brought the franchise back in full force into the 20th century. Assuming you don't require Ninja Gaiden II to do the same thing, it will be the best action platformer of the year if not longer. This game doesn't do anything new, which in many ways isn't a bad thing at all! It takes exactly what was great about Ninja Gaiden and made it faster, stronger, bloodier, harder and more beautiful than ever before. I have to admit, I believe they did have to tone down the visuals on the environments a bit to maintain a steady 60fps (frames per second - 60 fps is what game developers strive for to provide fluid gaming experience), but this doesn't degrade the gameplay a single bit. In fact, if you would just stand there to look at the environment there is a good chance you would become headless very shortly.

"Why should I buy this game?" Instead of going into all the details regarding what rank the graphics, gameplay, sound, etc are 1-10 i'll just say why this game might be worth purchasing or not.

WHY I SHOULD BUY: The game has solid and fluid gameplay complete with amazing visuals are great mechanics. The game is a great challenge complete with a nice variety of weapons, all providing you different fighting styles and advantages, as well as making the game extremely hard to put down.

WHY I SHOULDN'T BUY: The game is a great challenge, but it's also so hard that sometimes it might make you put your controller through your TV. To some that is nice but to casual gamers that can be a turn off. The Story, though many will argue isn't important for a game like this, is almost non-existent. The Camera can be very annoying as well. Often you are attacked by people you do not even see. This can be avoided by using the left shoulder button and the right trigger button at the correct times to keep the camera behind you or looking the way you want. Eventually if you get into the game enough, hitting these buttons becomes part of your fighting style but a lot of casual gamers do not want to invest that much effort into something many other games make automatic.

As the title suggests, I own a 360. I have read and studied graphic comparisons, reviews and more between the two systems as long as they have been out. Until this game came out (MGS4) I was not planning on getting a Ps3 anytime soon. As someone that uses every feature my 360 has, this is my views and my impression on the Ps3 system as well as the game itself.

::=:: THE PS3 SYSTEM::=::

First I want to start with the ps3. I always heard good things about the system itself but that was never enough to make me go out and get one. The game selection for the 360 always attracted me, but now, especially with the release of Metal Gear Solid 4, it's a great time to pick one up. I use my laptop's Windows Media Center with my 360 to stream a huge amount of videos I have to my TV, which I honestly never expected the ps3 to be able to do, but it does. This was an awesome surprise. Not only does it detect my laptop, but also it sees the 5 other computers on my network that are sharing content and I can access them all! Not only that, I can access them from my ps3 remotely with my PSP through any WIFI connection. It's a weird feeling to be able to stream videos from your Laptop that is wirelessly connected to your Ps3 at home, while you are miles away on a handheld. The HDMI connection displaying everything at 1080P is breathtaking and blue ray movies truly do look stunning. The game menu is actually rather simple as well, but in a good way. It lays out everything in front of you but though it does that, it doesn't clutter you with content. You don't feel overwhelmed at all with the menus.

The games on the system look stunning. I have read countless reviews for games that go cross platform and I will admit; games like Call of Duty 4, Rainbow Six Vegas 2 and other cross platform titles do have better texture quality on the 360 but games that are literally designed for the Ps3 are amazing. I currently have Heavenly Sword and MGS4 (duh) and I have not seen graphics and draw distances like these on the 360. The power of this system seems limitless right now, and the games made specifically for it show it. The system also has Bluetooth built in, which lets me take my Bluetooth headset and merely hook it up to my system to use in games like Metal Gear Solid 4's online multiplayer. The backwards compatibility on the system works without a hitch, though I have had some lag with Metal Gear Solid 3. Apparently these new Ps3 systems merely emulate the Ps2 instead of how it worked with the old systems which actually had the real Ps2 emotion chip built in. This is why MGS3 lags on this system when it wouldn't lag on the original Ps3 systems.

Overall for the system this is an amazing deal. You get the 80 gig system which use to be $600 for $100 less but it also comes with a new release (and likely the best game the system has seen yet), and a duel shock 3 controller. That's nuts! I wouldn't suggest just buying the system by itself, but this deal is worth it. Now that I have the system I am finding more titles I wouldn't mind owning, so if you're a 360 fan, this system IS actually for you.

::=:: Metal Gear Solid 4 - Son's of the Patriots::=::

To date, as a person that is actually heavily into game development, I have not seen nor played a game that looks better, is more polished, and more innovative as this one. This game shouldn't even be referred to as a game, as it should merely be addressed to the public as an "Experience." Anyone that grew up with Snake and his adventures will get an experience out of this game that cannot be missed and expressed in words.

:~::GRAPHICS::~:

What can I say about the graphics that hasn't already been said? The two words that come to mind are: ABSOLUTLY GORGEOUS. Every "cinema" isn't even a video it's merely in game play being shown through cameras set at different angles. The Environments, player models, weapons, lighting is all top notch!

SCORE: 10/10

:~::STORY::~:

Every inch of this story is great and it ties up every loose end the series has. The story is told so that every cinema is well worth watching and no matter what you think you know, there are always new events that change EVERYTHING even until the last credit rolls (and afterward so watch on past the credits). Each character is built up well and has a lot of back-story to them. Since the story is so serious, there are a ton of Easter eggs to look forward to that not only make you laugh but make you enjoy the experience even more.

SCORE: 10/10

:~::GAMEPLAY::~:

As I sit here and write this, I am actually smirking because as someone who has beat the game and then has to describe the gameplay...well, there's no way to really do it without sounding like a gitty school girl. The polish and fine-tuning was immense. The stealth, camo, guns, customization, levels/environments, voice acting, story; everything involved in gameplay deserves more than a 10. You never get bored, and though the levels are a bit linier, you can beat through this game dozens of times and still have some extra to shoot for while having unique experiences each time.

SCORE: 10/10

:~::SOUND::~:

The voice acting was done by some serious talent and it shows. David Hayter (Solid Snake) does a beautiful job. This was definitely a step up from the first Metal Gear Solid. You have Phil La Marr (Vamp) who does the voice of Hermes in Futurama. The list goes on. Anyhow, the music, sound FX and voices are just outstanding and really help the game flow.
SCORE: 10/10

No one used this title yet? Seriously? Anyhow, I figured I would write a small review for this game. I don't think I have reviewed many games that would fit under the horror genre and it just seemed overdue. Warning though people, possible spoilers here.

Let me begin by saying that this game is outstanding. It's interesting playing this game along side Resident Evil 5 since they did launch very close to each other. The graphics and controls are just outstanding and though the graphics in Resident Evil 5 may be slightly better, the controls in Dead Space more than make up for the experience.

It starts with a simple blue fuzzy screen where a zoom up of the main character's girl friend's face makes you terrified that the game's graphics are going to be awful. And then, when you think you wasted your cash, you are pleasantly surprised by some truly breathtaking visuals. Time to relax, you made a good choice. The relaxation doesn't last too long because two and a half minutes of talking and continued pretty visuals later the S word hits the fan and you are thrown into danger. It reminded me of Resident Evil 1 back in 1996 where you knew there was nothing good that could come out of your present location, but you felt that false sense of security was justified. Wrong. They not only don't let that feeling last, but they also prove that if you didn't read the instructions and figured out how to run, you'll die quickly (like first instance of seeing an enemy kind of early). At this point you are thrown into the fire, and you have to survive and do things to help your remaining crew. The thing I liked most about this game over others I have played like it is that it really feels like your actions have purpose. The objectives aren't things you could see yourself skipping. For instance, your partner radios you tell you that the engines are offline so the gravitation pull of the planet is pulling the ship in and soon it may start doing things like exploding or starting on fire. Stopping that from happening is a great objective! Never once did I go, "Why" when they asked me to do something. It just felt like a great story playing out.

The ambience in the game was utterly outstanding. They had a ton of scares, some obvious and others not. With the incorporation of realistic physics, a good chunk scares are you just knocking into stuff and then freaking out thinking someone is behind you. Don't get me wrong though, it's done very well. The sound in the game helps a lot with the scare factors. You will be walking down what you assume is an empty hallway but you can hear the aliens crawling around in the vents above you, or in the walls. You will hear something crawling above you and suddenly be attacked from behind. It's not cheap though, they don't spawn out of nowhere, you just need to be aware of your surroundings and take note of vents, etc.

Once again, the graphics are outstanding. The shadows, shading, and bump mapping are done very well and it's not ridiculous. Little effects that they didn't even need to put in are there and this is especially noticed when you go into zero gravity or any place that outer space is involved ("but Garrett your on a space ship!" I know). What I mean by this is when you go into certain halls there is damage to the hull and you get to travel around the debris and look at the insane detail that was put into making the atmosphere realistic. Things float around, planets are in the distance, water flows out of the pipe in super slow motion, and the sound is extremely muted. The muted sound not only creates an awesome ambience but also masks any monster trying to bite your bum off.

Like mentioned earlier, the controls rock. Do not play this game then move to Resident Evil 5 because you will be quite displeased. You walk around and are able to do full 360s with the left analog stick while changing the camera with the right analog stick. They also help speed up your response time to danger by making it so you automatically turn and aim where you are looking. This is handy if you look over your shoulder, see someone and want to shoot them immediately instead of later on. Other aspects of gameplay were mentioned earlier like missions that actually mean something, but there is another thing that makes this game awesome. You have a series of technical abilities used for puzzles and combat that almost makes this game like 1/8th a Zelda title (I lol'ed at that so I kept it in). You can use them to lift and move objects, throw them and even slow down time. It's cool to see something about to impale you only to slow down its movements and blow it away ever so gracefully.

I think I covered everything. We have graphics, gameplay, sound, controls.... Oh yeah I forgot!

MENU and SHOPPING/WORKBENCH: The menu system is exactly what a game like this should have. Resident Evil 5 may have incorporated a real time menu that doesn't pause the game because you wouldn't want that in co-op play, but Dead space does it because it wouldn't make any sense to do otherwise! In space no one waits for your long paused decisions in order to maul you. That might be a bit extreme but this was the first game of this kind that I played that stripped the ability to pause it, pick your weapon carefully and then proceed. You have to think on your feet or die trying. Getting back on point, the actual menus are multi-layered holograms that just pop up wherever you need and actually shed light on the environment which I thought was an awesome detail. Audio and video messages not to mention any ship controls are all holograms as well and it really gives you an idea of how cool the technology is on this ship. The shopping which I mentioned in caps at the beginning of this paragraph is pretty cool too. Picture a robotic version of the merchant from RE4 and you pretty much got the idea of it. Cool thing is you can buy armor upgrades and actually see them applied to your character as well as buy, sell, store and hand in schematics to get upgrades, etc. It's been done before, but it works VERY well in Dead Space. Another interesting thing is the workbench. It's separate than the shopping center so you have to look out for them but you can use the work bench to upgrade such things as your suit's oxygen capacity, gun stats, armor stats, etc. This was very cool and it's also nice because if you don't want to use it, you don't have to. It's possible to beat the game without it, though you'd only be making it harder on yourself seeing its not very complex what so ever (which is a good thing).

I think that is about it. I think this is an amazing title that is completely worth the $20. I would suggest exploring this game's story so you are ready for the next one because it is the same main character.

$250 for the Vita may seem reasonable for a new portable, but there are hidden costs if you actually want to use it the way they advertise to you. Recent benchmarks show that not only are these memory cards significantly slower in regards to data throughput and data writing, but they only perform better as you have the higher cards. Loading a level in Wipeout will take you nearly a minute, while having a larger card will only save you about 10 seconds. The standard SD cards that you can pick up anywhere, and the same ones that the 3DS use have a significant performance increase compared to this new format Sony devised for a profit. The worst part about this card is that it is completely required in order to use the Vita in the manner that Sony advertised to you in the very first place.

That ladies in gentleman, is shady business.

There are a lot of positive reviews likely written directly after the item is delivered and the person is thrilled with their new toy, but take this review of an early adopter for consideration if you will.

The reason why this is the first game bundled with the Vita that you hear about is because of it's brand recognition. Before this game there was a long period of time that the Vita provided nothing that a console wouldn't, and also lacked in quality titles that only a hand held could offer. The answer to that was gravity Rush which came after months of waiting. It was a blast, but that was still really the only game that made this system uniquely worth having. Fast forward months and months later to this new Assassin's Creed game, which sorry, but is a watered down experience compared to the new console version out. It's good, it's just not as good as what else is offered out there. The point is, they are putting the AC:L and Vita together because they want to claim this game is worth owning the system for. Even if that was the case, what happens afterwards? The Vita is still being used as a perpetual tech demo, getting every toned down console game ported that it can. I really makes you wonder if you should just have a vita, or just have a PS3. They try to combat that by giving you a code to have both versions in very few select games but that adds to more problems, which is the memory card. It is a complete rip off. The memory cards are low performance and slow, not to mention nearly 4x (at launch, now 3x)the cost of other, higher performance memory cards like it and they completely required for the Vita's use. 4Gb is not only not enough space, but it will make your experience with this system abysmal as you will have to use their extremely clunky program to transfer items back and forth to manage the card and its limited size. Many games are even larger than the 4Gb memory card which instantly hinders your positive experience.

I ask you to consider that after the "WOW" of this new game wears off, what are you left with? You are left with a battery eating, heavy, supped up PSP that seeks to drain your patience and money through overpriced store items. Plants vs Zombies for example is $14.99 when you can get it for the iPad HD (using that as an example because its portable and has a gorgeous screen) for as low as $0.99 or even $6.99 at it's most expensive. The PSV's web browser is terrible and its more than apparent that it was just tacked on with little consideration for how it would perform. The system is great while you play a game that is worth owning but so far it's too few and far between to warrant a purchase. Gravity rush moved a lot of Vitas but then all those people pretty much had to wait for this game months later to enjoy the system again. There is nothing that says this will be different.
