I was pretty happy a couple months ago with this product, knowing it was finally starting to work properly and that another patch was coming in April. Here we are in May, 2 more patches later, and I'm encountering bugs in the Halo 4 campaign that weren't previously there. The game is a lot better than what it was at launch, but it still has a ways to go. If you're looking to buy an Xbox One for this game, DON'T. You're going to be in for a disappointing experience right off the bat, so skip it and go for Halo 5 this fall. The beta for Halo 5 was leaps and bounds better (bug free, smooth, it actually works) than the Master Chief Collection.

The core concept of this game is pretty neat with 4 players vs. a powerful monster, but it feels like the concept of making money from DLC also influenced the design of this game. For $60 it feels like you're getting half of the actual game; you basically get a meager 3 monsters to play as and a handful of characters to team up with. Sure, you can get more monsters and characters to make it more fun to play,  but it will cost you, a lot of money in fact. This is an otherwise decent game, but the DLC practices at play really make it a bad one to recommend.

This remaster is a lot more than just the PS3 version at 1080p. Playing with it these last 2 days, it's clear that texture resolution, shadows and lighting have been upgraded significantly. The geometry is the same, but this does not look like a PS3 game and is actually up there with some of the better looking titles on PS4.

The gameplay itself has aged well and it's kind of refreshing to play because there hasn't been anything like it since the release of the new consoles. It still has the most epic boss fights I've seen in a game, and I think picking God of War 3 for the remaster was the best choice (It's one of the best games in the franchise). The 60FPS framerate makes more of a difference here than in most games; the game opens with you fighting on the shoulders and arms of a moving Titan, while a boss claws into into it, twisting it this way and that. Between the moving ground, the scale of the boss, the special effects, and your character attacking it, there is a fluid visual display going on that at times is so impressive that it's beyond anything shown on PS4 so far.

My only gripe is the cutscene movies, which look like they are ripped straight from the PS3 version at 720p, possibly upscaled 1080p but not native (they are a little blurry and even have jaggies in them). The switch from cutscene to gameplay is a bit jarring because the quality is vastly different, but the cutscenes are still decent and more than serviceable. Also, the title screen looks unchanged from PS3 and doesn't make a good first impression.

I bought this bundle to replace a launch PS4 unit, because I love the Darth Vader design and the bundled retro games (Racer Revenge was one of my favorites on the PS2).

This review isn't for the game, but the system itself. Even though Sony does not advertise it, this model is HUGELY improved in quality over the launch units, and the units sold in the first year (it's actually a new model/hardware revision,CUH 1215A) . Unlike many of the PS4 models sold, there is no annoying CLICK! when it powers on and off (which caused the lights to flicker in my room), there is no loud wwwrrrRRRRR sound as the fan spins up, the LED light bar is brighter, the disc drive and fan noise is now quieter than the Xbox One (which is very quiet already), it produces far less heat, and the overall picture quality is a step above the launch models (brighter colors, clearer details, noticeable improvement of the HDMI output quality). All my games look better across the board, with the same video settings as before. It's really a shame (but also great) that anyone buying a PS4 for the first time now is getting an excellent product, while there are millions of people out there with cheaply made, lower quality older models.

If you're in the market for a console, this model is the best you can buy, and the best console overall (better graphics, more gamer-centric features, disc based games that can be played immediately (no 10GB day one patches like the Xbox), fast software updates, a lot more Japanese-made
games if that's your thing). If you're looking to make a smart purchase for a gamer this Christmas, you cannot go wrong with this.

I want to like the Xbox but this system has a lot of issues. The customer experience when using this system s pretty poor overall. When you buy a game, get ready to wait… and wait… before you can even play it. The game needs to install of the disc and install patches, sometimes over 10GB patches in size, before you can play. This can take hours for a single game.

This is also the only console that lets users accidentally buy the same digital game twice without telling your sibling or friend that you already own it… I bought the Deluxe Edition Rise of the Tomb Raider when it first came out, then my sister was allowed to re-buy it again accidentally in december with no warning on the game page in the store (the option to buy should be replaced with something like "Manage Game" instead of "Buy Now $64.99". There was an Xbox Live Gold discount on it, which seemed to enable a re-purchase. Thanks to Microsoft's No Refund policy, I'm not sure if I can get my money back...

The Oculus is magical. I like it because it is capable of so much - like the Development Kit versions of it, so much is possible if you tinker and explore with it. I just discovered that you can play many non-VR PC games in full 3D with it - if the game has been built for Nvidia 3D vision, it will run in 3D with the Rift using Steam VR Theater, even with an AMD graphics card (I use an R9 390X). The higher the frame rates you get, the better the 3D - an R9 390X can handle all the games I try with it so if you have an Nvidia card, you will be good if you have the equivalent GTX 980 or better. The Oculus also shines is with the 3D VR movie apps at your disposal - they are like YouTube but everything is in VR. I rode on the Thunder Mountain roller coaster at Disney World, all in 3D with 360 view. It was great! Oculus really proves its benefit with the videos.

Build quality is excellent - durable heavy duty plastics and great screen. It also fits my big head comfortably. I do not see the screen door effect on mine - there seems to be some sort of film that eliminates it that I can see when the screen goes dark (lots of tiny little bubbles it looks like). Also, I'm using a stock 3.4 Ghz i5 3570 - very slightly below the minimum Rift CPU requirements but it handles everything without issue. The Rift overall seems like very well designed, highly optimized technology.

Also worth noting - the rift requires USB 3.0 ports to power itself, and some 3.0 ports it just does not like. If you're using a USB 3.0 PCIe card, it has to have the Fresco Logic chipset. Just get the USB card recommended by Oculus on their website, which is very easy to install and high quality to boot.

I'll start with the good first: this console is very small, even smaller than the PS4 in a side by side comparison (about 1cm wider from side to side, but about 3.5 inches shorter front to back). It's extremely well built - gone are the creaky lightweight plastics and hollow feel of the original Xbox One, now replaced with thick, durable white plastic and a solid heavy feel for its size. The system looks expensive and high class. The upscaler is also really good - even backwards compatible Xbox 360 games (which run 720p natively) look absolutely great and crisp.

This Xbox requires your TV to be at least 60hz to select it's 4K option (due to some games running at 60 frames per second) and to enjoy HDR your TV will need to have HDR10 built in. So even if you have a 30hz 4K TV with Dolby Vision HDR, you might not be able to benefit at all. Keep this in mind.

We are 3 years into this console generation now, and it seems the PS4 is becoming the system of choice for most. However, I can say owning both that this white Xbox One S is nicer than the PS4 in its current form, both in terms of design, build quality and features (but a new 4K PlayStation is also right around the corner that will compete with this Xbox). If you're in the market for an Xbox, this is the model to get. The older Xbox One designs are cheaper, but you will get what you pay for in this case.

So I'll answer the questions everyone probably wants to know. There's been mixed reports of this PS4 model being whisper quiet, or as loud as the original. Besides a couple of games (Uncharted 4 and Infamous First Light) where the fan ramps up to about level 2 on a scale of 1 to 4, this model is so quiet that you can barely hear it unless you put your ear right next to the exhaust vents.

The system does have rubber feet on it - 3 of them, two underneath the front corners and one in the middle at the back, so the system is stable and does not wobble. Originally it looked as if the bottom was just molded plastic with plastic feet and my concern was poor molding would make it wobble all over, but this is not the case.

The system looks a lot nicer in person. It actually looks great, and I can describe here why. The pictures make the matte plastic look rough, and the system a grayish color - in person the system is dark black, and the matte plastic is softer. The bumps/texture of the plastic is much finer than the original, so it actually looks great with the glossy black PlayStation logo in the middle and from different angles. The pictures also don't catch the slanted parallelogram look well, but in person it's easy to see. Overall the design actually looks really nice.

The Bluray drive is the same as the other older PS4 models, with the same sounds and loading/spinning noises. The new 5Ghz network card also makes a very noticeable difference - this should have been included in the beginning, but at least it's here now!

Overall a great redesign, and a good buy!

I decided to purchase this game completely on a whim after having some spending money left on a Best Buy gift card. While it's pretty good as far as goat simulation is concerned, it does require the Steam engine. This isn't a problem for me since I already have a Steam account, but it does make me wonder why selling the game in this format was even necessary to begin with. The disc becomes permanently useless after the installation process. Also, ESRB rating this Mature is completely unwarranted, as the game contains little explicit content outside of some small references in the map -- and this can be filtered out.

As for the game itself, it does a great job of providing a few hours of immature fun -- mostly through lots of goat-initiated mayhem and weird easter eggs. You might find yourself configuring the game's graphics/settings at first in order to make the camera less jumpy and the controls smoother. I find that the game lags less in fullscreen. There are plenty of achievements and trophies to obtain -- and a handful of playable characters to unlock, including an ostrich and a giraffe. The game's entertainment value depends on the individual's sense of humor. If you manage to become bored, Steam's Workshop support offers some fun user-created mods with extra maps and a... quadrupedal Shrek?

Being a goat and destroying everything in your path is something I can see as a great outlet to let out any pent-up stress. I think the game's best played with someone to enjoy the goat's destructive antics with, and with as little knowledge of what to expect beforehand. It's silly, stupid, pointless fun... but fun nonetheless. You might be better off just getting a code for the game, but give it a try either way.

I have no idea why people have been calling this a bad game and seem to abhor Connor's character nearly to the point of disgust. Maybe that's because I'm a newbie to the Assassin's Creed series and haven't played any of the games before this. However, despite a few flawed gameplay mechanics and small bugs, I've encountered none of the game-breaking glitches many seem to attest to. Yes, running up buildings can be frustrating during chase sequences, but unless you're a spastic chimpanzee, it shouldn't be too much of a problem. The claims of poor optimization also do not hold much water for me, as the game ran incredibly fine (no FPS drops in Boston) and using a keyboard was especially comfortable. Admittedly, I did have to lower resolution in order to have the game run at its fastest, but the graphics are still breathtaking and I'm never really one to complain in that department.

While new to the franchise, I still found the story very interesting and enjoyed the progression. I loved starting out as the charismatic Haytham, but just as equally enjoyed my role as his stoic son, Connor. The modern day segments with Desmond were decent, but I was far more interested in Connor's story and Desmond's sometimes disrupted the immersion. Are the cutscenes as excessive as many claim? As someone who's played quite a few games that require reading walls of text, the cutscenes here were a cakewalk for me and I happened to very much enjoy the exposition they provided. My only real gripe with the game is that many of the optional objectives presented in each mission are next to impossible, and seeing a red X at the end of a sequence can be disheartening. Combat felt cluttered/stilted at times and relied too much on counters, but as my skill improved, it became a much smoother and more enjoyable process. The combo takedowns and kill animations provided some decent satisfaction.

The American Revolution is an overlooked subject in video games and it's actually really exciting getting to see the events you learned about in fourth grade history come to life. It's not entirely accurate, but a faithful representation for the most part. People complaining about the intro and linear missions are just impatient. I don't think it's a crime to have enjoyed this game.

I first borrowed a 3DS off a relative, in which time I was able to play and actually finish Super Mario 3D Land -- a game that allegedly needed 3D, but found myself seldom using. Part of my motivation for buying my own handheld was to complete some of the series I had already started on the DS, but also because I felt I was missing out on a great deal of entertaining titles. Like many others have stated, I think the 3D is a gimmick for the most part and I found it difficult to view for prolonged periods of time. With that said, why pay extra for a feature I'll hardly use? That's where the brilliant 2DS comes in.

Sadly, the 2DS has become a bit of a recurring joke in the Nintendo gaming community, but let not the admittedly awkward-looking, flat design of this product fool you. Once you actually hold this baby in your hands, you'll be surprised at how much more comfortable it is than the original clamshell. While the speakers aren't as loud here, this is never too much of an issue for me since I prefer to play in quiet areas to begin with. I mean, the price is incredible, it can do everything the 3DS can do (except close and display 3D obviously), and I'm not complaining.

Seeing as this is an "early access" title and is not a finished product, one should expect to come across a handful of bugs. However, as of now, the developers are active in keeping supporters in the loop and are consistently offering updates/fixes to any noticeable issues. I would recommend you grab this in a sale -- otherwise, I don't think it's worth any more than 15 bucks. That's not to say it's a bad or broken game, but the content is still relatively bare bones at the moment. If you can get this anywhere below that price, then I think this is a worthy investment.

The visuals are fresh and mesmerizing, the sound effects outperform my headphones, and the gameplay is very well-developed despite the game's early state. Just be prepared to die dozens of times before you can survive even a slightly significant amount of time. This is not something you can just breeze through with ease and I was caught off guard more times than I can count. Strategy is not an option here -- it is a necessity. Also, I have to commend the creators for purposely excluding zombies, which have become excruciatingly tiresome in the "horror" and "survival" genres. My only gripe with the game so far is that wolf attacks are all too frequent, so hopefully this issue is remedied in a future patch. Otherwise, this is still a wonderful game... and best played when cold or during the wee hours of the morning.

I feel like I'm in the minority whose played and loved both the Professor Layton and Ace Attorney series. Most of the people I'm seeing have played either one or the other, which is a shame. If you want to get the full enjoyment out of this crossover experience, I highly recommend you play at least the original trilogies of both series. They are worth your time and emotions. If this is your first time hearing about either character, don't even consider buying this game. Mostly because that's stupid. Also, consider the fact that both games are story-centric and filled to the brim with text before submitting a negative review complaining about that very fact. You are not this game's target audience and you need to leave.

Nonetheless, this is an exceptional game and should serve as a testament that crossovers are capable of pulling off much more than blatant fanservice, as Level-5 and Capcom have managed to produce an impressive title with gameplay styles that blend well. If a questionably canon crossover can bring me on the verge of tears... that's a pretty damn good crossover. And if Layton and Wright isn't the smartest combination in the known gaming universe, then one does not exist. The writing is fantastic and the character interaction is pulled off believably, with quirky dialogue and humor that have become a staple in both titles. I'm not kidding when I say that this game has what is probably the best plot twist to come out of either series, but of course... that's left for debate.

Other than the occasional (but minor) framerate lag, the only issue I could find was the fact that when I was playing as Wright, I wanted to go back to Layton. And when I was playing as Layton, I wanted to go back to Wright. Mostly because they always left me at cliffhangers, but that's not really a bad thing. The puzzles here are noticeably easier and absolute cannon fodder to anyone who's breezed through puzzles in other Layton games. Truthfully, this is a good thing for me, as I really hate some of the math problems they've thrown at me in earlier games. The court sessions here, on the other hand, were personally more challenging than anything else I've experienced in the Ace Attorney series, as they required a lot less of the logic I was accustomed to (being "witch trials" and all) and cross-examining multiple witnesses at once can be overwhelming at times. Though I'd have to say that adds more to the intensity of the court drama and is in no way a con. At the end of the day, I can very well say that this was a great experience worth the time and money, made even better by the fact that I've been a fan of both characters for a good while now. If you're a fellow fan and you're wondering if you should buy this, all I can tell you is that you definitely should.

This is my first One Piece game. I have played neither the Pirate Warriors nor Unlimited series before, so I cannot use any previous games as a point of reference in regards to Unlimited World Red. However, what is present in this game is exceptionally executed and an expansion to Oda's long-running franchise that is clearly far from being an unforgivable cash grab. Whether you have a 2DS or 3DS, you should know that the 3D option is not available for this game regardless. I don't think it really needs it, but 3D purists might be disappointed.

Nonetheless, the graphics are well-polished and stay as true to the aesthetic of the anime as possible. The campaign is relatively short and its storyline, while new, isn't anything you haven't already seen in the source material. I mean that literally. You traverse the locations of various arcs and fight the illusions of enemies that the Straw Hats have faced before. There are plenty of side quests, updates to the main hub, and collectibles that can eat away hours of gameplay. I hear people saying that a Circle Pad Pro is a requirement, but... you must be psychotic to suggest I should shell out a fortune for what amounts to nothing more than a single extra button. To each his own, of course, but I'm personally finding no trouble in playing without it, as the "L" button is a quick fix that immediately places the camera behind the character.

The highlight of the game for me personally was the "Battle Coliseum" mode. There's a decent roster of characters that do not take an eternity to unlock and the combat is not scaled by performance. I hate having a good time with a game, only to have it remind me that I suck. 'Tis a shame there's no online multiplayer, but there's more than enough content to keep me invested. Definitely recommended for those who like the RPG and "hack 'n' slash" genres, but even better for established fans of One Piece.

The first Paper Mario and Thousand Year Door were enjoyable turn-based RPG games. Super Paper Mario abandoned those roots, but still made up for it by delivering a solid story and characters. Sticker Star feels somewhat watered down compared to those games, but it's still a genuinely fun and innovative 3DS title. However, due to the amount of times I may or may not have spent screaming at my device, my personal rating for the game is bumped down just a star. Still, this is nowhere as bad as people make it out to be.

That said, there are some considerably frustrating moments in this game, such as the often unguided locations of "Thing Stickers" that are a requirement to overcome certain bosses/obstacles. Backtracking continuously in order to nab stickers you missed isn't very fun. Also, you should keep in mind that this title lacks the frequent leveling up in previous Paper Mario games, and the progression that is available is quite bare. In other words, fighting enemies felt unnecessary unless I wanted coins. No partners/pixels either, other than Kersti. What really duped me at the end, though, was that there was no save. The game takes you right back where you left off before fighting Bowser. This was excusable in the first game, but seeing as TTYD and SPM both saved at the end, it's actually quite disheartening. The satisfaction of beating the campaign isn't as fulfilling here because of that.

Like I said, though, this isn't too bad of a game. In fact, I actually grew to prefer the new sticker-based combat system. It's fun (when the enemies aren't too overwhelming), creative, and generally well-developed. The fun of peeling off stickers combined with the game's graphics and animations actually sold the whole "Paper" concept a lot better than the first three titles. The music, if not quite as catchy or memorable, still gives off a good, jazzy vibe and really helps set the mood. There are some aspects of the pre-release version that I would've loved to see implemented, but what I was given was still plenty satisfying.

Overall, the quirky dialogue and humor of the first three games is mostly intact, if minimal. If you're looking for a new story in the Mario franchise and a colorful cast of characters, Sticker Star is not the game. This is a good 20-25 hour experience, but there isn't much to do outside of the campaign other than filling up the sticker museum. Recommended? Sure. That's mostly up to you.

I can't say much about how Dark Moon holds up to the original Luigi's Mansion on the Gamecube since I've never played it, but I found this game to be a thoroughly satisfying experience. The single-player campaign consists of short levels that ‒ while linear/directed ‒ require a bit of exploration and thinking in order to complete. While they might take a few plays to get used to, the controls are generally easy to grasp and not too complex. Plus, sucking up ghosts with the Poltergust 5000 is a ton of fun. Anyone who hasn't played the first game is easily caught up to speed with how everything works, as Professor E. Gadd consistently reminds the player what to do and how to operate the devices Luigi uses once they're introduced.

My favorite part of the game has to be the online multiplayer, as it adds a creative spin to the already stellar gameplay and encourages teamwork rather than rivalry. You can easily find yourself killing hours here. Hunter, Rush, and Polterpup are all mostly equally fun modes that each have something pretty unique to offer. For Americans, I'd say the best time to play online is during the day. At night, finding decent players can be quite a bit difficult, and there are only a few Japanese people on there. I suspect this loosens up at some point as the time shifts in the Eastern Hemisphere, but I digress. Unfortunately, as with all multiplayer games (especially those with co-op), there are trolls who enjoy souring the experience for others by hurling spike seeds at you for some unprovoked reason, deliberately refusing to step on their tile in Rush mode, or making nary an effort to win. People bumping into you to steal your key and leaving your game before crucial moments can also be a bit frustrating. Be wary of these people!

Basically, it's a really fun game that grows on you if it doesn't impress you initially. There's plenty of content offered here without being overwhelming. Even after two years, the price for this game is still above $20 and it's well-deserved, in my opinion. Definitely recommended.

Of all the games I played so far this year, this is one of the best. It has a unique and creative story that takes place up in the clouds in a place called Columbia. I shouldn't need to go word for word about the story. I will say that with Elisabeth, the partner that you rescue utilizes good A.I. and differs on the difficulty on how much she helps you. The story to the end is a pretty trip and the title of game rings what the meaning is at the end.

The graphics are great but more importantly it is done in a cool unique artistic style, somewhat like other past games but stands out on its own as does the enemies you encounter that blend well within the world.

The gameplay is really fun and incredible and stands out as a different FPS by doing one major thing different, zip lining. You can move from area to area by getting on a zip line to travel. Its pretty cool and makes the game stand out completely. It also does a unique job in combat by letting you mix plasmas which is similiar to other past games. They are upgradable and you can mix them up during battle. The weapons are upgradable and makes a big impact during combat.

I highly recommend this game. It all boils down to gameplay and its one fun ride. The graphics are nice, the music is very moving and fitting, and it has a story that you would hold onto for great conversations.

This alongside Bioshock Infinite are two of my favorite gaming experiences this year. It is very different than other Tomb Raider games. You don't do backflips, handstands, and such. It plays more like Uncharted. You do have puzzle elements but they are mostly optionable as side quest for treasure. It though has a clever level design in how its a restriced open world. As you play you will gain new abilities which lets you get to new areas like the design of Super Metroid and the latest Batman games.

Now as for the gameplay, it is really incredible. There is an upgrade system for you weapons and your tools. There is a lot of collecting that can be done. The combat is very precise and fun if it is melee or shooting.

Graphically, it is stunning to look at. It has set pieces like that of Uncharted. The game borrows a lot from Uncharted. Lara Croft is shown to be vunerable as you she plays throughout the game. This is a reboot but as a prequal since it is her first adventure. I highly recommend this game. It has great music that builds on the tension and things always stays fresh. The game seems grounded in reality but as you play, you will see that it still retains some of that Tomb Raider like story.

As for the collector's edition. It is ok. I don't think its a big deal for the game. I recommend just getting the regular version.

This game is incredible. If eye candy is your thing than you might want to look elsewhere. It plays and looks like an old school game. This game is all about the fast paced twitch gameplay done to incredible music with a twisted story. The music is incredible. The gameplay is no slouch either. One wrong move and your dead. You only need to get hit once to die. They are small levels though and it reloads fast to try again if you do die. You use various weapons and unlock new ones and have different masks that you acquire to wear. The story is twisted and has an incredible trippy ending that must be seen. I highly highly recommend this game. It is so cheap. If you don't like using a keyboard, it is compatible with the 360 controller, and on top of that, this game is coming out on the Vita.

This is easily one of the best and newest JRPGs out right now. That is not saying a lot but it is a great one that doesn't deserve to be passed up and it doesn't stray away from why the series is good or change things up to broaden its fanbase. Unlike some JRPGs the series still retains visual contact with your enemies on the screen so you won't enter a random battle without noticing it beforehand. It has a lot of customization and your able to upgrade everything from your gels to heal yourself to everything you wear.

The story is also pretty cool and it has a good meaning behind it. There is a lot of character development and you choose though how much of it you actually want to experience. There will be times when you are able to push select if you choose to watch the characters mingle amongst each other. It can sometimes be long, sometimes not and plays out through voice, text, and still images. There is though cutscenes in the game and they play out nicely. Visually, it is has vibrant nice colors and great animations, and nice visual effects during combat.

The game also has a lot of replay value. After the credits role, the game doesn't actually end. Even beyond that, there is a Game + Mode and it allows you to gain or lose certain things through a second playthrough. This game has 100s of hours of gameplay because of that and the many sidequests you can go on. I recommend this game for JRPG fans.

The Last of Us is easily one of the best games of the year. It starts off the beginning with the plague and then shifts to the aftermath quickly. Its good to experience the story itself without giving much detail. There is a lot that could spoil little things that are surprises that happen throughout the game.

What I loved?

There is a mix between fighting and hiding. You can get through some areas by without fighting but some encounters you will have to but its mixed very well.

The characters throughout the game will talk about area you are in giving it a sense of realism and talking about what once was. Ellie doesn't know much about he world before so she often asks about things within the world she sees as you travel.

There is a nice sense of exploration for items necessary to upgrade your abilities, to make items, and such. There is also documents, comics, and such to be found.

Humans are sometimes a bigger threat than the affected.

It is a beautiful looking game.

The story is very moving and is one of the finest examples of developing characters seeing their struggles and seeing how the bond between Jolie and Ellie form.

Those are the strong points. There isn't much weak about it. Its an incredible experience. There are some impactful things happen that I thought would end the game but it kept going. I beat the game and can tell you it is well told from beginning to end. I highly recommend this game. The Survival edition comes with a nice dynamic theme background and the art book is pretty nice. I don't think its necessary to get but I happy with it, especially for such an incredible game that was really addicting to play, incredible to look at, and so immersive.

I am a multi-console owner who also has a Xbox One (see my profile for PS4 review). I was a huge supporter of the PS3/360/Wii and have the Wii U. I have to say that the Xbox One is impressive in user interface in what you can do with it but its a bit complex in using create things such as Snap where you can have two windows open at the same time. It does have some cool improvements such as sleeker achievement designs when they pop up (you can change their colors) and them each having pictures when you check them out. It even have a nicer design to compare your achievements with others. There is now even achievements to watch movies and tv shows or even downloading an app. They are separate from your gaming achievements are achievements such as watch 20 episodes of a tv show, watch so many tv shows after 9pm, and such.

The controller is much improved. I haven't been able to try the rumble feature in the triggers which is a big cool improvement in the design of the controller but overall I am not as impressed with it as I am with the PS4 controller. The analog sticks feel more loose in comparison and the d-pad is a bit too low. Overall it works but it would have been nice if the controller was a bit bigger. The Xbox logo lights up white which looks very cool.

The design of the hardware itself as in the look if it is pretty bulky. It would have been nice if it was something other than square. It is bigger than the 360. The kinect looks a lot better and works extremely well and can tell its a huge improvement. Now inside the system itself, it has the windows 8 design. I am not a fan of it. It looks nice but I don't like navigating it and this design is terrible to look for games. I think they could improve by at least have categories to look up genres but goes from popular to new and that is all. Snap is the coolest thing. You can literally watch a tv show on netflix or hulu plus and jump back in the game in an instant. You can do the same thing by having your cable provider connected through Xbox Live and look through its in-system guide to find what to watch and do the same thing. Now they also have video recorder so you can record your gameplay and even do a picture-in-picture of yourself and edit it of your gameplay footage.

I think the weakness of Microsoft consoles is they take few risks and don't provide an extensive library of new IPs on a yearly basis but this time around they have Titanfall on the way which is the most anticipated next gen game to come out on all systems only. It will only be available on the Xbox One. You have Halo which is one of the biggest franchises that will make a return and you have Forza which launched that is arguably the best current racing franchise. Games Played:

Dead Rising 3

If your interested in the game, I recommend it if your exclusively into multiplayer gaming. First of all the collector's edition is too expensive for what it offers. The statue is made of plastic material. It feels sturdy enough and nicely designed but it losses its appeal when you realize its not made of polystone. The art book is nice and the poster is nothing special.

Now the game itself is worth it for 60 dollars but you have to be heavily into multiplayer. The campaign mode isn't much of a campaign mode and doesn't tell much of a story at all. You go through missions but nothing memorable. The strength of the game is the mobility you play as a pilot traversing around parkour style and the Titans that you get through the game. The more kills you get the faster you get a Titan. A cool aspect is after you achieve your objective be it death match, taking over zones, and such you will be given one last life right before the end to either escape via spaceship or take out those evacuating. It is a cool twist to end the match. Besides that, there are different modes such as Titan only mode where everyone has to kill so many of each others' Titans to win.

As for stats, there is a lot and there isn't a lot of weapons but its a bit made up for by the Titans having their own weapon mods as well. The stats are bare compared to franchises like Call of Duty and Battlefield. Besides weapons and mods, you do have the ability to gain abilities such as extended invisibility, quicker re-load, and such. Now the music is great and it looks great. I highly recommend this game. I don't consider it a reason for an Xbox One but consider it a game that is a must for Xbox One owners.

This new and improved system is impressive because of the following 3 reasons:

1. Energy efficient- The new PS3 Slim uses less than half the energy than the old version. If you use the PS3 all the time like I do this will result in visible results on your monthly energy bill! Thats a very big plus indeed!

2. Finger print-less finish- Finally there is a PS3 that isn't coated in a gallon of clear coat, It looks clean even when its not now.

3. Size and storage- Smaller means less space to use up in your entertainment system and more storage = more demo's and extras you can fit on the hard drive.

Overall the energy savings alone is a reason to upgrade and if your a heavy user like me then I wouldn't doubt it if the system pays for it self in energy savings over time. A great improvement and great buy!

I really wanted to like this game but there are a number of things that has made me really dislike it.  Number one is the crummy save system.  Instead of saving the game where you left off before you died the game either sends you back to a HQ where you tediously have to reload your guns and ammo or it starts at a checkpoint where you have to go through all the things you did before.  The sneak doesn't work because the too numerous Nazis can apparently see everything and through walls and behind trees so it is an almost useless skill.  if you expect to win a shoot out, forget it for once the silly Nazi blows his magic whistle the Nazi spawn out of the ground faster than Darkspawn and you will never kill them all as they spawn right in front of you and behind.  Sean is a weak character who dies easily when the Nazi spawns pop out of the ground and see through the trees.  You do a lot of tedious running for your life in this game looking for safe places to hide only to find that most of the time when you get there you can't get in because the all-seeing, all knowing Nazis saw you from a hundred yards away.  If there were this many Nazis in France in the 1940's all seeing and all knowing, they would have won the war.  What could have been a great game is just ruined because of the silliness of spawning Nazis with magic whistles.  I shot so many Zeppelins from a Turret gun  that I ran up the money to more than 10 ks.  Repeat this is not a game for shooters. One of the most annoying games ever.

This game has the worst controls of any game I have ever played.  They simply suck.  The game quickly becomes very boring as you leap and jump your way around 15th century Italian cities, looking for people to kill with a bunch of fun sucking conditions such as find five impossible to find people without being seen in less than a minute or else you will de-synchronize.  Or beat up the no-goodnik husband cheating on his too ugly wife.  The controls just don't work with this game as the contextual context makes your character dive when he should jump or turns on your good for little eagle eye when you want your goons that you hired to beat up the guards of the loot you don't need.  The game is very tedious.  I thought The Saboteur was the most annoying, tedious and stupid game I have ever played but this game is right next to it.  A big waste of money.

This review is based on my personal experience with this game.  First there are no seamless neighborhoods as there are in the Windows versions.  That is a drag as you have to watch loading screen after loading screen appear.  While the game is fun to play the loading time is ridiculous long.  Maybe there is something wrong with my XBox but I just finished playing Mass Effect 2 repeatedly and had no problem with it and there was no load time for hardly anything in that game.  My real gripe is, and this is the one that is sucking the life out of this game for me, is that when saving the game I have repeatedly encounter failure after failure.  Even when the save is working it takes up to twenty seconds or more for the game to save.  Again, I have not had this problem with any of the other games I have played recently.  The closest is Mass Effect but as that is an older game that might be expected but even that game saved correctly.  It certainly was not the case with Mass Effect 2, or Assassin Creed 2 or even Rumble Rose, an older game I still like to play.  All of those game save quickly and as they should.  I would like to like this game.  It has some neat features on it such as the house building tool but, alas, even that has limits on the amount of stuff you can buy.  My two musicians got so rich they were able to build three houses and remodel a 4th  and each time Johnny Storm appeared preventing even more decorations or remodeling.  What is the point of having so much money if you can't spend a little bit of it?  There are some other aspect of this game that I dislike.  The time of the day goes by too fast.  By the time you eat a sandwich, go to work, go to that potty, go to shower, it is another day so that leaves hardly anytime of socialization unless you use karma powers which you have to unlock.  I had to turn the aging thing off as it is also a fun sucker since every 17 Sims day your character ages up.  I was really annoyed to find that by the time one of my Sims became a Rock Star she turned into an cripple stereotypical old lady chewing her gum and her green hair white.  That sucked royally.  Mind you I don't object to the aging feature, it is that the character aged so quickly and turned on the eve of her success so she did not get to reap the benefits of all her hard work playing on street corners and working in the music hall.  Sorry to say but this game just doesn't cut it for me because of the tediousness of loading screens and the failure to save properly making you replay things you have already achieved.

I enjoyed my first play through of this game as a mage, but the second one has been a bug filled nightmare with my warrior moving either not at all or at a snail pace when in combat.  He either ends up dead or the enemies are dead before he lands a single blow he is so slow.  Not entirely sure when this happened as it was not that way in the beginning.  When calling the dog to combat the warrior freezes up entirely and is unable to move at all so the dog has had to go.  There are dialogue sections that are out of order such as Merrill talking about the fate of the keeper even before that quest is has been given, and other bugs that just make this second play through very tedious and boring.  If you played the first game, you will recognize that this game is a cut down version of that with a less of everything from skills to interactions with your team mates.  In the first game you could actually end up caring about the fate of your companions and that is much harder to do in the second game. Lack of an x button so you can actually see what you are picking up is annoying.  In the first game you could see if the the things you picked up was actually worth anything.  There is a lot of repetition of objects you pick up such stuff as raven feathers.  The flaws that were in the first game concerning making money are carried over into this game but since most of the stuff in the second game are junk anyway that might not be a big deal.  However, Hawke like the Warden is just a glorified junk man picking up stuff that really don't have much worth.  Maybe EA should have named him Sanford after Sanford and Son.  I loved the first game but have soured quickly on the second since the warrior is so unplayable.  It just has stopped being fun and there is no guarantee that the problem with him will not happen if a new game is started.  I played the first game over thirty time, but I don't see that happening with DA  2 unless the problems are fixed.  Lots of bugs in this game with even a mission that you can not complete as it simply isn't all there.

Not sure I care for the story line about a Mechanic  (see Charles Bronson Jan-Michael Vincent movie) who wants to be the number one.  Graphics didn't thrill me much but then again, I didn't play it for very long as it quickly got annoying and didn't hold my short attention span.  I'll stick to games I like such as Dragon Age, Mass Effect and the Uncharted games rather than this game.  I am sure this game will find some fans for this slash and hack kind of thing. Onechanbara was okay but I found it rather primative.  None of those game had you pressing R3 and moving it in a certain direction to finish off the foe.  I am sure that there are games I will like much better than this one and are better than this one too.

While UnCharted 3 is breathtakingly beautiful, action-packed, and, at times, even exciting, ultimately it is one of the the most disappointing games I have ever played.  The main story is ok, if you like long lengthy passages where all you do is go on long walks in the bizarre, or the museum or the desert where you do very little other than walk and get plot filler.  There is not enough Elena or Chloe in the story and what is there is basically walkon roles.  Where the game really becomes miserable and vile, however, is in the split screen co-op where you get to fight dead people from the previous games, many of whom are impossible to kill even when you reach level 40.  They have gatekeepers, the have bosses, they have chokers--all of whom are nearly impossible to kill even when hit with a bazooka or a hammer. What were the developers thinking to make a game that is nearly impossible to beat? They have guns that don't kill even the lesser enemies as they ought, and when you try to roll, more times than naught you will end up deader than a doornail.  I liked the first two games, no that is too mild, I loved them.  They were two of the best games I ever played, although not without their faults.  They came as close to perfect as anyone can expect of a game.  But this version, well that is another story.

It was, at first, very confusing but we soon figured things out.  However, when we took a break and attempted to take up from the spot we stopped, only one of us could play. Dishonored 2 is the sequel to the dishonored one of my favorite games of the last generation and seeing a sequel I was excited to dip my toes back into the world. What I got was a pretty disappointing sequel to the first Dishonored game. Now at first I thought it was just me so I went back and played the first game and nope it was still phenomenal. So what happen let's find out.

Pros:
I'll start with a brief positive and say that the game's art style of whale punk style looks good here as it did in the first game unfortunately that's all I can say positive about the game.

Cons:
Gameplay, limited by the morality system from the first game and the difficulty scale enemies can either be dumb or really sharp and know your exact location when you make the slightest noise. Making the gameplay not as fun as the first game where there was a balance to it and in this game they just botched it. To the point where it became a drag just playing this game. Again I went back to the first game and it did not have this issue that the sequel has.

Story, another plague and another political conspiracy in a mostly recycled story but with Emily taking the helm of course you can play as Corvo too but he's not as fun or powerful as Emily so playing as him you really miss out. The story is forgettable and Lore has been retcon for some reason. I can not tell you any memorable characters in the plot because they all suck. Like the outsider from being this mysterious figure malicious in the first to being jollier in the sequel. They never explained this change it was just retconned

Performance, it is now 2019 it been years since the launch and while performance has been improved it still runs poorly. It's still buggy and this game will not be fixed as Bethesda is pretty much done with the franchise as this game and death of the outsider sold like trash. So we got a fundamentally weak game at it's core and bad performance to add insult to injury. Fantastic.

Verdict.
Many say that sequels are often a disapointment, but this was my first encounter with a truly disgusting excuse of one. Having such a marvel of a game be rubbed in the dirt like this is just pitiful. Well, I don't have to worry about more sequels as the franchise has been iced as the spin-off Death of the Outsider and this game sold as well as meat in a vegan festival. Other than that I have nothing more to say than the game is just awful. It failed in almost every level for me and that's something that rarely happens to games I play.

Fire Emblem Three Houses are the latest Fire Emblem game coming from the waifu revolution in the 3DS games. Nintendo has raised the stakes and taken the school system from Persona before long we will have a Dancing game spin-off on our hands. Jokes aside Fire Emblem Three Houses is the latest game in the Fire Emblem series coming strong after the 3DS and making a triumphant return to a home console in a decade. Take Game of Thrones meets Persona all in an Anime aesthetic and you have the Game of The Year and one of the best reasons to buy a Switch.

Fire Emblem Three Houses like other Fire Emblem’s before it is a tactical turn-based strategy game that takes a big focus on the characters this time around. With three houses to choose from hence the name three houses (brilliant right?). The characters are the best fire emblem has ever seen. I took the Black Eagle’s route and it was just fantastic in terms of the main story and the choices you were presented that give you an alternate route to take in the second part. However, by far the characters were the strongest part all with interesting stories and a great English dub. I surprising loved most of the characters all except one. Who I got halfway through the game and immediately benched and that was, of course, was Cyril. I, of course, heard great things about the other houses that I didn’t get to play. The Blue Lions and Golden Deer being on the same level as Black Eagles but of course, the Black Eagles are the best house. This game lives and dies by the characters because if you don’t like any of the characters you’re not going to like the game. With a school being introduced straight from Persona with a lot of people also citing Harry Potter but without it’s more Persona inspired. As you teach your companions outside of battle or just hang out with them, eat lunch with them or invite them for tea. Playing it made me reminisce a lot about Persona 5 the time management as the calendar moves along now in-game and not in real-time. Which is an improvement now you get to experience all the birthdays and events you could have missed without having to cheese the system and changing the dates on the 3DS settings.

The Story is the best Fire Emblem story to date with a Game of Thrones like House system with Three major powers of the fictional country of Fodlan. All whose heirs are attending the school as students with big plans for the future. It’s like if Game of Thrones was an anime. It’s the right blend of Western-inspired fantasy, all while being rooted in its Japanese roots. Separated into two parts White Clouds and Silver Snow. Part one is mostly similar regardless of what house you pick and part two is when the paths divulge based on the House you picked in the beginning. Setting for the perfect branching narratives and as mentioned before Black Eagles has two routes. Fire Emblem three house’s story of politics, the status quo and the dawn of change is well down. A surprisingly morally grey story with no real villain that gets it right mostly. The tactical gameplay fitting right in the setting. You have the Fire Emblem staple the builds, classes, and support system. That all comes together with the school setting as you can teach students specific builds and classes that don’t even match with the recommended ones. Like you can make all your warriors into mages if you want or make your healers into archers. You can also recruit other members from other houses and you can clean house on all the other houses. Which I mainly ignored except for those outside the house, One anecdote from my playthrough that shows the visceral gameplay was turning the weak Bernie into a Bow Knight and having her go 180 from useless to melting everyone. Another one is changing Petra from an Assassin to Wyvern Rider and scrambling the last month of the game to promote her the master class Wyvern Lord just barely making her a Wyvern Lord before the last boss fight and that satisfying feeling of getting her that master class was second to none. Finally, we have the graphics and the game doesn’t look bad it’s not the most good looking game ever. It relies mainly on the art style with the Anime cell shade aesthetics which isn’t bad I like that style. The models look good except a distance they start to look like mii’s especially Flayn. Still, this is the best looking Fire Emblem to date.

Fire Emblem isn’t perfect however and the game does have issues like all games do. Towards the end, the game just slogs on. Like I thought I defeated the final boss I was so satisfied with the conclusion and the game pulls a Bioshock 1 on me and says now you have to defeat the real bad guys. Which those two maps were not bad per se but it did ruin the pacing of the second part. The second issue I have is more of a pet peeve and that is the not so silent, silent protagonist. The protagonist talks in battle and in the dialogue he’s a mute. Why do they do this? I don’t know if they give your character a voice and they can’t even have him voice the anime cutscenes. I will never support this as if you already gave him a voice just have him voice game. Finally, the last issue I had with the game is it was a bit too easy especially Part two where I was an unstoppable war machine that crushed all that stand in its way. This more towards veterans of the fire emblem series if this is your first one disregard this criticism. However, if you’re a series veteran this will be one of the easiest fire emblems a series known for its crushing difficulty or as every game journalist will say the DARK SOULS of tactical strategy.

In conclusion, Fire Emblem Three Houses is my game of the year. Minor issues aside it has a great story, characters, and gameplay. Making it absolutely game of the year and a reason to buy a Switch. Those disappointed with the lack of a Persona 5 port on switch look no further than Three Houses which masterfully adapted a lot of the mechanics into the game flawlessly. Fire Emblem Three Houses is worth a buy, four routes new game plus you can easily drop a 100 hours. My first playthrough was 60 hours and after beating the game I immediately wanted to start a second playthrough as Blue Lions on New Game Plus. It's been a while since I wanted to replay a game immediately after just finishing it. Nintendo hit it out of the park this year after a lackluster last year with this game and Astral Chain. I cannot sing these games praise enough.

They did it, the mad lads at CD Projekt Red actually did it. They got the Witcher 3 on the Switch. It sure isn’t the prettiest  but it’s the Witcher on the go. Finally, I can kill monsters and experience one of the best game of this generation from my toilet seat. I see this as an absolute win.

Call of Duty has returned to us with a Modern Warfare reboot a series that fans wanted a return to since the dark ages of the futurist Call of Duty. First thing's first, I didn't buy the game on Amazon I bought it in the Playstation Store for the Preload feature and the preorder bonuses. So, Call of Duty has returned to Modern Warfare does it launch a renaissance of the franchise that returns it to its glory days where Call of Duty was the Fortnite of the era? Or does it end up being just another Call of Duty game? Well, the answer is no nothing will beat Fortnite except Minecraft. But does that mean Call of Duty Modern Warfare is a bad game? No.

I have to give Infinity War credit where credit is due they returned to Modern Warfare a series that the Call of Duty Community has wanted to return and they did it in a new direction but they did it. Now that I give them all due respect let me rip them to shreds. Be extremely cautious with Call of Duty games as they can either get better or worse. It can either be like Call of Duty WW2 where the game got better as time went on and it listens to the fans or it can either be a Black Ops 4 disaster where the game is decent at launch and they screw it all up to focus on a Battle Royale mode, ignored all the fans, and milking consumers for every penny $1 reticles everyone. Modern Warfare looks to be a step in the right direction with no loot boxes and free maps but I wouldn’t put it past them to backdoor this crap after everyone bought the game. As someone whose played pretty much every mainline Call of Duty game minus the very first one I pretty much know the series like the back of my hand and I know all the dirty tricks they pull with the series so before getting into the actual game there’s the disclaimer that I have to put in most games now being a “live service” is its all subject to change. I won’t update the score it would be rather moot to change a score of an old review the game was good and is bad so this is just the disclaimer and if you won’t risk it don’t get Modern Warfare. Now the game itself has the three signature pillars of Call of Duty Campaign, Multiplayer and Co-Op. Now the game itself has three main modes Campaign, Multiplayer, and Co-Op

The campaign, taking place in “Not Syria” a fictional country that the Russians have been occupying for 20 years. You have an evil Russian General who commits war crimes openly and freely from executing civilians to chemical warfare. The Geneva Convention need not imply this campaign. Where you play as three main characters from the SAS, CIA, and a freedom fighter. Modern Warfare fans will see familiar faces throughout the campaign who haven gotten the reboot treatment with the big one being Captain Price returning. The campaign was fun and a pleasant surprise. I haven’t had fun with a Call of Duty campaign since Black Ops 2 and Modern Warfare while being over the top and hyperbolic as possible with some scenes genuinely surprised me that they show war crimes. While this has gaming journalist shaking it’s not that bad if you’ve seen a Modern combat Hollywood film in the past decade. Veteran mode is the way it’s meant to be played otherwise you see the dumb enemy AI and next thing you know you’ve taken out the entire Russian Army with a cinder block running circles around them, while they shrug and say must have been the wind. Yes, Modern Warfare is the spiritual successor to Skyrim. While not as good as the original Modern Warfare Trilogy, Modern Warfare is not bad I would like to see more they set up the story to be continued so hopefully we get more updates that we won’t but we are getting a Modern Warfare 2 again as this game sold well. Spec Ops was set to have “campaign lore” but its barebones and has no story.

Multiplayer, what every Call of Duty player cares about while the campaign has its fans it's a one and done affair. Now the game takes a new direction with the Multiplayer as it plays a lot like Battlefield in many ways. Which has angered a lot of people who returned to this game expecting Modern Warfare 2? The Multiplayer reminds me a lot like Ghost where the maps are big for Call of Duty Standards. Which makes it a campers paradise running and gunning is a death sentence as it’s not viable due to the size of most of the maps and the campers who lurk in most of the buildings. The core gameplay is great everything has been revamped, a new engine has finally graced call of duty the game looks so photorealistic at times playing it with a 4K HDR display I did double-takes to admire the scenery the best looking Call of Duty game all the staple 60 frames. Most of the modes return with two new standouts that are fun and addicting Gunfight and Ground War. The gunfight is a tense 2v2 multiple rounds that reminded me of RS6 Siege which is a good thing. Ground War the large scale 32v32 this where the Battlefield comparisons come in but it’s still the Call of Duty gameplay just bigger, the main problem is the lack of maps with only two so far. Which perfectly illustrates the biggest issue with Modern Warfare’s multiplayer. The maps suck. Another new Call of Duty another botch set of forgettable maps hell all of Black Ops 4 maps were recycled from older COD games. The meta is always going to change as the game gets older. Right now, I don’t have an issue with it campers and grenade spam is annoying but rather nostalgic for Call of Duty veterans who dealt with this back in the original modern warfare. It does something new with the Call of Duty formula which has gotten backlash from purists who wanted a pure return of Modern Warfare. Ok, Boomer. The original Modern Warfare trilogy is easily playable of course they’re not going to make the same game with a fresh coat of paint. Call of Duty is a franchise that can’t win regardless they either change too much and people get mad or they play it too safe and people get mad. At this point you know if you like Call of Duty or not.

Spec-Ops, it’s horde mode with no Zombies thank God I was sick of the Zombies. However, this is a basic horde mode that fits the bare minimum. I don’t have friends so this game mode wasn’t as fun.

In conclusion, Call of Duty Modern Warfare is a well-done reboot. It’s not the best Call of Duty but it’s far from the series’ worse. The ball is now in Activation’s court are they going to continue this momentum. Provide free maps and keep the game supply drop free or are they going to execute order 66 and backdoor all the egregious monetization as they did with Black Ops 4. Well, it’s Activation so the bar isn’t exactly high. They already shot themselves in the foot with the spec-ops mode being a year exclusive on Playstation. Even though I have the game on Playstation this is a multiplatform game with cross-play it shouldn’t have platform-exclusive content. Despite that, Modern Warfare was a step in the right direction and with the right leadership, this game can age like wine if they listen to the community and give them what they want. It’s not that hard but never underestimate these companies to miss open goals like this. I very cautiously recommend Modern Warfare as it gives the fans what they want and appears to be a gesture of goodwill. The only question now is can Call of Duty Modern Warfare keep the goodwill going? Finger’s Crossed.

Hello There, seven years ago a great disturbance in the force happened millions cried out in agony as Disney bought Lucasfilms for 4.05 billion dollars. Changing the franchise forever since then it’s been a dark time for Star Wars. The new movies have been mediocre minus Rogue One and the games have been a disaster with the Battlefront reboot being a tragedy. Although to be fair they did turn around Battlefront 2 from the loot box third impact that was its launch. Needless to say, Star Wars has seen better days under George Lucas then it has with Disney so far, but we have the game-changer in the making first The Mandalorian show, The return of Clone Wars, and finally Fallen Order a single-player Star Wars game by EA the same company that back in 2017 declared the death of Single Player and pledged to make nothing but live service games. Through some type of sorcery we have Fallen Order a single-player, story-driven Star Wars game from EA and it’s good.

Graphics are good it is the free space for most modern games unless you’re Fallout 76. The game is also well optimized on PC with this being EA’s return to Steam after leaving the Platform to launch Origin it’s still needed to run the game but being back on Steam is great. Which compared to the console versions is experiencing some technical difficulties. The environments are rendered well and it can push some of the high-end PCs to the limit.

The story, taking place after Episode 3 and before Episode 4 you play as Cal Kestis a survivor of Order 66. After being outed as a Jedi, by the inquisitors, Cal must escape and must fight the empire and fight for his fallen order. Stormtroopers hit things and the inquisitors are on the hunt, find familiar faces from the Clone Wars, Rebels, and the movies. In a surprising well-written canon story with a male lead, the force is not female with this one. The voice acting and performances are well done the graphics of the game capture the uncanny valley. They got the guy who plays The Joker on Gotham to be a Jedi another Joker playing a Jedi with Mark Hamill being the original. The game is also very long with my first playthrough taking 15 hours to complete by doing the main game and some exploring for upgrades. It’s a long game so it’s not 4 hours no refunds kid experience which given this is EA is surprising. A great story that found the perfect balance of a personal story the story of Cal and the grand scale the rebellion. The first good EA Star Wars story beating Battlefront 2’s dreadful campaign which all I remember was Han Solo had an awful beard and Luke was Luke and not some hermit who had crippling depression.

Gameplay, the game takes the Jedi Academy gameplay of actually having to parry and counter with your lightsaber rather than button mashing it like in the new battlefront games. The game is like a mash-up of the new God of War reboot and Dark Souls. What does being the DARK SOULS of Stars Wars games mean? The game is more forgiving than a Dark Souls and the game has a baby mode, I mean story mode that people can use if they just want to experience the story. I played it in Jedi Master the second-highest difficulty and it was alright to get through there were parts where the game handed me my ass cheeks on a silver platter because I would mess up a block, I didn’t dodge in time, or underestimated the Storm Troopers that swarmed me. Yes, Jedi Fallen Order has competent Storm Troopers a complete disregard of the canon. All joking aside, minus a few parts the game wasn’t the hardest GAME ever! As the story went on and you got more powerful with your abilities and went through the hero’s journey of being the virgin padawan to the Chad Jedi Knight all that rewarding. You can’t beat the feeling of going back to a beginning planet where the optional boss spider turned you inside out and coming back stronger and giving the spider a reckoning. The game is not only lightsaber fights and force magic there is also a fair bit of exploring. Giving me the feeling of playing God of War, as it has that same Metroidvania design. Of having linear levels coming back to access the previously blocked parts when you have new abilities and going off the beaten path to look for upgrades or cosmetics for Cal, BB1, and your ship. Going back to the difficulty the game is comparable to God of War’s higher difficulty levels. Where I beat the game in the second-highest difficult in a challenging but fairway. But getting curb stomped literally by the Valkyries in the end game. Fallen Order’s gameplay stole the show. They could have gone easily for the mass market button-mashing lightsabers still would've sold well but they went out of there way to give players a challenge. Are you sure this is an EA game? Well, it does have its problems.

Customization, mostly for Cal’s outfits you unlock different colored ponchos that look pretty lame compared to his default outfit. I would have loved to have seen a bunch of outfits from the expanded Star Wars universe but Disney probably won’t allow it because they hate fun which leads me to the biggest problem that I experienced with the game.

No dismemberments, it got annoying seeing you mow down stormtroopers in a satisfying matter only to have some annoying red line like you drew on them with marks. I don’t want the game to be gory and violent either they had dismemberments in the prequels I remember seeing Mace Windu beheaded Jango Fett as a kid it was bloodless and clean. The older Star Wars games had it I remember playing them as a kid and I turned out fine being a high functioning member of society. It’s not even consistent either you can dismember the animals and monsters in the game but you can’t the Storm Troopers. While this is mainly a nitpick it ended being such a pet peeve throughout the entire experience. We were this close to achieving greatness. I guess I should mention technical difficulties and long load screens that console users have been experiencing but I haven’t experienced any of those issues on my PC playthrough. Fallen Order has a well-optimized PC Port and the consoles get the short end of the stick in a reversal of roles.

In conclusion, Jedi Fallen Order is the best EA Star Wars game has put out. Definitely on the top of the Star Wars games list. Kotor is still the greatest Star Wars game ever made until they remake it. Star Wars is turning a new leaf we have a great game a great television show out with the Mandalorian. We have the ending to the god awful Disney Trilogy coming soon and we have the second coming of Christ with the Kenobi Series. The times are a-changing for Star Wars and it looks like a New Hope is on the horizon for the franchise to course-correct after being lukewarm for all these years. I give Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order 9 baby Yoda's out of 10. A surprise, to be sure, but a welcome one.

Pokemon Sword and Shield is the latest Pokemon game and in a series first the main game comes to a mainline Nintendo console and it’s the controversial Pokemon game to date. Where the Pokemon community is furiously divided between two camps of those who just want more Pokemon and those who feel Gamefreak has rested on their laurels with the franchise. Has the Pokemon franchise seen better days? Is the fan reaction justified? More importantly, is Sword and Shield even good? The answers are Yes and kinda. Long story short Pokemon Sword and Shield are yet another regression in the franchise but its not at all the worst game in the franchise that’s Let’s Go Pikachu and Eevee those games were hot garbage. How do Sword and Shield stack up, in the world’s most profitable franchise that even beats Disney until Disney buys Pokemon? I’m joking... (or am I?)

Let’s start with what the game did right as it’s not a complete fumble first the new Pokemon are well done nice fits the region ok Galar the United Kingdom of the Pokemon universe. The Legendaries are the best new Pokemon. Regional variations return but they mostly suck minus FarFetch. The characters are good I liked the characters throughout the main story. While the story sucked and believe me we will get to it later. The characters were memorable they have character development and arcs. The main rival Hop nearly defeated me in the final endgame battle with me barely managed to win with my final pokemon. A surprise to be sure but a welcomed one there hasn’t been a decent rival since Pokemon Red and Blue. Finally, the main battling system the rock vs scissors gameplay is still good. Yes, it’s the same core gameplay from 1996 when the game first came out. However, if it ain’t broke don’t fix it. The main series gameplay is still fun to play assembling and watching your team grow throughout your journey. Getting my Axew in a raid. Evolving him to the powerhouse Haxorus and go on to dominate most battles minus the fairy Pokemon. Few games give you that progression from going to rookie to champion and while Pokemon S&S is not the hardest Pokemon game at all. It’s still more difficult than the previous generations 6&7 by a mile. Some of the final battles towards the end got me by surprise specifically the Champion and final rival battle. While Pokemon S&S did stuff right it also dropped the ball in a lot of things.

Graphics, they’re not good. Pokemon’s mainline game makes it to HD for the first time and the debut results are not good. The game reuses 3Ds models and you can tell when the trees a meme is forming comparing the trees of S&S to Ocarina of Time. The funny part is there are trees in the game that look nice the town with the fairy Pokemon gym looks good. It shows game freak rushed things or are holding back the real versions of the game for the Ultra releases. These Graphics suck you don’t have to make it photorealistic and top end but you can at least get the Wild Area the “open world” area to run at a locked 30 playing the area while connected to the internet is a slide show. The animation these are allegedly brand new animations and were the reason why 60% of the Pokedex was Thanos snapped out of the game. I can tell you these animations are not new and are not good it's the same animations and Gamefreak lied. Not using the potential of the switch which can run games Doom and the Witcher 3 and you’re telling me we can’t get better graphics and framerate?

Dexit, they got rid of over half the Pokemon in this game they tell us it was quality over quantity but that was a lie. We did not get a graphical boost so big that it warranted most of the Pokemon getting removed. In a pokemon first they made it so you cannot transfer any Pokemon from the previous generation. Why? Because it was a clear rush they can lie all they want about how they refine everything to make everything a masterpiece but it’s fake news. Speaking of stuff they removed a lot of stuff from the previous generations of pokemon. Megas gone, Z moves gone, but it’s alright you have Gigamax pokemon now your Pokemon can turn to giants that’s the gimmick of this generation that will be in the generation 4 remakes and will almost certainly be dropped in the 9th gen. I remember when Black and White 2 gave you everything plus the kitchen sink they did not skip a feature. Now we are three new generations in new hardware and we get less than what we got before. Few franchises can get away with this but Pokemon is one them they’re the Madden of Nintendo games. It still gets worse.

The story, while I like the characters and they’re own subplots the story did not do them any favors. For one it’s short 7 hours give or take as it pretty much gym hopping non-stop with the main grunts being soccer hooligans for one of your rivals. The main bad guy’s reasoning for doing what he did was comical I thought it was satire. SPOILERS (skip this paragraph) if you don’t care about spoiler the “plot” is. The region is going to run out of energy in a thousand years and if you don’t summon the legendary Pokemon and start the apocalypse we will all die in thousands of years. What? I know these games are primarily geared towards children but this is just plain stupid. So you stop Pokemon Trainer Greta Thunberg and that's it. There's nothing else to say I know the last game was just cutscenes everywhere and it annoyed everyone but this they didn’t even try they just gym hopping to the stadiums and coming out in footie uniform on the telly. Also, the time has come. It's time to give pokemon voice acting. Seeing dull animations that are not even expressive Voice Acting would have helped, well good voice acting. Seeing text while it’s nostalgic the franchise has to evolve which transitions to my final point.

Stagnation, the Pokemon games are stuck in the 1990s. You know I know it. The fact is it's the current year and Gamefreak hasn’t caught up with the times despite being on modern hardware and living in the age of the internet, they still have the antiqued models. Game Freak can patch all the Pokemon in a massive update adding back the national dex they won’t because they’re boomers who will probably release Ultra Sword and Ultra Shield with the national dex.
