Phoenix Wright - Ace Attorney is a great game. As a legal, mystery buff, this game appealed to me very much. Another major bonus is that it's anime (which I love). It's an entertaining,humorous and charming click and point game with plenty of reading. If reading puts you off, then do not buy this game. I repeat: do NOT buy this game. 90% of it requires reading. I, for one, loved it. I love games that require deduction and putting on your thinking cap. I love solving mysteries and cases. It's part of the reason why I love shows like Boston Legal, The Practice, Law and Order. Some people have complained that there's little gameplay and it's true - but at its heart, Phoenix Wright's gameplay is all about investigating the truth through cross-examination and listening to testimonies. You can also look for clues at a crime scene and interview key witnesses. My chest swells with (a small) victory every time I get it right.

You're thrust into the role of Phoenix Wright. He's a young and budding lawyer fresh out of law school who works for Fey & Co law firm. The first case starts off with your buddy being accused of murder. Since it's Phoenix's first case, he is guided by the beautiful Mia Fey (chief) to navigate you through the jungle of legal tricks and fundamentals. The bevy of characters is an eclectic, zany bunch. I smiled in amusement at the jokes and clever dialogue. I loved how Phoenix gets tongue-tied around pretty ladies.

There are a total of five cases. Each case is episodic since there is a continuity to the story. At the beginning of every case, you are presented with an introduction of the murder scene. While the first case was fairly easy, the ensuing cases were complex. Trust me, I sat there dumbfounded while scrolling through the evidence frantically. "What would Bobby Donnell or Alan Shore do??" Don't let the simple mechanics of the game fool you, sometimes it gets quite challenging.

This game is well-suited for the DS's and 3DS's dual screen. (I have a 3DS.) The top screen is for the animation and text, while the bottom touch screen is where you engage with it. Aside from touching the screen in order to read the following text, you can also choose an answer in the form of a multiple choice (location and so forth) and check out Court Records. The Court Records hold the evidence you've collected. Each evidence (picture) is accompanied by a brief description (can't tell you how many times I've re-read 'em).

During trial, and specifically during a witness's testimony, you must find contradictions in their statements. You must discredit them in order to acquit your client. So you get the option of either asking the witness (and I must say, what a SKETCHY, SHIFTY-EYED BUNCH!) to explain what they meant by a particular statement or presenting the court with evidence. You are allowed to read/replay the testimony as many times without being penalized by the judge. And trust me, you'll find yourself re-reading their statements until it's practically committed to memory. You only get penalized when you present the court with irrelevant/inaccurate evidence.

There's not much of an audio in terms of a dialogue except for hollering "OBJECTION," "HOLD IT," and "TAKE THAT!" In spite of this, the music made up for it. It was suitable and changed tempo every time there was a new development.

All in all, I enjoyed this game. This was my first game in this series and I have consequently bought the rest. If you have a DS or 3DS, pick up this game. I know that there's an influx of point and click game apps for a cheaper price tag, but this game is wonderfully-constructed. Recommended. Can't wait for Professor Layton vs Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney coming this August. I hope my review helped in your purchasing-decision.

After Playing Gone Home and loving it, I wanted to play more of the same type of game. My friend, Google, directed me to To the Moon. Granted, I did have my reservations. I wasn't keen on the pixelated graphics and I didn't think anything could be as exquisitely developed as Gone Home. WRONG. WRONG. WRONG. It goes to show never to judge a game by its graphics. To the Moon is a heart-rending, emotionally-charged,mesmerizing and UNFORGETTABLE game. It's like reading a beautiful novel. The characters came to life because I found myself caring about them. It's almost like I knew them. It stayed with me long after I finished it (and I was sad to see it end). I kept on thinking about Johnny and River and had to remind myself that they're fictitious characters.

The writing is top-notch. The dialogue is real. I loved the witty banter between Dr. Watts and Dr. Rosalene. Dr Watts's comments are hilarious. I found myself laughing out loud. There's a lot of humor in this bittersweet story.

The music is beautifully haunting. Evocative and melancholic. The soundtrack is what stirred my emotions. I swear, there were times when I deliberately stopped doing anything and just closed my eyes and enjoyed the sounds of the piano. I loved every moment of this game. I'm absolutely staggered by the storytelling. Staggered! The story is told backwards and I can't see it done any other way. If you want excellent storytelling and a tender love story, please, please play this game. There's little gameplay because the game is very story-focused, and what a story! It's the story of Johnny, an old man on his deathbed. His dying wish is to go to the moon, so he signs up for Sigmund Corp where Dr. Rosalene and Dr Watts recreate his memories. The game takes you from one memory link to the next through a timeline - and that's where the rich, multi-layered story unfolds.

It's essentially a point and click game. Aside from moving from point A to point B, you collect memory links (which is very easy) and then create a memento in the form of a picture. You must flip square tiles in order to create them. It's fairly easy, too. So basically, that's the gameplay element. As I've previously stated, there's very little gameplay. Even if you've never played any type of game in your life, you'll still be able to play this game with ease. It's very simple. To the Moon is a visual novel - where the story is front and center and gaming takes a backseat.

At some point during my playthrough, my seven year old nephew saw me playing and stayed to watch me. At first, I figured he'd get bored because there's a lot of textual reading (and he's averse to reading), but I was surprised to see him engrossed in the story. He begged me not to continue playing without him and wanted to see how it ended. So in other words, this game will draw you in and never let go until the end credits... Keep tissues nearby because I guarantee that your eyes will prick with tears.

Whether you're a gamer or not, please play this game. The last time my emotions were acutely heightened by a game was when I played The Walking Dead by Telltale Games. I downloaded To the Moon from Steam and it was worth every dollar! Like a good book, I'll want to re-experience this unforgettable tale. I'm pretty jaded when it comes to love, but this tale reignited the romantic in me. Please play it - it'll leave a lasting impression on you - guaranteed!

Ghost Trick is an immensely fun game. I found myself having a hard time putting it down. You play the role of a ghost. You've just died *no spoilers* and have no idea who you are and why you were murdered (at a junkyard, no less). So you set off to solving the mystery of your death (with the guide of a desk lamp - I'm not kidding). Along the way, you save potential victims via Powers of the Dead. Not everyone possesses these powers, but you certainly do. While you can save others, you can't use your powers to save yourself (bummer - at least long enough to trim the cone-inspired hair 'do).

You can rewind four minutes prior to the victim's demise and find a way to alter their fate. You do so by possessing and manipulating inanimate objects. There's an hourglass and you must save the victim before time runs out. Honestly, I don't find myself enjoying a game if I must perform under a time-constraint (that's just me). But the game is forgiving in a way that lets you rewind time at any given time (without being penalized).

This game reminds me a lot of Tiny Thief and Limbo in terms of manipulating your environment. So if you liked those games, you'll like Ghost Trick.

The first chapter serves as a tutorial. At first, I was a bit overwhelmed (especially when I had to get used to the idea of being dead AND save a beautiful red-head from being murdered *no spoilers*), but by the end of the first chapter, I found the mechanics to be intuitive and a total breeze.

I bought this game while not knowing that it was produced by the same Phoenix Wright series' creators. The animation, colorful characters (I absolutely loved the heroic Pomeranian) and clever dialogue that I loved in the PW series translates quite seamlessly in Ghost Trick. While I loved PW in its entirety, I think Ghost Trick would appeal to people who didn't enjoy PW because it has a bit more gameplay. Granted, there's a lot of reading, but not quite as much as PW, in my humble opinion.

This is a trial and error type of game. You keep trying different solutions and techniques until you find the one that works. I recall trying different tactics over 8 times until I gave up and consulted a guide. I was a bit peeved because I performed that technique, but not in the same sequence. So the game's TOO linear. That said, don't let it put you off from buying it, because it is very fun and addicting.

The highly-anticipated second season of The Walking Dead kicks off with our intrepid heroine Clem who is joined by Christa and Omid. When the end credits rolled for Season 1, I thought to myself, "How the heck will Clem manage without Lee? And more importantly, how will a small girl defend herself against the undead?" I was eager to know how Telltales will make it work. And they did - with flying colors.

(no spoilers) In this season, in addition to fighting the undead, she must learn to outsmart raving lunatics, AKA humans. Who woulda thunk it that the surviving psychos would decide to showcase their lunacy during the apocalypse? This season's storyline is relentlessly tense, gripping, and one hella of a ride! In order to survive the onslaught of zombie attacks, Clem uses evasion and defense moves such as scampering away, dodging, or picking up anything from her environment and using it as a weapon. Her small build comes in handy since she can crawl through tight spaces.

Every time I played the Walking Dead, I was filled with melancholy at Clem's grim situation. My heart went out to Clem every time she gazed at anyone with her sad, amber eyes. Clem has certainly mentally and emotionally grown since last season. It is evident via her mannerism and her choice of words. Among the adults, she's a very keen listener, while some of the adults regard her as a nuisance. She's become a wee bit hardened - but who wouldn't in her situation?

If you loved the first season, then you'll certainly love this one. If you haven't played the first season, then what are you waiting for?

If you haven't played any game by Telltale yet, then you're in for a real treat. Following the colossal success of The Walking Dead, Telltale Games based their follow-up, five-episodic game based on the comic series: Fables the wolf among us by Bill Willingham. It is reminiscent of The Walking Dead in terms of the mechanics and a gritty, compelling storyline and each episode ends with a cliffhanger.

I absolutely loved The Walking Dead. Its explosive finale left me in a somber mood and tears streaking down my face (damn you Telltale Games), so I wondered what this game would do to me. This game had my brain totally scrambled. I drew up a list of suspects and asked myself What Would Nancy Drew Do? While I didn't exactly cover myself in innards and slay zombies, I had to chase bad guys and get badly beaten up.

Who doesn't like fables and fairy tales? Snow White, The Little Mermaid, Little Red Riding Hood, Beauty and the Beast to name a few. Better yet, who doesn't like a fairy tale story with a dark twist? A murder mystery. The Wolf Among Us is a noirish, gritty crime story. You play as the (Sherriff Bigby) Big Bad Wolf (whom I must admit, developed a crush on - maybe it's his deep, gravelly voice or the way he dotes on Snow White *sigh*) in Fabletown which is set in New York City. Someone is offing the fairy tale characters and it's your job to find the perp. The problem is that everyone fears and/or hates you, so it makes your job a smidgen difficult.

As a mystery lover, I lapped this up like it was the finest thing since sliced bread. You get to question and interrogate (and, yeah, well torture) the fine and not-so-fine citizens of Fabletown. Each character is mysterious and harbors a well of secrets. The mystery is very well-crafted. There's more to it than what meets the eye.

Once you are introduced to a character and/or object, the game presents you with a backstory which you have the option to view in the Book of Fables. I loved the backstories of each of the characters, since it added depth to the game.
As much as I loved this game, it wasn't as emotionally-charged as The Walking Dead. That said, it's a great game in its own right. If you enjoyed The Walking Dead, then look no further than this game. It's a violent game (lots of brawls) and there's some nudity (topless scenes). This game is geared strictly towards adults. The voice acting is top-notch. Some of the actors that lent their voices in the Walking Dead like Dave Fennoy, Melissa Hutchinson, and Erin Ashe are lending their voices in The Wolf Among Us ( I was surprised to learn that some of the actors lent their voices to more than one character! What a talented bunch!) The dialogue is interesting, and the gameplay is simple yet highly entertaining. I highly recommend this story-driven, entertaining game. Kudos to Telltale Games for producing another winning title under their belt.

I'm not in the habit of replaying the same game on another device, but this game was so memorable, melancholic and beautifully-executed, I had to make it part of my Vita library. Oh, yeah, and if you're a trophy hunter, then you'll be delighted to know that the platinum is very easy to obtain.

I'm a fan of LBP. I played the first and second part, including the PS Vita version (not all of it, truth be told). When this game was unveiled at E3, I was stoked, even though I knew that Media Molecule weren't partaking in the project.

Okay, the pros: I loved the introduction of the new characters. They're cute and added a freshness to the series. The charm and humor are all found here.

Cons: The levels grow increasingly and infuriatingly hard. Enough to put me off from playing. I love a good challenge, but this game is aimed at children and I can't believe the difficulty level. I love platformers such as Mario, Rayman Legends, etc, but this game was too difficult. As an adult, I honestly can't believe it's aimed at children. My seven year old nephew was particularly tearful during a Swoop (bird) level. He begged me to help him. My nephew isn't a newbie when it comes to platformers. He's very good. And for the first time in my life, I see him tearful for not being able to beat it level after several attempts.

One of LBP2's noteworthy features was that it featured a Dive In. A place to meet new players and join them in their pods. I am disappointed that it hasn't been brought back in LBP3.

This game's camera isn't steady, especially when you're playing with another person. I often end up not seeing where I'm going because the camera is jerky.I often get cheap deaths due to it. I haven't had this sort of issue with the previous LBP installments.

This game is also buggy. So buggy, that I found myself floating into nothingness. I actually beat a hard level due to the bugs. After floating into nothingness for several seconds, I found myself at the end of the level. The loading time is very long. On several occasions, I thought that my console froze on me due to its lengthy loading time.

All in all, I'm extremely disappointed and don't recommend this game.

This is the first FPS game I played on the Vita. And this is my first game in the series. I'm aware that this game received ample criticism, but I jumped into the game because opinions are always subjective.

I haven't finished the game yet (I'm on chapter 3), but I've played it enough to get the basic feel of the game.

I like this game. The mechanics are solid and smooth. Resistance Burning Skies is an EXTREMELY linear game. So linear, that in one playthrough, you can find all the Grey Tech cubes (a form of an upgrade for your weapons). So if you hate linear games, then this game is not for you. Open-world maps aren't my cup of tea because I'm ashamed to admit that I get lost. If I'm playing Borderlands (which I LOVE), I play it with a friend because I'm map-illiterate. LOL.

I understand and applaud how the developers incorporated the touchscreen of the Vita into its gameplay. However, in the heat of a battle (like another reviewer said), I don't like the idea of removing my fingers and swiping the screen. It makes me uneasy. I'm the mash-em-type of gal, so this feature didn't appeal to me much.

Tom Riley is a firefighter and you can use his ax in order to melee the enemies. As far as I can tell, you can only melee by touching the ax icon on the screen and it can only be done once (and not in rapid succession). This, too, didn't appeal to me much. I like to melee to my heart's content by mashing on a button and not touching the touchscreen.

There are eight weapons and each weapon has a secondary fire. Each secondary weapon requires touching the screen. So far I have 5 (I think) of the weapons and they're pretty decent with good gun power. My favorite so far are the Auger and Carbine.

After perusing the list of trophies, this game seems to be an easy platinum. So if you're a trophy hunter and want a solid, short FPS shooter on the Vita (something you can do while commuting, etc) then this game is for you. As I previously said, I haven't played the Resistance game on the PS3, so I dunno how it compares to it. But to compare a handheld game to a console version is unfair in my opinion. If you decide to buy this game, I hope you enjoy it.

MASS EFFECT 2 vs MASS EFFECT 1

Bioware hasn't made a cutting-edge-technology game until now. ME1's graphics looked sexy in conversation-mode, but got a bit chunky in action-mode, and bizarrely pop-in-y in cutscene-mode. All of those tech-engine problems have been solved. They've been spanked like a naughty librarian. Like, if ME1 was Kate Beckinsale in Uncovered, then ME2 is like Kate Beckinsale in Underworld. If you rank graphics by sexiness per game-hour, Mass Effect 2 could give Uncharted 2 a run for its money. It's the most attractive Bioware game ever. This totally changes my outlook on the future. If Bioware can step up and make such a fantastic looking, smooth-playing bio-rpg in 2010, then I no longer think the world will end in 2012, and I'm going to stop nagging my hot wife about her carbon footprints (hottie can get a little dirty). Mass Effect 2 makes anything possible.

ME2 vs MODERN WARFARE vs HALO vs GEARS OF WAR

Mass Effect is a first-person shooter because they want shooter money. MW2 sold like 20 million copies. Halo 3 sold like 11 million copies. Gears of War both sold like 6 million copies each. Mass Effect 1 sold like 2 million copies. And its fps controls were suspect. ME2's controls feel fantastically better than ME1, they feel like AAA fps controls. ME2 has much better story than the comp. BUT. 1. No real multiplayer. 2. No constant action. Bioware makes Story-RPGs. (This is a beautiful thing.) A 35 hour game, I would guess, has 25 hours of interactive conversation and cutscenes, and 10 hours of shoot-shoot bang-bang. Mass Effect 2 has 4-star shoot-shoot experiences--inside a 5-star choose your own sci-fi adventure story. If you know Bioware, you know this. If you don't know Bioware, learn what they are, and what they are not. Mass Effect 2 is all about STORY.

I play all three types, warrior, tech, superpowers. I play all three ways, good, naughty, wild card. I play male and female, and go though all the "romances." And I play all the side quests. Even if you layer that action, it's a 120 hour + game. That's fantastic entertainment at 99 cents per two-hour session. That's as good a deal, per hour, as getting blu-rays from an online mail-it-to-me company. That's like 12 novels long. Like 5 complete seasons of TV. Bioware's the only developer on the planet that makes this kind of beautiful uniqueness. This kind of awesomeness only comes around once every few years. Is this flavor of hot awesomeness perfect? No. Is amateur pornography perfect? No. Sometimes the pacing is off, or the dialogue excessive. But it more than gets the job done. The job is to delight. To experience a genuine human story--even if you're a lesbian space thief. Mass Effect 2 is classic VG storytelling. And better written than 99% of sci-fi novels, tvs, and movies.

7 - The hero leads his party in their final mission to position them for the ultimate war.

8 - The hero leads his party to victory against the endless enemy hoards and defeats the ultimate villain.

Dragon Age 2 includes only sequences 1, 3 & 4. The unreliable narrator, in this case, is a cheap device, made of short cut scenes, used to patch over the missing story holes.

Since having only three sequences would make the game too short, Bioware pumped up sequence 1 with an extra 16 hours of random side quests, most of which recycle the same generic dungeons over and over. This was done to reduce development costs.

The game ends immediately after sequence 4, with a 30-second endgame cutscene that basically says, please look forward to a new hero and a new world in Dragon Age 3.

So, knowing all that up front, Dragon Age 2 is still, for me, a 5-Star RPG Experience. Of the top 200 bestselling PS3 games of all time, only 6 are RPGs. I like Oblivion. I dislike Fallout 3, Fallout NV, FFXIII, and Demon's Souls. And I love Dragon Age: Origins.

Dragon Age 2, it turns out, I love even more than DA:O. The graphics, while weak, are better than the previous. The new art design fits the world perfect. The combat is faster, equally tactical, and casting spells feels 400% more powerful. And sequence 3, with the big brooding horny guys, is one of the most intensely awesome Bioware experiences I've ever played. Indeed, sequence 3 alone, allows me to forgive all of the game's flaws.

My only other regrets are... They should have brought back Morrigan 2.0 instead of Flemmeth 2.0, and given her a bigger role. They should have made the end cut scene longer, with artistic depictions of the fates of the companions and chosen love interest. They should have made the character model of Aveline a hottie instead of an ugly. And they should have allowed the freedom to have naked threesomes.

But it's like they say... 50% of a Bioware game is better than 10 Square-Enix games.

Rhythm Thief is a very cool game. Even if you are not a fan of anime art style you should enjoy the rhythm games that the storyline uncovers through gameplay. The game does not consist of only rhythm tapping and swiping games, but a lot of conversations and collecting of stuff in between. This can be good or bad depending on the type of player you are. Basically, the main character Raphael runs around Paris with his dog to uncover a terrible secret and an evil conspiracy on the way. (this premise is introduced in the trailers. Not spoiler) While music and rhythm games are the main element there is much traversing of the streets and areas to find various characters for information or items. You are also tasked with finding sounds, and landmarks. What this means is every time you arrive to a new location you'll see a detailed background. You have to click around it to find a prize, which is converted to coins. Coins can later be turned in to unlock extra content within the game.

In fact a lot of the art and the clicking is very similar to art of Professor Layton games. But do not confuse the two in gameplay. There are no difficult puzzles to solve in this one. I'd even say a lot of the filler content between the rhythm games is very easy and can be an annoyance. It could take awhile after a main rhythm game until you reach the next one. This will probably be fun for kids, but for adult gamers could be a distraction since there is no meaningful reward for the game itself.

The rhythm games are clever and inventive. They do not simply have to do with dancing on the street for the NPCs to watch, but escaping, running, fighting, playing instruments, and anything you can think of. The developers made a smart move by allowing free access to each rhythm game found within the game in a separate menu so you can try to get perfect scores as much as you like. One game I've found required using the gyroscope to catch things. That actually did not work too well because the gyroscope lags and can't catch up to the game easily, but that game is an exception and is a side mission.

Most of the art in the game is relatively traditional looking anime for kids. Not what people may associate with "bright spiky hair", maybe more tame, kid friendly anime art. I'd say it resembles such cartoons like Astro Boy, in which many characters are caricatures. Some of the art and dialogue may be too cutesy and irrelevant. But behind that is a solid game.

OPINION ON REVIEWING:
If you are looking at the review section of Diablo III on Amazon and wonder why all the negative reviews, and why all the complaining? Is this game actually bad? No, the game is not bad, and many of the reviews are simply from disgruntled people who vote down the product because they do not like how Blizzard uses tough measures against piracy by requiring constant internet connection for playing single player, not just for multiplayer. To be fair there are some long and elaborate negative reviews for Diablo III, which actually review the game, content, and gameplay. Those are ok. Read them if you want a fair opinion. But the majority of the 1 star reviews are simply posted in protest of the publisher developer's practices. If you look at them you can see whether it says "Amazon Verified Purchase" next to the 1 star reviews. Not surprisingly they are not. Thing is there is an active community of players over the world. They congregate in some forums where sometimes they are told and encouraged to go and leave a negative review for some games on sites such as Amazon because you do not have to have purchased the game here to leave a review.

There are also many reviews from the first week of the game's release which are negative because the servers were down. I'd actually say those are legitimate negative reviews because people wanted to play single player and were barred from it over that week's weekend. However if you wanted more fair reviews of the gameplay itself you should check the aggregate reviews of the game from sites like metacritic and gamerankings and look for average score from professional review websites, which is about 85% , not from disgruntled fans. Even if one were to believe that the "professional" review sites were bribed into giving this game higher scores, there is no way it deserves 1 star out of 5, so the rational thing would be just ignore those that are from people who have not purchased the game here on Amazon. Just my opinion.

COMMENTS ABOUT THE GAME:
Now for the game itself. I must say I am very happy with it. Of course it is not the same as Diablo II and by that I do not mean it is worse. You get a bunch of classes to choose from such as Barbarian, Monk, Witch Doctor etc. You get to choose whether it is a male or a female. Not too much customization there. However, each of the characters you pick has their own mini story and dialogue that unravels through the game. You do not get to pick moral decisions like in D&D rpgs, it is just not that. For each of the characters you get a rather diverse skill tree and unique skill modifiers in form of runes. However, none of these skills that you unlock as you play are set permanently. You are allowed to redistribute your abilities to try out for the best combos you want. Biggest focus is on finding and managing the exotic and rare weapons. They may not seem as vital at first because if you've just installed and began to play the game, it may be kind of easy until you go further in. When the enemies get tougher you'll start to pay attention to weapons and that is where the focus of this Diablo installment is. You are also given the ability to "forge" your own weapons" but sometimes it is pointless because you are not able to forget that very rare super weapon anyway. It does help when you cannot find appropriate armor for your level however.

One feature I enjoyed when playing single player is I that the chest and the items you find are carried over to another playthrough if you start another campaign with an entirely different character. The gold you collect is shared as well. It is helpful because it may encourage the player to replay the game with other characters and find use for that one rare item you may have found as a Barbarian but weren't able to use because it was "Wizard Only"

Graphics options give a wide variety of settings. This is nice because looks like Blizzard wanted as many players as possible to be able to play Diablo III without upgrading their rig. My PC can run the game on above average settings, but sometimes I prefer the low graphics, high performance mode simply because I like stable framerate without occasional slow downs.

COMMENTS ON THE COLLECTOR'S EDITION:
I rarely buy collector's editions of games, but a friend recommended I buy it this time. Honestly the package is pretty nice. You get the documentary with the developers talking about game creation. The soundtrack. You get a decorative USB holder that looks like Diablo's skull, and a USB drive shaped like a shard, which contains DIABLO II and and LORD OF DESTRUCTION expansion (No Diablo I) It is strange because it would cost the company nothing to include Diablo I as well. There is a huge album with drawings, but I did not unwrap it. You also get codes for few decorative items for your character for in-game use. It is angel wings and 2 dyes. They seem pretty useless if you ask me.
The USB and the USB stand are nice souvenirs and the box itself which contains the collector's edition is huge. It is literally same size as the white XBOX. For collector's it is a must because the skull souvenir is well made. But I think I'd rather have bought the standard edition.

I've played this game a number of hours now and I can honestly say this is a pretty awesome Resident Evil game. The types of areas including dark alleys, halls, and mysterious fortresses are here.

Whether it is good or bad the game seems to be more action oriented, although it depends what difficulty you play it on. I started off with the hardest difficulty to get a feel what it is like. This is the mode where the game becomes truly "survival horror" as the zombies and monsters are more numerous and require more bullets. I found myself quickly scrambling for hiding areas and vantage points when surrounded by the enemy. Gets adrenaline pumping like before though of course not how it was with the good old RE1 or RE2. But it is not the game's fault. I grew up as a gamer and became desensitized to much horror and violence in games so we cannot really expect same old style thrills.

The game has a decent coop mode for playing with friends and that can really help with high difficulty settings because when your partner is AI you pretty much play on your own because they only cause damage to zombies sometimes, and when they do, it is lower damage than yours. Still my CPU partner managed to finish some zombies.

The one thing about this game that I'd have changed is I would have first made it more paced like RE5, or 3DS RE Revelations. Those games have your character run slower than here. In this one your character can run and sprint faster than you'd like sometimes when there may be zombies just around the corner, and there are many moments like this. Also I would have adjusted the game to maybe have less detailed in graphics but to be more stable as far as frame rate. For example if you played Resident Evil 5 and then Resident Evil 6 you'd have noticed RE5 is smoother, and RE6 is slightly less smooth. Feels like 30 or 32 frames in RE5 and 30-27 frames here.

Also pretty cool feature are random encounters with NPCs which are mostly there to create drama and have little actual effect on you. The scenes are frequently cheesy and over acted, but that is how it was with RE games before. Usually they are not plot related but rather observations by main characters

So overall I think Resident Evil 6 deserves about 4 out of 5 stars because you get pretty consistent and relevant gameplay that is easy to be engrossed in and enjoy. Sometimes you'll be surprised by quick time events (which you simply love or hate), and more darkness throughout the game. Unusual settings where RE franchise didn't go before. Old familiar characters to be played as. Stats and skills to be gained to have your skills upgraded.

Overall it is very nice with some fine running not done well. I recommend this as a BUY. I have an important piece of advice for you if you are undecided whether to get Resident Evil 6, if you are looking for honest opinions look for those reviews with "amazon verified purchase" label next to them. Many of the 1 star reviews are left by trolls who have a vendetta against publisher Capcom and go from site to site leaving zero score reviews.

I am avid gaming enthusiast who played games for over sixteen years. I also worked in the industry of gaming. After having played dozens of modern games on all current gen systems I've began to lean toward classics to give me some gaming diversity and to experience historical gaming.

As you may know Midway as a company does not exist now. They bankrupted sometime in 07 or 08 and the brand was eventually purchased by Warner Brothers who are now the owner and publisher of all Midway games. Until Midway went down Xbox Live had very nice versions of Midway games in digital download form. They were made by Digital Eclipse and were very nice. They always gave a perfectly emulated original game as well as newer and "improved" versions with higher definition art and backgrounds. These versions were taken off XBLA and for some time no one had access to Robotron 2084, Smash TV, Joust, etc etc.

This collection of games is developed for WB by somewhat legendary developer Backbone Entertainment who made collections of Sega games and other retro games before. They are all well emulated versions of original games. They have good screen options and background selections, but the actual games are just identical original games. You do not get options to play any kind of "improved" or HD versions of the classic games. Just a lot of original games.

I have to give this game 4 out of 5 because the original classics are all well done and emulated, have leaderboards, and decent controls. But since there are no improvements of any kind at all such as was done before by Digital Eclipse for XBLA a star has to be taken away.

I had to get it because currently it is the only way to play Midway games on modern consoles.

Battleship for Xbox 360 is not too bad for a film based tie in title. We all know film related games are usually not of the same quality as most games. The game does not really follow any plot from the film, but lets us play some kind of parallel story where you run around the Hawaii Islands with guns and at the same time control the huge American ships that are in the water around the Island. You hide behind a rock and open your interface. There you see the map of the area, your location, the enemy ships, and your ships. You can order your ships to move closer to the enemy to attack them while you shoot aliens in FPS gameplay mode on land.

Battleship XBOX 360 almost pulls it off with this cool concept. Graphics are not too bad. You are treated to visuals of a tropical island and cool alien and earth ships on the water in the ocean. What could be wrong with this?

Simply that the game is not polished and has a lot of bugs. You know how sometimes you want to explore the game area by going to extreme edges of the maps? Well if you do it here, you will find so many invisible walls you'll lose count. When there is supposed to be collision with some rock or cliffs you'll hit an invisible wall because the developers either were lazy, or did not have the time to create proper collision.
The guns are not very balanced. The alien gun and the M16 variant of human weapon just shoot directly. Generally very accurate, but not realistic hit detection like in Call of Duty for example. You are able to aim down iron sights, but still the guns are too perfect they feel like toys.
The enemy AI is rather dumb. They'll often just bunch together and just shoot directly. There is no strategy in them.
There are also rocks and spots in which you can get stuck and would have to restart the level to continue.
The game is also not very hard on Hardest difficulty.

Still it is somewhat fun to play because of the ships strategy. Some cutscenes are cool, alien ships drop off troops very impressively. Achievements are easy and if you collect them they are valuable.

This game is very unique in a good way. Directed by the Japanese director known for "Killer 7" the game clearly shows the somewhat irreverent post-modern style. I would say some levels could even be described as avant-garde. This may be good or bad, depending how you look at games. If you enjoy traditional character types and story where you expect normal dialogue and linear progression this isn't exactly it. The game has very strange and often creepy dialogue, it somewhat objectifies women, (and men) hence my previous description "irreverent".

The game heavily focuses, perhaps as a parody, on cyberpunk style. You and other characters casually have cybernetic limbs and implants and everyone acts casually like they're not there.
At the same time the gameplay is shown in high contrast, dark shadows, environment and is accompanied by 70s acid jazz music . Not exactly to my liking but it plays only in the main menu.
It has an interesting mini game where your character is going on dates with different girls over the world. You have to go on those dates to get new weapons or items actually. So the game is definitely aimed at men.

Gameplay itself feels like a very good button mashing combo pressing fighting game. You unlock moves as you gain crystals. You have to learn the righty timing to get the moves to work. Have to know when to use what melee weapon or item. So the gameplay is very solid. Graphics may not be the best, and in fact they are kind of abstract frequently, but it does not hinder anything. Action looks stylish and exciting. The main character is somewhat relatable male.

It should be mentioned that the game is very violent and you will see some things you would never expect to see in games as far as violence or suggestive sexual content. Whether you like that type of thing or not it makes this game all the more special and worth to check out.

I am about 50hrs in and around chapter 5 and thought it would a good time to just write about my general thoughts of FFXV. (NO SPOILERS) I'll hold back a lot of info so you can discover on your own.

For starters - it's recommended that you first watch King's Glaive prior to playing- just my opinion because i did, and it was awesome to watch how things tied together.

The game is beautiful, the characters. environment - everything is like eye candy and its not just the Cut scenes. The story, the little dialogue between the characters, the subtle jokes on each other really helps getting to know the characters.

Combat is different from any of the usual FF series and it takes a few battles to get used to- in the sense it's not a turn base, you have to rely on running around, blocking, jumping, selecting weapons/magic, warping, teamwork. After 50 hrs, it still feels weird because the camera angle gets blocked by a bush or tree while you are fighting, it's rather annoying when you have to rotate the view mid button mashing and you can't see your enemy to know when to block. But for the most part, the combat is smooth, UNTIL i can't see. But it is fun - taking down something 10x your size, or taking on an army of 18 with backup constantly raining down from the sky. Just don't underestimate the Hunts - i did a few times even though my "level" was higher - they can easily overwhelm your group if you are unprepared.

Leveling/skilling - you gain exp as you would in any FF game, kill things and do quests - but instead of getting the exp instantaneously you tally all EXP you earned when you find a place to rest (camping, motel, hotel). As you gain EXP you gain AP to activate nodes in your ascension tabs, whether it's for giving a new teamwork skill to your teammate, a new skill for Noct, Boosting HP/Strength/Vitality/Mag for the group and plenty more- it cost different amount of AP. (I personally think this part here makes the game too easy in comparison to all of the FF series, it's not as in depth as I would have liked it to be- as there are a small amounts of skill trees and only a few are character specific.. it'll take a while to get the AP to fill it all but i wished it was more in depth)

3 ways to travel: By foot: you basically can run/walk/jump anywhere you looks like you can, Regalia (car): you can travel by any road that's not blocked and with enough gas, Chocobo!: same as if by foot but faster and on steeper terrain.

I am in no rush to complete the game, I am actually enjoying all the side stuff opened after Chapter 3, all the hunts, dog tags, exploring, things for Cindy, taking pictures, doing things for the researcher. Lots to do, and i heard even if i missed a sidequest i can go back and complete it later, so that why I am going to advance a few chapters and see what else opens up.

Final thoughts: Over all i think the game has a lot to offer- very well made, from graphics (excellent) to story (Over all story so far is good but not great). Load time was a little long even on the PS4 Pro, but once it loads, everything is smooth as butter. Game play is great with the exception of the camera view hiccup. I look forward to finishing the game on my own time then starting a new game+ and whatever DLC is coming next.

Great new entry in the Pokemon series. As a long-time fan, it is nice that they are still improving the games with each iteration-- it would be really easy for them to put out a sub-par product and still get sales. I have already put ~120 hours into this game (about 30 or so in the story with oodles of time in the post-game), but even with that time investment I will buy it again for the Nintendo Switch and play through again :P.

Some of the great quality of life improvements over the previous games:

No more HMs
Previously, you had to make room on your Pokemon for story-based moves (and have specific types of Pokemon in your party), but this is no longer the case!

Great story
The story in this game is one of the best in the series, possibly the best (over B/W), though this will probably differ somewhat based on personal taste

UI Improvements
If you ever had to look up type matchups to see if a move was Super Effective/ Not Very Effective, you are in luck: after you have battled a Pokemon, your move effectiveness is always displayed on your moves in the lower screen.

IV Judging all Pokemon in your PC boxes at any PC
This is huge for anyone that breeds Pokemon: after unlocking it, you can see the IVs for any Pokemon in your PC (which streamlines the IV checking process significantly).

EV display in Summary screen
This is a slight step back (as you could normally see this in the bottom screen at any time), but when you press the Y button on a Pokemon Summary it shows you the current EV investment for the Pokemon (with sparkles if a stat is maxed). It is nice having the same UI for the IVs and EVs in the same spot.

Basically, if you have ever liked Pokemon (or just want to try a fun game), try this out. It is totally worth it. If you are thinking of trying another Pokemon game after Pokemon GO, you will not be disappointed-- the actual gameplay here is so much better. Just buy this and a fitbit :P.

This handbrake/shifter is a work of art as far as game controllers go. I'm used to mostly plastic junk but this controller is the real deal. I'm a huge fan of racing games and have had a modest setup for about 10 years now that I've been evolving over time. I have a Playseat and Logitech G27 wheel and pedals which is old now but still works ok. I plan to upgrade to the Thrustmaster racing wheel and pedals soon. I am playing on PC, and for some reason the description on this item makes it look like it only works for XBOX One. It actually works for XB1, PS4, and PC. You do need compatible wheels for console use, and I'd check the Thrustmaster website for more info if you plan to use this for console and aren't sure if your wheel is compatible.

The handbrake option is very cool, and can be adjusted for horizontal or vertical mode depending on your driving style, but I have been using this as a sequential shifter and it's been amazing. The shifts feel crispy and clicky and just what I've been wanting from a shifter. It's similar to the World Rally style sequential shifters when you have the handle sticking straight up and it is just an amazing experience. I had to mount the shifter, and I used a metal plate to mount it to my racing chair so it wouldn't move around.

The shifter assembly itself is heavy and larger than expected. The handbrake/shifter knob is nice quality and feels like something that could be on an actual car. This is a big investment but if you are trying to get that real feel of a handbrake or sequential shifter, this is the best one I've ever used. and it's not even close. I plan to pair this with the Thrustmaster TS-XW with Sparco P310 (https://www.amazon.com/Thrustmaster-TS-XW-Racer-Sparco-P310-Competition/dp/B074VDDK7X) for my dream racing setup.

I don't really have anything negative to say about this. The quality and feel is just way better than expected. The cost is probably the biggest downside, but this shifter is just a small part of the total cost of building a racing simulator for PC, especially if you have a motion platform.

Great pair of wireless headphones with microphone made for the XBOX 1. Just plug in the USB dongle and it detects the headset and just works. Headset is made of plastic but it feels high quality and has comfortable cloth ear cups and isn't uncomfortable even after hours of playing. Sound quality is better than expected with decent bass and overall nice tone.

Another great feature of these is they also work great for PC. Just plug in the USB device and Windows detects both the headphones and mic automatically. Sounds and works great and volume on both PC and XB is nice and loud with minimal distortion at high volumes.

Overall a great wireless headset. No noticeable latency and better build and audio quality than expected for a headset under 100 dollars. I'm giving this 4.5 stars, but I decided to round up because this headset really caught me off guard with how nice it is. The headset is fairly light as well, so even younger kids will be able to wear this when gaming without the weight bothering them. The adjustable sides go from very small to fairly large and these should fit just about any head size.

I know Turtle Beach doesn't have the best reputation for good quality headsets, and especially their wireless headsets have always left something to be desired over the years. However, I wanted a decent headset with mic for my XB1 and seeing streamers like Dr. Disrespect use a version of the Stealth 600 every day on stream I figured they can't be that bad... and they really aren't bad at all.

The earcups are a cloth material but are comfortable and don't make my ears hot, even after hours of playing. Everything on the headphones is plastic and I'm a bit worried about the part that adjusts the headphone size breaking. It seems flimsy but as long as I don't drop or sit on them they should be ok. The flip down microphone is great. Just pull it down and it unmutes. Flip it back up to mute, no need to feel for a mute button on the earcups.

All the controls are on the left side where the mic is. You can turn the power on and off and select different features like enhances bass and "superhuman hearing" which is good for first person shooter games to help hear footsteps. I don't really like any of those special modes, so I keep it on the regular mode. The power will shut off on its own if you don't use it for a while, so if you turn off your Xbox and forget to power down the headphones, they power off on their own. You can cancel the auto shutdown by pushing the power button when the guy's voice warns you.

Audio quality on these is good. nice crisp sound and the mic works decently as well. The battery lasts a while and can be charged with a micro USB cable, and the headphones work with the cable plugged in too. The white and green color match the XBOX One S pretty well and overall I'm really happy with these. My main criticism is the quality of the part where the headphones adjust, they just seem like they will break if I'm not careful. Other than that, these are some of the more comfortable headphones I've worn for gaming. I prefer the cloth ear cups to the fake leather, those always make my ears hot. This is probably one of the best Turtle Beach products I've ever used. Hopefully they continue on this path to making decent quality headphones at a reasonable price.

I do want to note that these work on XB1 of course but also on any Windows PC. Just plug the USB dongle to your motherboard and it automatically detects the headphones and they work great with almost no latency, even on a high FPS gaming PC.

This is a plug and play controller that works great on both Windows 10 and XBOX One. It comes with a long cable that might not be long enough if you sit back far from your TV. I'm using this mainly on my Windows 10 computer to play games like Rocket League and Skyrim that I enjoy more with a controller. The front of it almost looks like a colorful version of the standard white XB1 controller, and it feels similar too which is a good thing because it's a very high quality controller. All the buttons are in the right place and the thumbsticks have nice grip on them. The 4 triggers have a nice feel to them and it's overall a very solid controller.

However, this is a NERF controller and of course the back is coated with a Nerf-foam material that's super comfortable to hold. It's soft but not super squishy and feels really nice to hold compared to the normal hard controller. So I'm a big fan of the foam, it makes this a great choice for PC controller gaming. The power cable is detachable but it stays in really well and has a channel to help guide it so you don't put it in sideways and damage the delicate micro USB connector. I wish they would stop using this connector but it is very common and you can use your own micro USB cable if you want a shorter or different one. A 10 foot cable is a little much since my PC is right next to me and I'm right in front of the monitor. I'm very happy with this controller, there's no unnecessary turbo feature or extra buttons, it's just a normal XB controller and all the buttons are high quality and it has a great feeling overall.

I've been using an Astro A40 TR wired headset for years now on both XBOX 1 and PC and I'm a big fan of the A40 in general because it's the most comfortable gaming headset I've found and the sound is pretty good for gaming. I never got the wireless A50 because I didn't think it was worth it expense just to remove the wire. However, this entry level A20 headset is really interesting to me because the price makes it much more accessible to a wider audience, and because it works on both PC and XBOX, you can easily switch between the two platforms. XBOX uses optical audio and is easy to set up. PC just plugs right in with USB, there's absolutely no setup needed. 2 Micro USB cables are included and you can use the little box to charge your headset.

Compared to the A40, the A20 headset is a lot smaller and seems designed for smaller heads. However, when fully opened up, the headset does fit me fine but I am at the absolute limit and I wouldn't recommend this for someone with an extra large head. That's my main complaint about this headset, it's a bit small. Other basic Astro features have also been eliminated to keep the cost down so you can't remove the ear cups, microphone, and there are no magnetic tags on the side. The good side of all this is the headset is still very comfortable and has the standard cloth ear cups which don't get sweaty and are comfortable to wear for hours at a time. The top headband has a soft rubber material that has a nice cushion. It may cause sweating for bald heads on a hot day but I was not able to confirm this personally. I find the overall comfort to be pretty good, similar to the A40, but a little tighter on the ears for an adult head.

Sound quality is not bad. I'm listening to music right now and it's decent. Slightly bass heavy and not as crisp as high end headphones but overall it's better than expected. There is almost no noticeable audio latency and the wireless system is reliable and has decent range. I'm able to walk into the next room and grab a snack without the audio cutting out but it will cut out if you go far enough away from the transmitter/receiver unit. There are a few preset audio EQ settings but only the first one is useful for listening to music. The other ones modify the sound for games to help hear ambient sound better like footsteps and it does work ok but I prefer the first setting because it sounds the best to me. There is no surround sound, it's just stereo but it does sound pretty good as I mentioned. Microphone quality is fine, not as good as the A40 but people could hear and understand me fine. The microphone mutes itself when you raise it up and there's no other mute button. The other controls besides the EQ on the right side of the headset are the power button and a wheel that controls volume. There are buttons above and below the wheels to adjust voice or game volume.

Battery life is very good. 15 hours is advertised and I find myself only needing to charge it every few days, using it a few hours each day. You can charge it on the transmitter box or on any USB port. There is no way to input your own audio and the transmitter box is not a mixamp, it's basically the same as one of those little dongles that plugs into a PC USB port, but it's able to work with XBOX as well as PC and you can tuck it out of the way if you don't want to use it to charge but you will lose a bit of range. Headset can still be used when charging so even if the battery runs out you can keep using it if you have the charging cable nearby.

I didn't even mention that this is the Call of Duty version. Aside from some different colors and branding, it's the same as the normal A20. There design is very monotone grey and black and there is a large A20 on each side with the CoD logo and some grey digi camo. I do like the basic design but that's a matter of taste and the normal XBOX version of this headset features the usual green accents but is more black and less silver. The transmitter box is all black with a subtle CoD skull logo and looks pretty clean.

Astro Command Center: This is software that is free on Astro's website and installs in about 5 seconds on PC. It allows you to adjust EQ and microphone noise gate settings and save them to the headset. You can also adjust the default voice/game balance. The software does allow you to do advanced EQ 5 band adjustment which can really mess up the sound but I was able to get it sounding more how I like it by boosting bass a bit and cutting some of the midrange (around 500hz) that felt muddy to my ears. I'll keep messing with this but I've saved my custom setting to one of the presets I wasn't using and it's been pretty good so far.

Overall, I'm pretty impressed with how nice this headset is at this entry level price point. It's super bare bones so don't expect to be able to customize it at all unless you want to slap some stickers on the sides or something. It's a bit small and not very adjustable and I find myself wishing I could tilt the ear cups in sometimes but I'm also used to wearing the A40 TR headset which is wired but has a more premium feel. Don't expect super bass or 7.1 surround sound with these, but for a nice looking, well built basic wireless headset with good battery life, this is an excellent choice. I have never used the Astro A50 wireless but I do still have a pair of A38 Bluetooth headphones that I reviewed years ago and they are still hanging in there after using them so much and taking them everywhere. The A20 isn't quite the same quality level as other Astro products but it's not bad at all and an affordable way to get into a decent wireless headset for PC or console gaming.

There's a lot to like about this XBOX One controller. It works great on XB1 and Windows PC and both systems, it has the general shape and feel of the original controller, and it adds some pretty interesting features. The adjustable height triggers are the most interesting to me, and the ability to shorten the travel distance of the left and right trigger independently is useful for games where you are clicking fast to fire a weapon. The adjustment is easy to make quickly without looking and no tools are required so it's probably my favorite feature.

My second favorite thing are the 2 programmable buttons on the back, which you use your ring fingers to tap. This is great because you can assign one of the other buttons there, especially useful for games where you need to go between the right thumb stick and one of the XYBA buttons, and it can actually give you a competitive advantage in some games. The buttons are easily programmable by holding down the program button, pushing the button you want to reassign and then pushing the left or right extra button to program it in.

Other nice features include the long over 9 foot braided cable with a micro USB end. This cable is nicer than other wired controllers I've used since it has a locking end that snaps in place but can be removed easily if needed. Other micro USB cables can be used but they won't lock into place like the original cable. The adjustable LED colors are kind of fun, nice for seeing your controller in a dark room and easy to change colors by pushing a button on the back of the controller. The 3.5mm audio jack on the bottom is like the newer model XB1 controller and works with most analog gaming headsets.

The only thing I don't love about this controller is the finish on the top. It looks nice but it's a bit slippery for my hands. I'm trying to get used to it but I still prefer the original white XB1 controller if I have a choice. There is absolutely nothing wrong with the buttons, D pad, or thumb sticks, which all look and feel very much like the original controller. The controller has a high quality look and feel but I almost wish they used rough plastic on the face of it which wouldn't look as nice but would have more grip. I was able to use a cloth to rub the rubbery surface to remove any oils and make it less slick so that helped a bit.

I've been using this controller mostly for PC gaming, it works well and allows me to keep my XB1 controllers with that system and not worry about ever changing out batteries. For some games like the Witcher 3 and Rocket League, I prefer a controller and the programmable buttons have given me a lot of options for new play styles to help me improve, especially on fast paced first and third person games.

This PDP controller stays true to the standard Xbox One controller but it does add button remapping via software as well as a couple new hardware buttons for sharing images or videos and the directional pad can be used to adjust audio level, which I appreciate since you don't have to take your hands off the controller to do so.

A 3.5mm headphone jack is included which is expected these days, and works with most headsets. I prefer a wired controller for Windows, no batteries to replace and I'm sitting so close to my monitor that I don't really notice the cable anyway. The overall quality of this controller is very good, and none of the buttons or triggers feel especially cheap. I do think the ability to remap the buttons as well as things like trigger deadzones is very useful although you will need to download the PDP control app.

For XB1 and other consoles, this is plug and play and a decent option for an extra controller if you don't mind it being wired. I got used to it quickly although I do forget about the share button, and haven't really used it except to test that it works. Overall, a good controller and I'm happy with it for Windows games that use a controller.

While I really like this gaming headset, it has some things that I was expecting at this price point. The microphone is not removable, and it doesn't flip up like a lot of headphones. The best you can do is bend it out of the way a bit, kind of annoying but not a huge deal. The overall feel of the buttons is ok, but not as nice as the higher end Razer headsets. The USB-C dongle works well and plugs right into the PS5, making it very easy to connect and start using. Microphone quality is ok, which makes it even more annoying that it's not removable.

The Bluetooth mode is pretty cool, allowing you to quickly switch between your PS5 and other BT devices after you've connected them. There is an app to adjust EQ settings, but I found that the default settings sound the best to me so I only used it once to check it out and I haven't used it since. You can create a custom EQ setting and save it to the headset if you want. I felt that the bass mode just made everything sound more muddy and not as clear.

Comfort is very good when playing for a long time and the overall audio quality is better than I was expecting. For the price, this is a nice 2.4ghz wireless headset and has been great for late night PS5 gaming sessions without waking up sleeping members of my family, as long as I talk quietly into the mic.
